title: Political Science: Political Data & Statistics
text:
Skip to Main Content

Introduction

Political Data & Statistics

Datasets are collections of quantitative or other numeric data gathered from surveys, interviews, or other means that can be analyzed using specialized software such as Stata, SPSS, or R. This section list both publicly available and subscription datasets relevant to political science studies.

Frequently Used Data Sources

-

Sage Data
This link opens in a new window

-
- This link opens in a new window

Sage Data aggregates datasets sourced from reputable public and private organizations, such as OECD, China Data Online, the United Nations, and the U.S. Census. It covers topics across many subject areas, including education, population and income, industry, commerce, trade, housing and construction. Users can create custom extracts and download files in delimited, SAS, or shapefile formats.

-

Harvard Dataverse This link opens in a new window

Dataverse is the world's largest open source research data repository of social science research datasets. It facilitates making data available to others, and allows you to replicate others' work more easily. Researchers, data authors, publishers, data distributors, and affiliated institutions all receive academic credit and web visibility.

-

Inter-University Consortium for Political and Social Research (ICPSR)
This link opens in a new window

ICPSR is a social science repository that includes curated data sets pertaining to many disciplines within the social sciences. ICPSR contains original codebooks and descriptions of methodology, offers multiple file format downloads, and links data to relevant scholarly research. Users can search at the variable level and trace datasets to their use in academic publications. The archive also includes data-driven learning guides for those teaching with data.

Users must register for an account to access. To register, click on “Login” and “Create an account”. Once registered, click on “Login” and use the “Sign in with email” option to access the database.

-

IPUMS This link opens in a new window

IPUMS provides census and survey data from around the world integrated across time and space. IPUMS integration and documentation makes it easy to study change, conduct comparative research, merge information across data types, and analyze individuals within family and community contexts. Data and services available free of charge.

-

The Quality of Government (QOG) Institute This link opens in a new window

The QOG Institute at the University of Gothenburg studies good governance and corruption on a global scale. QoG provides a range of datasets available for free, and data visualization tools. QoG Standard Dataset contains the most qualitative variables from the Standard Dataset. The QoG Expert Survey is a dataset based on our survey of experts on public administration around the world, available in an individual dataset and an aggregated dataset covering 107 countries.The QoG OECD dataset covers countries who are members of the OECD. The EU Regional Data consists of 450 variables from Eurostat and other sources, covering three levels of European regions - country, major socio-economic regions and basic regions for the application of regional policies.

-

Statista
This link opens in a new window

Statista aggregates data on markets, industry, politics, economics, and population. Users can export datasets in a variety of formats. Sources include trade publications, market and opinion research institutions, government sources, business and economic databases, reference publications, media sources, and scholarly articles. Include Statista's "Global Consumer Survey", which helps marketers understand consumer behavior and brand interaction.

-

Statistical Insight
This link opens in a new window

Statistical Insight provides indexing and abstracts for federal, state, and international statistical publications as well as selected business and professional publications containing statistics. Approximately 20% of the federal statistical publications are available in full text. This resource includes all content from the American Statistics Index (ASI), Statistical Reference Index (SRI), and Index to International Statistics (IIS), including Statistical Datasets. Dates of coverage: 1973 to present.

title: Political Science: Political Economy
text:
Skip to Main Content

Introduction

Political Economy

Political economy is the systemic study of economic forces in society. The field of political economy covers topics such as social choice, electoral competition, public choice, public economics, and comparative electoral systems. The following list of reference materials, databases and resources are recommended for conducting research in this area of study. Before using the recommended article databases below to start your research, here are a few tips when choosing databases:

- Locate background information with a subject encyclopedia such as The SAGE Encyclopedia of Economics and Society .

- Look for articles in a general article database such as EBSCO Discovery .

- Use subject databases such as EconLit for subject-specific articles.

Background Resources

-

New Palgrave Dictionary of Economics Online (Palgrave Macmillan) This link opens in a new window

The online edition of The New Palgrave Dictionary of Economics contains the full text of the 8 volume print edition with continual updates. More than 1,500 economists contributed almost 1,900 signed entries; more than 1,000 of the entries are new or 'heavily revised' and expanded. Along with the descriptions of economic method from earlier editions, this edition includes much information on 'what those methods have found.' It also offers new emphasis on advances that have occurred in microeconomics, Bayesian theory, game theory, and behavioral, international, and experimental economics.

-

Oxford Encyclopedia of Economic History This link opens in a new window

International in scope and spanning all time periods of human history, The Oxford Encyclopedia of Economic History includes 900 original articles by noted scholars from more than thirty-five countries. Articles range from 500-word entries on inventors, theoreticians, and industry leaders to overarching, 8,000-word essays on markets, industries, and labor. With coverage ranging from accounting and advertising to zoning and zoos, this landmark works stands at the busy intersection of history and the social sciences.

-

The SAGE Encyclopedia of Economics and Society This link opens in a new window

The SAGE Encyclopedia of Economics and Society emphasizes the contemporary world, contemporary issues, and society. Contains 4 volumes with approximately 800 signed articles ranging from 1,000 to 5,000 words.

General Article Databases

The two largest general academic databases are EBSCOhost and ProQuest Central . Known primarily by their vendor names, EBSCO and ProQuest are aggregators of individual databases that use a single search interface. Each contain a combination of full-text and citation databases and provide a varied mix of scholarly journals, trade publications, general magazines, and newspaper resources. EBSCO and ProQuest are also multidisciplinary , which means they cover a wide range of subject areas.

-

ProQuest Central
This link opens in a new window

ProQuest Central is a large, multidisciplinary database with over 11,000 titles, with over 8,000 titles in full-text. It serves as the central resource for researchers at all levels in all markets. Over 160 subjects areas are covered extensively in this product including business and economics, health and medical, news and world affairs, technology, social sciences and more.

Key Economic Article Databases

-

ABI/INFORM
This link opens in a new window

ABI/INFORM features full-text journals, dissertations, working papers, key business, and economics periodicals. Researchers can locate country- and industry-focused reports, and its international focus provides a picture of companies and business trends around the world.

-

EconLit
This link opens in a new window

EconLit is published by the American Economic Association and indexes and abstracts a wide range of economics-related literature. An expanded version of the Journal of Economic Literature (JEL) indexes of journals, books, and dissertations, EconLit covers both economic theory and application. Coverage dates: 1969 to present.

-

EconPapers This link opens in a new window

EconPapers is the search interface for RePEc (repec.org), an open access database of over 700,000 scholarly business and economic working papers, 1, 000,000 journal articles, 4,000 software items, 27,000 downloadable books and 27,500 book chapters. Most publications are available full text, although access to some journal articles requires an institutional subscription.

-

Fed in Print This link opens in a new window

Index to all Federal Reserve Board and Banks' publications with selected full text in more recent years.

-

NBER Working Papers
This link opens in a new window

The National Bureau of Economic Research (NBER) includes the entire run of NBER Working Papers and NBER working paper series on historical factors in long-run growth and the NBER Technical Working Papers.

-

OECD
This link opens in a new window

-

OECD (formerly OECD iLibrary) is the online portal for the Organization for Economic Co-operation and Development. The OCED content includes book collections, policy reports, statistical abstracts, and the OECD.Stat tool, with which users can create custom extracts from the OECD data warehouse.

-

RePEc (Research Papers in Economics) This link opens in a new window

RePEc (Research Papers in Economics) is a collaborative effort of hundreds of volunteers in 75 countries to enhance the dissemination of research in Economics and related sciences. The heart of the project is a decentralized bibliographic database of working papers, journal articles, books, books chapters and software components, all maintained by volunteers. The collected data is then used in various services as described below.

-

SSRN's Economics Research Centers Papers This link opens in a new window

Social Science Research Network is devoted to the rapid worldwide dissemination of social science research and is composed of a number of specialized research networks in each of the social sciences. NOTE: In order to subscribe to the NYU network one must create an account with their NYU email address. Please note that when accessing through off-site connection you may encounter a login screen which indicates you can 'login anonymously.' If you reach this choose to login anonymously and you will be granted access.

-

World Bank - Publications and Documents This link opens in a new window

The World Bank is a development institution which seeks to reduce poverty in middle-income and creditworthy poor countries.The Publications and Documents section offers the following full-text free resources: (1) Documents and Reports provides operational documents, formal and informal research papers, and most bank publications;(2) The Open Knowledge Repository (OKR) provides free access to thousands of research outputs and knowledge products on development, and (3) Archives provides official World Bank records from 1946 to the current.

title: Political Science: Political Theory
text:
Skip to Main Content

Introduction

Political Theory

How should a state be governed? What is the best form of government for a society? How should we choose our political leaders? These are typical questions posed in the area of political theory. This section list major databases useful for locating information and articles in the areas of political philosophy and political theory.

- Use a subject encyclopedia such as the Encyclopedia of Political Theory to learn key political theory concepts.

- Search for research articles in a general, multidisciplinary database such as ProQuest Central .

- Use philosophy subject-specific databases such as Philosopher's Index .

Background Resources

-

Encyclopedia of Political Theory

The online edition of the Encyclopedia of Political Theory examines the ideas of the major political theorists from before Plato to our own times. Key Themes include: Ancient Thought; Applied Ethics; Biographies; Comparative Theory; Constitutional Thought; Critical Theory; Democratic Thought; Early Modern Thought; International Theory; Justice; Liberal Theory; Medieval Thought; Modern Theory; Power and Authority; Religious Thought; Self and Community.

-

The Oxford Handbook of Political Theory

The electronic edition of The Oxford Handbook of Political Theory provides comprehensive and critical coverage of political theory. In this book, forty-five articles by distinguished political theorists look at the state of the field, where it has been in the recent past, and where it is likely to go in future. They examine political theory's edges as well as its core, the globalizing context of the field, and the challenges presented by social, economic, and technological changes.

-

Routledge Encyclopedia of Philosophy

by

Edward Craig (Editor)

The REP consists of ten volumes of the world's most eminent philosophers writing for the needs of students and teachers of philosophy internationally. Over 2000 entries ranging from 500 to 15,000 words in length - thematic, biographical and national 10 volumes consisting of over 5 million words of text plus considerable bibliographic material.

-

The Shorter Routledge Encyclopedia of Philosophy

by

Edward Craig

The Shorter REP presents the very best of the acclaimed ten volume Routledge Encyclopedia of Philosophy in a single volume. It makes a selection of the most important entries available for the first time and covers all you need to know about philosophy, from Aristotle to Wittgenstein and animals and ethics to scientific method. Comprising over 900 entries and covering the major philosophers and philosophical topics.

-

The Encyclopedia of Political Thought

by

Michael T. Gibbons

Examines the history of political thought from antiquity to contemporary political theory and political philosophy. This and other resources listed will provide the following: explanations of the main concepts of political theory; titles of important books written about topic; names of authors who have written about topic, information about major political theorists and their key theories and methods; lists of related articles or additional political theory resources.

Key Political Theory Reference Databases

-

Cambridge Histories Online
This link opens in a new window

sections.title: Introduction · Political Theory
sections.text:
How should a state be governed? What is the best form of government for a society? How should we choose our political leaders? These are typical questions posed in the area of political theory. This section list major databases useful for locating information and articles in the areas of political philosophy and political theory.

- Use a subject encyclopedia such as the Encyclopedia of Political Theory to learn key political theory concepts.

- Search for research articles in a general, multidisciplinary database such as ProQuest Central .

- Use philosophy subject-specific databases such as Philosopher's Index .

sections.title: Background Resources
sections.text:
-

Encyclopedia of Political Theory

The online edition of the Encyclopedia of Political Theory examines the ideas of the major political theorists from before Plato to our own times. Key Themes include: Ancient Thought; Applied Ethics; Biographies; Comparative Theory; Constitutional Thought; Critical Theory; Democratic Thought; Early Modern Thought; International Theory; Justice; Liberal Theory; Medieval Thought; Modern Theory; Power and Authority; Religious Thought; Self and Community.

-

The Oxford Handbook of Political Theory

The electronic edition of The Oxford Handbook of Political Theory provides comprehensive and critical coverage of political theory. In this book, forty-five articles by distinguished political theorists look at the state of the field, where it has been in the recent past, and where it is likely to go in future. They examine political theory's edges as well as its core, the globalizing context of the field, and the challenges presented by social, economic, and technological changes.

-

Routledge Encyclopedia of Philosophy

by

Edward Craig (Editor)

The REP consists of ten volumes of the world's most eminent philosophers writing for the needs of students and teachers of philosophy internationally. Over 2000 entries ranging from 500 to 15,000 words in length - thematic, biographical and national 10 volumes consisting of over 5 million words of text plus considerable bibliographic material.

-

The Shorter Routledge Encyclopedia of Philosophy

by

Edward Craig

The Shorter REP presents the very best of the acclaimed ten volume Routledge Encyclopedia of Philosophy in a single volume. It makes a selection of the most important entries available for the first time and covers all you need to know about philosophy, from Aristotle to Wittgenstein and animals and ethics to scientific method. Comprising over 900 entries and covering the major philosophers and philosophical topics.

-

The Encyclopedia of Political Thought

by

Michael T. Gibbons

Examines the history of political thought from antiquity to contemporary political theory and political philosophy. This and other resources listed will provide the following: explanations of the main concepts of political theory; titles of important books written about topic; names of authors who have written about topic, information about major political theorists and their key theories and methods; lists of related articles or additional political theory resources.

title: Political Science: Public Opinion Data & Survey Research
text:
Skip to Main Content

United States

-

American National Election Studies (ANES) This link opens in a new window

The American National Election Studies (ANES) produces high quality data on voting, public opinion, and political participation to serve the research needs of social scientists, teachers, students, policy makers and journalists who want to better understand the theoretical and empirical foundations of national election outcomes.

-

American Public Opinion and US Foreign Policy Series This link opens in a new window

This series of quadrennial studies was designed to investigate the opinions and attitudes of the general public and a select group of opinion leaders on matters relating to United States foreign policy and to define the parameters of public opinion within which decision-makers must operate.

-

Annual Survey of Governments This link opens in a new window

State and local government employment and finance data. Holdings cover 1973-1992. More recent years can be downloaded from the U. S. Census Bureau website's Federal, State, and Local Governments page.

-

Database on Ideology, Money in Politics, and Elections (DIME) This link opens in a new window

The Database on Ideology, Money in Politics, and Elections (DIME) is intended as a general resource for the study of campaign finance and ideology in American politics.

-

Dataverse This link opens in a new window

An open source web application for sharing and locating datasets in the social and physical sciences.

-

National Black Election Studies This link opens in a new window

The purpose of this data series was to provide large-scale scientific surveys and make possible in-depth investigation of the political attitudes, perceptions, and electoral behaviors of a large, representative national sample of adult Black Americans. The studies permit analyses and change in the Black community on a scale that had not been possible before the series began.

International

-

AmericasBarometer This link opens in a new window

The survey is produced by the Latin American Public Opinion Project (LAPOP). It is the only scientifically rigorous comparative survey that covers 28 nations including all of North, Central, and South America, as well as a significant number of countries in the Caribbean. The AmericasBarometer data sets feature a common core set of questions that has been asked from 2004 to present day. In addition, LAPOP has datasets that date back to the 1970s.

-

Asia Foundation This link opens in a new window

Conducts public opinion surveys in several Asia-Pacific countries.

-

Council of European Social Science Data Archives (CESSDA) Portal This link opens in a new window

Gateway to many kinds of research data and metadata, including sociological surveys, election studies, longitudinal studies, opinion polls, and census data.

-

Eurobarometer Survey Series. 1970+ This link opens in a new window

Large set of surveys measuring public opinion in the countries of the European Union, on a wide variety of topics.

-

European Values Study This link opens in a new window

The European Values Study is a large-scale, cross-national, and longitudinal survey research program on basic human values. It provides insights into the ideas, beliefs, preferences, attitudes, values and opinions of citizens all over Europe. It is a unique research project on how Europeans think about life, family, work, religion, politics and society.

-

LAPOP - Latin American Public Opinion Project This link opens in a new window

Since the 1970s, Mitchell Seligson and his colleagues and students have systematically surveyed the citizens of Latin America on their political views—specifically on democratic values and their behaviors related to democracy. Some surveys were also conducted outside of Latin America, and the number of survey rounds conducted per country varies from one to over a dozen. The LAPOP Data Repository at Yale University contains (as of January 2009) all available datasets through 2008.

-

Polity IV: Political Regime Characteristics and Transitions This link opens in a new window

This Web site contains information on and access to the most recent update of the Polity data series, originally designed by Ted Robert Gurr. The Polity IV Project continues the Polity research tradition of coding the authority characteristics of states in the world system for purposes of comparative, quantitative analysis.

-

World Values Survey This link opens in a new window

World Values Survey (WVS) is a global research project that explores people’s values and beliefs, their stability or change over time and their impact on social and political development of the societies in different countries of the world.

Survey Question Databases

-

iPOLL database This link opens in a new window

The best finding aid to locate national US public opinion polls rich in a particular subject, iPOLL contains half a million survey questions and answers asked in the US over the last 70+ years by more than 150 survey organizations.

-

Roper Center Public Opinion Archives This link opens in a new window

Archives datasets from thousands of surveys with national adult, state, foreign, and special subpopulation samples. Along with such basic information as survey organization, interview dates, and type of sample, most catalog entries include abstracts indicating the subjects covered by the questions in the survey. **To search, click on "Data Access" and then "IPoll Databank"; you'll be prompted to sign in with your email address.

-

Gallup Brain This link opens in a new window

Gallup Brain Questions and answers from The Gallup Poll since 1935. No raw data for analysis.

-

Polling the Nations This link opens in a new window

A compilation of more than 14,000 surveys conducted by over 1000 polling organizations in the US and 100 other countries from 1986 to the present time. The pollsters included are: U.S. polling organizations (e.g., Harris International, The Pew Center); Universities (e.g., Rice University, University of Maryland); Newspapers (e.g., New York Times, Los Angeles Times); Television news organizations (e.g., CBS, NBS, Fox, CNN); World polling organizations (e.g., Eurobarometer).

-

Pew Global Attitudes Project Key Indicators Database This link opens in a new window

Online data analysis; published questions and responses; and raw data for download. Covers 55 countries going back to 2002.

Introduction

About the Collection

The United Nations and International Documents Collection at Bobst Library has been a full depository library for UN documents since 1949. It is also a Food and Agriculture Organization of the United Nations (FAO) and World Tourism Organization (WTO) depository library since 1965 and 2003, respectively. It houses historical documents from the League of Nations and the UN Conference on International Organizations as well as publications from the Council of Europe, International Atomic Energy Agency (IAEA), Inter-American Development Bank (IADB), International Labour Organization (ILO), International Monetary Fund (IMF), Organization of American States (OAS), Organisation for Economic Co-operation and Development ilibrary (OECD), World Health Organization (WHO) and World Bank Group.

text:
Skip to Main Content

Rebecca Maniates

Email Me

Contact: New York University Abu Dhabi
+971-262-84562

Subjects: Business , Economics , Politics , Public Policy and Administration , Social Sciences , Sociology

Introduction

The Social Research and Public Policy (SSRP) program offers a variety of courses covering a range of subject areas including economics, history, law, political science, and sociology, as well as courses in quantitative and qualitative research methods. Please use the databases and other resources suggested in this guide to locate resources for your SSRP course.

General Article Databases

The two largest general academic databases are EBSCOhost and ProQuest Central . Known primarily by their vendor names, EBSCO and ProQuest are aggregators of individual databases that use a single search interface. Each contain a combination of full-text and citation databases and provide a varied mix of scholarly journals, trade publications, general magazines, and newspaper resources. EBSCO and ProQuest are also multidisciplinary , which means they cover a wide range of subject areas.

-

ProQuest Central
This link opens in a new window

ProQuest Central is a large, multidisciplinary database with over 11,000 titles, with over 8,000 titles in full-text. It serves as the central resource for researchers at all levels in all markets. Over 160 subjects areas are covered extensively in this product including business and economics, health and medical, news and world affairs, technology, social sciences and more.

-

JSTOR
This link opens in a new window

JSTOR provides access to scholarly journals, primarily in the humanities and social sciences. In addition to journal articles, users can access book chapters, ebooks, and primary source documents.

Introduction

Background Research

While you might have a particular research topic in mind, you may not be familiar with the events, people, or issues involved. Using a good secondary source for background research can provide you with that information. This page lists relevant general and economics specific reference databases which include encyclopedias , dictionaries , handbooks, and other economics related background resources. Here are several tips when choosing reference materials.

- Locate background information or learn key political concepts from a subject encyclopedia such as The Encyclopedia of Philosophy and the Social Sciences .

- Search one of the many online reference databases listed below such as Blackwell Reference Online .

sections.title: Introduction · Background Research
sections.text:
While you might have a particular research topic in mind, you may not be familiar with the events, people, or issues involved. Using a good secondary source for background research can provide you with that information. This page lists relevant general and economics specific reference databases which include encyclopedias , dictionaries , handbooks, and other economics related background resources. Here are several tips when choosing reference materials.

- Locate background information or learn key political concepts from a subject encyclopedia such as The Encyclopedia of Philosophy and the Social Sciences .

- Search one of the many online reference databases listed below such as Blackwell Reference Online .

sections.title: Full-Text Online Reference Databases
sections.text:
-

Cambridge Histories Online
This link opens in a new window

Over 250 of these well-known, used and trusted volumes published since the 1960s are available online; covers 14 subject areas, including General History, Regional History, Literary Studies, Philosophy, and Religious Studies.

-

CQ Press at Sage Knowledge
This link opens in a new window

The CQ Press Library at Sage Knowledge (formerly the Political Reference Suite of Online Editions) aggregates reference materials, encyclopedias, and primary source documents on legislative history in the United States.

-

Credo Reference
This link opens in a new window

Online collection of dictionaries, encyclopedias, biographical sources, quotations, bilingual dictionaries, and measurement conversions covering topics from the arts to the sciences.

-

Gale eBooks (formerly Gale Virtual Reference Library)
This link opens in a new window

Search across a range of encyclopedias, dictionaries and more.

-

Oxford Bibliographies
This link opens in a new window

-

Oxford Bibliographies presents constantly updated articles that contain citations (with annotations) and commentaries for sources across the disciplines. Users can search topics and gather relevant journal article and book citations, online resources, data sources, and more.

-

Oxford Handbooks Online
This link opens in a new window

-

Oxford Handbooks Online contains the complete text of the Oxford Handbooks series, including titles in business, history, literature, music, philosophy, and more. Oxford Handbooks Online also contains pre-print articles.

-

Oxford Reference Online
This link opens in a new window

Provides full-text access to dictionaries, language reference, Islamic studies and subject reference works published by Oxford University Press.

-

Reference Universe (Paratext)
This link opens in a new window

Search across a number of reference works to find entries on a topic. Searches across 18-million articles in 40,000 reference books from 750 publishers.

-

Sage Knowledge
This link opens in a new window

Sage Knowledge is a social sciences digital library. It includes an expansive range of SAGE eBook and eReference content, including scholarly monographs, reference works, business case studies, handbooks, series, videos, professional development titles, and more.

Finding Economic Policy Resources

Economic policy research encompasses a variety of information resources. Although academic, scholarly or peer-reviewed articles and publications are considered the most appropriate sources for university level research and writing, you might also have need of general magazines and news articles. Before using the recommended article databases to start your research, here are a few tips when choosing databases:

- Start your research in a general article database such as EBSCO Discovery or ProQuest Central .

- Use economic subject-specific databases such as EconLit .

- If your assignment requires the use of scholarly, academic or peer-reviewed articles, try databases such as JSTOR

Key Economic Article Databases

-

ABI/INFORM
This link opens in a new window

ABI/INFORM features full-text journals, dissertations, working papers, key business, and economics periodicals. Researchers can locate country- and industry-focused reports, and its international focus provides a picture of companies and business trends around the world.

-

EconLit
This link opens in a new window

EconLit is published by the American Economic Association and indexes and abstracts a wide range of economics-related literature. An expanded version of the Journal of Economic Literature (JEL) indexes of journals, books, and dissertations, EconLit covers both economic theory and application. Coverage dates: 1969 to present.

-

EIU Viewpoint
This link opens in a new window

-

Economist Intelligence Unit's (EIU) country analysis and forecasts covers over 200 countries and highlight political, economic and business developments in all significant markets, both established and emerging. Includes access to the "CountryData" and "Market Indicators and Forecasts" modules.

For access to economic statistics, analysis, and forecasts for China's 31 provinces and 292 largest cities, click 'More' in the top right corner.

-

EconPapers This link opens in a new window

EconPapers is the search interface for RePEc (repec.org), an open access database of over 700,000 scholarly business and economic working papers, 1, 000,000 journal articles, 4,000 software items, 27,000 downloadable books and 27,500 book chapters. Most publications are available full text, although access to some journal articles requires an institutional subscription.

-

Fed in Print This link opens in a new window

Index to all Federal Reserve Board and Banks' publications with selected full text in more recent years.

-

NBER Working Papers
This link opens in a new window

The National Bureau of Economic Research (NBER) includes the entire run of NBER Working Papers and NBER working paper series on historical factors in long-run growth and the NBER Technical Working Papers.

-

OECD
This link opens in a new window

-

OECD (formerly OECD iLibrary) is the online portal for the Organization for Economic Co-operation and Development. The OCED content includes book collections, policy reports, statistical abstracts, and the OECD.Stat tool, with which users can create custom extracts from the OECD data warehouse.

-

RePEc (Research Papers in Economics) This link opens in a new window

RePEc (Research Papers in Economics) is a collaborative effort of hundreds of volunteers in 75 countries to enhance the dissemination of research in Economics and related sciences. The heart of the project is a decentralized bibliographic database of working papers, journal articles, books, books chapters and software components, all maintained by volunteers. The collected data is then used in various services as described below.

-

SSRN's Economics Research Centers Papers This link opens in a new window

Social Science Research Network is devoted to the rapid worldwide dissemination of social science research and is composed of a number of specialized research networks in each of the social sciences. NOTE: In order to subscribe to the NYU network one must create an account with their NYU email address. Please note that when accessing through off-site connection you may encounter a login screen which indicates you can 'login anonymously.' If you reach this choose to login anonymously and you will be granted access.

-

World Bank - Publications and Documents This link opens in a new window

The World Bank is a development institution which seeks to reduce poverty in middle-income and creditworthy poor countries.The Publications and Documents section offers the following full-text free resources: (1) Documents and Reports provides operational documents, formal and informal research papers, and most bank publications;(2) The Open Knowledge Repository (OKR) provides free access to thousands of research outputs and knowledge products on development, and (3) Archives provides official World Bank records from 1946 to the current.

Rebecca Maniates

Introduction

The Social Research and Public Policy (SSRP) program offers a variety of courses covering a range of subject areas including economics, history, law, political science, and sociology, as well as courses in quantitative and qualitative research methods. Please use the databases and other resources suggested in this guide to locate resources for your SSRP course.

General Article Databases

The two largest general academic databases are EBSCOhost and ProQuest Central . Known primarily by their vendor names, EBSCO and ProQuest are aggregators of individual databases that use a single search interface. Each contain a combination of full-text and citation databases and provide a varied mix of scholarly journals, trade publications, general magazines, and newspaper resources. EBSCO and ProQuest are also multidisciplinary , which means they cover a wide range of subject areas.

-

ProQuest Central
This link opens in a new window

ProQuest Central is a large, multidisciplinary database with over 11,000 titles, with over 8,000 titles in full-text. It serves as the central resource for researchers at all levels in all markets. Over 160 subjects areas are covered extensively in this product including business and economics, health and medical, news and world affairs, technology, social sciences and more.

-

JSTOR
This link opens in a new window

JSTOR provides access to scholarly journals, primarily in the humanities and social sciences. In addition to journal articles, users can access book chapters, ebooks, and primary source documents.

title: Social Research and Public Policy: Data & Statistics
text:
Skip to Main Content

Rebecca Maniates

Email Me

Contact: New York University Abu Dhabi
+971-262-84562

Subjects: Business , Economics , Politics , Public Policy and Administration , Social Sciences , Sociology

Finding Social Policy Statistics

Datasets are collections of quantitative or other numeric data gathered during surveys, interviews or other means that can be analyzed using specialized software such as Stata, SPSS, or R. This section list both publicly available and subscription datasets relevant to social research and public policy studies.

Frequently Used Data Sources

-

Sage Data
This link opens in a new window

-
- This link opens in a new window

Sage Data aggregates datasets sourced from reputable public and private organizations, such as OECD, China Data Online, the United Nations, and the U.S. Census. It covers topics across many subject areas, including education, population and income, industry, commerce, trade, housing and construction. Users can create custom extracts and download files in delimited, SAS, or shapefile formats.

-

Harvard Dataverse This link opens in a new window

Dataverse is the world's largest open source research data repository of social science research datasets. It facilitates making data available to others, and allows you to replicate others' work more easily. Researchers, data authors, publishers, data distributors, and affiliated institutions all receive academic credit and web visibility.

-

Inter-University Consortium for Political and Social Research (ICPSR)
This link opens in a new window

ICPSR is a social science repository that includes curated data sets pertaining to many disciplines within the social sciences. ICPSR contains original codebooks and descriptions of methodology, offers multiple file format downloads, and links data to relevant scholarly research. Users can search at the variable level and trace datasets to their use in academic publications. The archive also includes data-driven learning guides for those teaching with data.

Users must register for an account to access. To register, click on “Login” and “Create an account”. Once registered, click on “Login” and use the “Sign in with email” option to access the database.

-

IPUMS This link opens in a new window

IPUMS provides census and survey data from around the world integrated across time and space. IPUMS integration and documentation makes it easy to study change, conduct comparative research, merge information across data types, and analyze individuals within family and community contexts. Data and services available free of charge.

-

The Quality of Government (QOG) Institute This link opens in a new window

The QOG Institute at the University of Gothenburg studies good governance and corruption on a global scale. QoG provides a range of datasets available for free, and data visualization tools. QoG Standard Dataset contains the most qualitative variables from the Standard Dataset. The QoG Expert Survey is a dataset based on our survey of experts on public administration around the world, available in an individual dataset and an aggregated dataset covering 107 countries.The QoG OECD dataset covers countries who are members of the OECD. The EU Regional Data consists of 450 variables from Eurostat and other sources, covering three levels of European regions - country, major socio-economic regions and basic regions for the application of regional policies.

-

Statista
This link opens in a new window

Statista aggregates data on markets, industry, politics, economics, and population. Users can export datasets in a variety of formats. Sources include trade publications, market and opinion research institutions, government sources, business and economic databases, reference publications, media sources, and scholarly articles. Include Statista's "Global Consumer Survey", which helps marketers understand consumer behavior and brand interaction.

-

Statistical Insight
This link opens in a new window

Statistical Insight provides indexing and abstracts for federal, state, and international statistical publications as well as selected business and professional publications containing statistics. Approximately 20% of the federal statistical publications are available in full text. This resource includes all content from the American Statistics Index (ASI), Statistical Reference Index (SRI), and Index to International Statistics (IIS), including Statistical Datasets. Dates of coverage: 1973 to present.

Social Security Research - U.S.

-

Research, Statistics, & Policy Analysis This link opens in a new window

The research and policy analysis information section of the U.S. Social Security website is the result of a collaborative effort among three ORDP offices—the Office of Research, Demonstration, and Employment Support, the Office of Research, Evaluation, and Statistics, and the Office of Retirement Policy. All three offices work together to conduct research and policy analysis and disseminate the results of their research in a variety of publications that are available on this website.

Social Security Research - International

-

Social Security Programs Throughout the World This link opens in a new window

U.S. government publication produced by the Social Security Administration which highlights the principal features of social security programs in more than 170 countries. Published in collaboration with the International Social Security Association (ISSA), one of four regional volumes is issued every six months.

International Statistical Sources

-

OECD
This link opens in a new window

-

OECD (formerly OECD iLibrary) is the online portal for the Organization for Economic Co-operation and Development. The OCED content includes book collections, policy reports, statistical abstracts, and the OECD.Stat tool, with which users can create custom extracts from the OECD data warehouse.

-

UNdata
This link opens in a new window

-

UNdata is the data download portal of the United Nations. Users can search by country, year, and indicator and create custom data extracts to download. UNData also includes an API that developers can use to query, display results externally, and download to local storage for further analysis. The data portal includes datasets from the United Nations Statistics Division (UNSD), World Health Organization (WHO), and more.

title: Academics
text:
Academics






The 21st century requires rigorous, broad, and imaginative educational training. NYU Abu Dhabi provides extraordinary opportunities for individual exploration and growth, and prepares students to succeed in a truly global world.




















A New Model of Education







NYUAD, with an exceptional liberal arts and sciences college at its core, attracts students from across the United Arab Emirates and around the world, representing over 120 countries and six continents.

Beyond the Classroom







Global education is an essential component of NYU Abu Dhabi’s educational mission and curriculum. It is realized through a careful sequence of interrelated academic and intercultural experiences over four years that foster greater intercultural understanding towards social responsibility — globally and locally.

As we prepare to turn the page to the next chapter of our lives, I carry with me the cherished memories of our time together. Regardless of the directions we take in life, the profound impact of NYUAD will always remain deeply ingrained within us.
























































































Choosing a Major

Not sure what you want to do? It's OK! Students typically declare a major after first year.


Get inspired by reading about our students' favorite courses.

- Advanced Probability — Mathematics

- Exploring the Human Condition — Literature and Creative Writing

- Introduction to Political Theory — Political Science

- All majors and minors








As an NYU Abu Dhabi student, I learned the power of digesting and navigating intellectual discomfort as both a window for personal growth and for constructive conversations. With the growing global crisis on forced migration, the Rhodes allowed me to engage with a diverse cohort of visionaries committed to the delivery of humane, effective, and sustainable outcomes.


Just like all of my classmates, I was able to cultivate my safe space to thrive and ask questions, which happened to be in the ERB. Being just a door away from scientists, researchers, and individuals with whom I share similar interests was particularly inspiring.

title: Arab Film Studio Young Filmmakers Workshop
breadcrumbs: Arab Film Studio Young Filmmakers Workshop
text:
Arab Film Studio Young Filmmakers Workshop











The Arab Film Studio Young Filmmakers Workshop, a collaboration between Image Nation Abu Dhabi and NYU Abu Dhabi, is a three-week program for Emirati high school students that enables and enhances filmmaking skills.

Participants from across the UAE are exposed to the teachings and experience of leading industry professionals. From screenwriting, and directing to camera and post-production, the three weeks come to a close with a screening of a collection of short films that are written and directed by the participants.





















Eligibility Criteria

- Participating students must be below 18 years of age and must be currently in 10th or 11th grade.

- Father and/or mother must be a holder of an Emirati passport.


Important Dates

Dates will be announced soon.

| Date | Description
| TBA | Application Deadline

| TBA | Selection workshop

| TBA | Announcement of the new class
| TBA | Workshop








Apply to the AFS Young Filmmakers






























The program emphasizes and builds on students’ talents and skills, which are honed and brought to light through extensive courses that address the various aspects of filmmaking.

Location

All courses take place at the NYU Abu Dhabi campus, allowing students to have a full experience of learning filmmaking in a higher education institution.



-






- Provide a learning environment that will enable the students to tell stories that will contribute to the development of critical thinking.
- Nurture the creative potential of the students and stimulate originality of thought through the development of individual expression.
- Maintain the collective memory, history and identity of the people of the United Arab Emirates through their unique cultural expression.
- Develop the necessary skill-set for writing, directing and producing a short film. Students will gain experience in various production roles while crewing on each other’s films.
- Develop the necessary skill sets for creating soundtracks and sound design for film. Students will learn a bit of everything one needs to know when doing sound and/or music for film.
- Learn techniques necessary to break down a script, identify its sound needs, plan for shooting/sound recording and bring a script to the screen.


-





During the three weeks, the students participate in rigorous classes and activities giving them the opportunity to tap into their storytelling skills. By the completion of the program, the students learn and enhance their skills in writing, directing, and producing a short film.

Each student is required to create a one-minute film that will be showcased in front of their peers, faculty, and family during the final ceremony.

Classes typically take place at NYU Abu Dhabi Art Center from 10am until 5pm, followed by a film screening and discussion until 9pm on assigned dates. All classes are mixed gender.



-






- Workshop expenses are covered by Image Nation Abu Dhabi.

- Lunch is provided on workshop days.

- Transportation and Accommodation are not provided.










Application

Before submitting the online application please have the following documents ready for upload:

- Short story (an invented tale): in English, one page long, font size 12, single space

- Letter of motivation: in English, half page long, font size 12, single space

- Official school transcript

Selection Day

- Participants will be notified by early May if they have been shortlisted.

- Shortlisted candidates will be required to attend a selection workshop sometime in May of the participating year.

Enrollment of New Class

- Accepted students will be notified in June.
- Once students are accepted and have agreed to participate, they are sent a packet of required enrollment forms to fill out.
- Up to 12 students are selected to participate in the Arab Film Studio Young Filmmakers Workshop.






















Scandar Copti

Assistant Arts Professor of Film

Scandar Copti is an acclaimed filmmaker and visual artist, known for his awarded film Ajami. His first full-length feature film, Ajami, (co-directed by Yaron Shani) has won more than 15 awards worldwide to include the Camera d'Or Special Mention at the Cannes Film Festival. Ajami was also nominated for the 82nd Academy Awards in the Best Foreign Film category. Formerly a mechanical engineer, he has written, directed, and edited fiction, documentary, and experimental films. His video art projects were exhibited worldwide at venues such as Gutman Museum, b_tour Foothold Festival, Beit Alkarmeh, and the Oslo Kunstforening Art Gallery, among others. Copti was part of the team that launched the Doha Film Institute where he headed the Education department; he headed the Film and New Media program at NYU Abu Dhabi from 2014 to 2017. Currently, Copti is teaching filmmaking at NYUAD and developing his next feature film 'Happy Holidays.'



























Carlos Guedes

Associate Professor of Music

Carlos Guedes is a Portuguese composer, media artist, educator, and researcher, with a multifaceted activity whose creative work comprises several commissions of music for contemporary dance, theater, film and interactive installations, aside from traditional concert music. Carlos Guedes has composed music for several short and feature films, some of them with awards in international film festivals. He created the course “Designing sound for scene and screen” at NYUAD an elective for the programs in Film, Theater, and Music, that addresses the many aspects of sound design for film and theater. His latest creation “Jinn,” premiered at NYUAD’s Art Center on October 10, 2018, is a multimedia collaborative work combining live and pre-recorded electronic music, instrumental music, dance, film, and live motion capture in novel and engaging ways.

title: Creative Writing Intensive Program
text:
Creative Writing Intensive Program






July 6–10, 2026








Tell the stories only you can tell

At NYU Abu Dhabi’s Creative Writing Intensive, you will explore your voice, develop your ideas, and learn how to expand your craft as a writer. This selective, university-level program brings together motivated students for an immersive week of writing, feedback, and creative discovery.










Apply














Duration: 1 week | Commuter program | Grades 10–12






Unlock your potential as a writer at NYU Abu Dhabi

Join a small, ambitious cohort of students for an intensive week of creative exploration and intellectual growth. Through hands-on workshops and guided practice, you will develop the skills to write with intention, crafting compelling narratives, exploring new forms and innovative expression, and building confidence in your creative voice.

From the foundations of lyrical structure to the challenges of narrative arrangement and character development, you will engage with both the theory and practice of writing that moves people. Gain the analytical edge and expressive power to take your ideas further.

Whether you are an aspiring writer or simply curious about the craft of writing, this program will challenge and inspire you.










Program Snapshot

- Dates : July 6-10, 2026
- Duration : One week (five instructional days)
- Daily Instruction : Three hours per day (15 total hours)
- Location : NYU Abu Dhabi, Saadiyat Island Campus
- Format : Commuter program (no residential accommodation)
- Application Fee : AED 184 (non-refundable)
- Tuition : AED 6,000
- Combined Programs Option : AED, 10,000
- Application Deadline: June 19, 2026 
For more information, please contact: nyuad.highschoolprograms@nyu.edu .








View the Engineering and Innovation Program

Students may take the Creative Writing, and Engineering and Innovation programs concurrently.

A unique blend of academic rigor and hands-on creative practice in a dynamic university setting.

- Immersive learning : Experience university-level instruction in a focused, one-week format.
- Academic and practical approach : Engage with both the theory and practice of creative writing through interactive labs and innovative assignments.
- Small, selective cohort : Approximately 20 students for a personalized approach.
- Hands-on workshops : Develop original writing through daily interactive sessions.
- Interdisciplinary exploration : Explore the craft of writing across genres and media, including visual forms.
- Portfolio development : Produce original work to build your writing portfolio.
- No prior experience required : Open to motivated beginners and experienced writers alike.




















Who Should Apply?

This program is designed for students who:

- Are aged 15–18 (entering Grades 10–12)
- Have an interest in writing, literature, or communication
- Are motivated to experience university-level learning
- Are curious, creative, and open to new ideas
Students from the UAE are especially encouraged to apply.








The NYU Abu Dhabi Experience







Study at a globally recognized NYU campus.

At NYU Abu Dhabi, you will:

- Learn from NYU faculty, mentors, and trained teaching assistants.
- Engage with a diverse, international academic community.
- Experience a rigorous yet supportive learning environment.
This is a chance to experience university-level learning at a world-class institution.








Safety and Student Experience

The safety and well-being of all participants are top priority.

All participants are minors, and the program strictly adheres to NYU’s Minors Protection Policy and UAE regulatory standards.

- All staff, including faculty, teaching assistants, and program personnel, undergo security clearance and mandatory safeguarding training.
- Students are under full supervision at all times during program hours.
- A minimum 1-to-5 staff-to-student ratio ensures close oversight and support.
These measures reflect NYU Abu Dhabi’s commitment to providing a safe, structured, and secure learning environment.

title: Program Structure
text:
Program Structure





Over five intensive days, you will explore the art and craft of writing through a combination of workshops, discussions, and creative exercises.








What You Will Do

- Participate in daily interactive writing labs focused on various elements of literary development.
- Develop techniques in narrative arc and structure.
- Explore character psychology.
- Analyze lyrical patterns across different media.
- Engage in collaborative discussions and peer feedback.









Program Highlight

An experiential learning session at Louvre Abu Dhabi , where students will explore visual literacy and the relationship between art, narrative, and meaning.
































What You Will Gain

By the end of the program, you will:

- Distinguish tensions between form and content.
- Gain the awareness necessary to account for the reader.
- Analyze character psychology and apply it to your own writing.
- Recognize literary themes across different media and formats.
- Demonstrate your unique literary voice through original work.
- Apply key literary techniques in your writing.
- Develop confidence in expressing ideas clearly and creatively.
- Produce original written work for your portfolio.
- Gain exposure to university-level expectations and learning.














Faculty




















Gregory Pardlo

Program Head, Literature and Creative Writing; Professor of Literature and Creative Writing














Gregory Pardlo is a graduate of Rutgers University-Camden. He received an MFA from NYU as a New York Times Fellow in Poetry, an MFA in nonfiction from Columbia University as a Teaching Fellow, and an MPhil from the CUNY Graduate Center. Pardlo is the author of Digest, winner of the 2015 Pulitzer Prize for Poetry; Totem, winner of the 2007 American Poetry Review / Honickman Prize; and translator from the Danish of Niels Lyngsø’s, Pencil of Rays and Spiked Mace . Air Traffic , a memoir in essays, was published by Knopf in 2018. His most recent book, Spectral Evidence , was long listed for the 2024 National Book Award in poetry. His poems and essays have appeared in The New Yorker , Playboy , American Poetry Review , Boston Review , The Nation , The New York Times , Ploughshares , Tin House , and two editions of Best American Poetry , as well as many anthologies, including the Norton Anthology of Contemporary African American Poetry . He is the recipient of fellowships from the New York Public Library's Cullman Center, the Guggenheim Foundation, the New York Foundation for the Arts, and a fellowship for translation from the National Endowment for the Arts. He has received other fellowships from the Civitella Ranieri Foundation, MacDowell, the Lotos Club Foundation, and Cave Canem. Pardlo is Poetry Editor of Virginia Quarterly Review and advising editor for Callaloo , a journal of African diaspora arts and letters.







Contact

For more information, please contact: nyuad.highschoolprograms@nyu.edu .

text:
Engineering and Innovation: Robotics and Intelligent Systems Program






July 6-10, 2026








Build the future through robotics and innovation

At NYU Abu Dhabi’s Engineering and Innovation: Robotics and Intelligent Systems Program, you will explore how engineering, coding, and intelligent systems come together to solve real-world challenges. This selective, university-level program brings together motivated students for an immersive week of hands-on learning, experimentation, and innovation.










Apply














Duration: 1 week | Commuter program | Grades 10–12






Discover the world of robotics and intelligent systems at NYU Abu Dhabi

Join a small, ambitious cohort of students for an intensive week of engineering exploration and academic growth. Through interactive labs, collaborative problem solving, and hands-on experimentation, you will develop foundational skills in robotics while exploring how intelligent systems are shaping the future.

From engineering design and computational thinking to the real-world demands of robotics and innovation, you will engage with both the theory and practice of technology that impacts everyday life. Gain the analytical mindset, technical confidence, and creative problem-solving skills needed for the next generation of innovation.

Whether you are already interested in STEM or simply curious about how robotics impacts everyday life, this program will challenge and inspire you.










Program Snapshot

- Dates: July 6-10, 2026
- Duration: One week (five instructional days)
- Daily Instruction: Three hours per day (15 total hours)
- Location: NYU Abu Dhabi, Saadiyat Island Campus
- Format: Commuter program (no residential accommodation)
- Application Fee: AED 184 (non-refundable)
- Tuition: AED 6,000
- Combined Programs Option: AED, 10,000
- Application Deadline: June 19, 2026 
For more information, please contact: nyuad.highschoolprograms@nyu.edu .








View the Creative Writing Intensive Program

Students may take the Engineering and Innovation, and Creative Writing programs concurrently.



















Why This Program?

A unique blend of academic rigor and hands-on engineering practice in a dynamic university setting.

- Immersive learning: Experience university-level instruction in a focused, one-week format.
- Academic and practical approach: Engage with both the theory and practice of robotics, engineering, and intelligent systems through interactive sessions and innovative assignments.
- Small, selective cohort: Approximately 20 students for a personalized approach.
- Hands-on experience: Build and experiment with robotics systems through collaborative activities.
- Interdisciplinary exploration: Explore the intersection of robotics, coding, design, and intelligent systems.
- Project-based learning: Complete a project focused on AI and robotics to showcase your learning and technical development.
- No prior experience required: Open to motivated beginners and students with previous STEM experience alike.




















Who Should Apply?

Is this you? Join the next generation of innovators!

We’re looking for bold thinkers and future creators ready to dive into the world of high-tech discovery.

This is your next step if you:

- Are 15–18 years old (entering Grades 10–12) and ready for a challenge
- Interested in learning more about engineering, AI, robotics, coding, and cutting-edge innovation
- Crave a head start on university-level experience
- Possess a relentless curiosity and a drive to solve the world's toughest problems

Students from the UAE are especially encouraged to apply.








The NYU Abu Dhabi Experience







Study on a globally recognized NYU campus.

At NYU Abu Dhabi, you will:

- Learn from NYU faculty, mentors, and trained teaching assistants.
- Engage with a diverse, international academic community.
- Experience a rigorous yet supportive learning environment.
This is more than a summer program — it is a chance to experience university-level learning at a globally recognized institution.








Safety and Student Experience

The safety and well-being of all participants are top priority.

All participants are minors, and the program strictly adheres to NYU’s Minors Protection Policy and UAE regulatory standards.

- All staff, including faculty, teaching assistants, and program personnel, undergo security clearance and mandatory safeguarding training.
- Students are under full supervision at all times during program hours.
- A minimum 1-to-5 staff-to-student ratio ensures close oversight and support.
These measures reflect NYU Abu Dhabi’s commitment to providing a safe, structured, and secure learning environment.



Contact

For more information, please contact: nyuad.highschoolprograms@nyu.edu .

title: Program Structure
breadcrumbs: Engineering and Innovation: Robotics and Intelligent Systems Program
text:
Program Structure





Over five intensive days, you will explore robotics and intelligent systems through a combination of workshops, labs, and collaborative projects.








What You Will Do

- Participate in hands-on robotics labs and engineering activities.
- Explore robotics systems, coding concepts, and computational thinking.
- Develop engineering design and problem-solving techniques.
- Learn how intelligent systems are applied to real-world challenges.
- Work collaboratively on technical challenges and project development.
- Apply engineering concepts to practical scenarios.









Program Highlight

Students will complete a robotics-focused project that integrates the concepts explored throughout the week.
































What You Will Gain

By the end of the program, you will:

- Understand foundational engineering, AI, and robotics concepts.
- Develop problem-solving and computational thinking skills.
- Apply engineering design principles to hands-on challenges.
- Build confidence in technical collaboration and innovation.
- Complete a practical project for your portfolio.
- Gain exposure to university-level STEM learning.














Contact

For more information, please contact: nyuad.highschoolprograms@nyu.edu .

title: NYUAD PhD Pathways Program
text:
NYUAD PhD Pathways Program






Program Philosophy













A first of its kind in the UAE, NYUAD’s PhD Pathways Program aims to address the challenge of underrepresentation of Emirati PhDs and professors in higher education, through enhanced and early access to research experience, mentorship, skill acquisition, exploration of research careers, and graduate school preparation. The NYUAD PhD Pathway Program is currently open only to NYUAD students.
















I am really passionate about teaching students and guiding them towards making gradual discoveries about the social world.


About the Program

-





To be selected for this program, NYUAD'students must:

- Be a UAE citizen and a holder of the UAE family book.
- Have declared a major (summer before junior year).
- Have an excellent academic record indicative of potential for advanced study (min GPA: 3.5).
- Submit a completed application, including:
- A personal statement that indicates interest in pursuing doctoral education and commitment to participate fully in the program.

- A letter of recommendation from a faculty member.

- Signed program contract.

- Complete the entry interview successfully.


-





Selected fellows will:

- Conduct closely mentored research with a faculty member in an academic discipline of their choice.

- Participate in workshops to develop a wide range of meta-professional skills that will help them in academia or in the professional world, such as public speaking and presentation skills, resume/CV writing, time management, leadership, financial literacy, and negotiation and self-advocacy.

- Be advised on graduate school planning , including program selection, preparation for the GRE or other exams, support for application writing, education on funding opportunities, and negotiating an offer.
- Attend and present at conferences . Students will be encouraged to find at least one conference of their choice, and submit and present their research in order to gain real-world experience pertinent to successful PhD career paths.
- Take part in social activities , information sessions, periodic check-in meetings, social gatherings, and the official program completion ceremony


-





NYUAD PhD Pathway fellows are expected to adhere to the following guidelines and responsibilities:

- Engage in mentored research (35 hours per week) over the summer.
- Complete a one-credit Summer Directed Study Course.
- Complete weekly logs based on your progress with your mentor, individualized research, and graduate school preparation milestones.
- Complete the Mock Capstone Project Proposal using the options given. Be sure to detail the research problem, question(s), theme or issue to be addressed, and the significance, why the research is needed, and the broader implications of the proposed research.

- Complete program evaluations at the end of each summer.
- Attend all designated program workshops and events throughout the year.
- Be committed to the program.
To ensure a productive and successful experience for students, mentors, and the program staff, we expect students to be mindful of the following principles:

- Maintain good academic standing throughout your undergraduate degree at NYU Abu Dhabi.
- Proactively manage your own progress through the program.
- Communicate and work responsibly with your faculty mentors.
- Be committed to the philosophy of this program.
- Respond in a timely and responsible fashion to all communications sent regarding the program obligations, from any department.
- Inform the Pathways Program staff at the earliest if your personal circumstances or academic goals and plans change.

For further guidelines and detailed information, please refer to the student handbook (PDF).



-





The mentor’s role will be instrumental in shaping the research experience and future trajectory of our NYUAD PhD Pathway students. The program staff will provide support and ensure a rewarding research experience for all participants. Mentors will provide direction and guidance to help fellows refine their research interests and develop them into a substantial paper, project, or Capstone.








Faculty Mentors














- Tarek Abdoun
- Rana AlMutawa
- Wisam Alshaibi
- Laure Assaf













- Kevin Coffey
- Jemima Frimpong
- Alberto Gandolfi
- Gabriel Koehler-Derrick













- Nader Masmoudi
- Veda Narasimhan
- Nikos Nikiforakis
- Luca Maria Pesando










-





Students selected to be a part of the NYUAD PhD Pathway Program will receive funding support in the following formats:

- Summer stipend or research expenses. Please note that If you are enrolled in another summer research program, you will not be eligible for payment for both programs.
- GRE preparation and university application fees
- Research expenses, if needed and justified
- Funding to produce posters or other materials for final presentations
- Summer housing on campus, as long as students are expecting to conduct research on campus or prefer to live on campus during the summer rather than at home.



-





A complete application must include:

- Official transcripts
- Personal Statement (750 words)
- Your rationale for participating in the NYUAD PhD Pathway Program
- Your research interests
- Your current level of preparation to apply for PhD programs
- Your plans after graduation
- Why you want to pursue a PhD and where (if known)
- How this program will help in your PhD application journey

- One recommendation letter



























Recent Graduate Program Acceptances










Khalil Kashwani

Mentored by Professor Alberto Gandolfi, Khalil received an offer to join the NYUAD Global PhD Program starting in fall 2025, where he will pursue his postgraduate studies in Mathematics.








Rayan AlNaqbi

Mentored by Professor Tarek Abdoun, Rayan has received an offer to pursue her master’s studies in Geotechnical Engineering at UC Berkeley, starting in fall 2025.








Naser AlHumaidi

Mentored by Professor Nader Masmoudi, Naser received an offer from the NYUAD Global PhD Program to pursue advanced studies in Mechanical Engineering.
















Alya AlHbtari

Mentored by Dr. Veda Narasimhan, Alya was awarded the prestigious Rhodes Scholarship and will begin her studies at the University of Oxford. She will pursue an MSc in Global Governance and Diplomacy alongside a Master’s in Public Policy, with the aim of advancing the UAE’s foreign aid strategies through her academic and professional journey.








Ali Kashwani

Mentored by Professor Kevin Coffey, he received an offer from Boston College to pursue his master’s studies in philosophy, with plans to continue on to a PhD. His academic interests focus on the history and philosophy of science and epistemology.















When picking a PhD program, students should make sure that there are people at the department whose interests overlap.It is important to have a senior researcher around who can advise you on which topics of research are interesting and feasible within your chosen field of interest.


Look for a program where faculty research aligns with your passions, and make sure the advisor’s mentoring style suits your needs. Finding a collaborative and supportive environment is key for long-term success and personal growth.


Program Team and Contact Information

The NYUAD PhD Pathway team is available to provide clarification on the selection process, services offered, and general inquiries related to the program at nyuad.phdpathways@nyu.edu .


Fatma Abdulla

Senior Associate Vice Chancellor and Senior Vice Provost

Asma Alblooshi

Assistant Director, PhD Pathways Program

title: Sheikh Mohamed bin Zayed Scholars Program
breadcrumbs: Sheikh Mohamed bin Zayed Scholars Program
text:
Sheikh Mohamed bin Zayed Scholars Program





The Sheikh Mohamed bin Zayed Scholars Program offers a select cohort of talented university students access to specially designed courses, lectures, leadership experiences, networking, and graduate school counseling.

We admit scholars from among the most outstanding students at the three federal UAE universities: Higher Colleges of Technology, the United Arab Emirates University, and Zayed University.

The Scholars Program has been developed in close consultation with His Highness Sheikh Mohamed bin Zayed Al Nahyan, Her Highness Sheikha Mariam bint Mohamed bin Zayed Al Nahyan, UAE federal universities, and New York University Abu Dhabi.

New York University Abu Dhabi is grateful to His Highness Sheikh Mohamed bin Zayed Al Nahyan for his generous support and generosity.

























Program Goals

Academic and Professional Development

We offer an unparalleled and rigorous educational, cross-cultural, and leadership-development experience to outstanding university students in their third or fourth years of college study in the UAE.

Network

We provide access to NYU’s global research, educational, and leadership network, to foster greater awareness of international issues and challenges, and to develop in our Scholars the capacity to shape their future academic and professional goals and lead in government, industry, academia, and other fields.

Graduate School Advising

We prepare our exceptional Scholars for graduate and professional study at institutions of their choice.

title: Application and Selection Process
breadcrumbs: Sheikh Mohamed bin Zayed Scholars Program
text:
Application and Selection Process





The SMSP application and selection process includes several stages. Students submit an application through the online SMSP application system, and each participating university nominates candidates to be considered by the SMSP Selection Committee. Finalists are then invited to participate in Selection Days.



Application Deadline

Applications must be complete and submitted through the SMSP application system by March 1, 2027 .

For questions about the application process, please contact your university:


Zayed University

Email: SMSP@zu.ac.ae




United Arab Emirates University

Email: SMSP@uaeu.ac.ae

Higher Colleges of Technology

Email: hct-smsp@hct.ac.ae






Eligibility

To apply to SMSP, students must:

- Have completed at least four fall/spring semesters by the time the program begins in September. Students may apply during their fourth semester.
- Be enrolled at their home university when the program begins in September.
- Submit a complete application by the application deadline.
Only students nominated by their home university will be reviewed by the SMSP Selection Committee.








What We Look For

SMSP does not have a minimum required GPA or IELTS/TOEFL score. Candidates are expected to:

- Demonstrate intellectual curiosity and a strong record of accomplishment.
- Have excellent English language skills.
- Have strong interpersonal skills and be eager to contribute to the cohort.
- Demonstrate creativity or other talents.
- Show leadership potential.
- Be enterprising, adaptable, and willing to take on new experiences.







Selection Process








Application

Students submit a complete application through the SMSP application system by the application deadline.

University Nomination

Each participating university reviews its applications and nominates up to 20 students to move forward in the selection process. Nominations are submitted to SMSP by university representatives.

Finalists Chosen

The SMSP Selection Committee reviews the 60 nominated applications and selects approximately 36 finalists. Finalists are invited to attend Selection Days.

Selection Days

Finalists complete the final stage of the selection process over two separate days, including several interviews, a group exercise, and a writing exercise. The new cohort is announced in the summer.

Program Starts

The new cohort begins the program in September, with classes held approximately every other weekend throughout the academic year.








Application Requirements

Applicants must submit:

- Biographical Information
- Student/Parent Consent Form
- CV or resume
- Essays
- Academic project
- Video
- Official academic transcript
- Two faculty letters of recommendation
Applications must be complete by the application deadline. Incomplete applications will not be considered.
