title: Activities
text:
Activities












The Government and Public Policy research cluster supports a variety of activities, including conferences and workshops, a quarterly seminar series, and research funding for individual members.





















Activity Highlights










Seminar Series

Government and Public Policy sponsors a quarterly seminar series that hosts intellectual and scholarly leaders from across the social sciences. Past speakers include Margaret Levi and Michael Hechter.








Event Funding

The cluster actively supports conferences, workshops, and retreats, including the NYUAD Pademic Politics Workshop (April 2023), the Yonsei-NYUAD Joint Workshop on Domestic Politics and International Relations (May 2023), and many others.








Cluster Member Accomplishments

Cluster members have won numerous awards. Recent highlights include:

Elisabeth Anderson receiving the 2022 Outstanding Contribution to Political Sociology Award from the Political Sociology Section of the American Sociological Association and J. Andrew Harris receiving the 2022 Elinor Ostrom Award for the Best Article published in the Journal of Theoretical Politics awarded by the Formal Theory Section of the American Political Science Association.














Other Activity



Workshop on Intersection between Domestic Politics and International Relations

Organized by Sujeong Shim and J. Andy Harris (joint with Global Dynamics)

On May 18-19, 2023, NYUAD and Yonsei University hosted a workshop that brought together international relations and comparative politics scholars whose research addresses important political economy issues of our time, ranging from democratic backsliding and the rise of China to foreign aid and human rights.


NYUAD Pandemic Politics Conference

Organized by Joan Barcelo and Robert Kubinic

On April 4th, 2023, the Pandemic Politics Workshop convened approximately twelve researchers from the US, Europe, Central Asia, and the UAE. The workshop focused on presenting research aimed at understanding and modeling the impacts of the pandemic on governments and societies. The papers showcased a variety of methodologies, ranging from survey experiments to big data Twitter analysis and network modeling. A central theme of the conference was the challenges governments faced in responding to the evolving dynamics of the pandemic. The workshop emphasized the necessity for robust and comprehensive models of human behavior to predict and elucidate the potential effects of government policies during pandemics.


Seed Funding for Works in Progress

"Formation of Macroeconomic Expectations within Production Networks" Jordan Norris (NYUAD), Saten Kumar (AUT), Samreen Malik (NYUAD)

Firms are interconnected through market competition, input-output relationships, and collaborative ventures. However, the understanding of how macroeconomic information is transmitted across firms and the factors that influence this flow remains limited. To address this gap, a dataset has been developed that captures these linkages. The dataset comprises 2000 interconnected firms and includes critical details such as the number of suppliers, primary suppliers, share of input from the main supplier, number of customers, and primary customers. The next steps involve surveying and experimenting with firm managers, necessitating further enrichment of the dataset with additional pairs, currently underway.


Seed Funding for Works in Progress

"Out-Group Tax Compliance and Tax Morale: Evidence from Survey Experiments in Brazil and Turkey," Yusuf Magiya (NYUAD) and Giuliana Pardelli (NYUAD)

This project conducted a face-to-face survey experiment in Turkey to examine how outgroup tax evasion affects tax morale and evaluations of outgroups compared to ingroup tax evasion. Using a factorial survey design, participants were presented with vignettes depicting individuals varying in tax compliance status, access to public goods, economic status, and ethnic background. The findings revealed that exposure to tax evasion reduced overall tax morale and led to more negative evaluations of individuals involved in evasion. Importantly, outgroup tax evasion intensified negative evaluations of individuals to a greater extent than it affected tax morale, highlighting distinct impacts on outgroup perceptions in comparison to ingroup evaluations.

title: Publications
text:
Publications












Publications from Inequality cluster members showcase a wide-range of theoretical and empirical work from scholars across different programs in the social science division, reflecting the truly interdisciplinary nature of the study of inequality, as well as the power of cross-disciplinary collaborations.
















-

Recent Publications

Pesando, L. M. , and Abufhele, A. " Declining Quantity and Quality of Births in Chile Amidst the COVID-19 Pandemic ." Population and Development Review, Early View (2023).

Liu, F., Holme, P., Chiesa, M., Alshebli, B. , Rahwan, T . " Gender inequality and self-publication are common among academic editors ." Nat Hum Behav 7, 353–364 (2023).

Darity Jr, William A., Hamilton, D., L. Myers Jr, S., N. Price, G., & Xu, M. "Racial Differences in Time at Work Not Working." ILR Review 75, no. 3 (2022): 552-572.

title: Markets, Organizations and Decisions (MOD)
text:
Markets, Organizations and Decisions (MOD)












Mathematical modeling of human behavior and economic, social and political phenomena, with a special focus on markets, networks, organizations, and strategic decision making.

title: DRAFT - Undergraduate Education
text:
If you want to succeed on a global scale, you’ll need a university that meets you on your level. At NYU Abu Dhabi, exceptional students from six continents come together to solve today’s most pressing challenges. You’ll gain more than a global mindset — you’ll be prepared to change the world.







Our campus on Saadiyat Island brings together students and faculty from all over the world.

Here, students develop their academic foundations with a distinctly intercultural and interdisciplinary lens, preparing them to engage creatively with difference and grow their perspectives through global experience.









Apply to NYU Abu Dhabi































Majors and Minors

NYUAD students receive either a Bachelor of Arts (BA) or a Bachelor of Science (BS) degree, depending on their major.



























Core Curriculum

The Core prepares graduates to address major global challenges, including the pursuit of equality, justice, peace, health, sustainability, and a rich understanding of humanity.



























Undergraduate Research

At NYUAD, research is not limited to the senior year or advanced courses. Research is a fundamental mode of learning applicable at every level of study.

















Graduation Requirements for Undergraduates













NYUAD’s J-Term Courses

Immersive learning experiences engaging students deeply with the people and the places where they study.








Semester Abroad

Students can spend up to two semesters studying at NYU's 15 academic centers around the world.
















Community-based Learning

Students engage with organizations, communities, and professionals in the UAE and more than 25 countries.








Summer Research and Internships Abroad

Students work and learn alongside leading organizations, professionals, and researchers in communities around the world.




























What Makes NYU Abu Dhabi Unique?










100%

NYUAD students study abroad







15

NYU Global Academic Centers







45

J-Term classes abroad















Career Development

Support in choosing a major, gaining professional experience, developing a solid CV, meeting industry insiders, and applying to graduate school or global awards.








Visiting Students

NYU New York and NYU Shanghai students: Experience NYU Abu Dhabi as an undergraduate student or researcher.








Electives

Undergraduate electives at NYU Abu Dhabi include pre-professional and language courses.
















Apply to NYU Abu Dhabi







Financial Aid and Scholarships







Life on Campus

Christopher Luwanga's journey to becoming a space entrepreneur embodies the education dream, and the courage to reach for the stars.

title: Core Curriculum
text:
Core Curriculum






Expanding Horizons

NYU Abu Dhabi’s Core Curriculum forms the heart of our mission to provide an international student body with an outstanding, expansive education.

The Core draws on the diversity and cultural wealth of the world’s traditions and spans the content and methodologies of 21st-century disciplines across the Arts and Humanities, Engineering, Science, and Social Science. It offers Core Competencies that will help graduates address major global challenges, including the pursuit of equality, justice, peace, health, sustainability, and a rich understanding of humanity.

It fosters modes of thinking and habits of mind central to well-rounded intellectual development and to global citizenship and leadership. The Core is our mission, manifested.








Core Structure

The NYUAD Core consists of two Core Colloquia, each of which addresses a significant global challenge from multidisciplinary perspectives, and four Core Competency Courses, one each in the four categories.



Take the Core Abroad

Students can fulfil Core requirements at many of NYU's global sites.



















Confronting Global Challenges

Taught by faculty from all divisions, Core Colloquia aim to offer multidisciplinary, global perspectives and substantively engage two or more of the Core Competencies. These seminars help nurture civic awareness fundamental to global citizenship and leadership by developing your abilities to grapple with the complex conceptual and ethical dimensions of global issues, to communicate respectfully across cultural difference, and to devise problem-solving strategies. They remind us that your individual academic experiences contribute to our collective efforts to make NYUAD a new model of higher education for a global world.

The cooperation needed to address the world’s most pressing challenges depends upon a rich understanding of humanity itself, a sense of how societies and individuals have developed in relation to one another and to other species, to the environment, to technologies, and to ideas — both sacred and secular — about the universe. When it comes to tackling such challenges, Core Colloquia may raise questions to which there are no easy answers. But learning to pose good questions is itself an important skill, as is learning to approach them from multiple points of reference. Rather than simply taking the idea of a “global perspective” as a given, these courses require us to ask what it means to think about such enduring and urgent challenges across cultures, borders, disciplines, languages, and time.











Four Core Competencies

- Arts, Design, and Technology
- Cultural Exploration and Analysis
- Data and Discovery
- Structures of Thought and Society
No single course can provide competency in a subject or mode of thought, but the Core offers opportunities to begin to develop competencies in key areas that will be fundamental to your education here at NYUAD and throughout the rest of your lives. The Core Competencies represent a well-rounded approach to inquiry, to habits of mind, and to modes of scholarly and creative practice.

With the full range of academic disciplines as starting points, these courses give every student some experience with thinking critically and contextually about culture, social institutions, ideas, and the natural world, as well as experience in problem- solving, design, and other creative work. These courses, which may also be taken as general electives, will provide not only a broad foundation for your undergraduate studies, but also an opportunity to explore subjects you may never have encountered otherwise with faculty members from a range of disciplines.







Their guidance and insights might offer you new perspectives on your chosen field of study or open up new vistas on the vast storehouse of human knowledge, experience, and expression. Most importantly, Core Competency courses should offer ways of thinking with which you can approach the world around you and should demonstrate the relevance of a range of disciplinary thinking to life beyond the classroom.

title: Community-based Global Learning
text:
Community-based Global Learning






Learning in, with, and from communities.

Community-based global learning is a core pillar of NYU Abu Dhabi's liberal arts mission. Over 300 NYUAD courses have specially designed fieldwork that allows students to engage directly with organizations, communities, and professionals in the UAE and more than 25 countries.

Faculty encourage students to approach these encounters with the same intellectual rigor as any lecture or assigned reading. From boardroom meetings in Dubai International Financial Center (DIFC) to the shores of Belize, each experience functions as a primary academic text: to be observed, analyzed, and brought into critical dialogue with the course. Students learn not simply by observing communities, but by listening, participating, and understanding issues in their local context.










Building Homes in Nepal







Meditating in Thailand







Archaeological Dig in Abu Dhabi













Building Responsible Citizens

Across four years, Community-based Global Learning builds something that cannot be taught from a textbook alone: the capacity to act with ethical intelligence as a responsible citizen and leader in their communities. In an age of artificial intelligence, these carefully curated, context-based experiences are what make an NYU Abu Dhabi education distinctive.







Community-based global learning is practiced across disciplines throughout the academic year, bringing community partners into the classroom as co-educators and taking students into the field as researchers.








Field Visits in the UAE



Empathy

Students in the J-Term class “Empathy” with NYU Professor Bryan Waterman visited Fiker Institute, a global think tank founded by Dubai Abulhoul Alfalasi, Class of 2017.

Practising Politics and Government in the Age of Disruption

NYU Abu Dhabi students visit the CNN Abu Dhabi studio with their J-Term professor, David Cameron, former Prime Minister of the United Kingdom (eighth from the left), during the course he taught on “Practising Politics and Government in the Age of Disruption.”

Maritimity and Global Societies

During the J-Term course “Maritimity and Global Societies,” students explored the fundamentals of maritime archaeology through hands-on training in the campus swimming pool.

Louvre Abu Dhabi

The Louvre Abu Dhabi, our neighbor on Saadiyat Island, is among the most frequent destinations for class visits and workshops at NYUAD.






Local Partners







NYU Abu Dhabi approaches its partnerships with local communities and organizations as relationships of mutual exchange. The University brings its academic knowledge and resources to every engagement and is equally committed to learning from the expertise and lived insight of the communities it works with.

Over the last decade, NYUAD students have engaged with over 200 local organizations from cultural institutions and research labs to humanitarian agencies and grassroots initiatives. These partnerships ground their learning in relationships, responsibility, and social impact.







Follow Us


Study Away | Visiting Students | Community-based Learning

title: J-Term
text:
J-Term





NYUAD’s J-Term courses are designed as two-week, intensive, and highly immersive learning experiences during January. They intensify student focus, offer site-specific fieldwork, and engage students deeply with the people and the places where they study.

Students focus exclusively on one subject while learning directly from the people, communities, environments, and institutions around them in over 25 countries. By immersing themselves in a place and a central question that location can uniquely help answer, they discover connections that are difficult to make from a distance.

The result can transform how students understand a subject, the world around it, and ultimately themselves.



An NYUAD student carving into wood for their J-Term course: "Maritimity and Global Societies: Arabian Seafarers and the Making of the Modern World






Fulfill Core Curriculum Requirements

All J-Term courses count in the NYUAD undergraduate curriculum within the Core Program as “J-Term Core Field Colloquia.” Students must take two J-Term Core Field Colloquia over four years, one course in Abu Dhabi and one course abroad.








Questions of the Human Experience

Each J-Term course centers on a significant, hard-to-answer, timely, and timeless question that the faculty and students explore together through multiple disciplinary and cultural lenses.













What can national dress reveal about identity, belonging, and power?

Khulood Alawadi, "Dressing the Nation," held in Abu Dhabi












How can arts and culture drive transformation and healing in post-conflict societies?

Phloeun Prim, "Arts for Transformation," held in Cambodia












How and why does childhood unfold so differently across societies?

Luca Pesando, "Unequal Childhoods," held in Florence

















A Truly Global Experience

Every NYUAD student takes one J-Term course abroad.








Financial Aid

J-Term courses abroad are fully funded for all students and will not affect a student's financial aid.














During J-Term, the World Is Your Classroom

J-Term courses invite students to look up from their books to engage directly with the cities, people, and questions their classes explore.

Courses taught in Abu Dhabi use the UAE as a “real-world text.” Courses taught abroad are based in NYU’s distinctive Global Network of program sites , or fully taught in countries outside of the Global Network — such as Bangladesh, Cambodia, Greece, India, Jordan, Kenya, Morocco, Nepal, Rwanda, and South Africa.



Where Science Meets the Canvas

J-Term 2026: Learning Beyond the Classroom, Grounded in the World

J-Term courses bridged technology, sustainability, and inclusivity across the globe.

Starting 2025 with Energizing J-Term Courses

With 70 courses offered, students were exposed to a range of global topics with field trips to get into the heart of the matter.

My passion for education and instructional game design was sparked during my introduction to the Interactive Media (IM) program and the MakerSpace.

J-Term 2024: Bringing Lessons Back Home

As J-term students return from across the globe, they bring back with them lessons that are uniquely an NYUAD experience inspired by the very core of






World-renowned Faculty







Courses are taught by scholars, writers, artists, journalists, and policy analysts, who teach only during the J-Term, as well as distinguished professors from NYUAD, NYU New York, and other leading universities.

Although the J-Term is short, the intensity of shared experience between professors and students tends to foster an unusually strong bond that lasts long after J-Term ends.


































J-Term Around the World



Documenting the Environmental Crisis

Students in “Documenting the Environmental Crisis,” Film and New Media Professor Surabi Sharma’s J-Term class, listen intently during a walking tour of Sambhavna Trust Hospital in Bhopal, India.

Transnational Cities, Abu Dhabi, Dubai, Paris

Professor Davide Ponzini took students in his course “Transnational Cities, Abu Dhabi, Dubai, Paris” for a walking tour of Dubai Expo City.

Ribbons of Blue: Urbanization on the Coastal Fringe

As part of their coursework for “Ribbons of Blue: Urbanization on the Coastal Fringe,” students had to collect water samples from streams in Middlesex, Belize.

The Science of Colors

Linking physics and chemistry to pigments found in food, students studied how molecular structure determines color in a tie-dye session as part of President Emeritus Andrew Hamilton's J-Term course “The Science of Colors.”

Democracy in Britain: Crisis and Change in Modern Politics

Lord Stewart Wood took students in his course “Democracy in Britain: Crisis and Change in Modern Politics” to the House of Commons in London to watch local politicians debate live.

Knowledge Mobilization: Bridging Science, Policy, and Practice in Zambia

Students engaged with loyal youth at Tiko, a non-profit organization in Zambia, as part of Professor Janet Njelesani’s course “Knowledge Mobilization: Bridging Science, Policy, and Practice in Zambia.”

Disability and Development

Students from NYU Abu Dhabi and the University of Zimbabwe, in Pamuzinda, Zimbabwe, for the J-Term course “Disability and Development.”

The city of Istanbul was a living syllabus, and its ferries, mosques, alleyways, restaurants, and musicians all contributed to the course in ways no reading could.


This experience taught me that education is deeply connected to culture, society, and opportunity. Studying fairness in university applications while in India allowed me to see how structural factors actually affect access to education. The contrast between what seemed fair in theory and what I observed in practice made me more aware of how inequality shapes people's lives.


This was one of the most impactful courses I’ve taken at NYUAD. It made me think, reflect, and critique so many decisions we make as individuals, as communities, and on a global scale. I’m leaving this course with a deeper awareness as a computer science student, and with a more thoughtful understanding of how I engage with technology and the world around me.

sections.title: J-Term
sections.text:
J-Term





NYUAD’s J-Term courses are designed as two-week, intensive, and highly immersive learning experiences during January. They intensify student focus, offer site-specific fieldwork, and engage students deeply with the people and the places where they study.

Students focus exclusively on one subject while learning directly from the people, communities, environments, and institutions around them in over 25 countries. By immersing themselves in a place and a central question that location can uniquely help answer, they discover connections that are difficult to make from a distance.

The result can transform how students understand a subject, the world around it, and ultimately themselves.



An NYUAD student carving into wood for their J-Term course: "Maritimity and Global Societies: Arabian Seafarers and the Making of the Modern World

title: Summer Research and Internships Abroad
text:
Summer Research and Internships Abroad






Putting academic and career interests into practice.







At NYU Abu Dhabi, students can participate in full-time funded internships and undergraduate research in the UAE and abroad. This experiential learning allows students to work and learn alongside leading organizations, professionals, and researchers in communities around the world.

Through hands-on experience, students deepen their academic interests, develop professional skills and networks, and learn how to collaborate effectively across cultures and contexts — experiences that can open new possibilities for careers and graduate study.








Typically, 500+ students participate in summer research and internships across 60 countries.










A researcher in NYUAD's Center for Technology, Economics, and Development (CTED) helps a farmer register on the CTED blockchain app to trade her commodities.










Whether it's working with Professor of Economics Yaw Nyarko and his team at the Center for Technology and Economic Development (CTED) in a town in Ghana surveying local farmers, or traveling to the Gran Sasso National Laboratory in Italy to do research on dark matter, NYUAD students extend their learning beyond the classroom during the summer.

By working directly with organizations and professionals, students develop critical skills and cross-cultural understanding, enhancing both their personal and academic growth with professional experience.





















Summer Research







Students conduct research both at NYUAD and other universities and centers around the world under the supervision of faculty. NYUAD provides competitive grants covering travel, room and board for up to eight weeks to support these experiences.



Explore Summer Research































Summer Internships







Through summer internships, students gain real-world experience while immersing themselves in diverse cultural settings. These internships provide hands-on learning alongside professionals in fields, such as business, non-profit organizations, arts, and technology.



Explore Summer Internships

Minors in the NYU Global Network

Where comparable NYUAD minors do not already exist, NYUAD students may be able to complete one of the many academic minors offered elsewhere in the NYU global network. Students interested in completing one of these minors would ordinarily take most or all of the required courses in New York, Shanghai, and/or one of the other global sites. However, appropriate NYUAD courses may also be used toward completion of an NYU minor. Directed Study courses generally cannot be used to meet global network minor requirements. For a list of NYU contacts for minors in New York, please visit the Cross-School Minor Contacts page .

sections.text: Where comparable NYUAD minors do not already exist, NYUAD students may be able to complete one of the many academic minors offered elsewhere in the NYU global network. Students interested in completing one of these minors would ordinarily take most or all of the required courses in New York, Shanghai, and/or one of the other global sites. However, appropriate NYUAD courses may also be used toward completion of an NYU minor. Directed Study courses generally cannot be used to meet global network minor requirements. For a list of NYU contacts for minors in New York, please visit the Cross-School Minor Contacts page .

title: Career Development
text:
Career Development





The Career Development Center (CDC) plays an integral role in the undergraduate experience at NYU Abu Dhabi, providing guidance, advising, programs, and resources to students during their time at NYUAD, and beyond.

Students are supported in an iterative process of discovering and refining their strengths, choosing a major, and gaining professional experience — from developing a solid CV, to meeting industry insiders, to applying to graduate school or global awards.



Mission and Vision

Mission: To empower undergraduate and graduate students with the skills, knowledge, experiences, and connections to be successful in their futures.



Vision: Every student graduates equipped to build the future they want.























Video: The Career Development Center helps students find their path.








Invested in the Journey

It's all about the process. We’re building skills for a lifetime of learning and growing.










Advising

Individualized, tailored advise helps students explore their interests, clarify their goals, and strategize for success.








Mentorship

Professionals in the NYUAD community give students an understanding and insight into real-world challenges.








Events and Programs

Students explore different industries, learn about options, and network with potential employers, right here on campus.














Finding the Right Path

Students supported in navigating and evaluating their next step — whether it's working, studying, or another adventure.










Jobs and Internships

The CDC help students find internships, part-time jobs, and student organizations so they can gain professional experience before graduation.








Graduate Study

Is graduate school the right next step? Advisors help students decide if it's worth the investment.








Global Awards

The CDC works closely with students to identify global awards competitions that help them achieve their post-graduate goals.














Where Do NYUAD Students Go?










Graduate Outcomes

NYUAD graduates have a global vision, sprawling to more than 90 countries around the world.








Internship Map

Discover where NYUAD students have worked via our interactive global internship map.








Life Beyond Saadiyat

The Class of 2024 launch from NYU Abu Dhabi with a bold willingness to experiment, blending technical expertise with human-centered approaches, and bringing fresh perspectives to the industries they now enter.

title: Undergraduate Research
text:
Undergraduate Research





Research is an important part of education at NYU Abu Dhabi and research opportunities are threaded throughout the undergraduate program across all four academic divisions.

Students become active investigators and experience the challenge, creativity, and rigor involved in grappling with unanswered questions, proposing answers, considering problems from new angles, and developing data.

At NYUAD, research is not limited to the senior year and to advanced courses. We understand research as a fundamental mode of learning that is applicable at every level of study. The required courses in most majors consider research methods and clarify the distinctive approaches of the disciplines. The Capstone Project required in the students' senior year is a research-intensive experience.



It is deeply fascinating to learn how big datasets are constructed from scratch... I now understand the importance of questioning and acknowledging details as well as biases in a dataset before using it for research.







Grants

NYUAD offers the following competitive grants:

- Grants to support students who have secured non-credit summer research positions, under the direction of a faculty supervisor; and
- Conference grants to support students who have been selected to present their research at local and international academic conferences.







Featured Research




































NYUAD and the XENON Dark Matter Program

NYUAD undergraduates have the opportunity to engage in fantastic summer research projects that take them around the world. Several students traveled to Gran Sasso National Laboratory in Italy to participate in the effort to understand dark matter, that mysterious substance that theoretically accounts for more than 80 percent of the total mass of the universe.















News










Starting a Conversation on Culture and Sustainability

A research project promoting sustainable transportation includes an abaya design that allows users to comfortably ride a bicycle.








Building Web-Based Psychology Experiments

NYU Abu Dhabi’s Post-graduation Practical Training Program allows seniors to work on faculty research projects after graduation.








When Curiosity Did Not Kill the Cat

A child’s curiosity on why the feather grass awn swirls and un-swirls throughout the day became a research publication.














Undergraduate Research Reports

title: Visiting Students
text:
Visiting Students












Every semester, NYU Abu Dhabi is home to visiting students from NYU in New York and NYU Shanghai. As one of NYU’s three degree-granting campuses, NYUAD provides access to over 600 courses across 26 majors ranging from engineering and social sciences to the sciences , and arts and humanities .





























Video: From TeamLabs to desert safaris, see how visiting students kicked off fall 2025 at NYUAD.

Life on Campus






























Video: A day in the life at NYU Abu Dhabi.












On campus, your average day can take you from a cutting-edge research laboratory or engineering design studio to an experimental black box theater or woodworking shop. In the city, you can spend time taking a stroll across fish and vegetable souqs, exploring the city’s emerging art scene, or drinking Karak chai in a small, corner shop on Hamdan Street.

If you choose to study abroad at NYU Abu Dhabi, you will become a part of a very diverse and tight-knit campus community. We can’t wait to welcome you to our home!

title: Semester Abroad
text:
Semester Abroad





NYUAD students come from the UAE and all over the world to study together in Abu Dhabi. Depending on their major, students can spend up to two semesters studying at NYU's 15 academic centers around the world.

Study Abroad as Part of the Degree

Whether in Paris, New York, Sydney, or elsewhere in NYU’s global network, students continue making progress toward their NYUAD degree while immersing themselves deeply in the study of a new language, culture, history, and host community.

Financial Aid

Student financial aid is fully applicable to the cost of the study abroad semesters.















Ramadan at NYU Abu Dhabi

Arab-American visiting student Aya Berri is navigating her first Ramadan in Abu Dhabi, in a community that fasts and prays together.

Academic Variety and Professional Growth

Bismark Buernortey Buer, Class of 2026 shares his study abroad story at NYU Tulsa.

Stepping Outside My Comfort Zone

Stepping outside my comfort zone taught me how much I can learn and who I can become when I let unfamiliar places, languages, and people shape me.

Growth Happens Quietly

Paris taught me that growth happens quietly.

A Formative Experience

My study away semester not only showed me the career path that I wanted to take, but that helped me grow into the person I've always dreamed of being.








More Student Stories

























Global Support System

NYUAD study away programs are coordinated by the Office of Global Education and Outreach, which supports students before, during, and after their experiences abroad to maximize local engagement, intercultural learning, promote safety and health, and help students contribute as responsible global citizens in the communities they join — wherever they are in the world.

title: Climate Leadership Program
text:
Climate Leadership Program

Climate Leadership Program












Sustainability Businesses Are Rapidly Evolving in Other Regions through Cultural and Technological Innovations








Industries in the GCC need professionals that can keep up with the pace of change.

The Climate Leadership Program at NYU Abu Dhabi is a specialized, tailored program designed for businesses in the region and is aimed at leveraging sustainability and climate change mitigation as core drivers for future growth and success in an era of rapid transformation.

Led by a team of the brightest sustainability experts from academia and industry, the program delivers unique insights, aligning with sector-specific experiences and cutting-edge research. Participants can select industry-specific subjects and gain revolutionary insights, driving toward a sustainable future and its economic opportunities.









Dates

- April 15-17, 2024 : Three-day foundation module
- May 2-3, 2024 : Two-day sector expert module 

Download brochure to learn more













Register Your Interest




















* Indicates a required field.


Having difficulty with this form? Please let us know .



























The program consists of a three-day foundation module followed by a two-day sector expert module, delving into sustainability, climate change, and strategic opportunities for climate leadership. Geared toward C-suite and Senior Executives involved in sustainability strategies, the program is designed for medium to large organizations operating in the UAE and the Middle East. It emphasizes real-world industry innovations, offers unparalleled access to our stimulating learning environment alongside transformative insights, and equips participants to identify climate change mitigation opportunities.

"This program is an outstanding chance to help fast-track businesses into the fantastic world of the latest sustainability opportunities. These exciting prospects for new growth and innovation are on the horizon, and NYUAD is committed to actively helping organizations and individuals benefit."

-- Harald Freissmuth, Program Director

The program aims to prepare the next generation of leaders to create value beyond traditional business frameworks, fostering confidence in addressing climate change challenges and creating sustainable business strategies. Through immersive learning experiences and innovative technology, the program ensures actionable real-world approaches for organizational climate change mitigation mandates — ensuring your leaders remain at the forefront of innovation.

As the global landscape evolves, so too should sustainable business leadership. The path to tomorrow starts here.
















Faculty

-











Harald Freissmuth, Executive Facilitator: Industry Expert, NYUAD

Harald has over 20 years of experience in the sustainability technology sector and international energy industry. He has served in various leadership roles, including C-level, senior executive, and board positions, with public corporations, private equity firms, and family-owned businesses.

Harald has gained a deep understanding of transformational key drivers in various industries throughout his career.

He possesses extensive expertise in sustainability technologies, including ESG strategies, carbon markets, technology assessment, and R&D. He is well-versed in driving the acceleration of new technologies to reach commercial readiness levels while also developing comprehensive and integrated business models.

He is a valuable resource to impact sustainability positively with his proficiency in both technical and commercial aspects of sustainable technologies.

Harald is passionate about bringing to market the latest innovative sustainability technologies and developing related new sustainable business models.

He is a corporate sustainability advisor for multiple industries, a sustainability think-tank founder, and develops sustainability strategies and methodologies, including executive management support.

Harald received a PhD in Technology and Economics from École Nationale Supérieure des Mines de Paris in France, a BSc and MSc in Petroleum Engineering and Business Administration from MUL University Leoben Austria and a degree in automobile engineering from Technical College Moedling in Austria.

He lived and worked in Asia, Asia-Pacific, Caspian, India, Europe, and the Middle East.
















-











Executive Director, Transition Investment Lab, NYUAD

Bernardo Bortolotti is Executive Director of the Transition Investment Lab at NYUAD, professor in economics at the University of Turin, Italy, and Director of the Sovereign Investment Lab at Bocconi University in Milan. His research focuses on the complex relationships between state and markets, with special emphasis on state ownership of firms, regulation, corporate finance, and corporate governance.

He is one of the leading international experts in privatization, state-assets management and divestiture, and sovereign wealth funds. His work appeared in major academic economics and finance journals, and he has published two books with Oxford University Press. He has been Executive Director of Fondazione Eni Enrico Mattei.

He has advised the World Bank, the Initiative for Policy Dialogue, the Italian Ministry of the Economy as secretary of the Global Advisory Committee on Privatization, the Italian Audit Office, listed firms and public and private financial institutions. He received his PhD in economics from the Université Catholique de Louvain.

title: DRAFT - Executive and Professional Education
text:
DRAFT - Executive and Professional Education

DRAFT - Executive and Professional Education






NYU Abu Dhabi Executive Education – Driving Innovation Across Borders and Industries













Designed for professionals and organizations at every stage of development, our programs combine academic expertise with practical application to build skills, strengthen leadership, and create lasting impact.









Register Your Interest

























Partnering for Impact

NYU Abu Dhabi Executive Education designs and delivers tailored learning experiences aligned with your organization's strategic priorities and workforce development goals, through a meaningful and collaborative partnership.

Drawing on NYU Abu Dhabi’s world-class faculty, interdisciplinary expertise, and global perspective, we are committed to developing impactful programs that strengthen leadership, drive innovation, and support organizational excellence.








Access Expertise Across NYU

Based at NYU Abu Dhabi, our programs draw on faculty and expertise from across NYU, bringing together interdisciplinary perspectives and global expertise to address individual and organizational learning needs.










Explore Solutions for Organizations

Bespoke learning and development programs designed around strategic priorities.


























Our Approach

Built upon four core pillars, NYU Abu Dhabi’s programs are structured to cultivate agile learning and facilitate practical, real-world application.














User-centered Design

NYU Abu Dhabi tailors every component of your program to solve the organizational challenges your teams face today. We build on the expertise and institutional knowledge participants already hold, and we deliver programs that strengthen capabilities on the job and improve business performance measurably.













Cohesive and Adaptive

The program operates as a continuous, connected ecosystem rather than a series of isolated sessions. Preparatory assignments and activities between modules weave your team's use cases into the curriculum, so the design adapts as your organizational needs evolve.





















Applied and Reflective Learning

We balance a comfortable learning environment with rigorous challenges that deliver results. Our scenario exercises, curated to meet your organization’s goals, invite collaboration among peers and structured daily reflection. Writing, debriefing, and processing each day’s lessons convert new information into lasting habits and strengthen how participants lead.













At the Intersection of Industry and Academics

NYU Abu Dhabi Executive Education gives participants a competitive edge by connecting insights across diverse fields of study. Our programs draw on the humanities, social sciences, management, technology, philosophy, and sustainability, so you build the perspective to lead confidently in a complex global landscape, grounded in real world application and industry practice.

















Executive Education Programs

Explore sample programs and workshops offered by NYU Abu Dhabi Executive Education.








Participating Faculty

Meet our world-renowned faculty participating in NYU Abu Dhabi's Executive Education programs.








Research Centers

Discover the NYU Abu Dhabi research centers driving innovative solutions to global challenges.

title: Research Centers
text:
Research Centers





Discover the NYU Abu Dhabi research centers driving solutions to global challenges and informing our Executive Education programs.










Center for Behavioral Institutional Design (C-BID)

A globally recognized research hub that explores in depth the origins of human behavioral diversity, undertakes the development of empirically informed theories of human behavior, leads their application to public policy, and builds capacity in behavioral social science in the public and private sectors.








Center for Interdisciplinary Data Science and Artificial Intelligence

A cross‑disciplinary hub where mathematicians, computer scientists, engineers, and social scientists join forces to push the boundaries of data‑driven discovery.  








Center for Cyber Security

A world-class cyber security center partnering with key local universities, industry, and government agencies to facilitate cyber security research, education, and practice in the UAE and GCC region.
















Fubon Center for Technology, Business, and Innovation

The Fubon Center’s mission is to foster relationships between scholars and changemakers in academia, industry, and government and enhance our constituents’ access to the resources they need to contribute meaningfully to scholarship and practice.








Center for Sustainable Business

The NYU Stern Center for Sustainable Business (CSB) aims to unleash the transformative potential of business to solve societal challenges at speed and scale. CSB's unique applied research into the Return on Sustainability Investment™ is helping companies identify and invest in sustainability-linked value creation.








Center for the Future of Management

Fosters cutting-edge research on major shifts in the global business landscape, and the challenges and opportunities they present for business leaders, strategists, and managers. The center is comprised of a set of initiatives, each focused on understanding a distinct shift in the business environment and the associated dynamics, challenges, and opportunities.
















Volatility and Risk Institute

An interdisciplinary center for research and analysis of financial and nonfinancial risks. It serves as a designated hub to support risk-related research and collaboration among scholars, practitioners, and policymakers. It supports, promotes, and facilitates risk analysis, assessment, and measurement.

title: Executive Education
text:
Executive Education

Executive Education






The Office of Executive Education designs, develops, and delivers customized and open enrollment programs to meet the needs of organizations and executives.













NYU Abu Dhabi’s Office of Executive Education is uniquely positioned to support the development efforts that organizations need to meet these challenges. Founded on the principle that executive development needs to be collaborative, relevant, and measurable, the OEE’s purpose is to design a new and more relevant approach to executive development that is fit for the challenges and business environment of the 21st century.









Request more information

























For Organizations

Global organizations today face complex issues that can’t be solved by generic solutions. We challenge, inspire, and prepare your leaders to take on complex issues, implement your company's vision, and develop the tools to be successful change agents.



See details



















For Individuals

Our open-enrollment Executive Programs are designed for executives to retool, advance, and expand skills and knowledge.



See details





















Areas of Expertise

Our experts design course content frameworks, work with organizations to establish course schedules, identify the best instructors to facilitate the programs, provide logistical support for program execution, and ensure quality assurance through post-program assessment and evaluation.








Global Network

NYU’s global reach enables our faculty to have deep international experience. As a result, our programs empower professionals to excel both locally and globally.














Our Impact




















The OEE is committed to value creation for people and organizations. We achieve transformational results by working in partnership with organizations to co-create bespoke, future-focused learning designs that empower people, develop leaders, and enhance the strengths of businesses.










See details


























Value Creation Empower your employees through online learning




















Our digital learning solutions are fully customized to meet the needs of your organization and designed to help you thrive in a changing world.



Learn more

title: Executive Education for Organizations
text:
Executive Education for Organizations






We challenge, inspire, and prepare your leaders to take on complex issues, implement your company's vision, and develop the tools to be successful change agents.








Global Network with a Global Reach













NYU Abu Dhabi, located at a new crossroads of the world, enriched by the intellectual vitality and research opportunities of a new world-class research institute, and benefiting from an active connection to NYU New York and other NYU global sites, provides the finest educational opportunity in the world for professional development.

Our world is witnessing drastic change, faster than ever. In a borderless business world, organizations must continuously adapt and evolve within their changing markets. Constant change requires the ability to adapt, lead, and maintain a vision based on common values and desired results. Leading diverse teams and creating agile organizations is yet another challenge.



Request more information


















NYU Abu Dhabi’s Office of Executive Education (OEE) is uniquely positioned to support the development efforts that organizations need to meet these challenges. Founded on the principle that executive development needs to be collaborative, relevant, and measurable, The OEE designs a new and more relevant approach to executive development that is fit for the challenges and business environment of the 21st century.

We support regional objectives of the UAE National Charter 2021, Abu Dhabi Economic Vision 2030, and Saudi Vision 2030, with transformational programs that focus on executive development in areas such as leadership, digital transformation, operational excellence, economics, innovation and intrapreneurship, global policy-making, culture and the arts, healthcare, and education, among others.

The OEE is committed to value creation for people and organizations. We achieve transformational results by working in partnership with organizations to co-create bespoke, future-focused learning designs that empower people, develop leaders, and enhance the strengths of businesses.

Our custom executive education programs target organizations' specific business needs and build rock-solid alignment around their strategic goals.

A custom program with NYUAD is a transformational learning journey that delivers meaningful and enduring change — from within. Together, we open your organization to breakthrough thinking and empower your people to navigate volatility and uncertainty to deliver the competitive advantage and sustainable growth you need to thrive — today and tomorrow.














Professional Achievement







Participants successfully completing NYU Abu Dhabi programs receive a Certificate of Professional Achievement. Professional development programs are accredited for recognition by the Emirates National Qualifications Authority or the UAE Commission on Academic Accreditation, as appropriate.





















Our Approach, Our Impact

Focused on Business Results













The Office of Executive Education designs, develops, and delivers customized and open enrollment programs to meet the needs of organizations and executives.

Our work begins with a blank canvas, and through real collaboration, we gain an in-depth understanding of your business’s learning needs and strategic goals.







We partner with your organization throughout the entire process of design and delivery. Our work begins with understanding, empathizing with, and challenging your assumptions, vision, and objectives through needs assessment interviews with key stakeholders and a review of organizational challenges and competencies.




















We work closely to fine-tune our understanding of your organization, culture, challenges, and opportunities, and to ensure the curriculum meets your objectives.










How We Work With You












DISCOVER













DESIGN













DELIVER




























Transformational Learning Experiences







NYUAD Office of Executive Education specializes in creating highly customized, results-oriented programs that address proprietary challenges. We ensure that each custom program is tailored to the organization's and participants' desired outcomes and includes business-driven, action-learning initiatives.







Our programs enable leaders to act upon their new perspectives and establish business cultures that drive your organization’s growth.








Our Programs Stand on Key Pillars






























Bespoke Assets

Each program is tailored to address specific challenges. Learning methodologies, technology, and our experts are shaped by the organization’s needs.








Cultural Awareness

Our custom programs have a global perspective with local resonance, integrating key topics with specific cultural and linguistic contexts.






















True Partnerships

Co-creation for us is a mindset that guides our relationships with clients from day one.








Industry Expertise

Our industry experts understand the big issues that shape our world.




















Value Creation

We pride ourselves on having a flexible learning approach. We partner with clients who have the ability and desire to embrace a process of continuous learning and transformation. Utilizing best-practice methodologies, our learning journeys will have a lasting impact on your executives.

Our programs typically incorporate a blend of learning tools such as classroom sessions, discussions and debates, workshops, simulations, role-plays, case studies, outdoor activities, projects, and learning expeditions.

Using a variety of carefully selected impact metrics, we go beyond value creation — we empower your people and create the path for your organization to thrive.








Learning Formats










Face-to-Face

Our face-to-face solutions break silos — creating real connections — and find actionable solutions.








Online

From live sessions to pre-recorded lectures, we create scalable solutions for organizations, ideal for a large number of participants from multiple locations.








Blended

Our blended solution brings the best of both worlds. Our state-of-the-art Learning Management System enables us to incorporate online elements into our face-to-face programs, ensuring continuous learning.
















Contact Us

sections.title: Global Network with a Global Reach
sections.text:
NYU Abu Dhabi, located at a new crossroads of the world, enriched by the intellectual vitality and research opportunities of a new world-class research institute, and benefiting from an active connection to NYU New York and other NYU global sites, provides the finest educational opportunity in the world for professional development.

Our world is witnessing drastic change, faster than ever. In a borderless business world, organizations must continuously adapt and evolve within their changing markets. Constant change requires the ability to adapt, lead, and maintain a vision based on common values and desired results. Leading diverse teams and creating agile organizations is yet another challenge.

sections.title: Request more information
sections.text:
NYU Abu Dhabi’s Office of Executive Education (OEE) is uniquely positioned to support the development efforts that organizations need to meet these challenges. Founded on the principle that executive development needs to be collaborative, relevant, and measurable, The OEE designs a new and more relevant approach to executive development that is fit for the challenges and business environment of the 21st century.

We support regional objectives of the UAE National Charter 2021, Abu Dhabi Economic Vision 2030, and Saudi Vision 2030, with transformational programs that focus on executive development in areas such as leadership, digital transformation, operational excellence, economics, innovation and intrapreneurship, global policy-making, culture and the arts, healthcare, and education, among others.

The OEE is committed to value creation for people and organizations. We achieve transformational results by working in partnership with organizations to co-create bespoke, future-focused learning designs that empower people, develop leaders, and enhance the strengths of businesses.

Our custom executive education programs target organizations' specific business needs and build rock-solid alignment around their strategic goals.

A custom program with NYUAD is a transformational learning journey that delivers meaningful and enduring change — from within. Together, we open your organization to breakthrough thinking and empower your people to navigate volatility and uncertainty to deliver the competitive advantage and sustainable growth you need to thrive — today and tomorrow.

sections.title: Professional Achievement
sections.text: Participants successfully completing NYU Abu Dhabi programs receive a Certificate of Professional Achievement. Professional development programs are accredited for recognition by the Emirates National Qualifications Authority or the UAE Commission on Academic Accreditation, as appropriate.

sections.title: Our Approach, Our Impact · Focused on Business Results
sections.text:
The Office of Executive Education designs, develops, and delivers customized and open enrollment programs to meet the needs of organizations and executives.

Our work begins with a blank canvas, and through real collaboration, we gain an in-depth understanding of your business’s learning needs and strategic goals.







We partner with your organization throughout the entire process of design and delivery. Our work begins with understanding, empathizing with, and challenging your assumptions, vision, and objectives through needs assessment interviews with key stakeholders and a review of organizational challenges and competencies.




















We work closely to fine-tune our understanding of your organization, culture, challenges, and opportunities, and to ensure the curriculum meets your objectives.

title: Global Education
text:
Global Education






NYU New York , NYU Abu Dhabi, and NYU Shanghai form the backbone of NYU’s global network of degree granting campuses and academic centers across six continents that enable seamless international mobility of students and faculty in their pursuit of academic and scholarly activity.








The World as Your Classroom




















J-Term

J-Term courses are designed as highly immersive learning experiences that take place during the year. Intellectually linked to their locations, J-Term takes advantage of local resources; explore the history, culture, economy, and society of the host communities. The courses illuminate the interdependence of local knowledge and global awareness while fostering cross-cultural research and insights into complex global issues.



- Where Science Meets the Canvas

- Learning Beyond the Classroom, Grounded in the World

- Teaching Politics and Disruption in Abu Dhabi

Learn about J-Term



















Semester Abroad

Students may spend up to two semesters of their NYUAD education studying abroad in NYU’s Global Network of academic centers.



Student Stories from Abroad

- A Passion for Discovery

- Just Explore

- Science is a constantly changing field

Learn about Semester Abroad































Summer Experiential Learning Abroad

During the summer, undergraduate students are able to engage in full-time research and internships in world-class institutions around the world. This gives students the opportunity to hone their research skills by becoming active investigators who demonstrate creativity and learn the ability to tackle new and exciting challenges.



- Valuable Insights Gained from Summer Research

- Bloom Like a Flower

Learn about Summer Experiential Learning Abroad



















Community-Based Global Learning

Through Community-based Learning Programs in the UAE, NYU Abu Dhabi guides students in reading and engaging with the dynamic text of the real world.



- J-Term Takes Students Around UAE

- Students Explore UAE in Experiential Learning

- Four Exciting UAE-based Courses

Learn about Community-based Global Learning



















Every NYUAD student can study abroad during their four-year degree










1700+

Students took J-Term Courses Abroad







700+

Students took a Semester Abroad







500+

Students took Summer Research and Internships Abroad







30

Countries



















Immersive and Concentrated Experiences in the UAE and Abroad







Global education is an essential component of NYU Abu Dhabi’s educational mission and curriculum. It is realized through a careful sequence of interrelated academic and intercultural experiences over four years that foster greater intercultural understanding towards social responsibility — globally and locally.

































































Engineers for Social Impact at NYU Abu Dhabi







Engineers for Social Impact supports and complements the mission of the Engineering Division and the broad goals of NYU Abu Dhabi through courses that emphasize experiential learning and projects that develop globally-relevant, locally-sustainable designs to meet challenges and deliver on opportunities that enable individuals across global communities to more effectively realize their aspirations and ambitions.



Learn more about Engineers for Social Impact








NYU's Global Academic Centers

NYU's global academic centers complement the three portal campuses, allowing students to study away for a semester or longer at a site of their choice. Each site offers a range of courses, permitting students to complete core requirements — as well as co-curricular activities to explore the region, meet local students and figures, and use new language skills — and is characterized by a distinct academic identity.


- Accra

- Berlin

- Buenos Aires

- Florence

- London

- Los Angeles

- Madrid

- New York

- Paris

- Prague

- Shanghai

- Sydney

- Tel Aviv

- Tulsa

- Washington, DC






World Renowned Faculty Teach at J-Term







The January Term courses are taught by renowned scholars, writers, artists, journalists, and policy analysts, who teach only during the J-Term, as well as distinguished professors from NYU, NYUAD, and other leading universities.










David Cameron

Former British Prime Minister







Ghazi Al Mulaifi

Grammy-Nominated Musician







Ouided Bouchamaoui

Nobel Laureate








A Semester Abroad at NYUAD Opened Gateways to the World

Studying anthropology in a new cultural context gave this NYU student Gladybel Morales a fresh lens on the world.


Read about the global experience of our students

- A Reflection on J-Term

Master's Programs at NYUAD

NYU Abu Dhabi master's programs are designed to take full advantage of the University's location at the center of a global crossroads. The unique culture and experiences provided in the region will provide students with a perspective that prepares them to engage the future with a global mindset.

title: Apply
text:
Apply






Application and Admissions Process














- An applicant's bachelor’s degree does not have to be in the arts, but the application should demonstrate the mastery needed to engage effectively with graduate-level work in this program.

- To be eligible for admission to an NYUAD master's program, an applicant needs to have completed the equivalent of a four-year US bachelor's degree. Official transcripts certifying conferral of a bachelor’s degree are required before the student can start the program.








Apply Now

Deadline February 15, 2027

Questions before you apply?

Join an information session








-





Prepare the following required information when you are ready to start an application:

- Transcripts from all post-secondary institutions you have attended (copies accepted)

- Proof of English Proficiency (select the appropriate option in the application)

- You are from a designated list of English-speaking countries

- You have completed at least 4 years in a university program taught entirely in English

- Self-reported test scores for proof of English proficiency. Minimum scores: Academic IELTS = 6.5 / TOEFL iBT = 90 / DuoLingo = 120.

- A current CV or resume

- Essays responding to specific prompts provided in the application. Essays give you the opportunity to fully present yourself to the Selection Committee, and to provide insight into your experiences, goals, and thought processes.

- Two letters of recommendation. You will provide the name, title and email of two recommenders. They will receive a request from NYUAD to upload a letter of recommendation for your application.

- Artist’s Portfolio. Please view more information in the Artist’s Portfolio section below.

You have the option in the application to indicate if you would like to be considered for an academic merit-based scholarship. No other information needs to be included in the application.

Any information or materials submitted to NYU Abu Dhabi after the final application deadline are not guaranteed to be reviewed or considered by the Selection Committee.

You will receive an email when there are updates to your application status that can be viewed on the Application Status Portal. Your final official decision will be posted to your status page, and an admission decision from any other source of communication will be not considered official nor binding.

NYU Abu Dhabi reserves the right to validate the accuracy of your application information with appropriate sources, including the right to contact relevant individuals and organizations.



-






- Verification: After submitting your application, the admissions office checks that all supporting documents have been uploaded correctly and are readable. After this verification, the applications are made available to the Selection Committee for the initial review.

- Initial Review: The Selection Committee begins reviewing submitted applications after the application deadline. The committee looks at information from all parts of the application to form a complete picture of the applicant’s potential fit with the program.

- Shortlist: The Selection Committee places applicants who have the best fit for the program on a “shortlist”. These applicants are invited to an interview with the Selection Committee (usually online).

- Interview: During the interview, the applicant has the opportunity to provide more details about their motivations, education and experience. This gives the Selection Committee a more complete understanding of the applicant before making an admissions decision.

- Admissions Decision: Applicants who are offered admission will be notified by email to check the Application Status Portal where the admission letter can be viewed and downloaded. The applicant needs to confirm acceptance of the offer.

- Offer Acceptance: The applicant confirms acceptance of the admission offer via the Application Status Portal and pays the confirmation deposit.

Note! You must receive a UAE security clearance, and obtain an appropriate UAE visa if required by your residency status. NYU Abu Dhabi will facilitate these processes for admitted students. If for any reason you cannot obtain the security clearance or visa, your admissions offer may be rescinded.



-





The MFA application requires you to submit an artist’s portfolio. The total number of submitted works cannot exceed 20 items of your recent artwork. This is an integral part of the admissions review process.

Videos for time-based work can be submitted in place of digital images. Videos can be a compilation of various works, but the total running time cannot exceed five minutes per video. Genres appropriate to video documentation include video art, performance, and kinetic art, but not documentation of sculptures or exhibitions.

All portfolios must be submitted via the NYUAD MFA online applicatio n . Do not send hard copies of your portfolio or artwork to NYU Abu Dhabi. Such materials cannot be appended to your application file, nor can such submissions be returned to applicants.

- Media files up to 5GB

- These file formats are supported:

[Slide] .bmp, .gif, .jpg, .jpeg, .png, .tif, .tiff

[Video] 3g2, .3gp, .avi, .m2v, .m4v, .mkv, .mov, .mpeg, .mpg, .mp4, .mxf, .webm, .wmv; Apple ProRes is supported.








Important Information About Application Eligibility

- ​​​​​​​A three-year degree is usually acceptable to be considered for admission to an NYUAD master's program if the applicant completed 13 years of school before completing the three-year degree. For example, most three-year degrees from the UK and Europe are acceptable. We are not able to provide a definite answer before evaluating the applicant's transcripts.

- In addition to the information above, the online application provides instructions to guide you. All sections of the application and the required supporting documents must be submitted online by the deadline. Incomplete applications will not be reviewed. Do not submit any hard copy materials to NYU Abu Dhabi as part of the application process.

sections.title: Application and Admissions Process
sections.text:
- An applicant's bachelor’s degree does not have to be in the arts, but the application should demonstrate the mastery needed to engage effectively with graduate-level work in this program.

- To be eligible for admission to an NYUAD master's program, an applicant needs to have completed the equivalent of a four-year US bachelor's degree. Official transcripts certifying conferral of a bachelor’s degree are required before the student can start the program.

sections.title: Apply Now
sections.text:
Deadline February 15, 2027

Questions before you apply?

Join an information session








-





Prepare the following required information when you are ready to start an application:

- Transcripts from all post-secondary institutions you have attended (copies accepted)

- Proof of English Proficiency (select the appropriate option in the application)

- You are from a designated list of English-speaking countries

- You have completed at least 4 years in a university program taught entirely in English

- Self-reported test scores for proof of English proficiency. Minimum scores: Academic IELTS = 6.5 / TOEFL iBT = 90 / DuoLingo = 120.

- A current CV or resume

- Essays responding to specific prompts provided in the application. Essays give you the opportunity to fully present yourself to the Selection Committee, and to provide insight into your experiences, goals, and thought processes.

- Two letters of recommendation. You will provide the name, title and email of two recommenders. They will receive a request from NYUAD to upload a letter of recommendation for your application.

- Artist’s Portfolio. Please view more information in the Artist’s Portfolio section below.

You have the option in the application to indicate if you would like to be considered for an academic merit-based scholarship. No other information needs to be included in the application.

Any information or materials submitted to NYU Abu Dhabi after the final application deadline are not guaranteed to be reviewed or considered by the Selection Committee.

You will receive an email when there are updates to your application status that can be viewed on the Application Status Portal. Your final official decision will be posted to your status page, and an admission decision from any other source of communication will be not considered official nor binding.

NYU Abu Dhabi reserves the right to validate the accuracy of your application information with appropriate sources, including the right to contact relevant individuals and organizations.



-






- Verification: After submitting your application, the admissions office checks that all supporting documents have been uploaded correctly and are readable. After this verification, the applications are made available to the Selection Committee for the initial review.

- Initial Review: The Selection Committee begins reviewing submitted applications after the application deadline. The committee looks at information from all parts of the application to form a complete picture of the applicant’s potential fit with the program.

- Shortlist: The Selection Committee places applicants who have the best fit for the program on a “shortlist”. These applicants are invited to an interview with the Selection Committee (usually online).

- Interview: During the interview, the applicant has the opportunity to provide more details about their motivations, education and experience. This gives the Selection Committee a more complete understanding of the applicant before making an admissions decision.

- Admissions Decision: Applicants who are offered admission will be notified by email to check the Application Status Portal where the admission letter can be viewed and downloaded. The applicant needs to confirm acceptance of the offer.

- Offer Acceptance: The applicant confirms acceptance of the admission offer via the Application Status Portal and pays the confirmation deposit.

Note! You must receive a UAE security clearance, and obtain an appropriate UAE visa if required by your residency status. NYU Abu Dhabi will facilitate these processes for admitted students. If for any reason you cannot obtain the security clearance or visa, your admissions offer may be rescinded.



-





The MFA application requires you to submit an artist’s portfolio. The total number of submitted works cannot exceed 20 items of your recent artwork. This is an integral part of the admissions review process.

Videos for time-based work can be submitted in place of digital images. Videos can be a compilation of various works, but the total running time cannot exceed five minutes per video. Genres appropriate to video documentation include video art, performance, and kinetic art, but not documentation of sculptures or exhibitions.

All portfolios must be submitted via the NYUAD MFA online applicatio n . Do not send hard copies of your portfolio or artwork to NYU Abu Dhabi. Such materials cannot be appended to your application file, nor can such submissions be returned to applicants.

- Media files up to 5GB

- These file formats are supported:

[Slide] .bmp, .gif, .jpg, .jpeg, .png, .tif, .tiff

[Video] 3g2, .3gp, .avi, .m2v, .m4v, .mkv, .mov, .mpeg, .mpg, .mp4, .mxf, .webm, .wmv; Apple ProRes is supported.








Important Information About Application Eligibility

- ​​​​​​​A three-year degree is usually acceptable to be considered for admission to an NYUAD master's program if the applicant completed 13 years of school before completing the three-year degree. For example, most three-year degrees from the UK and Europe are acceptable. We are not able to provide a definite answer before evaluating the applicant's transcripts.

- In addition to the information above, the online application provides instructions to guide you. All sections of the application and the required supporting documents must be submitted online by the deadline. Incomplete applications will not be reviewed. Do not submit any hard copy materials to NYU Abu Dhabi as part of the application process.

- After submitting the application, applicants will not be able to change or add information. Applicants will receive a link to the Application Status Portal to track the status.
