title: Courses
breadcrumbs: MSc Interdisciplinary Data Science and Artificial Intelligence
text:
Courses





The two-year full-time MSc program requires the completion of 36 credit hours as outlined below.



Structure

| Requirements | Course Details

| 1 required course

0 credits | Data Science for Everyone Bootcamp

| 5 required courses

15 credits | Probability and Statistics; Machine Learning; Introduction to Data Science; Introduction to Artificial Intelligence; Ethics and Legal Considerations for Data Science
| 5 elective courses

15 credits | Advanced electives
| 2 Master's Thesis

6 credits

| Research project at NYUAD or in collaboration with industry partners
| 2 Winter School courses

0 credits | Two required courses
| 4 Data Science and AI Seminar

0 credits | Four required courses






Specializations

Since Interdisciplinary Data Science and Artificial Intelligence are vast fields, students will have substantial flexibility in selecting electives that align with their academic and professional interests. In consultation with their faculty mentor and the Graduate Program Head, each student will develop a personalized course plan that leads to an informal focus in a specific area, culminating in a capstone research thesis.

Below are examples of potential focus areas, based on course offerings and faculty expertise:

- Health Informatics : Applications of machine learning and data science in healthcare and biomedical research
- Urban Mobility and Logistics : Data-driven approaches to urban transport, supply chains, and traffic operations
- (Arabic) Natural Language Processing : AI models for language processing, with a focus on Arabic and multilingual contexts
- Human-Machine Interaction : Designing AI-driven systems for enhanced user experience and interaction
- Computational Social Science : AI-driven analysis of human behavior, policy, and social dynamics
- Mathematical Foundations and AI Theory : Core algorithmic foundations, optimization, and theoretical advancements in AI
- Data Science and Economics : AI applications in financial modeling, economic decision-making, and quantitative analysis







Course Descriptions















Required

-





Credits : 0

Occurring the summer before students begin coursework, this mandatory, 0-credit, in-person course is designed to ensure that all students meet baseline requirements in programming and quantitative reasoning. During this bootcamp, students will gain a strong foundation in Python programming, basic probability and statistics, calculus and linear algebra, and regression analysis. Note that the bootcamp is included as part of regular program tuition and is required for all admitted students.



-





Credits : 0

This J-Term program, held in Abu Dhabi, is a key feature of the program. This program will be held jointly for both active cohorts of students (first-years and second-years). First-year students will participate in short courses taught by faculty, while second-year students will participate in small-group research workshops with visiting faculty organized by theme (with first-year students in the audience). Both cohorts will mix for a Hackathon that concludes the Winter School, where teams of mixed first-year and second-year students led by a visiting or NYUAD faculty member produce a pilot study that can lead to an interdisciplinary research collaboration.



-





Credits : 3

Description

This foundational course focuses on data manipulation, cleaning, visualization, and processing using Python and a related suite of data science libraries. Students will learn how to apply Data Science tools to underpin hidden data patterns and trends and improve decision- making, introducing fundamental tools, and improving students’ fluency in data science. It is a hands-on, programming-based course.



-





Credits: 3

Description

This foundational course introduces the basic notions of Probability theory, including common probability distributions, random processes, Markov chains. It focuses on building students’ statistical reasoning skills through a rigorous study of confidence intervals, hypothesis testing,regression analysis, and elaborates the difference between Frequentist and Bayesian statistics.



-





Credits: 3

Description

This foundational course teaches the most important Machine Learning (ML) algorithms and their applications. Students will learn the theoretical foundations of machine learning, and practice the implementation and application of machine learning techniques to real world problems. Topics include: (i) supervised learning (e.g. logistic regression, random forests, support vector machines, ensemble methods, and neural networks), (ii) unsupervised learning (e.g., clustering, dimensionality reduction, recommender systems), and (iii) applications and case studies (e.g., apply ML to the development of smart robots perception, text understanding (web search, anti-spam filter), computer vision, speech processing, health informatics, etc.).



-





Credits: 3

Description

Introduction to Artificial Intelligence is an immersive course that provides students with a robust foundation in the core principles and methodologies driving modern AI systems. The curriculum spans a diverse array of topics, beginning with problem-solving techniques and search algorithms essential for navigating complex decision spaces. Students will delve into knowledge representation and reasoning, learning to structure and manipulate information to enable intelligent behavior. The course also explores natural language processing and computer vision, examining methods that empower machines to interpret and generate human language, as well as process and analyze visual information, all while considering the broader ethical implications of AI technologies. Through a blend of theoretical lectures and practical assignments, participants will gain hands-on experience in designing and implementing AI solutions, equipping them to develop intelligent systems capable of tasks such as game playing, language translation, and pattern recognition. By the end of the course, students will not only have a comprehensive understanding of various AI approaches but also the ability to critically evaluate their strengths and limitations.



-





Credits: 3

Description

In this workshop-based course, students are introduced to and practice the skills of argumentation, research, and clarity of expression. In the first half of the class, students learn the craft of artistic writing, from the ground up — constructing one analytic piece in increments. The second part of the semester is devoted to putting these skills into professional practice, as students write artist statements, reviews of current work, personal essays, creative pieces, and more. Students read top critics in their fields as well as writers from the canon particularly relevant to their own work.



-





Credits : 3

Students will have two options for their Master's thesis:

1- A research project conducted exclusively at NYUAD working with the student’s mentor,

2- An applied research project conducted in collaboration with a local partner.

While the first option is more research-oriented, the second option will allow students to do their applied research project through a part-time internship with a local partner under the guidance of their academic mentor, with the aim of applying the conducted research to a specific local context. In both cases, students will learn how to produce a research paper in Data Science and how to apply data science. Students who pursue applied projects will have the opportunity to use NYUAD’s resources to become well-versed in combining theoretical approaches and solving real-world problems. Master's Thesis 1 serves as the initial phase of the project, allowing students to delve into the foundational aspects of their comprehensive data science project. During this phase, students will focus on project proposal development, planning, conducting a literature review, data acquisition, and preliminary analysis. Master's Thesis 2 represents the continuation of the project and provides students with the opportunity to further advance their research or applied project by producing novel insights. In this phase, students will share their thesis research progress, engage in discussions to address ongoing challenges, and maintain a consistent momentum towards producing their final report.



-





Credits : 0

This zero-credit course, taken every semester, introduces students to some of the active areas of research in Data Science. Invited speakers from both academia and industry will give 90-minute presentations every week during the academic year, and will meet with students in small groups as well. Moreover, by hosting leading keynote speakers, this seminar will expose students to managerial, entrepreneurial and leadership skills.






Electives

Students are required to take at least five elective courses, allowing them to explore specific areas of interest in consultation with their mentor and the Graduate Program Head. These electives draw upon the interdisciplinary nature of the program and the expertise of faculty across various divisions. These courses include but are not limited to the following:

-





Credits : 3

Topics include complete metric spaces, the contraction mapping theorem, Principal Component Analysis, Low rank approximation and Compression, Elements of abstract Integration, Least Squares problems and their regularizations, inner product spaces, Reproducing Kernel Methods.



-





Credits: 3

Description

This foundational course teaches about the algorithms, tools, and methods needed to process and analyze large amounts of data beyond the capabilities of typical research hardware. This course will cover real-world applications that require massive data analysis and how they can be implemented on Big Data platforms. The course will consist of lectures based on both textbook material and scientific papers, as well as programming assignments to provide students with hands-on experience on building data-intensive applications using existing Big Data platforms.



-





Credits : 3

This course is designed to provide detailed understanding of the physics, instrumentation, and signal processing methods used in X-ray (projection radiography), X-ray computed tomography, nuclear medicine (SPECT/PET), optical imaging, ultrasound imaging, and magnetic resonance imaging (MRI).



-





Credits : 3

Topics include the potential outcomes framework, natural experiments, and the growing field of applying data science tools to causal learning.



-





Credits : 3

This course covers topics such as migration and mobility, housing, traffic networks, remote sensing and imaging, policing, and more. This seminar-based course also covers applications from diverse fields, such as sociology, psychology, data science, and machine learning. It covers the use of computational techniques to model and predict social phenomena using real data.



-





Credits : 3

Topics include image classification, image segmentation, object localization, and object detection.



-





Credits : 3

This course introduces the algorithmic techniques necessary for mining massive amounts of data. This includes randomized approximation algorithms for streaming data, randomized numerical linear algebra and its applications to dimension reduction and clustering, algorithms for graph analysis, and large scale machine learning.



-





Credits : 3

This course is an introduction to the use of innovative large datasets collected from the web, or from exhaustive administrative datasets, from surveys and from field experiments and lab experiments, starting from concrete questions and actual research experience of social scientists.



-





Credits : 3

This course introduces the fundamentals of neural networks, with applications to text data, image data, audio data, and other structured data.



-





Credits : 3

This course will introduce students to data science in environmental science, including the nature of environmental data and the use of relevant computational tools and software packages in Python.



-





Credits : 3

This course presents an overview of the management and utilization of health-related data to support decision-making. This includes (i) clinical data, such as data collected within electronic health records and clinical decision support systems, (ii) public health data, and (iii) bioinformatics data such as proteomics. The course also introduces state-of-the-art artificial intelligence and machine learning advances in the field of health informatics.



-





Credits : 3

Topics include data representations of text, recurrent neural networks, and transformers; this course will be taught in the HuggingFace Python ecosystem and will have some focus on Arabic NLP.



-





Credits : 3

Topics include convex and non-convex optimization, duality, stochastic gradients, and derivative-free optimization.



-





Credits : 3

This course will discuss topics such as basic concentration inequalities, random vectors in high dimension, matrix concentration inequalities, community detection, covariance estimation and clustering, matrix completion, spiked models and outliers detection, information plus noise models, random graphs, together with their applications to machine learning and data science.



-





Credits : 3

This course explores the intersection of robotics, artificial intelligence, and human interaction. It aims to equip students with the knowledge and skills to design, develop, and analyze robots that can interact socially with humans in various contexts.



-





Credits : 0

This course introduces students to the fundamentals of data and physics-driven urban traffic operations management by first developing models of traffic physics at the microscopic, mesoscopic, and macroscopic levels along with the scaling laws that connect them. The models inform various tools operating at the interface of traffic physics and data-driven optimization.



-





Credits : 0

This course will introduce students to (i) advanced state-of-the-art computational methods relevant to healthcare problems, (ii) the nature of diverse heterogeneous clinical data, such as electronic health records and medical images, (iii) the challenges of translating such solutions into clinical settings, including model failures, regulation, etc., as well as (iv) the use of relevant tools such as Python, ML libraries, Github, latex, and neptune.ai.










Sample Course Structure

| Fall Semester

The course also explores natural language processing and computer vision, examining methods that empower machines to interpret and generate human language, as well as process and analyze visual information, all while considering the broader ethical implications of AI technologies. Through a blend of theoretical lectures and practical assignments, participants will gain hands-on experience in designing and implementing AI solutions, equipping them to develop intelligent systems capable of tasks such as game playing, language translation, and pattern recognition. By the end of the course, students will not only have a comprehensive understanding of various AI approaches but also the ability to critically evaluate their strengths and limitations.



-





Credits: 3

Description

In this workshop-based course, students are introduced to and practice the skills of argumentation, research, and clarity of expression. In the first half of the class, students learn the craft of artistic writing, from the ground up — constructing one analytic piece in increments. The second part of the semester is devoted to putting these skills into professional practice, as students write artist statements, reviews of current work, personal essays, creative pieces, and more. Students read top critics in their fields as well as writers from the canon particularly relevant to their own work.



-





Credits : 3

Students will have two options for their Master's thesis:

1- A research project conducted exclusively at NYUAD working with the student’s mentor,

2- An applied research project conducted in collaboration with a local partner.

While the first option is more research-oriented, the second option will allow students to do their applied research project through a part-time internship with a local partner under the guidance of their academic mentor, with the aim of applying the conducted research to a specific local context. In both cases, students will learn how to produce a research paper in Data Science and how to apply data science. Students who pursue applied projects will have the opportunity to use NYUAD’s resources to become well-versed in combining theoretical approaches and solving real-world problems. Master's Thesis 1 serves as the initial phase of the project, allowing students to delve into the foundational aspects of their comprehensive data science project. During this phase, students will focus on project proposal development, planning, conducting a literature review, data acquisition, and preliminary analysis. Master's Thesis 2 represents the continuation of the project and provides students with the opportunity to further advance their research or applied project by producing novel insights. In this phase, students will share their thesis research progress, engage in discussions to address ongoing challenges, and maintain a consistent momentum towards producing their final report.



-





Credits : 0

This zero-credit course, taken every semester, introduces students to some of the active areas of research in Data Science. Invited speakers from both academia and industry will give 90-minute presentations every week during the academic year, and will meet with students in small groups as well. Moreover, by hosting leading keynote speakers, this seminar will expose students to managerial, entrepreneurial and leadership skills.

sections.title: Course Descriptions · Electives
sections.text:
Students are required to take at least five elective courses, allowing them to explore specific areas of interest in consultation with their mentor and the Graduate Program Head. These electives draw upon the interdisciplinary nature of the program and the expertise of faculty across various divisions. These courses include but are not limited to the following:

-





Credits : 3

Topics include complete metric spaces, the contraction mapping theorem, Principal Component Analysis, Low rank approximation and Compression, Elements of abstract Integration, Least Squares problems and their regularizations, inner product spaces, Reproducing Kernel Methods.



-





Credits: 3

Description

This foundational course teaches about the algorithms, tools, and methods needed to process and analyze large amounts of data beyond the capabilities of typical research hardware. This course will cover real-world applications that require massive data analysis and how they can be implemented on Big Data platforms. The course will consist of lectures based on both textbook material and scientific papers, as well as programming assignments to provide students with hands-on experience on building data-intensive applications using existing Big Data platforms.



-





Credits : 3

This course is designed to provide detailed understanding of the physics, instrumentation, and signal processing methods used in X-ray (projection radiography), X-ray computed tomography, nuclear medicine (SPECT/PET), optical imaging, ultrasound imaging, and magnetic resonance imaging (MRI).



-





Credits : 3

Topics include the potential outcomes framework, natural experiments, and the growing field of applying data science tools to causal learning.



-





Credits : 3

This course covers topics such as migration and mobility, housing, traffic networks, remote sensing and imaging, policing, and more. This seminar-based course also covers applications from diverse fields, such as sociology, psychology, data science, and machine learning. It covers the use of computational techniques to model and predict social phenomena using real data.



-





Credits : 3

Topics include image classification, image segmentation, object localization, and object detection.



-





Credits : 3

This course introduces the algorithmic techniques necessary for mining massive amounts of data. This includes randomized approximation algorithms for streaming data, randomized numerical linear algebra and its applications to dimension reduction and clustering, algorithms for graph analysis, and large scale machine learning.



-





Credits : 3

This course is an introduction to the use of innovative large datasets collected from the web, or from exhaustive administrative datasets, from surveys and from field experiments and lab experiments, starting from concrete questions and actual research experience of social scientists.



-





Credits : 3

This course introduces the fundamentals of neural networks, with applications to text data, image data, audio data, and other structured data.



-





Credits : 3

This course will introduce students to data science in environmental science, including the nature of environmental data and the use of relevant computational tools and software packages in Python.



-





Credits : 3

This course presents an overview of the management and utilization of health-related data to support decision-making. This includes (i) clinical data, such as data collected within electronic health records and clinical decision support systems, (ii) public health data, and (iii) bioinformatics data such as proteomics. The course also introduces state-of-the-art artificial intelligence and machine learning advances in the field of health informatics.



-





Credits : 3

Topics include data representations of text, recurrent neural networks, and transformers; this course will be taught in the HuggingFace Python ecosystem and will have some focus on Arabic NLP.



-





Credits : 3

Topics include convex and non-convex optimization, duality, stochastic gradients, and derivative-free optimization.



-





Credits : 3

This course will discuss topics such as basic concentration inequalities, random vectors in high dimension, matrix concentration inequalities, community detection, covariance estimation and clustering, matrix completion, spiked models and outliers detection, information plus noise models, random graphs, together with their applications to machine learning and data science.



-





Credits : 3

This course explores the intersection of robotics, artificial intelligence, and human interaction. It aims to equip students with the knowledge and skills to design, develop, and analyze robots that can interact socially with humans in various contexts.



-





Credits : 0

This course introduces students to the fundamentals of data and physics-driven urban traffic operations management by first developing models of traffic physics at the microscopic, mesoscopic, and macroscopic levels along with the scaling laws that connect them. The models inform various tools operating at the interface of traffic physics and data-driven optimization.



-





Credits : 0

This course will introduce students to (i) advanced state-of-the-art computational methods relevant to healthcare problems, (ii) the nature of diverse heterogeneous clinical data, such as electronic health records and medical images, (iii) the challenges of translating such solutions into clinical settings, including model failures, regulation, etc., as well as (iv) the use of relevant tools such as Python, ML libraries, Github, latex, and neptune.ai.

Funding





Completing a master’s degree takes a large investment of time, effort, and funds. In recognition of this, NYU Abu Dhabi strives to provide scholarships for all students admitted to this program. Over recent years, most applicants admitted to NYUAD master's programs were offered NYUAD scholarships that typically cover between 50 and 85 percent of the tuition and fees.













However, NYUAD funding does not cover travel, housing or living expenses during the program. For that reason, applicants should create a budget before applying and be confident that their personal and external funding will cover the remaining costs of tuition and their living expenses during this full-time program.

To discuss your budget for studying in this program, please contact the Graduate Admissions office: nyuad.graduateadmissions@nyu.edu .

NYUAD Scholarships

Applicants should indicate in the application if they want to be considered for an academic merit-based scholarship. The information provided in the application is sufficient, and no additional information needs to be submitted by the applicant. Academic merit is determined by the selection committee during the admissions process. Top-ranked candidates are offered larger scholarships.

NYUAD scholarships typically cover between 50 and 85 percent of the tuition and fees. In rare circumstances, top academically-ranked admitted applicants may be offered scholarships covering almost all of their tuition and fees.








Ruwwad Zayed Program

The Ruwwad Zayed Program is a merit-based university scholarship for high-potential Emirati and Arab youth who are based in the UAE and will be pursuing the MSc Interdisciplinary Data Science & AI degree.

Scholars will receive full academic funding, tailored leadership development, and comprehensive support services to strengthen both their personal academic and professional growth.

Apply Directly to the Ruwwad Zayed Program



-





Students will need to source funds to pay for housing, travel, living expenses, and the tuition and fees balance not covered by NYUAD scholarships. These sources usually include:

- Personal and family funds

- Student loans

- External scholarships
EducationUSA is a US Department of State network of over 430 international student advising centers in more than 175 countries and territories. These offices offer financial advice for international students.



-





Students are expected to use personal and external funds to cover part of their total expenses. For that reason, students should prepare a budget now so that they are able to focus fully on studies during the program.

title: Learning Outcomes
breadcrumbs: MSc Interdisciplinary Data Science and Artificial Intelligence
text:
Learning Outcomes





Upon successful completion of the MSc in Interdisciplinary Data Science and Artificial Intelligence (MIDSAI) at NYU Abu Dhabi, students will have achieved the following program learning outcomes:

Specialized Knowledge

Articulate highly specialized knowledge of data science and artificial intelligence, at the interface between data science, artificial intelligence, and other domain science(s), including recent developments and emerging trends.

Advanced Problem-solving Skills

Demonstrate advanced skills that integrate knowledge in computing theory, languages, algorithms, mathematical and statistical models, and the principles of optimization to formulate and develop innovative solutions to academic/professional problems with intellectual independence.

Advanced Research Skills

Develop new skills and knowledge through undirected study, self-training, and bibliographic research, in order to design, create, and implement a research project.

Interdisciplinary Techniques and Perspectives

Apply advanced data analysis and computational modeling techniques to a variety of interdisciplinary problems. Students will learn to work effectively in interdisciplinary teams, leveraging diverse skills and perspectives to address complex data science challenges.

Effective Communication of Findings

Demonstrate the ability to effectively communicate data science findings to a variety of audiences, including domain experts and non-technical stakeholders.

Implications to Society

Understand and address the ethical, legal, and societal implications of data science and artificial intelligence, including issues of privacy, bias, and fairness.

Self-evaluation and Growth

Self-evaluate performance, learning needs, and professional knowledge in new and novel contexts related to data.

sections.title: Learning Outcomes
sections.text:
Learning Outcomes





Upon successful completion of the MSc in Interdisciplinary Data Science and Artificial Intelligence (MIDSAI) at NYU Abu Dhabi, students will have achieved the following program learning outcomes:

sections.title: Breadcrumbs · Specialized Knowledge
sections.text: Articulate highly specialized knowledge of data science and artificial intelligence, at the interface between data science, artificial intelligence, and other domain science(s), including recent developments and emerging trends.

sections.title: Breadcrumbs · Advanced Problem-solving Skills
sections.text: Demonstrate advanced skills that integrate knowledge in computing theory, languages, algorithms, mathematical and statistical models, and the principles of optimization to formulate and develop innovative solutions to academic/professional problems with intellectual independence.

sections.title: Breadcrumbs · Advanced Research Skills
sections.text: Develop new skills and knowledge through undirected study, self-training, and bibliographic research, in order to design, create, and implement a research project.

sections.title: Breadcrumbs · Interdisciplinary Techniques and Perspectives
sections.text: Apply advanced data analysis and computational modeling techniques to a variety of interdisciplinary problems. Students will learn to work effectively in interdisciplinary teams, leveraging diverse skills and perspectives to address complex data science challenges.

sections.title: Breadcrumbs · Effective Communication of Findings
sections.text: Demonstrate the ability to effectively communicate data science findings to a variety of audiences, including domain experts and non-technical stakeholders.

sections.title: Breadcrumbs · Implications to Society
sections.text: Understand and address the ethical, legal, and societal implications of data science and artificial intelligence, including issues of privacy, bias, and fairness.

sections.title: Breadcrumbs · Self-evaluation and Growth
sections.text: Self-evaluate performance, learning needs, and professional knowledge in new and novel contexts related to data.

title: Program Structure
breadcrumbs: MSc Interdisciplinary Data Science and Artificial Intelligence
text:
Program Structure





The MSc in Interdisciplinary Data Science and Artificial Intelligence is a two-year, full-time, in-person program delivered on the NYU Abu Dhabi campus. To earn the degree, students must complete 10 courses (36 credits) and a thesis, designed to provide both a strong foundation in data science and AI while having the flexibility to explore interdisciplinary specializations.








Balanced Curriculum

Students will benefit from a balanced curriculum that combines foundational data science and artificial intelligence coursework with the flexibility to explore a personalized area of interest under the guidance of faculty experts in globally significant applied topics.

Student-centered

The program offers a student-centered experience with mentorship throughout the program and is distinguished by a year-long master’s thesis. This project allows the student to forge a deep knowledge base on a specific research area.

Exposure to Emerging Trends

The program also provides unique exposure to emerging trends through a Data Science and AI Seminar series and an immersive Winter School, where students engage with cutting-edge research and industry applications in AI and Data Science.

Built-in Global Network

Connecting students with NYU faculty in New York or Shanghai. The program features visiting faculty and international speakers, and research placements may involve collaborations with regional and international partners.

title: Research
breadcrumbs: MSc Interdisciplinary Data Science and Artificial Intelligence
text:
Research





The MSc Interdisciplinary Data Science and Artificial Intelligence (MIDSAI) is poised to significantly advance various research activities across diverse clusters. These clusters harness cutting-edge AI and data science technologies to address real-world challenges like healthcare, urban informatics, robotics, social sciences, and sustainable development. Students and faculty engage in transformational research and practical applications through collaborations within these clusters, which are aligned with institutional and UAE strategic priorities.







Research-intensive

Students engage in research from the start:


- A full-year thesis on either academic or industry problems.
- Annual two-week research workshops, culminating in a hackathon.
- A regular data science seminar bringing speakers from academia and industry.
- Opportunities to work closely with faculty on real, interdisciplinary research questions. 












Engineering Research Clusters














- Robotics and AI : Students explore human-robot interaction and control systems in collaboration with the NYUAD Center for Artificial Intelligence and Robotics (CAIR) , contributing to innovations in robotics through AI.

- Urban Informatics : Research in this cluster develops data science and AI tools to address problems in transportation, urban fairness, and decision-making. Students will collaborate with NYUAD Center for Interacting Urban Networks (CITIES) researchers.

- Wireless Communications : The focus is on data-driven models for optimizing next-generation networks.








Motion capture techniques enable understanding the role of vision, touch, and proprioception in human-environment interactions













Science Research Clusters










Scalp electrodes used in electroencephalograms











- Interdisciplinary Data Science and AI : Research aims at advancing fundamental theory in probability and machine learning, and translating those breakthroughs into high‑impact tools to serve the UAE, the wider Arab world, and global society. Students will have collaborations with the NYUAD Center of Interdisciplinary Data Science and AI (CIDSAI) .

- Neuroscience and Brain Behavior : Data science techniques analyze datasets to gain insights into human behavior, enhancing courses related to AI applications in social science.

- Complex Biological Systems : Students apply computational modeling to understand complex biological behaviors, enriching life sciences research.

- Quantum Computing and Technology : The research involves quantum machine learning applied to various real-world problems and provides opportunities for quantum technology exploration. Students will benefit from collaborations with the NYUAD Center for Quantum and Topological Systems (CQTS) .

- Artificial Intelligence and Natural Language Processing : Research areas include Arabic natural language processing, machine translation, text analytics, and dialogue systems. Students can collaborate with NYUAD's Computational Approaches to Modeling Language (CAMeL) Lab .














Social Science Research Clusters














- Computational Social Science : Students analyze large-scale social data, addressing societal inequalities and informing policy-making with data-driven insights.

- Government and Public Policy : AI and data science tools are used to model and analyze government policies for a positive societal impact.




















Innovative Applications and Faculty-led Research




















- Healthcare : AI-driven research in personalized diagnostics, treatment, and post-COVID conditions enhances medical outcomes and patient care.

- Human-Machine Interaction (HMI) : AI systems are developed to improve engagement recognition and understanding of emotions in collaborative environments.

- Assistive Technologies : AI supports navigation for visually impaired individuals and learning tools for ADHD students.

- Social Equity and Ethics : Studies focus on editorial diversity, digital inequality, and AI fairness in medical applications.

- 3D Computer Vision and Robotics : Research in vision-language models and medical imaging supports advancements in robotics and healthcare.

- Natural Language Processing and Knowledge Graphs : Multilingual NLP systems enhance social behavior studies and knowledge alignment.














- Environmental Support : AI models aid urban systems management and assess crowd behavior to mitigate pandemic risks.

- Explainable AI : Research on AI-assisted decision-making enhances transparency and collaboration in fields like healthcare.
The program fosters interdisciplinary collaboration, preparing students to tackle global challenges with AI and data science insights and emphasizing the importance of ethical considerations and societal impact.

title: PhD Programs
text:
PhD Programs






PhD Programs at NYUAD focus on Engineering and Science

NYU Abu Dhabi provides pioneering PhD programs for students looking to make a global impact. Students in our PhD programs work on exciting research projects under the guidance of world-class faculty, in a global network of scholars, with access to cutting-edge facilities.

The PhD in Astrophysics and Space Systems is completed entirely at the NYUAD campus.

The Global PhD Programs are started at the New York campus and completed at the NYUAD campus. These programs are offered in collaboration with NYU Tandon School of Engineering, NYU Graduate School of Arts and Science, and NYU Steinhardt.








PhD in Astrophysics and Space Systems







The PhD in Astrophysics and Space Systems (PASS) is the first of its kind in the UAE, and the region. Created in part to support the UAE’s mission to establish itself as a leader in space science, this program aligns with the UAE’s National Space Strategy 2030. This interdisciplinary program bridges the fields of Astrophysics and Engineering and aims to inspire the next generation of space explorers.

This program is different from the Global PhD fellowships because it is completed in its entirety on the Abu Dhabi campus, where students will complete a multi-year-long research project under the supervision of world-class faculty.

Applications open in mid-September for the following fall intake.










View PASS Program Info











Online Information Sessions

Learn more about the program, the NYUAD campus, and the unique experience a graduate program in the UAE offers.



Request More Information

Register for an Information Session













Global PhD Student Fellowships













Each program offers a unique opportunity to engage in a global setting, where students will begin their coursework in New York and complete their research in Abu Dhabi.

Global PhD students complete the program coursework in New York City (1-2 years) before coming to NYUAD to complete their research and thesis.

To apply for the NYUAD Global PhD Student Fellowship use the application for the New York program and indicate your preference to conduct research at NYUAD. Applications marked with this preference are shared with NYUAD program faculty. Applications open in mid-September for the following fall intake.








Key Features of the Global Fellowship PhD Programs

- New York University degree upon graduation
- Access to the extraordinary resources at NYU
- Graduate coursework in New York
- Cutting-edge research opportunities in NYU Abu Dhabi’s labs
- Tuition, fees, and health insurance provided throughout the program
- Generous research assistantship and stipend provided by NYU Abu Dhabi throughout the program
- Assistance for degree-related travel between Abu Dhabi and New York
- Campus accommodation at no cost in Abu Dhabi
- A contribution toward accommodation costs in New York
- Career development assistance at both campuses

title: Global PhD Student Fellowship in Biology
breadcrumbs: Global PhD Student Fellowship in Biology
text:
Global PhD Student Fellowship in Biology





The NYU Abu Dhabi Global PhD Student Fellowship in Biology is offered in collaboration with the Graduate School of Arts and Science at NYU New York. The program offers training in a broad range of biological research fields, including developmental genetics, genomics and systems biology, molecular and cellular biology, evolutionary biology, and infectious disease.

The program generally involves one to two years of classwork at NYU New York, followed by three to four years of research at NYU Abu Dhabi. If selected, the doctorate is fully funded under the NYU Abu Dhabi Global PhD Student Fellowship.














Key Features of the Fellowship

- New York University degree upon graduation
- Access to the extraordinary resources of the NYU Graduate School of Arts and Science
- Graduate coursework in New York
- Cutting-edge research opportunities in NYU Abu Dhabi’s labs
- Tuition, fees, and health insurance provided throughout the program
- Generous research assistantship and stipend provided by NYU Abu Dhabi throughout the program
- Assistance for degree-related travel between Abu Dhabi and New York
- Campus accommodation at no cost in Abu Dhabi
- A contribution toward accommodation costs in New York
- Career development assistance at both campuses








Learn How to Apply

Applications open in mid-September for the following Fall intake















Our Research

See where you can do biology research at NYU Abu Dhabi.








What happens in the NYU Department of Biology?

Offers training in a broad range of biological research fields, including developmental genetics, genomics and systems biology, molecular and cellular biology, evolutionary biology, and infectious disease.








Biology PhD at NYU

Find out more information about NYU's requirements for a PhD in Biology














Graduate Student Highlight










PhD Student Shares Her Wonder of Biology

Biology is Momal Taimoor’s lens to understanding the world. That perspective has led her to pursuing a PhD in biology as a Global PhD Fellow at NYU Abu Dhabi and to author a children’s book about science.








"For a researcher, it's a dream come true"

Biology student Wael Abdrabou can quickly process data from his fieldwork in Burkina Faso because of NYU Abu Dhabi’s excellent lab facilities.








Finding the right research environment

PhD fellow Patrice Delaney grew up on an island, so she has always been interested in studying our natural world.

sections.title: Global PhD Student Fellowship in Biology
sections.text:
Global PhD Student Fellowship in Biology





The NYU Abu Dhabi Global PhD Student Fellowship in Biology is offered in collaboration with the Graduate School of Arts and Science at NYU New York. The program offers training in a broad range of biological research fields, including developmental genetics, genomics and systems biology, molecular and cellular biology, evolutionary biology, and infectious disease.

The program generally involves one to two years of classwork at NYU New York, followed by three to four years of research at NYU Abu Dhabi. If selected, the doctorate is fully funded under the NYU Abu Dhabi Global PhD Student Fellowship.

sections.title: Key Features of the Fellowship
sections.text:
- New York University degree upon graduation
- Access to the extraordinary resources of the NYU Graduate School of Arts and Science
- Graduate coursework in New York
- Cutting-edge research opportunities in NYU Abu Dhabi’s labs
- Tuition, fees, and health insurance provided throughout the program
- Generous research assistantship and stipend provided by NYU Abu Dhabi throughout the program
- Assistance for degree-related travel between Abu Dhabi and New York
- Campus accommodation at no cost in Abu Dhabi
- A contribution toward accommodation costs in New York
- Career development assistance at both campuses

title: Application Process
breadcrumbs: Global PhD Student Fellowship in Biology
text:
Application Process





Graduate Studies in the Arts & Sciences (GSAS) Fellowship candidates apply using the standard online application for admission to a GSAS PhD program. There is no separate application for the NYUAD Global PhD Student Fellowship. Interested students should indicate their preference for conducting research at NYUAD in their PhD application to the GSAS.

Applicants will be notified of their Fellowship status upon acceptance to NYU, or as soon as possible thereafter.

Selection

Selection for the NYUAD Global PhD Student Fellowship is highly competitive, and faculty at NYU and NYUAD will take a range of factors into consideration. This may include past academic performance, test scores, recommendation letters, and research compatibility, among other criteria.

Application Deadline

Applications open in mid-September for the following fall intake. The application deadline is typically between December 1 and December 15 for the following fall intake. Please note that applications are only accepted for the fall semester, as we do not offer spring admission.

Visit the GSAS Application Resource Center for more information on how to apply.

title: Research
breadcrumbs: Global PhD Student Fellowship in Biology
text:
Research






NYUAD Biology Labs










Laboratory of Algal, Systems, and Synthetic Biology

Our group aims to explore fundamental questions on evolution, phenotype-genotype relations, and metabolism of algae. We use Chlamydomonas reinhardtii as a model organism to explore these questions at systems level and extend our findings to other algae that we ourselves are isolating from the UAE and other locations.








The Idaghdour Lab

The Idaghdour laboratory uses statistical genetic methods and multiple types of high-throughput genomic data including genome sequencing, epigenetic and transcriptomic profiling, proteomics and metabolomics to study these interactions in the human circulating immune system.








Marine Microbial Ecology

Research in the Amin lab focuses on how marine microbes interact with each other and with their environment. To study these interactions in a complex environmental setting, a wide variety of chemical and biological techniques are utilized including metabolomics, genomics, natural product characterization, and coordination chemistry.














Research Highlights

Exciting research is happening at NYU Abu Dhabi.










Is Our Environment Contributing to Fatty Liver Disease?

Arsenic — a naturally occurring environmental toxicant — causes fatty liver disease in zebrafish, says biologist Kirsten Sadler Edepli.










Increased Sulfur Metabolism is a Likely Survival Mechanism for UAE Algae

Biologist Kourosh Salehi-Ashtiani sheds light on how algae’s potential adaptations in the region have evolved to cope with environmental conditions, such as drought and salinity.










All Things Must Adapt

As environments change, so do the plants, animals, and people living in them, say biologists Stéphane Boissinot, Shady Amin, and Youssef Idaghdour.




















Fighting Malaria

Researchers including Youssef Idaghdour traveled to Burkina Faso to figure out how genetics might be responsible for the wide variation in the severity of the disease.

title: Finding the Right Research Environment
breadcrumbs: Global PhD Student Fellowship in Biology
text:
Finding the Right Research Environment






PhD researcher Patrice Delaney grew up on an island, so she has always been interested in studying the natural world







Humans, plants, and animals all live in a chemically rich environment. Most of what we’re exposed to is harmless, but some toxins can cause disease.

Arsenic, for example, occurs naturally in groundwater. In places where water is unfiltered, people can be exposed to levels that exceed the safety threshold set by the World Health Organization.

Patrice Delaney, a Global PhD Fellow in Biology , and the research team in the Sadler Edepli Lab at NYU Abu Dhabi are investigating how pollutants in the environment could affect our health.

Patrice’s interest in environmental toxicology stems from childhood growing up on an island - City Island - located in the Bronx of New York City. “I’ve always been interested in marine life,” she says.

As a young biology major at college in New York, Patrice chanced upon an internship at NYU Abu Dhabi with Associate Professor of Biology John Burt , who works on coral reef ecology research in the Arabian Gulf. The internship at NYUAD solidified Patrice’s interest in pursuing environmental biology. So she finished college in New York and applied for the Global PhD Fellowship at NYU Abu Dhabi.



In terms of resources for science, NYUAD is a no brainer for me.









Working With Advisors

NYUAD’s five-year fellowship programs unite students with experienced faculty advisors from both Abu Dhabi and NYU New York.

Face-to-face time with faculty and constant feedback is particularly important in the lab environment, Patrice says. She and Professor Kirsten Sadler Edepli connect almost daily to review data and see how things are going. Easy access to advanced research equipment is helpful too.

Advice For Prospective Graduates

- Know yourself and your work style is, then find an advisor that fits that.
- Talk to current members of the lab and use them as a model. If that’s a good fit, then it’s probably the right direction.
- Be proactive. It's going to be five years of your life.

Related Videos






























A study from NYU Abu Dhabi shows that exposure to arsenic — a common compound present naturally in the Earth’s crust that is lethal to those exposed to high levels — causes fatty liver disease in zebrafish.
























NYU Abu Dhabi, on Abu Dhabi's Saadiyat Island, sits only about a kilometer away from a massive coral reef that's trying to survive some of the most extreme environmental conditions in the world.

title: “For a researcher, it’s a dream come true.”
breadcrumbs: Global PhD Student Fellowship in Biology
text:
“For a researcher, it’s a dream come true.”






PhD biology student Wael Abdrabou can quickly process data from his fieldwork in Burkina Faso because of NYU Abu Dhabi’s excellent lab facilities







Sweating through the humidity some 35 kilometers from Ouagadougou in Burkina Faso, Wael Abdrabou and his colleagues from NYU Abu Dhabi concentrate on drawing a blood sample from a child. Abdrabou and the team of researchers travel to the west African country often to study the impact of malaria on local children.

With more than two million cases of malaria detected in 2015, the nationwide epidemic requires urgent attention. Abdrabou, a Global PhD Fellow in Biology , is trying to figure out why the responses to malaria differs from one child to another and from one ethnic group to another. Children between 2 and 12 are the most commonly affected group.

Before and After Malaria













The team draws samples from unaffected children before the rainy season, followed up during major transmission season, and then gather samples from children who are found to be infected.

With so many variables including ethnic background and age, Abdrabou is trying to address a lot of factors through different biological approaches such as metabolomic, transcriptomic, and genotype profiling.

“I’m grateful to be able to work on all these omics data and pursue something novel attempting to integrate between all of them in the context of malaria... It’s a huge project,” he said.




















Thanks to research funding from NYUAD, Abdrabou and his colleagues can afford to study the complete metabolic profiles of small molecules (metabolites) in young children and investigate the role and impact these metabolites have on the progression of infection. They use different approaches to study both hosts and parasites at a metabolome and genome-wide level.

“For a researcher, it’s a dream come true,” Abdrabou said. Not needing to wait for equipment means Abdrabou can run sample tests quickly and easily. “This lab for me has the right resources to learn as well as to expand and further advance my research,” he added.

“The graduate program is set up in a really interesting way.”

PhD fellows at NYUAD get to study their courses at the New York campus for a year, and then come back to Abu Dhabi to complete their project.

“You get exposed to two great campuses: one in New York, and one in Abu Dhabi,” Abdrabou explained. The Egyptian who moved to the United States over 20 years ago thinks the location of NYUAD is ideal: “I get an American education in a land I really enjoy being in.”

Finding the Right Mentor

Looking at the research Idaghdour Lab got Abdrabou excited about working on diverse omics data and other projects with Assistant Professor of Biology Youssef Idaghdour .

“Your mentor is like a compass. He directs you towards the right direction… and that’s how I feel with Professor Youssef.” Wael Abdrabou, Global PhD Fellow in Biology

Abdrabou also says while it’s good to have a starting point to your research, he has learned that things can change, especially once you’ve had an in-depth conversation with your mentor. “A mentor who will push you to do things that are outside of the norm.”

“I feel treated like a postdoc rather than PhD student.”

As a graduate student, Abdrabou gets to work on things that are usually reserved for postdoctoral students such as writing grants, and doing Institutional Review Board approval for doing research work. “Professor Youssef trusts me with these projects… and gives me a lot of control,” Abdrabou said.

All these added responsibilities has helped Abdrabou become familiar with establishing studies from the start and getting approvals.

During his time at NYUAD, Abdrabou was also published in Nature Metabolism and also received the NYU Charlotte Pann Research Award for senior doctoral student who has demonstrated outstanding research accomplishments and potential.

“This kind of experience prepares me for what’s next."














Related Video
























NYU Abu Dhabi works closely with researchers in Burkina Faso to figure how genetics might be responsible for the wide variation in the severity of malaria.

title: Structure and Schedule
breadcrumbs: Global PhD Student Fellowship in Biology
text:
Structure and Schedule





Global PhD Students complete all degree requirements set by GSAS and the respective NYU Department. The following is a typical sequence for students, but each student’s course of study will be determined in consultation with his or her faculty advisor and the department’s Director of Graduate Studies.

Term Sequence, Locations, and Degree Phases

Summer 1 in Abu Dhabi

Orientation for students will usually occur at the end of July, and students will remain in Abu Dhabi over the next month to complete the UAE visa process before heading to New York.

Year 1 in New York — Coursework and Lab Rotations

Students begin their coursework in New York. Interested students conduct a lab rotation in Abu Dhabi during this phase, giving them the chance to become acquainted with NYUAD and potential faculty advisors.

End of Year 1 — Research Location Selection

By the end of Year 1, students secure an eligible NYUAD faculty member’s endorsement for conducting dissertation research in an Abu Dhabi lab. If the selection is approved by the NYU department and the NYUAD graduate committee, the student will be offered a Global PhD Student placement.

Summer 2 in Abu Dhabi — Research

Global PhD Students spend the summer in Abu Dhabi to obtain their UAE visas and conduct directed research with their faculty advisors.

Year 2 in New York or Abu Dhabi — Coursework or Research

Students finalize coursework and exams in New York, or pursue research in Abu Dhabi as needed.

Year 3 and Beyond in Abu Dhabi — Completion of Thesis, Research, and Dissertation

Students prepare their dissertations in Abu Dhabi under their advisors' direction.

Dissertation Defense in New York or Abu Dhabi

Defense location will depend upon committee makeup and any departmental requirements.







Contact Us

For more information about our programs, please contact nyuad.graduateadmissions@nyu.edu .

sections.title: Term Sequence, Locations, and Degree Phases
sections.text:
Summer 1 in Abu Dhabi

Orientation for students will usually occur at the end of July, and students will remain in Abu Dhabi over the next month to complete the UAE visa process before heading to New York.

Year 1 in New York — Coursework and Lab Rotations

Students begin their coursework in New York. Interested students conduct a lab rotation in Abu Dhabi during this phase, giving them the chance to become acquainted with NYUAD and potential faculty advisors.

End of Year 1 — Research Location Selection

By the end of Year 1, students secure an eligible NYUAD faculty member’s endorsement for conducting dissertation research in an Abu Dhabi lab. If the selection is approved by the NYU department and the NYUAD graduate committee, the student will be offered a Global PhD Student placement.

Summer 2 in Abu Dhabi — Research

Global PhD Students spend the summer in Abu Dhabi to obtain their UAE visas and conduct directed research with their faculty advisors.

Year 2 in New York or Abu Dhabi — Coursework or Research

Students finalize coursework and exams in New York, or pursue research in Abu Dhabi as needed.

Year 3 and Beyond in Abu Dhabi — Completion of Thesis, Research, and Dissertation

Students prepare their dissertations in Abu Dhabi under their advisors' direction.

Dissertation Defense in New York or Abu Dhabi

Defense location will depend upon committee makeup and any departmental requirements.

title: Application Process
breadcrumbs: Global PhD Student Fellowship in Biomedical Engineering
text:
Application Process





Engineering Fellowship candidates apply using the standard NYU Tandon School of Engineering online application for admission to an Engineering PhD program. There is no separate application for the NYUAD Global PhD Student Fellowship. Interested students should indicate their preference for conducting research at NYUAD in their PhD application to the School of Engineering.

Applicants will be notified of their Fellowship status upon acceptance to NYU, or as soon as possible thereafter.

Selection for the NYUAD Global PhD Student Fellowship is highly competitive, and faculty at NYU and NYUAD will take a range of factors into consideration. This may include past academic performance, test scores, recommendation letters, and research compatibility, among other criteria.

Applications usually open in mid-September for the following fall intake. The application deadline is typically December 1 for the following fall intake. Please note that applications are only accepted for the fall semester, as we do not offer Spring admission.

Application Requirements

The School of Engineering Graduate Admissions website has more information on the PhD application process, including requirements, deadlines, and other useful tips. There is no separate application for the NYUAD Global PhD Student Fellowship.

Please note that candidates in Engineering can only be considered for the Fellowship if they will hold a relevant master's degree before enrolling. Candidates who will not have a master's degree are still welcome to apply for the NYU School of Engineering PhD, but cannot be considered for the Fellowship until they have earned the equivalent of a master's degree.

Specific PhD application requirements vary by department. In general, you will be asked to provide:

- online application form
- application fee
- official transcripts, with English translations if applicable
- statement of purpose
- resume of curriculum vitae
- letters of recommendation
- proof of English proficiency, if applicable
Current NYU PhD students in Engineering may be eligible to apply for the fellowship. All interested students should contact their departments and the NYUAD Graduate Programs Office for further information.

Expectations from Fellowship Recipients

Fellowship recipients are expected to maintain a cumulative grade point average of 3.0 or better for continued financial support, meet Graduate School and departmental standards of satisfactory academic progress, and remain in good standing with their School of Engineering department.

NYUAD Global PhD students must obtain a US student visa to enroll at the School of Engineering, and a UAE residency visa to receive NYUAD funding. Fellowship recipients will be provided with additional information.

title: Research
breadcrumbs: Global PhD Student Fellowship in Biomedical Engineering
text:
Research






NYUAD Biomedical Engineering Labs










Advanced Microfluidics and Microdevices Laboratory

AMMLab is currently working with diverse facets of miniaturization and integration in biology, life sciences, and medicine, which includes the conception, engineering, and utilization of novel micro and nanotechnologies to manipulate, stimulate and study biological entities.










Clinical Artificial Intelligence Lab

Supporting clinical decision-making using AI, data science, and machine learning driven tools.








Integrated BioElectronics Laboratory

The Integrated BioElectronics Lab aims at advancing the engineering and applications of silicon integrated technology interfacing with biology in a variety of forms ranging from implantable biomedical devices to unobtrusive wearable sensors.


















Laboratory for Advanced Bio-Photonics and Imaging (LAB-π)

Focused on the development and clinical translation of smart devices for medical imaging, diagnostics, and monitoring using novel optical technologies








Laboratory for Advanced Neuroengineering and Translational Medicine

The Ramadi Lab for Advanced Neuroengineering and Translational Medicine develops innovative approaches for the modulation of neural activity throughout the body. We combine mechanical, electrical, materials, and bio-engineering toolkits towards designing minimally invasive technologies for neuromodulation.












Laboratory for Immuno Bioengineering Research and Applications (LIBRA)

Deciphering the role of mechanical factors on immune cells through basic research, to unveil new insights into immune homeostasis and dysregulation for innovative translational applications. Our team achieve this overall goal through the use of model systems that integrates Immuno-mechanobiology, Microenvironment Mimicry, and Video-omics.
















Reverse Bioengineering Lab

Revolutionizing biomedical engineering by reconstructing complete human and animal bodies using cutting-edge engineering techniques - Reverse Bioengineering.








Micro- and Nanoscale Bioengineering Lab

Our research areas include liquid biopsy 
on microfluidic biochips and high throughput drug screening using whole 
model organisms such C. elegans .













NetBio Group

Blending theory with experiments, we focus on the behavior of networks with particular emphasis on synthetic biology applications.


















The Vijay Lab

3D Printing and Bioprinting for tissue engineering, regenerative medicine, drug testing, and medical devices


























Research Highlight

Exciting research is happening at NYU Abu Dhabi.










Print and Probe

Mohammad Qasaimeh explains how 3D printers could improve access to technologies essential for scientific discovery.

Applications usually open in mid-September for the following fall intake. The application deadline is typically December 1 for the following fall intake. Please note that applications are only accepted for the fall semester, as we do not offer Spring admission.

Application Requirements

The School of Engineering Graduate Admissions website has more information on the PhD application process, including requirements, deadlines, and other useful tips. There is no separate application for the NYUAD Global PhD Student Fellowship.

Please note that candidates in Engineering can only be considered for the Fellowship if they will hold a relevant master's degree before enrolling. Candidates who will not have a master's degree are still welcome to apply for the NYU School of Engineering PhD, but cannot be considered for the Fellowship until they have earned the equivalent of a master's degree.

Specific PhD application requirements vary by department. In general, you will be asked to provide:

- online application form
- application fee
- official transcripts, with English translations if applicable
- statement of purpose
- resume of curriculum vitae
- letters of recommendation
- proof of English proficiency, if applicable
Current NYU PhD students in Engineering may be eligible to apply for the fellowship. All interested students should contact their departments and the NYUAD Graduate Programs Office for further information.

Expectations from Fellowship Recipients

Fellowship recipients are expected to maintain a cumulative grade point average of 3.0 or better for continued financial support, meet Graduate School and departmental standards of satisfactory academic progress, and remain in good standing with their School of Engineering department.

NYUAD Global PhD students must obtain a US student visa to enroll at the School of Engineering, and a UAE residency visa to receive NYUAD funding. Fellowship recipients will be provided with additional information.

text:
Research






NYUAD Chemical Engineering Labs










Micro- and Nanoscale Bioengineering Lab

The lab's primary research interests encompass various aspects of micro- and nanoscale bioengineering, including biosensors, point-of-care diagnostics, organ-on-a-chip systems, medical devices, and biomimetics.








NetBio Group

Blending theory with experiments, we focus on the behavior of networks with particular emphasis on synthetic biology applications.








Water Research Center

Promoting innovative research in water desalination, wastewater treatment, environmental policy, and social issues that will lead to water security and sustainability.














Research Highlight

Exciting research is happening at NYU Abu Dhabi.










Solved: Mystery of the Lizard Tail

In a new study published in the journal Science, a team of researchers led by NYUAD Associate Professor of Mechanical Engineering and Bioengineering Yong-Ak (Rafael) Song, presents the first-ever rigorous biophysical model of lizard tail autotomy.

breadcrumbs: Global PhD Student Fellowship in Chemical Engineering
text:
Structure and Schedule















Global PhD Students complete all degree requirements set by the NYU Tandon School of Engineering department they are admitted in.

The following is a typical degree sequence, but each student’s course of study will be determined in consultation with his or her faculty advisor and the department’s Director of Graduate Studies. Most students participate in their fellowship for a duration of 4-5 years.


































Summer One in Abu Dhabi

Before starting classes in New York, students spend 4-6 weeks in Abu Dhabi to obtain their UAE visas and familiarize themselves with the campus, labs, and faculty.













Year One in New York

Students undertake coursework with their Department in New York.













J-Term and Summer Term in Abu Dhabi

During the first year, students return to Abu Dhabi for the January and summer terms, to maintain their UAE residency status and pursue research with their advisors.





















Year Two and Onward in New York or Abu Dhabi

Most students will spend this year in Abu Dhabi conducting research with their advisors. Some may return to New York for an additional semester, if needed.













Dissertation Defense in New York or Abu Dhabi

Defense location will depend upon committee makeup and any departmental requirements

title: Global PhD Student Fellowship in Chemistry
breadcrumbs: Global PhD Student Fellowship in Chemistry
text:
Global PhD Student Fellowship in Chemistry





The NYU Abu Dhabi Global PhD Student Fellowship in Chemistry is offered in collaboration with the Graduate School of Arts and Science at NYU New York.

The program generally involves one to two years of classwork at NYU New York, followed by three to four years of research at NYU Abu Dhabi. If selected, the doctorate is fully funded under the NYU Abu Dhabi Global PhD Student Fellowship.














Key Features of the Fellowship

- New York University degree upon graduation
- Access to the extraordinary resources of the NYU Graduate School of Arts and Science
- Graduate coursework in New York
- Cutting-edge research opportunities in NYU Abu Dhabi’s labs
- Tuition, fees, and health insurance provided throughout the program
- Generous research assistantship and stipend provided by NYU Abu Dhabi throughout the program
- Assistance for degree-related travel between Abu Dhabi and New York
- Campus accommodation at no cost in Abu Dhabi
- A contribution toward accommodation costs in New York
- Career development assistance at both campuses








Learn How to Apply

Applications open in mid-September for the following Fall intake.















Our Research

See where you can do chemistry research at NYU Abu Dhabi.










Graduate Chemisty at NYU

Make discoveries in all fields of Chemistry, including biophysical, chemical biology, inorganic, materials, organic, physical, and theory.








NYU Department of Chemistry

Benefit from a highly interdisciplinary and collaborative environment, including strong interactions within NYU units in New York, Abu Dhabi and Shanghai.














Graduate Student Highlights










Advancing Organic Synthesis Through a Global PhD Fellowship

With a foundation in organic synthesis, Global PhD Fellow Thowfik Salam joins NYUAD to advance research at the intersection of chemistry, innovation, and interdisciplinary collaboration.








More Than Just Research Work

Wegood Awad, NYU Abu Dhabi global PhD fellow in chemistry, shows how her graduate studies went beyond lab work and publications.








Strong Relationships and Communication

"I absolutely loved exploring New York during my free time, but my favorite part of my time at NYU Abu Dhabi has been the richness of our Chemistry department."

For more information about our programs, please contact nyuad.graduateadmissions@nyu.edu .

text:
Research






NYUAD Chemistry Labs










Naumov Group

The Smart Materials Lab is the leading team with regards to chemistry research in the UAE, with research output that, according to the Nature Index, accounts for an impressive 63 percent in 2015 and 67 percent in 2016 of the total chemistry publications from groups within the country, both in the fractional count and weighted fractional count.








Trabolsi Research Group

The Trabolsi Research Group designs and develops smart materials to tackle two of today’s biggest challenges: better healthcare and clean water for all. Our research group brings together chemistry, nanoscience, and materials engineering to turn scientific discovery into real-world solutions.








Healy Lab

The Healy lab's mission is to harness the tools of bioinformatics, automated synthesis and high-throughput screening to streamline the process from natural product gene cluster to preclinical drug candidate.


















Kirmizialtin Lab

The Kirmizialtin Lab operates at the intersection of physical chemistry, molecular simulation, and data science. The group develops methods that enhance the accuracy and efficiency of simulations and applies them to challenges in biology, chemistry, and materials science. The group develops physical models and high-fidelity simulations to investigate the interactions between biomolecules and their binding partners. A major focus integrates computation with experimental data through machine learning.








Life Molecules and Materials Lab

The Life Molecules and Materials Lab investigates the physical principles by which biomolecules self-organize to orchestrate cellular functions such as signaling, molecular sorting, and information processing. Our primary interests lie in proteins, lipids, and nucleic acids. We employ single-molecule optical tweezers to dissect the folding and assembly of proteins and RNA, and advanced light microscopy to study biomolecular phase separation under crowded, cytoplasm-like conditions.








Materials NMR Lab

The Materials NMR Lab addresses the challenges of climate change and the demand for energy by using solid-state Nuclear Magnetic Resonance (NMR) spectroscopy as a primary tool. Research themes: 1. Utilizing solid-state NMR to understand the structure-property relationships in less ordered systems with unique optoelectronic properties. 2. Endogenous Dynamic Nuclear Polarization 3. Developing NMR methodology to understand the mechanism of heterogeneous catalysis.
















Amatov CatalySIS Lab

The Amatov CatalySIS lab develops chemistry that is not only conceptually interesting and fundamentally novel but also offers robust solutions for sustainable synthesis. The lab develops new synthetic methods and catalytic processes using redox-active organic molecules that simultaneously mimic transition metals, photoredox catalysts, and even enzymes in useful transformations. Particular interest is given to designing and using persistent organic radicals as redox-active catalytic platforms.


























Research Highlights

Exciting research is happening at NYU Abu Dhabi.










Bright Hot Crystals

Led by Panče Naumov, NYUAD researchers achieve solid state Thermochemiluminescence with crystals that emit light when heated.










Mother Nature's Untapped Healing Potential

Natural product research is seeing a renaissance, Kristin Gunsalus explains.
