title: NYU Tulsa FAQs · NYUAD Students
text:
NYU Tulsa FAQ's for Engineering Students

(As of November 2025)

Academics and Course Enrollment

Q: How many courses am I permitted to take in spring 2026 as part of the NYU Tulsa program?

A: Students must maintain full-time status by being enrolled in at least 12 credits overall. To maintain legal F-1 visa status, students must be enrolled in at least 12 credits overall, and 16 credits are needed to stay on track for graduation. The typical semester class schedule includes two courses offered at NYU Tulsa (minimum 8 credits) and two courses offered at the University of Tulsa. To be eligible for the F-1 student visa from NYU, students must enroll in at least 8 credits at NYU Tulsa.

Q: How do credit hours work for courses taken at the University of Tulsa (TU) as NYUAD course equivalencies?

A: Engineering elective equivalencies can be found here . Courses marked as equivalencies will be counted regardless of credit hour discrepancies. Some University of Tulsa courses are three credits instead of the typical NYUAD four-credit courses, but this still counts as an equivalency as long as the course is marked as approved. Engineering elective equivalencies can be found elsewhere.

Q: Can I take courses at the University of Tulsa as general electives?

A: Please email us the courses you are interested in taking so that the relevant program faculty can review them.

Q: How will I enroll in University of Tulsa (TU) courses?

A: Students should have completed the pre-registration form through the Study Away Portal. TU course registration is different from NYU’s registration process. TU staff will review students' course preferences and determine their eligibility to enroll based on prerequisites and co-requisites, which can be found under each course listing. Once you have been enrolled in a TU course, the NYU Global Academics team will provide you with your TU enrollment and class schedule. As an NYU Abu Dhabi student, the courses you take at TU must be approved by the relevant NYU Abu Dhabi Engineering program.

If you have questions about equivalencies, please email nyuad.tulsastudyaway@nyu.edu

Q: May I take a third engineering course at the University of Tulsa (TU) (i.e., may I take five classes in total?)

A: This may be possible within the parameters of the NYUAD Overload policy, but students will have to request pre-approval. The maximum number of credits NYU students can take at the University of Tulsa is 9.

Q: I don’t see a track for Civil Engineering students – can I study Civil Engineering at the University of Tulsa?

A: Currently, the University of Tulsa does not offer Civil Engineering courses. If students are on track with their major requirements, they might be able to work out a plan allowing them to take other relevant classes at NYU Tulsa and TU that will help them make meaningful progress in their degree.

Q: Are there NYU Tulsa courses that are approved to count as NYUAD Core courses?

A: Yes, approved Core course equivalencies are offered in both the fall and spring semesters. These include:

Cultural Exploration & Analysis (CCEA)

CORE-UA 9700 : Expressive Culture: Topics: Native Arts in Contemporary America

Cultural & Artistic Practices (CDAD)

SOC-UA 9970 / UPADM-GP 9410 : Topics: Revitalizing the American City: Challenges and Strategies for Vibrant and Inclusive Development

S tructures, Thought, & Society (CSTS)

IDSEM-UG 9700 / SOC-UA 9970 : Black Capitalism and the Quest for Economic Freedom in America

POL-UA 9994 / UPADM-GP 9227 : Topics: Constructive Policymaking at the Subnational Level

The Engineering Industry Challenge Course and Internship Opportunities

Q: What is the Industry Challenge course, and who will I work with?

A: The Industry Challenge is a practical project that engages students with a real-world challenge in the clean energy industry. It is embedded in a 4-credit NYU Tulsa course that counts as a general engineering elective. Engineering students must enroll in this 4-credit course.

Course Title: American Clean Energy Industry: Case Study Tulsa (ENGR-UH 3190).

Industry Partnerships: The course will partner with two companies: Aimright Testing & Engineering and Sun Wolf Equipment Repair.

Course Description: This course explores the global and American energy industries and the shift from fossil fuels to green energy through scientific, economic, policy, and ethical lenses. Emphasizing Tulsa’s significant role in the American energy industry, it covers the structure and history of the energy sector, renewable energy technologies, and the economics of transitioning to green energy. The course explores how politics, public policy, international agreements, and ethical considerations influence the energy landscape, utilizing Tulsa as a case study to examine local impacts and strategies. In a major assignment for the class, the students will collaborate on a semester-long industry challenge with a local energy-focused company.

Q: Can I intern with a company outside of the Industry Challenge course during the semester?

A: No, engineering students must be enrolled in the Industry Challenge course, which serves as their internship opportunity during the semester at NYU Tulsa.

Q: I’m interested in interning in Tulsa over the summer. Am I guaranteed an opportunity?

A: Placement in a specific industry or company cannot be guaranteed. Students must apply and be selected. Students enrolled at NYU Tulsa for the Spring 2026 semester may be eligible to apply for an unpaid summer internship in Tulsa, depending on the visa regulations in effect at the time. The priority deadline for summer internships is March 15.

Q: How does Curricular Practical Training (CPT) work for me if I study away for the entire academic year?

A: Based on current US F-1 visa regulations, students enrolled in the United States for the entire 2025-2026 academic year (e.g., Fall 2025 at NYU New York, and Spring 2026 at NYU Tulsa) will be eligible to apply for CPT if they secure a qualifying summer experience for Summer 2026. Students are required to enroll in the NYUAD summer directed study course. Opportunities outside of Tulsa are not possible due to visa regulations.

Q: Can NYU students engage in research projects in labs at the University of Tulsa?

A: Currently, this is not possible.

Financial Aid and Scholarships

Q: H ow does financial aid work while I’m studying away?

A: During your semester abroad, NYUAD will bill you the same full-time tuition and insurance rate fees as when studying in Abu Dhabi. You will not be charged for the NYUAD mandatory book fee, Abu Dhabi housing, or Abu Dhabi meal plan costs. However, you will incur charges for room and board based on the housing assigned to you by NYU Tulsa.

The financial aid coverage remains the same as when you are studying in Abu Dhabi. For example, if you are on a full-aid scholarship, your room costs will be covered up to the published housing cap rate for your study away site. If you receive partial support for housing, the same amount will be applied to your account. If you receive no housing support, the full housing amount will be charged to your student bill and will be your responsibility to cover.

Q: What is the $6,000 USD NYU Tulsa Scholarship, and who is eligible for it?

A: All NYU Abu Dhabi students enrolled at NYU Tulsa for the spring 2026 semester will receive an additional scholarship of $6,000 USD. This scholarship is separate from any existing financial support from NYU Abu Dhabi and is made possible by the generous support from the George Kaiser Family Foundation. It is in addition to the study away allowance students may receive.

Q: How is the $6,000 USD NYU Tulsa scholarship distributed?

A: The $6,000 USD scholarship will first be applied to any outstanding balance on your semester bill. Once there is no remaining balance, the remainder of the $6,000 US dollars will be refunded to you.

Q: Are there tax implications for the $6,000 scholarship?

A: You need to check with the Financial Aid Office for specific guidance on tax implications.

Q: Is there additional funding available for the semester?

A. While NYU Tulsa offers a scale of financial aid for enrolled students, NYU Abu Dhabi students enrolled at NYU Tulsa will all receive the $6,000 USD additional scholarship described above.

Q: How will financial support work for the summer if I remain in Tulsa for an internship?

A: If you secure a summer internship in Tulsa, you will follow the established summer funding process through the Career Development Center. Students should plan to apply for the NYUAD CDC Summer Internship Grant if they need University funding, noting that funding is competitive and not guaranteed. Students are not eligible for the NYU Tulsa Scholarship in the summer.

Housing and Campus Life Arrangements

Q: Is housing fully covered for me while I’m enrolled at NYU Tulsa for the semester?

A: If your financial aid package covers housing in Abu Dhabi, NYUAD will cover shared accommodation up to the standard rate in the program-approved housing at NYU Tulsa. Single accommodation is only possible if you are registered with and approved by the Moses Center through its established process. If you choose to reside in a single room without meeting the Moses Center conditions, you should expect to cover the difference in cost for the single room. Financial aid will not cover this additional cost.

If you receive partial financial support, the support value for housing does not change while you study away or even if you have an approved Moses Center housing accommodation.

Read more above about the additional $6,000 USD scholarship for students enrolled in NYU Tulsa.

Q: What types of housing are available at NYU Tulsa?

A: NYU-arranged housing is guaranteed and required as part of the study away program. Student housing is arranged in apartments, with most living in shared double-room spaces. The facilities are located in the heart of the city, in the Blue Dome District. Students can easily commute to classes (about a 15–20 minute walk to the NYU Tulsa Academic Center).

Q: Does the University of Tulsa partnership allow NYU students to use their facilities?

A: Yes, NYU students can use student facilities at the University of Tulsa.

Related official links:
https://students.nyuad.nyu.edu/academics/global-education/study-away/study-away-guidelines/

title: Study Abroad Pathways · NYUAD Students
text:
NYUAD deans and faculty have identified site preferences within the NYU global network for NYUAD majors with an eye toward developing students as well-rounded scholars of the liberal arts and sciences, highly competent producers of knowledge in a field of specialization, and socially responsible members of any community they choose to join.

Key factors for selecting site preferences include the following:

- Connecting majors to existing site strengths and local assets

This includes considering

- Current and projected Study Abroad site strength and capacity over time

- The availability or likelihood of availability of local facilities (e.g., laboratories)

- Collaborating with renowned local research institutions or projects through the local sites and new NYU centers of research excellence

- Teaming with outstanding site faculty on courses or undergraduate research projects

- The availability of or possibility for local internships in pre-professional settings or research projects in labs for majors

- Developing collaborative teaching and research projects with stellar departments of local universities

- NYUAD faculty mobility opportunities at the site and in relation to coordination of course offerings

- Developing students as scholars in their fields of specialization

This includes incorporating what students study abroad into:

- The sequence of knowledge and skill development within the major specific to their semester abroad

- Training for discipline-specific research (e.g., methods of inquiry, fieldwork, laboratory work) or creative production in the arts

- The possibility of taking or staging courses that explore important interdisciplinary questions related to the major

- The availability of direct enrollment courses at outstanding local universities

- Preparation for Capstone projects (e.g., data collection, pilot projects, comparative work, access to archives and collections)

- Strategic positioning for graduate school and prestigious fellowships

- Developing students as well-rounded scholars and global citizens within the liberal arts and sciences tradition

- Offering liberal arts and sciences core course experiences abroad that continue to explore "big questions" from a global perspective while placing those perspectives into specific local context

- Providing students with a broader range of electives across the liberal arts and sciences than is possible at NYUAD alone

- Guiding students through courses, co-curricular activity, and experiential learning opportunities toward developing greater intercultural understanding toward social responsibility:

- How to create social ties across difference, including recognizing boundaries and deference behaviors common to the community students are engaging

- Developing the language and socio-linguistic behaviors needed in that community to create social ties, navigate boundaries and apply deference behaviors

- How to access, elicit, interpret, and generate knowledge with ethical intelligence within the culture(s) of that community

- How to respect a variety of knowers and ways of knowing in the host community, i.e., appreciating and applying epistemological diversity

- How to reflect critically on their own positionally (e.g., personal identity, socio-cultural identity, political identity)

- How to foster and convey empathy in the face of difference

- How to hold the tension of the opposites within formal and informal community contexts to create a safe and productive space for dialogue

Study Abroad Pathways by Major

These paths represent general directions for study away in the major. Students will work with their faculty mentors to determine what is appropriate for their individual academic program.

- Arab Crossroads

Recommended Global Sites

Sophomore Spring | Junior Fall

NYU New York | NYU New York

Requirements

-
Recommended semesters for study abroad are Sophomore Spring and/or Junior Fall.

-
Students should be on campus in Abu Dhabi in the spring of the junior year to work with faculty on Capstone project idea development and take upper division major courses including Problems and Methods .

-
Students should complete 3 courses: Emergence of the Modern Middle Eas t OR Making of the Muslim Middle East ; Anthropology and the Arab World OR Gulf Urban Societies ; Introduction to Modern Arabic Literature OR Masterpieces of Premodern Arabic Literature before studying away.

-
Students are strongly encouraged to begin their required Arabic Language studies before going abroad.

-
It is strongly recommended that not more than two non-language ACS courses be taken while studying away.

-
Students must plan to be in Abu Dhabi for the entire senior year (fall and spring semesters) to work on their capstone completion as well as on any other remaining requirements in preparation for timely graduation.

- Study away is an option only in the semester(s) explicitly noted in this pathway. Other semesters must be spent on campus in Abu Dhabi.

- Art and Art History

Recommended Global Sites

Sophomore Spring | Junior Fall

NYU Berlin | NYU Berlin

NYU Florence | NYU Florence

NYU London | NYU London

NYU Madrid | NYU Madrid

NYU Paris | NYU New York

NYU Prague | NYU Paris

NYU Tulsa | NYU Prague

| NYU Tulsa

Requirements

-
Art & Art History students study away in either the spring semester of their Sophomore year or the fall semester of their Junior year. They are required to be at NYUAD during their spring semester in Junior year.

-
Requests to take two semesters away will only be considered when supported by a compelling academic plan and rationale.

-
Students must have completed Ways of Looking and Ways of Making before taking a semester abroad.

-
Only one art history or studio art/design course taken during the semester abroad can be counted as an elective towards the major requirements.

-
The Art and Art History program strongly encourages students to diversify their education by taking courses outside their major while studying abroad.

-
Students must review course offerings at away sites carefully and they must discuss their study away plans with their program mentors before applying for their semester abroad.

-
Please note: Not all NYU global sites offer art history or studio arts/design courses. With a few exceptions elsewhere, studio arts/design courses are effectively available only in New York, but students should be aware that, though there are many courses listed, these courses are in high demand and it is very often difficult to secure a place. The other away sites largely do not offer studio arts/design courses. Therefore, students who are focusing on practice are strongly advised to take all or most of their practice-based courses at NYUAD in order to avoid disappointment and to use the semester abroad to diversify their education. As far as art history is concerned, there are courses at several sites. But some away sites offer art history courses only infrequently and some do not offer them at all. Students must therefore review course offerings at the away sites carefully and discuss their plans with their academic advisor in the program.

-
Areas of particular interest to Art & Art History at away sites include:

-

-
Art and education, museums, architecture, ancient art: Berlin

-
Art and the city, visual culture and colonial Latin America: Buenos Aires

-
Renaissance art, Roman and Etruscan arts, gardens: Florence

-
British art, design and architecture: London

-
Major works of European art from the Baroque to the 19th century, Spanish art: Madrid

-
French medieval art, Impressionism, Post-Impressionism, Cubism, Surrealism, non-Western and East Asian art: Paris

-
New York has the greatest variety of courses, but please note the comments on enrollment described above.

-
If access to museums and galleries, and immersion in art are factors in choosing an away site, then Berlin, London, Madrid, Paris and New York are the sites that will give you this most of all, with the addition of Florence for anyone who wants to specialize in the art of the Italian Renaissance.

- Study away is an option only in the semester(s) explicitly noted in this pathway. Other semesters must be spent on campus in Abu Dhabi.

- Biology

Recommended Global Sites

Sophomore Spring OR Junior Fall OR Junior Spring

NYU New York

NYU Shanghai

NYU Sydney

Requirements

-
Students may study abroad either in the Spring of their Sophomore year, or the Fall or Spring of their Junior year. Study abroad is an option only in these semesters. Other semesters must be spent on campus in Abu Dhabi.

-
To qualify, students must complete the Foundations of Science sequence (6 courses), Calculus , Multivariable Calculus , and Human Physiology before studying abroad.

-
Students planning to study abroad in their Junior Spring must complete the Capstone Research Seminar before. All other students must complete the Capstone Research Seminar prior to their Senior year.

-
Foundations of Science , Human Physiology, and the Capstone Research Seminar are offered every semester, and students should plan accordingly.

-
Only one biology elective taken while studying abroad will be counted towards the major. Other biology courses will be counted as general electives.

-
Students must discuss their study abroad plan with their major advisor and the biology program head before submitting their application.

-
A second semester abroad is not permissible. Studying abroad during the senior year is not permissible.

-
Study away is an option only in the semester(s) explicitly noted in this pathway. Other semesters must be spent on campus in Abu Dhabi.

- Business, Organizations and Society (BOS)

Recommended Global Sites

Sophomore Spring | Junior Fall OR Spring

NYU Madrid | NYU London

NYU Prague | NYU Los Angeles

NYU Shanghai | NYU New York

NYU Sydney | NYU New York: NIIF (Spring Only)

NYU Tel Aviv | NYU Shanghai

NYU Tulsa | NYU Tulsa

| NYU Washington DC

Requirements

-
BOS majors can apply to study away for up to two semesters as noted above.

-
Study away is an option only in the semester(s) explicitly noted in this pathway. Other semesters must be spent on campus in Abu Dhabi.

-
It is recommended that students use their study away to take courses that add depth and breadth to the Business, Organizations and Society (BOS) major by taking electives that are not typically offered at NYU Abu Dhabi. The focus of the study away experience should not be completing foundational courses required for the BOS major. Students are encouraged to take advanced electives abroad, especially in their second study away, if eligible for such. To access these electives, especially at NYU Stern or NYU Shanghai, students need to plan accordingly to complete all the prerequisites before departure.

-
Students who wish to study away for a second semester are strongly encouraged to consider global sites with advanced business electives that add depth to their BOS major. Most global sites (except New York) have for-credit and non-credit internship opportunities. Students should identify sites with opportunities that are better aligned with their job/career interests, capstone project interests, and/or academic trajectory.

-
Students must have a cumulative GPA of 3.0 or above to apply for the first study away and 3.25 or above to apply for the second study away.

-
Students are required to take the following courses before going abroad for the first time – Statistics for the Social and Behavioral Sciences (SOCSC-UH 1010), at least two Business Foundations courses ( Management & Organizations (BUSOR-UH 1003), Strategic Management (BUSOR-UH 1004), Principles of Marketing (BUSOR-UH 1001J ), Introduction to Accounting (BUSOR-UH 1501) , Foundations of Financial Markets ( ECON-UH 2510 )), and the Math requirement ( Calculus with Applications to Economics (MATH-UH 1013) or equivalent (e.g., any section of Calculus )).

-
Before going abroad for a second semester away, students are required to complete the Social Impact or Ethics elective, their required Economics course, and Research Methods (Prerequisite for Management Track Capstone) OR Introduction to Entrepreneurship (Prerequisite for Entrepreneurship Track Capstone), in addition to the first study away requirements noted above.

-
Students interested in the NIIF program must apply through a separate competitive process. Please review and follow the specific application instructions for NIIF through the provided link . Students participating in NIIF must plan to study in Abu Dhabi for the fall semester of their Junior year and will study in New York in the spring of their Junior year.

Students must complete Foundations of Science 1-6 , Calculus , Multivariable Calculus , Organic Chemistry 1 before going abroad. Organic Chemistry 2 can be taken abroad (in the above-mentioned sites).

-
Research Seminar has to be completed in Junior Fall for students studying away in Junior Spring, and in Junior Spring for students studying away in Junior Fall ( Research Seminar is offered every semester)

-
A second semester abroad is not permissible. Studying away during the senior year is not permissible.

-
Students are encouraged to discuss their study away plan with their major advisor before submitting their application.

-

- Computer Science

Recommended Global Sites

Sophomore Spring | Junior Fall

NYU Paris | NYU New York

| NYU Paris

| NYU Shanghai

| NYU Sydney

| NYU Tulsa

| KAIST

Requirements

-
Study abroad in Sophomore Spring is possible only at NYU Paris. Please review the conditions below.

-
Please note that if you do not qualify to study away in Paris in the Sophomore Spring semester, this does not mean that you can request two study away semesters later on. The only other possible semester for study away is Junior Fall.

-
Before studying abroad in Sophomore Spring, students committed to majoring in Computer Science must have successfully completed the following courses in Abu Dhabi — Introduction to Computer Science (or Computer Programming for Engineers with a grade of A- or above), Discrete Math , Data Structures , and Calculus with Applications . Students must achieve a grade of B or higher in at least two of these four courses.

-
Students approved to study abroad in Sophomore Spring who have not completed Algorithms and/or Computer Systems Organization in Abu Dhabi are required to take these courses during their study away semester at NYU Paris. Students who plan to study away in Junior Fall, must have declared the Computer Science major prior to that, and before studying abroad in Junior Fall, they must have successfully completed the following courses — I ntroduction to Computer Science (or Computer Programming for Engineers with a grade of A- or above), Discrete Math , Data Structures , Calculus with Applications , as well as Algorithms , and Computer Systems Organization .

-
Students must be at NYUAD in the spring semester of their junior year to work with faculty on their Capstone project development by way of the Research Seminar in Computer Science , and take upper-division courses in the major.

-
Students can apply to study away only once or twice as per the pathway outlined above. Sophomore Spring study away can only happen at NYU Paris. Students can apply for a semester of study away at NYU Paris in Sophomore Spring, and then apply for a second study away – if eligible – in Junior Fall in any of the programs outlined in this pathway. Note that neither study away terms are guaranteed. Students must meet the eligibility criteria to qualify.

-
Study away is an option only in the semester(s) explicitly noted in this pathway. Other semesters must be spent on campus in Abu Dhabi.

- Economics

Sophomore Spring | Junior Fall OR Spring

NYU Florence | NYU Accra

NYU London | NYU New York

Requirements

-
It is recommended that students plan to spend a single semester abroad in either spring of sophomore year or fall or spring of junior year. It is not possible to study away for the full junior year.

-
Before a study away semester in Sophomore Spring, students must complete Markets ; Statistics for the Social and Behavioral Sciences ; Calculus ; and either Global Economic, Political, and Social Development in Historical Perspective (GEPS) or Introduction to Macroeconomics .

-
Before a study away semester in the fall of junior year, students must – in addition to the above courses– also complete Intermediate Microeconomics , Intermediate Macroeconomics , Data Analysis , and Multivariable Calculus .

-
Before a study away semester in the spring of junior year, students must – in addition to the above courses – also complete Economics of Imperfect Markets and Introduction to Econometrics .

-
A second study away semester requires a GPA of at least 3.5.

-
The following courses must be completed in Abu Dhabi: Calculus , Multivariable Calculus , ECON-UH 2020 Data Analysis , and SOCSC-UH 3220 Econometrics . In addition, we strongly recommend that students take all required courses for the Economics major in Abu Dhabi, and use study away as an opportunity to explore electives (in and outside the Economics major). In addition to pedagogical reasons, there are logistical reasons for this recommendation:

-
the prerequisites for required courses sometimes differ across global sites (see examples of such differences in requirements in the Additional Notes section below),

-
required courses at major global sites often have limited spaces.

-
For both reasons above, academic plans that rely on taking required courses abroad can be disrupted. Students planning to take required courses during study away – against our recommendation – should plan carefully to ensure they can meet major requirements in a timely manner and without delaying graduation.

-
For the concentration “Quantitative Economic Analysis”, NYU New York is recommended. For the concentration “Finance and Market Studies”, NYU London, NYU New York, NYU Shanghai and NYU Tel Aviv are recommended. For the concentration “Applied Economics and Economic Policy”, NYU Accra, NYU Florence, NYU Paris, and NYU Washington DC are recommended.

Additional Notes

-

-
Students interested in finance should note that Introduction to Accounting and Foundations of Financial Markets (as well as, sometimes, Corporate Finance ) are prerequisites for most finance electives at study away sites, so students must plan to take these courses in Abu Dhabi prior to their study away semester.

-
Either GEPS or Introduction to Macroeconomics is a prerequisite for Intermediate Macroeconomics at the study away sites and no other courses are accepted as equivalent at these sites.

-
Multivariate Calculus is a prerequisite for Intermediate Microeconomics at the study away sites, in particular at NYU London.

-
Students should also note that to be eligible for advanced economics electives (300-level courses) at the study away sites, students must have completed Multivariable Calculus , Data Analysis , Intermediate Microeconomics , and Intermediate Macroeconomics . This is difficult to accomplish for students hoping to study away in the spring of sophomore year.

-
Study away is an option only in the semester(s) explicitly noted in this pathway. Other semesters must be spent on campus in Abu Dhabi.

- Engineering

Study away is an integral component of the NYUAD engineering curriculum and is highly recommended for all engineering students. Students who have a cumulative GPA of 3.0 and above at the time of the study away application qualify to study away during the spring semester of their junior year, as long as they have also met the requirements detailed below. Outstanding students who have a GPA of 3.9 and above at the time of the study away application may also qualify for a second study away semester during the fall semester of their junior year.

Study away is an option only in the semester(s) explicitly noted in this pathway. Other semesters must be spent on campus in Abu Dhabi.

Option 1:

Junior Spring

NYU New York (Tandon School of Engineering)

NYU Tulsa

National Taiwan University (NTU)-- open to Computer and Electrical Engineering students

Requirements

To qualify for the Junior Spring study away semester in New York or Tulsa, students must have a cumulative GPA of 3.0 and above at the time of the study away application (i.e. fall semester of the sophomore year.) They must have completed Foundations of Science 1 & 2 , C omputer Programming for Engineers , Design and Innovation , and the following courses relevant to their engineering discipline:

Bioengineering: Foundations of Science 3 & 4, Differential Equations for Engineers, Linear Algebra, Bioengineering Principles

Computer Engineering: Discrete Math, Linear Algebra, Hardware Design, Object-Oriented Programming, Data Structures and Algorithms, Computer Organization and Architecture

Civil Engineering: Ordinary Differential Equations or Differential Equations for Engineers, Structural Systems, Project Management, Geotechnical Engineering, Transportation and Traffic Engineering, Structure and Properties of Civil Engineering Materials

Electrical Engineering: Linear Algebra, Ordinary Differential Equations, Advanced Circuits, Electronics, Signals and Systems

General Engineering: Multivariable Calculus, Linear Algebra, Discrete Math or Ordinary Differential Equations or Differential Equations for Engineers, Statics, Conservation Laws, Circuits

Mechanical Engineering: Differential Equations for Engineers, Dynamics, Fluid Mechanics, Thermodynamics

Option 2:

Junior Fall and Junior Spring (2 semesters)

NYU New York (Tandon School of Engineering)

NYU Tulsa

National Taiwan University (NTU)-- open to Computer and Electrical Engineering students (Spring only)

Requirements

Students who have a cumulative GPA of 3.9* and above at the time of the study away application (i.e. fall semester of the sophomore year) may also qualify for a second study away semester in New York or Tulsa in the fall of their junior year. Those students must have completed Foundations of Science 1 & 2 , Computer Programming for Engineers , Design and Innovation , and the following courses relevant to their discipline:

Bioengineering: Differential Equations for Engineers, Linear Algebra, Foundations of Science 3 & 4, Bioengineering Principles

Computer Engineering: Discrete Math, Linear Algebra, Hardware Design, Object-Oriented Programming, Data Structures and Algorithms

Civil Engineering: Ordinary Differential Equations or Differential Equations for Engineers, Fluid Mechanics, Advanced Solid Mechanics

Electrical Engineering: Ordinary Differential Equations, Advanced Circuits

General Engineering: Multivariable Calculus, Linear Algebra, Discrete Math or Ordinary Differential Equations or Differential Equations for Engineers, Statics, Conservation Laws, Circuits

Mechanical Engineering: Ordinary Differential Equations, Dynamics, Fluid Mechanics

* Please note that the 3.9 cumulative GPA is a minimum requirement, which does not guarantee the second study away semester. All other course requirements must be met as well.

- Film and New Media

Recommended Global Sites

Sophomore Spring | Junior Fall

NYU Accra | NYU Accra

NYU Buenos Aires | NYU Los Angeles

NYU London | NYU New York

NYU Madrid | NYU Prague

NYU Sydney | Juniors may select from other study abroad sites according to interest in developing content for their Capstone projects

NYU Tulsa |

Requirements

-
Recommended semesters for study abroad are Sophomore Spring OR Junior Fall.

-
All Film and New Media majors are required to take Concepts in Film and New Media , Sound, Image and Story , and Techniques for Safety and Production in Abu Dhabi before studying abroad.

-
Film and New Media Practice majors are encouraged to take Practices of Narrative Filmmaking or Practices of Documentary Filmmaking in Abu Dhabi, but could be approved to take an equivalent course while studying abroad.

-
Film and New Media students are required to take either Cinematic Expression: Method, Sketches in Junior Spring or Archives, Methods, Screens as a corequisite with the Capstone Seminar in Senior Fall. Cinematic Expression is offered in Junior Spring as a prerequisite for the Capstone Seminar . Archives, Methods, and Screens is offered in the Senior Fall semester as a corequisite with the Capstone Seminar .

-
Students are required to be on campus in Abu Dhabi for the spring of their junior year to prepare for the Capstone, and are required to take the Capstone Seminar in the fall of senior year to develop the concept for their senior Capstone project.

-
Students are encouraged to take courses at the global sites on topics not usually offered at NYU Abu Dhabi. Students are also encouraged to take courses that might help them with the research for their capstone project. Students should plan to meet with their capstone mentors to discuss their electives and focus area.

-
Study away is an option only in the semester(s) explicitly noted in this pathway. Other semesters must be spent on campus in Abu Dhabi.

NYU Florence |

Requirements

-
The sites listed above for Sophomore Spring, in alphabetical order, have the richest demonstrated record of history course offerings. However, site selection depends on the interests and curricular needs of each student, which should be discussed with the student’s major advisor.

-
Recommended semesters for study abroad are Sophomore Spring and/or Junior Fall.

-
Students will ideally take the required course History and Globalization in Abu Dhabi in the fall of sophomore year, prior to the first study away semester.

-
Students should be on campus in Abu Dhabi for the spring of junior year to work with faculty on preliminary capstone project development, and to take the required course Writing History .

Students generally need to take at least one history course per semester to complete the History major on time.

Students should take courses at the global sites on topics not regularly offered in Abu Dhabi.

Study away is an option only in the semester(s) explicitly noted in this pathway. Other semesters must be spent on campus in Abu Dhabi.

Requirements

-
Prior to studying away, students must have completed Understanding Interactive Media – Critical Questions & Theories and at least one other Interactive Media required course: Introduction to Interactive Media; Communications Lab; Communication & Technology.

Students who have not completed the 4 required Interactive Media courses will need to study away at NYU Shanghai, where they must register in the appropriate courses to fulfill these requirements. The 4 required courses are: Understanding Interactive Media – Critical Questions & Theories; Introduction to Interactive Media; Communications Lab; Communication & Technology .

Students who wish to take Interactive Telecommunications Program (ITP) courses in New York may only do so in their Junior Fall semester, as these courses are closed to Sophomores.

Study away for a second semester would not be approved by the program if students have not completed all 4 required Interactive Media courses (Understanding Interactive Media – Critical Questions & Theories; Introduction to Interactive Media; Communications Lab; Communication & Technology ).

Recommended Global Sites

NYU Florence | NYU London Track (Junior Fall)

NYU London Track |

NYU New York |

NYU Paris |

Requirements

-
The Legal Studies Program strongly encourages its students to develop advanced level proficiency in one or more foreign languages. The sites for Sophomore Spring have been identified because each may afford the possibility for language study, and/or offer Legal Studies elective courses, and/or present opportunities for internships and leadership training. Site selection depends on student interests and curricular needs, which should be discussed with the student’s major advisor.

-
Recommended semesters for study abroad are Sophomore Spring or Junior Fall or Junior Spring, depending on the progress students have made in the major and their rationale for study away.

-
Students are required to take at least one of the six required Legal Studies courses in Abu Dhabi prior to the first study away semester. All Legal Studies required courses must be taken in Abu Dhabi during the four years of a student’s undergraduate education.

-
Students majoring in Legal Studies must be in Abu Dhabi during the fall and spring of their senior year in order to fulfill the Capstone requirements.

-
Students should take advantage of the wide array of courses at global sites on topics specific to understanding the complexity of cultures of the host country/region, courses towards minors that can broaden the context for their Legal Studies, or courses towards the breadth of a liberal arts education generally not available in Abu Dhabi.

Study away is an option only in the semester(s) explicitly noted in this pathway. Other semesters must be spent on campus in Abu Dhabi.

Sophomore Spring | Junior Spring

Any Study Abroad site | Any Study Abroad site where Capstone research can be conducted

Requirements

-
Students are required to take either Literary Interpretation or Introduction to Creative Writing before studying abroad.

-
Courses in Literature and Creative Writing are available throughout the global network. Students are encouraged to use their first semester of study away to explore fields of study that complement the major in Literature and Creative Writing.

-
Students choosing to apply for a second semester abroad should do so in consultation with their major mentor, who can help them develop a proposal justifying the second semester. The proposal should take into account the students’ academic plans and goals, and should be geared towards a capstone project or other academic endeavor, as well as towards the global site that the student proposes to visit.

-
Students are required to take Problems and Methods in the fall of junior year. Because this course helps students with their preliminary capstone proposals, students must take this course before a second semester away. The program thus suggests that students may study away in the spring semesters of the sophomore and junior years.

-
Students are encouraged to pursue language studies as a complement to the major in Literature and Creative Writing. The NYU global sites offer opportunities to develop language proficiency in an immersive environment, and we recommend that, where possible, students take at least one course that focuses on the literature of the host country.

Study away is an option only in the semester(s) explicitly noted in this pathway. Other semesters must be spent on campus in Abu Dhabi.

| NYU Sydney

NYU Los Angeles | NYU Los Angeles

NYU Berlin | NYU New York

Recommended Global Sites

Sophomore Spring | Junior Fall

NYU Berlin | NYU London

NYU Buenos Aires | NYU New York

NYU Florence | NYU Washington DC

NYU London | NYU Tulsa

NYU Madrid |

NYU Prague |

Requirements

- Before going abroad, students must take Statistics for the Social and Behavioral Sciences , Introduction to Political Thinking ( IPT ), as well as two other foundational/introductory courses for the major ( Political Thinking in Practice (PTP), Social, Political, and Economic History (SPEH) or Social, Political, and Economic Thought in Historical Perspective (SPET) )

* For those in the Class of 2029 ONLY: Political Thinking in Practice ( PTP ) will only be offered starting in Fall 2026. We will therefore waive the requirement to have taken PTP , or to have taken four foundational/introductory courses as described above before Study Away 1. In other words, students in the Class of 2029 must take Statistics for the Social and Behavioral Sciences , Introduction to Political Thinking ( IPT ) , and one foundational/introductory course for the major ( Political Thinking in Practice (PTP), Social, Political, and Economic History (SPEH) or Social, Political, and Economic Thought in Historical Perspective ( SPET ) ).

-
It is recommended that students use Sophomore Spring for study away to explore the breadth of the liberal arts curriculum at the global sites, rather than focusing primarily or wholly on completing courses required for the Political Science major.

-
Students who wish to spend a second semester abroad, normally in the fall of junior year, must have completed all five courses noted above. *For those in the Class of 2028, the old requirement still applies. In addition, they must develop a proposal that justifies the second semester away with respect to their academic plan and goals, and should be geared towards a capstone project or other academic endeavor related to the global site they are proposing to visit.

-
It is strongly recommended that all Political Science majors take their required methods courses at NYUAD. They also must complete their methods requirements before senior year.

-
Students applying for their first semester abroad must have a cumulative minimum GPA of 3.0; for the second semester abroad, there is a minimum GPA requirement of 3.5.

Study away is an option only in the semester(s) explicitly noted in this pathway. Other semesters must be spent on campus in Abu Dhabi.

- Psychology

Recommended Global Sites

Sophomore Spring OR Junior Fall

NYU Berlin

NYU London (Abnormal and Personality course offerings)

NYU New York (not recommended for Sophomore Spring)

NYU Shanghai (Neural and Social Science course offerings)

NYU Sydney (Mental Health and Health Psychology course offerings)

NYU Tulsa

NYU Washington DC

KAIST

Requirements

-
Students majoring in Psychology are encouraged to use one semester abroad as an opportunity to fulfill general elective requirements outside of psychology, to explore a new culture, to learn a new language, etc. This study away experience does not need to be justified in terms of fulfilling specific course requirements in psychology. However, a second study away experience does need to be justified in terms of progress in the major, capstone, research, or preparation for graduate school.

-
Students should complete at least 3 of the 4 required courses for Psychology ( Introduction to Psychology, Research Methods in Psychology, Biopsychology, and Statistics ) before going abroad.

-
Study away is an option only in the semester(s) explicitly noted in this pathway. Other semesters must be spent on campus in Abu Dhabi.

- Social Research and Public Policy

Recommended Global Sites

Sophomore Spring | OR Junior Fall | OR Junior Spring

NYU Accra | NYU Accra | NYU Accra

NYU Buenos Aires | NYU Florence | NYU Florence

NYU Florence | NYU Madrid | NYU Madrid

NYU Madrid | NYU New York | NYU New York

NYU Paris | NYU Shanghai | NYU Shanghai

NYU Shanghai | NYU Sydney | NYU Sydney

NYU Sydney | NYU Tel Aviv | NYU Washington DC

NYU Washington DC | NYU Washington DC | NYU Tulsa

NYU Tulsa | NYU Tulsa |

Philosophy

-
The timing and extent of study abroad vary from student to student. Study away benefits should be carefully weighed against other academic or extracurricular projects such as taking courses with standing faculty, preparing Capstone projects, double majoring, research assistantships, and community-based work at NYUAD.

-
NYUAD faculty will provide help and advice on how to optimize planning for study abroad in light of each student’s academic standing, academic plan, and goals.

-
Opportunities such as summer programs, J-Term courses, and regional academic seminars should contribute to students’ international experiences without disrupting the students’ work in the major to the extent that a full year away has the potential of doing.

Requirements

General

- We require consultation with your major mentor before deciding on your study away pathway (whether you study away once or twice away) and the optimal study away site.

-
Students who decide late to major in SRPP, or have other projects that take up significant parts of their first and sophomore year, are allowed to spend no more than a single semester away, which could be in the spring of their sophomore year or the fall or spring of their junior year.

-
Study away is an option only in the semester(s) explicitly noted in this pathway. Other semesters must be spent on campus in Abu Dhabi.

-
Studying away in senior year is NOT allowed under any circumstance. SRPP majors are required to spend senior year in Abu Dhabi to work with faculty on their Capstone projects (although preparation for Capstone may begin in junior year and/or summer between junior and senior year.)

-
Students should specify how they plan to satisfy the major requirements in their four-year plan. SRPP majors should complete most of the requirements of the major, as well as key elective courses, before senior year. Study away may not be approved if these requirements cannot be completed before senior year because a student plans to be away. Electives and required courses provide the background, framework, and skill sets needed to complete the capstone requirement.

-
Prerequisites for classes planned during study away should be taken in Abu Dhabi.

-
During junior year, we only allow studying away for one semester. The rationale relates to capstone preparation and the importance of forging relationships with program faculty to facilitate capstone and post-graduation plans (such as applications to graduate schools).

-
During study away, we recommend focusing on courses that are not offered at NYUAD. Taking at least some electives with SRPP program faculty before senior year is necessary for effective development of the capstone and for identifying a suitable capstone advisor. In particular, students must complete at least one Methods elective before the start of senior year to prepare for their capstone project.

-
We do not recognize Methods electives taken during study away, unless already pre-approved or specifically recommended by the Associate Program Head. Students are strongly encouraged to take their Methods electives in Abu Dhabi.

-
Students accepted for study away (e.g., for Sophomore Spring) who decide to cancel (for whatever reason) must not assume they will have the same opportunity the following year.

-
The best internship opportunities (immediately following study away) are usually found in the smaller sites, especially Accra, Washington DC, Tel Aviv, and Tulsa; we recommend aiming for internships in junior year as you will have gained more skills that you can bring to bear on your internship activities.

-
We encourage students interested in internships to consider Accra as a study away site.

-
We encourage considering the new NYU Tulsa site for study away. Benefits include additional funding, the possibility of internships, and the possibility of receiving support to obtain H1-B visa for post-graduation plans.

-
Programs of particular interest to students majoring in SRPP at global sites are:

-
Global leadership program, public policy, politics: Washington DC

-
Child development, global public health, developmental social science: Accra

-
Anthropology, migration, business, global public health: Sydney

-
Middle East conflict and politics: Tel Aviv

-
Urban Studies: Berlin

-
European politics, culture, and art: Madrid

-
Public policy and education: New York

-
Law, society, and humanities: Florence

-
History, business, and psychology: London

-
Culture, arts, business, entrepreneurship, tech: Tulsa

-
Business, management, demography, migration: Shanghai

-
Computer science, data sciences, computational social science: Paris and Shanghai

-
Political, historical, or cultural sociology: DC

Second study away

-
Students who wish to apply for a second semester away should consult with their major mentor (first step) and should arrange a meeting with the Associate Program Head (second step)

-
Students interested in a second study away semester should have a minimum cumulative GPA of 3.4 (i.e., 3.4 or above).

-
Students interested in a second study away semester should provide a clear rationale for doing so. Study abroad should always be connected to a clearly stated and realistic academic endeavor with respect to the proposed study away site. Optimal uses of study abroad include coursework and internship opportunities not offered in Abu Dhabi; or larger connected projects such as completing courses for a minor connected to the study away site, or fieldwork for the capstone or other research project.

-
Before a second semester abroad, students must complete the following courses in Abu Dhabi:

-
Two of the Foundations of Social Science courses

-
One Methods elective

-
Failure to comply with the above requirements will result in a denial, with no room for negotiation.

Students who apply for study abroad, having declared a Theater major MUST have completed at least two courses in theater – one required (either Making Theater or Thinking Theater ) and one elective.

The Theater program capstone course progression begins in Abu Dhabi Junior Spring with the Capstone Seminar . Students majoring in theater are expected to be in Abu Dhabi for their Junior Spring and senior year.
