title: Funding Guidelines FAQs · NYUAD Students
text:
Housing Charges FAQs

Q: What expenses will be posted on my student bill while I’m studying away?

A: During your semester abroad, NYUAD will bill you the same full-time tuition and insurance rate fees as when you are studying in Abu Dhabi. You will not be charged for the NYUAD mandatory book fee, Abu Dhabi housing, or Abu Dhabi meal plan costs; however, you will incur charges for room and board based on the dormitory assigned to you by the host site.

The financial aid coverage remains the same as when you are studying in Abu Dhabi. For example, if you are on a full-aid scholarship, your room costs will be covered up to the published housing cap rate listed above. If you receive partial support for housing, the same amount will be applied to your account. If you receive no support for housing, the full amount for housing will be charged to your student bill.

Q: I did not receive the housing allocation for the dormitory I selected. Who do I reach out to regarding the cost?

A: Housing assignments are made by the host site based on availability. Please reach out to the housing team at your site for any room change requests. NYUAD cannot influence these decisions.

title: Study Away in New York · NYUAD Students
text:
Academic Guide

New York University is comprised of 18 schools, twelve of which offer undergraduate courses. NYUAD students studying in New York are advised to consider programs and courses offered in the schools listed below.

The links below provide useful information about each school relevant to study away, its programs, recommended courses for NYUAD students, and best practices for registering for courses.

While the majors and programs offered by each school may correlate to NYUAD's majors and minors, students and their mentors must bear in mind that each NYU school has its own application and admissions process. Students at NYU New York have been admitted to a specific school and program. CAS and Gallatin are the only schools where students are generally able to register for courses without restrictions as long as the prerequisites for the courses are fulfilled. It is possible for NYUAD students to take courses at other schools, but there are often guidelines and procedures that must be followed. Students should NOT automatically expect that they will be permitted to take courses offered by a program, regardless of their major, GPA, or completed prerequisites.

Registration

Registration information will be available on the enrollment portal under the Academics heading. It is essential that all students validate courses in their shopping carts on Albert prior to registration. Students should complete the checklist item for New York Registration Procedure and complete the Course Registration Request forms as needed. If further questions arise after reading the provided information, contact gpnyc@nyu.edu for support.

When planning your course schedule, please note that no courses can be guaranteed. It is a poor strategy to plan a schedule that includes courses you must complete during your semester in New York in order to graduate on time or make progress in your major.

If you are experiencing difficulties during the registration process or drop/add period, you should always contact the NYUAD alias for New York study away registration, nyuad.registrar@nyu.edu . You should NOT contact instructors, advisors, or deans at any of NYU’s schools. It can create confusion and often results in making a relatively straightforward issue more difficult than need be.

Exceptions

Please note the following commonly requested exceptions:

- Graduate-level courses — If you wish to enroll in a graduate-level course, you must have a strong GPA in that area of study, be endorsed by the academic mentor, the NY department, and be pre-approved by the Vice Provost for Academic Administration.

- School of Professional Studies — Enrollment in courses in the School of Professional Studies is not generally permitted. Exceptions, while rarely granted, can be considered on a case-by case-basis by application to the Vice Provost for Academic Administration.

- Online Courses — Students may NOT take online courses for degree credit. If a student wishes to pursue an online course they will be responsible for self-funding it.

- Internship Courses — Internship courses are not readily available in New York. Please do not pursue internship opportunities that require course credit in order to participate. Further, it is unlikely that NYUAD will accept academic credit for an internship.

Liberal Arts Colleges

- College of Arts and Science (CAS)

The College of Arts and Science (CAS) is NYU's largest undergraduate school with over 60 majors and 80 minors. Many NYUAD students will find that programs in this school most closely resemble their programs at NYUAD. Registering for courses at CAS therefore poses few problems provided that the prerequisites for the selected courses have been fulfilled. Students should work closely with their mentors when choosing those courses. Those who plan to register for lecture courses with multiple sections should be prepared to be in a class with well over 100 students.

Biology , Economics , Mathematics , Computer Science , and Psychology are among the most popular majors at NYU New York. As a result, courses in those departments fill extremely quickly. Students should take particular care to make sure they have the correct prerequisites for courses in these departments and that the course validates in the shopping cart on Albert. Attempting to register for a course that is not listed on your Course Intent Form on the Enrollment Portal , particularly if the course requires special permissions during or after registration, will likely result in the course being filled before you have access to it. Please note the following:

- The calculus sequence in the Mathematics department is not an appropriate fit for students who need to complete calculus courses for their majors.

- In addition to meeting all of the requirements above for enrollment in graduate-level courses, students hoping to take a graduate-level Math course must complete an application form .

- Students who wish to take Biology courses will be limited to one undergraduate course during the first week of registration. Please note certain upper-level Biology courses will be restricted to matriculated CAS Biology majors the first week of registration. Should space still be available in Biology courses after that week, students will be able to register for additional courses. Students who completed Organismal Biology/Human Physiology may be eligible to take one 1000-level graduate Biology course if they have approval of their mentor and the Vice Provost for Academic Administration.

- Because Introduction to Computer Science in Abu Dhabi is taught using a different programming language than the Introduction to Computer Science course in NY, students wishing to take Data Structures must pass a placement exam in order to enroll. Please note that the NYU Tandon Data Structures and Algorithms course will not count for the NYUAD Computer Science major or minor.

- For students interested in courses that are part of the College Core, NYUAD is only permitted a limited number of seats in the CAS Core program and students will not be able to register for a College Core course on their own through Albert. Those who indicate that they wish to take a College Core course on their course intent form will have the best chance of being registered for such a course.

- A student planning to take Arabic in New York and moving from Elementary 2 to Intermediate 1 or from Intermediate 2 to Advanced 1 will be required to take a placement exam. All students, regardless of home campus, are required to take these exams.

- Students who are continuing another foreign language that they have previously studied within the NYU network may continue their studies at the appropriate level without a placement test.

Enrollment under any other circumstance is contingent upon a placement test. French, German, and Spanish language exams are available here . (The password is your NYU login password.) Language placement exams for Cantonese, German, Greek (Modern), Hebrew, Italian, Japanese, Korean, Latin, Mandarin (simplified and traditional), Portuguese, and Russian may be taken online here . Online placement exams should be completed well BEFORE registration so that your results can be entered into Albert in time for registration. Students who wish to take the Arabic, Hindi, Persian, Turkish, and Urdu exams should contact the NYU New York study away office. These exams are given on site during the first week of classes.

- Gallatin School of Individualized Study

The Gallatin School of Individualized Study is among the smallest undergraduate programs at NYU. Rather than offer majors and designated programs, Gallatin allows its students to craft their own program of study. Gallatin students take courses offered by Gallatin and, when approved, at other NYU schools. Students should work closely with their mentors and consult the Study Away Equivalency Chart if they want a Gallatin course to count towards their majors or the Core Curriculum.

NYUAD sstudents are encouraged to take Gallatin courses in the following areas and should be able to register for those courses without issue, space permitting:

- Interdisciplinary Seminars

- Writing Program

- Arts Program

- Community Learning Initiative

Students will not be permitted to register for courses in the First Year Program (course code FYSP-UG).

Gallatin courses are small (15 students per class), and therefore may be a comfortable fit for NYUAD students used to an intimate classroom setting.

- (Global) Liberal Studies

Situated within the NYU’s Arts and Science programs, (Global) Liberal Studies is a 4-year program that allows students to specialize in one of five concentrations with courses centered on issues of globalization: Art, Text, and Media; Critical Creative Production; Culture and Social Identities; Law, Ethics, and Religion; Politics, Rights, and Development. Within those concentration NYUAD students may take courses in Advanced Writing Studio, Cultural Foundations, Global Topics (regularly vary each semester), and Social Foundations. Sophomore Seminar may be appropriate for some students, and advanced students may qualify for Senior Colloquia or Seminars.

Students interested in (Global) Liberal Studies courses should indicate those courses on their course intent form and will be enrolled in courses with available space one week after registration.

NYU Professional Schools

If a a student is interested in specialized or upper-level courses offered by a professional or pre-professional school, exceptions will be necessary (to be explored further below). NYUAD students should note that all NYU students are required to follow this same procedure.

NYU offers a variety of minors in partnership with NYU's professional and pre-professional schools. NYUAD students interested in taking courses in pre-professional schools that have special admissions policies should first look at the courses offered through the cross-school minors first since they will pose the fewest registration problems, space permitting.

Read more on Cross-School Minors

- College of Global Public Health

The College Global of Public Health (GPH) offers an indisciplinary program in which students study global public health and a major sponsored by another NYU school. The Global Public Health major focuses on six areas:

- Biostatistics

- Epidemiology

- Health Policy

- Environmental health

- Sociobehavioral Health

Students interested in taking courses offered by this school must wait one week after majors have registered to enroll. Non-majors will not be eligible to take UGPH-GU 60 UG Experiential Learning and UGPH-GU 100 Pre-Health Honors.

- Leonard N. Stern School of Business

The Leonard N. Stern School of Business offers ten concentrations within the business studies majors. The Stern program is cross-disciplinary, integrating liberal arts and business courses. NYUAD students are limited to the Open Access Courses available to non-Stern students. Four of those courses are available to non-Stern students the first week of registration; NYUAD students may only register for the non-Stern sections of these courses:

- Principles of Financial Accounting (ACCT-UB 1)

- Foundations of Financial Markets (FINC-UB 2)

- Management and Organizational Analysis (MGMT-UB 1)

- Introduction to Marketing (MKTG-UB 1)

Students also should consider courses from the minors and specializations available to all NYU students:

- Advanced Mathematical Methods (with CAS)

- Business of Entertainment, Media, and Technology (with Steinhardt and Tisch)

- Business Studies (with CAS)

- Public Policy and Management (with Wagner, see below)

- Social Entrepreneurship (with Wagner, see below)

For students interested in taking an intermediate or advanced Stern course, specific open access courses will be open to non-Stern students one week after registration initially opens.

The prerequisites for those courses must be met in order to register and courses not on the list are not open to non-Stern students. It is recommended that students use the edit swap feature in Albert for the intermediate and advanced courses to increase the likelihood of registering for the course once it opens to the NYU Community. Space cannot be guaranteed and certain Stern courses may never open to non-Stern students. All Stern graduate courses (MBA and PhD programs) are closed to undergraduate students .

Stern has strict policies about changing sections of a course that is already filled. Students should not ask instructors for permission to change sections or to be added to a closed course. Those requests should be sent to nyuad.registrar@nyu.edu .

Stern does not permit the auditing of courses.

Stern does NOT waive pre-requisites. Do not contact an instructor or the Stern advising office to request exceptions to this rule.

-

- Tandon School of Engineering

The Tandon School of Engineering (SoE) is located in neighboring downtown Brooklyn. Tandon is one of New York's most comprehensive schools of engineering, applied science, and technology.

Enrollment in Tandon courses can be done through the Albert student registration system. However not all NYUAD engineering courses that will count as pre-requisites are recognized in Albert. As a result, students planning to enroll in courses within the Tandon must work directly with their mentor and Dean Sinanoglu on their course registration and may need to be issued permission codes for their courses. Note: students should not ask for permission codes for multiple sections of the same course.

The commute from Tandon to Washington Square is about 30 minutes each way. There is a free NYU shuttle services from Washington Square to Tandon, but the pick-up times are limited. Care should be taken to schedule classes that can accommodate this travel time.

In particular, Film and New Media students may be interested in courses offered by the Integrated Digital Media Program (DM-UY XXXX). Students may contact Eric Maiello ( em1680@nyu.edu ) starting October 15 for permission codes.

Tandon also offers 13 cross-school minors that are open to all NYU students.

- Silver School of Social Work

The Silver School of Social Work provides a rich environment for the education professional social workers, offering programs at the undergraduate, master's, and doctoral level. NYUAD students interested in courses at the Silver School should consider courses in the joint CAS-Silver School minors in Social Work or Poverty Studies:

Read more on the Social Work Minor and Minor in Poverty Studies .

If students are interested in courses outside of the cross-school minor, those courses should be listed on the course intent form to facilitate the possibility of registering for the course.

- Steinhardt School of Culture, Education, and Human Development

The Steinhardt School of Culture, Education, and Human Development offers just under 20 undergraduate programs in: Applied Psychology, Studio Art, Teacher Education, Health, Media Studies, Music and Music Professions, and Theatre (musical and education). These programs have a pre-professional focus and students apply to be admitted into a specific major. NYUAD students are encouraged to look at the cross-school minors open to the NYU community in the following programs:

- American Sign Language (Department of Applied Psychology)

- Child Development and Social Intervention (with the Child Study Center)

- Communicative Sciences and Disorders (with CAS)

- Digital Art and Design

- Educational Theater

- Food and Nutrition Studies (with CAS)

- Global and Urban Education Studies (with CAS, Social Work, and Wagner)

- Studio Art

- Media, Culture, and Communication

Should a student wish to take a Steinhardt course not included in the cross-school minors, special arrangements will need to be made.

Students majoring in Music or Art and Art History who would like to take advanced courses, will need special arrangements made with those departments well in advance, although there can be no guarantee permission will be granted. Students should include special requests on the course intent form, work with their mentors, and contact nyuad.registrar@nyu.edu .

- Tisch School of the Arts

Tisch School of the Arts is one of the leading arts conservatory programs in the country. The undergraduate program consists of the Maurice Kanbar Institute of Film and Television, the Institute of Performing Arts, the Skirball Center for New Media, the Clive Davis Department of Recorded Music, and the Department of Art and Public Policy. Admission to one of these programs is highly competitive and access to most Tisch courses tends to be restricted to Tisch students. NYUAD students interested in Tisch courses should first consider the Open Arts courses available to all NYU students or courses in the following cross-school minors:

- Art and Public Policy

- Asian Film and Media

- Cinema Studies (with CAS)

- Dance

- Documentary

- Film Production

- Game Design

- Performance Studies

- Producing

Film and New Media students should indicate at least seven courses they wish to take on their course intent forms. Registration will be done in conjunction with Film and Television’s advising office at least one week after registration opens for the spring semester and during early July for the fall semester. No guarantees can be made that students will be registered for specially requested sections or for their top choices. Moreover, students should not expect to take four Film courses. Sight and Sound: Documentary is the only Sight and Sound course that might open to NYUAD students; all other Sight and Sound course will not be available unless permission is received from the NYUAD Film and New Media program head prior to registration.

The following courses listed here are open to all students, and students may register for these courses on their own. Film students should also consider Tish Open Arts courses and Gallatin Arts courses , which are available the first week of registration.

Film and New Media students may also be interested in courses offered by the Interactive Telecommunications Program (ITP). ITP is a graduate-level program, but courses are available to undergraduates with special permission from the department. Please note that the advanced nature of ITP courses require students to be extremely committed to the course and demonstrate a high level of achievement. Film students might also consider the Tandon Integrated Digital Media program (see above).

After the initial registration period, non-majors may only request changes to their schedule by completing the Course Enrollment Request Form for Non-majors . You may only submit three classes. Submitting this form places you on an in-house waitlist only, and does not guarantee that you will be enrolled in a Kanbar Film & TV course. If a course is available, you will be contacted with instructions on how to enroll. Please do not expect to be contacted until close to the start of the semester. You should not contact any administrator in the Film & TV division or an NYUAD administrator with requests for updates.

Theater majors who wish to take studio courses will need to work closely with their mentors on audition tapes and interviews that will be submitted to Tisch for possible assignment to the Playwrights Horizons Theater School, Experimental Theater Wing, or Classical Acting Studios. There is no guarantee that NYUAD students will be admitted to a Tisch Drama program. If a student wishes to take courses outside of the Drama department, those courses should be listed on the course preference form and efforts will be made to register a student for requested courses. Theater students should also consider Tish Open Arts courses and Gallatin Arts courses , which are available the first week of registration.

Recorded Music : The Tisch Clive Davis Institute provides undergraduates with business and artistic training in recorded music. Students matriculated in this program have specially auditioned. There is limited access to recorded music courses for Music majors who have completed appropriate coursework in Abu Dhabi. Registration would occur after Tisch Recorded Music majors register and would be dependent on available space.

- Robert F. Wagner School Graduate School of Public Service (undergraduate minor)

The Robert F. Wagner Graduate School of Public Service offers advanced programs leading to the professional degrees of Master of Public Administration, Master of Urban Planning, Executive Master of Public Administration and Doctor of Philosophy. Undergraduates can take advantage of Wagner's programs and faculty by taking courses in the cross-school minors:

- Social Entrepreneurship (with Stern)

- Public Policy and Management (with Stern)

- Social and Public Policy (with CAS)

- Multifaith and Spiritual Leadership (with CAS and Silver)

Registration is open to NYU undergraduates on a first-come, first-served basis.

- School of Professional Studies (SPS)

Courses in the School of Professional Studies (SPS) cannot be counted toward a degree at any NYU school due to the nature of the coursework. Students should not consider SPS courses as viable options while on a study away. Further, almost all SPS courses require a separate tuition charge not covered by financial aid. Courses that are typically designated with a subject code suffix of "-CE" and would not be covered or count toward degree requirements.

Related official links:
https://students.nyuad.nyu.edu/academics/global-education/study-away/course-equivalencies/study-away-equivalencies/new-york/

- Global and Urban Education Studies (with CAS, Social Work, and Wagner)

- Studio Art

- Media, Culture, and Communication

Should a student wish to take a Steinhardt course not included in the cross-school minors, special arrangements will need to be made.

Students majoring in Music or Art and Art History who would like to take advanced courses, will need special arrangements made with those departments well in advance, although there can be no guarantee permission will be granted. Students should include special requests on the course intent form, work with their mentors, and contact nyuad.registrar@nyu.edu .

- Tisch School of the Arts

Tisch School of the Arts is one of the leading arts conservatory programs in the country. The undergraduate program consists of the Maurice Kanbar Institute of Film and Television, the Institute of Performing Arts, the Skirball Center for New Media, the Clive Davis Department of Recorded Music, and the Department of Art and Public Policy. Admission to one of these programs is highly competitive and access to most Tisch courses tends to be restricted to Tisch students. NYUAD students interested in Tisch courses should first consider the Open Arts courses available to all NYU students or courses in the following cross-school minors:

- Art and Public Policy

- Asian Film and Media

- Cinema Studies (with CAS)

- Dance

- Documentary

- Film Production

- Game Design

- Performance Studies

- Producing

Film and New Media students should indicate at least seven courses they wish to take on their course intent forms. Registration will be done in conjunction with Film and Television’s advising office at least one week after registration opens for the spring semester and during early July for the fall semester. No guarantees can be made that students will be registered for specially requested sections or for their top choices. Moreover, students should not expect to take four Film courses. Sight and Sound: Documentary is the only Sight and Sound course that might open to NYUAD students; all other Sight and Sound course will not be available unless permission is received from the NYUAD Film and New Media program head prior to registration.

The following courses listed here are open to all students, and students may register for these courses on their own. Film students should also consider Tish Open Arts courses and Gallatin Arts courses , which are available the first week of registration.

Film and New Media students may also be interested in courses offered by the Interactive Telecommunications Program (ITP). ITP is a graduate-level program, but courses are available to undergraduates with special permission from the department. Please note that the advanced nature of ITP courses require students to be extremely committed to the course and demonstrate a high level of achievement. Film students might also consider the Tandon Integrated Digital Media program (see above).

After the initial registration period, non-majors may only request changes to their schedule by completing the Course Enrollment Request Form for Non-majors . You may only submit three classes. Submitting this form places you on an in-house waitlist only, and does not guarantee that you will be enrolled in a Kanbar Film & TV course. If a course is available, you will be contacted with instructions on how to enroll. Please do not expect to be contacted until close to the start of the semester. You should not contact any administrator in the Film & TV division or an NYUAD administrator with requests for updates.

Theater majors who wish to take studio courses will need to work closely with their mentors on audition tapes and interviews that will be submitted to Tisch for possible assignment to the Playwrights Horizons Theater School, Experimental Theater Wing, or Classical Acting Studios. There is no guarantee that NYUAD students will be admitted to a Tisch Drama program. If a student wishes to take courses outside of the Drama department, those courses should be listed on the course preference form and efforts will be made to register a student for requested courses. Theater students should also consider Tish Open Arts courses and Gallatin Arts courses , which are available the first week of registration.

Recorded Music : The Tisch Clive Davis Institute provides undergraduates with business and artistic training in recorded music. Students matriculated in this program have specially auditioned. There is limited access to recorded music courses for Music majors who have completed appropriate coursework in Abu Dhabi. Registration would occur after Tisch Recorded Music majors register and would be dependent on available space.

- Robert F. Wagner School Graduate School of Public Service (undergraduate minor)

The Robert F. Wagner Graduate School of Public Service offers advanced programs leading to the professional degrees of Master of Public Administration, Master of Urban Planning, Executive Master of Public Administration and Doctor of Philosophy. Undergraduates can take advantage of Wagner's programs and faculty by taking courses in the cross-school minors:

- Social Entrepreneurship (with Stern)

- Public Policy and Management (with Stern)

- Social and Public Policy (with CAS)

- Multifaith and Spiritual Leadership (with CAS and Silver)

Registration is open to NYU undergraduates on a first-come, first-served basis.

- School of Professional Studies (SPS)

Courses in the School of Professional Studies (SPS) cannot be counted toward a degree at any NYU school due to the nature of the coursework. Students should not consider SPS courses as viable options while on a study away. Further, almost all SPS courses require a separate tuition charge not covered by financial aid. Courses that are typically designated with a subject code suffix of "-CE" and would not be covered or count toward degree requirements.

title: Study Away Policy · NYUAD Students
text:
N YUAD Study Away Policy

Semester-Long Study Away in the NYU Global Network : Students may spend up to two semesters studying abroad at academic sites mostly within the NYU global network, which includes the degree-granting campuses in New York, Abu Dhabi, and Shanghai, and 13 global academic centers: Accra, Berlin, Buenos Aires, Florence, London, Los Angeles, Madrid, Paris, Prague, Sydney, Tel Aviv, Tulsa, and Washington, DC. These global academic centers connect students from NYU Abu Dhabi, NYU Shanghai, and NYU New York who study together and experience the diversity of NYU’s global network. Each of the centers offers courses in the local language, history, and culture, academic lectures by distinguished faculty and leaders of the local communities, and co-curricular activities to explore the region, meet local students and figures, and develop new language skills.

Global Pathways for Study Away : NYUAD faculty have identified site preferences within the NYU global academic centers for each NYUAD major with an eye toward developing students as well-rounded scholars of the liberal arts and sciences, highly competent producers of knowledge in a field of specialization, and socially responsible members of any community they choose to join. These pathways represent general directions for study away in each major. Students work with their faculty mentors and assigned Global Education advisors to determine what study away plan is most appropriate for their individual academic program.

Alternative Study Away Programs : The majority of NYUAD students will study away at one or more of the NYU global academic centers to take advantage of the unique curricular and technological offerings of NYU’s global network. However, if a student’s academic program would significantly benefit from instruction not available at the NYU global network sites or in Abu Dhabi, students have the opportunity to be considered to study away at one of NYU’s partner institutions by participating in a student exchange. The International Exchange Program enables select students to study at a variety of institutions—all distinguished research universities—while earning NYU credit and being immersed in the culture of some of the world’s most exciting cities.

Preparation for Study Away : Careful academic and logistical preparation is required for students who intend to study away. Students must attend group and individual study away advising sessions and consult with their faculty mentors early in their academic careers to be certain study away experiences can fit well with their major requirements and progress toward graduation. Some programs have specific prerequisites, including the completion of courses related to a particular language, region, culture, discipline, research methodology, or issue.

Academic Credit : Academic credit from study away programs within the NYU global network is treated like credit awarded for coursework at NYU Abu Dhabi. All courses from study away programs are recorded on the student’s transcript. Grades from courses offered by the NYU global network sites or other credit-bearing programs taught by NYU Abu Dhabi or NYU faculty are recorded on the transcript and factored into a student’s NYUAD grade point average (GPA). Credits for courses taken at non-NYU or non-NYUAD programs are subject to the NYUAD policy for transfer credit and are not included in GPA calculations.

Graduation Requirements : All successfully completed courses taken at NYU global academic centers automatically count toward the 128 minimum credit hours required for graduation. However, students must consult with their faculty mentors in advance of study away and refer to online study away equivalency charts (available on the student portal) to determine whether courses taken abroad can be used to fulfill specific NYUAD graduation requirements, such as the Core or the major. Courses taken at non-NYU programs generally require prior approval by the faculty to count toward the total credit hours’ requirement.

Full-time Student Status : Students must maintain full-time status and carry the equivalent of a four-course workload for that status while participating in any semester study away programs. Students may earn credit for no more than 18 credits on any semester study away program unless they receive prior authorization for an overload from NYU Abu Dhabi.

Costs : In general, fees for approved semester long study away programs are similar to those for a semester at NYU Abu Dhabi. Financial support is applied to cover these costs the same way it is when a student is studying in Abu Dhabi.

Application Process : Although study away is encouraged at NYU Abu Dhabi, the opportunity to participate in any study away program is a privilege and the application process is competitive.

Application Timeline : NYU Abu Dhabi has one annual preliminary application deadline of November 25 for study away programs in the coming academic year. This early deadline helps upper-class students and their faculty mentors do long-range planning for study away to ensure these important experiences fit well with the selection of a major, normal progress toward graduation, and preparation for the Capstone Project during the student’s senior year. First-year students can apply by June 1 of their first year for study away in the spring semester of their sophomore year. Final applications are typically due by January 15 for fall semester study and by August 15 for spring semester study.

Students may typically apply to study away as early as the second semester of their sophomore year and as late as the second semester of their junior year. Study away before or after this time frame requires exceptional approval from the Office of Global Education upon recommendation from the student’s mentor or the special determination of an academic program. The application process for participation in study away programs includes the preliminary and the final application stages with required deadlines as listed above. Interested students must meet all NYUAD and NYU global network application deadlines. Programs outside the NYU’s global network require students to complete the program’s own application process in addition to the NYUAD forms and may have different (often earlier) deadlines.

Selection Process : Selection for any study away program is based on a student’s academic record, the strength of the application materials, and academic preparation for and suitability of the chosen program to the individual student’s academic goals. The competitiveness of the application process varies based on the number of applicants, and the allotment of limited spaces on some programs. The goal of a first semester of study away is to advance students as well-rounded scholars and global citizens within the liberal arts and sciences tradition. For most students, the second semester of sophomore year presents an ideal time to place the “big questions” of their globally- focused core courses into a new local context, explore new subject areas before finalizing their choice of majors by the end of sophomore year, develop a higher level of competency in a foreign language, and develop greater intercultural understanding toward social responsibility through sustained engagement of difference and the ability to navigate that difference toward greater common ground and common good. A second semester of study away—if approved — needs to be carefully designed and planned to support a student’s development as a scholar in their field(s) of specialization.

Students must present a compelling academic rationale for their program choice and course selection, demonstrating that the chosen program and courses: provide essential academic content for their field(s) of specialization that would otherwise not be available at NYU Abu Dhabi, provide the opportunity to conduct research towards developing the capstone project (e.g. data collection, piloting a research area, comparative work, access to archives and collections, specialized arts practice training,) connect the student with local faculty and/or field experts in the host site who can provide essential guidance on capstone project work or other essential research/arts practice, and allow the student to put their theoretical and research training into guided practice in a way that benefits specifically from the cultural context of the host country.

The Office of Global Education is charged with reviewing study away applications and selecting students. Applications for the second semester away are also reviewed by the faculty in the student’s chosen major(s).

J-Term and Study Away Semesters : Students who entered Fall 2026 or later must successfully complete at least one J-Term course before they can become eligible for a study away semester.

title: Study Away Program Updates · NYUAD Students
text:
Attention : First- and Second-Year Students Planning to Major in BOS, Computer Science, or Economics

We regret to inform you that the Global Studies Track will no longer be available as a study away program due to changes to its visa-related status. The last cohort of the program is the current juniors who are participating in this 2024-2025 academic year. We cannot accept or review applications for future years.

We understand the serious impact this may have on your academic and career planning. You are welcome to contact the study away advisors in Global Education, your faculty mentors, the ARC, and/or the Career Development Center (CDC) for guidance.

As you rethink how to obtain professional experience in the United States or elsewhere, please be mindful of the following options and resources:

- Unpaid, For-Credit Internships: You can apply for summer grant opportunities, including in New York or Washington DC if you find an unpaid internship or undergraduate research project in these locations where NYU has an academic presence and where the appropriate visa status can be supported. Pursuing unpaid internships through summer grants and the one-credit directed summer study course that facilitates the visa continues to offer a practical way of building your CV/resume. More information about Summer 2025 opportunities will be posted on the Student Portal by January 2025.

- J-1 Visa Mobility Awareness Session with Fragomen: This winter, the CDC in collaboration with the immigration law firm Fragomen will be hosting a session about J-1 visa possibilities for US-based internships and early career experience, as part of their Career Mobility Education series. This will include the opportunity to connect 1:1 with an immigration lawyer for junior and senior students. Details will be shared on Handshake.

- Alternative Study Away Site Options & Internships: You can also consider applying for the semester study abroad programs noted below that include an internship course and facilitated internship opportunities. General information about these internship opportunities can be found here . Please also explore the links below:

title: NYUAD Institute · NYUAD Students
text:
The NYU Abu Dhabi (NYUAD) Institute is a major hub of intellectual and creative activity, advanced research, and higher education. It operates in two closely linked areas of activity: Research and Programs. The Institute creates singular opportunities for leading faculty members from across the arts, humanities, social sciences, sciences, engineering, and the professions to carry out creative scholarship and conduct research on issues of major disciplinary, multidisciplinary, and global significance. The Institute hosts academic conferences, workshops, lectures, film series, performances, and other public programs directed to local audiences; to NYUAD faculty, students, and staff; and to the worldwide academic and research community.

All Institute public events are free and transportation is provided to the venue of the event. Students can find out about Institute events and research by going on the Institute’s website . In addition, the Institute publishes monthly brochures and posters that can be found around campus. Students are also welcome to suggest public programs, and can get involved with Institute events and volunteer with the Institute by emailing nyuad.institute@nyu.edu , or visiting our office in Humanities Building (A6)-1172C .

title: Undergraduate Academic Policies · NYUAD Students
text:
Accommodating Course Assessment Adjustments

- Spring 2020 First-Year Transcript (“Covered Grades”) Policy

In response to the transition to online teaching and the various disruptions students and faculty are facing in their lives and academic experiences, NYU Abu Dhabi will apply its First-Year Transcript (“Covered Grades”) Policy for all NYU Abu Dhabi students in NYU’s global network on an opt-in basis for the spring 2020 semester.

- View the policy

- Spring 2020 Course Assessment Adjustments

In the move to online teaching and learning some adjustments to course schedules and course assignments are likely. Individual faculty members have broad latitude in making the adjustments that they feel are necessary best to achieve and assess the existing course learning outcomes laid out in their syllabus. Students should be prepared to work cooperatively with faculty in accommodating reasonable changes to syllabi. The Office of Academic Affairs, in consultation with the Deans, has developed guidelines for any necessary changes.

- View the guidelines

Academic Policies

The following is a summary of Academic Policies at NYU Abu Dhabi. Unless otherwise noted, students should direct all questions or concerns regarding these policies to their Faculty Mentor, who will liaise with the appropriate members of the university administration as needed.

Title | Description | Keywords

Absences | Guidance on student absences. |

Academic Integrity Policy and Procedure | The relationship between students and faculty at NYU Abu Dhabi is defined by a shared commitment to academic excellence and is grounded in an expectation of fairness, honesty, and respect. | Academic, Dishonesty, Integrity, Policy, Faculty, Plagiarism, Cheating,

Academic Standing | This policy defines good academic standing and outlines the steps that will be taken to ensure students are informed of their academic standing, are helped if they have a temporary lapse, and are assisted in finding alternatives to NYU Abu Dhabi, if necessary. | students academic standing policy

Access to Educational Records | NYU Abu Dhabi is fully committed to the protection of the privacy of student records. | student educational record policy academic

Adding and Dropping Courses | Within the following time frames, a student may add or drop a course (or section) without record on the student's permanent transcript. | students academic add drop course transcript

Advanced Standing | Information on high school coursework or for external assessments, such as AP or IB exams. | students academic advanced standing credit policy

Attendance | Although the administration of NYUAD does not supervise attendance of classes, it supports the standards established by instructors. | students academic attendance course policy

Auditing | Students will be permitted to audit a course with the permission of the course's primary instructor. | students academic auditing policy

Commencement Marching Eligibility | Eligibility to participate in the NYUAD Commencement Ceremony. | eligibility to participate in the NYUAD Commencement Ceremony

Course Load | Information on the student course load. | students academic course load policy

Degree Completion in Residence | Students must be in residence in Abu Dhabi for their final semester of enrollment (immediately prior to graduation) except in rare cases. | Degree Completion in Residence

Directed Studies | The approval process for a Directed Study must be completed prior to start of the semester. |

Double Counting | Information on how courses may count for more than one requirement. | students academic course requirements policy

Exemptions | All exemptions related to the completion of degree requirements are by application to the appropriate Academic Dean. | students degree exemptions requirements policy

Final Semester Assessments | Information on scheduling final assessments, weighting, proctoring, missing exams, and conflicts. |

First-Year Writing Seminar | This policy is designed to ensure that students prioritize enrolling in this course during their first year of enrollment. |

Grade Appeal | To dispute an assigned grade, students must appeal directly to the instructor of record. | students academic grade dispute change

Grading | How grades are computed at NYUAD. | students academic grade grading policy

Graduation Honors | NYUAD will have Latin honors and departmental honors at the time of graduation. | students academic latin departmental honors policy

Incompletes | An incomplete grade of "I" will be permitted only in extraordinary circumstances that prevent a student from completing required course work by the end of the semester. | student academic incomplete policy

Accommodating Course Assessment Adjustments

- Spring 2020 First-Year Transcript (“Covered Grades”) Policy

In response to the transition to online teaching and the various disruptions students and faculty are facing in their lives and academic experiences, NYU Abu Dhabi will apply its First-Year Transcript (“Covered Grades”) Policy for all NYU Abu Dhabi students in NYU’s global network on an opt-in basis for the spring 2020 semester.

- View the policy

- Spring 2020 Course Assessment Adjustments

In the move to online teaching and learning some adjustments to course schedules and course assignments are likely. Individual faculty members have broad latitude in making the adjustments that they feel are necessary best to achieve and assess the existing course learning outcomes laid out in their syllabus. Students should be prepared to work cooperatively with faculty in accommodating reasonable changes to syllabi. The Office of Academic Affairs, in consultation with the Deans, has developed guidelines for any necessary changes.

- View the guidelines

title: Albert Student Information System · NYUAD Students
text:
Named after the New York University founding father, Albert Gallatin, Albert is the portal to NYU’s student information system. It can be used by students who have an authorized NYU Net ID and password to browse the course catalog, view classes being offered in a semester, plan and enroll in classes, view class and exam schedules, view and request transcripts, update personal details

All students, former students, alumni, faculty and administrators now have access to Albert , NYU's online student information system. You can also navigate to Albert from NYUHome , under the academics tab. A valid NetID and password are required.

Albert Instructions

General instructions on using Albert are available from the NYU Registrars Office.

You can also review our registration guides for step-by-step instructions on how to validate , add (enroll) , drop , swap , and more.

How to use the " Shopping Cart " to plan course enrollment (adding and validating classes): https://www.nyu.edu/students/student-information-and-resources/registration-records-and-graduation/albert-help/training/students/registration/add.html

Forgot Password
To retrieve your NYU Login password, please visit the NYU Start page .

Forgot Password and Password Reminder
If you forgot your NYU Login password and password reminder, please contact the IT Service Desk or dial 88888 from any campus phone.

Unable to Access Albert with a Valid NetID and Password
If you are able to successfully sign into Student Portal but are having trouble in accessing Albert, please contact the IT Service Desk or dial 88888 from any campus phone.

title: Graduation Requirements · NYUAD Students
text:
Last updated May 8, 2026

To graduate from NYU Abu Dhabi you are required to complete:

- 128 credit hours

- Core Curriculum courses:

- A First-Year Writing Seminar , completed in your first year

- Four Core Competency courses (CSTS, CADT, CCEA, CDAD)

- One Core Colloquium Course taught at NYUAD during a regular semester

- Two J-Term Field Colloquium courses — 3 credits each

- One course that satisfies the following:

- Islamic Studies
(Denoted by courses with an X suffix, e.g., ACS-UH 1810 X Making of the Modern Middle East)

- An academic major

- Two physical education (PHYED-UH) activities

- A Capstone Project

- And maintain a cumulative grade point average (GPA) of at least 2.0

128-Credit Hour Requirement

Most courses at NYU Abu Dhabi are four credits each. Generally students will need to enroll in 16 credits each semester.

Writing

Because strong writing is so important to academic success in every career and in every academic major, NYUAD requires all students to take a First-Year Writing Seminar in their first year.

NYUAD Core Curriculum

Students are required to complete seven Core Curriculum courses, including one colloquium, two field colloquia, and one course in each of the four Core Competency areas. Colloquia are courses that are highly interdisciplinary and combine at least two of the broad areas of knowledge described in the competency areas. These courses can be found only in the Core and will not be cross-listed with major or minor programs.

Competency courses can be specifically designed Core courses or they may be courses offered within other academic programs that are cross-listed with one or more of the competency areas.

The four competencies are:

- Arts, Design, and Technology

- Cultural Exploration and Analysis

- Data and Discovery

- Structures of Thought and Society

The Core also requires that students have taken at least one course that satisfies an Islamic Studies (X) requirement.

The Islamic Studies requirement can be met through many courses across the curriculum and in the Core.

— Read more on the Core Curriculum

Academic Major

Meeting the requirements for an academic major is central to completing your education. If you have a good idea of what you want to major in, you can focus on the requirements of the individual major or majors that you are considering. However, it is perhaps even more important to think about how to select your major. — Read more

- View the sample major course schedules

Physical and Health Education Requirement

Undergraduate Students are required to complete two unique seven-week Physical and Health Education (PHYED) courses during their academic career. Each semester, there are a wide variety of courses to choose from in disciplines such as swimming, martial arts, and yoga. We suggest that you identify courses that look interesting to you and aim to include them in your academic program over your first two years. Please note that participation in a recognized University Sports Team does count toward one of your PHYED requirements as long as attendance and participation criteria are met — attendance to 80% of total games and practices in a semester. Also remember that physical activity is often an excellent way to break up your time and we hope that you will participate in physical activities well beyond the two required activities. The attendance and commitment of PHYED classes applies to both NYUAD students and students studying away at NYUAD and your grade will appear on your transcript. — Read more on the Physical Education Requirement

Capstone Project

The Capstone experience can be one of the most meaningful activities in your undergraduate career. It will be the time when you are able to combine talents developed over the full range of your academic preparation, as well as an opportunity to demonstrate to yourself, your peers, and the faculty the breadth of your learning. However, the Capstone experience doesn't really figure much into planning for your first-semester courses, so you can safely defer consideration of this important requirement until later semesters. — Read more on Capstones

Minimum GPA Requirement

- Students are required to have a minimum GPA of 2.0 or above to be considered in good academic standing. Additionally it is important to note the following: Only courses in which grades of C or better are earned may be counted toward the completion of your major or toward satisfying any core requirements.

- During your first year, only courses in which you earn a grade of at least C- count toward the 128 credit hours that you need to graduate (see the Transcript Policy for more details).

- How do I explore options so that I can choose the best major?

- What courses will best prepare me for my specific postgraduate career?

title: Graduation, Diplomas, and Commencement · NYUAD Students
text:
Graduation Process

- How do I know if I am on track to graduate?

Review your Degree Progress Report (DPR) each semester in Albert. Contact your academic advisor before each enrollment period begins (when the enrollment shopping cart opens), and as you approach graduation. Awarding of degrees depends on successful completion of all requirements in your DPR — take action to officially resolve any requirements marked as Not Satisfied.

Documentation and Verification

- Awarding Degrees

Degrees are awarded by the Office of the Registrar. Once awarded, your record is finalized(!) and no changes can be made, including grade changes or updates to your major or minor.

At the beginning (before the end of add/drop of the 14-week session) of your final term or semester, be sure to check your Degree Progress Report in Albert to ensure your declarations are properly listed and none of your requirements are marked as Not Satisfied. No additional minor(s) or majors can be added after the add/drop period of the 14-week session of your final semester. Students can have a maximum of two majors and two minors. Additional minors above two are removed in the order that the student declared them.

The degree conferral dates are listing on the academic calendar and students can view their degree completion on their transcript starting the week after the conferral date.

- Will I receive a transcript when I graduate?

Students can order your official transcripts at any time through the National Student Clearinghouse .

Before you place your order, please follow these important steps:

-
Check Your Degree Status First: Log into Albert and review your unofficial transcript. Make sure your degree is officially listed as "posted" (you can find this in the top left-hand corner).

-
Send Directly to the Recipient: When ordering official transcripts, have the National Student Clearinghouse send the transcript directly to the graduate school or company requesting it.

Important: Do not send the transcript to yourself first with the plan to forward it. Once you open or forward a transcript, it is no longer considered official. Copies sent to yourself will have the words "Unofficial" appear in the background. When sending directly to a company or school, the word "Unofficial" does NOT appear. Students can always order a copy of their transcript for their own records but graduate schools will not accept official transcripts if it comes directly from the student. The National Student Clearinghouse is the official provider of NYU transcripts and the transcript is sent through an NYU registrar's email address.

- How do I get proof that I graduated if I can’t wait for my diploma?

After completing your degree program, a degree completion letter will be issued after the conferral date.

- My employer/immigration is asking for a graduation verification letter. What should I do?

After completing your degree program, a degree confirmation is sent to each student to use for employment, graduate schools, etc. Students should check their email the day after the conferral date for their degree confirmation letter (graduation verification).

Diploma Information

- When will I receive my diploma?

Diplomas are shipped approximately 6-8 weeks following conferrals, provided there are no holds on your record. The date you receive your diploma would not match the conferral date on your diploma and transcripts. The conferral date is the official date of record, you could receive your physical diploma from that date onward - when it's ready for distribution, and as long as there are no active diploma holds on your record.

Important Information about Account Holds and Diplomas

Below is a list of holds managed by the Bursar’s Office. If a " Y" appears in the column next to a hold, it means that hold will block you from registering for classes and/or receiving your diploma.

To avoid any delays in getting physical or electronic (CeDiploma) diploma, students should make sure to clear all holds before graduation.

Timing on the release of the hold and issuing the CeDiploma: Once you clear a hold with Student Finance or the Bursar’s Office, it can take an additional 2 to 3 weeks for the CeDiploma (electronic diploma) to be generated and ready for download from the original release date as the university processes the request.

For questions about the holds students should contact either:

- NYUAD Student Finance ( nyuad.studentfinance@nyu.edu ) or

- NYU Bursar's Office ( bursar.studentaccounts@nyu.edu )

Code | Description | Registration Hold | Diploma Hold

ZAG | Account at Collection Agency | Y | Y

ZBB | Bursar Balance | |

ZCO | Internal Collections | Y | Y

ZDE | De-Enrollment for Non-Payment | Y |

ZDP | Diploma Hold | | Y

ZLS | Loan Services Hold | Y | Y

ZNC | Account at Collection Agency | Y | Y

ZNF | Not Financially Cleared | |

ZNP | Not Eligible for Payment Plan | |

ZPA | Payment Agreement | Y | y

ZPC | Pre-Collections | Y | Y

ZRG | Registration Hold | Y |

ZRP | Returned Payment Hold | |

- What information will be on my diploma?

Your diploma serves as a formal certificate of your degree. It includes:

-
Your Full Name (as specified in your graduation application)

-
Degree Type (e.g., Bachelor of Arts or Bachelor of Science)

-
Date of Conferral

-
Latin Honors (if applicable)

Please note: Majors and minors are recorded on your official transcript rather than the diploma itself. For students with a double major, the diploma will reflect the primary degree type associated with your capstone coursework.

- Will my major and minor be printed on my diploma?

Your diploma will list the degree of your Capstone major degree level (e.g., Bachelor of Arts or Bachelor of Science) and not the major(s). The diploma does not list any minors and that information can be found on the transcript.

- I’m completing two majors and they have different degrees (BA and BS), will they both show on my records?

Both majors and degrees will appear on your transcript if they are declared, however only your primary degree level in which your capstone work was completed (e.g., Bachelor of Arts, Bachelor of Science - not major) will appear on your diploma.

- Can the name on my diploma be different from my transcripts?

The name printed on your diploma will be based on your selection on the Diploma Options page in Albert, where you can choose either your Primary or Preferred name. Students can update their primary name by submitting a copy of their passport to the NYUAD Office of the Registrar at least two months before graduation so requests can be processed in a timely manner. This page becomes available once they are applied to graduate (usually within the first four weeks of the final semester). Please note that all name changes must be submitted at least two months prior to your commencement date. Requests made after this deadline will require you to order and pay for a replacement diploma after your degree is officially conferred.

Note: For ministry authentication and verification of your diploma, it is highly recommended that the name on your diploma matches your transcripts (Primary name) and your passport.

Please note that name changes require processing time to reflect on your credentials. Allow at least one month after your name change is approved for the update to appear on a new printed diploma or CeDiploma.

- What is a CeDiploma and how can I order one?

CeDiplomas are certified electronic diplomas for secure electronic sharing. Your CeDiploma/electronic diploma will be ordered on the 15th of the month following conferrals and available shortly after. Any holds will prevent a CeDiploma from being created and will delay the issuance by 2-3 weeks after the hold is cleared.

Timing on the release of the hold and issuing the CeDiploma: Once you clear a hold with Student Finance or the Bursar’s Office, it can take an additional 2 to 3 weeks for the CeDiploma (electronic diploma) to be generated and ready for download from the original release date as the university processes the request. Please note that name changes require processing time to reflect on your credentials. Allow at least one month after your name change is approved for the update to appear on a new printed diploma or CeDiploma.

For questions about the holds students should contact either:

- NYUAD Student Finance ( nyuad.studentfinance@nyu.edu ) or

- NYU Bursar's Office ( bursar.studentaccounts@nyu.edu )

Visit NYU Albert and:

- Click on Grades and Transcripts

- Click on the E-Diploma link

- Click on the CeDiploma link at the bottom of the page

Please note:

- There is a $14.95 fee for this service

- CeDiplomas/CeCertificates are available for students who graduated after January 1, 2016. If you graduated before that date, you may order a CeDiploma/CeCertificate by following the ordering instructions at “ Replacement Diplomas ".

- Is there any way to expedite the diploma process?

Unfortunately the diploma process cannot be expedited due to the number of students graduating each year.

- Can I get my diploma if there is a diploma hold on my records?

No, your diploma cannot be released until the diploma hold is resolved.

- Can someone pick up my diploma for me?

Once available, you will receive an email allowing you to select your preference: picking up your diploma, having someone pick it up on your behalf, or having it shipped to you.

- How do I attest my diploma?

Follow the procedures outlined on the UAE Ministry of Education's website for attesting your degree. For more information contact the NYU Abu Dhabi Career Development Center .

- My diploma has been lost, damaged, etc. How do I get another one?

If you have graduated from NYU Abu Dhabi and your diploma was lost or has been damaged, you may purchase a replacement diploma by completing the online form accessible in the Albert portal in the Other Resources tab.

See additional information on Diplomas on the NYU Paper and Electronic Diplomas page .

Commencement and Ceremony Information

- Where can I find information about Commencement ceremonies, regalia, tickets, etc.?

Visit the CDC for information and questions related to ceremony logistics starting in the spring semester.

- What is my conferral date?

Conferral dates are included in the online Academic Calendars.

- What’s the difference between conferral and Commencement?

Conferral is when your degree is officially recognized as awarded. Commencement is the ceremony in celebration (or anticipation) of degree completion.

- Do I receive my diploma at the commencement ceremony?

Degree conferral takes a few weeks after final grades are posted and are not available upon Commencement. Diplomas are usually shipped to graduates 6-8 weeks after Commencement.

- I will be finishing my degree during the summer. When will I be able to participate in the Commencement ceremony?

Students who only have one class that can completed in the summer (after the spring semester) are eligible to participate in the May graduation ceremony. Students with more than one class needed to complete their degree after the spring semester are eligible to participate in the graduation ceremony in the following year. Information about summer program participation in commencement ceremonies is published each year by the Senior Year Newsletter. Look for information in the fall semester of your final year.

Honors and Awards

- How do I know my class ranking?

NYU Abu Dhabi does not calculate or maintain class ranking for their students. Latin honors can be used to indicate what quartile of the class a student is in. Latin honors is based on degree GPA and does not include first year grades in the calculation.

- Who qualifies for honors? What are the criteria for Latin honors?

The cutoffs of Latin honors vary for each NYU school and department; those published on the New York website are for the respective New York schools and departments. NYU Abu Dhabi does not publish the cutoffs because our student body numbers are still fluctuating greatly as we grow. However, the criteria used at NYU Abu Dhabi is the top 5 percent (summa cum laude), next 10 percent (magna cum laude), and then finally the next 15 percent (cum laude) of the graduating class in each academic division. The GPA used to determine latin honors does not include first year grades.

- How do I know if I received Latin Honors?

The degree GPA (which does not include first year grades) and any Latin Honor (latin honor calculations also do not include first year grades) can be found on both the official and unofficial transcripts after the degree is awarded. The degree GPA and any latin honors will appear toward the top left area, under your biographic information, at the beginning of your undergraduate record. Every undergraduate is considered for honors regardless of when they complete their degree. If a student qualifies at the time of degree completion, the honor will be listed on the diploma and transcript — once the diploma is conferred.

Note: NYU Abu Dhabi does not publish GPA cutoffs for Latin honors or Founder's Day (University Scholars) awards.

- How do I know if I qualified for the Founders' Day (University Scholars) award?

The annual Founders' Day Awards are calculated for each graduating cohort (across all academic divisions), with the cutoffs set each March of the top 40 percent of the graduating class at each school. They are announced every April 21st for eligible students who have/will graduate(d) between the past spring and current spring semesters. The Founders' Day award is based on the cumulative GPA of all courses taken, including coursework taken in the first year.

Students who become eligible after publication of an award year (e.g. reach the top 40% after April 21st or complete their degree after April 21st) will be awarded in the following award year. Students who graduate off-cycle (Summer, Fall, January) could be eligible in the next annual award cycle.

GPA standards for this award are derived each April from spring graduating cohorts. NYUAD does not publish GPA cutoffs for awards. The award is granted to the top 40% of the graduating class, and eligible candidates are notified annually (April 21st).

Note : NYU Abu Dhabi does not publish GPA cutoffs for Latin honors or Founder's Day (University Scholars) awards.

Related official links:
https://students.nyuad.nyu.edu/student-affairs/career-development/job-search/degree-attestation/

sections.title: Graduation Process
sections.text:
- How do I know if I am on track to graduate?

Review your Degree Progress Report (DPR) each semester in Albert. Contact your academic advisor before each enrollment period begins (when the enrollment shopping cart opens), and as you approach graduation. Awarding of degrees depends on successful completion of all requirements in your DPR — take action to officially resolve any requirements marked as Not Satisfied.

sections.title: Documentation and Verification
sections.text:
- Awarding Degrees

Degrees are awarded by the Office of the Registrar. Once awarded, your record is finalized(!) and no changes can be made, including grade changes or updates to your major or minor.

At the beginning (before the end of add/drop of the 14-week session) of your final term or semester, be sure to check your Degree Progress Report in Albert to ensure your declarations are properly listed and none of your requirements are marked as Not Satisfied. No additional minor(s) or majors can be added after the add/drop period of the 14-week session of your final semester. Students can have a maximum of two majors and two minors. Additional minors above two are removed in the order that the student declared them.

The degree conferral dates are listing on the academic calendar and students can view their degree completion on their transcript starting the week after the conferral date.

- Will I receive a transcript when I graduate?

Students can order your official transcripts at any time through the National Student Clearinghouse .

Before you place your order, please follow these important steps:

-
Check Your Degree Status First: Log into Albert and review your unofficial transcript. Make sure your degree is officially listed as "posted" (you can find this in the top left-hand corner).

-
Send Directly to the Recipient: When ordering official transcripts, have the National Student Clearinghouse send the transcript directly to the graduate school or company requesting it.

Important: Do not send the transcript to yourself first with the plan to forward it. Once you open or forward a transcript, it is no longer considered official. Copies sent to yourself will have the words "Unofficial" appear in the background. When sending directly to a company or school, the word "Unofficial" does NOT appear. Students can always order a copy of their transcript for their own records but graduate schools will not accept official transcripts if it comes directly from the student. The National Student Clearinghouse is the official provider of NYU transcripts and the transcript is sent through an NYU registrar's email address.

- How do I get proof that I graduated if I can’t wait for my diploma?

After completing your degree program, a degree completion letter will be issued after the conferral date.

- My employer/immigration is asking for a graduation verification letter. What should I do?

After completing your degree program, a degree confirmation is sent to each student to use for employment, graduate schools, etc. Students should check their email the day after the conferral date for their degree confirmation letter (graduation verification).

sections.title: Diploma Information
sections.text:
- When will I receive my diploma?

Diplomas are shipped approximately 6-8 weeks following conferrals, provided there are no holds on your record. The date you receive your diploma would not match the conferral date on your diploma and transcripts. The conferral date is the official date of record, you could receive your physical diploma from that date onward - when it's ready for distribution, and as long as there are no active diploma holds on your record.

Important Information about Account Holds and Diplomas

Below is a list of holds managed by the Bursar’s Office. If a " Y" appears in the column next to a hold, it means that hold will block you from registering for classes and/or receiving your diploma.

To avoid any delays in getting physical or electronic (CeDiploma) diploma, students should make sure to clear all holds before graduation.

Timing on the release of the hold and issuing the CeDiploma: Once you clear a hold with Student Finance or the Bursar’s Office, it can take an additional 2 to 3 weeks for the CeDiploma (electronic diploma) to be generated and ready for download from the original release date as the university processes the request.

For questions about the holds students should contact either:

- NYUAD Student Finance ( nyuad.studentfinance@nyu.edu ) or

- NYU Bursar's Office ( bursar.studentaccounts@nyu.edu )

Code | Description | Registration Hold | Diploma Hold

ZAG | Account at Collection Agency | Y | Y

ZBB | Bursar Balance | |

ZCO | Internal Collections | Y | Y

ZDE | De-Enrollment for Non-Payment | Y |

ZDP | Diploma Hold | | Y

ZLS | Loan Services Hold | Y | Y

ZNC | Account at Collection Agency | Y | Y

ZNF | Not Financially Cleared | |

ZNP | Not Eligible for Payment Plan | |

ZPA | Payment Agreement | Y | y

ZPC | Pre-Collections | Y | Y

- What information will be on my diploma?

Your diploma serves as a formal certificate of your degree. It includes:

-
Your Full Name (as specified in your graduation application)

-
Degree Type (e.g., Bachelor of Arts or Bachelor of Science)

-
Date of Conferral

-
Latin Honors (if applicable)

Please note: Majors and minors are recorded on your official transcript rather than the diploma itself. For students with a double major, the diploma will reflect the primary degree type associated with your capstone coursework.

- Will my major and minor be printed on my diploma?

Your diploma will list the degree of your Capstone major degree level (e.g., Bachelor of Arts or Bachelor of Science) and not the major(s). The diploma does not list any minors and that information can be found on the transcript.

- I’m completing two majors and they have different degrees (BA and BS), will they both show on my records?

Both majors and degrees will appear on your transcript if they are declared, however only your primary degree level in which your capstone work was completed (e.g., Bachelor of Arts, Bachelor of Science - not major) will appear on your diploma.

- Can the name on my diploma be different from my transcripts?

The name printed on your diploma will be based on your selection on the Diploma Options page in Albert, where you can choose either your Primary or Preferred name. Students can update their primary name by submitting a copy of their passport to the NYUAD Office of the Registrar at least two months before graduation so requests can be processed in a timely manner. This page becomes available once they are applied to graduate (usually within the first four weeks of the final semester). Please note that all name changes must be submitted at least two months prior to your commencement date. Requests made after this deadline will require you to order and pay for a replacement diploma after your degree is officially conferred.

Note: For ministry authentication and verification of your diploma, it is highly recommended that the name on your diploma matches your transcripts (Primary name) and your passport.

Please note that name changes require processing time to reflect on your credentials. Allow at least one month after your name change is approved for the update to appear on a new printed diploma or CeDiploma.

- What is a CeDiploma and how can I order one?

CeDiplomas are certified electronic diplomas for secure electronic sharing. Your CeDiploma/electronic diploma will be ordered on the 15th of the month following conferrals and available shortly after. Any holds will prevent a CeDiploma from being created and will delay the issuance by 2-3 weeks after the hold is cleared.

Timing on the release of the hold and issuing the CeDiploma: Once you clear a hold with Student Finance or the Bursar’s Office, it can take an additional 2 to 3 weeks for the CeDiploma (electronic diploma) to be generated and ready for download from the original release date as the university processes the request. Please note that name changes require processing time to reflect on your credentials. Allow at least one month after your name change is approved for the update to appear on a new printed diploma or CeDiploma.

For questions about the holds students should contact either:

- NYUAD Student Finance ( nyuad.studentfinance@nyu.edu ) or

- NYU Bursar's Office ( bursar.studentaccounts@nyu.edu )

Visit NYU Albert and:

- Click on Grades and Transcripts

- Click on the E-Diploma link

- Click on the CeDiploma link at the bottom of the page

Please note:

- There is a $14.95 fee for this service

- CeDiplomas/CeCertificates are available for students who graduated after January 1, 2016. If you graduated before that date, you may order a CeDiploma/CeCertificate by following the ordering instructions at “ Replacement Diplomas ".

- Is there any way to expedite the diploma process?

Unfortunately the diploma process cannot be expedited due to the number of students graduating each year.

- Can I get my diploma if there is a diploma hold on my records?

No, your diploma cannot be released until the diploma hold is resolved.

- Can someone pick up my diploma for me?

Once available, you will receive an email allowing you to select your preference: picking up your diploma, having someone pick it up on your behalf, or having it shipped to you.

- How do I attest my diploma?

Follow the procedures outlined on the UAE Ministry of Education's website for attesting your degree. For more information contact the NYU Abu Dhabi Career Development Center .

- My diploma has been lost, damaged, etc. How do I get another one?

If you have graduated from NYU Abu Dhabi and your diploma was lost or has been damaged, you may purchase a replacement diploma by completing the online form accessible in the Albert portal in the Other Resources tab.

See additional information on Diplomas on the NYU Paper and Electronic Diplomas page .
