title: Revised Requirements for Graduation · NYUAD Students
text:
Minimum Number of Credits, Core, and J-Term

Starting in the 2024-2025 academic year, NYUAD will implement the following graduation requirement changes: the number of total credits required to graduate is reduced to 128; the number of required J-Terms is reduced from three to two; and the Core curriculum is changing to incorporate more experiential learning through the Core Field Colloquium courses that will be offered only during J-Term. Please read the details of the new policies below.

Why Were the Changes Made?

Importance of Experiential Learning: Across higher education institutions, experiential learning has been increasingly recognized as a key component of a university education. While many NYUAD courses offer significant learning of this kind, it has not previously been a degree requirement in itself. A revised Core requirement fully recognizes the importance of carefully curated experiential learning opportunities by embedding them into the two required J-Term courses with place-based fieldwork.

Elimination of June Term: Students have indicated that they strongly prefer January courses to June courses, largely to allow the summer term to be devoted to completing summer courses, pursuing internships, and conducting research.

Reduced Minimum Number of Graduation Credits: With 140 credits required for a bachelor's degree, NYUAD was out of alignment with the minimum of 128 graduation credit hours required by NYU New York, NYU Shanghai, and most other US and UAE universities. This change brings NYUAD into alignment.

Shorter J-Term: To increase the length of the summer term between spring and fall semesters, the NYU University Senate modified the academic calendar for all campuses of NYU, beginning this coming academic year 2024-2025. This change is intended to allow students an enhanced opportunity to pursue research, employment, summer courses, or internships in the summer, and to recharge their batteries. This change shortens the amount of time allotted for January Term from approximately 14 class days to 10 or 11, depending on the year. With the shorter number of days, it is not possible to provide sufficient instructional hours to meet the requirements for a four-credit course, which is the norm for Core, major, and minor courses. During the transitional year of 2024-2025, however, we will offer some J-Term courses that satisfy these requirements.

Revised Graduation Requirements

To achieve the goal of enhancing the student experience, while adapting to institutional changes, the following updates will be made to the credit structure, Core Curriculum, and J-Term program.

- Minimum Required Credits for Graduation

The minimum number of credits required to earn a Bachelor's degree at NYU Abu Dhabi has been reduced to 128 credits for all students, new and returning. Students must complete all major and core requirements and may still choose to earn more than 128 credits within eight semesters with a typical course load of 16 credits per semester.

Additional semesters beyond eight must be approved through an Academic Petition submitted to the Academic Resource Center (ARC).

Under the revised guidelines students must:

- Complete all requirements for an academic major (including a Capstone experience and a minor if required by the specific major).

- Complete all requirements for the Core curriculum.

- Complete two J-Term courses.

- Complete two physical education courses.

- Earn at least 128 credits.

- Achieve at least a 2.0 cumulative grade point average (GPA).

- Core Curriculum

The revised Core requirement is as follows:

- One First-Year Writing Seminar

- Four Core Competency courses (CSTS, CADT, CCEA, CDAD)

- One Core Colloquium Course taught at NYUAD during a regular fall or spring semester

- (New) Two J-Term Field Colloquium courses — 3 credits each - A J-Term Field Colloquium cannot be used toward the 14-week Core Colloquium requirement.

Eligibility

- Students entering fall 2024 or later must follow the revised Core requirement.

- Returning students who matriculated prior to fall 2024 will have the option to remain in the previous Core program or transition to the new revised Core — provided they have taken no more than one J-Term course thus far (including Design and Innovation).

- J-Term

Starting with the January Term 2025, the following changes to J-Term will apply.

J-Term Requirement: All students, new and returning, are required to complete only two J-Term courses to graduate.

Students who matriculated prior to fall 2024 may still complete three J-Terms if they so choose. These students may petition to complete a fourth J-Term only if absolutely essential for their on-time graduation as determined through an Academic Petition submitted to the Academic Resource Center (ARC).

Students who matriculate at NYUAD as of fall 2024 or later are limited to two J-Term courses. These students may petition to complete a third J-Term only if absolutely essential for their on-time graduation as determined through an Academic Petition submitted to the Academic Resource Center (ARC).

Length and Credits: Beginning in January 2025, J-Term courses will include 10 or 11 class days and will count for 3 credits.

Core Field Colloquia: Beginning in January 2025, all J-Term courses will count in the Core Program as Core Field Colloquia and will include a significant experiential learning component. During 2025 some, but not all, J-Term courses will also continue to count for existing major and/or Core Competency requirements for returning students. Students who matriculated prior to fall 2024 can view which degree requirements a J-Term course counts toward (if any) on the Course List and Syllabi page .

The 2025 January and June J-Terms will be the last opportunity for returning students to take courses that count toward existing major and/or Core Competency requirements.

Courses with a Regional Academic Seminar: The category of J-Term courses with regional academic seminars (RAS courses) are being phased out. Returning students who have not yet had a J-Term course with an RAS and wish to take one will have one last chance to take such a course in 2025. Students matriculating fall 2024 are not eligible for RAS J-Term courses in 2025.

Fully Away Courses: All students remain eligible for one fully away J-Term course.

Registration: Beginning with January Term 2025, all students will self-register for J-Term courses (both January and June) through Albert in the same way they register for fall and spring semester courses. Specific rules will apply; please review them here .

June J-Term Phase Out: One last June J-Term will be offered in 2025. In subsequent years all J-Term courses will be offered in January only. As in previous years, students are not able to take both a summer course and a June-Term course in the same summer as these courses overlap.

ENGR-UH 1021 Design and Innovation Course: Design and Innovation will continue to be offered in January and June and will continue to count for 2 credits. However, the course will no longer fulfill the J-Term requirement for students taking it in January 2025 or later. For students who took this course prior to January 2025, Design and Innovation will continue to fulfill the J-Term requirement.

More detailed information about implementation and registration of the new J-Term requirements can be found on the Global Education page .

Accessing Support

We acknowledge that the technical aspects of these changes may generate some specific questions for students. We have developed a support system to assist students in navigating these changes, especially in the transitional academic year 2024-2025. This includes J-Term group advising sessions offered by Global Education (to be announced on the student portal soon), guidance from the Academic Resource Center (ARC) at nyuad.arc@nyu.edu, support from the student Global Education Officers (GEOs), and assistance from the Offices of Global Education at nyuad.globaleducation@nyu.edu and the Registrar at nyuad.registrar@nyu.edu.

You'll find a Frequently Asked Questions section on this page, as well as more detailed J-Term focused Guidelines , Registration Process , and Frequently Asked Questions on the Office of Global Education website.

J-Term Implementation

- Course Selection

Beginning in September 2024, students will self-register for a 2025 J-Term course through Albert. The detailed registration process and guidelines are outlined here . Students should make sure that they have no holds in place that prevent them from registering for classes as enrollment is done through Albert.

- Students who have completed two or more J-Term courses will register first on Tuesday, September 24, 2024.

- Students who have completed one J-Term course will register on Wednesday, September 25, 2024.

- Exact registration appointment times will be displayed in Albert by September 21, 2024.

Returning students who have already completed two or more J-Terms do not need to register for a 2025 J-Term course if they prefer not to take a J-Term at all. Students who have completed fewer than two J-Terms are expected to register for a 2025 J-Term — either in January or June. While it is possible to defer taking a J-Term until a later year, we strongly recommend that you take a J-Term in your first and second year so as to leave your junior and senior year breaks available for internships, research, and Capstone preparation.

Engineering students may register for the Design and Innovation course at the same time they register for their J-Term class. Students enrolled in Computer Programming for Engineers (ENGR-UH 1001) in the fall can register for Design and Innovation in either January or June. Students planning to take Computer Programming for Engineers in the spring may register for Design and Innovation in June only. Students registering for Design and Innovation may also register for a J-Term course in whichever term they are NOT enrolled in Design and Innovation . It is NOT possible to register for a J-Term course and Design and Innovation in the same term (January or June.)

- Registration Notes

Students who have already completed three J-Term courses will NOT be able to register for an additional J-Term course without the prior permission of the Vice Provost for Undergraduate Education. Permission can be sought through an Academic Petition submitted to the Academic Resource Center (ARC). Approval will typically be granted only when the additional J-Term is essential for on-time graduation.

Students who have taken a prior Away J-Term course (including having withdrawn from or failed one) will not be able to register for an Away J-Term. The same rule applies to students who have taken a prior J-Term course with a regional academic seminar (including having withdrawn from or failed one.) Additionally, as per long-standing rules, students who have taken a course with a regional academic seminar but have not completed a J-Term fully in Abu Dhabi will not be able to register for an Away J-Term until they have completed an Abu Dhabi-based J-Term.

First-year students and returning students who have already taken a J-Term course with a regional academic seminar will not be able to enroll in a J-Term course with a regional academic seminar. As an exception, since 2025 will be the last year in which J-Terms with regional academic seminars are offered, returning students who have not yet had one will be permitted to enroll in one — even if they have not yet had an Abu Dhabi J-Term.

Students who are studying away in the fall are not eligible for a January Term course that is taught fully away, nor for one with a regional academic seminar (RAS Course). Students who are studying away in the spring are not eligible for a June Term course that is taught fully away, nor for one with a regional academic seminar.

The restriction against an RAS course after study away is long-standing. We have had to also prohibit Away J-Terms after study away due to a significant increase in refusals from various countries to consider visa applications from students studying abroad.

- Second Round of J-Term Registration

Once all eligible students have had a chance to register, and if there are sufficient vacancies left, we may hold a second round of J-Term registration for those vacant seats. The same limitations as described above will be implemented.

- J-Term and Revised Core

Returning students who wish to follow the revised Core requirements will need to notify the Registrar's Office of this plan by completing the New Core Option for NYUAD Students form by September 15, and MUST still have eligibility for two J-Term courses so as to be able to complete the two-course Core Field Colloquium requirement.

Deadline: September 15, 2024

FAQ for the 128 Minimum Credit Degree Program

- Do returning students need to do anything to move to the minimum 128 credit requirement or will it be processed automatically?

It will happen automatically.

- Will major requirements change as a result of the 128 minimum credits requirement?

Major requirements have not been impacted by this change. Returning students should connect with an Academic Advisor in the ARC to discuss how the new credit requirement will affect their individual 4-year plan.

- If I have already earned 128 credits, can I graduate even if I didn’t complete all requirements?

No. Students are expected to complete all their degree requirements even if they have already earned 128 credits.

- Will returning students complete all major requirements in sequence if they move to 128 credits? For example, if they move to 128 will they be able to complete their Capstone on cycle?

Students should still plan on utilizing the established eight semesters of financial aid support to complete their degree requirements "on schedule." While early graduation may become a possibility, it will always be viewed as an exception to expectations and not a normal practice. Indeed, some majors may not even permit "off-cycle" Capstone projects.

- If I meet the 128 requirements to graduate but I want to stay with the 140-credit degree requirement so I can complete a double major or a non-required minor, will I be able to?

As long as you can complete your degree in eight semesters, it is possible to take extra credits and/or complete a second major or minor(s). It is not possible to extend extra semesters for the purpose of completing a second major or minor(s) beyond the minimum required for the degree.

- If I meet the 128 credit degree requirements before I’ve completed 8 semesters, can I graduate early?

The University is unlikely to permit early graduation when it requires students to complete their Capstone project "off cycle." NYUAD encourages students to complete eight semesters of study. This is especially true for students considering graduate school, since many require four years of undergraduate coursework.

- Will employers or graduate schools look at my degree as less valuable or rigorous because I only completed 128 credits?

While we can't speak for employers or graduate schools, 120 to 128 credits is a standard across most countries employing the US credit-hour system, so it should not pose any barriers. NYU New York, NYU Shanghai, and most top-tier US universities require a minimum of 128 credits for a bachelor’s degree.

- If I change from 140 credits to 128 credits, will I be able to change back to 140 credits at a later date?

Since there is no material benefit to changing to 140 credits, all students will remain with the 128 credit requirement. Students who can graduate in eight semesters must graduate in eight semesters even if their credit total falls somewhere between 128 and 140.

sections.title: Minimum Number of Credits, Core, and J-Term
sections.text: Starting in the 2024-2025 academic year, NYUAD will implement the following graduation requirement changes: the number of total credits required to graduate is reduced to 128; the number of required J-Terms is reduced from three to two; and the Core curriculum is changing to incorporate more experiential learning through the Core Field Colloquium courses that will be offered only during J-Term. Please read the details of the new policies below.

sections.title: Minimum Number of Credits, Core, and J-Term · Why Were the Changes Made?
sections.text:
Importance of Experiential Learning: Across higher education institutions, experiential learning has been increasingly recognized as a key component of a university education. While many NYUAD courses offer significant learning of this kind, it has not previously been a degree requirement in itself. A revised Core requirement fully recognizes the importance of carefully curated experiential learning opportunities by embedding them into the two required J-Term courses with place-based fieldwork.

Elimination of June Term: Students have indicated that they strongly prefer January courses to June courses, largely to allow the summer term to be devoted to completing summer courses, pursuing internships, and conducting research.

Reduced Minimum Number of Graduation Credits: With 140 credits required for a bachelor's degree, NYUAD was out of alignment with the minimum of 128 graduation credit hours required by NYU New York, NYU Shanghai, and most other US and UAE universities. This change brings NYUAD into alignment.

Shorter J-Term: To increase the length of the summer term between spring and fall semesters, the NYU University Senate modified the academic calendar for all campuses of NYU, beginning this coming academic year 2024-2025. This change is intended to allow students an enhanced opportunity to pursue research, employment, summer courses, or internships in the summer, and to recharge their batteries. This change shortens the amount of time allotted for January Term from approximately 14 class days to 10 or 11, depending on the year. With the shorter number of days, it is not possible to provide sufficient instructional hours to meet the requirements for a four-credit course, which is the norm for Core, major, and minor courses. During the transitional year of 2024-2025, however, we will offer some J-Term courses that satisfy these requirements.

sections.title: Revised Graduation Requirements
sections.text:
To achieve the goal of enhancing the student experience, while adapting to institutional changes, the following updates will be made to the credit structure, Core Curriculum, and J-Term program.

- Minimum Required Credits for Graduation

The minimum number of credits required to earn a Bachelor's degree at NYU Abu Dhabi has been reduced to 128 credits for all students, new and returning. Students must complete all major and core requirements and may still choose to earn more than 128 credits within eight semesters with a typical course load of 16 credits per semester.

Additional semesters beyond eight must be approved through an Academic Petition submitted to the Academic Resource Center (ARC).

Under the revised guidelines students must:

- Complete all requirements for an academic major (including a Capstone experience and a minor if required by the specific major).

- Complete all requirements for the Core curriculum.

- Complete two J-Term courses.

- Complete two physical education courses.

- Earn at least 128 credits.

- Achieve at least a 2.0 cumulative grade point average (GPA).

- Core Curriculum

The revised Core requirement is as follows:

- One First-Year Writing Seminar

- Four Core Competency courses (CSTS, CADT, CCEA, CDAD)

- One Core Colloquium Course taught at NYUAD during a regular fall or spring semester

- (New) Two J-Term Field Colloquium courses — 3 credits each - A J-Term Field Colloquium cannot be used toward the 14-week Core Colloquium requirement.

Eligibility

- Students entering fall 2024 or later must follow the revised Core requirement.

- Returning students who matriculated prior to fall 2024 will have the option to remain in the previous Core program or transition to the new revised Core — provided they have taken no more than one J-Term course thus far (including Design and Innovation).

- J-Term

Starting with the January Term 2025, the following changes to J-Term will apply.

J-Term Requirement: All students, new and returning, are required to complete only two J-Term courses to graduate.

Students who matriculated prior to fall 2024 may still complete three J-Terms if they so choose. These students may petition to complete a fourth J-Term only if absolutely essential for their on-time graduation as determined through an Academic Petition submitted to the Academic Resource Center (ARC).

Students who matriculate at NYUAD as of fall 2024 or later are limited to two J-Term courses. These students may petition to complete a third J-Term only if absolutely essential for their on-time graduation as determined through an Academic Petition submitted to the Academic Resource Center (ARC).

Length and Credits: Beginning in January 2025, J-Term courses will include 10 or 11 class days and will count for 3 credits.

Core Field Colloquia: Beginning in January 2025, all J-Term courses will count in the Core Program as Core Field Colloquia and will include a significant experiential learning component. During 2025 some, but not all, J-Term courses will also continue to count for existing major and/or Core Competency requirements for returning students. Students who matriculated prior to fall 2024 can view which degree requirements a J-Term course counts toward (if any) on the Course List and Syllabi page .

The 2025 January and June J-Terms will be the last opportunity for returning students to take courses that count toward existing major and/or Core Competency requirements.

Courses with a Regional Academic Seminar: The category of J-Term courses with regional academic seminars (RAS courses) are being phased out. Returning students who have not yet had a J-Term course with an RAS and wish to take one will have one last chance to take such a course in 2025. Students matriculating fall 2024 are not eligible for RAS J-Term courses in 2025.

Fully Away Courses: All students remain eligible for one fully away J-Term course.

Registration: Beginning with January Term 2025, all students will self-register for J-Term courses (both January and June) through Albert in the same way they register for fall and spring semester courses. Specific rules will apply; please review them here .

June J-Term Phase Out: One last June J-Term will be offered in 2025. In subsequent years all J-Term courses will be offered in January only. As in previous years, students are not able to take both a summer course and a June-Term course in the same summer as these courses overlap.

ENGR-UH 1021 Design and Innovation Course: Design and Innovation will continue to be offered in January and June and will continue to count for 2 credits. However, the course will no longer fulfill the J-Term requirement for students taking it in January 2025 or later. For students who took this course prior to January 2025, Design and Innovation will continue to fulfill the J-Term requirement.

More detailed information about implementation and registration of the new J-Term requirements can be found on the Global Education page .

sections.title: Accessing Support
sections.text:
We acknowledge that the technical aspects of these changes may generate some specific questions for students. We have developed a support system to assist students in navigating these changes, especially in the transitional academic year 2024-2025. This includes J-Term group advising sessions offered by Global Education (to be announced on the student portal soon), guidance from the Academic Resource Center (ARC) at nyuad.arc@nyu.edu, support from the student Global Education Officers (GEOs), and assistance from the Offices of Global Education at nyuad.globaleducation@nyu.edu and the Registrar at nyuad.registrar@nyu.edu.

You'll find a Frequently Asked Questions section on this page, as well as more detailed J-Term focused Guidelines , Registration Process , and Frequently Asked Questions on the Office of Global Education website.

sections.title: J-Term Implementation
sections.text:
- Course Selection

Beginning in September 2024, students will self-register for a 2025 J-Term course through Albert. The detailed registration process and guidelines are outlined here . Students should make sure that they have no holds in place that prevent them from registering for classes as enrollment is done through Albert.

- Students who have completed two or more J-Term courses will register first on Tuesday, September 24, 2024.

- Students who have completed one J-Term course will register on Wednesday, September 25, 2024.

- Exact registration appointment times will be displayed in Albert by September 21, 2024.

Returning students who have already completed two or more J-Terms do not need to register for a 2025 J-Term course if they prefer not to take a J-Term at all. Students who have completed fewer than two J-Terms are expected to register for a 2025 J-Term — either in January or June. While it is possible to defer taking a J-Term until a later year, we strongly recommend that you take a J-Term in your first and second year so as to leave your junior and senior year breaks available for internships, research, and Capstone preparation.

Engineering students may register for the Design and Innovation course at the same time they register for their J-Term class. Students enrolled in Computer Programming for Engineers (ENGR-UH 1001) in the fall can register for Design and Innovation in either January or June. Students planning to take Computer Programming for Engineers in the spring may register for Design and Innovation in June only. Students registering for Design and Innovation may also register for a J-Term course in whichever term they are NOT enrolled in Design and Innovation . It is NOT possible to register for a J-Term course and Design and Innovation in the same term (January or June.)

- Registration Notes

Students who have already completed three J-Term courses will NOT be able to register for an additional J-Term course without the prior permission of the Vice Provost for Undergraduate Education. Permission can be sought through an Academic Petition submitted to the Academic Resource Center (ARC). Approval will typically be granted only when the additional J-Term is essential for on-time graduation.

Students who have taken a prior Away J-Term course (including having withdrawn from or failed one) will not be able to register for an Away J-Term. The same rule applies to students who have taken a prior J-Term course with a regional academic seminar (including having withdrawn from or failed one.) Additionally, as per long-standing rules, students who have taken a course with a regional academic seminar but have not completed a J-Term fully in Abu Dhabi will not be able to register for an Away J-Term until they have completed an Abu Dhabi-based J-Term.

First-year students and returning students who have already taken a J-Term course with a regional academic seminar will not be able to enroll in a J-Term course with a regional academic seminar. As an exception, since 2025 will be the last year in which J-Terms with regional academic seminars are offered, returning students who have not yet had one will be permitted to enroll in one — even if they have not yet had an Abu Dhabi J-Term.

Students who are studying away in the fall are not eligible for a January Term course that is taught fully away, nor for one with a regional academic seminar (RAS Course). Students who are studying away in the spring are not eligible for a June Term course that is taught fully away, nor for one with a regional academic seminar.

The restriction against an RAS course after study away is long-standing. We have had to also prohibit Away J-Terms after study away due to a significant increase in refusals from various countries to consider visa applications from students studying abroad.

- Second Round of J-Term Registration

Once all eligible students have had a chance to register, and if there are sufficient vacancies left, we may hold a second round of J-Term registration for those vacant seats. The same limitations as described above will be implemented.

- J-Term and Revised Core

Returning students who wish to follow the revised Core requirements will need to notify the Registrar's Office of this plan by completing the New Core Option for NYUAD Students form by September 15, and MUST still have eligibility for two J-Term courses so as to be able to complete the two-course Core Field Colloquium requirement.

Deadline: September 15, 2024

sections.title: FAQ for the 128 Minimum Credit Degree Program
sections.text:
- Do returning students need to do anything to move to the minimum 128 credit requirement or will it be processed automatically?

It will happen automatically.

- Will major requirements change as a result of the 128 minimum credits requirement?

Major requirements have not been impacted by this change. Returning students should connect with an Academic Advisor in the ARC to discuss how the new credit requirement will affect their individual 4-year plan.

- If I have already earned 128 credits, can I graduate even if I didn’t complete all requirements?

No. Students are expected to complete all their degree requirements even if they have already earned 128 credits.

- Will returning students complete all major requirements in sequence if they move to 128 credits? For example, if they move to 128 will they be able to complete their Capstone on cycle?

Students should still plan on utilizing the established eight semesters of financial aid support to complete their degree requirements "on schedule." While early graduation may become a possibility, it will always be viewed as an exception to expectations and not a normal practice. Indeed, some majors may not even permit "off-cycle" Capstone projects.

- If I meet the 128 requirements to graduate but I want to stay with the 140-credit degree requirement so I can complete a double major or a non-required minor, will I be able to?

As long as you can complete your degree in eight semesters, it is possible to take extra credits and/or complete a second major or minor(s). It is not possible to extend extra semesters for the purpose of completing a second major or minor(s) beyond the minimum required for the degree.

- If I meet the 128 credit degree requirements before I’ve completed 8 semesters, can I graduate early?

The University is unlikely to permit early graduation when it requires students to complete their Capstone project "off cycle." NYUAD encourages students to complete eight semesters of study. This is especially true for students considering graduate school, since many require four years of undergraduate coursework.

- Will employers or graduate schools look at my degree as less valuable or rigorous because I only completed 128 credits?

While we can't speak for employers or graduate schools, 120 to 128 credits is a standard across most countries employing the US credit-hour system, so it should not pose any barriers. NYU New York, NYU Shanghai, and most top-tier US universities require a minimum of 128 credits for a bachelor’s degree.

- If I change from 140 credits to 128 credits, will I be able to change back to 140 credits at a later date?

Since there is no material benefit to changing to 140 credits, all students will remain with the 128 credit requirement. Students who can graduate in eight semesters must graduate in eight semesters even if their credit total falls somewhere between 128 and 140.

Registration Information

- Preparing to Register

To prepare for registration we recommend you follow these important steps:

Check your registration appointment day and time by signing into the Albert Student Center and reviewing your appointment information displayed in the Enrollment Dates section. Students should register in at least 16 credits to stay on track with degree requirements (students should contact the Academic Resource Center (ARC) with any questions about how many credits to register for in a semester).

Remember to only register for courses at the site location you will be studying at. Example: If you are studying in Abu Dhabi you are not able to enroll in coursework in New York (online or otherwise).

Online Coursework Information : Students at most study away locations may take one online course, provided it is offered directly by their host site - courses from other locations are not permitted. However, online coursework is strictly prohibited for students studying in London, Accra, or Abu Dhabi.

-
Course Limit: Eligible students may take a maximum of one online course offered directly by their host location in a semester/session.

-
Site Restrictions: Online courses hosted by other locations or campuses are not permitted. The online course must be offered at the site the student is at for the semester/session.

-
Exempt Locations: Online coursework is entirely unavailable to students studying in London, Accra, or Abu Dhabi.

Check for registration holds in the Albert Student Center . Some holds may block you from registration. Click "Details" in the "Holds" section to see contact and resolution information. Students should check for any holds before the registration cycle and have them cleared by the relevant department. The Office of the Registrar is not able to adjust, override, or cancel any holds that are from the Finance Office, Library, CDC, Dean of Students and/or the Student Health Center and students need to clear those holds directly with those offices.

Meet with your academic advisor to discuss your class schedule and degree requirements.

Update your contact information by signing into the Albert Student Center and clicking "Personal Information." You are required to have current contact information, an "NYU Emergency Alert" mobile phone number, and an emergency contact. If you had study away in a previous semester make sure to update your address back to your NYUAD address in the system.

Use the "Shopping Cart" and "Validate" tools to start planning your schedule. You can also review our registration guides for step-by-step instructions on how to validate , add , drop , swap , and more!

Students are expected to be registered in a full-time load before the start of the semester and attend classes from the first day.

Email the Office of the NYUAD Registrar if you have any registration concerns.

- Registration Holds

Types of Holds

A hold on a student's account arises from unresolved obligations like unpaid fees, overdue books, incomplete forms, and/or academic concerns. Resolving holds requires communication with relevant departments such as the Office the Bursar (or Student Finance) . Once addressed, students can smoothly resume their academic registration activities and diploma collection. Below outlines the types of holds students might encounter in Albert and how to contact the respective departments for assistance . Students can have more than one active hold. Students should include their N Number when contacting an office so that they can research any requests.

Please note that NYU policy states that i f a student owes payment on tuition, fees, loans, or other charges (such as housing, dining, or activities/services), the University reserves the right to deny registration, withhold the issuance of a diploma upon graduation and any other information regarding the student’s record.

Financial Hold - This is the most common hold that prevents students from registering in courses. Please contact Student Finance at nyuad.studentfinance@nyu.edu for information on how to remove this hold. Students are not able to register with a finance hold. The Office of the Registrar is not able to override or remove any financial holds and this must be done directly with the Student Finance Office. This hold will also prevent a student from collecting a diploma. This hold does prevent a student from registering for classes.

Payment Plan Enrollment Hold - " Not Eligible for Payment Plans " - Can prevent a student from registration. It is placed on all NYU students who have a balance. If a student carries a balance then this hold can prevent future enrollment. Students should check with Student Finance to see when the hold will begin to prevent registration. Students should contact Student Finance at nyuad.studentfinance@nyu.edu for information about this type of hold. It does not prevent diploma distribution/collection.

Library Hold - This hold will prevent registration. Please reach out directly to lib-nyuad-circ@nyu.edu for information on how to remove the hold. The Office the Registrar is not able to override or remove any library holds. This student will also prevent a student from collecting a diploma. This hold does prevent a student from registering for classes.

Dean of Students Hold - please reach out to nyuad.dos@nyu.edu for information on how to remove the hold. This hold does prevent a student from registering for classes.

Abu Dhabi Dean Transcripts Hold - Please contact the Career Development Center ( CDC ) to remove this hold. It is usually related to external test prep and examination costs. Until this hold is removed, your official transcript and diploma will not be released. This student will also prevent a student from collecting a diploma. The CDC can be reached at nyuad.career@nyu.edu . This hold does prevent a student from registering for classes.

Admissions Hold - Students need to contact nyuad.admissions@nyu.edu to remove any hold related to Admissions. This type of hold is usually related to students needing to submit their final high school transcripts and/or high school graduation confirmation. This hold does prevent a student from registering for classes.

Sample holds include: RMD - New Admit Missing Creds - does not prevent registration but needs to be addressed within the semester in which it was assigned or student could be prevented from future registration. Most common for a missing credentials holds is that a student needs to submit final high school transcripts (reason: UGA - Proof of High School Graduation Needed ).

Health Center Holds - for information on how to complete the mandatory health modules please reach out to nyuad.healthcenter@nyu.edu . This hold does prevent a student from registering for classes.

Major Declaration (this hold will prevent registration until it is resolved) - Please complete a major declaration form (found on the Student Portal > Academics > Registrar > Forms ). Students are not be able to enroll for classes until this hold has been cleared and the student has declared a major. It can take time for any major declaration to be processed as it is reviewed by the Academic Division on a weekly basis.

Minor Declaration (this hold will prevent registration until it is resolved) - Please complete a minor declaration form to add an approved minor, as required by your major. Until this hold is removed, you are able to drop classes, but will NOT be able to add any classes.

Major Track - Your major requires a track, that has not yet been declared. Please contact the Office of the NYUAD Registrar ( nyuad.registrar@nyu.edu ) indicating which track you are pursuing. Until this hold is removed, you are able to drop classes, but will NOT be able to add any classes.

Passport Hold - A hold has been placed on your record as you have not yet provided your valid passport details via the Student Portal. A student will not be able to enroll into classes until this hold is removed. Please contact the Global Education Office ( nyuad.globaleducation@nyu.edu ) to resolve this hold.

Leave of Absence Hold/Term Withdraw Hold - Please contact the Office of the NYUAD Dean of Students ( nyuad.dos@nyu.edu ) to ensure all formalities for returning from leave have been completed. Until this has been done and the hold is removed, a student will not be able to enroll in any classes. Make sure to follow any timelines when returning from leave that is outlined in the leave of absence letter.

Registration Hold - Please contact the Office of the NYUAD Registrar ( nyuad.registrar@nyu.edu ). Until this hold is removed, students are able to drop classes, but will NOT be able to add any classes.

Dean’s Wellness / Abu Dhabi Wellness Hold - When you are ready to return from

your Leave of Absence or Term Withdraw, and before enrolling for classes, you will need to reach out to the NYUAD Health Center if you have a Dean's Wellness hold. Please contact nyuad.healthcenter@nyu.edu and nyuad.dos@nyu.edu for information regarding this hold. This hold does prevent registration until it is cleared.

Immunization/Vaccination Holds - This registration hold will remain until you gain immunization compliance by receiving the missing vaccination(s), on or off campus, or uploading the required documentation to the Student Health Center Portal . Once your requirements are complete, please allow a few days for your documentation to be reviewed and the registration hold to be removed. Once the hold is removed, you may register for classes until the Add/Drop deadline. If you have questions about your vaccination requirements, please contact nyuad. immunization @nyu.edu .

Important Information About Account Holds & Graduation

Below is a list of holds managed by the Bursar’s Office. If a "Y" appears in the column next to a hold, it means that hold will block you from registering for classes and/or receiving your diploma.

To avoid any delays in getting physical or electronic (CE) diploma, students should make sure to clear all holds before graduation.

Timing on the release of the hold and issuing the CE Diploma: Once you clear a hold with Student Finance or the Bursar’s Office, it can take an additional 2 to 3 weeks for the CE Diploma (electronic diploma) to be generated and ready for download from the original release date as the university processes the request.

For questions about the holds students should contact either:

- NYUAD Student Finance ( nyuad.studentfinance@nyu.edu ) or

- NYU Bursar's Office ( bursar.studentaccounts@nyu.edu )

Code | Description | Registration Hold | Diploma Hold

ZAG | Account at Collection Agency | Y | Y

ZBB | Bursar Balance | |

ZCO | Internal Collections | Y | Y

ZDE | De-Enrollment for Non-Payment | Y |

ZDP | Diploma Hold | | Y

ZLS | Loan Services Hold | Y | Y

ZNC | Account at Collection Agency | Y | Y

ZNF | Not Financially Cleared | |

ZNP | Not Eligible for Payment Plan | |

ZPA | Payment Agreement | Y | y

ZPC | Pre-Collections | Y | Y

ZRG | Registration Hold | Y |

ZRP | Returned Payment Hold | |

- Registration Times

Registration for the fall and spring semesters typically begins approximately two months or more before the start of each semester. Students can see their appointment times in Albert. While the appointment time is the first opportunity to enroll in classes for the semester via Albert, students can view available courses and add classes to the shopping cart prior to the appointment time.

Appointment Times: Please note that these appointments are in Eastern Standard Time; depending on the time of year, either eight or nine hours must be added to determine the time in Abu Dhabi. Appointment times are based on the number of completed credits from the end of the prior semester (substandard grades from the first year and incompletes grades are not included in the number of completed credits). Note: Appointment time are not based on the year when a student was admitted.

Enrollment timelines and class schedule information (standard for all study away sites and NYU Abu Dhabi):

Fall semester class schedule typically is posted online in mid-March with registration starting in mid-April

Spring semester class schedule typically is posted online in mid-October with registration starting in mid-November

January-Term (known as J-Term) class schedule typically goes online in late September and registration starting within the same month

Summer schedule usually is posted online by late-Feb with registration in late Feb (check the Student Portal at the start of the spring semester any updates to the summer schedule timeline)

- Enrollment in First Year Writing Seminars and Colloquia

All students are required to successfully complete a First Year Writing Seminar during their first year. Places in these classes are reserved for students who have not yet met this writing requirement. Other students who are interested in taking these classes are encouraged to add themselves to the waitlist as places may become available at a later date. Places in these classes are also reserved initially for students who are required to take them. Students need to complete their Colloquia requirement on schedule and should work with the Academic Resource Center (ARC) for any planning assistance.

- Physical Education Course Registration Process

All NYUAD undergraduate students are required to complete two Physical Education courses as part of their degree requirements. Half of the places in the Physical Education classes in each semester are usually reserved for students who have yet to complete this requirement. Therefore, students who have completed their PE requirement may not be able to register for a Physical Education class that appears to be open (or may be dropped in order for other students who need to complete their PE requirement can enroll). In such instances, students are encouraged to add themselves to the waitlist as places may become available at a later date. Physical Education courses are open to undergraduate students only.

- Study Away Course Registration

The Course Intent Form for students studying in New York is now available through the Global Programs Academics Portal . Please carefully read the Registration Procedures Guide available on the portal and complete the appropriate course request form. For students studying at all other NYU global locations, please contact Global Academics global.acadmin@nyu.edu directly for questions about registration.

- Study Away Online Course Registration

Students at most study away locations may take one online course, provided it is offered directly by their host site - courses from other locations are not permitted. However, online coursework is strictly prohibited for students studying in London, Accra, or Abu Dhabi.

-
Course Limit: Eligible students may take a maximum of one online course offered directly by their host location in a semester/session.

-
Site Restrictions: Online courses hosted by other locations or campuses are not permitted. The online course must be offered at the site the student is at for the semester/session.

-
Exempt Locations: Online coursework is entirely unavailable to students studying in London, Accra, or Abu Dhabi.

Once addressed, students can smoothly resume their academic registration activities and diploma collection. Below outlines the types of holds students might encounter in Albert and how to contact the respective departments for assistance . Students can have more than one active hold. Students should include their N Number when contacting an office so that they can research any requests.

Please note that NYU policy states that i f a student owes payment on tuition, fees, loans, or other charges (such as housing, dining, or activities/services), the University reserves the right to deny registration, withhold the issuance of a diploma upon graduation and any other information regarding the student’s record.

Financial Hold - This is the most common hold that prevents students from registering in courses. Please contact Student Finance at nyuad.studentfinance@nyu.edu for information on how to remove this hold. Students are not able to register with a finance hold. The Office of the Registrar is not able to override or remove any financial holds and this must be done directly with the Student Finance Office. This hold will also prevent a student from collecting a diploma. This hold does prevent a student from registering for classes.

Payment Plan Enrollment Hold - " Not Eligible for Payment Plans " - Can prevent a student from registration. It is placed on all NYU students who have a balance. If a student carries a balance then this hold can prevent future enrollment. Students should check with Student Finance to see when the hold will begin to prevent registration. Students should contact Student Finance at nyuad.studentfinance@nyu.edu for information about this type of hold. It does not prevent diploma distribution/collection.

Library Hold - This hold will prevent registration. Please reach out directly to lib-nyuad-circ@nyu.edu for information on how to remove the hold. The Office the Registrar is not able to override or remove any library holds. This student will also prevent a student from collecting a diploma. This hold does prevent a student from registering for classes.

Dean of Students Hold - please reach out to nyuad.dos@nyu.edu for information on how to remove the hold. This hold does prevent a student from registering for classes.

Abu Dhabi Dean Transcripts Hold - Please contact the Career Development Center ( CDC ) to remove this hold. It is usually related to external test prep and examination costs. Until this hold is removed, your official transcript and diploma will not be released. This student will also prevent a student from collecting a diploma. The CDC can be reached at nyuad.career@nyu.edu . This hold does prevent a student from registering for classes.

Admissions Hold - Students need to contact nyuad.admissions@nyu.edu to remove any hold related to Admissions. This type of hold is usually related to students needing to submit their final high school transcripts and/or high school graduation confirmation. This hold does prevent a student from registering for classes.

Sample holds include: RMD - New Admit Missing Creds - does not prevent registration but needs to be addressed within the semester in which it was assigned or student could be prevented from future registration. Most common for a missing credentials holds is that a student needs to submit final high school transcripts (reason: UGA - Proof of High School Graduation Needed ).

Health Center Holds - for information on how to complete the mandatory health modules please reach out to nyuad.healthcenter@nyu.edu . This hold does prevent a student from registering for classes.

Major Declaration (this hold will prevent registration until it is resolved) - Please complete a major declaration form (found on the Student Portal > Academics > Registrar > Forms ). Students are not be able to enroll for classes until this hold has been cleared and the student has declared a major. It can take time for any major declaration to be processed as it is reviewed by the Academic Division on a weekly basis.

Minor Declaration (this hold will prevent registration until it is resolved) - Please complete a minor declaration form to add an approved minor, as required by your major. Until this hold is removed, you are able to drop classes, but will NOT be able to add any classes.

Major Track - Your major requires a track, that has not yet been declared. Please contact the Office of the NYUAD Registrar ( nyuad.registrar@nyu.edu ) indicating which track you are pursuing. Until this hold is removed, you are able to drop classes, but will NOT be able to add any classes.

Passport Hold - A hold has been placed on your record as you have not yet provided your valid passport details via the Student Portal. A student will not be able to enroll into classes until this hold is removed. Please contact the Global Education Office ( nyuad.globaleducation@nyu.edu ) to resolve this hold.

Leave of Absence Hold/Term Withdraw Hold - Please contact the Office of the NYUAD Dean of Students ( nyuad.dos@nyu.edu ) to ensure all formalities for returning from leave have been completed. Until this has been done and the hold is removed, a student will not be able to enroll in any classes. Make sure to follow any timelines when returning from leave that is outlined in the leave of absence letter.

Registration Hold - Please contact the Office of the NYUAD Registrar ( nyuad.registrar@nyu.edu ). Until this hold is removed, students are able to drop classes, but will NOT be able to add any classes.

Dean’s Wellness / Abu Dhabi Wellness Hold - When you are ready to return from

your Leave of Absence or Term Withdraw, and before enrolling for classes, you will need to reach out to the NYUAD Health Center if you have a Dean's Wellness hold. Please contact nyuad.healthcenter@nyu.edu and nyuad.dos@nyu.edu for information regarding this hold. This hold does prevent registration until it is cleared.

Immunization/Vaccination Holds - This registration hold will remain until you gain immunization compliance by receiving the missing vaccination(s), on or off campus, or uploading the required documentation to the Student Health Center Portal . Once your requirements are complete, please allow a few days for your documentation to be reviewed and the registration hold to be removed. Once the hold is removed, you may register for classes until the Add/Drop deadline. If you have questions about your vaccination requirements, please contact nyuad. immunization @nyu.edu .

Important Information About Account Holds & Graduation

Below is a list of holds managed by the Bursar’s Office. If a "Y" appears in the column next to a hold, it means that hold will block you from registering for classes and/or receiving your diploma.

To avoid any delays in getting physical or electronic (CE) diploma, students should make sure to clear all holds before graduation.

Timing on the release of the hold and issuing the CE Diploma: Once you clear a hold with Student Finance or the Bursar’s Office, it can take an additional 2 to 3 weeks for the CE Diploma (electronic diploma) to be generated and ready for download from the original release date as the university processes the request.

For questions about the holds students should contact either:

- NYUAD Student Finance ( nyuad.studentfinance@nyu.edu ) or

- NYU Bursar's Office ( bursar.studentaccounts@nyu.edu )

Code | Description | Registration Hold | Diploma Hold

ZAG | Account at Collection Agency | Y | Y

ZBB | Bursar Balance | |

ZCO | Internal Collections | Y | Y

ZDE | De-Enrollment for Non-Payment | Y |

ZDP | Diploma Hold | | Y

ZLS | Loan Services Hold | Y | Y

ZNC | Account at Collection Agency | Y | Y

ZNF | Not Financially Cleared | |

ZNP | Not Eligible for Payment Plan | |

ZPA | Payment Agreement | Y | y

ZPC | Pre-Collections | Y | Y

ZRG | Registration Hold | Y |

ZRP | Returned Payment Hold | |

- Registration Times

Registration for the fall and spring semesters typically begins approximately two months or more before the start of each semester. Students can see their appointment times in Albert. While the appointment time is the first opportunity to enroll in classes for the semester via Albert, students can view available courses and add classes to the shopping cart prior to the appointment time.

Appointment Times: Please note that these appointments are in Eastern Standard Time; depending on the time of year, either eight or nine hours must be added to determine the time in Abu Dhabi. Appointment times are based on the number of completed credits from the end of the prior semester (substandard grades from the first year and incompletes grades are not included in the number of completed credits). Note: Appointment time are not based on the year when a student was admitted.

Enrollment timelines and class schedule information (standard for all study away sites and NYU Abu Dhabi):

Fall semester class schedule typically is posted online in mid-March with registration starting in mid-April

Spring semester class schedule typically is posted online in mid-October with registration starting in mid-November

January-Term (known as J-Term) class schedule typically goes online in late September and registration starting within the same month

Summer schedule usually is posted online by late-Feb with registration in late Feb (check the Student Portal at the start of the spring semester any updates to the summer schedule timeline)

- Enrollment in First Year Writing Seminars and Colloquia

All students are required to successfully complete a First Year Writing Seminar during their first year. Places in these classes are reserved for students who have not yet met this writing requirement. Other students who are interested in taking these classes are encouraged to add themselves to the waitlist as places may become available at a later date. Places in these classes are also reserved initially for students who are required to take them. Students need to complete their Colloquia requirement on schedule and should work with the Academic Resource Center (ARC) for any planning assistance.

- Physical Education Course Registration Process

All NYUAD undergraduate students are required to complete two Physical Education courses as part of their degree requirements. Half of the places in the Physical Education classes in each semester are usually reserved for students who have yet to complete this requirement. Therefore, students who have completed their PE requirement may not be able to register for a Physical Education class that appears to be open (or may be dropped in order for other students who need to complete their PE requirement can enroll). In such instances, students are encouraged to add themselves to the waitlist as places may become available at a later date. Physical Education courses are open to undergraduate students only.

- Study Away Course Registration

The Course Intent Form for students studying in New York is now available through the Global Programs Academics Portal . Please carefully read the Registration Procedures Guide available on the portal and complete the appropriate course request form. For students studying at all other NYU global locations, please contact Global Academics global.acadmin@nyu.edu directly for questions about registration.

- Study Away Online Course Registration

Students at most study away locations may take one online course, provided it is offered directly by their host site - courses from other locations are not permitted. However, online coursework is strictly prohibited for students studying in London, Accra, or Abu Dhabi.

-
Course Limit: Eligible students may take a maximum of one online course offered directly by their host location in a semester/session.

-
Site Restrictions: Online courses hosted by other locations or campuses are not permitted. The online course must be offered at the site the student is at for the semester/session.

-
Exempt Locations: Online coursework is entirely unavailable to students studying in London, Accra, or Abu Dhabi.

text:
This form is for 14-week and second 7-week classes only . The prior form for first 7-week classes closed on Friday, March 27 (UAE time).

Students who do not complete this form by May 1 at 4:00 pm Abu Dhabi time will be assumed to want to have their 14-week and any second 7-week courses graded normally.

Transcript (Covered Grades) Policy

On the form below, please indicate which courses, if any, you wish to have grades covered by the Transcript Policy. If you are a first-year student, all courses are automatically covered by the Transcript Policy and will follow that policy for the spring semester. If you are not a first-year student, you may select as many or as few courses to be covered as you like. If taking the class as “Covered” then only a grade of C or better can be used to satisfy requirements (major, minor, core, prerequisite).

Pass/Fail Policy:

If you opt to have a course converted to pass/fail it will earn credit toward graduation for any grade D or higher. However, no course taken pass/fail can be used to satisfy prerequisite requirements.

For more complete information about the impact of various Spring 2026 grading options, please refer to the online FAQ page .

The deadline for submitting this form has passed.

title: First Year Students Final Transcripts · NYUAD Students
text:
Submitting Your Final Transcript

All first year students must submit final transcripts. Final Reports and final transcripts are due July 1. Please be sure to arrange with your school’s college or guidance counselor to receive your Final Report. This document is available in the Recommenders section of your Common App account, and should be sent to the Office of Undergraduate Admissions in New York:

NYU Undergraduate Admissions
ATTN: NYU Abu Dhabi
383 Lafayette Street
New York, NY 10003
USA

Your final high school transcript, showing the date of your graduation, should accompany your Final Report. Your Final Report, with final transcript and date of graduation is due by July 1. The only students for whom extensions will be granted are those enrolled in schools or curricula where transcripts or final exams will not be available until a later date.

Please be advised, however, that you will not be allowed to register for classes this fall until we have received your final transcript. You should also be aware that you cannot hold a space at more than one college or university after May 1.

For additional information on any holds related to final high school transcripts please contact nyuad.admissions@nyu.edu .

title: Ordering Transcripts · NYUAD Students
text:
Request Official Electronic or Mailed Transcripts

- If you are able to access NYUHome/Albert

- Request an official eTranscript from your Albert Student Center .

- The Request Official Transcript link can be found under the My Academics section of Albert Student Center.

- If you need to send attachment(s) with your transcript, use the eTranscript option.

- If you are unable to access NYUHome/Albert

- Order directly from National Student Clearinghouse.

Important: Do not send the transcript to yourself first with the plan to forward it. Once you open or forward a transcript, it is no longer considered official. Copies sent to yourself will have the words "Unofficial" appear in the background. When sending directly to a company or school, the word "Unofficial" does NOT appear. Students can always order a copy of their transcript for their own records but graduate schools will not normally accept the transcripts if it comes directly from the student. The National Student Clearinghouse is the official provider of all NYU transcripts and the transcript is sent through an NYU registrar's email address.

Notes:
- There is a small fee for eTranscripts.
- eTranscripts can be sent with up to two attachments that the student can upload (e.g. supporting application documents).
- Learn more about eTranscript ordering and eTranscript costs .
- Transcripts sent to schools or employment offers should use this official NYU service.
- Students should enter “New York University” for the school that they are requesting the transcript from (please note: NYUAD is part of the NYU system and all transcript official records are processed through New York University by the National Student Clearinghouse).
- The National Student Clearinghouse can send the transcript electronically or through various mailing options.
- The transcript legend is included in the electronic version as a “paperclip” attachment in the .pdf document.
- Transcripts are a complete record of courses taken and students are not able to order individual semester(s) of their coursework.

Request an Unofficial Transcript

Unofficial transcripts can be viewed and printed from the Albert Student Center .

- The View My Unofficial Transcript link can be found under the My Academics section of the Student Center. Be sure your pop-up blocker is switched off on your browser.

title: Spring 2026 Grading Policies · NYUAD Students
text:
Last updated: March 12, 2026

Standard Letter Grade

Grade | Counts Toward GPA (Official Transcript) | Counts Toward GPA (Unofficial Transcript) | Satisfies Major, Minor, Core Requirements | Meets Prerequisite | Grade Shown on Official Transcript | Counts Toward 128 Credits

A - C | Yes | Yes | Yes | Yes | A, A-, B+, B, B-, C+, C | Yes

C- | Yes | Yes | No | No | C- | Yes

D, D+ | Yes | Yes | No | No | D, D+ | Yes

F | Yes | Yes | No | No | F | No

W | No | No | No | No | W | No

Covered Grade (Transcript Policy)

Grade | Counts Toward GPA (Official Transcript) | Counts Toward GPA (Unofficial Transcript) | Satisfies Major, Minor, Core Requirements | Meets Prerequisite | Grade Shown on Official Transcript | Counts Toward 128 Credits

A - C | No | Yes | Yes | Yes | SC | Yes

C- | No | Yes | Yes (Degree Progress Exception needed) | No | SC | Yes

D, D+ | No | Yes | Yes (Degree Progress Exception needed) | No | Does not show | Yes

F | No | Yes | No | No | Does not show | No

W | No | No | No | No | Does not show | No

Pass/Fail

Grade | Counts Toward GPA (Official Transcript) | Counts Toward GPA (Unofficial Transcript) | Satisfies Major, Minor, Core Requirements | Meets Prerequisite | Grade Shown on Official Transcript | Counts Toward 128 Credits

A - C | No | No | Yes | No | P | Yes

C- | No | No | Yes | No | P | Yes

D, D+ | No | No | Yes | No | P | Yes

F | Yes | Yes | No | No | F | No

W | No | No | No | No | W | No

Opt for Both Covered Grade and Pass/Fail
Unofficial transcript shows grades of P/F

Grade | Counts Toward GPA (Official Transcript) | Counts Toward GPA (Unofficial Transcript) | Satisfies Major, Minor, Core Requirements | Meets Prerequisite | Grade Shown on Official Transcript | Counts Toward 128 Credits

A - C | No | No | Yes | No | P | Yes

C- | No | No | Yes | No | P | Yes

D, D+ | No | No | Yes | No | P | Yes

F | No | Yes | No | No | Does not show | No

W | No | No | No | No | Does not show | No

Definitions

- First-Year Students : Students who entered NYUAD fall 2025

- Cumulative GPA : The GPA that appears on your Unofficial Transcript and that starts with your first semester at NYUAD. Used for internal purposes such as study away, internships, and at times, student employment.

- Cumulative Degree GPA : The GPA that appears on your Official Transcript starting with your second year at NYUAD. This GPA is calculated after your conferral at NYUAD.

- Successfully Completed : Also referred to as "SC," this shows on the Official Transcript for courses obtained with a C- or higher.

Overview of Grading Options for Spring 2026

Standard Letter Grade

- No changes; courses follow the standard NYUAD grading policy.

- Letter grades appear on the unofficial and official transcripts.

- Counts toward the final GPA.

- "C" or higher satisfies Major, Minor, Core, and prerequisite requirements.

- For first-year students, normal transcript policy applies.

Covered Grades (Transcript Policy)

- Courses that are graded with a "C" or higher will meet prerequisite requirements.

- Courses that receive a "D" or higher will count towards satisfying major, minor, or core requirements.

- On the official transcript, grades of "C-" or higher appear as "SC" and grades of "D" or lower do not appear.

- All grades count in the official GPA but not in the final GPA.

Pass/Fail

- Courses with "D" or higher are converted to a "P" (Pass) and an "F"(Fail) remains an "F."

- A "P" grade does not count towards the final GPA, but an "F" does.

- Passed courses count toward degree requirements but cannot be used to satisfy prerequisites.

- Students can opt for one or more courses in spring 2026 as P/F which does not count toward the three courses normally permissible.

Covered Grades (Transcript Policy)

- Courses that are graded with a "C" or higher will meet prerequisite requirements.

- Courses that receive a "D" or higher will count towards satisfying major, minor, or core requirements.

- On the official transcript, grades of "C-" or higher appear as "SC;" grades of "D" or lower do not appear.

Covered Grades and Pass/Fail

- Applying both options results in "P" for "D" or higher, while "F," or "W" do not appear on the official transcript.

- "D" or higher grades do not count toward the Official GPA, but an "F" will count toward the Final GPA.

- Passed courses count toward degree requirements but cannot be used to satisfy prerequisites.

- In this option, the unofficial transcript will show either "P" or "F" depending on the grade.

Three Core Spring 2026 Rules

- Any grade above an "F" may fulfill a major, minor, or Core requirement this semester.

- A prerequisite still requires at least a "C" or higher.

- A "D" or "D+" still counts toward the 128 credits required for graduation this semester.

Important Notes

- Prerequisites : Only the Standard Letter Grade and Covered Grade Option (courses completed with a "C" or better) will allow students to meet prerequisite requirements, as outlined in the charts above.

- Degree Requirements : Pass/fail grades count towards degree requirements and overall completed credits if the class is "passed." Covered grades count toward degree requirements if the grade is "D" or higher.

- GPA Impact

- Pass/Fail : A "P" grade does not impact the official or Final GPA. A grade of "F" impacts the Official and Final GPA if not also covered under the Covered Grade option.

- Covered Grade : All grades do not count towards the Final GPA; they do count towards the Official GPA.

- Official Transcripts : Depending on the grading basis option, courses may or may not appear on the official transcript.

- Unofficial transcripts : All courses will show regardless of which grading option is selected. In the cases of a Pass/Fail, you will either receive a "P" or an "F: on your unofficial transcript.

- First-year students and Study Away : First-year students who choose pass/fail for their courses will have a limited number of courses counted toward their gpa before their eligibility for study away is determined. This may impact the study away decisions.

- Capstone : Capstone courses are also covered by these temporary options.

- Foreign language classes at Study Away Sites : Required foreign language classes at study away sites cannot be taken as pass/fail and need to be taken for a letter grade. However, required language classes at the study away sites can be elected to follow the covered grading policy.

Deadlines and Eligibility

- How to Apply : Complete the Spring 2026 Course Grading Selection form , which will be published on March 23 and will be sent out to all students.

- How to confirm that your request was submitted : Once your grading options have been submitted, you will receive a confirmation email. If it doesn't arrive within an hour, please resubmit your request. If the issue persists, check your spam folder and contact nyuad.registrar@nyu.edu before the grading deadline.

- Deadline for first 7-week classes : March 27, 2026, at 4pm (GST)

- Deadline for 14-week classes and second 7-week classes : May 1, 2026, at 4pm (GST)

- Limits : Upper-division students may declare all courses P/F this semester. This does not count toward your career limit of three.

- First-Year Students : You are allowed to declare one or more course P/F this semester (this is an exception to the usual rule and remember that all first year grades are still included in the covered grade policy). Please note if you select this option, the number of courses that count in your Official GPA will be limited for study away eligibility and may not be as beneficial to your study away application. It is best to speak with an Academic Advisor at the ARC regarding your selection.

- Students currently on an NYU Study Away : These policies apply to all NYUAD students based on their home school, regardless of where they are currently studying (New York, Shanghai, etc.). The deadline to elect the grading options follow the deadlines as listed above (please note that graduate level coursework is not eligible for covered grading - only pass/fail).

- Students currently on an NYU Study Away and taking courses at a partner school (such as Tulsa or Sydney Universities): Students need to submit any grading options by the May 1 deadline through email at nyuad.registrar@nyu.edu and include the course name and number.

- Graduate study courses (including at study away sites): Graduate-level coursework is not eligible for covered grading; only the Pass/Fail grading option is allowed.

- Students on Exchange Program courses in the spring semester: If you are participating in an exchange program this spring (such as Trinity or a university in Korea), you must follow the grading options and policies of your host university. Restriction: Covered grading is not an option for exchange courses. Any pass/fail options must be arranged directly with the exchange university/college.

- Visiting Students from NYU New York and NYU Shanghai : Visiting students can only use the pass/fail option. Please check with your home school on how pass/fail will impact your degree progress and if it can be used towards your degree requirements. Visiting Students can complete the online form but should then forward the email response to their home school to review and process any grade change requests. Remember not to select the covered grade option. Only the home school can approve any pass/fail request(s).
