- On the official transcript, grades of "C-" or higher appear as "SC" and grades of "D" or lower do not appear.

- All grades count in the official GPA but not in the final GPA.

Pass/Fail

- Courses with "D" or higher are converted to a "P" (Pass) and an "F"(Fail) remains an "F."

- A "P" grade does not count towards the final GPA, but an "F" does.

- Passed courses count toward degree requirements but cannot be used to satisfy prerequisites.

- Students can opt for one or more courses in spring 2026 as P/F which does not count toward the three courses normally permissible.

Covered Grades (Transcript Policy)

- Courses that are graded with a "C" or higher will meet prerequisite requirements.

- Courses that receive a "D" or higher will count towards satisfying major, minor, or core requirements.

- On the official transcript, grades of "C-" or higher appear as "SC;" grades of "D" or lower do not appear.

Covered Grades and Pass/Fail

- Applying both options results in "P" for "D" or higher, while "F," or "W" do not appear on the official transcript.

- "D" or higher grades do not count toward the Official GPA, but an "F" will count toward the Final GPA.

- Passed courses count toward degree requirements but cannot be used to satisfy prerequisites.

- In this option, the unofficial transcript will show either "P" or "F" depending on the grade.

sections.title: Three Core Spring 2026 Rules
sections.text:
- Any grade above an "F" may fulfill a major, minor, or Core requirement this semester.

- A prerequisite still requires at least a "C" or higher.

- A "D" or "D+" still counts toward the 128 credits required for graduation this semester.

sections.title: Three Core Spring 2026 Rules · Important Notes
sections.text:
- Prerequisites : Only the Standard Letter Grade and Covered Grade Option (courses completed with a "C" or better) will allow students to meet prerequisite requirements, as outlined in the charts above.

- Degree Requirements : Pass/fail grades count towards degree requirements and overall completed credits if the class is "passed." Covered grades count toward degree requirements if the grade is "D" or higher.

- GPA Impact

- Pass/Fail : A "P" grade does not impact the official or Final GPA. A grade of "F" impacts the Official and Final GPA if not also covered under the Covered Grade option.

- Covered Grade : All grades do not count towards the Final GPA; they do count towards the Official GPA.

- Official Transcripts : Depending on the grading basis option, courses may or may not appear on the official transcript.

- Unofficial transcripts : All courses will show regardless of which grading option is selected. In the cases of a Pass/Fail, you will either receive a "P" or an "F: on your unofficial transcript.

- First-year students and Study Away : First-year students who choose pass/fail for their courses will have a limited number of courses counted toward their gpa before their eligibility for study away is determined. This may impact the study away decisions.

- Capstone : Capstone courses are also covered by these temporary options.

- Foreign language classes at Study Away Sites : Required foreign language classes at study away sites cannot be taken as pass/fail and need to be taken for a letter grade. However, required language classes at the study away sites can be elected to follow the covered grading policy.

sections.title: Three Core Spring 2026 Rules · Deadlines and Eligibility
sections.text:
- How to Apply : Complete the Spring 2026 Course Grading Selection form , which will be published on March 23 and will be sent out to all students.

- How to confirm that your request was submitted : Once your grading options have been submitted, you will receive a confirmation email. If it doesn't arrive within an hour, please resubmit your request. If the issue persists, check your spam folder and contact nyuad.registrar@nyu.edu before the grading deadline.

- Deadline for first 7-week classes : March 27, 2026, at 4pm (GST)

- Deadline for 14-week classes and second 7-week classes : May 1, 2026, at 4pm (GST)

- Limits : Upper-division students may declare all courses P/F this semester. This does not count toward your career limit of three.

- First-Year Students : You are allowed to declare one or more course P/F this semester (this is an exception to the usual rule and remember that all first year grades are still included in the covered grade policy). Please note if you select this option, the number of courses that count in your Official GPA will be limited for study away eligibility and may not be as beneficial to your study away application. It is best to speak with an Academic Advisor at the ARC regarding your selection.

- Students currently on an NYU Study Away : These policies apply to all NYUAD students based on their home school, regardless of where they are currently studying (New York, Shanghai, etc.). The deadline to elect the grading options follow the deadlines as listed above (please note that graduate level coursework is not eligible for covered grading - only pass/fail).

- Students currently on an NYU Study Away and taking courses at a partner school (such as Tulsa or Sydney Universities): Students need to submit any grading options by the May 1 deadline through email at nyuad.registrar@nyu.edu and include the course name and number.

- Graduate study courses (including at study away sites): Graduate-level coursework is not eligible for covered grading; only the Pass/Fail grading option is allowed.

- Students on Exchange Program courses in the spring semester: If you are participating in an exchange program this spring (such as Trinity or a university in Korea), you must follow the grading options and policies of your host university. Restriction: Covered grading is not an option for exchange courses. Any pass/fail options must be arranged directly with the exchange university/college.

- Visiting Students from NYU New York and NYU Shanghai : Visiting students can only use the pass/fail option. Please check with your home school on how pass/fail will impact your degree progress and if it can be used towards your degree requirements. Visiting Students can complete the online form but should then forward the email response to their home school to review and process any grade change requests. Remember not to select the covered grade option. Only the home school can approve any pass/fail request(s).

title: Spring 2026 Grading Policy FAQs · NYUAD Students
text:
Last updated: March 18, 2026

How do I know if I submitted my course request for the grading options correctly?
Once submitted, you will receive a confirmation email. If it doesn't arrive within an hour, please resubmit your request. If the issue persists, check your spam folder and contact nyuad.registrar@nyu.edu before the grading deadline.

I want the regular grading on my transcript this semester, do I have to do anything?
Students who do not submit the form by the deadline will have the standard grading posted for their classes.

If I change my mind later, can I change the course back to a letter grade or another grading option?
No, you cannot. Please do not submit the selection form until you are certain. Declaring a course P/F or as a Covered grade cannot be undone. Meet with an Academic Advisor at the Academic Resource Center to review the options prior to your selection.

What is the difference between Pass/Fail Policy and the Covered Grade policy?
Pass (P) grades show on all transcripts (except for first-year students who already benefit from the covered grade policy) but don’t factor into GPAs. Under the Covered Grade Policy, grades of C- or better show a grade of Successfully Completed (SC) on the Official Transcripts, and anything below a C- do not show.

Will my professor know which grading option I'm selecting?
No, your professor will be assigning you a regular letter grade. If selected the Pass/Fail or Covered Grade option, Albert will convert the grade accordingly. Unless you tell your professor, they will not even know what grading option you select.

How many courses can I declare pass/fail this semester?
Students can elect one or more courses as pass/fail this semester. This semester does not count toward your total limit of three (3) pass/fail classes during your undergraduate career.

First Year Students: please note if you select this option, the number of courses that count in your Official GPA will be limited for study away eligibility and may not be as beneficial to your study away application.

What if I have already opted to take a class pass/fail this semester? Does that count toward my three (3) pass/fail classes?
No, it would not count toward your three pass/fail class limit.

If I take the course pass/fail now and later decide that I want/need to take a course that has this as a prerequisite or if I change to a major or minor that requires the course, what happens?
You would need to speak with an advisor in the Academic Resource Center regarding your options, including potentially submitting an academic petition .

I'm a first-year student, and all of my courses are already covered by the transcript policy. Do I need to do anything?
Not unless you want to declare a course pass/fail. In this case, you would need to elect the option for pass/fail in the Spring 2026 Course Grading Selection form.

Will this hurt my chance for Study Away?
Study away requirements remain the same with a minimum GPA of 3.0. Please work with an Academic Advisor to select the option that is best for you.

What about graduate schools? Won't they want to see my grades?
Students should think about this carefully and reach out to the CDC. What we have seen in the past is that graduate schools (including medical schools) are open to special grading circumstances during trying semesters. This semester would definitely fall under that category, and you should reach out to any schools that you are thinking about to see how they would handle this type of situation.

How will this affect my eligibility for graduation honors?
Graduation honors are based on final grade point averages so work with your Academic Advisor to ensure you are selecting the best option for you.

Can I still withdraw from a course?

- The withdrawal deadline for the first 7-week courses has passed. The 14-week and second 7-week withdrawal deadline will be open until April 24, 2026, 4pm GST.

- For students who withdrew from their course(s) before February 20, 2026, the "W" withdrawal grade will remain on the transcript.

What are the grading options available for Capstone?
For students enrolled in Capstone, you can elect any of the grading options as outlined.

I am a visiting student at NYUAD. Does this apply to me?
Visiting Students from NYU New York and NYU Shanghai can only use the pass/fail option. Please check with your home school on how pass/fail will impact your degree progress and if it can be used towards your degree requirements. Visiting Students can complete the online form but should then forward the automated email response to their home school to review and process any grade change requests. Remember not to select the covered grade option. Only the home school can approve any pass/fail request(s).

I am on a study away, what about my foreign language class that I need to take for a letter grade? Can I take that class pass/fail?
Required language classes at the study away sites need to be taken for a letter grade but can be covered. Students will not be able to take these classes as pass/fail.

If you are currently studying away and have courses at a global partner site (such as Tulsa or Sydney University) and your courses are not listed on the grading basis form, you can still request to take them as pass/fail or covered.
For students at study away sites such as Tulsa and Sydney:

How to Apply

To submit your request, please follow these steps:

-
Email the Registrar: Send an email to the NYUAD Office of the Registrar at nyuad.registrar@nyu.edu .

-
Include Course Details: Clearly list the course names and course numbers you wish to take as pass/fail and/or covered grading.

-
Keep a Record: Save a copy of the sent email for your personal records.

Important Deadline

-
Deadline: May 1, 2026

-
Policy: Requests are final. You will not be able to change your grading option back after this deadline.

Can I take graduate courses pass/fail and/or covered while on study away or in Abu Dhabi?
Graduate classes do not fall under the covered grading policy on a study away. Students can opt for pass/fail grading options for graduate courses but NOT covered grading

I am currently studying away and have courses at a global partner site (such as Tulsa or Sydney universities) and your courses are not listed on the grading basis form, you can still request to take them as pass/fail but not covered.
For students at study away sites such as Tulsa and Sydney:

How to Apply

To submit your request, please follow these steps:

-
Email the Registrar: Send an email to the NYUAD Office of the Registrar at nyuad.registrar@nyu.edu .

-
Include Course Details: Clearly list the course names and course numbers you wish to take as pass/fail. Partner sites do not have a covered grading option and students will want to plan accordingly.

-
Keep a Record: Save a copy of the sent email for your personal records.

Important Deadline

-
Deadline: May 1, 2026

-
Policy: Requests are final. You will not be able to change your grading option back after this deadline.

I am currently on a study away on an exchange program (such as Trinity University or a university in Korea). Can I still take classes pass/fail and/or covered?
Unfortunately students at exchange program sites need to follow the policies of the local university. Pass/fail and/or covered grading is not an option for exchange coursework. Please note Tulsa and Sydney is not an exchange program site and should follow the instructions noted above.

Related official links:
https://students.nyuad.nyu.edu/academics/academic-resources/academic-advising/academic-petition-process/

title: Research · NYUAD Students
text:
Note: AY 26-27 information will be updated by October 2026.

As part of our commitment to fostering a dynamic research environment, the Office of Student Research offers multiple avenues for students to gain experience in research and scholarly activities.

Please review the list below of key student research opportunities and AY 25-26 deadlines. Information sessions will be held as follows:

- Tamayyuz Research Fellowship: December 9, January 8 and January 20. RSVP here .

- Summer research grants and summer research assistant program: February 12, February 19, February 26. RSVP here .

Summer Opportunities

- Summer Research Assistant Program | Deadline: March 5 (on-campus and remote), April 15 (on-campus and remote) and May 5 (remote only)

Summer Research Assistant Program : NYUAD faculty appoint NYUAD undergraduate and masters students during the summer to work on faculty research projects.

Positions should be full-time (35 hours per week) and take place remotely unless the work has to be completed on campus.

Note: All positions must be advertised on Handshake before the appointment form is submitted.

Dates | Funding Amount and Source | Deadline | Submitted by Faculty or Student?

Positions can begin on one of the following dates: Monday, May 18, 2026 Monday, June 1, 2026 Monday, June 22, 2026 Positions can end on one of the following dates: Friday, June 19, 2026 Friday, July 10, 2026 Friday, July 24, 2026 Friday, August 14, 2026 | Funded by faculty OTPS funds. AED 38.50 for undergraduates and AED 59.00 per hour for Masters students. For undergraduates, an additional $188 per week if the student is based on campus. | March 5 and April 15 for on-campus or remote opportunities. May 5 for remote opportunities. | Faculty

- Post-graduation Practical Training Program | Deadline: March 5 and April 15

Post-graduation Practical Training Program : NYUAD faculty can appoint graduating students to work on faculty research projects after graduation.

Note: All positions must be advertised on Handshake before the appointment form is submitted.

Appointment Dates | Funding Amount and Source | Deadline | Submitted by Faculty or Student?

All appointments must be full-time (35 hours per week) for one of the following date options: May 20 - June 20 (≈3 weeks) May 20 - July 10 (≈6 weeks) | Funded by Faculty OTPS Funds. $500 per week for student stipend and $188 per week for student housing charge (graduating seniors); - $770 per week for student stipend (graduating masters students). | March 5 and April 15 | Faculty

- Summer Research Grants | Deadline: March 13 (extended to March 16) and April 13

Summer Research Grants : Students can apply for funding support if they have secured full-time internal or external summer research internship/experiential learning positions.

Appointment Dates | Funding Amount and Source | Deadline | Submitted by Faculty or Student?

Between May 18 - August 14 | Up to $4,000 from the Office of Student Research, depending on the location of the research. | March 13 (extended to 16) and April 13 | Student

Academic Year Opportunities

- NYUAD Tamayyuz (Excellence) Research Fellowship | Deadline: February 27

NYUAD Tamayyuz (Excellence) Research Fellowship : Provides an opportunity for graduating seniors to apply for a prestigious one-year research fellowship position following their graduation.

Appointment Dates | Funding Amount and Source | Deadline | Submitted by Faculty or Student?

September 1, 2026 - August 31, 2027 | Monthly stipend and benefits for the duration of the appointment. Funded by the Office of Student Research. | February 27 | Student submits application. Faculty submits letter of recommendation.

- Student Assistantship Program | Deadline: Rolling

Student Assistantship Program : Provides students at NYUAD with on-campus work experience opportunities within academic and administrative departments throughout the school year.

Note: Administered by the Career Development Center.

Appointment Dates | Funding Amount and Source | Deadline | Submitted by Faculty or Student?

Throughout the academic year | Funded by faculty OTPS funds. All undergraduate students are paid a fixed rate of AED 38.5 / USD 10.48 an hour; Masters’ students are paid a set rate of AED 59 / USD 16.06 an hour. . | Rolling | Faculty

- Conference Grants | Deadline: Rolling

Conference Grants : Students can apply for financial support if they have been invited to present their research or creative works at conferences or exhibitions.

Appointment Dates | Funding Amount and Source | Deadline | Submitted by Faculty or Student?

Throughout the academic year and summer | Up to $1,500 to assist students with logistical costs associated with attending the conference. | Rolling | Student

- Laidlaw Scholars Leadership and Research Program | Deadline: January 29, 2027

Laidlaw Scholars Leadership and Research Program : Supports students in becoming global citizens and change-makers by combining rigorous research with leadership training over an 18-month period.

Appointment Dates | Funding Amount and Source | Deadline | Submitted by Faculty or Student?

Throughout the academic year and summer | Up to USD 4,000 per year in your first and second years for the summer projects. | January 29, 2027 | Student

General Information

- Conducting Research in the Local Community

If you are a student who would like to conduct research in the local community (e.g., conducting surveys or interviews in public places or taking pictures/filming in public places), you must first speak to Nancy Wallach, at nbw3@nyu.edu for the appropriate steps before you begin your research. This applies to IRB-approved research and research that does not require IRB approval. Students in Abu Dhabi and Dubai have been in trouble with the local police before for benign research in the community and we would like to help you avoid any trouble with the police.

- IRB Approval Process — Conducting Research in the Community

The Human Research Protection Program is designed to help you:

- Determine if your work must be reviewed and approved by the NYUAD IRB

- Understand local regulations, federal regulations, and the NYUAD procedures concerning human subjects in research

- Prepare an application for review and approval to the NYUAD IRB

- Respond to any concerns or requested revisions the NYUAD IRB may request after the initial review

At NYUAD, all research involving human subjects (funded or not funded) must be reviewed and approved by the University's Institutional Review Board (IRB) before being carried out. The NYUAD IRB is authorized to review and approve research involving human subjects through a Federalwide Assurance, an agreement with the US Department of Health and Human Services, through the Office for Human Research Protections (OHRP). — Read more

sections.title: General Information
sections.text:
- Conducting Research in the Local Community

If you are a student who would like to conduct research in the local community (e.g., conducting surveys or interviews in public places or taking pictures/filming in public places), you must first speak to Nancy Wallach, at nbw3@nyu.edu for the appropriate steps before you begin your research. This applies to IRB-approved research and research that does not require IRB approval. Students in Abu Dhabi and Dubai have been in trouble with the local police before for benign research in the community and we would like to help you avoid any trouble with the police.

- IRB Approval Process — Conducting Research in the Community

The Human Research Protection Program is designed to help you:

- Determine if your work must be reviewed and approved by the NYUAD IRB

- Understand local regulations, federal regulations, and the NYUAD procedures concerning human subjects in research

- Prepare an application for review and approval to the NYUAD IRB

- Respond to any concerns or requested revisions the NYUAD IRB may request after the initial review

At NYUAD, all research involving human subjects (funded or not funded) must be reviewed and approved by the University's Institutional Review Board (IRB) before being carried out. The NYUAD IRB is authorized to review and approve research involving human subjects through a Federalwide Assurance, an agreement with the US Department of Health and Human Services, through the Office for Human Research Protections (OHRP). — Read more

title: Conference Grants · NYUAD Students
text:
The Office of Student Research offers conference grants to support students who have been invited to present their research or creative work through a competitive selection process. Grants may be used during the fall, spring, or summer terms, with a maximum award of $1,500 per conference . Please note that only one student can be funded to present a given paper or research project.

Which Type of Conference Will be Supported

The organization sponsoring the conference must be considered by the faculty of NYUAD to be among the very best examples of venues for research, scholarship or performance in the arts. Examples of such experiences are an invitation to present a juried research paper at a professional research conference or the exhibition of intellectual work (art work) at a gallery.

Can I Attend A Conference With A Faculty Member Who Is Already Attending A Conference?

Simply attending a conference will not be considered for support.

Students must attend the conference to present research (full presentation). Students cannot attend on behalf of a faculty to present a faculty member’s research. Students must have had significant involvement (e.g. co-authorship) in the research (actual direct research was involved) if in collaboration with a faculty member.

Qualifications

Students applying for a conference grant must meet the following qualifications:

- The student must be a full-time NYUAD student, currently enrolled.

- A grade point average of above 3.3 or otherwise indicative of sustained excellence of academic achievement ( includes first year grades ).

- The student must be in good academic standing.

- The student must be in good disciplinary standing.

- Evidence that the student is performing at a very strong academic level in his/her current load of courses.

- The student must not have already received NYUAD funding to present this same research at another conference.

- Students who are taking part in a semester abroad at the time of the conference will not be eligible to apply for funding.

- Students enrolled in J-Term courses will not be permitted to miss class in order to attend a conference.

- Graduate students must be enrolled in either MSc or MFA programs. Graduate students enrolled in the Global PhD Fellowship are not eligible for conference grants via the Office of Student Research. Funding is available for Global PhD Fellows through GPPO.

What Will The Research Conference Grant Support?

- Economy class airfare (as needed)

- Visa costs (only costs but not logistical support)

- Registration fees

- Conference accommodation

- Meals

Support up to $1,500 will be provided towards these costs but may not cover all costs.

Application Process

Students applying for a conference grant must follow the process below:

- If missing class at NYUAD, the student must inform their professors whose classes they are missing, and alternative arrangements to catch up with work will need to be approved by the professor before the student applies for funding.

- Before submitting the completed application, applicants must have their faculty supervisor and Mentor sign the Faculty Mentor Assessment Form , which needs to be included with their application.

- Applicants must ensure the following documentation is included with their application:

- Proof of invitation from the Conference

- Project Proposal

- If missing class in Abu Dhabi, confirmation of classes, and evidence that alternative arrangements have been made to catch up with work.

- Faculty Mentor Assessment Form

- The Office of Student Research will provide an outcome to the applicant within two weeks of the submitted conference funding request.

The entire proposal must be submitted online. If you have any questions, please contact Farhana Goha at nyuad.studentresearch@nyu.edu .

title: Laidlaw Scholars Leadership and Research Program · NYUAD Students
text:
Do you have the drive to become one of the leaders of the future? Are you excited by the opportunity to help tackle world problems? If so, this program is for you!

Deadline: January 29, 2027, 11.59 PM GST.

Information sessions for AY 26-27 will be held on the following days:

- Tuesday, October 27, 2026, from 1-1:40 PM

- Thursday, November 5, 2026, from 1-1:40 PM

- Tuesday, November 24, 2026, from 5-5:40 PM

- Tuesday, December 8, from 1-1:40 PM

- Wednesday, January 13, from 5-5:40 PM

Please RSVP here . A Zoom link and calendar invite will be shared with you closer to the date of the session.

The Laidlaw Leadership and Research Program is a transformative opportunity for undergraduate students who are passionate about making a meaningful impact through research and ethical leadership. The program runs at many leading universities across the globe, creating a large network of past and present scholars. It is generously funded by the Laidlaw Foundation.

In AY 25-26, NYUAD recruited the first cohort of NYUAD Laidlaw Scholars. Gaining a place on the Laidlaw Program is widely regarded as an indicator of exceptional academic and leadership promise. The call for AY 26-27 applications will open on November 26, 2026.

What Is the Laidlaw Program?

The Laidlaw Program supports students in becoming global citizens and change-makers by combining rigorous research with leadership training over an 18-month period.

You’ll gain:

- Hands-on summer research experience (1st summer) under the guidance of a faculty mentor

- Leadership skills through training and practical work, designed to challenge and inspire

- Opportunities to collaborate with an international network of over 2,000 Laidlaw Scholars from more than 20 leading international universities

- Funding to support your research and leadership experiences, as well as funding to attend one Laidlaw student conference in London

- A meaningful distinction to your resume and increase your marketability to employers

- Hands-on summer ' leadership in action' experience (2nd summer) at an external organization/NGO.

To find out more about Laidlaw Scholars, please visit the Laidlaw Foundation's website . Hear from a Laidlaw Scholar about their experience .

Program Structure

Summer Program: Year 1 (Research Summer)

- All Laidlaw Scholars will undertake research lasting six weeks in their first summer.

- Students will either be able to choose from a list of projects curated by faculty ( see here for summer 2026 positions - summer 2027 information to be updated by November 26, 2026 ) or propose their own project, but in all cases, will need an NYUAD faculty supervisor.

- Present your findings in a research showcase.

Summer Program: Year 2 (Leadership-in-Action (LIA) Summer)
The Leadership in Action project gives you the chance to build on skills and knowledge gained in the first year of the program. You will be working with communities in need, doing something to make the world a better place. You will take on a leadership-focused experience in an international or national setting.

Leadership Training

The Laidlaw Program is committed to supporting your development as an outstanding leader. The two key elements are Leadership Training and the Leadership In Action summer project.

In-Person Leadership Training at NYUAD
Spread through the first and second year and across 6-9 days, this specially tailored program for the NYUAD Laidlaw cohort will introduce you to key concepts in leadership. You will work with your cohort in depth to learn about:

- You, as a leader — and finding your leadership style

- Leading teams — adapting your style to others

- Leading in different workplace cultures

- Ethical leadership — understand the principles that underpin all good leadership

Online Ethical Leadership Training (University of Oxford)
Laidlaw scholars from all participating universities will come together to participate in Ethical Leadership workshops taught by the Oxford Character Project at Oxford University. Ethical leadership is one of the Laidlaw Program core values, and these modules tie together all your previous learning and leadership experiences.

In six stimulating and thought-provoking online seminars (one per month), you will consider different elements of character as it relates to leadership. A further group exercise each month will consolidate the learning, and give you the opportunity to meet and work with scholars from across the Laidlaw universities.

These workshops are the final formal leadership training elements of the program, and take place at the end of your second year in the program.

Funding

Whatever your financial circumstances, you can apply to the program in the knowledge that students are NOT expected to fund any element of the program themselves. It is generously paid for by a grant from the Laidlaw Foundation.

As Laidlaw Scholars, you will receive a grant of up to USD 4,000 per year in your first and second years for the summer projects. The grant is intended to cover any logistical costs associated with your summer research experience.

You will also be able to apply for additional funding to cover all or most travel costs where you are undertaking a project or trip within or outside the UAE. All travel and accommodation for other core activities will be provided by the program.

In exchange, you'll be expected to fully commit to all the program requirements.

Application Information

Eligibility

- The Laidlaw Scholarship Program is only available to NYUAD first-year and second-year undergraduate students.

- Second-year students are expected to have a minimum cumulative GPA of 3.0 or above.

- If students are accepted into the program and accept their placement, they must commit to the full requirements of the program.

- Students who will be studying in Sydney in Fall 2027 or Fall 2028 will not be eligible for the program due to Australian visa requirements and the implications these have for participation in the program’s required summer components.

Application Process

- Submit the following using this form [link to be updated in November] by January 29, 2027.

- Motivation : What motivates you to want to join this program? What particular qualities do you bring with you, and how do you plan to apply these qualities in the program? (Record a video interview for 60-90 seconds)

- Expected Outcomes : What benefits do you expect to derive from this leadership and research program, and how do you intend to apply what you will learn in your future life for the good of the world? (Max. 250 words)

- Leadership in Action : As a Global Citizen, what environmental or societal issues would you like to address in your Leadership in Action (LiA) project? Click here to learn more about LiAs. This proposal is not final — you’re welcome to include multiple ideas if you are not entirely sure at this stage. (Max. 250 words)

- Summer Research Project : Select which pre-identified summer research positions (select 3 in order of preference) you would be interested in, or submit a proposal for your own summer research project. (Max. 250 words). This can include a position you have secured with faculty yourself, or a project that you are proposing. For student-initiated research projects , students will also need to attach confirmation from an NYUAD professor, confirming that they endorse and will supervise your project.

- Your resume or CV

- Your unofficial transcript.

- Your application will be reviewed by a committee, including faculty and staff, after the closing date.

- Shortlisted candidates will be invited by email to a short online or in-person interview in February.

- Final decisions will be communicated by the end of February.

Review Criteria
Applications will be assessed based on:

- The strength of the match between the research project and the student's skills and goals.

- The potential for leadership and commitment to make a positive change to the community they live in and build a better world.

- The student’s commitment to ethical leadership.

- The student’s record of activities indicating research and leadership potential.

- The student’s understanding of the Laidlaw values.

Key Program Dates

- October 2026-January 2027: Information sessions to be held.

- November 2026: Application page to go live to students.

- January 29, 2027: Deadline for applications.

- February 2027: Students to be informed of the outcome of their application.

- April 2027: Laidlaw scholars will be invited to a retreat to connect as a group and explore/exchange ideas for the program.

- Summer 2027: Laidlaw Scholars take part in their research opportunity.

- Fall 2027 and Spring 2028: In-Person Leadership Training at NYUAD

- Fall 2027 and Spring 2028: Online Leadership Training by the University of Oxford

- October 2027: Laidlaw Scholars’ Conference — typically in the UK

- December 2027-February 2028: Laidlaw scholars will finalize their leadership in action plans.

- Summer 2028: Laidlaw Scholars take part in their LIA opportunity.

Terms and Conditions for Laidlaw Scholars

View the Terms and Conditions
By submitting an application to become a Laidlaw Scholar, you agree to be bound by these terms and conditions. Failure to comply could result in the withholding of some financial benefits from the scheme and/or the loss of your place on the scheme.

Each scholar agrees to:

- Attend the mandatory development events throughout their time as a scholar. The mandatory events are six to eight days of leadership training, and two six-week summer projects in years one and two of the program. Prior permission for unavoidable absence must be sought from the Program Manager/Director. Failure to attend the mandatory training or to produce the required project outputs to a satisfactory standard could result in loss of grants, a requirement to repay money that has been spent, and ineligibility to apply for other NYUAD summer-funded programs.

- Respond to communication from the program manager over the summer project period and during term-time.

- Attend research project meetings with the project supervisor/mentor and report on progress as agreed.

- Produce the required project outputs on time and in the format outlined by your supervisor or the Program Manager.

- Join the Laidlaw Scholars private social group (Laidlaw Scholars' Network) — allowing individuals to network with other scholars from their own and other universities, to share their experiences, answer questions, and act as mentors to new cohorts.

- Be open to participating in the production of content to be used on the Laidlaw Scholars website or the NYUAD website, and potentially be used for marketing the program.

- Keep the Laidlaw Scholars Program Manager updated with their progress and career information following graduation.

- Give back to scholars of the future by acting as a mentor.

- Abide by any other reasonable requests from the NYUAD Laidlaw Program, Laidlaw Foundation, or NYUAD.

title: NYUAD Tamayyuz Research Fellowship Program · NYUAD Students
text:
NYU Abu Dhabi's Tamayyuz Research Fellowship Program offers graduating seniors the opportunity to apply for a competitive and prestigious one-year research fellowship at NYUAD. This fellowship program aims to strengthen a student's research skills, retain outstanding academic talent within the region, contribute to the growth and development of research in the UAE, and act as a platform to make students more competitive for graduate school. It is an excellent opportunity for students to explore research directions and graduate school possibilities.

Fellows must be available for the duration of the appointment (from September 1, 2026 - August 31, 2027).

Deadline: AY 26-27 research fellowship applications are due February 27, 2026, at 5pm GST . Positions are subject to securing relevant funding for AY 26-27.

Online information sessions will include representatives from each of the centers. Sign up here for a session on December 9 (2:15-3:15 PM), January 8 (2:15-3:15 PM), or January 20 (4 PM).

What's Provided

- One-year (non-renewable) Research Fellowship, with a salary and fringe benefits, based at NYU Abu Dhabi.

- Research Skill Development: Access to technical and professional growth to ensure participants develop skills that yield strong candidates for graduate school. Emphasis is placed on hands-on experience while simultaneously shaping and preparing their own research projects.

- Professional Development: Working with existing faculty allows the student multiple interfaces to potential professional connections and attendance at seminars and conferences.

- Administrative assistance with preparing graduate school applications.

- Work space, full use of NYUAD’s library facilities, and accommodation provided by NYUAD, subject to availability.

What is the Criteria for Review?

Applications will be reviewed based on their individual merit. The criteria for evaluating the applications are as follows:

- The strength of the application.

- Evidence of a strong and consistent record of outstanding academic achievement.

- How the position contributes to the student’s career development plans.

- The strength of the research proposal, with clear anticipated research activities, a timeline and specific milestones.

- The strength of the supervising faculty’s recommendation letter.

Please note that for the divisional fellowship applications, the faculty committee may also take into consideration the following points when making decisions:

- Any specific outcomes outlined (e.g. publication).

- Impact of research within the UAE.

- Interdisciplinary research that has the potential for cross-cutting impact.

- Consideration for previously underrepresented disciplines.

Key Dates and Timeline

- December 9 (2.15-3.15pm) | January 8 (2.15-3.15pm) | January 20 (2.15-3.15pm): Information sessions to be held for students.

- February 27, 5pm GST: Deadline for fellowship applications.

- March 31: Intended date by which students and faculty are informed of the outcome and necessary clearances are initiated.

- April-May: Formal offers are made to students.

- September 1, 2026: One year appointment as a fellow begins.

Fellowships on Offer

Note that your application for each of the fellowship opportunities on offer are reviewed independently, and are not mutually exclusive, should you decide to apply to one or more of the fellowships.

-

Divisional Fellowships

NYU Abu Dhabi's Divisional Tamayyuz Research Fellowships

-

CITIES Fellowship

Tamayyuz Research Fellowship with CITIES

-

HBCTL Fellowship

Tamayyuz Research Fellowship with the Hilary Ballon Center for Teaching and Learning

-

OGI Fellowship

Tamayyuz Research Fellowship with the Office of Global Inclusion

-

OSS Fellowship

Tamayyuz Research Fellowship with the Office of Sustainability and Stewardship

-

CGSB Fellowship

Tamayyuz Research Fellowship with the Center for Genomics and Systems Biology

-

AI Fellowship

Tamayyuz Research Fellowship with the Office of Learning and Organizational Development

sections.title: What is the Criteria for Review?
sections.text:
Applications will be reviewed based on their individual merit. The criteria for evaluating the applications are as follows:

- The strength of the application.

- Evidence of a strong and consistent record of outstanding academic achievement.

- How the position contributes to the student’s career development plans.

- The strength of the research proposal, with clear anticipated research activities, a timeline and specific milestones.

- The strength of the supervising faculty’s recommendation letter.

Please note that for the divisional fellowship applications, the faculty committee may also take into consideration the following points when making decisions:

- Any specific outcomes outlined (e.g. publication).

- Impact of research within the UAE.

- Interdisciplinary research that has the potential for cross-cutting impact.

- Consideration for previously underrepresented disciplines.

title: AI (L&OD) · NYUAD Students
text:
Deadline for proposals: February 27, 5pm GST

The AI Research Fellow, reporting to the Office of Learning and Organizational Development, will leverage cutting-edge research and best practices across current and evolving Large Language Model (LLM) tools to accelerate institutional AI capability building. This role is critical in providing research-led tool development, actionable operational insight, and practical use case development for administrative and organizational teams.

Key Responsibilities

Project-Based Research and Operational Support:

- Execute project-based assignments that deliver actionable insights and operational support to the Learning and Organizational Development team, specifically focused on building institutional AI capabilities.

-
Track and research institutional initiatives, contributing directly to the growth of AI adoption and learning . This includes developing practical use cases, supporting team workshops, and continuously exploring and evaluating LLM tools for workplace integration.

-
Schedule, advertise, co-design, and facilitate monthly AI-focused learning sessions and ad hoc team-based learning.

Operational & Strategic Development:

- Collaborate with key institutional stakeholders, including the Hillary Ballon Centre for Teaching and Learning, the Provost Office, the Special Advisor on AI, the Library, Undergraduate Education, and Student Affairs.

-
Facilitate the adaptation of relevant common initiatives across all NYU campuses through participation in pilot programs, webinars, and workshops.

Independent Research Project:

- In addition to assigned projects, the Fellow will have the unique opportunity to lead and publish an independent research project of their own interest, focused on an area of AI capability building.

Candidate Qualifications

- A minimum cumulative GPA of 3.7, with evidence of a strong and consistent record of outstanding academic achievement.

- A proven desire to explore research opportunities and demonstrate intellectual curiosity.

-
Academic Excellence: Must be a high-achieving recent graduate capable of leveraging research and communication skills to benefit the university. Expected graduation with a bachelor's degree in May or summer 2026, providing all graduation requirements are met before September 1, 2026. Also available to those who have graduated in AY 25-26 or AY 24-25.

-
Technical Proficiency: Candidates must have recent experience demonstrating AI-enabled outcomes and the ability to translate technical knowledge into practical, administrative solutions.

-
Collaborative Mindset: Proven ability to work closely with a variety of campus stakeholders and leadership across different divisions.

-
Communication: Able to confidently communicate, co-design, and deliver high-quality team-based workshops.

-
Strategic Thinking: Capacity to provide critical operational support and develop initiatives that have a tangible impact for teams and individuals.

Professional Development Benefits

-
Leadership Development: The Fellow will be integrated into a structured development program, providing exposure to executive decision-making and university governance.

-
Broad Exposure: Gain deep insight into the university's work across multiple sectors, from operations and academics to research and programming .

-
Stakeholder Engagement: Gain direct experience working in partnership with the Senior Leadership team and various academic and operational divisions.

Application Process

Students who meet eligibility requirements and are interested in applying for the Tamayyuz Research Fellowship are required to submit the application form . Students should have the following documents ready before filling out the form.

- Student's Resume

- Cover Letter, outlining the student's interest, understanding and enthusiasm for AI Capability and understanding. Use case development in application for University administration. Note any previous experience within the field, and how the position contributes to career development plans (1-2 pages).

-
Research proposals for this position should be focused on a specific area of interest that the fellow would like to explore. Some examples are noted below but we are open to all proposals. Note this is not limited to students who are studying Computer Science, and coding skills are not required, though a conceptual understanding of Large Language Models and their evolution will be crucial for success.

A nudge: The thoughtful use of AI tools is encouraged, though personalize and ensure to reflect on your human and individual uniqueness.

Initiatives intended ​​in one or more AI capability related fields such as but not limited to practical use case development, administrative workflow optimization, deployment of chatbots, data analytics for institutional efficiency, and process automation. Measuring and evaluating impact.

Students should also include a budget outlining any anticipated research expenses and expected conference attendances should also be provided. Please ensure the budget request is no more than USD 5,000.

- One letter of support from a faculty member that supports the proposed research project and confirms the faculty member is able to provide research support and guidance for the duration of the fellow's research project. This can be submitted as part of the application, or the faculty member can send the letter by email directly to Natasha Putnins at nkp2014@nyu.edu .

title: CGSB Tamayyuz Research Fellowship · NYUAD Students
text:
Deadline for proposals: February 27, 5 pm GST

CGSB Goals and Mission

The Center for Genomics and Systems Biology (CGSB) is a research center dedicated to fostering and enhancing the research and training missions of NYUAD, where undergraduate students, graduate students, and postdoctoral scientists engage in research across disciplines facilitated by advanced instrumentation and computational support for high-throughput data collection, visualization, and analysis. The NYUAD CGSB operates in partnership with its sister center, NYU Biology’s CGSB, in New York, in an open organizational framework that enables transformative collaborative work across the globe, supported by joint technology and service platforms.

Researchers in the Center use global or “systems” level approaches to address the organization and function of biological systems at multiple levels: cells, organisms, populations, and ecosystems. This work is grounded in the ability to generate and analyze large datasets, which is revolutionizing the way biological research is conducted and is leading to new holistic views of how organisms develop, function, and evolve.

A unifying theme of the Center’s research programs is to understand how genomic information is transformed into the complex molecular networks that underlie cellular and organismal behaviors, how genomes evolve and adapt to changing environmental conditions, and how knowledge about these processes can be used to benefit society and our stewardship of the planet. To tackle these broad goals, the NYUAD-CGSB has established two major research programs that span key areas of genomics and systems biology: Biomedicine and Health, and Environmental Adaptation and Sustainability. More information on the research groups can be found here .

Candidate Requirements

- A minimum cumulative GPA of 3.7, with evidence of a strong and consistent record of outstanding academic achievement.

- A proven desire to explore research opportunities and demonstrate intellectual curiosity in genomics.

- Expected graduation with a bachelor's degree in fall 2025, spring or summer 2026.

Application Process

Students who meet eligibility requirements and are interested in applying for the CGSB’s Tamayyuz Research Fellowship must submit the application form . Please ensure the following documents are ready before filling out the form.

- Student's Resume

- Cover Letter outlining the student's interest, understanding, and enthusiasm for research in Genomics or Systems Biology, previous experience within the field, and how the position contributes to career development plans (1-2 pages).

- Student's Transcript.

- Research Proposal, demonstrating anticipated research activities, a timeline, and specific milestones (2-4 pages). A section of the proposal (~250 words) should be dedicated to explaining how the proposed project aligns with CGSB’s vision and mission .

- One letter of support from a CGSB faculty member who supports the proposed research project and confirms the faculty member can provide research support and guidance for the duration of the fellow's research project. The faculty member should send the letter by email directly to Enas Qudeimat at eq6@nyu.edu . Standing faculty are faculty with full-time appointments at NYUAD for Academic Year 2026-2027.

title: CITIES Tamayyuz Research Fellowship · NYUAD Students
text:
Deadline for proposals: February 27, 5pm GST

The Tamayyuz Research Fellowship in CITIES can appeal to students who wish to explore research directions and graduate school possibilities, specifically in the area of urban science, spanning disciplines from Engineering through Computer Science, Sociology, History, and the Arts.

The CITIES fellowship is awarded annually and was first activated in AY 19-20. Thanks to their talent and to the fellowship experience, our fellows were accepted to prestigious schools to pursue their careers. Such schools include the University of California Berkeley (USA), MIT (USA), and Politecnico di Milano (Italy).

Applications should be aligned with CITIES' vision and mission and its main research objectives . All projects related to Urban Science would be welcome. Projects with an NYUAD community engagement perspective (e.g. through data collection and other initiatives) are particularly encouraged. A section of the proposal (approx. 250 words) must be dedicated to explaining how the proposed project aligns with CITIES' vision and mission.

CITIES Goals and Mission

The NYUAD’s Center for InTeractIng urban nEtworkS (CITIES – مدن) is an interdisciplinary research center dedicated to advance urban science and promote cutting-edge research that is translated into practical, real-world solutions for the benefit of society. Our ultimate goal is to foster sustainable, resilient, and equitable cities. CITIES’ research focuses on the interactions between the physical, digital, and social layers. To that end, it leverages the expertise of faculty members from all NYUAD’ divisions (Engineering, Science, Social Science, and Arts and Humanities), and world-renowned scientific collaborators from multiple institutions, as well as stakeholders across the UAE and abroad. Our mission is to establish a vibrant and globally recognized knowledge hub for urban networks, bridge the gap between scientific significance and practical value, and further develop the human capital that will propel the city of Abu Dhabi and the UAE into a richer and more sustainable future.

Candidate Requirements

- A minimum cumulative GPA of 3.7, with evidence of a strong and consistent record of outstanding academic achievement.

- A proven desire to explore research opportunities and demonstrate intellectual curiosity in the area of urban science.

- Expected graduation with a bachelor's degree in May/Summer 2026, providing all graduation requirements have been met by September 1, 2026. Also available to those who have/will graduate in AY 25-26.

- A research focus that aligns with the mission and overarching goals of the research center.

Application Process

Students who meet eligibility requirements and are interested in applying for the CITIES' Post-graduation Research Fellowship Program are required to submit the Application Form . Please ensure you have the following ready before filling out the form.

- Student's Resume

- Cover Letter, outlining the student's interest, understanding, and enthusiasm for the work, any previous experience within the field, and how the position contributes to career development plans (1-2 pages).

- Research Proposal, demonstrating anticipated research activities, a timeline, and specific milestone (2-4 pages). The Research Proposal should give a clear indication of fit between the proposed work and CITIES' mission. A section of the proposal (~250 words) should be dedicated to explain how the proposed project aligns with CITIES' vision and mission. A budget outlining any anticipated field research expenses and expected conference travel should be provided.

- Recommendation Letter from faculty confirming he/she is available to supervise the student and supports the proposed research. Note that the faculty supervisor can be any standing faculty at NYUAD, regardless of their current involvement in CITIES, and is not part of the selection criteria. Standing faculty are faculty with full time appointments at NYUAD for the AY 26-27.

- All applications should be submitted by the deadline. If you have any questions, please email Adela Kovarova <ak6935@nyu.edu>.

Related official links:
https://students.nyuad.nyu.edu/academics/research/cities-post-graduation-research-fellowship-program/cities-post-graduation-research-fellowship-program-application-form/

text:

NYUAD's Tamayyuz Research Fellowship is designed to support a select cohort of exceptional NYUAD graduating students by providing a competitive opportunity for a prestigious one-year fellowship at NYUAD. This fellowship aims to encourage ingenuity in research pursuit, strengthen research skills, make students more competitive for graduate school, retain outstanding academic talent within the region, and contribute to the growth and development of research in the UAE. Please note up to eight fellowship positions across the divisions will be available for AY 26-27. Positions are subject to funding being secured.

Candidate Requirements

- A proven desire to explore research opportunities and demonstrate intellectual curiosity.

- Expected graduation with a bachelor's degree in May/Summer 2026, providing all graduation requirements have been met by September 1, 2026. Also available to those who have/will graduate in AY 25-26.

Application Process

Students who meet eligibility requirements and are interested in applying for the NYUAD Tamayyuz Research Fellowship are required to submit the Application Form . Please ensure you have the following ready before filling out the form.

- Student's Resume

- Cover Letter, outlining the student's interest, understanding and enthusiasm for the work, any previous experience within the field, and how the position contributes to career development plans (1-2 pages).

- Student's Transcript

- Research Proposal, demonstrating anticipated research activities, a timeline, and specific milestone (2-4 pages). A budget outlining any anticipated field research expenses and expected conference attendances should also be provided. Pl ease ensure the budget request is no more than $5,000.

title: HBCTL Tamayyuz Research Fellowship · NYUAD Students
text:
Deadline for proposals: February 27, 5pm GST

This particular fellowship with the Hilary Ballon Center for Teaching and Learning seeks to foster knowledge of pedagogy, liberal arts education, and community engagement in teaching and learning.

The context within which the HBCTL Fellow will work is one of faculty development around teaching. The Center applies evidence-based research on best practice to support the innovative efforts of NYU Abu Dhabi faculty. On a day-to-day basis, work can involve developing surveys to measure impact of programming, researching best practice around specific pedagogy, and preparing for conference presentations and outreach. The HBCTL works to make good teaching visible, and should the Fellow have an interest in this area, there is work to be done, such as encouraging participation in Course Evaluations. Additionally, each fellow receives individualized mentorship on research and professional development from the Center’s Director.

Candidate Requirements

- A minimum cumulative GPA of 3.7, with evidence of a strong and consistent record of outstanding academic achievement.

- A proven desire to explore research opportunities and demonstrate intellectual curiosity.

- Expected graduation with a bachelor's degree in Fall 2025, Spring or Summer 2026.

Application Process

Students who meet eligibility requirements and are interested in applying for the Post-graduation Research Fellowship Program are required to submit the Application Form . Please ensure you have the following ready before filling out the form.

- Student's Resume

- Cover Letter, outlining the student's interest, understanding, and enthusiasm for working in education, any previous experience within the field, and how the position contributes to career development plans (1-2 pages).

- Research Proposal, demonstrating anticipated research activities, a timeline, and specific milestones. Research proposals for this position should be focused on a specific pedagogy or type of learning. For example, are you interested in the impact of the Core Curriculum, of small classes, of J-Term learning, of student and faculty diversity? Is there a specific pedagogy you want to explore? Options include but are not limited to, active learning, technology-supported learning, problem-based learning, or project-based learning. Research interests can be on a broader scale as well. For example, you may want to do a comparative study on the impact of liberal arts education.

Once you have identified a specific area of our educational model and approach that interests you, you can share possible questions you would like to explore as part of your research project.

Your proposal should include 5-10 resources related to the subject area. It should include a title page, page numbers, and citations as relevant. Proposals should not be longer 3-5 pages in length. title: OGAE Tamayyuz Fellowship · NYUAD Students
text:
Deadline for proposals: February 27, 5pm GST

As part of the Office of the Vice Chancellor, the Office of Global Access and Engagement (OGAE) embodies NYU Abu Dhabi’s commitment to fostering belonging, ensuring equal access to opportunities, and strengthening our shared sense of community. Dedicated to cultivating a campus culture rooted in community and connection, the office leads initiatives that expand access, empower individuals to succeed, and advance the University’s mission of building a globally engaged community where everyone can thrive.

OGAE is responsible for leading and advancing NYUAD's implementation of practices and programs that foster access, engagement, belonging, and equal opportunity in our learning and working communities.

This Research Fellowship is a full-time, one-year leadership and research development fellowship program aimed at NYUAD students graduating with a bachelor's degree in May/Summer or recent graduates (1-2 years) of NYUAD seeking to leverage their significant research and co-curricular contributions to enhance the leadership and academic experience across the Global Network University, in partnership with the various academic divisions and the Leadership team. It is an excellent opportunity to contribute to the growth and development of the research infrastructure around inclusion and access within the UAE.

This fellow will carry out project-based assignments, and provide research support to foster inclusion and access across NYUAD. The fellow will have the ability to study questions about access, belonging, and global pedagogy which would be embedded through research opportunities in partnership with internal key stakeholders. The position expects individuals to provide valuable insight and operational support; they will be encouraged to drive and develop strategic initiatives to uplift OGAE and the University’s mission and vision. The projects the fellow will work on will stem from OGAE, in collaboration with other key stakeholders across the University. In addition to working on set projects assigned by the OGAE, the appointed fellow will have the opportunity to lead a research project of their own interest.

Candidate Requirements

- A minimum cumulative GPA of 3.7, with evidence of a strong and consistent record of outstanding academic achievement.

- Evidence of a strong and consistent record of outstanding academic achievement, and previous engagement with work related to inclusion, belonging, and access.

- A proven desire to explore research opportunities and demonstrate intellectual curiosity.

- Expected graduation with a bachelor's degree in May or Summer 2026, providing all graduation requirements are met before September 1, 2026. Also available to those who have graduated in AY 25-26 or AY 24-25.

Application Process

Students who meet eligibility requirements and are interested in applying for the Tamayyuz Research Fellowship Program are required to submit the Application Form . Students should have the following documents ready before filling out the form.

- Student's Resume

- Cover Letter, outlining the student's interest, understanding and enthusiasm for inclusion, belonging, and access, including noting any previous experience within the field, and how the position contributes to career development plans (1-2 pages).

- A Research Proposal, demonstrating anticipated research activities, a timeline, and specific milestones (maximum 2 pages). Research proposals for this position should be focused on a specific area of interest that the fellow would like to explore. Examples of this could include:

- Original research and creative activity that is informed and serves the diverse needs of communities.
b. Projects intended to help deepen inclusion, belonging, engagement, and access content that is being offered in the Core curriculum and better communicate to students where they are encountering the content, theories, and experiential opportunities.

c. Projects can inquire about structures of inequalities, notions of fairness, access and accessibility, and belonging on an organizational, local, regional, or global level.

- One letter of support from a faculty member that supports the proposed research project and confirms the faculty member is able to provide research support and guidance for the duration of the fellow's research project. This can be submitted as part of the application, or the faculty member can send the letter by email directly to fatiah@nyu.edu and sa5182@nyu.edu .

Related official links:
https://students.nyuad.nyu.edu/academics/research/post-graduation-research-fellowship-programs/oie-pgrfp/oie-post-graduation-research-fellowship-program-form/

title: OSS Research Fellowship · NYUAD Students
text:
Deadline for proposals: February 27, 5pm GST

NYU Abu Dhabi is committed to building and strengthening a university-wide culture of sustainability. Through research and outreach, NYU Abu Dhabi is a thought leader in sustainability advocating the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) of the United Nations. Inspired by Sheikh Zayed’s vision and legacy, we seek to have graduates across all divisions understand issues surrounding sustainability and how their work can contribute to a more sustainable world.

Office of Sustainability and Stewardship (OSS) Goals and Mission

Under the leadership of the Office of Sustainability and Stewardship (OSS), students, faculty, and staff work closely to transform NYUAD into one of the region’s leading campuses in sustainability. Through strategies that span every area of university life, we aim to reduce our greenhouse gas emissions, support teaching and research, and provide resources and guidance in establishing a culture of sustainability at NYU Abu Dhabi.

The Office works with academic divisions to support sustainability teaching and learning; with the community to raise awareness around sustainability through events; with NYU's Office of Sustainability in New York to ensure adaptation of relevant common sustainability initiatives and strengthen relationships across all NYU campuses; and with campus partners in energy engineering, operations, construction management, procurement, campus services, among others.

OSS Tamayyuz Research Fellowship

This Fellowship provides a unique opportunity to work closely with a variety of campus stakeholders and support efforts to advance sustainability across NYUAD. Throughout the one-year term, the fellow will gain broad exposure to the office's work from operations and academics to research, outreach, and programming, providing a comprehensive view of the university’s sustainability efforts.

As part of their role, the fellow will carry out project-based assignments and provide research support to advance sustainability across NYUAD. The fellow will have the opportunity to explore questions related to key sustainability areas such as carbon, energy, water, construction, waste, transportation, dining, and procurement, among others, in partnership with key institutional stakeholders. This includes contributing to major initiatives such as the Climate Action Plan , the Cool Food Pledge , Green Events , and Green Workplace Certification .

In addition to supporting OSS-led initiatives, the fellow will also have the chance to pursue a research project of their choosing.

Candidate Requirements

- A minimum cumulative GPA of 3.7, with evidence of a strong and consistent record of outstanding academic achievement.

- Evidence of a strong and consistent record of outstanding academic achievement, and previous engagement with work related to Sustainability.

- A proven desire to explore research opportunities and demonstrate intellectual curiosity.

- Expected graduation with a bachelor's degree in May or summer 2026, providing all graduation requirements are met before September 1, 2026. Also available to those who have graduated in AY 25-26 or AY 24-25.

Application Process

Students who meet eligibility requirements and are interested in applying for the Tamayyuz Research Fellowship are required to submit the application form . Students should have the following documents ready before filling out the form.

- Student's Resume

- Cover Letter, outlining the student's interest, understanding and enthusiasm for Sustainability, including noting any previous experience within the field, and how the position contributes to career development plans (1-2 pages).

- Research proposals for this position should be focused on a specific area of interest that the fellow would like to explore. Some examples are noted below but we are open to all proposals. Students should also include a budget outlining any anticipated field research expenses and expected conference attendances should also be provided. Please ensure the budget request is no more than USD 5,000.

- Original research in one or more sustainability-related fields such as but not limited to carbon, energy, water, construction, waste, transportation, dining, and procurement.

- Initiatives intended to help bolster action in sustainability on campus in one or more sustainability-related fields (as per above) and better communicate to NYUAD community members sustainability-related initiatives with the aim to promote a culture of sustainability on campus.

- One letter of support from a faculty member that supports the proposed research project and confirms the faculty member is able to provide research support and guidance for the duration of the fellow's research project. This can be submitted as part of the application, or the faculty member can send the letter by email directly to ma6947@nyu.edu .

Related official links:
https://students.nyuad.nyu.edu/academics/research/post-graduation-opportunities/nyuad-tamayyuz-research-fellowship/oss-tamayyuz-research-fellowship/oss-post-graduation-research-fellowship-application/

title: Role of Fellowship Supervisor · NYUAD Students
text:
Faculty Supervisor Guidelines

Faculty supervisors are responsible for supporting the intellectual and scholarly development of their research fellow by guiding and supervising their research, monitoring their progress, and acting as a mentor.

Supervision and Guidance

- Supervisors provide guidance, instruction, and encouragement in the research activities of their fellow.

- Supervisors take part in the evaluation and examination of their fellow’s progress, performance and navigation through the year-long fellowship.

- Supervisors play a critical role in providing advice about professional development, based upon the fellow’s career and academic interests.

- Supervisors should arrange regular meetings with fellows to ensure steady progress. The frequency of such meetings may be determined by the faculty supervisor. Whilst the faculty supervisor may appoint another member of their team to provide daily supervision, the faculty member is expected to remain the main point of contact from a supervisory perspective.

Academic Outputs

- Academic outputs allow research fellows to demonstrate ownership of their research. If supervisors actively collaborate on these academic works, it is important for both that their relative contributions are represented appropriately. To achieve these goals, supervisors should:

- Discuss with their fellow, at an early stage of their fellowship, authorship practices within the discipline and University policies about publications.

- Discuss and reach agreement with the fellow at the outset of collaboration, the way in which authorship will be shared, if appropriate, between the supervisor and the fellow, if applicable.

- Encourage the dissemination of the fellow’s research results by publication in scholarly and research journals, presentation at conferences and seminars if applicable.
