title: Post-graduation Practical Training Program · NYUAD Students
text:
Update for Summer 2026: As an exception for Summer 2026, positions may take place remotely from a student's home location if the professor is in agreement. In-person work possibilities will be determined by NYUAD leadership in early May.

The Post-graduation Practical Training Program (PPTP) allows faculty to appoint graduating NYUAD students to work on short-term research projects during the summer following their graduation. The program is designed to provide participants with an intensive training and professional development experience in order to strengthen the skills needed for successful application and transition to graduate school or the workforce.

The deadline for submission of the appointment form by faculty is March 5, 2026 and April 15, 2026. Submitting the appointment form by the earlier deadline allows students to receive a response sooner—typically within two weeks of the deadline.

All positions must be advertised on Handshake (under ' NYUAD On-Campus Student Employment ' with the job title noted as 'PPTP - Research Assistant') for a minimum of 5 working days. Students can review available opportunities on the page and should apply for relevant positions. Faculty should submit the appointment form (students do not have access to this) by one of the two deadlines once they have made their selections.

Appointment and Payment Details

Students should expect to receive their offer letter within two weeks of the deadline, if all eligibility criteria are met and the faculty supervisor has adequate budget to fund the position.

Appointments should begin and end based on one of the date options below. Positions must be full-time (35 hours per week) and students should work for no more than 7 hours a day. Hours worked beyond the maximum approved hours will not be compensated. Students must be based within the UAE and the work should be completed on-campus.

All undergraduate students are paid a fixed rate of USD 500 per week (USD 100 per working day). G raduating Master's students are paid at a rate of USD 770 per week (USD 154 per working day). Students will not be eligible to receive a meal plan or flight allowance and must make these arrangements themselves. The Office of Student Research will make arrangements for the transfer of funds to the student on a monthly basis.

Total payment amounts for undergraduate appointments are listed below:

​

Dates | Total Undergraduate Student Stipend* | Total Undergraduate Housing Cost**

May 20 - June 19 [≈3 weeks] | $1,800 | $752

May 20 - July 10 [≈6 weeks] | $3,300 | $1,316

*This amount will be adjusted if any administrative holidays fall during this period, or if a student is sick or unable to work. If a student is unable to work due to sickness or vacation days, the Office of Student Research should be informed and the total payment will be adjusted accordingly. Note the current holidays during the PPTP period: Arafat Day and Eid Al Adha: May 26-29 and Hijri New Year: June 17. Dates subject to change. **Faculty should note that the full housing cost may be charged, even if a student withdraws or leaves the campus before their previously scheduled end date.

Eligibility Criteria and Guidelines

- Students must have a valid UAE student residence visa through July 31, 2026. Visas cannot be extended for the purpose of PPTP.

-
Visas cannot be canceled before the PPTP end date, except for Golden Visa purposes, and only with prior approval from NYUAD administration. If you wish to cancel your visa earlier for any other reason, you will need to obtain approval from your faculty supervisor and NYUAD administration - this will result in your PPTP program ending earlier than the scheduled date. Please email nyuad.studentresearch@nyu.edu with any requests.

Kindly remember:

-
Unless you are approved to cancel your visa earlier for Golden Visa purposes, your UAE student residence visa will be canceled based on your PPTP program end date.

-
Your NYUAD health insurance will expire on July 31, 2026.

-
Students admitted to the NYUAD Global PhD Program are eligible only for a PPTP appointment ending June 20.

- The position must be under the direct supervision of a faculty member (or their designee) who will be required to provide regular mentorship and guidance.

- Students must attend a mandatory orientation session prior to graduation.

- Students may take part in a maximum of one PPTP position.

- Students must be enrolled in a Post-graduation Practical Training Directed Study Course, and must complete all assignments, including but not limited to weekly field logs, a final research report, and a program evaluation. This course does not appear on the undergraduate transcript.

- Students must be in good disciplinary standing (to be verified by the judicial officer).

- Students must abide by the NYUAD Student Code of Conduct and all NYUAD policies applicable to student status.

- Students should have met all graduation requirements (as confirmed by the Registrar's Office) by the time the appointment begins. If graduation requirements are not met, the position will have to be canceled. Students enrolled in a June-term or summer class will not be eligible.

-

Retractions, Withdrawals and Early Terminations

- Retraction: NYUAD has the authority to retract funding and support if it is determined that: The student failed to complete all requirements for graduation by the intended PPTP start date The student is no longer fully participating in the approved summer program as defined by the supervisor; The student is potentially detrimental to the health and safety of self and/or others, has falsified participation in the approved summer program, and/or has provided inaccurate data and/or information in support of his/her application. If the student is dismissed from the program under these circumstances, he/she will be responsible for returning the funding in its entirety to NYUAD.

- Early Withdrawal: If a student elects to withdraw from participation in the approved summer program after funding has been issued, they will be responsible for returning the funding in its entirety to NYUAD. If the summer experience is cancelled or shortened due to circumstances entirely beyond the student’s control, the Office of Student Research will determine the fair and reasonable amount of funding that will need to be returned. If funds are not returned, NYUAD reserves the right to withhold issuing of official transcripts or other university documents requested by the student and will place the encumbered amount on the NYUAD student’s account until it is collected.

- Poor performance: Students underperforming should be sent a written warning notice addressing their deficiencies by the supervisor; failure to correct these after mutual discussion and a two week notification can result in termination of the position. The Office of Student Research is to be immediately informed of these cases.

-
Visa Cancelation: For undergraduates, NYUAD will cancel the student visa upon receiving notification that a PPTP student has withdrawn or has been dismissed from the position.

Additional Information

- Copyrights, Inventions, Patents and Intellectual Property: Any copyrights, inventions, patents and intellectual property associated with your funded research activity are governed by NYU's Guidelines for Sponsored Research and other applicable policies. — View the policy

- Certification for Research Involving Human Subjects and/or Vertebrate Animals: If the research project contemplates the use of human subjects and/or vertebrate animals, faculty supervisors must obtain approval from the appropriate Regulatory Committees and comply with all the rules and standards as set forth by them. — View the policy

sections.text:
- Students must have a valid UAE student residence visa through July 31, 2026. Visas cannot be extended for the purpose of PPTP.

-
Visas cannot be canceled before the PPTP end date, except for Golden Visa purposes, and only with prior approval from NYUAD administration. If you wish to cancel your visa earlier for any other reason, you will need to obtain approval from your faculty supervisor and NYUAD administration - this will result in your PPTP program ending earlier than the scheduled date. Please email nyuad.studentresearch@nyu.edu with any requests.

Kindly remember:

-
Unless you are approved to cancel your visa earlier for Golden Visa purposes, your UAE student residence visa will be canceled based on your PPTP program end date.

-
Your NYUAD health insurance will expire on July 31, 2026.

-
Students admitted to the NYUAD Global PhD Program are eligible only for a PPTP appointment ending June 20.

- The position must be under the direct supervision of a faculty member (or their designee) who will be required to provide regular mentorship and guidance.

- Students must attend a mandatory orientation session prior to graduation.

- Students may take part in a maximum of one PPTP position.

- Students must be enrolled in a Post-graduation Practical Training Directed Study Course, and must complete all assignments, including but not limited to weekly field logs, a final research report, and a program evaluation. This course does not appear on the undergraduate transcript.

- Students must be in good disciplinary standing (to be verified by the judicial officer).

- Students must abide by the NYUAD Student Code of Conduct and all NYUAD policies applicable to student status.

- Students should have met all graduation requirements (as confirmed by the Registrar's Office) by the time the appointment begins. If graduation requirements are not met, the position will have to be canceled. Students enrolled in a June-term or summer class will not be eligible.

-

sections.title: Retractions, Withdrawals and Early Terminations
sections.text:
- Retraction: NYUAD has the authority to retract funding and support if it is determined that: The student failed to complete all requirements for graduation by the intended PPTP start date The student is no longer fully participating in the approved summer program as defined by the supervisor; The student is potentially detrimental to the health and safety of self and/or others, has falsified participation in the approved summer program, and/or has provided inaccurate data and/or information in support of his/her application. If the student is dismissed from the program under these circumstances, he/she will be responsible for returning the funding in its entirety to NYUAD.

- Early Withdrawal: If a student elects to withdraw from participation in the approved summer program after funding has been issued, they will be responsible for returning the funding in its entirety to NYUAD. If the summer experience is cancelled or shortened due to circumstances entirely beyond the student’s control, the Office of Student Research will determine the fair and reasonable amount of funding that will need to be returned. If funds are not returned, NYUAD reserves the right to withhold issuing of official transcripts or other university documents requested by the student and will place the encumbered amount on the NYUAD student’s account until it is collected.

- Poor performance: Students underperforming should be sent a written warning notice addressing their deficiencies by the supervisor; failure to correct these after mutual discussion and a two week notification can result in termination of the position. The Office of Student Research is to be immediately informed of these cases.

-
Visa Cancelation: For undergraduates, NYUAD will cancel the student visa upon receiving notification that a PPTP student has withdrawn or has been dismissed from the position.

title: Summer Research Assistant Program · NYUAD Students
text:
Note: Summer research grants and summer research assistant program information sessions: February 12, February 19, February 26. RSVP here .

The Summer Research Assistant Program provides NYUAD faculty the opportunity to appoint NYUAD students during the summer to work on tasks to advance faculty research projects. These paid positions must have specific schedules and deliverables. Research assistants should not be paid to work on their Capstone projects.

The deadline for faculty to submit the hiring request form is as follows:

- March 5, 2026 (on-campus and remote positions)

- April 15, 2026 (on-campus and remote positions)

- May 5, 2026 (remote positions only)

Note that students do not have access to this form. All positions must be advertised on Handshake (under ' NYUAD On-Campus Student Employment ' with the job title noted as 'Summer Research Assistant') for a minimum of 5 working days. If a faculty member is employing a student who is already currently on an existing assistantship contract during the spring semester, and there is no change to the job description duties, the faculty member does not need to re-advertise the position on Handshake - and can proceed with submitting the hiring request form for the summer position.

Appointment Details

Appointments should begin and end based on one of the date options below. Positions must be full-time (35 hours per week) and students should work for no more than 7 hours a day. Hours worked beyond the maximum approved hours will not be compensated.

All undergraduate students are paid a fixed rate of AED 38.5 / USD 10.48 an hour and Masters students are paid a set rate of AED 59 / USD 16.06 an hour. Students will not be eligible to receive a meal plan or flight allowance and must make these arrangements themselves.

Total payment amounts for undergraduate appointments are listed below:

Dates | Total Approximate Undergraduate Student Stipend** | Total Undergraduate Housing Cost, if the student is based on campus

Monday, May 18, 2026 - Friday, June 19, 2026 | $1,467 | $940

Monday, May 18, 2026 - Friday, July 10, 2026 | $2,567 | $1,504

Monday, May 18, 2026 - Friday, July 24, 2026 | $3,301 | $1,880

Monday, May 18, 2026 - Friday, August 14, 2026* | $4,401 | $1,880

Monday, June 1, 2026 - Friday, July 10, 2026 | $2,127 | $1,128

Monday, June 1, 2026 - Friday, July 24, 2026 | $2,861 | $1,504

Monday, June 1, 2026 - Friday, August 14, 2026* | $3,961 | $1,504

Monday, June 22, 2026 - Friday, July 24, 2026 | $1,834 | $940

Monday, June 22, 2026 - August 14, 2026, Friday* | $2,934 | $940

*Note that students will not be able to reside in on-campus housing beyond July 25. Positions beyond this date must take place remotely, from the student’s home location. **This amount will be adjusted if any administrative holidays fall during this period, or if a student is sick or unable to work. Students should not be compensated for administrative holidays or sick days.

Student Eligibility Requirements

- Students must have a valid UAE residence visa for the duration of the position.

- Students must be at least 18 years old. If the student is under 18 years of age, the NYUAD Dean of Students must authorize this exception.

- Undergraduate students will not be eligible to remain in campus housing unless the position requires physical presence at NYUAD, in which case the faculty member appointing the student must cover this cost. For all non-campus based positions, students are expected to work remotely from their home location.

- Only NYUAD students can be appointed via the program. Visiting students are not eligible.

- Students can work a maximum of ONE on-campus summer research assistant position. Students being paid via this program during the summer will not be eligible to receive funding via other NYUAD summer programs (e.g. summer research grants, internships, Summer Academy Chaperone, RealAD funding, or any other summer program).

- US citizens and US Green Card holders hired are required to fill out a W4 form (Note: log in with N-Number for both user name and password initially). If you encounter any issues, please contact onboarding.studentassistantship@nyu.edu .

- Students must be in good disciplinary standing (to be verified by the judicial officer).

Offboarding

- Cause(s) for Immediate Termination: Positions may be terminated immediately and without notice of a remedial period if the student commits a major offense including but not limited to theft and misconduct. Any incident involving documented misconduct may affect future hiring of the student through the program.

- Early Withdrawal: In cases of students or supervisors looking to end the research assistant position early, a two-week written notification is required prior to a mutually discussed last day of work.

- Poor performance: Students underperforming in their assistant position should be sent a written warning notice addressing their deficiencies by the supervisor; failure to correct these after mutual discussion and a two-week notification can result in termination of the position. The Office of Student Research is to be immediately informed of these cases.

- Housing Charge: Faculty should note that the full housing cost may be charged, even if a student withdraws or leaves the campus before their previously scheduled end date.

Payment Cycle

Student payments are processed bi-monthly as follows:

For hours worked from the 1st-12th of the month:

- Students complete their timesheets between the 12th-14th of the month.

- Supervisors must review and approve their timesheets by the 17th of the month.

- Students are expected to receive payment at the end of the month.

For hours worked from the 13th - end of the month:

- Students complete their timesheets between the 1st-3rd of the following month.

- Supervisors must review and approve their timesheets by the 6th of the month.

- Students are expected to receive payment in the middle of the month.

Timesheets are to be submitted by the student and approved by the supervisor promptly within three payment cycles . Further delay will require submitting an off-cycle payment approval form, and a series of DOA approvals.

Additional Information

- Copyrights, Inventions, Patents, and Intellectual Property: Any copyrights, inventions, patents, and intellectual property associated with the funded research activity are governed by NYU's Guidelines for Sponsored Research and other applicable policies. — View the policy

- Certification for Research Involving Human Subjects and/or Vertebrate Animals: If the research project contemplates the use of human subjects and/or vertebrate animals, faculty supervisors must obtain approval from the appropriate Regulatory Committees and comply with all the rules and standards as set forth by them. — View the policy

- Equipment and Supplies: The titles to the equipment and supplies acquired with the summer research funding vests in NYUAD. All such equipment and supplies should be returned to the respective academic department/lab upon completion of the research activity.

title: Summer Research Grants · NYUAD Students
text:
Note: Summer research grants and summer research assistant program information sessions: February 12, February 19, February 26. RSVP here .

Important note on NY summer 2026 research

The university will not be able to process new visa applications, including issuing new I-20s for existing F-1 visa holders for summer 2026. Only I-20 extensions will be possible. As a result, only the following students will be eligible for University sponsored US visas:

- CPT eligible students : Students who will have spent the year (Fall 2025 & Spring 2026) in the US.

- Students who are spending the Spring 2026 Semester in any US-based NYU Campus.

Please read the Housing, Visa & Legal Requirements page and the 'application type' information below to find out more.

----

Students who have secured summer research positions may apply for financial support of up to USD 4,000 to assist with costs relating to traveling to and from the program, meals, accommodation, visa costs, and local transportation.

The summer research positions should involve a mentored investigation involving a researchable question or questions conducted by the student. The position should provide independent or directed research and include structured development in the skills required to perform those activities. It is an experiential learning opportunity that can result in an original contribution to a field of knowledge or provide an opportunity to develop students' autonomy and skills in conducting research, scholarship, or creative expression.

These experiences should build high-quality student research experiences that intentionally evoke students' curiosity, engage students in the process of discovery, and extend student learning through critical reflection. In all cases, the activities must be conducted under the direct supervision of a faculty member and, in most cases, will be within the domain or discipline of the student's major.

The grants are offered to students across all divisions and disciplines. Entry into the program is via a competitive application process and the Student Research Faculty Committee will evaluate applications based on individual merit.

Please note that the number of funded positions under a single faculty supervisor/organization may be capped. Faculty looking to offer a number of positions could consider funding the additional students from their own research funds. Additionally, s tudents who receive this grant will not be eligible to receive funding via other NYUAD summer programs (e.g. summer research assistant position, internships, or RealAD funding).

Deadlines

Application Type | Deadline

NYUAD Visa Support | March 13, 2026; 5 PM GST. Extended to March 16 at 9 am GST.

No NYUAD Visa Support | April 13, 2026; 5 PM GST. Extended to April 30 at 2 pm GST.

What are the application types?

- NYUAD Visa Support

Who: For students taking part in research in NYU New York, and for students planning to return to Abu Dhabi for summer research after studying abroad and require their visa to be renewed.

- F-1 visa support for research can be provided only to students with approved research positions at NYU.

- Other than US citizens and US green card holders, s tudents are only eligible for F-1 visa support for summer 2026 if they are studying at any NYU US site for the spring 2026 semester and have an active US visa.

- For other New York City opportunities, students may still apply for funding support as long as the host institution provides visa support .

- Students not requiring NYUAD visa support are also strongly encouraged to apply by this deadline if they have secured positions by then.

- No NYUAD Visa Support

For students staying in Abu Dhabi with valid UAE visas; students who do not need visas for their summer destinations; and students who have to procure their own visas for their global summer research. For NYU New York opportunities requiring visa support, applications submitted by this deadline will be reviewed on a case-by-case basis.

Application Process

- Eligibility Requirements

The following student and organization eligibility must be met in order for an application for a research grant to be considered:

- Full-time NYUAD student, currently enrolled

- Must have declared an intended major. The research position should usually be linked to the intended major.

- Students may not receive more than one type of award from the Summer Opportunities Program in the same summer. For example, they cannot be awarded a Summer Research Grant along with a Summer Internship Grant, a Summer Research Assistantship, RealAD funding, Summer Academy Chaperone position or any other similar NYUAD funded summer opportunity.

- Student must have secured a research position under the direct supervision of a faculty supervisor or a researcher who has been approved by the faculty to supervise the student. Supervisors will be asked to submit an evaluation of the student’s work at the end of the summer.

- If a student is doing their own research, and would like to apply for summer funding, they are required to have a faculty supervisor who is willing to provide regular mentorship and guidance throughout the summer on the progress of the research.

- The research opportunity should usually be no less than 6 weeks long.

- The research opportunity must be full-time (35 hours per week or as mandated by local law).

- Students who have failed the Directed Study Course in past summers are ineligible.

- Good disciplinary standing * (to be verified by the judicial officer)

Undergraduate Student Requirements:

- Whilst funding for sophomores and juniors will be prioritized, first year students may apply for funding.

- Good academic standing, with a minimum GPA of 3.3 (includes first year grades).

Graduate Student Requirements:

- Graduate students enrolled in a Master's program are eligible to apply only if they are continuing students and not graduating in summer 2026. The Global PhD Fellowship students are eligible to apply but will only be considered on an exceptional basis.

- Good academic standing, with a minimum GPA of 3.3.

* Good disciplinary standing indicates that a student has been duly enrolled in the University and is eligible to participate in all activities of the University. A student is presumed to be in good standing unless the student forfeits that status by established misconduct .

- How to Apply

The Summer Research Funding Program Application needs to be completed by the deadline. As part of the application, students are required to submit the following:

- Invitation letter ( download the template [DOCX]), which includes the following:

- Your faculty supervisor’s name and title

- Your name

- Where you will be stationed

- Start and end date

- Number of hours you will be working

- The position you have been offered

- The exact work you will be doing

- Funding Information

For students based outside of their hometown, the maximum grant amount is USD 4,000 and students can apply for funding support to cover flights, accommodation, meals, and local transportation costs.

For students based in their hometown, a one-off allowance of USD 250 will be provided to students approved for funding, to assist with any costs involved with taking part in their research program.

If in doubt, or for any other questions, please email: nyuad. studentresearch@nyu.edu .

- How do I work out my budget?

For students based anywhere other than their home town, students can apply for up to USD 4,000 for the following costs: flight, meals, accommodation, visa, and local transportation expenses.

Students based in their hometown will receive a one-off allowance of USD 250.

For non-NYUAD expenses, please refer to this link as a general guidance for the maximum amount you can expect to receive per week, if approved, based on the current cost of living in your selected location. A one-off allowance of $200, $500, or $800 can be provided for new flights, depending on the average flight cost required for your destination. You should include details of the proposed flight and quote in your budget breakdown. For positions based in the same location that you are studying at for Spring 2026, a one-off flight allowance of $200 can be provided to assist with flight change costs. The maximum grant amount is $4,000. A reminder that the grant is a supplemental amount to support your research expenses; kindly ensure that you have secured alternate sources of funding. We will also use the following Cost of Living Estimators to review your budget:

- Numbeo City Estimator and Cost of Living

The Office of Student Research will review your budget in detail before agreeing on the amount to be awarded.

For NYUAD positions: Please calculate using these figures:

- Housing: Free of charge, providing the student is funded by the Office of Student Research to do full-time research. For faculty-funded or self-funded positions at NYUAD, housing costs are USD 188 per week. In order to be considered for faculty or self-funded summer research, students need to also submit the summer research grant application form by the noted deadlines.

- Students intending to take part in research on the NYUAD campus should note that on-campus accommodation is valid only until July 25. If students wish to continue their research beyond this date, they should consider remote research options as funding for external accommodation in AD is not provided.

- Meals: USD 150 per week

- Flight: Students can request an allowance of $200, $500, or $800 to assist with new flight costs. You should include details of the proposed flight and quote in your budget breakdown. For students based at NYUAD for the spring semester, a one-off flight allowance of $200 can be provided to assist with flight change costs. Any amount in excess of this will have to be covered by the student. Please note that students are encouraged to secure opportunities in their hometown or in locations they are studying for their spring semester, to avoid the excessive costs involved with additional flights.

- Selection Process

As funding is limited, the Student Research Faculty Committee will review applications based on their individual merit. The criteria for evaluating the applications are as follows:

- Academic merit of the proposal.

- Goal of the project is clearly defined, with a sound research methodology

- Quality and feasibility of the proposed plans within the timeframe.

- The relationship of the project with the student’s academic program and/or interests. Applicants should have been able to demonstrate a clear link.

- The student’s ability to carry out the project.

- Applications for international opportunities should be able to justify the location. Can the same research be done with NYUAD faculty?

Proposals should provide a clear and logical description of the work to be done, the research / scholarly / creative methods, timelines and projected outcomes. Applications for international opportunities should also provide clear and strong justification for the location.

Finally, the budget request should be appropriate and commensurate with the activities proposed and the level of supervision be appropriate.

Students are strongly encouraged to review the criteria above before submitting their application. It is also advisable to have your summer research faculty supervisor review your application before submitting.

Please note that the number of funded positions under a single faculty supervisor may be capped. Faculty looking to appoint a number of students for summer research could consider funding the additional students from their own research funds.

- When will I hear back regarding funding decisions?

We aim to get back to students 3 weeks after each funding deadline.

Required Directed Study Course

All students supported — meaning funded or endorsed — for undergraduate research anywhere in the world will be enrolled in and must participate in the zero-to-one credit Summer Directed Study Course. Graded on a Pass/Fail basis, the course will appear on your NYUAD transcript. Any earned course credit will count towards the total 140 credits required for graduation but not towards any other degree requirements.

Students who are based at NYU New York must attend in-person classes on June 5, June 12, June 26, and July 10. Further dates may be communicated at a later stage. Please note that this requirement derives from U.S. government regulations and NYU has no control over it. The law mandates international students to be physically present in the summer course. Failing to meet the requirement will result in immediate cancellation of the visa and will jeopardize your ability to obtain a US visa in the future.

- Purpose of the Directed Study Course

The Directed Study course will appear on a student’s NYUAD transcript. The purpose of the course is multifold:

- It helps NYUAD monitor the quality and assess the learning during the research experience.

- It supports students in bringing critical reflection to experiential learning (theory to practice).

- It provides a mechanism for students to identify and have help with problems that arise over the summer.

- It allows students funded to be in the United States and who are non‐US citizens to meet visa eligibility requirements.

- It allows students to use their NYUAD transcript to document the summer opportunity.

- One Credit v. Zero Credit Course

- Undergraduate students who have been approved for a summer opportunity will be enrolled in the one-credit Directed Study Course.

- Graduate students who have been approved for a summer opportunity will be enrolled in the zero-credit Directed Study Course.

- Directed Study Course Protocol

- To pass the course, you must meet attendance requirements and complete all assignments, including, but not limited to weekly field logs, written assignments, a final paper, and a program evaluation. You will receive notification of enrollment in the course, the name of the grader who will mark and respond to your assignments, a syllabus for the course, and deadlines for assignments by email.

- Note: This course does not allow NYU Abu Dhabi to sign a convention de stage or any other similar document as required for internships in certain European countries (e.g., France.)

Start and End Dates

The earliest possible start date for summer research is May 18 and the last possible date is August 14 . However, NYUAD and New York-based positions have set start and end dates as listed below. All positions should be full-time (35 hours per week).

- NYUAD Summer Research Program Dates

Summer research positions based in Abu Dhabi must start on the Monday following one of the move-in dates below, and end on the Friday before one of the following move-out dates below:

-

Block | Move-In | Move-Out | Weeks

1 | May 17, 2026, Sunday | June 20, 2026, Saturday | 5 weeks

2 | May 17, 2026, Sunday | July 11, 2026, Saturday | 8 weeks

- What if I change my summer research dates?

If you withdraw from your summer research position, you will need to inform the Office of Student Research immediately. You will then be issued with a withdrawal letter, with instructions on the next steps, including how to pay back the owed funds.

Providing the Office of Student Research accepts the reason, you will not need to pay back non-refundable costs that have already been spent. You will, however, need to submit receipts to prove the costs were made and that they cannot be recovered. You will be required to pay the NYUAD Finance Office the remaining funds from your grant.

If you withdraw because you now wish to pursue another opportunity, e.g., an internship, you will be required to pay back the full amount of your award, even if non-refundable payments have already been made.

Please note that withdrawals or cancellations after the withdrawal deadline noted on the academic calendar will mean a W will be noted on your transcript for the directed study class.

sections.text:
Note: Summer research grants and summer research assistant program information sessions: February 12, February 19, February 26. RSVP here .

Important note on NY summer 2026 research

The university will not be able to process new visa applications, including issuing new I-20s for existing F-1 visa holders for summer 2026. Only I-20 extensions will be possible. As a result, only the following students will be eligible for University sponsored US visas:

- CPT eligible students : Students who will have spent the year (Fall 2025 & Spring 2026) in the US.

- Students who are spending the Spring 2026 Semester in any US-based NYU Campus.

Please read the Housing, Visa & Legal Requirements page and the 'application type' information below to find out more.

----

Students who have secured summer research positions may apply for financial support of up to USD 4,000 to assist with costs relating to traveling to and from the program, meals, accommodation, visa costs, and local transportation.

The summer research positions should involve a mentored investigation involving a researchable question or questions conducted by the student. The position should provide independent or directed research and include structured development in the skills required to perform those activities. It is an experiential learning opportunity that can result in an original contribution to a field of knowledge or provide an opportunity to develop students' autonomy and skills in conducting research, scholarship, or creative expression.

These experiences should build high-quality student research experiences that intentionally evoke students' curiosity, engage students in the process of discovery, and extend student learning through critical reflection. In all cases, the activities must be conducted under the direct supervision of a faculty member and, in most cases, will be within the domain or discipline of the student's major.

The grants are offered to students across all divisions and disciplines. Entry into the program is via a competitive application process and the Student Research Faculty Committee will evaluate applications based on individual merit.

Please note that the number of funded positions under a single faculty supervisor/organization may be capped. Faculty looking to offer a number of positions could consider funding the additional students from their own research funds. Additionally, s tudents who receive this grant will not be eligible to receive funding via other NYUAD summer programs (e.g. summer research assistant position, internships, or RealAD funding).

sections.title: Application Process
sections.text:
- Eligibility Requirements

The following student and organization eligibility must be met in order for an application for a research grant to be considered:

- Full-time NYUAD student, currently enrolled

- Must have declared an intended major. The research position should usually be linked to the intended major.

- Students may not receive more than one type of award from the Summer Opportunities Program in the same summer. For example, they cannot be awarded a Summer Research Grant along with a Summer Internship Grant, a Summer Research Assistantship, RealAD funding, Summer Academy Chaperone position or any other similar NYUAD funded summer opportunity.

- Student must have secured a research position under the direct supervision of a faculty supervisor or a researcher who has been approved by the faculty to supervise the student. Supervisors will be asked to submit an evaluation of the student’s work at the end of the summer.

- If a student is doing their own research, and would like to apply for summer funding, they are required to have a faculty supervisor who is willing to provide regular mentorship and guidance throughout the summer on the progress of the research.

- The research opportunity should usually be no less than 6 weeks long.

- The research opportunity must be full-time (35 hours per week or as mandated by local law).

- Students who have failed the Directed Study Course in past summers are ineligible.

- Good disciplinary standing * (to be verified by the judicial officer)

Undergraduate Student Requirements:

- Whilst funding for sophomores and juniors will be prioritized, first year students may apply for funding.

- Good academic standing, with a minimum GPA of 3.3 (includes first year grades).

Graduate Student Requirements:

- Graduate students enrolled in a Master's program are eligible to apply only if they are continuing students and not graduating in summer 2026. The Global PhD Fellowship students are eligible to apply but will only be considered on an exceptional basis.

- Good academic standing, with a minimum GPA of 3.3.

* Good disciplinary standing indicates that a student has been duly enrolled in the University and is eligible to participate in all activities of the University. A student is presumed to be in good standing unless the student forfeits that status by established misconduct .

- How to Apply

The Summer Research Funding Program Application needs to be completed by the deadline. As part of the application, students are required to submit the following:

- Invitation letter ( download the template [DOCX]), which includes the following:

- Your faculty supervisor’s name and title

- Your name

- Where you will be stationed

- Start and end date

- Number of hours you will be working

- The position you have been offered

- The exact work you will be doing

- Funding Information

For students based outside of their hometown, the maximum grant amount is USD 4,000 and students can apply for funding support to cover flights, accommodation, meals, and local transportation costs.

For students based in their hometown, a one-off allowance of USD 250 will be provided to students approved for funding, to assist with any costs involved with taking part in their research program.

If in doubt, or for any other questions, please email: nyuad. studentresearch@nyu.edu .

- How do I work out my budget?

For students based anywhere other than their home town, students can apply for up to USD 4,000 for the following costs: flight, meals, accommodation, visa, and local transportation expenses.

Students based in their hometown will receive a one-off allowance of USD 250.

For non-NYUAD expenses, please refer to this link as a general guidance for the maximum amount you can expect to receive per week, if approved, based on the current cost of living in your selected location. A one-off allowance of $200, $500, or $800 can be provided for new flights, depending on the average flight cost required for your destination. You should include details of the proposed flight and quote in your budget breakdown. For positions based in the same location that you are studying at for Spring 2026, a one-off flight allowance of $200 can be provided to assist with flight change costs. The maximum grant amount is $4,000. A reminder that the grant is a supplemental amount to support your research expenses; kindly ensure that you have secured alternate sources of funding. We will also use the following Cost of Living Estimators to review your budget:

- Numbeo City Estimator and Cost of Living

The Office of Student Research will review your budget in detail before agreeing on the amount to be awarded.

For NYUAD positions: Please calculate using these figures:

- Housing: Free of charge, providing the student is funded by the Office of Student Research to do full-time research. For faculty-funded or self-funded positions at NYUAD, housing costs are USD 188 per week. In order to be considered for faculty or self-funded summer research, students need to also submit the summer research grant application form by the noted deadlines.

- Students intending to take part in research on the NYUAD campus should note that on-campus accommodation is valid only until July 25. If students wish to continue their research beyond this date, they should consider remote research options as funding for external accommodation in AD is not provided.

- Meals: USD 150 per week

- Flight: Students can request an allowance of $200, $500, or $800 to assist with new flight costs. You should include details of the proposed flight and quote in your budget breakdown. For students based at NYUAD for the spring semester, a one-off flight allowance of $200 can be provided to assist with flight change costs. Any amount in excess of this will have to be covered by the student. Please note that students are encouraged to secure opportunities in their hometown or in locations they are studying for their spring semester, to avoid the excessive costs involved with additional flights.

- Selection Process

As funding is limited, the Student Research Faculty Committee will review applications based on their individual merit. The criteria for evaluating the applications are as follows:

- Academic merit of the proposal.

- Goal of the project is clearly defined, with a sound research methodology

- Quality and feasibility of the proposed plans within the timeframe.

- The relationship of the project with the student’s academic program and/or interests. Applicants should have been able to demonstrate a clear link.

- The student’s ability to carry out the project.

- Applications for international opportunities should be able to justify the location. Can the same research be done with NYUAD faculty?

Proposals should provide a clear and logical description of the work to be done, the research / scholarly / creative methods, timelines and projected outcomes. Applications for international opportunities should also provide clear and strong justification for the location.

Finally, the budget request should be appropriate and commensurate with the activities proposed and the level of supervision be appropriate.

Students are strongly encouraged to review the criteria above before submitting their application. It is also advisable to have your summer research faculty supervisor review your application before submitting.

Please note that the number of funded positions under a single faculty supervisor may be capped. Faculty looking to appoint a number of students for summer research could consider funding the additional students from their own research funds.

- When will I hear back regarding funding decisions?

We aim to get back to students 3 weeks after each funding deadline.

sections.title: Required Directed Study Course
sections.text:
All students supported — meaning funded or endorsed — for undergraduate research anywhere in the world will be enrolled in and must participate in the zero-to-one credit Summer Directed Study Course. Graded on a Pass/Fail basis, the course will appear on your NYUAD transcript. Any earned course credit will count towards the total 140 credits required for graduation but not towards any other degree requirements.

Students who are based at NYU New York must attend in-person classes on June 5, June 12, June 26, and July 10. Further dates may be communicated at a later stage. Please note that this requirement derives from U.S. government regulations and NYU has no control over it. The law mandates international students to be physically present in the summer course. Failing to meet the requirement will result in immediate cancellation of the visa and will jeopardize your ability to obtain a US visa in the future.

- Purpose of the Directed Study Course

The Directed Study course will appear on a student’s NYUAD transcript. The purpose of the course is multifold:

- It helps NYUAD monitor the quality and assess the learning during the research experience.

- It supports students in bringing critical reflection to experiential learning (theory to practice).

- It provides a mechanism for students to identify and have help with problems that arise over the summer.

- It allows students funded to be in the United States and who are non‐US citizens to meet visa eligibility requirements.

- It allows students to use their NYUAD transcript to document the summer opportunity.

- One Credit v. Zero Credit Course

- Undergraduate students who have been approved for a summer opportunity will be enrolled in the one-credit Directed Study Course.

- Graduate students who have been approved for a summer opportunity will be enrolled in the zero-credit Directed Study Course.

- Directed Study Course Protocol

- To pass the course, you must meet attendance requirements and complete all assignments, including, but not limited to weekly field logs, written assignments, a final paper, and a program evaluation. You will receive notification of enrollment in the course, the name of the grader who will mark and respond to your assignments, a syllabus for the course, and deadlines for assignments by email.

- Note: This course does not allow NYU Abu Dhabi to sign a convention de stage or any other similar document as required for internships in certain European countries (e.g., France.)

title: Housing, Visa, and Legal Requirements · NYUAD Students
text:
The university will not be able to process new visa applications, including issuing new I-20s for existing F-1 visa holders for summer 2026. Only I-20 extensions will be possible. As a result, only s tudents who are spending the Spring 2026 Semester in any US-based NYU Campus will be eligible for an I-20 extension.

United States

- F-1 Student Visa for New York

- PLEASE NOTE: Other than US citizens and US green card holders, any student going to New York for an NYUAD-funded and approved summer program must enter the United States on an F-1 student visa. You cannot participate in a summer program with a B1/B2 tourist visa. Students must already be at NYU NY for the spring 2026 semester to be eligible for a visa for summer 2026 research at NYU.

- F-1 Visa Support for Research: Visa support for research can be provided only to students with approved research positions on campus at NYU New York. For other New York City opportunities, students may still apply for funding support as long as the host institution provides visa support. Students not requiring NYUAD visa support are also encouraged to apply by this deadline if they have secured positions by then. Students are encouraged to reach out to their program providers as soon as possible to determine the type of visa they will need to participate in the program.

- F-1 Visa Course Requirement: Students who are not enrolled in a credit-bearing course must be enrolled in the one-credit Summer Directed Study Course in order to become eligible for the F-1 student visa.

- Summer Directed Study Course:

-
This course is legally required for all students receiving summer funding OR any form of support from NYUAD (including housing arrangements) to participate in a summer program — regardless of visa needs. Failing to attend this course will result in a cancellation of the US visa, and deportation.

- This course will appear on your NYUAD transcript and be graded on a Pass/Fail basis. To pass the course, you must meet attendance requirements and complete all assignments, including, but not limited to, field logs, written assignments, a final paper, and a program evaluation. If you drop the course past the drop/add window , you will receive a W, per academic policy.

- F-1 Visa Support for Students Currently Studying in the US:

-
Students who are studying in the United States (NYU Los Angeles, NYU New York, NYU Washington DC) for the spring semester who secure opportunities on the NYU New York campus for the summer and are enrolled in the summer directed course will be eligible for an I-20 extension to cover their summer program. The Office of Global Education will request this on your behalf. Please contact nyuad.studyawaysupport@nyu.edu if you have questions related to this process.

-

- Students who are seeking opportunities off campus should consult with the summer program provider to determine the appropriate visa type they should procure for their summer opportunity. It is important to note that there may be restrictions on switching visa statuses while in the United States.

- Directed Study Course Start Dates for NY Students

-

Students will be required to attend in-person sessions at the NY site. The sessions are currently planned for June 5, June 12, June 26, and July 10. Students need to make necessary arrangements to attend all the sessions in order to maintain their visa status. We will update these dates here once they are confirmed.

Please note that this requirement derives from U.S. government regulations and NYU has no control over it. The law mandates international students to be physically present in the summer course. Failing to meet the requirement will result in immediate cancellation of the visa and will jeopardize your ability to obtain a US visa in the future.

- Summer Housing at NYU New York

See here for summer housing at NYU New York rates. Payments work based on Sunday arrivals and Saturday check-out dates. There is no pro-rating for arrivals and departures outside of those dates.

- Latest Possible Arrival: Students must arrive in New York by June 1 in order to participate in all the required in-person sessions of the course.

- Date Options: Students approved for summer research or internships can opt for on-campus housing but must follow the process and deadlines outlined at the above link.

-

UAE

- UAE Student Residency Visa Support

- Students participating in a summer research opportunity in the UAE must be approved for an in-person summer program by the Office of Student Research to be reviewed for visa support.

- Students may not participate in UAE-based summer programs on a tourist visa. Doing so may negatively impact your future eligibility for a student residence visa and/or employment visa.

- Students whose visas are sponsored by their families should consult their parent’s employer for guidelines on participating in summer opportunities.

- Summer Housing at NYU Abu Dhabi

- Students intending on residing in campus housing must apply for campus housing by the deadline communicated by the Office of Residential Life. Housing can be provided only for the duration of the approved summer research position, and must not extend beyond July 25.

Other Locations

- Summer Programs Outside the UAE, USA, or Outside One’s Home Country

- Limitations of NYUAD Visa Support: PLEASE NOTE: NYUAD can assist only with the F-1 visa for approved summer programs in NYU New York, as well as with the UAE student residency visa. Other visas are solely the responsibility of the individual students.

- Securing a Visa to Work: Once you are approved for your summer program, you need to start the visa process for the country you will be traveling to. You should consult your program provider to determine if there is a specific type of visa you will need to procure. You should then find out the contact details of the embassy or consulate (either a website or a phone number) to confirm if you require a visa based on your nationality and length of program and if so, what the visa process entails.

- Commonly Required Documents: Each country may require different documents as part of the visa application. Some of the most commonly required documents are:

- Evidence of Financial Support : Be prepared to provide a copy of your summer grant award letter, as well as personal bank statements if the embassy requests them. The FAB prepaid card does not generate the type of statements most embassies expect to see. Be prepared to explain what your funding covers.

- Letter/ Certificate of Enrollment : Request this from the Registrar’s office.

- No Objection Certificate : Request this from your funding office listing the country you are traveling to, your travel dates, and a copy of your current passport. This information may already be included in your financial support memo.

- Proof of Insurance Coverage : Your GeoBlue insurance is valid throughout the summer. You should print your GeoBlue card along with the GeoBlue coverage brochure that can be downloaded from the Student Portal. The coverage brochure alone does not prove that you are covered — you MUST include your GeoBlue card with the packet.

- Process: Once you have all of the required documents, you are responsible for submitting your visa application at the visa center or embassy. To ensure this is processed as quickly as possible, you need to confirm your application is complete with all required documents and that you have paid all required fees. Students must cover all visa fees either using their summer grant or personal funds.

- Visa Protocol Guidance: Some countries will require the applicant to submit their application or biometrics in person or to attend an interview with prior appointment. Since this takes time, you should book an appointment for at least 4 weeks prior to your travel date. The time it takes to schedule an appointment as well as the visa processing time will vary greatly depending on location and time of year.

- Many visa applications require a point of contact in the country you will be traveling to. You need to clarify with your program provider who this person should be. Do not put a random person on the form as this person will need to verify your program details if contacted.

- The processing time for the visa will vary per country. The embassy has the right to request additional information at any stage of the process. You need to provide active contact details in case the embassy needs to contact you.

- The fact that an application for a visa has been accepted at your appointment does not guarantee that the visa will be issued. You need to track your visa status using the instructions provided at the time of submitting your application to ensure the application is still under way.

- If your visa is delayed for any reason, you are responsible for any arrangements associated with waiting for the visa. This includes airfare changes, housing and meals.

- Spain and France: If your research internship is in Spain or France, you will be legally required to provide a signed copy of an internship agreement form. Often called Convention de Stage , or Convenio de Prácticas. This is required for both international students and EU citizens.

- Please note that the university is legally unable to sign these forms and only enrolling in the NYU's Summer European Internship Program will provide NYU New York staff the ability to sign this document.

Countries ranked at a level 3 or 4 on the US Travel State webpage generally can't be approved for funding.

- Summer Housing at Other Locations

On-campus housing is only a possibility for NYU New York, DC, and NYUAD sites. For all other locations, including cities in which NYU has satellite campuses, students must secure their own housing arrangements.

Related official links:
https://students.nyuad.nyu.edu/academics/2023-2024-academic-calendar/

- Limitations of NYUAD Visa Support: PLEASE NOTE: NYUAD can assist only with the F-1 visa for approved summer programs in NYU New York, as well as with the UAE student residency visa. Other visas are solely the responsibility of the individual students.

- Securing a Visa to Work: Once you are approved for your summer program, you need to start the visa process for the country you will be traveling to. You should consult your program provider to determine if there is a specific type of visa you will need to procure. You should then find out the contact details of the embassy or consulate (either a website or a phone number) to confirm if you require a visa based on your nationality and length of program and if so, what the visa process entails.

- Commonly Required Documents: Each country may require different documents as part of the visa application. Some of the most commonly required documents are:

- Evidence of Financial Support : Be prepared to provide a copy of your summer grant award letter, as well as personal bank statements if the embassy requests them. The FAB prepaid card does not generate the type of statements most embassies expect to see. Be prepared to explain what your funding covers.

- Letter/ Certificate of Enrollment : Request this from the Registrar’s office.

- No Objection Certificate : Request this from your funding office listing the country you are traveling to, your travel dates, and a copy of your current passport. This information may already be included in your financial support memo.

- Proof of Insurance Coverage : Your GeoBlue insurance is valid throughout the summer. You should print your GeoBlue card along with the GeoBlue coverage brochure that can be downloaded from the Student Portal. The coverage brochure alone does not prove that you are covered — you MUST include your GeoBlue card with the packet.

- Process: Once you have all of the required documents, you are responsible for submitting your visa application at the visa center or embassy. To ensure this is processed as quickly as possible, you need to confirm your application is complete with all required documents and that you have paid all required fees. Students must cover all visa fees either using their summer grant or personal funds.

- Visa Protocol Guidance: Some countries will require the applicant to submit their application or biometrics in person or to attend an interview with prior appointment. Since this takes time, you should book an appointment for at least 4 weeks prior to your travel date. The time it takes to schedule an appointment as well as the visa processing time will vary greatly depending on location and time of year.

- Many visa applications require a point of contact in the country you will be traveling to. You need to clarify with your program provider who this person should be. Do not put a random person on the form as this person will need to verify your program details if contacted.

- The processing time for the visa will vary per country. The embassy has the right to request additional information at any stage of the process. You need to provide active contact details in case the embassy needs to contact you.

- The fact that an application for a visa has been accepted at your appointment does not guarantee that the visa will be issued. You need to track your visa status using the instructions provided at the time of submitting your application to ensure the application is still under way.

- If your visa is delayed for any reason, you are responsible for any arrangements associated with waiting for the visa. This includes airfare changes, housing and meals.

- Spain and France: If your research internship is in Spain or France, you will be legally required to provide a signed copy of an internship agreement form. Often called Convention de Stage , or Convenio de Prácticas. This is required for both international students and EU citizens.

- Please note that the university is legally unable to sign these forms and only enrolling in the NYU's Summer European Internship Program will provide NYU New York staff the ability to sign this document.

Countries ranked at a level 3 or 4 on the US Travel State webpage generally can't be approved for funding.

- Summer Housing at Other Locations

On-campus housing is only a possibility for NYU New York, DC, and NYUAD sites. For all other locations, including cities in which NYU has satellite campuses, students must secure their own housing arrangements.

title: Summer Research Grant FAQs · NYUAD Students
text:
- What is the difference between the summer research grant and summer research assistant program?

The summer research grant provides financial support for students who have secured summer research internship/experiential learning positions. The funding is provided by the Office of Student Research to assist with logistical costs. These positions should be structured to provide students with opportunities to learn and apply theoretical knowledge in a practical setting. Positions may offer the possibility of earning academic credit in addition to practical experience. This academic component reinforces the educational nature of the research internship.

The Summer Research Assistant Program allows NYUAD faculty to appoint NYUAD undergraduate and masters students during the summer to work on and advance faculty research projects. Students are paid an hourly rate and the position is funded by faculty. Individuals in paid research jobs are often expected to apply skills they have already acquired. The emphasis may be on efficiently contributing to the research team or project. Paid research jobs in the summer may resemble regular employment, with a primary emphasis on completing specific tasks and projects. The focus is often on contributing to ongoing research efforts.

Students may not be funded for both a summer research grant and the Summer Research Assistant Program.

- How do I define what constitutes ‘research’ versus an ‘internship’?

Research Opportunity

In a research opportunity, a student is supervised by a faculty mentor or a researcher (approved by the faculty to supervise the student), and the work consists of direct research on a specific research project/question. Examples include students conducting experiments in a lab, researching through library collections for work on/as part of an upcoming book that the student will co-author, or taking part in research-focused art programs.

Internship

A work-placement opportunity that is not supervised by a faculty mentor, but instead the student is interning in an office environment (e.g., a law firm, bank, etc.) or government agency in an effort to explore a possible career path. To apply for internship funding, please use the Internship Funding Application .

- Can I apply for summer funding if I am working on my Capstones?

If Capstone funding is available and the research relates specifically to the student’s Capstone project, students should apply for Capstone funding.

- What if I don't have my invitation letter but the deadline is approaching?

You are advised to submit your application even if you have not received written confirmation. Indicate in the application that you are waiting for written confirmation and will submit it as soon as it is received. Late applications cannot be considered.

- What if I am taking part in research not funded through the Office of Student Research?

For example:

- My Professor is funding my summer research through his research funds.

- I have secured a fully-funded summer research position and do not require funding.

- I am self-funding my summer research position.

Students taking part in any summer research activity must also complete the summer research grant application by the relevant deadlines.

This way, all logistical elements of the appointment are handled but using the faculty member’s budget if applicable. All students undertaking summer research activities need to be enrolled in the directed study course.

Note that the faculty grant for students must follow the same funding guidelines as summer research grants. On the NYUAD campus, this would include meals at USD 150 per week, NYUAD housing at USD 188 per week (charged directly to the faculty research funds), and USD 200 for a flight change/new flight if the student is based on campus.

- Can I be funded to take part in research in any country?

The company/organization must not have any economic and trade sanctions listed against them as stated by the Office Of Foreign Assets Control .

The country in which the research opportunity is located must not have any economic and trade sanctions or a travel alert or warning listed against them by the US Department of State . Students wishing to take part in individual projects over the summer should note that internships/research in countries with a level 3 or 4 alert will generally not be funded.

Please also be aware that some countries may have restrictions on the ability for students to take part in research, e.g., Spain and France.

- Can I be funded for more than one summer opportunity?

Students funded for a J-Term or summer course in AD are eligible to apply and be considered for another summer opportunity (e.g. internship, research, or RealAD show) as long as the two activities do not overlap. Double-dipping between receiving funding for research and other summer funded activities (e.g. a research assistant position, an internship, the RealAD show) is not permitted.

Please also note that students may not accept a funding award from the Office of Student Research and funding from faculty or Capstone funds — this would be in violation of university policy.

- I secured a non-NYUAD paid research opportunity. Can I still submit an application?

Yes, depending on the amount that you are being paid. For example, if you are being paid an amount of USD 3,000, you may only be eligible for up to USD 1,000. If you are being paid over the maximum grant for any type of application, then you most likely will not be eligible for any type of funding. These requests will be reviewed on a case-by-case basis.

- How many applications can I submit as part of Summer Research funding?

You are encouraged to submit one application for each application type. Should you be awarded funding for all applications, you can only accept one summer award. Funds are limited and will be distributed as fairly as possible.

- Arranging Summer Travel

- Please note that not all airlines and not all tickets allow destination changes.

- If the travel date of a student’s existing spring ticket needs to be adjusted to accommodate a summer program start date, the student must first request permission from the Student Mobility Team in the Office of Global Education — please do this before contacting Nirvana Travel.

- Students are not permitted to add a layover when adjusting a ticket purchased by the University unless there are no alternative viable routes available.

- Airport transfers are not provided for summer programs or for May departures from campus that have been changed and now fall outside of the official departure window.

- When purchasing their own summer tickets, students can choose to use NYUAD’s preferred travel agency, Nirvana Travel, or any travel provider.

- If a student chooses not to use NYUAD’s preferred travel agency, the university will not be able to assist later should any travel-related issues arise since the reservation would not be accessible by Nirvana.

- Students are required to submit their final flight information to their summer funding office. They are also required to enter that information into NYU Traveler. Failure to provide the information in these two ways may lead to canceling the funding award for this year, and will result in ineligibility for future years.

- Please note any extra fees incurred for this ticket change (over the Nirvana credit limit) will be your (student's) responsibility, and the payment will need to be made directly to Nirvana Travel.

- Questions specific to travel must be emailed to the Student Mobility Team and will be reviewed on a case-by-case basis.

We offer a comprehensive series of introductory and elective courses open to all majors, and some advanced practice courses that require prerequisites. title: Arts Practice Fellowship Program · NYUAD Students
text:
The Art and Art History Program offers an Arts Practice Student Fellowship program. This is a competitive, extracurricular opportunity for ambitious NYUAD students to work with our Arts Practice instructors outside of classes in the Arts Practice studios . Workshop Fellows will receive comprehensive training on key workshop tools and materials, mentorship and support with design and fabrication, access to sculpture materials and some storage, and supervised access to our workshop spaces.

Fellowships are competitive and selection will be based on the quality of the proposed project and a statement of commitment from the applicant to complete all necessary training and workshop sessions (estimated minimum time commitment of three hours per week).

Apply

The Application link will be posted when available. Fellowships are contingent on the studios being open and fully staffed to support physical production.

title: Arts Practice Studios · NYUAD Students
text:
The Art and Art History Program manages several studio spaces program manages several studio spaces to support student art production, each with its own specialty tools, materials, and supplies. Students are required to abide by the Shared Studio Contract while in the studios. Learn about each one's resources, manager, open hours, and associated classes below.

- Visual Design Lab, Room C3-112

Enlarge

The Visual Design Lab offers tools to take design projects from conception through prototyping and into production preparation. With a computer lab of MacBooks open 24/7, a design library, large-scale paper cutters, whiteboards, various hand tools, craft supplies, and much more, the Design Studio is a creative space ready for students to brainstorm and collaborate.

- Studio Manager: Erin Collins, Instructor of the Arts in Design

- Open hours: Varies by semester. Check with the space manager or in the space for posted open hours.

- Associated classes: Foundations of Graphic Design, Types of Art, Wayfinding, Re-Design

- Woodworking Studio, Room C3-041

Enlarge

The Woodworking Studio offers a state-of-the-art woodworking space with resources to create all kinds of wood-based projects, including both hand and power tools as well as a variety of specialized woods. Tool training is offered via the Visual Arts Workshop Fellowship Program and in associated classes.

- Studio Manager: Nelson Reyes, Associate Instructor of Arts Workshop

- Open Hours: By appointment only, email studio manager for requests

- Associated classes: Foundations of 3D, Projects in Sculpture, Wood, Foundations of 4D

- Sculpture Studio, Room C3-015

Enlarge

The Sculpture Studio offers a sculpture creation space to support traditional clay sculpture and mixed media and wood sculpture. Hand tools, clay, and pottery wheels along with other supplies are available. Tool training is offered via the Visual Arts Fellowship Program and in associated classes.

- Studio Manager: Nelson Reyes, Associate Instructor of Arts Workshop

- Open Hours: By appointment only, email studio manager for requests

- Associated classes: Foundations of 3D, Projects in Sculpture

- Textile Studio, Room C3-157

Enlarge

The Textile Studio offers basic and specialized sewing machines (including embroidery machines and an industrial serger), hand sewing supplies, fabrics, an 18th-century loom, dyeing lab, and equipment for all kinds of fiber arts.

- Studio Manager: Instructor of Costume Design

- Open Hours: Varies by semester. Check with the studio manager or in the space for posted open hours.

- Associated classes: Fiber Studio, Foundations of 3D

- Collaboratory, Room C3-161

Enlarge

The Collaboratory welcomes students, staff, and faculty to work independently on small projects, seek advice from instructors, and present proposals for outside projects for feedback. Citizens of the space are encouraged to collaborate and inspire each other's work, offering advice or simply by being curious. Various tools and materials are at hand to support these small works including model making supplies, 3D printers, vinyl printing/plotting, low-voltage electronics supplies, photo/video equipment, and more.

- Studio Manager: Dustin Foster, Instructor of Fabrication and Visual Arts

- Open Hours: By appointment only, email studio manager for requests.

- Scene Shop, Room C3-030

Enlarge

The Scene Shop hosts large-scale fabrication projects including artworks and set pieces for student productions. With woodworking and metalworking power tools, a large CNC router, and a paint deck, almost anything can be made here. Tool training is offered via the Visual Arts Workshop Fellowship Program and in associated classes.

- Studio Manager: Jonathan Bonner, Instructor of Theater Design

- Open Hours: By appointment only; email jon.bonner@nyu.edu for requests

- Associated classes: Foundations of 3D, Projects in Sculpture, Wood, Foundations of 4D

- Print and Photo Studio, Room C3-165

Enlarge

The Print and Photo Studio offers equipment and materials for screen printing, lithographic printing, linocut printing, and other types of specialty analog printing. It also offers a dedicated darkroom for analog photograph development.

- Studio Manager: Anna Kurkova, Mixed Media Instructor

- Open Hours: Varies by semester — View current hours

- Darkroom by appointment only.

- Associated classes: Introduction to Printmaking, Foundations of Photography, Projects in Photography

- Mixed Media Studio, Room C3-174

Enlarge

The Mixed Media Studio is a creative space full of drawing easels, light tables, natural light, canvases, and other mixed media and painting supplies as well as associated storage. It offers an ideal workspace for flat artworks.

- Studio Manager: Anna Kurkova, Mixed Media Instructor

- Open Hours: Varies by semester — View current hours

- Associated classes: Foundations of 2D, Projects in Painting

- Arts Practice Capstone Studios

Enlarge

Arts Practice seniors are issued a dedicated, individual Capstone Studio space in order to conduct their research and prepare for their Capstone Exhibition in the Spring. Their research is manifest, in large part, as objects and images. Having dedicated space to create, display, and consider this work is essential. Students receive daily instruction and critical feedback in these spaces which includes studio visits by faculty and visiting artists and critics.

- Studio Manager: Art and Art History Program

- Open Hours: none

- Associated classes: Arts Practice Capstone Seminar

title: Student Exhibition Program · NYUAD Students
text:
All students, both majors and non-majors, are invited to apply to exhibit in our student exhibition spaces. Selected students will be given access to the resources in the Art and Art History studios, including the support of the Arts Practice instructors . Students can apply for an exhibition at any time . Students are required to fill out the Student Exhibition Workbook if selected to produce their exhibition.

We offer several student-exclusive exhibition spaces: The Cube, a traditional gallery space in the C3 lobby; movable display boards; and several informal exhibition spaces in hallways around our studios.

Student Exhibition Spaces

- The Cube

Housed in the lobby of the Arts Center (C3) next to the Project Space Gallery and the Equipment Center, the Cube is the premier student exhibition space on the NYUAD campus. It is an approximately square gallery, with interior and exterior walls lighted for exhibition. Floor space is approximately 25 square meters, with internal wall space of 18 meters. The gallery entrance is always open. Cube Exhibitions generally run for three weeks and applications are very competitive since only a few slots are open each semester.

- Moving Boards

We have eight double-sided boards on wheels, each with a display area of 1 x 1.5 meters, painted black. These boards are suited for pop-up and short-term exhibitions, and frequently displayed in custom arrangements in the lobby, although they can be moved to other locations in the Arts building as well. These boards are ideal for displaying flat works like photographs and paintings. If you have an exhibition idea that is short-term or composed of a smaller amount of work than would suit a Cube exhibition, this is a good option to apply for.

- Pin-Up Gallery

Around our studio spaces, there are several long stretches of hallway that host rotating exhibitions of student work, primarily from our studio classes. Students not in these classes may still apply to display works that can be hung on the wall in these areas, however, applications will be subject to availability of the space. If you have an exhibition idea that is site-specific, short-term, or composed of a smaller amount of work than would suit a Cube exhibition, this is a good option to apply for.

Application Requirements

- You must be a full-time student at NYU Abu Dhabi.

- You must be able to commit six weeks to developing the project once it is approved.

- This commitment includes meeting weekly in accordance with an agreed upon schedule.

- Missing meetings or neglecting project duties may result in the delay or cancellation of the project.

- You must fill out the entire application to be considered.

Apply

Apply for an exhibition .
