title: Scholars Lunch: Student Faculty Lunch · NYUAD Students
text:
About the Program

The Scholars Lunch is a special program designed to help students build meaningful connections with professors beyond the classroom. Over a relaxed and informal lunch, students can explore academic interests, exchange ideas, seek guidance and mentorship, or simply enjoy engaging conversation with faculty on a more personal level.

It's a unique opportunity to engage, learn, and build lasting relationships over a shared meal.

Best of all — it’s free!

Sign up today and take part in an experience that enriches both your academic and personal journey.

How to Participate

- Sign up below by selecting the Scholars Lunch form for your desired division and faculty member.

- Lunch are confirmed on a first-come, first-served basis once three students have selected the same faculty member.

- The first three students matched with a faculty member will be invited to join them for lunch at D1, D2, or the Marketplace.

- Once the lunch is confirmed, one participating student can collect a complimentary meal voucher for the group from the Academic Resource Center (ARC) in the Campus Center (C2), floor 3, Room 3101.

- Enjoy an engaging lunch with your faculty and peers!

…And don't forget to snap a picture for us during lunch!

*You may sign up for no more than two (2) lunches per term.

**Requesting and accepting a scheduled lunch demonstrates courtesy and respect for your professor's time. Once a lunch has been confirmed, you are expected to attend. If you are unable to make it, please email to cancel in advance. If you fail to attend a lunch without prior notice, you will be removed from the program and will not be allowed to request additional lunches for the remainder of the term.

*** If a faculty member is in high demand, it may take some time before your lunch can be scheduled.

Sign Up Here for Arts & Humanities faculty !

Sign Up Here for Social Science faculty !

Sign Up Here for Science & Math faculty !

Sign Up Here for Engineering faculty !

Faculty Testimonials

I thoroughly enjoy the Scholars Lunch program. This was my second time participating in the program. Everything went off smoothly and the conversations are enjoyable and hopefully meaningful for the students.
--Surabhi Sharma: faculty, Arts & Humanities

I really enjoyed the opportunity to have an informal lunch with the students, and I will be happy to participate again in this program.
--Andrea Maccio: faculty, Science & Math

I really enjoyed it. I really enjoyed meeting students, including some I had never met before. Happy to participate again.
--Luca Maria Pesando: faculty, Social Science

Thanks for the great initiative, I found the experience great and would be looking forward to more in the future. Students coordinated well with all the logistics.
--Christian Haefke: faculty, Social Science

I really enjoyed the lunch and appreciated the chance to connect with the students in a relaxed setting. It was a pleasure meeting the students, both were engaging and thoughtful, and I enjoyed our conversation about their academic interests and future plans.

Everything was well organized. I’m glad to have participated, it was new and innovative experience for me and the students.
--Wael Rabeh: faculty, Science & Math

I enjoyed the lunch, and the students were engaging. I think the time allocated was just right. The students arrived on time and were eager to discuss their academic and professional aspirations. I look forward to other lunches next academic year.
--Nadine Debbas Achkar: faculty, Social Science

I think the Scholars Lunch is a wonderful opportunity. It provides the institutional framework for the students who are keen to do so to reach out and talk with faculty in a relaxed setting. Absent this framework, I believe most students would feel that cannot or should not reach out to faculty, so it is a very nice addition to the ways in which students can interact with faculty.
--Jean Imbs: faculty, Social Science

Thank you for organizing the Scholars Lunch program this spring. I really appreciated the opportunity to connect with students in a more informal setting. It was a great way to learn more about the student body on campus — their interests, concerns, and what they hope for in their interactions with faculty.
--Sujeong Shim: faculty, Social Science

Karam Fayad with Katerina Fialova, Nghia Nim, and Osama Zunaim during their Scholars Lunch.

Who We Are

The Center for Writing is the place to come to workshop any piece of writing at any stage of your process. All writers, from first-year university students to professionally published authors, benefit from workshopping their ideas, arguments, and written expression; a second set of eyes is just what you need to develop yourself further as a writer!

title: FAQs · NYUAD Students
text:
- Who can come to the Writing Center?

Everyone! The Writing Center is open to all students of NYUAD and the larger NYUAD community.

- What kind of projects can I bring to the Writing Center?

The Writing Center will help you with all kinds of writing and speaking projects, including class assignments, resumes and personal statements, application essays, oral expression and public presentations, creative writing pieces, ESL related writing, and Capstone projects.

- Does the Writing Center help with creative writing?

Yes, the consultants are more than happy to provide constructive feedback on your creative writing in any genre.

- Can I work on my resume, cover letter, and applications at the Writing Center?

Yes, the consultants will provide constructive feedback on any kind of application.

- Who are the consultants?

The consultants are professionally trained Writing Instructors from various disciplines, and NYUAD students who have trained as Peer Tutors.

- What can I expect from the Writing Center and how do I prepare for a session?

The Writing Center supports writers at any stage of the writing process, from brainstorming to polishing a final draft.

When preparing for a session, think about reasonable goals for your 45-minute consultation. Please bring two hard copies of your project. If you are working on a class assignment, please also bring a copy of the prompt.

- How do I make an appointment?

To make an appointment, please use our online registration system . One of our Consultants can help you book in person, or email nyuad.writing@nyu.edu if you need assistance navigating the system.

- Does the Writing Center accept walk-ins?

Yes. We do, however, suggest you sign up for an appointment as consultation slots fill up quickly. If a Writing Instructor has no appointment booked, they will accept drop-ins.

- What if I’m late for my appointment?

Please be on time for all consultations. If you are more than 15 minutes late, your appointment will be cancelled.

- What if I can’t make it to my appointment or if I have missed a consultation?

If you need to cancel or reschedule your appointment, please do so as early as possible. You can cancel in the system until 30 minutes before your appointment starts.

Please note that your account will be blocked if you miss three appointments.

- What do I do if my account is blocked?

Email nyuad.writingcenter@nyu.edu , our Writing Center Director will get in touch. But also, try not to miss your appointments!

- How often can I come to the Writing Center?

You can make up to two appointments per day and three appointments per week. These appointments should NOT be for the same writing assignment, especially if you have made two appointments for the same day. If you require more appointments, please email: nyuad.writingcenter@nyu.edu .

- Can I drop off or e-mail my paper before my appointment?

No. We want to work with you face to face and have a conversation about your writing, so please simply bring the paper along to your appointment. We expect you to present your paper in the consultation.

- Will the Writing Center proofread and edit my paper?

No, we want you to grow as a writer and critical reader. Consultants will support your editing and proofreading process and occasionally take a paragraph of your piece and work through it exemplarily.

- Does the Writing Center help with citations?

Yes, the Writing Center will help you learn and apply particular citation styles to your work. You are also encouraged to take advantage of our great library staff in Research Services who can help with research and citation questions.

- What is the difference between the Writing Program and the Writing Center?

The Writing Center is a part of the NYUAD Writing Program, which is the academic umbrella that oversees the First-year Writing Seminars and an array of writing-across-the-curriculum initiatives.

title: What We Offer · NYUAD Students
text:
From research papers to resumés, poems to personal statements, we welcome all forms of expression. If you've written it down, we want to workshop it. If you aren't sure how to start, we want to brainstorm with you. If you’re preparing to present something, we want to talk it through with you. Come find out how the NYUAD Writing Center can help you find your voice as an author, and support your development of your communication skills as a scholar and global citizen.

Consultations

The NYUAD Writing Center is staffed by a team of professionally trained Writing Instructors and Peer Tutors. The Writing Consultants meet individually with you for a 45-minute session. We offer consultations that are tailored towards your writing, science writing, and capstone projects, as well as your public and oral presentations. Our English language and TESOL specialists are available for supporting you in developing your English skills further.

We are here to intellectually engage with you and your writing and to support you in expressing your thinking as clearly as possible. While we also help you identify patterns of grammatical error in your drafts, we cannot offer proofreading services.

Make an appointment now !

How to Prepare for Your Writing Center Consultation

Since each conference is individually designed around your goals and needs, no two conferences will ever be the same. But, here are just a few questions that we might ask you during a writing center conference: How are you communicating your ideas to the reader? What's the strongest way to organize your thoughts? How effectively are you presenting your evidence? What are the larger implications of your claims?

We promise to push you as a thinker, a writer, and a communicator!

Make an appointment

- Please bring printed versions of your draft, one for you and one for your Writing Instructor.

- Please arrive a few minutes before your scheduled appointment; if you are more than 15 minutes late, we cancel your appointment.

- Writing is an ongoing and recursive process. Set yourself up for success by giving yourself plenty of time to work on revisions after the writing conference; don't schedule an appointment for the day your writing assignment is due.

- Be prepared to write. Bring something to write with and something to write on.

Cancellations

Please cancel/reschedule as far in advance as possible, and at the latest 30 minutes prior to the scheduled appointment.

Drop-in Appointments

In the event that Writing Consultants do not have scheduled appointments, they will accept drop-ins. If you wish to drop-in for a writing consultation, arrive a few minutes before the hour to see if there are any openings.

- Please arrive a few minutes before your scheduled appointment; if you are more than 15 minutes late, we cancel your appointment.

- Writing is an ongoing and recursive process. Set yourself up for success by giving yourself plenty of time to work on revisions after the writing conference; don't schedule an appointment for the day your writing assignment is due.

- Be prepared to write. Bring something to write with and something to write on.

sections.title: Consultations · Cancellations
sections.text: Please cancel/reschedule as far in advance as possible, and at the latest 30 minutes prior to the scheduled appointment.

sections.title: Consultations · Drop-in Appointments
sections.text: In the event that Writing Consultants do not have scheduled appointments, they will accept drop-ins. If you wish to drop-in for a writing consultation, arrive a few minutes before the hour to see if there are any openings.

title: Graduate/STEM Writing Consultations · NYUAD Students
text:
The Writing Center sponsors jointly with the Graduate and Postdoctoral Programs Office a Lecturer of Graduate/STEM Writing who is specially dedicated to scientific writing. He primarily assists graduate students and postdocs who are working on manuscripts, but he is also available for consultations with research assistants, research scientists, and others who are working on any scientific writing projects.

Appointments with our scientific writing specialist can be made through the regular appointment system by choosing the special Graduate/STEM calendar (not the default calendar). For questions or comments regarding scientific writing consultations, please contact visit the Scientific Writing Program Website (URL: https://wp.nyu.edu/sciwriabudhabi/ ).

Center for Brain and Health (CBH) Seminar Series | Dr Karlo Toljan

Monday, Oct 12 | 2:00 PM | A6-004 | View in Calendar
Title of the Event: Implementation of New Neuroimaging Biomarkers for Multiple Sclerosis: A Neurologist’s Perspective
Speaker: Dr Karlo Toljan, Staff neurologist, Cleveland Clinic Abu Dhabi, Clinical Assistant Professor of Neurology, Cleveland Clinic Lerner College of Medicine of Case Western Reserve University
Abstract:
The central vein sign (CVS) and paramagnetic rim lesions (PRLs) are neuroimaging biomarkers included in the 2024 McDonald criteria for multiple sclerosis (MS). Their assessment requires susceptibility-based MRI sequences, which have historically been absent from routine demyelination protocols. This review examines the biological basis of CVS and PRLs, summarizes expert recommendations for rating them, and uses clinical scenarios to illustrate their application in MS diagnosis and monitoring. Understanding these biomarkers and their appropriate use will support clinical practice and future MS research.

Center for Brain and Health (CBH) Seminar Series | Dr Karlo Toljan

Monday, Oct 12 | 2:00 PM | A6-004 | View in Calendar
Title of the Event: Implementation of New Neuroimaging Biomarkers for Multiple Sclerosis: A Neurologist’s Perspective
Speaker: Dr Karlo Toljan, Staff neurologist, Cleveland Clinic Abu Dhabi, Clinical Assistant Professor of Neurology, Cleveland Clinic Lerner College of Medicine of Case Western Reserve University
Abstract:
The central vein sign (CVS) and paramagnetic rim lesions (PRLs) are neuroimaging biomarkers included in the 2024 McDonald criteria for multiple sclerosis (MS). Their assessment requires susceptibility-based MRI sequences, which have historically been absent from routine demyelination protocols. This review examines the biological basis of CVS and PRLs, summarizes expert recommendations for rating them, and uses clinical scenarios to illustrate their application in MS diagnosis and monitoring. Understanding these biomarkers and their appropriate use will support clinical practice and future MS research.

Please note that students who entered the UAE with an entry permit this fall semester, or who are awaiting their UAE student visa renewal should not make travel plans until their UAE student residence visa has been approved and their Emirates ID card has been issued.

Date: 15th October, 2026
Time: 11:30 AM - 1:00 PM
Location: NYUAD, C1 - ERB Building, Room 120 (First Floor)

Brief Summary:
This talk challenges technology-first visions of the smart city and proposes a human-centered, community-informed approach to future urbanism in Abu Dhabi and the UAE. title: Opening Tomorrow! Nadie Nos Conoce Juntas Exhibition by Val Jimenez
text:
View All Announcements

Opening Tomorrow! Nadie Nos Conoce Juntas Exhibition by Val Jimenez

Nadie Nos Conoce Juntas
Exhibition by Val Jimenez (MFA Second Year Student)
Opening: Thursday, September 17 | 5:00–7:00 PM
The Cube, NYUAD Arts Center (Building C3)
On view: September 17–October 19
The NYUAD community is invited to the opening of Nadie Nos Conoce Juntas by Valeria Jimenez Quiroga.
The exhibition traces Valeria’s return to Cochabamba, Bolivia, her parents’ city of birth. Returning in search of a place she could call her own, she instead encountered a city that did not know her.
Through reflections, transparency, and distortion, the work explores memory, absence, displacement, and the distance between seeing a place and experiencing it. The Cube becomes a landscape of mountains, reflections, and invisible water, evoking Bolivia’s landlocked geography and the emotional distance of return.
The exhibition asks how we might exist together with a place that feels both familiar and unreachable, perhaps not in the land itself, but in memory.

MRI study here at NYUAD!

NYUAD’s Center for Brain and Health invites you to participate in a MRI study here on campus. The institute’s mission is to gain a better understanding of conditions prevalent in the region.
What will you do?
The study will take approximately 2.5 hours. We will collect demographic data, behavioral and visual data, brain scans in the MRI scanner, a saliva sample for whole-genome sequencing, and an OCT scan. You will be compensated up to 150 AED in vouchers.

CITIES Seminar Series with Prof. Dr. Khaled Galal Ahmed
The Human Smart City: Community Intelligence for the UAE Urban Future

Date: 15th October, 2026
Time: 11:30 AM - 1:00 PM
Location: NYUAD, C1 - ERB Building, Room 120 (First Floor)
*Lunch will be served

Brief Summary:
This talk challenges technology-first visions of the smart city and proposes a human-centered, community-informed approach to future urbanism in Abu Dhabi and the UAE. Through three research-based cases—adaptable public housing, community urban farming, and culturally responsive vertical housing- it demonstrates how everyday community practices can be translated into professional design intelligence and supported by smart technologies to create more adaptable, socially responsive, sustainable, and resilient urban environments.

African Studies Film Series: Black Girl | Thursday, October 8 | 7pm | C3 B101

African Studies Film Series: Black Girl | Thursday, October 8 | 7pm | C3 B101
Ousmane Sembène's landmark feature debut (1966) follows Diouana, a young Senegalese woman who travels from Dakar to the French Riviera to work for a French family, only to find herself trapped between two worlds. Widely regarded as the first Sub-Saharan African film by an African director to reach international audiences, it remains a foundational movie for African and postcolonial cinema. Co-hosted by NYUAD African Studies and the History Program, with a post-screening Q&A led by Professor Manthia Diawara.

title: Earn up to 450 AED in gratitude vouchers (Amazon)
text:
View All Announcements

Earn up to 450 AED in gratitude vouchers (Amazon)

The Sreenivasan Lab is recruiting female participants with regular menstrual cycles for a study on how hormones influence memory across the menstrual cycle, contributing to research in women’s health.
Participation involves:
• Completing a brief eligibility survey
• If eligible, providing a blood sample for COMT genetic testing
•Tracking your cycle using the Euki app and at-home LH urine test strips
• If eligible after cycle tracking, attending two in-person memory experiments (~90 minutes each) during different hormonal phases
• Providing two venous blood samples for hormone analysis (estrogen, progesterone, LH)
Participants must be available for both required in-person sessions. Eligibility requirements will be shared by email. The initial survey will collect only the minimal information needed to assess eligibility.
We’ll send a brief eligibility survey to get started: https://nyu.qualtrics.com/jfe/form/SV_egqnu2mCNMgRXgy

- Category: Job Opportunities, Internships & Volunteering

- Topic: Research

title: MRI Study Here on Campus!
text:
View All Announcements

MRI Study Here on Campus!

NYUAD’s Center for Brain and Health invites you to participate in a MRI study here on campus. The institute’s mission is to gain a better understanding of conditions prevalent in the region.
What will you do?
The study will take approximately 2.5 hours. We will collect demographic data, behavioral and visual data, brain scans in the MRI scanner, a saliva sample for whole-genome sequencing, and an OCT scan. You will be compensated up to 150 AED in vouchers.
Are you eligible?
You can participate if you are above 18 years of age, do not have a history of neurological conditions, are not pregnant at the time of the study, and do not have non-removable metal. You can only participate once.
If you are interested please email one of the researchers below:
Last names A-I contact Dana Alkalali: dna8993@nyu.edu
Last names J-R contact Jenna Al Taher: ja4261@nyu.edu
Last names S-Z contact Aysha Hamkari: aah698@nyu.edu
The Principal Investigator of this study is Dr. Bas Rokers.

- Category: Job Opportunities, Internships & Volunteering

- Topic: Research

Flu Shots Available

The Student Health Center continues to offer free flu vaccines to students, staff, faculty, and their families (children aged two and older). You can visit the Student Health Center during the following hours to receive your flu shot.

title: Volunteers Needed - Creators Circle
text:
View All Announcements

Volunteers Needed - Creators Circle

Join Creators Circle and gain hands-on experience working alongside People of Determination (PODs) through creative, inclusive, and skill-building workshops.
This is more than an arts workshop. It is a science-backed program designed to support creativity, cognitive and practical skills, confidence, independence, and entrepreneurship through simple, hands-on art making.
As a peer buddy, you’ll support PODs as they create handmade items such as upcycled tote bags and bead bracelets while building meaningful connections and learning together.
Register to volunteer here.
For questions, contact NYUAD Civic Engagement & Service at nyuad.civic.engagement@nyu.edu .

JOIN THE EVIDENCE-BASED INTERVENTION FOR DIABETES (EID) STUDY

You are invited to join the EID study at New York University Abu Dhabi i f you are at risk of Type 2 Diabetes and would like to make a lifestyle change.
What is my role in the study?
You may be asked to:
• Work with a Diabetes Prevention Coach in groups virtually for 6 weeks
• Attend sessions online
• Come to NYUAD for 2 research visits and each visit will take approximately 2 hours
You are eligible to participate if you:
• Aged 18 years or older
• Can read and write in Arabic and/or English
• Have access to a smartphone

text:

Artist Talks: For Purposes Other than Intended with Moza Al Mazrouei

Wednesday, October 07, 2026, 6-7:30PM, The Art Gallery Reading Room
Join us for a conversation moderated by Sarah Almehairi exploring Moza Al Mazrouei's artistic practice across sculpture, film, mixed media, writing, and curation. Moving between research and fiction, observation and participation, the discussion touches on authorship, selfhood, and the structures of power that shape how we see and understand the world.

About the series
Artist Talks is an artist-to-artist conversation series founded by Sarah Almehairi in 2020, initially held over Zoom and now hosted in person. The series brings together creatives based in or affiliated with the UAE to discuss their practices, forming part of Almehairi's broader effort to expand cultural discourse and further connect the local art community.
Light refreshments will be served after the talk. For more information and to RSVP, click here .

title: Fall Break Travel Reminders
text:
View All Announcements

Fall Break Travel Reminders

Please note that students who entered the UAE with an entry permit this fall semester, or who are awaiting their UAE student visa renewal should not make travel plans until their UAE student residence visa has been approved and their Emirates ID card has been issued.
Students cannot travel outside of the UAE if their visa is still under process. You will in fact be stopped at the airport by the immigration authorities, and not allowed to leave the country if your UAE visa processing is still ongoing.
Students planning personal travel outside the UAE during the upcoming Fall Break must keep in mind that if their travel is disrupted for any reason, or if they become stranded at their destination, they will be personally responsible for covering any accommodation, meals, flight changes, or other costs associated with their travel and the delay in returning to the UAE.

text:

Film Screening: From Istanbul to Cairo | C3-B101

Thursday, October 08, 2026, 5–6:30PM, C3-B101 Film Screening Room
Join the NYU Abu Dhabi Art Gallery for a special screening of the documentary From Istanbul to Cairo: A Thousand Ways of Being Modern ( D'Istanbul au Caire, mille manières d'être moderne ), directed by Ilana Navaro. The documentary explores how late 19th and 20th-century artists from the region developed alternative modernities, featuring contributions from key art historians—including Nada Shabout. The screening will be followed by a short talk with Dr. Masha Kirasirova, moderated by Dr. Nada Shabout.
Part of the public program for All Manner of Experiments .

title: Receive up to 450 AED in gratitude vouchers (Amazon)
text:
View All Announcements

Receive up to 450 AED in gratitude vouchers (Amazon)

The Sreenivasan Lab is recruiting female participants with regular menstrual cycles for a study on how hormones influence memory across the menstrual cycle, contributing to research in women’s health.
Participation involves:
• Completing a brief eligibility survey
• If eligible, providing a blood sample for COMT genetic testing
•Tracking your cycle using the Euki app and at-home LH urine test strips
• If eligible after cycle tracking, attending two in-person memory experiments (~90 minutes each) during different hormonal phases
• Providing two venous blood samples for hormone analysis (estrogen, progesterone, LH)
Participants must be available for both required in-person sessions. Eligibility requirements will be shared by email. The initial survey will collect only the minimal information needed to assess eligibility.
Here's a brief eligibility survey to get started: https://nyu.qualtrics.com/jfe/form/SV_egqnu2mCNMgRXgy

title: Center for Brain and Health (CBH) Seminar Series | Dr Karlo Toljan
text:
View All Announcements

Center for Brain and Health (CBH) Seminar Series | Dr Karlo Toljan

Monday, Oct 12 | 2:00 PM | A6-004 | View in Calendar
Title of the Event: Implementation of New Neuroimaging Biomarkers for Multiple Sclerosis: A Neurologist’s Perspective
Speaker: Dr Karlo Toljan, Staff neurologist, Cleveland Clinic Abu Dhabi, Clinical Assistant Professor of Neurology, Cleveland Clinic Lerner College of Medicine of Case Western Reserve University
Abstract:
The central vein sign (CVS) and paramagnetic rim lesions (PRLs) are neuroimaging biomarkers included in the 2024 McDonald criteria for multiple sclerosis (MS). Their assessment requires susceptibility-based MRI sequences, which have historically been absent from routine demyelination protocols. This review examines the biological basis of CVS and PRLs, summarizes expert recommendations for rating them, and uses clinical scenarios to illustrate their application in MS diagnosis and monitoring. Understanding these biomarkers and their appropriate use will support clinical practice and future MS research.

TONIGHT |“Musicianship in the 21st Century” by Cristóbal MarYán (NYUAD c/o 2015)

Join us for a talk by Mexican composer, sound designer, and former diplomat Cristóbal MarYán (NYUAD class of 2015)
Topic: “Musicianship in the 21st Century”
Date and Time: Thursday, October 8, 6:10-7:25 pm
Venue: C3 (Arts Center), Room 124
Cristóbal MarYán has been composer-in-residence for the Orchestra of the Americas and OAcademy. His works have been performed from New York to Sri Lanka by musicians and ensembles such as Yo-Yo Ma, the Minería Symphony Orchestra, the Mexico City Philharmonic, the Kontzertny Orkestr of the Tchaikovsky Conservatory, Carlos Miguel Prieto, the Tesla Quartet, Llewellyn Sánchez Werner, and the String Orchestra of New York City, among others.
From 2022 to 2024, he served as First Secretary and head of the Culture, Press, and Tourism sections at the Mexican Embassy in China, where, in addition to using music as a diplomatic tool, he fostered connections between Mexican and Chinese institutions, promoted Mexican artists, and managed high-impact cultural projects.

African Studies Film Series: Black Girl | TONIGHT | 7pm | C3 B101

Ousmane Sembène's landmark feature debut (1966) follows Diouana, a young Senegalese woman who travels from Dakar to the French Riviera to work for a French family, only to find herself trapped between two worlds. Widely regarded as the first Sub-Saharan African film by an African director to reach international audiences, it remains a foundational movie for African and postcolonial cinema. Co-hosted by NYUAD African Studies and the History Program, with a post-screening Q&A led by Professor Manthia Diawara.

title: Counseling Services · NYUAD Students
text:
On-campus Confidential Counseling Services

Counseling — or psychotherapy — is a confidential professional relationship that empowers students to address their personal problems in a non-judgemental, supportive space

The counseling relationship differs from friendships and patient-doctor contacts. Counselors are able to be objective because they are not involved in your daily lives.They don't give specific advice or tell you what to do. Instead, counselors serve as skilled listeners who help you clarify issues, uncover your feelings and help you develop strategies to manage problems more effectively.

NYUAD counselors follow a short-term counseling model with unlimited number of sessions at students' disposal. The number and frequency of sessions are solely based on each student's clinical needs and will be decided by the student and their counselor.

Commitment to Inclusiveness

The Health Center is committed to providing quality care to all members of the NYUAD community who rely on our service. We recognize that race, ethnicity, gender, sexual orientation, religion, culture and socio-economic status may affect the health of an individual and/or influence an individual's healthcare choices. With that in mind, we strive to be sensitive to the diverse needs of our student body. Our commitment is to treat all patients with respect, compassion, and sensitivity.

Our Team

View counselor profiles .

Other Options for Psychotherapy Outside of NYUAD

Students' local and international health insurance can be used for psychotherapy in the community outside of NYUAD for those students who prefer to do so.

We have ongoing partnerships with different mental health providers in the community. Your NYUAD counselors can help you identify most appropriate options for your specific needs.

What kind of problem is appropriate to discuss with a counselor?

Anything that troubles you.

Here is a partial list of common student concerns:

- Depression

- Homesickness

- Stress

- Anxiety

- ADHD

- Alcohol or drugs

- Eating concerns

- Academic anxieties

- Roommate and friendship problems

- Family problems

- Suicidal thoughts

- Sexual concerns

- Identity concerns

Initial Session

Typically, counseling involves an initial session where you meet with your counselor to discuss your primary concerns. From that point onwards, therapy can differ in frequency and content, but will always be confidential, collaborative, time-limited and using evidence based skills. Our counselors share a dedication to providing state-of -the-art services based on current research and thinking in psychology.

What is Cognitive Behavioral Therapy?

- Additional information about Cognitive Behavioral Therapy (CBT) approach.

- Common Myths and Misconceptions about CBT

Schedule an Appointment

Monday-Thursday , 9am-5pm
Friday , 9am-12pm, 2:30-5pm

Stop by our front desk at the Health Center or call us at +971-2-628-8100 to schedule an appointment to see a counselor. We are available Monday to Thursday between 9am-5pm and Friday 9am-12pm and 2:30-5pm. Alternatively, email us at nyuad.healthcenter@nyu.edu .

After-hours (after 5pm, Weekends)

The Wellness Exchange (Available 24/7)

To speak to a certified counselor for immediate support, the Wellness Exchange is available 24/7 at +971 2 628 5555 (85555 from campus) or via NYU Wellness Exchange App, available for Android & iPhone . The App functions 24 hours a day and in six languages.

The Wellness Exchange is your key to accessing NYU's exclusive health and mental health resources. This private, 24/7 hotline puts you in touch with professionals who can help address your day-to-day challenges, as well as other health-related concerns.

Wellness Exchange support includes support for:

- Academic stress

- Depression

- Sexual assault

- Anxiety

- Alcohol and other drugs dependence

- Eating disorders

- Relationship issues

- Adjustment difficulties

- Homesickness

- Just need someone to talk to

- To call about a friend etc.

No concern is too big or too small. The Wellness Exchange is here for you, whatever the reason.

NYU Relaxation and Mindfulness Resources

- NYU Relaxation Oasis

- Mindful NYU

title: Who Will Know? · NYUAD Students
text:
If you come forward with a complaint, who will find out? The answer depends on whether you tell a confidential resource or a private resource. In either case, no information will be shared with anyone outside of the process without your explicit permission. In other words, your story would never be shared with department chairs, faculty, classmate, media, etc. (and, your parents would only be told in an emergency situation).

Confidential

The people listed as confidential resources have the legal privilege of keeping your information private by not sharing it with anyone else without your permission. There are only a few times this would not hold true, including if there was an immediate concern for the health and safety of people in the NYU community — including you. At those times only the necessary information would be shared, not your entire story.

Private

Information that you share with anyone other than the confidential resources listed above will be shared with NYU's Title IX Coordinator and may also be shared with a limited circle of individuals who "need to know" in order to assist in the investigation and resolution. Sharing will happen only as absolutely necessary to aid in the investigation and resolution — and never with anyone outside the process.

title: FAQs · NYUAD Students
text:
General Questions

- I was assaulted, harassed, or stalked. What now?

If you have experienced any sexual misconduct, relationship violence or stalking, we are here to support you. You don’t have to handle this alone. Confidential counseling and medical support are available to assist you, 24 hours a day.

Visit or call the Student Health and Wellness Center at +971 2-628-8100 . Alternately, you can call a Crisis Response Counselor at the Wellness Exchange who can provide confidential guidance about your options — call +971 2-628-5555 for support.

Learn more about what to do after an incident .

- I was accused of sexual misconduct. What now?

NYU Abu Dhabi is committed to providing support for all members involved in a sexual misconduct case. If you are a student respondent — an individual accused of violating NYU’s Sexual Misconduct, Relationship Violence, and Stalking Policy , we urge you to seek support from your on campus resources. Speaking with a counselor — either at the Student Health and Wellness Center or through the Wellness Exchange — can provide you with a safe, confidential and compassionate listening space.

NYU Abu Dhabi also offers Student Support Facilitators to help complainants or respondents understand their rights and responsibilities as they relate to the investigation, fact-finding, report review, any appeal and resolution. While the Student Support Facilitator honors the privacy considerations of the individual, the Student Support Facilitator is not a confidential resource. The Student Support Facilitator serves to support students by answering questions, providing resources and appropriate referrals, and offering assistance throughout the process. The Student Support Facilitator at NYU Abu Dhabi may assist a complainant or respondent in identifying alternate sources for advocacy, legal representation, confidentiality or support; in managing academic, housing, access to dining facilities, and other immediate and on-going separation needs, as necessary.

- Will my conversations with NYU Abu Dhabi remain confidential?

While your story will never be shared with anyone outside of the process without your explicit permission, there are distinct differences between confidential and private conversations — which may impact your decision on who you wish to confide. Learn more .

- I have information that I think should be listed on this website. What can I do?

Student involvement and feedback are welcome! If there are topics or information missing from this website, or issues we need to further clarify, please contact nyuad.healthpromotion@nyu.edu or Remy Shanker to share your thoughts.

Definitions

- What is consent?

NYU's Sexual Misconduct, Relationship Violence, and Stalking Policy defines consent as "the affirmative agreement to engage in a specific sexual activity with another person. Consent requires an outward demonstration, through mutually understandable words or actions, indicating that an individual has freely chosen to engage in a sexual activity." Consent cannot be obtained through: (1) the use of force of coercion; or (2) by taking advantage of the incapacitation of another individual. Learn more .

- What is sexual misconduct?

Prohibited conduct in NYU's Sexual Misconduct, Relationship Violence, and Stalking Policy includes sexual or gender-based harassment, sexual assault, and sexual exploitation. Also prohibited are relationship violence, stalking, and retaliation:

- Sexual assault is having or attempting to have sexual contact with another individual by force or threat of force, without consent, or where that individual is incapacitated.

- Sexual harassment is any unwelcome sexual advance, request for sexual favors, or other unwanted conduct of a sexual nature, whether verbal, non-verbal, graphic, physical or otherwise.

- Gender-based harassment includes harassment based on gender, sexual orientation, gender identity, or gender expression, which may include acts of aggression, intimidation or hostility, whether verbal or non-verbal, graphic, physical or otherwise, even if the acts do not involve conduct of a sexual nature.

For the full definitions of these prohibited behaviors — as well as the definitions of sexual exploitation, relationship violence, stalking, and retaliation — see NYU's Sexual Misconduct, Relationship Violence, and Stalking Policy , which we encourage the NYU Abu Dhabi community to read.

- What is Title IX?

Title IX of the Education Amendments of 1972 is a comprehensive United States law that prohibits discrimination on the basis of sex in any federally funded education program or activity. Under Title IX, discrimination on the basis of sex can include sexual harassment or sexual violence, such as rape, sexual assault, sexual battery and sexual coercion. Therefore, every university has a responsibility to respond promptly and effectively to reports of sexual misconduct. If a school knows or reasonably should know about sexual harassment or sexual violence that creates a hostile environment, the school must take immediate action to eliminate the sexual harassment or sexual violence, prevent its recurrence and address its effects. Even if a student (or his or her parent) does not want to file a complaint or does not request that the school take any action on the student's behalf, if a school knows or reasonably should know about possible sexual harassment or sexual violence, it must promptly investigate to determine what occurred and then take appropriate steps to resolve the situation. A criminal investigation into allegations of sexual harassment or sexual violence does not relieve the school of its duty under Title IX to resolve complaints promptly and equitably. Learn more .

Resources

- How can I receive immediate support in a crisis?

NYU Abu Dhabi provides immediate comprehensive support for all survivors of sexual assault. A nurse and a counselor are available and on call 24-hours a day to provide support and connect students to resources. Additionally, the Wellness Exchange has Crisis Response Counselors (CRC) that are available by phone 24-hours a day, every day of the year to provide support for students.

The Student Health and Wellness Center and the Wellness Exchange will act as your personal liaison throughout the process of accessing care and services following a sexual assault. They will walk you through the medical, counseling, legal, academic and housing assistance options available.

Not only will they respond in an immediate emergency, but they also can help you plan and schedule any follow up services and support you might need. Call the Student Health and Wellness Center at +971 2-628-8100. When calling the Wellness Exchange hotline at +971 2-628-5555, just ask for the CRC. If you are abroad at an NYU global site, we have established local Wellness Exchange phone numbers you can call for help.

- What other resources does NYU Abu Dhabi offer?

Medical Assistance

In the immediate aftermath of a sexual misconduct incident it is critical that you receive any medical support you may need. Immediately call the Student Health and Wellness Center to speak with a doctor or nurse who can provide you with medical care: +971 2- 628-8100.

Counseling and Emotional Assistance

A survivor of sexual assault can experience emotional as well as physical consequences. Sexual assault is a traumatic experience that can have both immediate and long-term effects.

Initial reactions vary and may include shock, denial, anxiety, guilt, anger, and self-blame. A survivor may experience nightmares, changes in their eating patterns, and depression. Therefore, individuals who have been sexually assaulted are strongly encouraged to obtain help from a professional counselor as soon as they are ready after the incident occurs.

Students can contact the Student Health and Wellness Center at +971 2- 628-8100, Sunday to Thursday, 9am-5pm to set up an appointment with a counselor. Students can also call the Wellness Exchange at +971 2-628-5555 anytime to speak with a counselor over the telephone.

Understanding the Process

Complainants and respondents may have specific questions about the reporting, investigation and resolution process following a sexual misconduct complaint. Tina Wadhwa and Remy Shanker in Student Persistence and Well-being are non-confidential resources who can answer any questions you may have, and provide you with detailed information about what to expect if you are involved in a Sexual Misconduct, Dating Violence or Stalking situation. Further, they act as a liaison should you need support in filing a complaint or contacting the Title IX coordinator.

Residential Help

In some cases of sexual assault, you may have residential or housing needs. Ensuring your safety in your living environment is important, so we stand ready to assist in connecting you to the appropriate resources.

NYU's Office of Equal Opportunity (Title IX office) is available to discuss your housing needs and assist you in obtaining appropriate and available housing accommodations through our Residential Life and Housing Office. If you would prefer for your counselor to speak to the Title IX coordinator on your behalf, you can ask for their support by speaking with your NYU Abu Dhabi counselor or by calling the Wellness Exchange Hotline at +971-2-628-5555.

Academic Help

In the case of a sexual assault or any kind of sexual violence and misconduct, survivors may have a variety of responses and feelings that may impact functioning. We realize there may be academic needs, and we are available to help assist you in receiving support from your school. The Office of Equal Opportunity can assist you in this process and is able to keep information private, only sharing key information to those who need to know. You can contact title9@nyu.edu directly or ask your counselor for their confidential support.

Understanding Your Experience

- I was sexually assaulted in the past. What can I do?

Sexual assault, no matter when it happens, can change your life. It can change your view of yourself and others. You may experience changes in your sleeping and eating patterns. You may have nightmares or flashbacks about the assault. You may be afraid of being alone, or fear being in crowds. Support and help are available for you.

Students can contact the Student Health and Wellness Center at+971 2-628-8100 (Sunday to Thursday, 9am-5pm) to set up an appointment with a counselor . Students can also call the Wellness Exchange at 02-628-5555 anytime to speak with a counselor over the telephone.

- I don't know what to call my experience, but I don't feel comfortable with a sexual encounter I had. What can I do?

If you've had a sexual encounter that left you feeling uncomfortable or violated, but you are not quite sure what to call it, there are people available to listen and support you. Call the Wellness Exchange 24-hour Support Line at +971 2-628-5555 to speak with a counselor — you don't have to give your name. Alternately, you can visit or call the Student Health and Wellness Center at +971 2-628-8100. Either option can connect you with NYU Abu Dhabi resources.

- I'm feeling so many different emotions about this experience. Is this normal?

Reactions to a traumatic experience such as sexual assault vary from person to person. The following are examples of both physical and emotional reactions that a survivor might experience.

Physical Reactions:

- Aches and pains: headaches, back aches, stomachaches

- Sudden sweating, heart palpitations

- Changes in sleep patterns, appetite, interest in sex

- Constipation or diarrhea

- Easily startled by noises or unexpected touch

- More susceptible to colds and illness

Emotional Reactions:

- Shock

- Disbelief

- Embarrassment

- Shame

- Guilt

- Depression

- Disorientation

- Denial

- Fear

- Anxiety

- Anger

- Social withdrawal

- Self-blame

- Concern for the perpetrator

- Lack of concentration resulting in academic difficulties

Helping a Friend

- What can I do to help a friend?

Surviving a sexual assault can be a traumatic experience, and reactions can be varied, in time and in kind. You may be supporting a friend or family member who has survived a sexual assault, and many questions may arise in how to best support them, how to ask the right questions, and offer the best help.

It can be difficult to know how to handle such situations. We can help guide you in understanding your experience as a helper, and the ways to understand and support your loved one. These skills can be utilized regardless of the relationship, whether you're a friend, faculty, staff or parent.

To talk more about how to help a friend or family member you can call the Student Health Center .Alternately, you can call the Wellness Exchange anytime to speak with a counselor confidentially at +971 2-628-5555. We have also established local phone numbers to reach the Wellness Exchange if you are at a different NYU global site.

- What do I do if the assault has recently occurred?

In certain instances, a person may not know what actually happened. They may have woken up and are unsure whether they were assaulted. Again, empower them to make their own decisions. If they want to speak with a counselor, encourage them to contact the Student Health and Wellness Center at+971 2-628-8100 to set up an appointment with a confidential counselor. Students can also call the Wellness Exchange anytime to speak with a counselor over the telephone; it's confidential and available 24-hours a day, every day at +971 2-628-5555.

title: Sexual Misconduct Report Form · NYUAD Students
text:
If an act of sexual misconduct has been committed against you, you may consider filing a complaint against the person(s) responsible. We know that this can be a difficult decision, so we encourage you to discuss your options with a professional. Tina Wadhwa and Remy Shanker at Student Persistence and Well-being is a great first point of contact, or you can talk to a counselor at the Student Health and Wellness Center for support in deciding how you want to respond.

If you do choose to file a complaint, please use this form . Submissions using this form will be reviewed by NYU's Title IX Coordinator and the Office of Equal Opportunity, and you will receive a call within 48 hours requesting additional information.

PLEASE NOTE: Submitting this form begins a formal complaint. Alternatively, if you wish to speak confidentially to someone about your options before filing a formal report, professional counselors are available 24 hours a day, seven days a week by contacting the Wellness Exchange at +971 2-628-5555. Alternately, you can visit or call the Student Health and Wellness Center at +971 2-628-8100.

title: What Is Consent? · NYUAD Students
text:
NYU's Sexual Misconduct, Relationship Violence, and Stalking Policy defines consent as "the affirmative agreement to engage in a specific sexual activity with another person. Consent requires an outward demonstration, through mutually understandable words or actions, indicating that an individual has freely chosen to engage in a sexual activity." Consent cannot be obtained through: (1) the use of force of coercion; or (2) by taking advantage of the incapacitation of another individual.

We encourage you to familiarize yourself with the following details about consent:

- Pressuring someone repeatedly to engage in sexual activity is called coercion. Coercion is NOT consent.

Coercion is repeatedly reassuring your partner that the sexual activity is okay, that your partner will enjoy him/herself, and continuing with sexual activity. Coercion can include:

- Physically maneuvering your partner’s body when she or he keeps pulling away

- Asking repeatedly to engage in sexual activity until your partner says "yes"

- Stating that you will suffer some sort of physical consequence if your partner does not complete a sexual act with you

- An individual who is incapacitated lacks the ability to make informed, rational judgments and cannot consent to sexual activity.

You cannot obtain consent from someone who is:

- Drunk or high

- Passed out

- Asleep

- Physically incapacitated

- Mentally incapacitated

- Being engaged in a long-term partnership, including marriage, does not create automatic consent.

Long-term partners and married couples still need to get consent every time.

- Consent is valid only for that precise moment.

There is no such thing as blanket consent. Consenting to something at 9pm does not necessarily mean it's consensual at 9:15pm.

- Just because you've had consent before, doesn't mean you still do.

Engaging in consensual sexual activity earlier in the day/evening/week/month/year does not grant consent for future sexual activity.

- Consent can be withdrawn at any time.

Including in the middle of engaging in sexual activity.

title: What to Do After an Incident · NYUAD Students
text:
Coping with sexual misconduct, especially sexual violence, can present many challenges and emotions — but you don't have to handle it alone. It doesn't matter what time it is or how long ago something happened. Talk to the Wellness Exchange , the Student Health and Wellness Center , Health Promotions Student Persistence and Well-being , or someone you trust (a friend, loved one or family member) for support as you decide how you want to respond.

What to Do After an Incident?

- Once you're safe, contact the Student Health & Wellness Center for medical support

In the immediate aftermath of a sexual misconduct incident, it is critical that you receive any medical support you may need. Immediately call the Student Health and Wellness Center and speak with a doctor or nurse who can provide you with medical care at +971 2-628-8100.

- If you do not require medical support, call a counselor

Our Counseling Center (+971 2-628-8100 during business hours) or Wellness Exchange (+971 2-628-5555) have counselors on hand to offer confidential support over the phone, meet with you in person during emergencies and discuss your medical, mental health, and legal options. Counselors are available 24 hours a day, every day of the year.

- Read about confidentiality

Privacy and confidentiality have distinct meanings. Medical and mental health professionals are able to keep conversations confidential (subject to certain exceptions explained here ). Other NYU administrators, however, are only able to keep details private. Learn more .

- Be kind to yourself

Remember that an assault is never the survivor's fault. Counseling Services at the Student Health and Wellness Center offer you short-term counseling, self-improvement classes, referrals, and psychiatric medication services — most of which are free. Sexual assault is a traumatic experience that can have both immediate and long-term effects. Survivors of sexual assault are encouraged to obtain help from a professional counselor as soon as they are ready after the incident occurs. You don't have to go through this alone.

- It may also be useful to speak with the Office of Sexual Misconduct Support Services

Tina Wadhwa and Remy Shanker are non-confidential support that can provide you with detailed information about the policy and procedures related to the assessment, investigation and adjudication of a sexual misconduct violation. She can also connect complainants and respondents to campus resources.

- Consider making a formal report to NYU

Contact NYU's Office of Equal Opportunity at title9@nyu.edu , to submit a formal complaint, or report an incident online . Once you file a report with NYU, you may request that the matter remain private or that no investigation be conducted. However, NYU will balance that request against its commitment to a safe learning, living, and working environment for all community members. For more detailed information, please consult the policy .

- Consider academic or residential support

NYU will provide temporary or permanent protective accommodations and measures, which may include separation orders, residence modifications, academic accommodations or work schedule modifications, where appropriate and reasonably available under the circumstances. We will work with you to coordinate this assistance upon request, regardless of whether an investigation is pursued. Contact NYU's Office of Equal Opportunity at title9@nyu.edu for assistance.

title: New Student Housing · NYUAD Students
text:
New Student Housing

New Student Housing is applicable only to incoming freshmen who will be living on NYU Abu Dhabi's campus for the first time.

- Eligibility

NYUAD guarantees undergraduate housing to students for their academic careers provided the following conditions are met for the duration of their stay in housing:

- Students meet all application deadlines

- Students maintain full-time matriculated status

- Housing Rates and Agreement

Housing Rates

- Fall and spring semesters: USD 3,000 per semester

License Agreement

Please ensure you've read through our Global Housing Contract (PDF).

- Dates and Deadlines

Please visit our linktree for more information on housing dates and deadlines.

- Assignments

Geographic diversity is a primary variable in the room assignment process for first-year students. This model reflects the University’s value that students should network across geographic differences.

While we do our best to honor room preferences, due to availability, we cannot guarantee that all requests will be met.

The following criteria and application preferences are considered when assignments are made for incoming first-year students:

- Gender

- Reasonable Accommodations approved by the Moses Center pending availability

- Visitation Preference

- Geographic Diversity
Students may not submit requests for specific roommates during their freshman year at NYU. We feel it is important for all new students to meet new people, expand their interests, broaden their understanding of different regions and cultures, and stretch their comfort zones with all that NYU’s global network has to offer. We want our residents to celebrate each other’s commonalities and expect that they will respect each other’s differences.

- Responses to the housing lifestyle questionnaire (carries the least weight in the process)

- Roommates and Tips

A key experience of a college education is the opportunity to live and study with people from diverse backgrounds. This is uniquely true at NYU, where students are prepared to enter an increasingly global society by studying at campuses throughout the world.

Roommate Relations

Communication is key to a harmonious residence hall living experience. Residents receive their roommates’ contact information along with their assignment notice. Talking with roommates about how to arrange the room, how to decorate, and what items each person will bring is a good way to begin the conversation. Set ground rules about shared items and bills and discuss personal habits, sleeping schedules, study habits, musical tastes, guests, needs, wants, and expectations. Honesty, consideration, mutual respect, discussion, compromise, and understanding are crucial to learning to live together. If problems arise between roommates, residential college staff members are available to help work through roommate problems and/or to resolve the matter through mediation and arbitration.

Tips on Roommate Relationships

Living with a roommate can be one of the most rewarding experiences of your college career. Whether you find a new hobby, learn a new skill, or become good friends, living with a roommate can be fun! However, living with someone also has its challenges. Conflict is a normal part of roommate relationships, and it is important for these conflicts to be constructively addressed by everyone living in the room or apartment.

NYUAD administrators are available to assist you with any conflict you experience with your roommates or suitemates. Below is a guide for students living in the NYUAD residential colleges. This guide provides useful information that you can utilize in working through a conflict with your roommate. Try to utilize some of these skills in speaking with your roommate, and if you need assistance navigating your roommate relationship further, contact your Resident Assistant (RA).

Before Arriving

It is normal for you to be excited and anxious about living with a new roommate. Before arriving at your residential college, you should consider reaching out to your roommate(s) and speaking with her/him/them on the phone, email, or social media. This will give you an opportunity to get to know each other and begin to plan for your living experience. Remember, it can be difficult to get to know someone over technology, so be cautious about making quick judgments about your new roommate(s) before meeting her/him/them in person. Below are examples of topics that you and your roommate may want to consider discussing.

- Who's bringing or buying what for the room/suite? (i.e., TV, hot water pot, rug, dishes, pots and pans, etc.)

- Intentions for your room (i.e., is it a study or social space?)

- How are we decorating our room? (i.e., color scheme)

If and How Do We Want to Decorate?

Before you contact your soon-to-be roommate(s), it is important to think about your own personal needs so that you can express them accurately and openly when talking. It can be both challenging and fun to live with someone else, so it helps to let them know from the start what you need and vice versa. If you are a first-year student, you should also know that some of your preferences may change over time.

Great Expectations

Please keep in mind that everyone has different beliefs, values, experiences, communication styles, and expectations. With that being said, you and your roommate may become the best of friends, or you may only see each other when you’re in your room.

No matter how close you are, you have to work together to establish and maintain a positive living environment. Having the right attitude can make living with a roommate a little easier for everyone living in the room.

If you haven’t already done so, as soon as you get settled into your room, you should discuss your expectations honestly. The biggest conflicts often arise when expectations are not addressed from the beginning. Don’t put off talking to each other about your expectations, needs, quirks, and sources of aggravation or frustration. It is a great way to help manage conflict in the future. Issues such as room cleanliness, bedtime, borrowing one another’s things, and guests are the most common issues over which roommates tend to disagree.

- Reasonable Housing Accommodations

In accordance with applicable federal, state, and city disability laws, New York University will provide reasonable accommodations for students.

Visit the NYU Reasonable Housing Accommodation to learn more.

- What to Bring

General packing advice:

- You will be required to bring or purchase your own linens and bedding; this includes all pillows, sheets, blankets, pillow covers, towels, etc.

- Don’t pack more suitcases than you can carry on your own. Storage options are limited on campus.

- Bring clothes appropriate for the weather in the UAE. Be sure to be mindful of weather and cultural norms.

- Double-check that any electronic devices you plan to take are compatible with the local electricity and have the correct plug adapters. It’s also advisable to buy electronics in Abu Dhabi so you don’t need to worry about compatibility issues.

- You can get local currency in Abu Dhabi (there are foreign exchange centers in malls) or upon arrival at the airport.

- Do make appropriate arrangements for personal hygiene based on public health guidelines (masks, gloves, hand sanitizer, etc).

- Remember that storage on campus is limited and is not guaranteed for any student. You should only pack as much as you plan to bring back home with you when you check out.

Here are some additional items to consider bringing:

- Backpack/Tote Bag

- Sweatshirt, sweater, or shawl for cold evenings and air conditioning

- Photos, mementos, and other small things that make you feel at home

- Athletic sneakers, beach sandals, flip flops

- Traditional attire from your home country

- Vitamins, preferred off-the-counter painkillers, cough drops, etc.

- Snacks from home for quarantine

- Nail clippers

- Swimwear

- Notes on Attire

General Guidance

Given the diverse nature of the population of the UAE, one can see many different types of dress, including jeans, saris, dresses, business suits, and the UAE national dress (kandora and abaya). While there are no laws around dress codes, some public venues (e.g., malls and government offices) have dress code guidelines that may be enforced.

When thinking about what clothes one might need at NYUAD, it’s important to keep in mind that people typically refrain from wearing excessively revealing clothing. This generally means long trousers, a shirt that covers the shoulders and upper arms, and skirts, dresses, or shorts that reach the knee. Transparent or see-through clothing is not appropriate for any gender.

Different Seasons

For most of the year, lightweight clothing is suitable; however, most buildings in the UAE are air-conditioned, and a sweater or lightweight jacket may often be needed indoors. A sweater and jacket are needed during the winter months (December and January), especially in the evening.

On Campus

While on campus, students are generally expected to uphold the same guidelines for attire that they follow off campus. In residential colleges, dress tends to be casual, and students will likely want comfortable clothing for lounging and studying.

Workout Gear

Students interested in using the campus fitness center will want to pack workout gear/clothing. This includes appropriate footwear (running shoes, sneakers). Sandals, boots, and open shoes are not appropriate footwear. Jeans, denim, or revealing workout gear are not allowed in the fitness center.

- Former Students Advice

Here is some advice from students who were on campus during the last academic year about things they learned through personal experience:

- Keep track of and manage your campus dirhams because they will run out faster than you may think! Refer to the student portal Meal Plan for more information.

- Check Amazon, IKEA, the Convenience store, or other stores that deliver essentials or items for your room. It is better to order some stuff (like decorations, duvet covers, books, etc.) rather than buying these items in your home country.

- Bring one or two sweatshirts! It can get pretty cold inside campus buildings due to the AC.

- Don’t overpack or overbuy! Upper Class students are very often giving out their stuff so you might be able to get nice things for free.

- Communications

In accordance with University guidelines, all communications from NYUAD regarding housing are sent directly to students, not parents or guardians. This includes information pertaining to deadline dates and application instructions. Notices are sent by email.

Your NYUAD Net ID serves as your official NYUAD e-mail address. Notifications and information are sent to students at this email address only. It is each student's responsibility to check their University email regularly.

Related official links:
https://students.nyuad.nyu.edu/services/dining/meal-plan/

title: Academics · NYUAD Students
text:
During your time at NYUAD you will interact with a number of Academic areas:

- Writing Support

Looking for someone to read over your manuscript? Tired of nagging your colleagues to provide feedback? Wanting some extra polish before you submit to that competitive journal? Head to the Center for Writing.

Appointments can be made at any time, but are often most useful if there is a draft ready to be examined.

You can schedule an appointment with our Center for Writing.

- University Library

Located on the top floor of the Campus Center, the NYU Abu Dhabi Library provides spaces for engagement between faculty and students, complemented by quiet areas for concentration and contemplation. Comfortable reading areas and study rooms create a productive atmosphere for research. Service to scholars is the primary mission of the NYU Abu Dhabi Library. We provide resources and technologies needed for research and teaching and offer assistance in their use. To find out more go to the Library website .

- NYUAD Institute

The NYU Abu Dhabi (NYUAD) Institute is a major hub of intellectual and creative activity, advanced research, and higher education. Graduate Students are welcome to suggest public programs, and can get involved with Institute events and volunteer with the Institute by emailing nyuad.institute@nyu.edu , or visiting our office in Humanities Building (A6)-1172C. — Find out more about the NYUAD Institute

- Graduate Student Manual

NYUAD is committed to providing a supportive and structured environment for the development of scholars, researchers, and teachers. It is expected that the responsibilities of students, faculty, and staff will be discharged with impartiality, reason, and consistency. To this end, it is the responsibility of all members of the NYUAD community to respect and comply with all NYUAD Policies and Procedures as well as all University rules and policies. — Read the Graduate Manual (PDF).

- The Office of the University Registrar (NYU Enrolled Students)

The Office of the Registrar is here to assist you with everything you need to register for classes or make adjustments to your schedule, get a copy of your transcripts, and prepare to graduate. — Find out more about the NYU Registrar

- Office of the University Registrar (NYUAD Enrolled Students)

The Office of the University Registrar supports teaching and learning at NYU Abu Dhabi by maintaining the integrity of academic policies and the student information system. — Find out more about the NYUAD Registrar

- Course List

For a full syllabi of courses offered through our Graduate Programs, please follow the link to the Course List .

title: Awards · NYUAD Students
text:
The Graduate and Postdoctoral Programs Office runs annual awards that helps to recognise the achievements of our Graduate Students.

- NYUAD Graduate Student Leadership Award (Applications open in Spring 2026)

The NYUAD Graduate Student Leadership Award celebrates graduate students who have engaged in outstanding service that has positively impacted the campus or wider community.

Number of Awards: One award per calendar year

Nomination Criteria: To be eligible to participate, entrants must be a graduate student in good academic standing at NYUAD and be registered during the Spring Term. Self nominations are accepted. Eligible Students include Global PhD Fellows, Dissertation Fellows and Masters Students.

Nomination Requirements:
-CV or resume (No more than 2 pages, A4)
-Narrative response to these prompts (maximum of 2 pages, A4; must be written by the nominee)
Describe specific contributions you have made to either the NYUAD campus or to wider communities and showcase how your efforts provided a positive impact. How do these contributions exemplify leadership qualities that you have gained and/or developed through your experience as a graduate student?
-Letter of reference (1 Page, A4)
The letter should speak to the nominee’s general leadership abilities, ideally coming from someone who has directly observed and can evaluate their specific leadership qualities. It also should articulate the specific impact of the nominee’s efforts on the campus or communities described. This letter may be provided by a fellow team member, a mentor, or another individual who can give a first-hand account of the nominee’s leadership

Deadline for submissions: TBC

Submissions should be emailed to nyuad.graduateoffice@nyu.edu in a PDF or Word format and should follow the guidelines above, and be no more than 5 pages total.

Selection Process: A committee with representatives from the Graduate and Postdoctoral Programs Office will select the winner.

Prize: The awardee will receive an honorarium of $500 and a memento that signifies the appreciation of the institution.

Past Winners

- Graduate Student Leadership Award 2025: Devjoy Dev - 4th Year Global PhD Fellow in PhD Fellow in Biomedical Engineering

- Graduate Student Leadership Award 2024: Saifeldeen Abed Alrhman - 4th Year Global PhD Fellow in PhD Fellow in Chemical and Biomolecular Engineering

You can read more about Saifeldeen's Award at https://nyuad.nyu.edu/en/news/latest-news/community-life/2024/june/student-transforms-campus-accessibility-and-community-engagement.html

- Graduate Student Leadership Award 2023: Juan Esteban Villegas - 4th Year Global PhD Fellow in Electrical and Computer Engineering

You can read more about Juan's Award at https://nyuad.nyu.edu/en/news/latest-news/community-life/2023/june/let-there-be-light.html

- Graduate Student Leadership Award Winner 2022: Wegood Awad - Global PhD Fellow in Chemistry

You can read more about Wegood's Award at https://nyuad.nyu.edu/en/news/latest-news/community-life/2022/june/more-than-just-research-work.html .

- Graduate Student Leadership Award Winner 2021: Jad Mahmoud Halabi - Global PhD Fellow in Chemistry

title: Funding · NYUAD Students
text:
The Graduate and Postdoctoral Programs Office, alongside Student Affairs and the Office of Student Research offer a number of funding and research opportunities for students to assist their professional progress while at NYUAD.

On Campus Employment Opportunities

- Graduate Student On-Campus Jobs via Handshake

Graduate Students enrolled in either the MSc or MFA programs are eligible to apply for Student Assistantship Positions offered through Handshake . Graduate students receive a stipend of 59AED per hour for appointments.

You can find out more about the program by going to https://students.nyuad.nyu.edu/academics/research/student-assistantship-program/ .

Global PhD students and PASS PhD students are not eligible for the Student Assistantship Program at this time.

General Funding Programs

- Interview Travel Grant

The Career Development Center (CDC) offers interview travel grants to eligible NYUAD students through a competitive application process. This funding can help students cover the cost of attending a final round interview related to their post-graduation plans that must take place in person rather than virtually or by phone.

All Graduate students are eligible to apply.

To find out more go to https://students.nyuad.nyu.edu/student-affairs/career-development/funding/interview-funding/ .

- Summer Internship Grant

Graduate Students enrolled in either the MSc or MFA programs are eligible to apply for a Summer Internship Grant. This supplemental funding helps students pursue internships across the globe each summer.

Internships for the purposes of this grant are work-placement opportunities that are not supervised by a faculty mentor or researcher. The student is interning in an office environment or government agency in an effort to explore a possible career path.

You can find out more about the program by going to https://students.nyuad.nyu.edu/student-affairs/career-development/funding/internships/ .

Global PhD students are not eligible for the Student Assistantship Program at this time.

- PhD Travel Awards

Travel awards may be used toward presenting at conferences or similar events that will have a strong impact on the individual’s research profile. The award is open to NYUAD-affiliated Global PhD students and PASS PhD students in all disciplines.

Awards may vary in value, with each recipient being granted no more than $1,000 per award.

Students are normally eligible to receive a maximum of two travel awards from the Graduate & Postdoctoral Programs Office (GPPO) during their time in the program but due to limited funding, this is not guaranteed.

You can find more information on the awards by going to the Global PhD Travel Award Section of the Intranet .

You may also contact the GPPO - nyuad.graduateoffice@nyu.edu for any questions.

Students enrolled in our MFA or MSc programs are not eligible for PhD Travel Awards.

- Conference Grants

The Office of Student Research can offer conference grants to support students who have been invited to present their research or creative work, where the student was selected to participate through a competitive process.

Research conference grants may be expended during the fall, spring, or summer terms and the maximum award is $1,500 per conference.

Only one student may be funded to present a single paper or research project.

Graduate Students enrolled in either the MSc or MFA programs are eligible to apply for Conference Grants. To find out more, please go to https://students.nyuad.nyu.edu/academics/research/conference-grants/

Global PhD students are not eligible for Conference Grants and should apply for a PhD Travel Award instead.

- Graduate Student Family Support Program

The GPPO recognises that the scholarships and support offered to our PhD students may fall short of offering full financial support for students to have their spouses or family members accompany them for the full duration of their tenure at NYUAD. Hereby, the Graduate Student Family Support Program has been introduced to assist.

The grants are funded and administered by the Graduate and Postdoctoral Programs Office. For the academic year 2025-2026, the grant program will have an open application cycle to support students with qualifying costs to access grant funds. Funding for this grant is limited and grants will be disbursed as funding allows.

The program offers to offset the additional costs incurred by our students with families on a needs-based basis - it is not intended to cover all costs. Each family is eligible to apply for up-to $4,000 total in needs-based support for any of the qualifying costs incurred during the current academic year (the current academic year is September 1st 2025 to August 31st, 2026). Retrospective costs (i.e., Costs incurred in previous academic years) or future expected or estimated costs are not eligible. Grants are awarded annually, and students must reapply each year.

To find out more about this program, please go to The Graduate Student Family Support Program Page

The Graduate Family Support Program is open to Global PhD students and PASS PhD students only.

Graduate Students enrolled in either the MSc or MFA programs are not eligible for this program.

- Preskilling Professional Development Grant (PPDG)

The PPDG provides grants ranging from USD 200 to 500 to assist with the cost of preskilling courses. Recipients are expected to share the cost of any course priced above USD 500. The grant operates on a first-come, first-served basis and covers courses that must be completed within six months, no later than the end of the June term.

In addition to completing the course, the recipient is required to present their learnings in a 10-minute presentation during a "Lunch and Learn Session," coordinated with Ross Fleming, Associate Director of Graduate and Postdoctoral Support at rf82@nyu.edu . The session will be attended by NYUAD stakeholders, colleagues, and students. For career advising and support from the Career Development Center, contact Nabeel Mohammed, Career & Graduate School Advisor at nm4969@nyu.edu .

Courses eligible for this grant may include topics such as UX, Design, Coding, Cloud/FIN/ED/AG-Tech, Innovation, Advanced Research Methods, Scientific Writing, Cybersecurity, and more. The selected course should align with the recipient's professional development goals and demonstrate clear value in advancing their career in academia, research, or industry.

Application Scope & Timeline
The grant may be applied to courses focusing on skills such as writing, leadership, management, presentations, UX, Design, data/statistical courses, technology-based workshops, skill-focused conferences, and boot camps/hackathons that are not offered at NYUAD .

Aug. 25, 2025: Application Opens
Sept. 24, 2025: Application Deadline
Sept. 25-29, 2025: Application Review
Sept. 30, 2025: Notification of Results
Oct. 1, 2025: Fund Allocation
May 1, 2026: Last day to Submit Reimbursement

Budget Limit
USD 200 to 500, with a maximum of USD 500 per individual. Each recipient may apply twice during their NYUAD tenure.
