title: PhD Travel Awards · NYUAD Students
text:
Applications for Cycle 1 are now closed. Cycle 2 will open January 4th, 2027.

Travel awards may be used towards presenting a paper or poster at a conference in the respective field . The funds are intended to help you defray some conference registration and travel costs. The award is open to NYUAD-affiliated PhD students in all disciplines.

Awards may vary in value, with each recipient being granted no more than USD 1,000 per award. Awards may vary in value for each student.

Students are normally eligible to receive a maximum of two travel awards from the Graduate and Postdoctoral Programs Office (GPPO) during their time in the program, subject to funding availability.

Priority of Funding

Funding is prioritized based on the following criteria:

- Group A : Global PhD / Pass PhD students who have not received previous funding and are in the final year of their PhD program, and have a letter confirming they have been accepted as a speaker or presenter;

- Group B : Global PhD / Pass PhD students who have not received previous funding and are not in the final year of their program, and have a letter confirming they have been accepted as a speaker or presenter;

- Group C : Global PhD / Pass PhD students who have received previous funding, and have a letter confirming they have been accepted as a speaker or presenter;

Please note: Any Global PhD/Pass PhD student who has received additional funding support from another source will automatically fall into Group C. Further, any Global PhD / Pass PhD student who applies without an acceptance letter will not be considered for funding.

After Receiving the Funds and After the Conference

Within two weeks after the conference, PhD students who receive funding must submit a short, 1-2 paragraph article about their experience at the conference by email to the GPPO. Please include a picture from the conference if you have it. Acknowledgment of funding and a short report is an expectation of receiving the PhD Travel Award.

Funding Cycle Dates

Awards are open during the following Cycles only . Global PhD / Pass PhD students should therefore plan in advance and submit applications in line with the application cycle deadlines.

Cycle 1 – Travel between October 1, 2026 and January 31, 2027
Awards during Cycle 1 should be for travel that will take place between October 1, 2026 and January 31, 2027.

Applications open September 1, 2026. Applications close September 30, 2026. Decisions sent to students by October 7, 2026.

Payments will be made in October 2026 payroll.

Cycle 2 – Travel between February 1 and May 31, 2027
Travel between February 1 and May 31, 2027

Applications open January 4 to January 31, 2027. Decisions sent February 8, 2027

Cycle 3 – Travel between June 1 and September 30, 2027
Awards during Cycle 3 should be for travel that will take place between June 1, 2027 to September 30, 2027.

Applications open May 3 to May 30, 2027. Decisions sent to applicants by June 7, 2027.

Payments will be made in June 2027 payroll.

How to Apply

Please submit the application form .

Questions?

For any questions, please email nyuad.graduateoffice@nyu.edu .

title: Graduate Student Family Support Program · NYUAD Students
text:
Applications for AY26-27 are now open.

For this year we will allow health insurance costs from July or August 2026 to be claimed. This is the only exception we can provide. All other costs must be dated on or after 1st September 2026. We cannnot accept future dated invoices.

Graduate students’ families (a spouse, partner, and/or children) contribute to the rich diversity of the NYUAD community. For graduate student families with children, the dual role of parenting and being a graduate student is challenging, especially with regards to finances, childcare, and scheduling. Simultaneously, there is a great opportunity for families of graduate students to share in the rich NYUAD Culture.

The GPPO recognizes that the scholarships and support offered to our graduate students may fall short of offering full financial support for students to have their spouses or family members accompany them for the full duration of their tenure at NYUAD. Hereby, the Graduate Student Family Support Program has been introduced to assist. This program is open to Global PhD Students and PASS PhD Students only.

The grants are funded and administered by the Graduate and Postdoctoral Programs Office. For the academic year 2026-2027, the grant program will have an open application cycle to support students with qualifying costs to access grant funds. Funding for this grant is limited, and grants will be disbursed as funding allows.

The program offers to offset the additional costs incurred by our Global PhD and PASS PhD students with families on a needs-based basis — it is not intended to cover all costs. Each family is eligible to apply for up to USD 5,000* total in needs-based support for any of the qualifying costs incurred during the current academic year (the current academic year is September 1, 2026 to August 31, 2027). Retrospective costs (i.e., Costs incurred in previous academic years) or future expected or estimated costs are not eligible. Grants are administered annually, and students must make a new application for each claim.

*The total amount any student can claim in one academic year, across all qualifying costs, is USD 5,000.

Qualifying costs

Please review the following qualifying costs. The grant can only cover expenses that have been incurred during the current academic year . We cannot cover future expected or estimated costs or any expenses from previous academic years (no exceptions can be made):

- Direct costs associated with visa sponsorship or renewal (only applicable to UAE Sponsorship and UAE Visa issuance for spouses, partners, or dependent children)

Documentation required for support: Official receipts from UAE Government authorities/agencies showing expense; Credit card or debit card statements showing expense, copy of visa for spouse/partner or dependent children

- Direct costs associated with school fees (only applicable to school fees for dependent children aged between 3-18 registered in a school in the UAE)

Documentation required for support: Copy of Dependent Child Birth Certificate; Official receipts from an UAE Accredited School/Education Facility showing dependent children name(s) and enrollment; Credit card or debit card statements showing expense; Copy of visa for dependent children

- Direct costs associated with childcare - up to 25% of direct childcare costs may be claimed through the program (only applicable to dependent children under 3 and registered at a childcare facility in the UAE, or childcare costs provided through an official agency in the UAE)

Documentation required for support: Copy of Dependent Child Birth Certificate; Official receipts from UAE Government authorities/agencies showing expense (i.e., Tadbeer fees); Credit card or debit card statements showing expense; Copy of contract for childcare/nanny; In lieu of some or all of these documents, you may also provide a copy of the sponsorship letter for the domestic helper/nanny along with copies of their labor contract, confirming the name of the sponsor (which would normally be the name of the student), along with a signed confirmation of monthly salary from the domestic helper or nanny

- Direct costs associated with dependent health insurance (only applicable to spouses, partners, or dependent children who have an active UAE Visa and live in the Emirate of Abu Dhabi)

Documentation required for support: Official policy from Insurance Provider showing active policy with names of spouses/partner or dependent children; NYUAD paystub showing the expense has been debited from your salary; copy of visa for spouse, partner or dependent children

Financial Support offered by the Grant

The program offers to offset the additional costs incurred by our Global PhD Students with families on a needs-based basis — it is not intended to cover all costs. Each family is eligible to apply for up to USD 5,000 total in needs-based support for any of the qualifying costs incurred during the current academic year (the current academic year is September 1, 2026 to August 31, 2027).

- Retrospective costs (i.e., costs incurred in previous academic years) or future expected or estimated costs are not eligible

- Grants are awarded annually during the academic year (for AY26-27 the qualifying dates are September 1, 2026 through August 31, 2027), and students must reapply each academic year

- We recommend that students who have the most financial need should apply early to secure the highest chances of funding being available

- Grants are not guaranteed and are disbursed as funding allows, with priority given to the students who demonstrate the highest financial need

- Applicants may apply for any or all of the qualifying costs mentioned above

- Financial support will be paid out via Payroll as a lump sum. Students who are tax-domiciled in the US should note that any payments paid out may be subject to tax withholdings

Other Qualifying Criteria

- Must be an enrolled NYUAD Global PhD or PASS PhD student and in good academic standing with no financial holds

- Visiting Graduate Students or Master's students are not eligible

- To be eligible for any support, the family member, or members, must be living in the UAE with the student. Eligible family members are: direct dependents or spouses

- Financial support cannot be claimed for any family members living outside the UAE

- Married and/or partnered PhD/graduate students should submit only one application. Funds are disbursed on a per-family (not per-student) basis

- A simple financial statement will need to be completed as part of the application to help justify need.

How to Apply

Students may apply through our online portal — Graduate Student Family Support Application

Application notes

- Students may apply for any or all qualifying costs.

- Students may apply to the fund multiple times per year, but will only receive up to the maximum amount in any academic year (USD 5,000) and only if the fund has remaining funds to be disbursed.

- Applications will be responded to within 30 days from submission of all documents via their NYU Email address. Payments will be made to successful applicants at the next possible payroll date. Please allow up to 60 days.

- A fresh application must be submitted to the Program each year for support; any successful applications from previous years are not an indication of support for future years.

Important: If students falsify information or provide misleading supporting documentation on the grant application form, the grant funds will be rescinded, and they will be referred to the Office of Student Conduct.

The GPPO recognizes that the scholarships and support offered to our graduate students may fall short of offering full financial support for students to have their spouses or family members accompany them for the full duration of their tenure at NYUAD. Hereby, the Graduate Student Family Support Program has been introduced to assist. This program is open to Global PhD Students and PASS PhD Students only.

The grants are funded and administered by the Graduate and Postdoctoral Programs Office. For the academic year 2026-2027, the grant program will have an open application cycle to support students with qualifying costs to access grant funds. Funding for this grant is limited, and grants will be disbursed as funding allows.

The program offers to offset the additional costs incurred by our Global PhD and PASS PhD students with families on a needs-based basis — it is not intended to cover all costs. Each family is eligible to apply for up to USD 5,000* total in needs-based support for any of the qualifying costs incurred during the current academic year (the current academic year is September 1, 2026 to August 31, 2027). Retrospective costs (i.e., Costs incurred in previous academic years) or future expected or estimated costs are not eligible. Grants are administered annually, and students must make a new application for each claim.

*The total amount any student can claim in one academic year, across all qualifying costs, is USD 5,000.

sections.title: Qualifying costs
sections.text:
Please review the following qualifying costs. The grant can only cover expenses that have been incurred during the current academic year . We cannot cover future expected or estimated costs or any expenses from previous academic years (no exceptions can be made):

- Direct costs associated with visa sponsorship or renewal (only applicable to UAE Sponsorship and UAE Visa issuance for spouses, partners, or dependent children)

Documentation required for support: Official receipts from UAE Government authorities/agencies showing expense; Credit card or debit card statements showing expense, copy of visa for spouse/partner or dependent children

- Direct costs associated with school fees (only applicable to school fees for dependent children aged between 3-18 registered in a school in the UAE)

Documentation required for support: Copy of Dependent Child Birth Certificate; Official receipts from an UAE Accredited School/Education Facility showing dependent children name(s) and enrollment; Credit card or debit card statements showing expense; Copy of visa for dependent children

- Direct costs associated with childcare - up to 25% of direct childcare costs may be claimed through the program (only applicable to dependent children under 3 and registered at a childcare facility in the UAE, or childcare costs provided through an official agency in the UAE)

Documentation required for support: Copy of Dependent Child Birth Certificate; Official receipts from UAE Government authorities/agencies showing expense (i.e., Tadbeer fees); Credit card or debit card statements showing expense; Copy of contract for childcare/nanny; In lieu of some or all of these documents, you may also provide a copy of the sponsorship letter for the domestic helper/nanny along with copies of their labor contract, confirming the name of the sponsor (which would normally be the name of the student), along with a signed confirmation of monthly salary from the domestic helper or nanny

- Direct costs associated with dependent health insurance (only applicable to spouses, partners, or dependent children who have an active UAE Visa and live in the Emirate of Abu Dhabi)

Documentation required for support: Official policy from Insurance Provider showing active policy with names of spouses/partner or dependent children; NYUAD paystub showing the expense has been debited from your salary; copy of visa for spouse, partner or dependent children

sections.title: Financial Support offered by the Grant
sections.text:
The program offers to offset the additional costs incurred by our Global PhD Students with families on a needs-based basis — it is not intended to cover all costs. Each family is eligible to apply for up to USD 5,000 total in needs-based support for any of the qualifying costs incurred during the current academic year (the current academic year is September 1, 2026 to August 31, 2027).

- Retrospective costs (i.e., costs incurred in previous academic years) or future expected or estimated costs are not eligible

- Grants are awarded annually during the academic year (for AY26-27 the qualifying dates are September 1, 2026 through August 31, 2027), and students must reapply each academic year

- We recommend that students who have the most financial need should apply early to secure the highest chances of funding being available

- Grants are not guaranteed and are disbursed as funding allows, with priority given to the students who demonstrate the highest financial need

- Applicants may apply for any or all of the qualifying costs mentioned above

- Financial support will be paid out via Payroll as a lump sum. Students who are tax-domiciled in the US should note that any payments paid out may be subject to tax withholdings

sections.title: Other Qualifying Criteria
sections.text:
- Must be an enrolled NYUAD Global PhD or PASS PhD student and in good academic standing with no financial holds

- Visiting Graduate Students or Master's students are not eligible

- To be eligible for any support, the family member, or members, must be living in the UAE with the student. Eligible family members are: direct dependents or spouses

- Financial support cannot be claimed for any family members living outside the UAE

- Married and/or partnered PhD/graduate students should submit only one application. Funds are disbursed on a per-family (not per-student) basis

- A simple financial statement will need to be completed as part of the application to help justify need.

sections.title: How to Apply
sections.text: Students may apply through our online portal — Graduate Student Family Support Application

sections.title: Application notes
sections.text:
- Students may apply for any or all qualifying costs.

- Students may apply to the fund multiple times per year, but will only receive up to the maximum amount in any academic year (USD 5,000) and only if the fund has remaining funds to be disbursed.

- Applications will be responded to within 30 days from submission of all documents via their NYU Email address. Payments will be made to successful applicants at the next possible payroll date. Please allow up to 60 days.

- A fresh application must be submitted to the Program each year for support; any successful applications from previous years are not an indication of support for future years.

Important: If students falsify information or provide misleading supporting documentation on the grant application form, the grant funds will be rescinded, and they will be referred to the Office of Student Conduct.

title: Off-Campus Housing Allowance · NYUAD Students
text:
Graduate Students registered in a PhD program at NYUAD may avail housing allowance for off-campus accommodation, subject to qualifying criteria.

The Tawtheeq or Rental Agreement must be in the Graduate Students name to be eligible for the housing allowance.

- Who is eligible for this program?

Graduate students are eligible to apply for this program when the following conditions are met:

- They are enrolled in a PhD program and are in good standing

- They have a family size (Family is defined as the Graduate Student + Spouse/Partner + Children) that has outgrown the capacity of our on-campus apartments in A3-A4.

- The Family must have 3 children or more, or , 2 children of the opposite gender , with at least 1 of the children being aged 10 or over.

Important: Graduate students who have a spouse or partner who is an employee of NYUAD and are in receipt of a housing allowance are not eligible for support from this program.

- What amounts, if I am eligible, may I receive?

The amount of housing allowance offered via the program is flat-rate regardless of family size. The program will provide an allowance of 64 ,800AED per year per student for off-campus housing. This allowance is paid monthly (5,400.00AED per month) over a 12 month period via payroll.

80:20 Split Minimum

The allowance provided to graduate students must be used towards rent at an 80:20 split. This means that students must secure housing off campus that costs a minimum of 51,840AED per year (evidence will be provided via Tawtheeq or their rental agreement) including municipality fee costs (5% of your annual rent)

The remainder of the allowance (“the 20%”) can be used for other costs such as security deposits (either housing or utilities), commission fees or utility bills, etc.

A copy of Tawtheeq/rental agreement must be submitted to the GPPO confirming rental + municipality fees are at least 80% of the allowance per year. If rental and municipality fees is not at least 80% of the allowance (“51,840AED or more per year”), then the housing allowance will be cancelled and the student will be expected to return to their on-campus apartment.

The Tawtheeq or Rental Agreement must be in the Graduate Students name to be eligible for the housing allowance.

Eligible Dates

Students who are successful in the program will move off campus on, or before, September 1st 2026. Allowances will be active between September 1st, 2026 through August 31st, 2027. Allowances, on an exceptional basis, may begin before September 1st, 2026, subject to budgetary approval.

The end date of the allowance for any fiscal year will typically be 1 year from the date of the allowance being awarded or the end date stated in the applicant's fellowship appointment letter (GRA Contract), whichever comes first . It is typically not the end date listed in a lease agreement.

Graduate students may opt to receive some of, or all of, their allowance via a lump-sum rental payment advance in-line with the current HR housing-advance guidelines .

Graduate students must reapply for the housing allowance annually. A previous award is not a guarantee of a future award.

- When do I need to move off campus?

Students who are successful in the program will move off campus on, or before, September 1st 2026. Allowances will be active between September 1st, 2026 through August 31st, 2027. Allowances, on an exceptional basis, may begin before September 1st, 2026 subject to budgetary approval.

- Will there be any Exceptions to the Qualifying Criteria for those without Families?

Effective going forward, eligibility will be limited strictly to families whose size exceeds what can reasonably be accommodated in a two-bedroom campus apartment. For clarity, this means families with three or more children or families with 2 children of the opposite gender , with at least 1 of the children being aged 10 or over, as a two-bedroom unit can comfortably house a family of four.

Other factors — including wellbeing concerns, commuting considerations, or prior eligibility categories that were used in past formats of the program — will not qualify a student for this benefit. Students on campus with these concerns may approach the MOSES center or the Office of Equal Opportunity for workplace, or living, modifications or accommodations.

- If I qualify, how do I apply?

Graduate Students who believe they qualify for this program should email nyuad.graduateoffice@nyu.edu for more information.

- Off-Campus Support

The GPPO is limited in the support it can provide to graduate students who live off campus. Some best practices that should be adopted by graduate students who move off campus are:

- Keep your emergency contact and current address and contact information up to date on WorkDay

- Make sure you are registered on the RAVE Alert system

- Sign up for SAFE NYU and download the app

- Make sure that your housing has a Tawtheeq registered to the individual graduate student to be protected.

- Report any unsafe conditions or violations to our office who can help triage through local government platforms to have the situation resolved.

- What if I am already benefiting from this Program and living off-campus?

Students who are currently participating in the program will be grandfathered and may remain off campus through completion of their PhD, provided they remain in good standing. We are honoring existing commitments. You will be contacted by the GPPO team in Spring Semester to confirm if you are extending your off-campus arrangements.

- Overpayments

In the unlikely scenario that a graduate student receives an overpayment, Guided by Article 25 in the Federal Decree No. 33 of 2021, overpayments can be recovered from the monthly payroll, provided that the deducted amount does not exceed 20% of the total wage.

- Questions?

For any further questions, please contact Aysha Al Dhaheri at nyuad.graduateoffice@nyu.edu .

title: Global PhD Taxes · NYUAD Students
text:
For NYUAD Students on the Global PhD Program, you will spend up to 2 years in New York. During this period, you will have to navigate the US Tax System. We have put together this page to provide you with help and guidance.

The information provided is only a guidance and is not a substitute for professional tax counseling or for referring to the Internal Revenue Service (IRS) publications. Please consult with a qualified US Tax Professional individual for more detailed information concerning applicable tax policies and regulations. NYUAD is unable to provide specific tax advice to individuals.

We encourage you to check out the very helpful NYU Tax Advice which is often more up to date.

NYUAD has also put together this helpful PDF Download that has lots of questions and answers related to tax filing. Please review this fully for any Q&A.

- Obtaining your Social Security Number

A Social Security Number (SSN) is a unique, 9-digit number used for taxpayer identification, income reporting, and record-keeping purposes. Once issued, the number is valid for a lifetime. You should keep it safe and provide only as needed to US government agencies or credible financial institutions.

All Global PhD students need to obtain an SSN and start the process for obtaining one as soon as they arrive in the US. The Internal Revenue Service requires employers to use the SSN to report your wages and tax withholdings on the W2 issued in January of the year following the tax year. Hence, it is imperative that the SSN is obtained latest by Dec 15 of each year.

Please email Deidre Tabak, Assistant Director of Business Operations & HR at deirdre.tabak@nyu.edu to obtain the employment letter required to apply for the SSN. Dede will then guide you through the rest of the process.

You may find the NYU SSN Webpage a helpful source of information.

- Is my income subject to Tax Withholdings while in the US?

Yes.

During your full year (or any subsequent years) in the US your stipend, and any additional allowances, such as housing, family support etc. will be subject to US tax withholdings. The current rate of tax withholdings in the US is 12% Federal and between 3%-12% for NY State.

Once you relocate permanently back to Abu Dhabi, you should inform Flora Rajpurohit, fr37@nyu.edu so that your tax withholdings are stopped.

- Who at NYUAD can help me if I have Tax Related Questions?

Flora Rajpurohit, Assistant Director, Payroll Tax Services can provide you with guidance on any questions you may have related to US Taxation. You may contact Flora by email, fr37@nyu.edu

- What is NYU Glacier?

Glacier is a secure online system used for Nonresident Alien tax compliance.

It helps determine tax residency, withholding rates and income tax treaty eligibility for international students. NYU uses Glacier to ensure correct tax payment for their international students.

Please ensure you complete the Glacier submission as soon as you arrive in the US and for every tax year after that you spend in the US.
You need to download the forms generated by Glacier and email them to Flora at fr37@nyu.edu
This is necessary to ensure the correct tax withholdings are applied to your pay.

To set up a Glacier account, please email Deidre Tabak, Assistant Director of Business Operations & HR at deirdre.tabak@nyu.edu .

For a tutorial on how Glacier works, please go to the PDF for Glacier here .

You can access Glacier by going to https://www.online-tax.net/

- Do international students have to file a tax return?

Most F-1 students are considered nonresident aliens by the IRS.

If you received US-sourced income during the calendar year then you will need to file Form 8843 and Form 1040NR (federal tax return) to assess your federal income and taxes.

If you are a nonresident tax filer, and have NO U.S. source income you only need complete the IRS Form 8843 to fulfill your federal tax filing obligation by the filing deadline.

You may also be required to file a state tax return, depending on the state.

The below link contains information on how to identify US sourced income:

https://www.irs.gov/individuals/international-taxpayers/nonresident-aliens-source-of-income

- What is a Form 8843 and Who Must File One?

Form 8843 is not a U.S. income tax return. It is an informational statement required by the IRS for certain nonresident aliens who are in the US on F-1, J-1, F-2 or J-2 visas for tax purposes. It should be filled out for every nonresident present in the U.S. for the previous year, including spouses, partners, and children.

The instructions for completing Form 8843 can be found on page 3 and 4 of IRS form 8843 .

- Who can help me with my international student tax return and cover the costs?

Sprintax is the nonresident partner of choice and the only online federal and state self-prep tax software for nonresidents in the US.

By creating a Sprintax account you can easily prepare fully completed and compliant 1040NR (nonresident tax return) and form 8843 tax documents.

Create your Sprintax account with the link provided below. It is created specifically for NYU international students and scholars. By setting up your account through this link, NYU will cover the costs of the federal tax return, state tax return, and 8843, meaning no cost to you. Open your new Sprintax account by creating a User ID and password, or if you have an existing account on Sprintax, you can log in using your existing credentials.

NYU Sprintax Portal

Be sure to use the Sprintax codes we emailed to you when being prompted for any payment (search your NYU email for Need to Know: Tax). This way, you will be able to use the service for free. Contact us if don't have the Sprintax codes.

- Consequences of Not Filing Your Tax Forms

Penalties for not complying with the filing requirement can include but are not limited to:

- Denials of future requests for a Change of Status (especially to Permanent Resident)

- Denials of visa renewals at American Consulates/Embassies

- Fines and interest will accrue on unreported income and could result in more money being owed to the IRS in the future

- If filed more than 3 years late, a refund will not be remitted by the IRS to the taxpayer

If you don't file your tax forms with the IRS by the tax deadline, or need to correct a mistake, you may be able to submit an amended tax return or mail the necessary tax documents even after the deadline date.

Consult with a tax professional for assistance if you need to adjust a previously filed tax return.

- What documents do I need to complete my tax return?

You may not have or need some of these; this is a list of all documents you might need:

- Passport, Visa, I-94 record

- Exit and Entry Dates for all past US visits

- I-20, DS-2019, I-797, or other US immigration documents

- Social Security Number (if you don't have a Social Security Number, you may need an Individual Tax Identification Number, Sprintax will determine if this is the case, and if so, you will be prompted to fill out a Form W-7)

- Current US Address AND Permanent Foreign Address

- Name of Educational Institution or Sponsoring Organization

- All relevant tax form(s) for taxable purposes: Form(s) W-2, 1042-S, or 1099 as applicable
Scholarship or Fellowship grant letters (if no related Form 1042-S)

- Copy of past year’s tax forms (if you had any)

-
If you have more questions related to Taxes,

Look to our Tax Frequently Asked Questions page to find the answers to any of your lingering questions.

You can also find some Sprintax resources below to help explain the US tax system for nonresident international students and scholars:

- Sprintax F-1 International Student US Tax Guide and Blog

- Sprintax J-1 Visa Holder US Tax Guide and Blog

- Sprintax YouTube Channel

title: Graduate Events and Career Development · NYUAD Students
text:
The Graduate and Postdoctoral Programs Office, in cooperation with the Graduate Student Council, offers events throughout the year for Graduate students. Events range from social and wellbeing events, to professional development. Please keep an eye on this page for updates throughout the year.

Our events calendar is always the best way to see upcoming events and to sign up quickly.

You can access this using the link to your right, or by going here .

Early Career Researcher Mentoring Program

Hosted by Professor Emmanuel Tsekleves, Professor in Global Health Design Innovation at Lancaster University. The Early Career Researcher Mentoring Program is designed to provide comprehensive support and guidance to PhDs and postdocs pursuing academic and research careers.

The Early Career Researcher Mentoring Program is designed to provide comprehensive support and guidance to PhDs and postdocs pursuing academic and research careers. The program is designed to help with training Postdocs and PhD students with how to be successful in a career pathway in the Academy. Whether you want to become a professor, or stay in academic research, this program is for you. Our host Professor Emmanuel Tsekleves has mentored over 50 PhDs and postdocs, helping them find their footing, secure academic jobs, and flourish in faculty roles.

The program comprises a 5-days of mandatory in-person delivery (+2 additional optional days), complemented by offline materials and resources, 1:1 live Zoom sessions for 6 months following the program delivery, and asynchronous resources based on the 5P approach for accessibility by the entire postdoc/PhD student population at NYUAD.

You can find out more by going to the Early Career Researcher Mentoring Program page at https://students.nyuad.nyu.edu/graduate-students/nyuad-early-career-researcher-mentoring-program/

-

Resource Hub for Masters, PhD and Postdoctoral Scholars

We are pleased to share a dedicated resource hub designed to support Masters, PhD, and Postdoctoral scholars in navigating their professional and academic pathways. The Graduate Student Career Resources page curates essential tools, guides, and opportunities to help you:
• Explore diverse career pathways across academia, industry, and beyond.
• Prepare professional documents such as CVs, teaching and research statements, and fellowship applications.
• Connect with career events, networking sessions, and development programs.
Stay updated through the Wasserman Graduate Liaison Newsletter Tracker and the NYU Wasserman Events Calendar.

📍 Access the Resources: (Best accessed through your Desktop): Click Here

These resources are developed to help you make informed decisions and confidently take the next steps in your career journey. We encourage you to explore the page regularly as new tools and events are added each month.

-

Asynchronous Learning Content

- We provide access to many types of asynchronous online learning platforms free of charge.

-

- Versatile PhD

The Versatile Ph.D. is a web-based, socially positive business that helps universities provide graduate students with non-academic professional development. Our mission is to help graduate students and PhDs envision, prepare for, and excel in non-academic careers.

We want doctoral students to be informed about academic employment realities, educated about their non-academic career options, and supported in preparing for a wide range of careers so that in the end, they have choices. The key concept here is versatility: the ability to apply skills, abilities, and interests in various positions and fields.

https://versatilephd.com/

*Please note that if it is your first time signing into Versatile Ph.D., you will also need to register with your NYU email address

- 1:1 Writing Support from NYUAD for Graduate Students

GPPO is pleased to share with you that for Fall 2024 we have partnered with our Writing Center colleagues to provide 1:1 writing support.

The NYU Abu Dhabi Center for Writing provides support at any stage of the writing process. Our writing consultants are experienced readers and writers from multiple disciplines who work with you in one-on-one conferences to help develop any kind of written or oral material.

We are located in the GPPO suite C2 W212 meeting room W214.

To make an appointment go to nyuad.mywconline.com and select F 2024|Graduate Writing from the schedule drop-down menu.

- Imagine PhD

ImaginePhD is a free online career exploration and planning tool for PhD students and postdoctoral scholars in the humanities and social sciences.

Humanities and social sciences PhD students and their mentors have long recognized the need for more resources to help bridge the knowledge gap between doctoral education and the realm of career possibilities. ImaginePhD is designed to meet this need by allowing users to:

assess their career-related skills, interests, and values
explore careers paths appropriate to their disciplines
create self-defined goals
map out the next steps for career and professional development success

Go to ImaginePhD https://www.imaginephd.com

- myIDP

myIDP - a unique, web-based career-planning tool tailored to meet the needs of Ph.D. students and postdocs in the sciences.

myIDP provides:

Exercises to help you examine your skills, interests, and values
A list of 20 scientific career paths with a prediction of which ones best fit your skills and interests
A tool for setting strategic goals for the coming year, with optional reminders to keep you on track
Articles and resources to guide you through the process

Go to myIDP: https://myidp.sciencecareers.org/

- STEMPeers

STEMPeers TM is a 501(c)(3) organization registered in PA as PhD Career Support Group. The organization helps creates a growing network of STEM scientists that is involved in peer-to-peer mentoring and support.

STEMPeers has several online initiatives to its credit like Gurukool (A platform that helps people during job transitions via peer mentoring), ClubSciwri, The STEM times, MedNess, The Newsletter and Jidnyasa.

They have two annual conferences- Annual STEMPeers conference in USA and EuroSTEMPeers in Europe.

Go to STEMPeers: https://stempeers.org/

- Beyond the Professoriate - For Scholars interested in Non Academic and Academic Careers

Beyond the Professoriate is the only online professional development training platform for graduate students, postdocs, faculty, and PhDs that helps them successfully transition into academic or nonacademic careers. This research-driven platform is informed by nearly a decade of experience supporting PhDs to launch new careers with their skills and training.

Trusted by over 30 institutions (and growing), the platform helps grad students and PhDs leverage their education into meaningful careers, whether in academia or beyond the professoriate.

When logging in, choose 'New York University' as your Institution

Go to Beyond the Professoriate : http://institutions.beyondprof.com/

Related official links:
https://students.nyuad.nyu.edu/graduate-students/grad-events-and-career-development/graduate-student-calendar/
https://students.nyuad.nyu.edu/graduate-students/nyuad-early-career-researcher-mentoring-program/

AY26/27 Postgrad Lunch & Learn Series - October

GradSTEPS Workshop: Speaking with Impact - Advanced Communication Skills for Researchers and Professionals

Library C2 329

Introducing GradSTEPS (Skills Training for Employability and Professional Success), a program designed for graduate students and postdocs to enhance their skills and professional acumen. GradSTEPS offers tailored workshops, networking opportunities, and career resources, empowering participants to successfully transition to a rewarding career.

Tuesday 9th December

Speaking with Impact: Advanced Communication Skills for Researchers and Professionals

Communication and public speaking are among the most sought-after leadership skills for academic and career advancement, yet they are rarely taught with the same rigor as research methods themselves. This intensive, hands-on workshop equips researchers and academics to translate complex ideas for varied audiences, treating interpersonal communication not as a soft skill but as a gateway to career success, one that depends as much on emotional intelligence and self assurance as on technique.

Whether commanding a classroom, leading a meeting, or presenting at a conference, the ability to communicate with clarity and authority is what distinguishes a competent researcher from a compelling one. Participants will leave with concrete strategies for adapting their message across contexts, and a clearer sense of how communication skill shapes the next phase of their professional trajectory.

GradSTEPS Workshop: Mastering Academic Conferences: From Abstract Writing to Effective Delivery

Library C2 329

Introducing GradSTEPS (Skills Training for Employability and Professional Success), a program designed for graduate students and postdocs to enhance their skills and professional acumen. GradSTEPS offers tailored workshops, networking opportunities, and career resources, empowering participants to successfully transition to a rewarding career.

Wednesday 20th January

Mastering Academic Conferences: From Abstract Writing to Effective Delivery

This intensive, end-to-end workshop demystifies the academic conference circuit, equipping researchers to pitch their work with confidence and deliver presentations that leave a lasting impression. Moving beyond generic public-speaking advice, the session addresses the specific pressures of the conference environment: crafting an abstract that gets accepted, managing pre-conference anxiety, and staying composed under the scrutiny of a live audience.

Participants will work through practical strategies for handling difficult or hostile questions in Q&A, approaching networking as a skill rather than an ordeal, and reframing stage fright as a manageable part of scholarly performance rather than a personal failing. The workshop closes by situating the conference itself within a longer career arc — helping participants think strategically about how a single presentation can open doors to collaborations, visibility, and future opportunities.

By the end, participants will leave not just with tips, but with a working framework for approaching conferences as a recurring professional skill to be honed over a career, rather than a one-off hurdle to survive.

Thursday, January 21, 2027, 12-1:30pm

GradSTEPS Workshop: Finding Your Voice: Breath, Gravitas, and Instance

Library C2 329

Introducing GradSTEPS (Skills Training for Employability and Professional Success), a program designed for graduate students and postdocs to enhance their skills and professional acumen. GradSTEPS offers tailored workshops, networking opportunities, and career resources, empowering participants to successfully transition to a rewarding career.

Thursday 21st January, 12pm

Finding Your Voice: Breath, Gravitas, and Instance

A sixty-minute practical workshop on speaking with presence, adapted for an audience of researchers and PhD candidates. Participants work on four things: using the breath to control pace, using silence as punctuation, choosing tone deliberately, and replacing abstract claims with concrete instances. The session is built on practice rather than lecture. Participants record a thirty-second answer at the start, speak in three structured rounds in small pods, then record the same answer again at the end and compare the two. Nothing is assessed, scored, or shared.

Participants will leave able to:

- Control pace through the exhale instead of by effort

- Hold a pause long enough for a listener to absorb the point

- Move between warm, neutral, and weighted registers depending on what the moment needs

- Structure an answer as answer, reason, instance, then stop

- Turn a broad claim into one specific, true example

The practice prompts and question rounds will use research and career scenarios: explaining your work to a non-specialist, handling a sceptical question at a conference, and interview answers.

sections.text:
Library C2 329

Introducing GradSTEPS (Skills Training for Employability and Professional Success), a program designed for graduate students and postdocs to enhance their skills and professional acumen. GradSTEPS offers tailored workshops, networking opportunities, and career resources, empowering participants to successfully transition to a rewarding career.

Tuesday 9th December

Speaking with Impact: Advanced Communication Skills for Researchers and Professionals

Communication and public speaking are among the most sought-after leadership skills for academic and career advancement, yet they are rarely taught with the same rigor as research methods themselves. This intensive, hands-on workshop equips researchers and academics to translate complex ideas for varied audiences, treating interpersonal communication not as a soft skill but as a gateway to career success, one that depends as much on emotional intelligence and self assurance as on technique.

Whether commanding a classroom, leading a meeting, or presenting at a conference, the ability to communicate with clarity and authority is what distinguishes a competent researcher from a compelling one. Participants will leave with concrete strategies for adapting their message across contexts, and a clearer sense of how communication skill shapes the next phase of their professional trajectory.

sections.text:
Library C2 329

Introducing GradSTEPS (Skills Training for Employability and Professional Success), a program designed for graduate students and postdocs to enhance their skills and professional acumen. GradSTEPS offers tailored workshops, networking opportunities, and career resources, empowering participants to successfully transition to a rewarding career.

Wednesday 20th January

Mastering Academic Conferences: From Abstract Writing to Effective Delivery

This intensive, end-to-end workshop demystifies the academic conference circuit, equipping researchers to pitch their work with confidence and deliver presentations that leave a lasting impression. Moving beyond generic public-speaking advice, the session addresses the specific pressures of the conference environment: crafting an abstract that gets accepted, managing pre-conference anxiety, and staying composed under the scrutiny of a live audience.

Participants will work through practical strategies for handling difficult or hostile questions in Q&A, approaching networking as a skill rather than an ordeal, and reframing stage fright as a manageable part of scholarly performance rather than a personal failing. The workshop closes by situating the conference itself within a longer career arc — helping participants think strategically about how a single presentation can open doors to collaborations, visibility, and future opportunities.

By the end, participants will leave not just with tips, but with a working framework for approaching conferences as a recurring professional skill to be honed over a career, rather than a one-off hurdle to survive.

sections.title: The Postgrad Writers’ Room Fall 2026 · {{{title}}} · GradSTEPS Workshop: Finding Your Voice: Breath, Gravitas, and Instance
sections.text:
Library C2 329

Introducing GradSTEPS (Skills Training for Employability and Professional Success), a program designed for graduate students and postdocs to enhance their skills and professional acumen. GradSTEPS offers tailored workshops, networking opportunities, and career resources, empowering participants to successfully transition to a rewarding career.

Thursday 21st January, 12pm

Finding Your Voice: Breath, Gravitas, and Instance

A sixty-minute practical workshop on speaking with presence, adapted for an audience of researchers and PhD candidates. Participants work on four things: using the breath to control pace, using silence as punctuation, choosing tone deliberately, and replacing abstract claims with concrete instances. The session is built on practice rather than lecture. Participants record a thirty-second answer at the start, speak in three structured rounds in small pods, then record the same answer again at the end and compare the two. Nothing is assessed, scored, or shared.

Participants will leave able to:

- Control pace through the exhale instead of by effort

- Hold a pause long enough for a listener to absorb the point

- Move between warm, neutral, and weighted registers depending on what the moment needs

- Structure an answer as answer, reason, instance, then stop

- Turn a broad claim into one specific, true example

The practice prompts and question rounds will use research and career scenarios: explaining your work to a non-specialist, handling a sceptical question at a conference, and interview answers.

title: Graduate Life · NYUAD Students
text:

- Graduate Housing (A3/A4 Graduate Student Residences)

The graduate residences at NYU Abu Dhabi are furnished apartments in buildings A3 and A4, which are both co-ed. These residences include studio, one bedroom, and two bedroom apartments. The A3/A4 community is currently home to a mixed group of researchers, postdocs, and graduate students, and their families in some cases.

Graduate students who share a two-bedroom apartment are assigned same-sex roommates, but each student has their own separate bedroom and bathroom, while sharing the unit’s kitchen and lounge space.

Smoking is not permitted anywhere on campus, including in the A3/A4 residences, and this is strictly enforced. Pets are not allowed in A3/A4. Undergraduate students are not permitted to access A3-A4 unless prior approval is received from the GPPO.

Apartment Furnishings

Each apartment is fully furnished to ease students’ transition to Abu Dhabi. Furnishings differ slightly based on apartment size but generally include bed(s), bedside tables, a desk, chairs or couches, and a kitchen table if space permits. Standard kitchen appliances include a two-burner stove, oven, microwave, fridge with freezer, and up to four place settings. A set of linens and basic cookware is included. High-speed wireless internet, access to cable television service, and utilities are provided at no additional cost.

Provided furnishings generally may not be removed from the units.

Building Facilities

Each building has shared laundry facilities on the second level. (Washers and dryers may not be installed in individual apartments). The second level of each building also has lounge space and a multipurpose room for residents. The lounge is fully furnished including kitchen facilities, a television, games console, board games, coffee machine, foosball table, and wireless speakers.

Graduate RAs

For AY2024-25, we are excited to announce that we will have Graduate Resident Assistants assigned to help with community and social programming in the A3 and A4 Graduate Student Residences. More information will be posted on the Notice Boards located on the second floor in each building.

- A3 Graduate RA: Nour Elbery, nae7100@nyu.edu | MFA Class of 2026
- A4 Graduate RA: Terry Chen, tc3185@nyu.edu | MSc Econ Class of 2025

You should feel free to reach out to Nour or Terry during your stay on campus.

Visitor Policy

To register a guest to access the A3-A4 Graduate Student residences, please fill out the JRNY registration form available at https://nyuad.identigy.io/admin/goldmenu.php

Graduate students at NYU Abu Dhabi are subject to all relevant sections of the Student Conduct Policy .

The Career Development Center (CDC) is here to guide you towards achieving your future goals. Our team of advisors are dedicated to helping you find your career path and prepare for life after NYUAD.

Graduate Students can benefit from working alongside the NYU Abu Dhabi Career Development Center.

To find out more about the CDC and their resources, please go to https://students.nyuad.nyu.edu/student-affairs/career-development/

NYUAD has an on campus health center that provides services related to medical needs, counseling, dietitation, immunisations, sexual health and other medical related inquiries. To find out more go to https://students.nyuad.nyu.edu/student-affairs/health-center/ .

Student Success supports students with academic and personal coaching to help students thrive at NYUAD. To find out more about the services available please go to https://students.nyuad.nyu.edu/student-affairs/student-success-well-being/academic-and-personal-coaching/

The Wellness Exchange is your key to accessing NYU's exclusive health and mental health resources.

This private, 24/7 hotline puts you in touch with professionals who can help address your day-to-day challenges, as well as other health-related concerns.

To speak to a certified counselor for immediate support, the Wellness Exchange is available 24/7 at +971 2 628 5555 (85555 from campus) or via NYU Wellness Exchange App, available for Android & iPhone.

To find out more go to https://www.nyu.edu/students/health-and-wellness/wellness-exchange.html

- Student Conduct

Student Conduct at NYUAD supports the maintenance of a safe, accountable, and inclusive community. NYUAD is committed to providing education on the rights and responsibilities of communal membership and the development of individual students. To find out more about the Student Code of Conduct for NYUAD please go to https://www.nyu.edu/about/policies-guidelines-compliance/policies-and-guidelines/university-student-conduct-policy.html

The Graduate Student Council (GSC) is the voice of graduate students at NYUAD, representing their interests and ensuring their rights. The GSC also helps run events through the academic year for graduate students, enabling a sense of community and belonging for all graduate students who commute to, or live on, campus. To get in touch with the GSC please email nyuad.gradccl@nyu.edu .

title: NYUAD Early Career Researcher Mentoring Program · NYUAD Students
text:
Hosted by Professor Emmanuel Tsekleves , Professor in Global Health Design Innovation at Lancaster University. The Early Career Researcher Mentoring Program is designed to provide comprehensive support and guidance to PhDs and postdocs pursuing academic and research careers.

Apply for Program

Applications are now open for the 2027 cohort. You can apply by going to https://forms.gle/9ctsiL91haUKbqYH9 and the closing date is November 15th.

The Program

The Early Career Researcher Mentoring Program is designed to provide comprehensive support and guidance to PhDs and postdocs pursuing academic and research careers. The program is designed to help with training Postdocs and PhD students with how to be successful in a career pathway in the Academy. Whether you want to become a professor, or stay in academic research, this program is for you. Our host Professor Emmanuel Tsekleves has mentored over 60 PhDs and postdocs, helping them find their footing, secure academic jobs, and flourish in faculty roles.

The programme comprises pre-workshop preparation, a 5-day in-person intensive (25-29 January 2027), and reviewed virtual 1:1 consultations two weeks later, all structured around the proven 6P approach (Profile, Prestige, Papers, Projects, People, and Pedagogy). This framework addresses the multifaceted needs of emerging scholars, equipping them with the essential skills, knowledge, and strategies required for navigating the academic landscape, securing funding, publishing impactful research, building professional networks, establishing a strong academic identity, and demonstrating teaching excellence.

The program includes a combination of presentations, training sessions, group and individual mentoring sessions, workshops, mock interviews, and practical activities, providing a wellrounded and immersive learning experience tailored for highly motivated researchers ready to accelerate their academic careers.

Outcomes

- Researcher Confidence & Independence: Trainees will develop advanced skills to take ownership of their research, conduct independent research, and make strategic decisions about career advancement.

- Researcher Identity & Branding: Trainees will master their identity as researchers in their discipline and develop sophisticated academic brands and online presence.

- Research Communication & Networking: Trainees will learn elite strategies for communicating their research and building strategic professional relationships.

- Grant Writing Excellence: Trainees will acquire advanced knowledge and techniques for identifying funding opportunities, understanding review processes, and crafting winning grant proposals.

- Research Publication Mastery: Trainees will develop sophisticated approaches to writing, positioning, and publishing high-impact research articles.

- Teaching Excellence & Career Navigation: Trainees will master teaching portfolio development and learn advanced strategies for navigating academic career paths and job applications.

Asynchronous Resources

For those of you who were not able to attend the program, or want to refresh the content that was covered, we are happy to offer resources in both video and offline materials formats. The program has created asynchronous content to allow you to learn at a time of your choice, and to refer back to the content shared by Professor Tsekleves.

title: Services · NYUAD Students
text:
- From where to Eat on campus, and how to find discounts - there are a number of services available to you when a student at NYUAD

-

- Campus Dining

To find out about places to eat, menus for the week ahead, what is open, and how to get food delivered during evenings and nights, head to https://students.nyuad.nyu.edu/services/dining/

- Graduate Student Meal Plan

NYUAD offers a Graduate Student Meal Plan. This meal plan is available to all Graduate Students at NYUAD enrolled in either the Global PhD Program, or our MFA or MSc Masters Programs. The Meal Plan is only available for dining at the Abu Dhabi campus. Details on the plan, and how to buy it, are outlined below

-
What is the meal Plan?

Once purchased, the meal plan allows you to use 20 meal swipes that can be used on campus at our main dining outlets - Dining Hall East/West (D1 & D2).

- What is included with 1 meal swipe?

Any combination of items from the dining hall counters of your liking that produces a “meal” combo for the price/ value of AED31.50. Set combos are available from each counter but items may be mixed and matched from different counters also. You can ask any member of staff in the Dining Areas if you have any questions.

- Where can I use the meal swipes?

You can use meal swipes at our Abu Dhabi campus in Dining Hall East or West (D1/D2).

- How much time do I have to use my meal swipes?

Your meal swipes will be valid for the current academic year only (so any plans purchased from August 2021 will expire August 31st, 2022). Any unused meal swipes will be lost if not used, no carryovers are possible, and no refunds are issued once purchased.

- What is the cost of the meal plan?

The cost of 20 swipes is $163 + 5% VAT ($171.15). This charge will be added to your Student Billing Account once processed. No refunds are offered for unused swipes.

If you are a Global PhD student, your benefits package does not cover the cost of the meal plan.For any questions on how to pay for your meal plan, or how to pay off an outstanding balance on your student account, email nyuad.studentfinance@nyu.edu .

- How students use a swipe?

Your NYU ID card will be loaded with swipes which may be used at the cash register as payment at the Abu Dhabi outlets mentioned above. Literally a “swipe” with the ADNH cashier.

- How do I check my balance?

You can go to https://mealplans.nyu.edu/ .

- How do I sign up?

You can sign up to the meal Plan by filling out the Graduate Student Meal Plan Sign Up form. Once you sign up, your meal plan will be activated within 48 hours.

- Student Finance

For all questions on Student Finance such as how to pay your bill, how to access your billing account, or questions related to your financial award, please go to the Student Finance webpage at https://students.nyuad.nyu.edu/services/financial-services/

- Maps & Facilities

Find your way around campus with our Maps and Floor Plans, Reserve a space using the Space Reservation System, and find information on Opening Hours by going to https://students.nyuad.nyu.edu/services/campus-maps-facilities/

- Students with Disabilities

We encourage students to participate fully in all aspects of life at NYUAD. The Office of the Dean of Students works in close partnership with the Moses Center for Students Accessibility in New York to provide reasonable and appropriate accommodations for students with documented disabilities while here at NYUAD. To find out more about the services offered, please go to https://students.nyuad.nyu.edu/services/students-with-disabilities/

- Technology and IT Support

NYUAD Technology Group is NYUAD's central source for computer, network, telephone, and Internet services and works in conjunction with the central NYU ITS services in New York City to provide technical support for the whole NYUAD community.NYUAD Technology Group provides access to a variety of services and technology on campus. To find out more go to https://students.nyuad.nyu.edu/services/technology-and-support/

- Discounts with your Student/NYUAD ID

Your NYUAD ID card provides discounts and offers at various merchants and locations across the UAE - please visit https://students.nyuad.nyu.edu/services/promotions-and-discounts/ for more details

title: About Bookmarks · NYUAD Students
text:
The customizable Bookmarks menu gives you an easy way to navigate to the pages on the Portal you frequently visit. This new feature allows you to customize your menu by adding, deleting or re-ordering your favorite Portal pages.

Using the Bookmarks Menu

Where can I find the Bookmarks menu?
How do I add a Bookmarks?
How do I edit my Bookmarks list?
How do I delete a link I don't want?
How do I re-order the links?
Why can't I delete some of the links?
Why can't I add more than 15 links in my menu?

Where can I find the Bookmarks menu?
You can find the Bookmarks dropdown menu in the top menu bar of every page in the Portal.

Simply click the "Bookmarks" link and a dropdown menu will appear, displaying the list of links. We have added some default links into the list to get you started.

Back to top

How do I add a Bookmarks?
When you are viewing a page in the Portal that you'd like to add to your Bookmarks menu, simply click the star icon in the top menu bar of that page.

When you click the star icon, it will switch from white to yellow, and a message confirming the addition to your Bookmarks menu will display. Note: Any page in the Portal that has this yellow star, is a page that has been added into your Bookmarks menu.

Tip: To quickly remove this page from your Bookmarks menu, simply click the yellow star icon and a message confirming the removal will appear. When the removal is complete, the star icon will return to a white color.

Back to top

How do I edit my Bookmarks list?
When the Bookmarks dropdown menu is open, a link labelled "Edit Bookmarks" will be displayed at the bottom of the list of links.

When you click on "Edit Bookmarks," the delete and re-order icons should appear to the left and right of the links. These icons only appear when the dropdown menu is in edit mode.

Note: When the dropdown menu is in edit mode, use the "Cancel" link to cancel your changes or the "Save" link to save your changes. Clicking cancel or save will also take you out of edit mode.

Back to top

How do I delete a link I don't want?
There are two ways to delete a link from your Bookmarks menu.

1) When in edit mode, click the delete icon to the left of the link you want to remove.

If you delete the wrong link, click the "Undo" to the right of the deleted link or click the "Cancel" at the bottom of the menu.

2) In the same way you click the white star icon to add the link to your Bookmarks menu, click the yellow star icon to delete the link. Note: If a page has a yellow star icon instead of a white star icon, then this page is currently in your Bookmarks menu.

A message confirming the removal of the link from your Bookmarks menu will appear. Note: There is no "undo delete" when a page is removed this way.

When the removal is complete, the star icon will return to a white color.

Back to top

How do I re-order the links?
In edit mode, you will see a move icons to the right of the links.

Click the move icon, hold, drag and release.

Note: Remember to click save when you finish re-ordering your links.

Back to top

Why can't I delete some of the links?
Currently we can not add external links into the Bookmarks menu, only pages within the Portal can be added.

Based on user patterns and analytics, we have added the most popular external links into the menu and at this time they can not be removed or re-ordered.

Back to top

Why can't I add more than 15 links in my menu?
In order to fit the most common screen resolution without having to scroll to view the links, we have currently limited the number of links to 15. If you have reached 15 links in your menu and try to add an additional link, a maximum limit message will display.

Back to top

title: Bookstore · NYUAD Students
text:
What's In-Store?

NYUAD-branded merchandise, Etisalat and DU recharge cards, class material and supplies. A wide variety of fiction, non-fiction, and children's books, as well as textbooks, are also available for purchase.

Personal Local Mail and International Courier Service

The bookstore provides personal local mail and international courier services to students, faculty, and staff.

Textbook Return Program

To help you declutter and support affordable learning, we're launching a textbook return program. At the end of each term, you can conveniently drop off your unwanted textbooks in designated bins located across campus. These book bins are situated in the C2 and A6 lobby , as well as the following student lounges:

- A1-A and A1-C

- A2-A and A2-C

- A5-A and A5-C

- A6-A and A6-C

The bookstore will regularly collect these textbooks, sort them, and assess their condition for potential reuse in the following term, ensuring we're well-prepared for the upcoming semester. This is a good opportunity to free up space in your room and contribute to a more sustainable learning environment. Please remember to only place textbooks in the bins, and be aware that the bookstore will evaluate the books for reuse based on their condition.

title: Noon Lockers · NYUAD Students
text:
Noon lockers are available on campus for use by the NYUAD community and surrounding residential communities.

- Lockers are storage solutions that allow you to self-collect packages through a unique PIN.

- You can pick up your packages at a time that suits you, 24/7.

- Your packages will be stored safely in the lockers until you're ready to collect them, ensuring that they remain secure and protected.

- Your packages will be available for pickup for 5 days after the day of delivery. If your packages are not picked up in this timeframe, it will be returned to noon.

If you have any questions or need assistance, please contact nyuad.logistics@nyu.edu .

Share your feedback with noon at lockers@noon.com .

Location

The noon lockers can be found under the outdoor staircase between the Campus Center (C2) and The Arts Center (C3), next to Public Lift 3.

How It Works

Shopping

- Shop as usual on the noon app or website.

- At checkout, select the option to deliver to a noon locker.

- Choose the locker location on campus.

Collection

- Wait to receive your unique PIN via SMS and/or e-mail.

- Go to the locker location selected as indicated in the SMS or e-mail (within 5 days).

- Enter your PIN on the locker's screen.
There is only one possible place to enter the PIN - on the sole locker touchscreen. This can be done through the physical keyboard or the on-screen keyboard. If your PIN did not work, please call the noon customer service at 800-38888 immediately. Noon will try to resolve the issue as soon as possible.

Returns

You can return your packages using noon’s standard returns process. Raise a request through the noon app or website using an existing address. However, as of now, returning packages through noon lockers isn't possible.

If you used noon wallet credits to pay for the items the amount shall be funded as noon wallet credits within 24 hours.

If you used your card to pay for the items and your account refund preference is set to card refund, the amount shall be refunded to your card within 48 hours. The amount may take up to 14 business days to reflect in your bank account, depending upon the issuing bank. However, if you used a combination of card and noon wallet credits to pay for the items the amounts would be refunded to their respective payment source.

title: Numbering System · NYUAD Students
text:
A Guide to the Campus Numbering System

The campus is organized along a main street. On its south side are the A blocks, six triangular buildings that are numbered one through six from west to east. The north side includes the research building, campus center, arts center, and faculty residences.

The majority of classrooms are on the ground floors of buildings A1-A6, on the south side of the main street, with another 12 classrooms on the ground floor of C2, the Campus Center, on the north. Classes are not assigned to buildings by discipline. Humanities, Social Science, and Science classes could be in any of these buildings.

Faculty offices are organized by division. Most are on the first floors of buildings A1-A6, C1, C3 and C2 few offices in Level 2 and Level 3.

The principal buildings on campus have received the following names:

- A1 is the STEM Building.

- A2 is the Computational Building.

- A3 is the West Administration Building.

- A4 is the East Administration Building.

- A5 is the Social Science Building.

- A6 is the Humanities Building / NYUAD Institute.

- C1 is the Experimental Research Building.

- C2 is the Campus Center.

- C3 is the Arts Center.

The numbering system has two parts. The first part is the building (A2, for example) and the second part is a three- or four-digit room number (018, for instance). The first number in the second part of the numbering sequence tells you the floor. For example, if the room number begins with 0, it is on the ground floor. If it begins with 1, the room is on the first floor, and so on. Offices have odd numbers and workstations have even numbers. Each row of workstations has a number and each desk has a letter, for example 102A, 102B, etc.

Familiarization with the numbering system and sequence can tell you a lot about the office, classroom, or desk space you will be looking for:

- A2 018: This is a classroom in building A2 on the ground floor.

- A2 101: This is an office in building A2 on the first floor.

- A5 1109: This is an office in building A5 on the first floor.

- A5 1120A: This is a desk in a workstation in building A5 on the first floor.

Access to the student residences in A2, A5, and A6 is through the campus' second level, called the High Line. Each residence area comprises three buildings oriented around a quad or courtyard (for example, A2-A, A2-B, and A2-C, or A5-A, A5-B, and A5-C). In these residential buildings, each room has a three-digit number. The floor is indicated by the first digit, thus, 323 is on the third floor. Over time the residences may be named, but for now we are using this alpha-numerical system.

The Campus Center (building C2) contains the pool (Basement 1–Ground Level), the Gym (Levels 1-2), and the Library (Levels 3-4). Each two-story space is located in the middle of the Center. The offices in C2 are organized around these large volumes on every floor.

East, West, and North have been added to the room numbers to help orientation. For example, the Health and Wellness Center is C2 West 012 and Global Education is C2 West 204. There are two multipurpose rooms on the ground floor of the Campus Center; to the left upon entering is the West Forum, and to the right is the East Forum. The Academic Resource Center is C2 3101.

Here's a snapshot of what's in the Campus Center.

Basement 1 | Pool

Ground Floor | Health and Wellness Center, Registrar, Service Center, Dean of Students, IT Support, Classrooms

Level 1 | Gym, Fitness Room, Women's Gym, and other athletic facilities

Level 2 (High Line) | Marketplace, Global Education, Human Resources, Sheikh Mohamed Scholars Program, Admission

Level 3 | Library, Library Cafe, Academic Resource Center

title: Space Reservation Request · NYUAD Students
text:
Booking a Space on Campus

Students are able to request the C ampus Center Forums, large Conference Center spaces, specialized Arts Center rooms, lobby, lounges, and outdoor spaces via the EMS Space Reservation System .

You should fill out the form at least seven working days in advance of your event and allow at least two working days to receive a reservation confirmation. Please refer to the Space Guide for more details on location, capacity, and layout of each space.

For any other questions, please reach out to the Space Reservation team at nyuad.spacereservation@nyu.edu

Related official links:
https://students.nyuad.nyu.edu/services/campus-maps-facilities/space-reservation-request/space-guide/

title: Space Guide · NYUAD Students
text:
Campus Center (C2)

West Forum
This is the largest open, flexible space in the NYUAD Campus Center and is suitable for events hosting up to 200 people. The room is also equipped with two projectors, as well as with a sound system and wireless microphone capabilities.

East Forum
Similar to the West Forum, the East Forum is an open, flexible space in the Campus Center and is suitable for events hosting approximately 130 people. The room is also equipped with two projectors, a large screen, a sound system and wireless microphone capabilities.

Arts Center (C3)

*For Screening Room, Music Practice Rooms, and Rehearsal Studios inquiries contact nyuad.artspace@nyu.edu .

The Arts Center Main Lobby Area (C3)
1,000 square meter foyer available for pre-post performance receptions as an extension of ongoing events in The Arts Center building.

Black Box (001)
Formerly the Black Box Theater, the Black Box is a flexible, 333 square meter space with capacity of up to 150 audience members suitable for music, dance, theatre, and multi-disciplinary performances in a wide range of configurations. A portable sprung wood floor with marley is available on request.

Red Theater (002)
Formerly the Main Performance Theater, the Red Theater is a 700-seater theater suitable for music, dance, theater, and film. The Red Theater has a 550-square-meter stage and a 448-square-meter auditorium. With an adjustable 13- to 18-meter proscenium arch, 21-meter fly tower, serapid lift orchestra pit/fore-stage, adjustable acoustic panels, portable sprung wood floor with marley available (on request), digital projection and 35mm projector, full lighting and PA.

Blue Hall (003)
Formerly the Music Recital Hall, the Blue Hall has a 150-person seating capacity concert hall suitable for intimate concerts, dance performances, readings, and more. Digital projector for film and video 129-square-meter stage, no wing space or fly space. Portable sprung wood floor with marley available on request.

Screening Room (C3-B1-101)
60-seat screening room with Dolby digital projection and sound system. Modest production support available for performances, artist talks, panels.

Music Practice Rooms (007, 010, 121, 127, 133, 137)
Each music practice room is equipped with an upright piano, acoustic sound paneling, music stands, and some general seating. Different types of rooms include group rehearsal rooms, individual practice rooms, piano rooms, and a band practice room.

Rehearsal Studios (009, 014, 045, 144, 146)
Rehearsal rooms are designed as open space, ideally for theater or music, but could work for others as well. These rooms are equipped with hardwood floors, upright pianos, acoustic paneling, some general seating, and a couple of portable tables.

Outdoor Amphitheater (the High Line)
Outdoor amphitheater with raised concrete oval stage and semi-circular bench seating for 150 people. Best suited for events with limited production needs.

Conference Center and Humanities Building (A6)

Auditorium (008)
This is the largest space in the Conference Center, with a 300-person seating capacity. The type of events typically held in the Auditorium are large-scale lectures, panel discussions, film screenings, musical performances, forums, etc.

Lecture Hall (007)
This is a lecture hall space that can seat 180 people and has the added bonus of letting in natural light. Similar to the Auditorium, the Lecture Hall is suitable for large-scale lectures, panel discussions, film screenings, musical performances, forums, etc.

Lobby Spaces

Within most buildings on campus, lobby spaces can be reserved and used to host event receptions.

Outdoor Spaces

John E. Sexton Square
Generally the most sought-after outdoor space on campus, the John E. Sexton Square (previously known as Central Plaza) is the first space visitors see when they enter New York University Abu Dhabi. With its palm trees and benches decorating the center of the space, it is no wonder that this is the space that faces the main Campus Center of the University. The Central Plaza is an open space in which the community can hold outdoor events.

West Plaza
Situated between the buildings, the West Plaza is an open space in which the community can hold outdoor events. Please note that Facilities can only support events that require a limited power supply in this space. Additional charges may be incurred from the event support teams when using the West Plaza.

East Plaza
Situated between the buildings, the East Plaza is an open space in which the community can hold outdoor events. Please note that Facilities can only support events that require a limited power supply in this space. Additional charges may be incurred from the event support teams when using the East Plaza.

Classroom Spaces

Any instructional spaces, such as classrooms, cannot be reserved through the Space Reservation System and cannot be booked through the Space Reservation Team. You will need to email the Registrar's Office at nyuad.registrar@nyu.edu .

title: The Arts Center at NYUAD · NYUAD Students
text:
The Arts Center at NYU Abu Dhabi presents distinguished professional artists from around the world, student, faculty, and community productions.

The Arts Center offers NYUAD compelling programming that connects to the curriculum and illuminates the scholarly pursuits of students and faculty. Its range of public programs aim to animate and enrich the cultural life of both Abu Dhabi and the university through interaction.

Firmly rooted in the region but with a global reach, and embedded in the university while welcoming Emiratis and the local community, The Arts Center at NYUAD is an extraordinary addition to the local and international arts landscapes. Excellence, collaboration, creativity, accessibility, innovation, respect, and understanding are the core values that govern The Arts Center.

The Spaces

The Arts Center at NYUAD comprises an expansive complex of performance venues, technical resources, and educational facilities. It includes the following performance spaces:

- 700 seat Red Theater

- 150-300 seat Black Box Studio

- 150 seat Blue Hall

- 60 seat Film Screening Room

- Rooftop Amphitheater

- Project Room Exhibition Space

For more information, visit The Arts Center at NYUAD .
