title: Campus Sustainability · NYUAD Students
text:
Under the leadership of the Office of Sustainability and Stewardship , students, faculty, and staff work together to make NYU Abu Dhabi one of the region’s leading campuses in sustainability. Through initiatives across campus life, we work to reduce greenhouse gas emissions, support teaching and research, and build a culture of sustainability.

Creating a sustainable campus requires a collective effort. The first step is knowing what you can do – here's how you can contribute.

Office of Sustainability and Stewardship

Learn more about the Office of Sustainability and Stewardship and how we work with our partners across campus to achieve our goal of carbon neutrality.

Sustainable Living Guide

Explore our guidelines on waste reduction, recycling correctly, sustainable food and transportation choices, and donating responsibly.

Get Involved

Find student groups, research labs, community events, and volunteer opportunities to help build a more sustainable campus community.

Resources and Funding

Have an idea for a sustainability project? Explore NYU Green Grants to find the funding and resources needed to make it happen.

title: Community Events and Engagements · NYUAD Students
text:
Interested in volunteering to protect the environment or to attend events focused on sustainability?

The best way to stay up to date on sustainability-related volunteer opportunities at NYU Abu Dhabi is through the Civic Engagement and Service Portal . Through the portal, you can browse upcoming events, sign up for volunteer initiatives, and get involved in projects that make a real impact on campus and in the wider community.

Nurdle Hunting
Every semester, the NYU and Abu Dhabi community are invited to collect nurdles (small plastic pellets) from where they wash up on Saadiyat beach. The event is an opportunity for people of all ages to become more informed of ocean plastic pollution and to take care of our local ecosystem.

Mangrove Planting
NYU Abu Dhabi regularly organizes mangrove planting initiatives in collaboration with the Emirates Marine Environmental Group (EMEG), supporting the UAE’s goal of planting 100 million mangroves by 2030.

Mangroves are vital to climate action, acting as natural carbon sinks while also protecting coastlines from erosion and rising sea levels. These efforts contribute to the UAE’s broader commitment to preserving and expanding its mangrove ecosystems.

Environmental Education (Climate Fresk)
NYU Abu Dhabi partners with Climate Fresk, a global initiative dedicated to advancing climate education. Students can volunteer to become Climate Fresk facilitators, leading interactive workshops that teach the science behind climate change, encourage discussion and critical thinking, and empower youth to take meaningful climate action. This is a great opportunity to build leadership skills while contributing to environmental awareness in Abu Dhabi and beyond.

title: Research Opportunities · NYUAD Students
text:
Interested in exploring sustainability through research? NYU Abu Dhabi offers a range of labs and initiatives focused on topics such as climate science, biodiversity, sustainable materials, and environmental systems.

- Advanced Materials for Building Efficiency Research Laboratory (AMBER Lab)
Tackles pressing societal issues through fundamental and practical research in innovative and new construction materials.

- eARThumanities Research Initiative
With a view to interdisciplinary cooperation and coordination, this initiative explores the major transformational challenges arising from a rapidly changing climate.

- Center for Genomics and Systems Biology
Provides a nexus for cutting-edge life sciences research in the United Arab Emirates, with world-class facilities and resources to promote innovative advances in genomics and systems biology.

- Center for Global Sea Level Change
Combines observations and computer models to understand past, and project future, sea-level rise.

- Burt Marine Biology Lab
Research using the Arabian Gulf as a natural laboratory to study coral reef ecology in extreme environments and to understand how these may serve as a model for the possible impacts of future climate change on reefs elsewhere.

- Marine Microbial Ecology — Amin Lab
Focused on how seawater organisms interact with each other and how these interactions influence their ecosystem, from coral health to algal blooms to bioprospecting.

- S.M.A.R.T. Construction Research Group
Conducts world-leading research to deliver innovative frameworks, methodologies, models, and tools to improve the management of the different phases in the lifecycle of construction projects.

title: Student Groups · NYUAD Students
text:
Passionate about sustainability and interested in connecting with like-minded peers? Join one of our active Student Interest Groups and start making an impact.

Ecoherence
Ecoherence focuses on local sustainability issues, working to improve campus practices while raising awareness about everyday environmental impact among students, faculty, and staff. Members collaborate with university administration and campus partners to drive meaningful change.

Community Impact Includes:

- Partnering with dining services (ADNH) to replace Styrofoam takeaway containers with biodegradable alternatives and introduce reusable options

- Advocating for bans on plastic bags and microbeads in all on-campus stores

- Launching a Boomerang Bags initiative to encourage reuse within the communit

- Helping remove 500mL plastic water bottles from campus

- Hosting workshops on recycling, sustainable self-care, and menstruation

- Creating engaging and humorous awareness campaigns on environmental issues

Green House
Green House is an NYUAD-based youth think tank focused on climate change research and advocacy. Led by a core committee, the group hosts weekly meetings and organizes events throughout the year.

While it originally emphasized workshop-style learning, Green House has evolved into a platform for:

- Policy discussions and debates on climate issues

- Developing sustainability recommendations for NYU Abu Dhabi

- Participation in local and international conferences

A signature initiative is participation in the annual Conference of Parties (COP) , where a select group of students represent the UAE as youth diplomats. Participants typically specialize in specific climate topics and actively follow negotiations. Members are also engaged in climate advocacy and diplomacy both locally and globally.

Student Government Sustainability Committee
This committee serves as a bridge between the student body and university leadership on sustainability matters at NYU Abu Dhabi.

Core goals:

- Promote a culture of environmental mindfulness across campus

- Advocate for policies that improve the university’s sustainability and environmental footprint

- Engage students and administration in dialogue and awareness-building around sustainability challenges and opportunities

title: Resources and Funding · NYUAD Students
text:
Green Grants

Have an idea to make campus more sustainable? The NYU Green Grants Program is your chance to turn that idea into a real project, with funding and support to bring it to life.

Open to all NYU students (including NYU Abu Dhabi), Green Grants support creative, impactful sustainability initiatives that improve campus life, raise awareness, and drive long-term change.

You can receive:

- Up to USD 3,000 through Microgrants for smaller or pilot projects

- Up to USD 20,000 through Green Grants for larger, high-impact ideas

Whether you're interested in reducing waste, launching a campaign, testing new technology, or conducting applied research, this is an opportunity to take initiative and make a tangible difference on campus.

What Kind of Project Can I Propose?
The program funds innovative student-led (and community-led) projects that:

- Improve environmental performance on campus

- Foster sustainability awareness and engagement

- Support applied research and design

- Expand sustainability learning opportunities

- Test and showcase new ideas and technologies

Projects with long-term impact or potential to become permanent campus initiatives are especially encouraged.

Who Can Apply?
Any current NYU student, faculty member, or staff member can apply as a project lead.

- Students from any NYU campus or study-away site are eligible

- You can apply individually or as a team

- Larger projects can involve external partners (e.g., NGOs, alumni, community groups)

Types of Funding
Microgrants (up to USD 3,000)

- Ideal for pilot ideas or smaller-scale projects

- Rolling applications with quick turnaround (about 2 weeks)

Green Grants (up to USD 20,000)

- For larger, more innovative and scalable projects

- Awarded once per semester by a selection committee

How to Apply

- Reach out to the NYUAD Sustainability team at nyuad.sustainability@nyu.edu to discuss your idea

- Submit an Expression of Interest

- Schedule a consultation with NYU’s Office of Sustainability

- Complete your application (Microgrant or full Green Grant)

Timeline
Microgrants

- Accepted year-round

- Decisions typically within two weeks

Green Grants (Spring deadlines)

- Expression of Interest : December 4, 2026 (11:59pm ET)

- Consultation deadline: December 16, 2026

- Final application deadline : January 3, 2027 (11:59pm ET)

title: Sustainable Living Guide · NYUAD Students
text:
How-to Guide: Sustainable Practices for Students

From daily habits to bigger choices, this is your one-stop guide to living sustainably on campus.

Explore the information below for simple, effective ways to make a difference.

How to Reduce Waste on Campus
Reducing waste is the most effective way to lower your environmental impact. Explore these five tips on reducing our environmental impact on a day-to-day basis:

- Bring a reusable cup

- Skip single-use cups and bring your own for coffee or tea.

- You can also use the Cup4Card program:

- Go to the cashier in D2 and purchase a reusable cup (one-time fee of AED10)

- Return the used cup to the cashier to be washed and receive a card

- Next time, exchange your card for a clean cup

- Carry a reusable water bottle

- Small plastic bottles are no longer sold on campus – refill your bottle instead

- Tap water on campus is safe and regularly tested

- Use one of the 15+ refill stations across campus

- Print less paper - In March 2022, a soft printing cap of 1,000 pages per six months was introduced. Since then, our campus community has saved over 6.8 million Pages ! Here’s how you can contribute:

- Print double-sided (default on campus printers)

- Print two pages per sheet for readings, four per sheet for slides

- Sign documents digitally using Adobe Reader or Preview – no printing needed

- Use reusable takeaway containers - Our reusable container program is a sustainable way to take food back to your room or desk and it’s easy to join. How it works:

- Buy a token at the East Dining Hall, Marketplace, or the Convenience Store for AED 35.00 (non-refundable)

- Use the token to get a clean, reusable container for your takeaway meal purchased in the East Dining Hall or the Marketplace

- When you’re done eating, rinse the container and return it to a cashier

- Collect a new token to use on your next visit

- Single-use compostable takeaway containers are also available for AED3.25

- Plan low-waste events

- Use reusable plates, cups, and cutlery

- Borrow or loan items instead of buying new

- Order food based on confirmed RSVPs

- Offer vegetarian or vegan options

- Avoid printing flyers – share information digitally

- Share leftover food after the event (e.g., Hungry at NYUAD)

- Clean up and sort waste properly

- Use campus shuttles or public transport

How to Donate on Campus
At the end of every semester comes a move out period, where thousands of items – clothing, shoes, furniture, etc, in student dormitories that are perfectly re-usable end up getting thrown away. Instead of throwing away these items, here are a few ways to give them a new life or help out someone in need:

Luqya - The ReFind Shop

In collaboration with the Office of Civic Engagement and Service and ResLife, Luqya – The ReFind Shop is a campus initiative that gives pre-owned items a second life. Students can donate items at the end of each semester, which are then redistributed to incoming and returning students at the start of the next term.

Keep an eye out for Luqya’s official relaunch!

How to Segregate Waste Properly
At NYUAD, waste is separated into three main streams. Knowing where to put your items is the first step to recycling correctly.

- General Waste: Everything else that cannot be recycled (sent to landfill)

- Paper: Office paper, newspapers, magazines, and cardboard

- Cans and Plastics: Aluminum drink cans, tin cans, and hard plastics (e.g., empty water bottles)

How do I Recycle on Campus?
Did you know?

It’s essential to separate your waste and recycle correctly. Always make sure your recyclable items are clean before putting them in the recycling bin. If they’re not, they can contaminate the entire batch – causing all of it to be sent to landfill instead.

Avoid these common mistakes:

- Empty and clean your items before recycling

- Food or liquid residue can contaminate recyclables. If items are dirty, the entire batch may be sent to landfill.

- Don’t recycle soft plastics

- Items like candy wrappers, plastic wrap, and plastic bags cannot be recycled.
→ Put them in General Waste

- Know what parts can be recycled (and what can’t). Some items are made of mixed materials:

- Paper cups and juice cartons → General Waste (plastic lining makes them non-recyclable

- Coffee cup lids → Cans and Plastics

- Coffee cup sleeves → Paper and Cardboard

- Check before recycling pizza boxes

- Greasy pizza boxes → General Waste

- Clean pizza boxes → Paper

- Remove and discard the liner → General Waste

How to Make Sustainable Food Choices
What you eat – and how much you waste – has a real impact on the environment. Small changes in your daily habits can make a big difference on campus.

Reduce Food Waste

Our community throws away over 100 kg of food every day in the East Dining Hall (D2) alone. You can track the monthly average on the display at the D2 entrance.

Tips: Take only what you’ll eat, go back for seconds if needed, and be mindful of portions. Reducing food waste is one of the simplest and most effective ways to lower your environmental footprint.

- Try a more plant-based diet

- Shifting toward a more plant-based diet can significantly reduce your environmental impact. Plant-based foods generally require fewer resources, like water and energy, and produce fewer emissions.

- Make informed food choices by considering their carbon footprint

- Klimato is a carbon-labeling platform that helps measure and communicate the climate impact of the food we serve. It is currently being piloted at the Flavors of the World counter in D2 to help students make more informed, lower-carbon food choices.

- Menu items are categorized by climate impact (low, medium, or high), making it easier to choose lower-carbon meals. The emissions data also supports menu planning and ongoing efforts to reduce food-related emissions in line with the Cool Food Pledge.

title: Undergraduate Meal Plan · NYUAD Students
text:
Graduate students, please visit the Graduate Student Meal Plan (https://students.nyuad.nyu.edu/graduate-students/services/graduate-meal-plans/) page for more information.

The NYUAD Undergraduate Meal Plan is designed to be simple, convenient, and flexible, giving you access to a variety of dining options across campus throughout the semester.

Your meal plan consists of three Digital Campus Currencies, each serving a different purpose and automatically loaded to your NYUAD ID card according to the published schedule.

Digital Campus Currencies

Two currencies refresh every week and don't carry over. The third is semester-long and more flexible about where it goes — including a one-time top-up at the start of term.

Meal Swipes

- Amount : 12 meals per week, resets every Monday at 12:10am.

- Where : Use at D1 and D2 dining halls.

- When : Expires every Sunday at approximately 11:30pm UAE — does not roll over.

Flex Dining Dirhams

- Amount : AED 84 per week, resets every Monday at 12:10am.

- Where : Use at Marketplace, D1, and D2 dining halls.

- When : Expires every Sunday at approximately 11:30pm UAE — does not roll over.

Campus Dirhams

- Amount : AED 346 every other week.

- Where : Use at all dining venues and the Convenience Store.

- When : Begins August 31, 2026 and expires at the end of the fall 2026 semester.

- One-time top-up : on August 31 only, students also receive an additional AED 346 in Campus Dirhams — a one-off semester-start load, on top of the regular biweekly amount, meant for beginning-of-semester food and grocery purchases. It's the same currency, just an extra deposit.

Arrival Privileges

Extra value on top of the regular plan.

Move-in doesn't count against your regular fall 2026 allocation.

Student Category | Arrival Date 2026 | Days | Meal Swipes | Flex Dining | Campus Dirhams

First years | August 23 | 8 | 14 | AED 84 | AED 198

Visiting students | August 26 | 5 | 10 | N/A | AED 125

Returning students | August 29 | 2 | 4 | N/A | AED 50

Schedule — How the Weeks Run

- Your approved arrival date — arrival privileges begin.

- August 31 — first day of classes; regular fall 2026 plan begins, plus the one-time AED 346 top-up.

- Every Monday, 12:10am — Meal Swipes and Flex Dining Dirhams refresh. Campus Dirhams reload every other Monday.

- Every Sunday, ~11:30pm — unused swipes and flex dining expire: they don't roll over.

- December 23, 2026 — semester ends; the final week's allocation is prorated.

Partial Week — If Your Week Is Cut Short
Early arrival or the final week of term rarely lines up with a full Monday–Sunday cycle. Here's what a partial week is worth.

Eligible Days | Meal Swipes | Flex Dining | Campus Dirhams

1 day | 2 | N/A | AED 25

2 days | 4 | N/A | AED 50

3 days | 6 | N/A | AED 75

4 days | 8 | N/A | AED 100

5 days | 10 | N/A | AED 125

6 days | 10 | AED 84 | AED 150

7 days (full week) | 12 | AED 84 | AED 173

Example: the fall 2026 plan ends Wednesday, December 23 — a three-day final week. That means six swipes + AED 75 dirhams, and no flex dining that week.

Campus Dirham Vendors

Campus Dirhams and the one-time top-up work anywhere on this list. Full board Meal Swipes and Flex Dining Dirhams are limited to D1, D2, and Marketplace.

- A List Popsicle - Blacksmith Coffee - Boba Bae Juices - Campus East (D2) - Campus West (D1) - Day Mart Convenience Store - Escape from New York Pizza | - Lingua Coffee - Marketplace - Mysk Café - Night Souq - Read & Refuel Café - Sushi Counter

How to Use Your Meal Privileges

Simply present your NYUAD student ID card to the cashier and specify which of the three digital campus currencies you would like to use to pay for your transaction.

Frequently Asked Questions

Do I need to sign up, or activate anything?
No. Eligible undergraduates are enrolled automatically, and all three currencies load onto your ID on schedule with no activation step.

Can I opt out?
Only if you're an approved commuter who meets the waiver requirements. Applying doesn't guarantee approval.

Do unused swipes or flex dining roll over?
No — both expire at the end of their weekly cycle, every Sunday around 11:30pm. Campus Dirhams are the exception — they last until the end of the semester.

Why did I get fewer swipes or dirhams than expected?
Your allocation is prorated any week your plan covers fewer than seven days — typically during early arrival or the final week of term.

How do I check my balance?
Check your meal plan balance (https://mealplans.nyu.edu/textpage.php?pageid=590&skey=88daf210a5961588f8745cd3738bfc66&cid=156&).

J-Term and Spring Meal Plan Privileges

January Term 2026 Meal Plan Privileges
If you are enrolled in a January Term course or an approved Capstone at NYU Abu Dhabi, you will receive a prorated meal plan based on your arrival and departure dates.

The plan includes Campus Dirhams , Full Board Meal Swipes , and Flex Dining Dirhams . Students attending overseas RAS may receive prorated meal swipes for the days they are on campus.

- Full Board and Flex Dining Dirhams reset every Sunday evening at midnight.

- Campus Dirhams expire at the end of the term: January 18, 2026, at 11pm UAE . If you are enrolled in spring 2026, you will receive the meal privileges for Sunday as well.

Spring 2026 Meal Plan Privileges
Your regular spring term meal privileges will be loaded on January 19, 2026, the official first day of the term.

Weekly 12 x Full Board meal swipes and AED 84 of Flex Dining Dirhams

- Activation date : Every Monday morning (starting January 19, 2026)

- Expiration date : Every Sunday around 11pm

- You receive 12 x meal swipes each week, which can be used in the dining halls (D1 and D2).

- Additionally, you will receive AED 84 Flex Dining Dirhams each week you can use at the Marketplace, D1, and D2.

Campus Dirhams (Bi-weekly Allocation of AED 346)

- Activation date: Every other Monday (starting January 19, 2026)

- Expiration date: At the end of the semester

- AED 346 Campus Dirhams will be deposited into your student card every other Monday morning. These funds can be used at all dining venues on campus and the Convenience Store.

One-time Semester Allocation — Campus Dirhams, AED 346

- Activation date : January 19, 2026 ONLY

- Expiration date : At the end of the semester

- AED 346 Campus Dirhams will be deposited into your student card, to allow you to make some up-front purchases for your refrigerator.

Graduate students, please visit the Graduate Student Meal Plan (https://students.nyuad.nyu.edu/graduate-students/services/graduate-meal-plans/) page for more information.

The NYUAD Undergraduate Meal Plan is designed to be simple, convenient, and flexible, giving you access to a variety of dining options across campus throughout the semester.

Your meal plan consists of three Digital Campus Currencies, each serving a different purpose and automatically loaded to your NYUAD ID card according to the published schedule.

sections.title: Digital Campus Currencies
sections.text: Two currencies refresh every week and don't carry over. The third is semester-long and more flexible about where it goes — including a one-time top-up at the start of term.

sections.title: Digital Campus Currencies · Meal Swipes
sections.text:
- Amount : 12 meals per week, resets every Monday at 12:10am.

- Where : Use at D1 and D2 dining halls.

- When : Expires every Sunday at approximately 11:30pm UAE — does not roll over.

sections.title: Digital Campus Currencies · Flex Dining Dirhams
sections.text:
- Amount : AED 84 per week, resets every Monday at 12:10am.

- Where : Use at Marketplace, D1, and D2 dining halls.

- When : Expires every Sunday at approximately 11:30pm UAE — does not roll over.

sections.title: Digital Campus Currencies · Campus Dirhams
sections.text:
- Amount : AED 346 every other week.

- Where : Use at all dining venues and the Convenience Store.

- When : Begins August 31, 2026 and expires at the end of the fall 2026 semester.

- One-time top-up : on August 31 only, students also receive an additional AED 346 in Campus Dirhams — a one-off semester-start load, on top of the regular biweekly amount, meant for beginning-of-semester food and grocery purchases. It's the same currency, just an extra deposit.

sections.title: Arrival Privileges · Schedule — How the Weeks Run
sections.text:
- Your approved arrival date — arrival privileges begin.

- August 31 — first day of classes; regular fall 2026 plan begins, plus the one-time AED 346 top-up.

- Every Monday, 12:10am — Meal Swipes and Flex Dining Dirhams refresh. Campus Dirhams reload every other Monday.

- Every Sunday, ~11:30pm — unused swipes and flex dining expire: they don't roll over.

- December 23, 2026 — semester ends; the final week's allocation is prorated.

Partial Week — If Your Week Is Cut Short
Early arrival or the final week of term rarely lines up with a full Monday–Sunday cycle. Here's what a partial week is worth.

Eligible Days | Meal Swipes | Flex Dining | Campus Dirhams

1 day | 2 | N/A | AED 25

2 days | 4 | N/A | AED 50

3 days | 6 | N/A | AED 75

4 days | 8 | N/A | AED 100

5 days | 10 | N/A | AED 125

6 days | 10 | AED 84 | AED 150

7 days (full week) | 12 | AED 84 | AED 173

Example: the fall 2026 plan ends Wednesday, December 23 — a three-day final week. That means six swipes + AED 75 dirhams, and no flex dining that week.

sections.text: Simply present your NYUAD student ID card to the cashier and specify which of the three digital campus currencies you would like to use to pay for your transaction.

sections.title: Frequently Asked Questions
sections.text:
Do I need to sign up, or activate anything?
No. Eligible undergraduates are enrolled automatically, and all three currencies load onto your ID on schedule with no activation step.

Can I opt out?
Only if you're an approved commuter who meets the waiver requirements. Applying doesn't guarantee approval.

Do unused swipes or flex dining roll over?
No — both expire at the end of their weekly cycle, every Sunday around 11:30pm. Campus Dirhams are the exception — they last until the end of the semester.

Why did I get fewer swipes or dirhams than expected?
Your allocation is prorated any week your plan covers fewer than seven days — typically during early arrival or the final week of term.

How do I check my balance?
Check your meal plan balance (https://mealplans.nyu.edu/textpage.php?pageid=590&skey=88daf210a5961588f8745cd3738bfc66&cid=156&).

sections.title: J-Term and Spring Meal Plan Privileges
sections.text:
January Term 2026 Meal Plan Privileges
If you are enrolled in a January Term course or an approved Capstone at NYU Abu Dhabi, you will receive a prorated meal plan based on your arrival and departure dates.

The plan includes Campus Dirhams , Full Board Meal Swipes , and Flex Dining Dirhams . Students attending overseas RAS may receive prorated meal swipes for the days they are on campus.

- Full Board and Flex Dining Dirhams reset every Sunday evening at midnight.

- Campus Dirhams expire at the end of the term: January 18, 2026, at 11pm UAE . If you are enrolled in spring 2026, you will receive the meal privileges for Sunday as well.

Spring 2026 Meal Plan Privileges
Your regular spring term meal privileges will be loaded on January 19, 2026, the official first day of the term.

Weekly 12 x Full Board meal swipes and AED 84 of Flex Dining Dirhams

- Activation date : Every Monday morning (starting January 19, 2026)

- Expiration date : Every Sunday around 11pm

- You receive 12 x meal swipes each week, which can be used in the dining halls (D1 and D2).

- Additionally, you will receive AED 84 Flex Dining Dirhams each week you can use at the Marketplace, D1, and D2.

Campus Dirhams (Bi-weekly Allocation of AED 346)

- Activation date: Every other Monday (starting January 19, 2026)

- Expiration date: At the end of the semester

- AED 346 Campus Dirhams will be deposited into your student card every other Monday morning. These funds can be used at all dining venues on campus and the Convenience Store.

One-time Semester Allocation — Campus Dirhams, AED 346

- Activation date : January 19, 2026 ONLY

- Expiration date : At the end of the semester

- AED 346 Campus Dirhams will be deposited into your student card, to allow you to make some up-front purchases for your refrigerator.

title: Responsible Dining · NYUAD Students
text:
We work hard to plan menus and campus programs that promote sustainable living and health and wellness. If you have a healthy, environmentally friendly idea to improve dining services on campus, please contact us!

Sustainable Efforts

- Reusable Takeaway Containers

Our reusable container program is a sustainable way to take food back to your dorm room or desk and it’s easy to join.

Buy a token at the East Dining Hall, Marketplace for AED 35.00 (non-refundable).

Use the token to get a clean, reusable container for your takeaway meal purchased in the East Dining Hall or the Marketplace.

When you’re done eating, rinse the container and return it to a cashier.

Collect a new token to use on your next visit.

Compostable takeaway containers are also available for AED 3.25

- Discontinuation of 500ml Bottled Water

On February 2017, small 500 ml plastic water bottles were removed and are no longer be available for purchase on campus. Only the 1.5 liter water bottles will remain on sale. In addition, as of March 2020 the water dispensers along with 5 gallon plastic water jugs were removed from campus. Only the 1.5 liter water bottles will remain on sale for a limited time.

- Food Waste

Food waste burdens waste management systems, exacerbates food insecurity, making it a major contributor to the three planetary crises of climate change, nature and biodiversity loss, and pollution and waste. According to the UNEP Food Waste Index Report 2021 , it is estimated that around 931 million tons of food waste was generated in 2019, 61 per cent of which came from households, 26 per cent from food service and 13 per cent from retail. This suggests that 17 per cent of total global food production may be wasted.

The NYUAD campus services office in collaboration with the office of Sustainability and Stewardship and ADNH, NYUAD's catering vendor are working to develop a comprehensive, community participant strategy that will target to minimize food waste from dining on campus and reinforce NYUAD's commitment in tackling the climate crisis through scholarship, research, but also action in its operations as well.

Nutrition Labels

We have been working very hard to bring nutritional data of our menus on campus to help you make the perfect choices when it comes to the food you place on your plates.

Not only do we believe that this will help assist in portion control, dietary management and reduce food waste, but we also believe that you, our community, will also be able to search for foods that are suitable for your preference, for example high in protein, suitable for vegetarians, dishes without nuts and much more!

Nutritics has quickly grown to be the nutrition management system software for clients across 165 countries and with their system, we are able to bring nutritional data for hundreds of recipes right at your

> Download the Nutritics Label Guide (PDF)

Special Dietary Needs

Our menus are designed to meet variety of dietary considerations such as Halal, vegans, vegetarians, glucose-intolerant individuals, and other special dietary requirements. Food containing nuts will have its ingredients clearly identified and will be isolated from other foods as much as is reasonably possible.

Ingredients and nutrition information for food served at the hot counters are displayed for your convenience to help you make smart choices and to manage your dietary needs effectively.

If you have specific dietary needs, please talk to dining staff directly or email nyuad.dining@nyu.edu .

Food containing nuts will have its ingredients clearly identified and will be isolated from other foods as much as is reasonably possible.

Ingredients and nutrition information for food served at the hot counters are displayed for your convenience to help you make smart choices and to manage your dietary needs effectively.

If you have specific dietary needs, please talk to dining staff directly or email nyuad.dining@nyu.edu .

title: What's New · NYUAD Students
text:
A Taste of What's New in Campus Dining for AY 2026-2027

As we welcome the Community back for the new academic year, we are thrilled to announce a number of new and exciting updates at NYUAD Dining!

CHÚFÁNG Now Open

D1 West Dining Hall welcomes CHÚFÁNG, the first dedicated Chinese dining concept introduced in the history of the NYUAD dining operation.

As part of the D1 Dim Sum counter, the new outlet with feature Chinese hotpot and made-to-order stir-fry.

NYUAD EATS: The Dining App
We are starting with Grab&Go, moving towards other outlets and, before you know it, across Campus for ordering both dine-in and takeaway.

Stay tuned for more details!

CHICKA-GO Has Arrived to Save Your Lunch Break!
D2 East Dining Hall is swooping in with CHICKA-GO – our all-new, epic rotisserie chicken.

Seasoned to perfection and roasted till golden, it’s available whole, half, or by the portion.

Not all heroes wear capes... some just bring serious flavor.

The REUSABLE FOODWARE Initiative
NYUAD has always been a strong advocate for food containers and beverage cups. This year we are automating the process, as we look toward stopping single-use foodware by 2028.

NEW Food and Beverage Menus
We have incorporated all NYUAD Community’s comments into our new dining menus. Keep telling us what you like (or don’t like) and we will make it happen!

Survey QR codes can be found across dining outlets on all tables.

Our Mindset
We have taken these new initiatives and prepared unique concepts (with more on the way), as part of our commitment to continuous improvement.

But we also remain committed to supporting the Community, which makes us mindful of costs that come not only from better quality options, but also from inflation.

Food product price inflation remains a global issue, even more this year, driven by the recent geopolitical and regional developments and incidents, particularly impacting key commodities like eggs, beef, chicken, vegetables, and coffee, which have repeatedly made international news over the last months.

It is because of our commitment to support the Community that NYUAD Dining continues to absorb the vast majority of these increased costs.

- You will see no price changes in pre-cooked meals in both Dining Halls

- In Market Place, out of more than 200 food offerings, a mere handful of adjustments were applied - and even those are only in a couple of make-your-own beef/chicken choices.

- You will see prices drop for plant-based meat meals, as part of our Sustainability and Cool-Food strategy.

- Almost all breakfast items will remain unaltered, with the inclusion of a few better-quality add-ons, as per the community’s requests.

- More one-swipe meals have been added, while the Swipe-It-Forward initiative, for internally donating unused meal allowance, continues this year with increased weekly availability.

- While coffee is the commodity with the biggest cost increase, the price of all our basic coffee and beverage options will remain unchanged; for a few of our more premium choices, such as our new specialty recipes or higher-end brands, you may see a difference of a dirham or two, but given these choices were not previously available, we consider it an enhancement, not an adjustment.

We have made many preparations for this academic year, but we need your help to make campus dining even better. Here are three simple ways to help us improve quality and manage costs:

- Share your feedback daily: Tell us what's working and what isn't so we can make real-time improvements.

- Reduce food waste: Take only what you’ll eat – it directly helps us keep dining costs down for everyone.

- Get the facts directly: Unsure about a menu change, price, or policy? Check official dining channels or ask our team.

Announcements for Dining

Monday, October 12, 2026

-
DINING OPERATING HOURS - FALL BREAK

Dear All,
Please be informed of the dining operating hours during the Fall Break, from Monday, 19 October, to Monday, 26 October 2026 , as outlined below:

- D2: Open daily from 19–26 October.
- D1: Closed from 19–24 October; reopening on Sunday, 25 October.
- Market Place: Open from 19–23 October, closed on Saturday, 24 October, and reopening on Sunday, 25 October.
- Read & Refuel Cafe: Open from 19–23 October, closed on Saturday, 24 October , and reopening on Sunday, 25 October. Kindly take note of the operating schedule and plan accordingly.

- Category:
Service Notifications

- Topic: Dining

-
Posted
on Monday, October 12, 2026

- Posted by:

Joselyn Jusayan Ilumin

-
Permalink

title: Announcements · NYUAD Students
text:
Who Can Post

Only selected students are allowed to post announcements.

Is This Announcement Appropriate?

- What to post

- Operational updates (IT outage, administrative holidays, library hours).

- Deadline notices and links to exam schedules.

- Event registration notices.

- Volunteer opportunities.

- Short reminder about an upcoming event, with a link to the calendar .

- What not to post

- Personal classifieds (sale or lost items).

- Community forums (carpools, shopping trips, sporting leagues).

- Third-party contests or promotions.

- Lengthy event details. Learn now to use the events calendar.

- Information about Abu Dhabi events not related to NYUAD.

How to Post

- Click the post button on the intranet

Click the Post button. Your name will appear as the author of the post and you will see a permalink at the bottom. Add an announcement by clicking the Post button located at the top of the Student Portal homepage and fill in the following fields.

- Category

Choose the relevant category for your announcement. As users have the option to view announcements via category, selecting the right category ensures your message falls in the appropriate place.

List of categories:

Deadlines | For example, academic papers, research funding, work evaluation deadlines.

Discounts, Deals & Promotions | Student/faculty/staff discounts, deals and promotions.

Events & Activities | University-related events and activities.

Job Opportunities, Internships & Volunteering | Jobs, internships and volunteering opportunities.

Learning & Development | Training and courses for personal growth and development.

New Hires, Changes & Departures | Introducing new hires, change of departmental structure, and departures of colleagues.

News & Information | News and general information for the University.

Policies | Policy changes and updates.

Service Notifications | Changes in hours, location, and regular services provided. For example, change in dining hours, announcing official public holidays, relocation or cessation of services.

- Title

A short statement about your event that captures attention, avoiding caps or special characters.

- Message

Type or paste the body of your announcement in this section. You can format the content using the Rich Text Editor buttons.

- Publish Date

Enter the date the announcement should appear on the Intranet or Student Portal (the default is set to "today").

- Expiration Date

Enter a date no more than 30 days from the Publish date. Expired announcements will no longer show on the announcement landing page.

- Location

Choose Abu Dhabi or New York or both depending on which location the announcement is targeted to.

- Audience

Choose Students to post your announcement on the Student Portal; Faculty and/or Staff to post to the Intranet. By choosing both groups, your announcement will automatically be included on both the Portal and Intranet.

- Topic

Choose the relevant topic for your announcement.

How To Edit/ Delete

- To edit

Click on the desired announcement and select Edit. If the changes are significant (new location or time for an event, for example), check the Promote this update box and click the Save button. Your announcement will be marked with a blue flag, but will not be moved to the top of the announcements queue.

- To delete

Click on the desired announcement and select Delete. You will receive notification that the announcement has been deleted. Note that there is no "undo" for deletions.

View Announcements Based on Your Preferences

- View by Category or Date

View announcements based on your preferences and needs. Select either category or date on the top right hand of the announcement page.

View by Category
The announcements will be arranged by categories in alphabetical order. Empty categories with no announcement tagged to it will not appear. In each category, the 10 latest announcements are shown in chronological order. To view later non-expired posts, click on the "load more" button.

Categories

Deadlines | For example, academic papers, research funding, work evaluation deadlines.

Discounts, Deals & Promotions | Student/faculty/staff discounts, deals and promotions.

Events & Activities | University-related events and activities.

Job Opportunities, Internships & Volunteering | Jobs, internships and volunteering opportunities.

Learning & Development | Training and courses for personal growth and development.

New Hires, Changes & Departures | Introducing new hires, change of departmental structure, and departures of colleagues.

News & Information | News and general information for the University.

Policies | Policy changes and updates.

Service Notifications | Changes in hours, location, and regular services provided. For example, change in dining hours, announcing official public holidays, relocation or cessation of services.

View by Dates
The announcements will be arranged in chronological order by date, with the latest announcement on top. For each day, the 10 latest announcements will be shown. To view later non-expired posts, click on the "load more" button.

Style Guide

- Keep it short!

Announcements will be quickly glanced over not read and studied. Put important info in the first couple sentences and keep it under 150 words.

- Don't repost

Reposting clogs up the section and creates a poor reader experience.

- Don't USE ALL CAPS or special characters ***

It's just like shouting, and a page of loud and messy announcements is difficult to navigate.

- Use link

Link to a webpage or an intranet page with more details whenever possible. This keeps the announcement concise and increase the likelihood of your message being read. Do check that all your links are working.

- Post announcements close to deadlines and event dates

Users appreciate information that is more immediate and relevant.

- Use the Events Calendar for full event details

Targeted at the NYUAD community, the events calendar houses detailed event information. Announcement post is meant to be a short summary, with a link to the event calendar. See how to post an event calendar here .

- Provide contact info

Allows user to get in touch for more information.

About Emergency and Urgent Announcements

These announcements will appear above the top menu of all pages on the Intranet and Student Portal with a red icon. Only certain individuals can post Emergency or Urgent Announcements. For more information please contact nyuad.web@nyu.edu .

- What are considered emergency and urgent announcements?

- A threat to the health or safety of the NYU Abu Dhabi community or property, which has been assessed and confirmed by the Senior Leadership Team.

- A department has identified an issue — such as potential risk to the community or property of NYU Abu Dhabi, or disruption of critical services — that requires an Urgent, Non-Emergency message to be sent to all NYUAD community members.

Related official links:
https://students.nyuad.nyu.edu/calendars/
https://students.nyuad.nyu.edu/

title: Color · NYUAD Students
text:
Primary Palette

NYU’s signature violet plays a key role in the University’s identity. The NYU violet and black make up the two primary colors in the NYU Abu Dhabi palette.

sections.title: Primary Palette
sections.text: NYU’s signature violet plays a key role in the University’s identity. The NYU violet and black make up the two primary colors in the NYU Abu Dhabi palette.

title: Accent Palette · NYUAD Students
text: The accent palette is meant to work alongside the primary and neutral palettes. These accent colors can be used for a wide variety of collateral but should always be used sparingly and never as the dominant color in a project.

title: Gradient Palette · NYUAD Students
text:
The gradient palette is meant to help add depth and a subtle color variation without overpowering a design. Each gradient swatch is specifically created using RGB or CMYK colors.

- DO NOT create your own gradient without prior approval from the design team.

title: Neutral Palette · NYUAD Students
text: The neutral palette consists of a variety of warm grays. Combine this palette with our brighter violet and accent colors for a more sophisticated look and feel. In cases where you find colors too harsh or strong, try replacing with one of these neutral options.

title: Violet Palette · NYUAD Students
text:
The violet palette is meant to further drive home the idea of “violet pride.” Using these various shades of violet help provide a strong sense of visual cohesion while creating a sense of harmony.

title: Department Identity · NYUAD Students
text:
Creating Your Own Logo

Do I Need My Own Logo?

As a general rule, NYU Abu Dhabi academic units and administrative departments are not permitted to have a unique logo. Individual logos at this level reduce the impact and effectiveness of the University’s brand.

Logos for special events, research groups, or Student Interest Groups recognized by, affiliated, or funded by the University (secondary logos) are permitted.

- A unique logo can be used to mark special occasions such as annual events, campaigns, and anniversaries. The duration of the use of this logo is short-term, and promotes and identifies only this particular event.

- The University logo, four torch emblem, and the Arabesque pattern MAY NOT be used — in part or whole — in the creation of the unique logo or graphic identifiers. In cases where the NYU Abu Dhabi connection is not obvious to audiences, the NYU Abu Dhabi logo or a sentence identifying the relationship with NYU Abu Dhabi and its mission, should be included.

- Alternatively, if these groups would like to create a close brand affiliation with NYU Abu Dhabi, they should use the violet, neutral, and accent palette, and/or the brand typefaces to create a visual connect with the University.

Groups seeking to create a unique logo or graphic identifier must request permission from the Office of Public Affairs’ design team: nyuad.design@nyu.edu and must work with a professional designer, which will ensure that any secondary logo harmonizes with NYU Abu Dhabi visual identity standards.

title: Wordmarks · NYUAD Students
text:
For internal communications and creative collateral meant for the NYU Abu Dhabi community and campus, using the primary logo is not necessary. The NYU Abu Dhabi department wordmark has been developed as a simple solution for your internal communication needs.

Your wordmark comes in three variations (left aligned, centered, and right aligned.)

- DO NOT use your NYU Abu Dhabi wordmark outside the community or off-campus, unless approved by the NYU Abu Dhabi design team

- Office name cannot exceed more than three lines

To request an official department wordmark, please contact nyuad.design@nyu.edu .

Benefits of using your NYU Abu Dhabi wordmark:

- Increased flexibility with creativity and design

- Fewer restrictions

- No color restrictions

- Acceptable to use on swag or apparel items

- Design team approval optional

title: Arabesque Pattern · NYUAD Students
text:
The NYU Abu Dhabi Arabesque pattern was specifically designed as a device to bring NYU’s iconic torch together with textures inspired by Islamic patterns.

The Arabesque pattern can be used to provide projects with as sense of color, texture, and identity whilst giving a subtle nod to NYU Abu Dhabi and the region. It can be set to medium transparency and overlaid on photos or even used with a gradient to fade out and blend into its surroundings.

- The pattern must always be cropped at its center point or faded out to a zero opacity

- The pattern must always be monocromatic

- The pattern’s opacity can be turned down to provide a more subtle texture

- DO NOT tamper with the pattern itself in any way

title: Four Torch Emblem · NYUAD Students
text:
The four torch emblem has been adopted as a symbol of NYU Abu Dhabi. It was taken from the Arabesque pattern and is meant to bring NYU’s iconic torch together with textures inspired by Islamic patterns.

- Only show the four torch emblem in an official color from the NYU Abu Dhabi palette.

- All torches must be the same color

- The four torch emblem is ideal for use on merchandise and apparel

- DO NOT rotate the four torch emblem. The four torch emblem must form a cross

- DO NOT use the four torch emblem on backgrounds that do not provide adequate contrast

- DO NOT flip the four torch emblem. The torch flames must point to the right

- DO NOT place elements in close proximity to the four torch emblem. The four torches are an element on their own. Follow the clear space guidelines

title: NYUAD Logo · NYUAD Students
text:
This is the primary NYU Abu Dhabi logo. This logo plays an essential role in representing the University. Consistent and appropriate use of this logo can powerfully advance the recognition of our institution. Here are some important rules when using the NYU Abu Dhabi logo:

The NYU Abu Dhabi logo can only be shown in NYU violet, black, or white.

By combining the torch in the box logomark with the NYU logotype and use of Arabic script we can create a distinctive visual identity that can be protected from impostors or unauthorized uses.

- Only use the NYU Abu Dhabi logo in situations that call for the official mark of the University

- The NYU Abu Dhabi logo should only appear once on a homepage or communications piece

- Follow the clear space guidelines as stated in this section

- DO NOT alter, or modify the logo in any way

- DO NOT remove the torch from the box

- DO NOT remove the Arabic text

- DO NOT use previous versions of the logo

- DO NOT place elements in close proximity to the logo

- DO NOT use the logo on backgrounds that do not provide adequate contrast

- DO NOT add a colored shape around the logo

Clear Space

Maintain an appropriate amount of clear space around the logo. There should be a clear space the height of the single torch around the entire logo. The same rules apply when the logo is used vertically.

Minimum Size

To maintain full legibility, always use discretion when sizing the logo. It should never be the most dominant element on the page.

title: Logo Misuse · NYUAD Students
text:
The logo should never be used or altered in the following ways.

DO NOT use colors other than NYU violet, black, or white. DO NOT use different colors within the logo.

DO NOT stretch or distort the logo.

DO NOT rearrange the elements, remove the vertical line or use the torch as a stand alone element. DO NOT distort or remove the Arabic text, or redraw the logo.

title: Logo Placement · NYUAD Students
text:
When placing the logo over colored backgrounds, the logo must be legible and shown clearly.

- For dark backgrounds, it is recommended to use the white logo

- When using the violet or black logo, ensure the torch is always white

- DO NOT use the logo over a busy background image

- DO NOT use the purple or black logo on dark backgrounds where there isn’t enough contrast for it to stand out

- DO NOT allow the background to show through the torch on the black or violet versions of the logo

title: Social Media Logo · NYUAD Students
text:
Social Media Logo

The social media logo is reserved for official University social media accounts only. If you would like to request to use the NYU Abu Dhabi social media logo please contact nyuad.design@nyu.edu .

Note: The torch should never be removed from the logo and used alone as an identifier in social media.

Social Media Lockups

Having an NYU Abu Dhabi social media lockup is the best way to communicate your official connection to the University online. If your office has its own social media channels, you can request an official NYU Abu Dhabi social media lockup. To do so, please send a request to nyuad.design@nyu.edu .

title: Vertical Usage · NYUAD Students
text:
For instances where the primary logo does not fit proportionally, the logo can be used vertically. Rotate the logo counterclockwise on a 90-degree angle. The torchmark should always be at the bottom.

DO NOT alter, or modify the logo in any way.

title: Photography · NYUAD Students
text:
Imagery should capture the NYU Abu Dhabi community in a way that demonstrates energy, enthusiasm, and excellence. The photography we use across University channels should be impactful, dynamic, and bold. Our general approach to photography of the NYU Abu Dhabi community is a reportage style, capturing discreet and intimate moments across campus that create a cohesive and inspiring set of images.

Professional or institutional photos and videos should still feel dynamic and bold, but take on a more sophisticated feel. Staged portraiture should feel refined and polished with natural light used as often as possible.

title: Color Overlays · NYUAD Students
text:
Color overlays are used for graphic impact when drawing in someone’s attention or when a level of excitement is needed. This works well when tying together elements on a page or when type is needed over a photograph, adding legibility to the heading.

- The colors used in an overlay should strictly be from the NYU Abu Dhabi color palettes

- The use of color overlays should not significantly reduce the legibility of an image or heading

title: Style and Writing Guide · NYUAD Students
text:
An impactful brand speaks a common language, despite the fact it speaks to different people from different places. NYU Abu Dhabi is one of the most diverse communities on the planet. Students, our primary audience, come from 100+ countries and speak 100+ languages, but we also communicate with faculty, researchers, staff, and the Abu Dhabi community.

These editorial guidelines are intended to help you communicate effectively and consistently on a variety of mediums including websites, social media, newsletters, and print marketing collateral.

This is an evolving style guide and we are constantly adding to it and revising current sections. If you have suggestions for things to include or can’t find what you’re looking for, please contact nyuad.public.affairs@nyu.edu

title: Typography · NYUAD Students
text:
Primary Fonts

- English
NYU’s primary typeface, NYU Perstare, is available in a range of weights and styles, lending it versatility and adaptability to a range of messaging needs. Use NYU Perstare for all kinds of communications. Take advantage of the wide variety of weights to create clear type hierarchies across a range of visual tones, whether your content is a simple flyer or a complex report.

Get NYU Perstare
NYU community members with an NYU NetID can download the desktop version of NYU Perstare.

Type Specimen Sheet
Download the type specimen (PDF) to pin up in your office.

- Arabic

Print

When designing for print, TheSansArabic is the primary typeface that compliments the NYU Abu Dhabi brand.

To Purchase this Typeface
TheSansArabic can be purchased online, in single weights, from LucasFonts at www.lucasfonts.com/fonts/thesansarabic/ . At this time, the University does not have an institutional license.

Online

Cairo has been selected as the substitute for TheSansArabic online, and can be downloaded for free from Google fonts .

Alternative Fonts

- English
In some situations, our brand typeface is not available. So we selected three backup options to maintain the integrity of our visual identity. View and download the complete Montserrat font family at Google Fonts .

For Google Workspace: Montserrat

For Email and Microsoft 365: Helvetica and Arial

Helvetica is our first system font alternative for NYU Perstare. It is widely available on Mac operating systems, in Google cloud-based documents, and in Adobe applications and can be used when NYU Perstare and Montserrat are not available. Helvetica may require installation on Windows operating systems.

Arial is our second system font alternative for NYU Perstare. It is always available on both Windows and Mac operating systems and can be used when NYU Perstare, Montserrat, and Helvetica are not available.

- Arabic
For NYU Abu Dhabi administrators, staff, faculty, and students not directly involved with graphic design projects, Droid Arabic Naskh has been selected as the substitute for TheSansArabic and Cairo.

Download Droid Arabic Naskh for free at https://fontlibrary.org/en/font/droid-arabic-naskh .

title: Commencement Photos and Videos · NYUAD Students
text:
Commencement Media Use – What Your Choice Means

Your response to the Commencement Media Release Form affects the use and sharing of photos, video, and audio recorded during Commencement-related activities.

The following information is intended to clarify what is and is not included depending on whether you indicate Yes or No on the form.

This form applies only to graduation related activities or events leading up to Commencement day and after the ceremony, such as:

- Commencement portraits

- Commencement video

- Yearbook (print and digital)

- Social Media coverage (Instagram, YouTube, LinkedIn, TikTok)

- Ceremony livestream (including stage screen playback during ceremony)

- Commencement stage photos next to the NYUAD banner

- Post-event video uploads on NYUAD’s YouTube channel

- All Ma’a Salama activities (including Senior Kashtah trips, Milestone events, Senior Walk, Ma’a Salama Week, etc.)

If You Give Permission (Saying YES)

By selecting “Do give permission”, you consent to being photographed, filmed, or recorded for Commencement-related print, digital, online, and promotional content produced or authorized by NYUAD, including everything mentioned in the section above.

If You Do NOT Give Permission (Saying NO)

By selecting “Do NOT give permission”, you are opting out of the use of your image, likeness, or voice for any NYUAD-authorized, commencement-related media.

If you indicate No, NYUAD will not :

-
Use your image or video in any Commencement-related social media posts

-
Feature you on NYUAD websites or Commencement pages

-
Include you in the livestream of the ceremony on YouTube and stage screen, or final edited ceremony video online

-
Capture or share your Commencement stage photos with you

-
Use photos or videos of you taken on Commencement day or any Ma’a Salama activities leading up to Commencement

Important Exception: Commencement Portraits

You will receive a soft copy of your Commencement portrait taken during the scheduled photoshoot prior to Commencement regardless of whether you indicate Yes or No on the release.

If you indicate No on the Commencement Media Release, your portrait will not be used, published, or distributed in any Commencement-related printed, digital, online, and promotional materials.

Why a Commencement-Specific Media Release?

A separate, commencement-specific media release has been introduced to address the unique circumstances related to graduation events and to ensure clarity, transparency, and student choice.

Important: The student media release form you have signed previously remains relevant for everything that is not related to Commencement.

Our Commitment

If you do not give permission, NYUAD will make every reasonable effort to ensure that your image, likeness, or voice does not appear in official Commencement-related materials. In the event of incidental capture, we will work to exclude you from any final or published content produced by NYUAD or its authorized agents.

Questions?

If you have questions about the Commencement Media Release, please email nyuad.photography@nyu.edu

title: Best Practices · NYUAD Students
text:
Best Practices

- Be Authentic

Represent yourself accurately and be transparent about your role at NYU. Admit when you make mistakes and correct inaccurate information. Consider that you are in an academic environment and the implications of utilizing a NYU-provided platform that automatically identifies you in your role at NYU.

- Be Smart

Social media is "real life." Behavior in social media is no different than in e-mail, public speech, classroom lecture, conversation with friends, or a poster on a wall. Anything considered inappropriate offline is likely also inappropriate online. When in doubt about whether to share or not, it's better to be safe than sorry.

- Be Thoughtful

Be mindful of what is considered appropriate behavior in different countries and cultures around the world and of how your words, actions, and images may be perceived. Know your audience and think before you post.

- Be Respectful

Are you aware of the UAE's photo sharing laws? Be sure to respect individual privacy and don't break the law.

- Be Mindful of Relationships

Think through creating friend/fan/follower connections where authority relationships exist. Many times you cannot control someone sharing your content or adding you to their connections, thereby gaining access to your content.

- Be Clear

When acting as a representative of the NYU community, clearly identify you or your group's relationship to NYUAD. If you are a member of the NYUAD community, but acting in social media as an individual, make it clear that you are expressing your own opinion and not that of the University.

- Be Prepared

When creating or managing a social media account for an NYUAD entity, ensure access credentials are shared by at least two people in case one team member is unreachable or no longer at the University. Develop an editorial calendar to keep things fresh.

- Be "NYUAD"

Remember you represent NYUAD; read NYUAD's Style Guidelines when creating profile/avatar images, graphics, or written content. Speak in accordance with your role at the University. Don't publish confidential or proprietary information relating to NYUAD or its partners.

- Be Successful

Create a social media strategy: identify your audience, account's personality, goals, staffing, content calendar, and other tools for success before jumping in. Take advantage of University resources that can help you succeed.

Content Marketing Plan Template

The key to success is to plan. Use our content marketing plan template to get started.

Other Helpful Resources

Learn the skills and best practices you need to run social media like a pro. We recommend subscribing to newsletters, blogs, and webinars to learn the fundamentals, plan your content, and drive meaningful results on social.

title: NYUAD Social Media Ambassador Program · NYUAD Students
text:
Become an NYU Abu Dhabi Social Media Ambassador!

Are you passionate about sharing your NYUAD experience? Join the Social Media Ambassador Program and become a representative of NYUAD across your global experience!

Responsibilities

- Share your academic achievements and faculty interactions, campus life and activities, cultural experiences in Abu Dhabi, wellness and well-being, career growth, achievements, and fun challenges and trends.

- Promote events, academic opportunities, and NYUAD initiatives.

- Engage with the NYUAD community and inspire others through creative content.

We’re Looking for Students Who Are:

- Active on social media platforms (Instagram, TikTok, Facebook, X, LinkedIn)

- Passionate about storytelling and connecting with the global NYU community

- Creative with photos, videos, reels, and stories

By joining, ambassadors will be compensated hourly for their work, get exclusive access to special events around campus, network with students, faculty, and alumni worldwide, receive NYUAD swag, and build their social media portfolio while gaining hands-on experience.

Ready to inspire others? Apply now by filling out the application form in the link below!

title: Financial Aid and Renewal · NYUAD Students
text:
Be sure to remove pop-up blockers from your browser in order to access additional links.

Returning Student Financial Aid FAQ

- How to review your financial aid award

Your most up-to-date financial aid award is readily accessible on your NYU Albert Student Center by clicking on the Finances tab (the tab is on the left-hand side).

Returning students will receive notification from the NYU Abu Dhabi Office of Financial Aid with more details in early July on how to access your award for the upcoming year.

- Financial aid renewal — Non-UAE Nationals

Your financial aid will be renewed each academic year at the same level that you accepted upon Admission to NYU Abu Dhabi, as long as you meet the following requirements:

- Earn academic credit in a minimum of 75 percent of the cumulative attempted credit hours.

- Maintain a cumulative grade point average of at least 2.0.

- Enroll full-time (12 credits or more in the fall and spring semesters).

More information on Academic Standing can be found under the Academic Policies .

All continuing students can expect their awards for the upcoming academic year to be available in NYU Albert by early July .

- Financial aid renewal — UAE Nationals

Your Sheikh Mohamed bin Zayed NYUAD Scholarship for Exceptional Emirati Students will be renewed annually as long as you:

- Earn academic credit in a minimum of 75 percent of the cumulative attempted credit hours.

- Maintain a cumulative grade point average of at least 2.0.

- Enroll full-time (12 credits or more in the fall and spring semesters).

More information on Academic Standing can be found under the Academic Policies .

Personal Support Award (Falcon Dirhams)
If you had received the Sh. Mohamed Personal Support (Falcon Dirhams) in a prior academic year, this award will be renewed automatically.

Emirati students who never filed a CSS Profile upon admission or in any previous academic year, and who would like to be reviewed for the need-based Personal Support Award (Falcon Dirhams), will need to submit a CSS Profile application. For details about the process, you should review this publication: UAE National Undergraduate Students - CSS Profile Instructions

All continuing students can expect their awards for the upcoming academic year to be available in NYU Albert by early July .

- Aid Proration under Full-Time Enrollment

If you are in your final semester and have been approved by the Academic Resource Center (ARC) to enroll under full-time credits (fewer than 12 credits), your tuition grant will be prorated based on the number of credits you enroll in.

If you enroll in:

- 6-8 credits, your NYUAD Tuition Grant will be prorated by 50% of the semester amount that you receive.

- 9-11 credits, your NYUAD Tuition Grant will be prorated by 75% of the semester amount that you receive.

Contacts

If you have questions about enrollment, please contact the Academic Resource Center (ARC) at nyuad.arc@nyu.edu .

If you have questions about the tuition charges or any other items on your university bill, please contact Student Finance at nyuad.studentfinance@nyu.edu .

If you have any additional questions about your financial aid, you should email us, the Office of Financial Aid at nyuad.financial.support@nyu.edu .

- CSS Profile — non-UAE National Students

Returning students are not required to submit a new CSS Profile to renew their financial aid. The CSS Profile is only required at the time of admission.

If there has been a change to your financial situation that was not captured on your initial CSS Profile, you may consider submitting a Returning Undergraduate Appeal . If you are in your 2nd, 3rd, or 4th year, the Office of Financial Aid encourages you to submit a new CSS Profile. Submitting a new CSS Profile will provide our office with the most up-to-date information for the appeal funding consideration.

Please note: submitting an appeal request or a new CSS Profile does not automatically guarantee appeal funds will be granted. If you are eligible to receive appeal funds, this additional award is a one-time grant for the semester in which it is offered; it will not be automatically renewed in subsequent semester(s) as NYUAD does not re-evaluate for renewable grants in subsequent years.

Appeal deadlines and notification dates are available on the NYU Financial Aid website under the Abu Dhabi campus information.

- CSS Profile — UAE National Students

If you have received the Sh. Mohamed Personal Support (Falcon Dirhams) in a prior academic year, this award will be renewed automatically. Another CSS Profile is not necessary.

Emirati students who never filed a CSS Profile upon admission or in any previous academic year and who would like to be reviewed for the need-based Personal Support Award (Falcon Dirhams) need to submit a CSS Profile application.

- NYU (Abu Dhabi) CSS school code is 2785.

- UAE National Undergraduate Students CSS Profile Instructions

- Upon completion of the CSS Profile, financial documentation will be requested for verification purposes. The Office of Financial Aid will email you at your NYU email address what is needed and how to upload your documentation to IDOC .

For 2026-2027, the annual personal support award is $2,364 for the academic year ($1,182 per semester). Demonstrated financial need and full-time enrollment (12 credits or more per semester) are required.

The Student Finance Office will be in communication regarding the disbursement of this award if you are eligible.

For questions about your semester university bill, refunds, or payments, you should contact the Student Finance Office at nyuad.studentfinance@nyu.edu

- IDOC: Additional Documentation Requested for the CSS Profile

The Office of Financial Aid will notify you if additional documentation is required to finalize our review of your CSS Profile. You will need to submit all documents through the Institutional Documentation Service (IDOC) portal via CollegeBoard's website . IDOC is a portal that NYU uses to securely obtain supporting financial documentation.

We strongly recommend that any documents, such as wage statements, uploaded to IDOC are submitted in English or with an English translation and figures converted into US Dollars (you can write the conversion on the document and indicate the currency that was used and date).

Additionally, be sure to include your name and NYU ID number (N#) on all of the pages that you are uploading. Submitting documents without an English translation and figures converted into US Dollars may result in a delay in reviewing your documentation.

- NYUAD Personal Support/ Sh. Mohamed Personal Support (Falcon Dirhams) Award

If your financial aid includes this award, you will receive additional information from the Student Finance Office about disbursement. If you have any questions about the disbursement of the NYUAD Personal Support/ Sh. Mohamed Personal Support award, you may email the Student Finance Office at nyuad.studentfinance@nyu.edu .

UAE Nationals who receive the Sheikh Mohamed bin Zayed NYUAD Scholarship for Exceptional Emirati Students and who would like to be reviewed for the need-based Sh. Mohamed Personal Support (Falcon Dirhams) award will need to submit a CSS Profile one time to be reviewed. For more information, refer to the following sections:

- CSS Profile - UAE National Students

- UAE National Undergraduate Students CSS Profile Instructions

For more information regarding where and how you can use this award, please refer to: Falcon Dirhams Available Vendors .

- NYUAD Travel Support Award

If your financial aid offer includes the NYUAD Travel Support (home travel), you should note that it is not a monetary award. Instead, you will receive additional information from the Office of Global Education regarding travel arrangements.

The Office of Global Education - Student Mobility administers travel for home, J-Term, and study away semesters for eligible students. For additional questions, you may email nyuad.studentmobility@nyu.edu .

- Estimated Cost of Attendance (COA)

The estimated cost of attendance (COA) represents the estimated annual cost for the current academic year as a full-time undergraduate student. These amounts may be slightly different than the actual charges on your university bill, as these figures are an estimate. The COA on the website reflects the fall and spring semesters only. Being enrolled in 12-18 credits is considered being a full-time student. If you are enrolling in summer and/or J-Term(s), the estimated COA for those semester(s) will be accessible on NYU Albert closer to the start of each semester.

Annual adjustments to the costs and fees at NYU Abu Dhabi may be necessary and should be expected. The estimated COA consists of direct and indirect expenses. The estimated cost of attendance is considered when renewing financial aid awards.

Direct expenses are costs that are charged by the university. The Student Finance Office will send out billing notifications each semester. Charges that will be displayed on your university bill will include tuition, books, health insurance, and NYU housing and food. Please note that in accordance with the Federal Decree Law No (8) of 2017, a Value Added Tax (VAT) will be applied to Estimated Health Insurance and the Estimated Meals (food) portion at the rate of 5 percent. Students are responsible for any remaining balance(s) that are not covered by your financial aid, which may include VAT charge(s) and any acquired fines (i.e., replacement ID, keys/cleaning/damage fees, late fees, etc.). If you have any questions regarding billing or charges you will need to contact our colleagues in the Student Finance Office at nyuad.studentfinance@nyu.edu . If you would like to learn more about how the itemized awards apply to your university bill, you should refer to the Student Finance Office: eSuite account section of the FAQs.

Indirect expenses are costs, estimated within the COA, that students may incur during the academic year. These estimates can be used for planning purposes for items that you should consider. You will not see these charges on your semester’s university (bursar) bill. These estimated expenses may vary for each student. Indirect costs include estimated personal and estimated travel expenses.

- Waiving and/or Opting out of Expenses

Financial aid awards can only be used for the specific charges they are designated for and cannot be applied to other fees. If a student waives, reduces, or opts out of a fee covered by an award, that aid cannot be redirected to other charges.

For example, if a student has a Food Grant as part of their aid and they decide to waive the NYU meal plan, the Food Grant will be cancelled as the charge will be removed from their bill.

- Studying Away

The NYU tuition, NYUAD health insurance, and AD Insurance VAT costs will remain the same as if you were studying in Abu Dhabi when enrolling in an NYU global site for your study away semester.

NYU housing and meal (food) charges will vary depending on the study site that you select. Your financial aid semester awards will apply the same way and for the same amounts towards your billed charges. Similar to any other semester that you are enrolled in, if a student's financial aid does not cover the entirety of the charges, the student will be responsible for the costs beyond those covered by their NYU Abu Dhabi financial aid.

As you are planning, you should make note that some of the costs, while studying away, may differ from when you are studying in Abu Dhabi. Such differences may be in your NYU housing/food or travel expenses. We advise that you review the estimated Study Away Costs for each NYU global site that you are considering from the NYU Office of Global Programs website .

We also recommend that students to contact the NYUAD Office of Global Education at nyuad.studyawaysupport@nyu.edu for any questions regarding the study away process.

- Student Finance Office: eSuite account

Below is an explanation of how your aid is applied to your university bill, which you can access via the eSuite portal.

If your financial aid offer includes:
NYUAD Tuition Grant or the Sh. Mohamed Scholarship — the amount offered will automatically apply to tuition charges.

NYUAD Book Grant — the amount offered will automatically apply to your NYUAD book charges.

NYUAD Health Insurance Grant — the amount offered will automatically apply to your NYUAD health insurance charges.

NYUAD Housing Grant or Sh. Mohamed Housing Grant — the amount offered will automatically apply to your NYU housing.

Note: If you opt out of NYU housing and meal plan, your NYUAD Housing Grant/ Sh. Mohamed Housing and NYUAD Food Grants will be canceled, as you will not incur charges for housing and meals through NYUAD. If you choose to retain only the NYUAD meal plan, your NYUAD Food Grant will remain unchanged. Grants cannot be transferred to other charges or carried forward to future semesters.

- Financial Aid and Leave of Absence (LOA)

Upon your return, you must meet the following: have earned academic credit in a minimum of 75 percent of the cumulative attempted credit hours, that you have a cumulative grade point average of at least 2.0, and enroll full-time (12 credits or more in the fall and spring semesters).

More detailed information about NYUAD academic standing can be found on the public website Academic Policies page and the student portal page on Leaves of Absence .

- Required J-Term Sessions

These are classes that NYU Abu Dhabi students must enroll in to meet their degree requirements. Although these are NYU Abu Dhabi classes, the course might be taught abroad, at various NYU sites. Only NYU Abu Dhabi students are eligible to enroll in these classes.

NYUAD tuition, program fee, and on-campus housing and meal (food)* charges will be covered by NYU Abu Dhabi for your required J-term session(s) as determined by your degree requirements. Please refer to the J-Term Academic Policy on the student portal for more information.

* In accordance with the Federal Decree Law No (8) of 2017, a Value Added Tax (VAT) will be applied to the Meals charge at the rate of 5%. Students who receive partial financial aid during the fall and spring semesters will be responsible for covering the VAT charges during any given semester, including J-Term and summer.

Summer Study in Abu Dhabi
These are the classes offered by NYU Abu Dhabi during the summer session that must be on campus. NYUAD tuition and on-campus housing and meal (food)* charges will be covered for an Abu Dhabi-based summer class . Additional summer terms may be supported based on demonstrated academic need, as determined by Academic Affairs. Please refer to the Summer Academic Policy on the student portal for more information.

* In accordance with the Federal Decree Law No (8) of 2017, a Value Added Tax (VAT) will be applied to the Meals charge at the rate of 5%. Students who receive partial financial aid during the fall and spring semesters will be responsible for covering the VAT charges during any given semester, including J-Term and summer.

Summer Study Away
These are classes during the summer session that are abroad and are offered by other NYU schools. NYU Abu Dhabi does not offer grant aid for summer classes abroad that are offered at other NYU schools. For tuition charges/billing inquiries, please contact the Student Finance Office at nyuad.studentfinance@nyu.edu .

- How to Manage, Budget, and Save Your Money

NYU is dedicated to providing a range of resources to help you build your financial literacy skills and knowledge to help you achieve financial stability and positive well-being during university and beyond. Visit our website to learn more about money management, understanding credit, saving, and other resources.
