We understand that sometimes institutional scholarships alone might not be sufficient to cover all of your educational costs. In addition to using your own financial resources, savings, and payment plans with NYUAD, students can research external scholarships that can be used at NYUAD.

There are various external organizations that offer scholarships to students pursuing an undergraduate degree in different majors. We recommend that you actively search for external scholarships, not just in your first year but in subsequent years as well, as some organizations may offer scholarships to students in their third or fourth year.

You can start your research on the NYU Financial Aid site under Scholarships and Grants from Other Organizations . Additional note: these links lead to third-party sites, so while we provide them as a helpful resource, NYUAD does not control or endorse their specific content.

Additionally, if you receive external scholarships, please notify us of this resource. External scholarships are considered in determining the amount of financial aid you receive from NYU Abu Dhabi. Your combined awards (from NYUAD and the external source) cannot exceed the annual estimated cost of attendance.

Students who have questions or concerns about their financial aid are encouraged to contact us.

Email: nyuad.financial.support@nyu.edu
Phone: US: +1-212-998-4488 (10am-4pm EST) | UAE: ​+971-2-628-7861 (10am-4pm GST).

Please include your NYU student ID number (your N#) in your email and have it available if you call.

sections.text:
- How to review your financial aid award

Your most up-to-date financial aid award is readily accessible on your NYU Albert Student Center by clicking on the Finances tab (the tab is on the left-hand side).

Returning students will receive notification from the NYU Abu Dhabi Office of Financial Aid with more details in early July on how to access your award for the upcoming year.

- Financial aid renewal — Non-UAE Nationals

Your financial aid will be renewed each academic year at the same level that you accepted upon Admission to NYU Abu Dhabi, as long as you meet the following requirements:

- Earn academic credit in a minimum of 75 percent of the cumulative attempted credit hours.

- Maintain a cumulative grade point average of at least 2.0.

- Enroll full-time (12 credits or more in the fall and spring semesters).

More information on Academic Standing can be found under the Academic Policies .

All continuing students can expect their awards for the upcoming academic year to be available in NYU Albert by early July .

- Financial aid renewal — UAE Nationals

Your Sheikh Mohamed bin Zayed NYUAD Scholarship for Exceptional Emirati Students will be renewed annually as long as you:

- Earn academic credit in a minimum of 75 percent of the cumulative attempted credit hours.

- Maintain a cumulative grade point average of at least 2.0.

- Enroll full-time (12 credits or more in the fall and spring semesters).

More information on Academic Standing can be found under the Academic Policies .

If you had received the Sh. Mohamed Personal Support (Falcon Dirhams) in a prior academic year, this award will be renewed automatically.

All continuing students can expect their awards for the upcoming academic year to be available in NYU Albert by early July .

If you are in your final semester and have been approved by the Academic Resource Center (ARC) to enroll under full-time credits (fewer than 12 credits), your tuition grant will be prorated based on the number of credits you enroll in.

If you enroll in:

- 6-8 credits, your NYUAD Tuition Grant will be prorated by 50% of the semester amount that you receive.

- 9-11 credits, your NYUAD Tuition Grant will be prorated by 75% of the semester amount that you receive.

If you have any additional questions about your financial aid, you should email us, the Office of Financial Aid at nyuad.financial.support@nyu.edu .

- CSS Profile — non-UAE National Students

If you are in your 2nd, 3rd, or 4th year, the Office of Financial Aid encourages you to submit a new CSS Profile. Submitting a new CSS Profile will provide our office with the most up-to-date information for the appeal funding consideration.

Please note: submitting an appeal request or a new CSS Profile does not automatically guarantee appeal funds will be granted. If you are eligible to receive appeal funds, this additional award is a one-time grant for the semester in which it is offered; it will not be automatically renewed in subsequent semester(s) as NYUAD does not re-evaluate for renewable grants in subsequent years.

Appeal deadlines and notification dates are available on the NYU Financial Aid website under the Abu Dhabi campus information.

- CSS Profile — UAE National Students

If you have received the Sh. Mohamed Personal Support (Falcon Dirhams) in a prior academic year, this award will be renewed automatically. Another CSS Profile is not necessary.

Emirati students who never filed a CSS Profile upon admission or in any previous academic year and who would like to be reviewed for the need-based Personal Support Award (Falcon Dirhams) need to submit a CSS Profile application.

- NYU (Abu Dhabi) CSS school code is 2785.

For 2026-2027, the annual personal support award is $2,364 for the academic year ($1,182 per semester). Demonstrated financial need and full-time enrollment (12 credits or more per semester) are required.

The Student Finance Office will be in communication regarding the disbursement of this award if you are eligible.

For questions about your semester university bill, refunds, or payments, you should contact the Student Finance Office at nyuad.studentfinance@nyu.edu

- IDOC: Additional Documentation Requested for the CSS Profile

The Office of Financial Aid will notify you if additional documentation is required to finalize our review of your CSS Profile. You will need to submit all documents through the Institutional Documentation Service (IDOC) portal via CollegeBoard's website . IDOC is a portal that NYU uses to securely obtain supporting financial documentation.

We strongly recommend that any documents, such as wage statements, uploaded to IDOC are submitted in English or with an English translation and figures converted into US Dollars (you can write the conversion on the document and indicate the currency that was used and date).

Additionally, be sure to include your name and NYU ID number (N#) on all of the pages that you are uploading. Submitting documents without an English translation and figures converted into US Dollars may result in a delay in reviewing your documentation.

- Estimated Cost of Attendance (COA)

The estimated cost of attendance (COA) represents the estimated annual cost for the current academic year as a full-time undergraduate student. These amounts may be slightly different than the actual charges on your university bill, as these figures are an estimate. The COA on the website reflects the fall and spring semesters only. Being enrolled in 12-18 credits is considered being a full-time student. If you are enrolling in summer and/or J-Term(s), the estimated COA for those semester(s) will be accessible on NYU Albert closer to the start of each semester.

Annual adjustments to the costs and fees at NYU Abu Dhabi may be necessary and should be expected. The estimated COA consists of direct and indirect expenses. The estimated cost of attendance is considered when renewing financial aid awards.

Direct expenses are costs that are charged by the university. The Student Finance Office will send out billing notifications each semester. You will not see these charges on your semester’s university (bursar) bill. These estimated expenses may vary for each student. Indirect costs include estimated personal and estimated travel expenses.

Financial aid awards can only be used for the specific charges they are designated for and cannot be applied to other fees. If a student waives, reduces, or opts out of a fee covered by an award, that aid cannot be redirected to other charges.

For example, if a student has a Food Grant as part of their aid and they decide to waive the NYU meal plan, the Food Grant will be cancelled as the charge will be removed from their bill.

title: Pre-Paid Cards · NYUAD Students
text:
Welcome to the FAB Prepaid Card information page. The FAB prepaid card will be issued to you at the start of your academic year and active until your graduation year. The purpose of FAB cards is to upload salary payments, stipends, reimbursements, and any other allowances and amounts due to NYUAD Students. All students regardless of their financial aid eligibility are entitled to receive a FAB Prepaid Card.

FAB Card Details

1. Collect Your FAB Card

If you have not already collected your FAB card, please visit the Student Link Center:

Campus Center (C2), Ground Floor

2. Fill Acknowledgement Form

Once you have collected your card, please notify student finance by filling the Acknowledgement Form of FAB card collections available in the student portal that the card is in your possession so that we safely and securely transfer the funds to your FAB card.

3. ATM PIN Setup

FAB card PIN to be set via FAB ATM only (DO NOT RESET). PIN set up can be done with UAE only. You will need to go physically to an ATM. See the ATM locations .

Unfortunately, this works only for UAE contact numbers, if you do not have one; you can fill out the form once you have a local SIM. You should also use this form to update your contact information in case of change of your contact information over the years.

Important note: This is the only way to generate a PIN on your card, the student finance card administrator or FAB contact center cannot generate a PIN for you.

4. Download the PayIT App

FAB provides a digital wallet product called PayIT that can be used to conduct payments domestically and make transfers or conduct transactions in a number of countries. Kindly ensure that the PayIT application is installed prior to departing the UAE as this is only available for download in the UAE. You can find details regarding the PayIT app below .

In case you face any issues from PayIT, all related concerns user(s) should directly contact below PayIT wallet customer care channels. Kindly include "NYU" in the subject of the email .

PayIT Wallet App Contact Support Channels
Phone number: +971-600-543-3229
Email: help@payit.ae (Using the registered email ID in PayIT wallet application)

5. Setup UAE Mobile Number

To be updated with the card to receive OTP’s of online transactions. You are expected to carry their sim even if outside the UAE. Please fill the Update Contact Information Form with your active UAE mobile number.

Using Your FAB Card

- Monitor Your Card Transactions

To monitor your transactions on your FAB prepaid card account, log into the FAB Card system and follow the login instructions.

Bank Statements
To receive a bank statement, please email the card administrator at nyuad.studentfinance@nyu.edu . Please allow five working days for the statement to be returned to you as it needs to be requested from the FAB team.

- Card Holder Fees

Please refer to the below table of fees applicable to your FAB prepaid card.

Charge Type | Amount | When | Who

Set-up Fee | Free | |

Card Replacement (lost/stolen) | AED 25.25 | Per usage | Cardholder

Card Closure | Free | |

Decline Fee | AED 2.1 | Per usage | Cardholder

FAB ATM — Cash Withdrawal | Free | |

FAB ATM — Balance Enquiry | Free | |

SWITCH ATM (UAE) — Cash Withdrawal | AED 2.1 | Per usage | Cardholder

SWITCH ATM (UAE) — Balance Enquiry | AED 2.1 | Per usage | Cardholder

FAB letter statement stapmed | AED 25.25 | Per request | Cardholder

- Withdrawal Limits

Please refer to the below table of transaction limits applicable to your FAB prepaid card.

Type | Limit

ATM Withdrawal Limit (Daily) | AED 5,000

Transaction Limit (Daily) | AED 5,000

- Card Transactions and Transferring Funds

The cards you have are prepaid cards managed through an NYUAD program, they are not traditional bank accounts, therefore only the University can transfer the funds into your prepaid card account. It is not possible for another entity to transfer funds into your prepaid card account.

You can use your card for card transactions at ATM machines, POS machines in stores and make online purchases.

It is possible to make a transfer to another account if you are eligible to use the PAYIT application and you are transferring to a country that is on the PAYIT platform. Please see details below under the PAYIT section.

In summary the transactions that can take place through your FAB prepaid cards are:

- Withdrawals

- Point-of-sale transactions (swiping of cards)

- Online transactions

- PAYIT transfers, if eligible

- PAYIT App (Digital Wallet)

FAB provides a digital wallet product called PAYIT that can be used to conduct payments domestically and make transfers or conduct transactions in a number of countries. Check if your country is included (PDF).

- General information (PDF)

- How to install the PAYIT App (PDF)

- How to make domestic payments using PAYIT (PDF)

- Card Benefits

As a recipient of a FAB prepaid card you are eligible to avail a number of benefits within the UAE.

- Please see the latest offers through FAB .

- View the Visa Platinum benefits .

Please note: these benefits are subject to change. Student Finance has no influence or control over these benefits and they are solely provided by FAB.

Safeguarding Your FAB Prepaid Card

You are responsible for the safety of your FAB Prepaid card. Please keep your Card and PIN safe at all times.

- If You Are Unable to Withdraw or Swipe Your Card

If you are unable to withdraw funds or use your prepaid card at any of the merchant stores or online, first please ensure that you are:

- Within the withdrawal limit of AED 5,000 per day

- Within the transaction limit of AED 5,000 per day

If you are within the above limits, please contact the card administrator through nyuad.studentfinance@nyu.edu .

Contact the FAB Card Administration

- Lost or Stolen Card

IF you have lost your card or suspect it has been stolen, please contact the FAB customer service line directly without delay at 600 5222 98 to block your card.

After blocking your card, please reach out to the Program Administrators at the NYUAD Student Finance Office nyuad.studentfinance@nyu.edu .

- Fraudulent Transactions on Your Account

To monitor your transactions on your FAB prepaid card account:

- Log into https://ppc.magnati.com/ppc- inquiry/ online or;

- Download the application

Transaction Dispute

You are strongly encouraged to regularly monitor your account to verify transactions made on your card. If you notice a fraudulent transaction appearing on your account statement, you should report it immediately by filling out the dispute form (PDF) and emailing it to nyuad.studentfinance@nyu.edu .

If you wish to block your card or reset your PIN you can contact the FAB customer service line directly without delay at 600 5222 98.

Important items to keep in mind when filing a dispute:

- Fraudulent transactions must be reported to FAB within 60 days from the date of the transaction. Student Finance will log the dispute form with FAB on your behalf however will need 3 days to do so. Please take this into account when emailing your dispute form to Student Finance.

- Please be advised that investigations undertaken by FAB may take up to 180 days to be resolved.

- Please also note that if the said transaction is in pending status FAB will only be able to raise the case once the transaction settles (eight days from the date of transaction).

- Wirecard Balance

If you have a substantial balance on your Wirecard, you should have received a notification from Student Finance opting to transfer the balance to your (or your guardian's or relative’s) bank account, as you cannot access the funds until you return to campus. You can also wait until you pick up your FAB card upon your return to campus. In order to opt for one of the options, kindly submit the Wirecard Balance Refund form here to submit your preference.

If your balance on Wirecard is less than AED 100, you will have to wait to access the funds upon your return to campus.

Safeguarding Your Prepaid Card

As the card holder you are responsible for the safety of your FAB Prepaid card. Please keep your Card and PIN safe at all times, here are some helpful hints and tips:

Security Tips

- Sign the strip on the back of your credit card as soon as you receive it.

- Get a PIN loaded onto your card as soon as possible.

- Never let anyone else use your credit card.

- Keep your credit card in a safe place.

- Don’t let your credit card bend or get scratched.

- Keep your card away from magnetised objects.

PIN Protection Tips

- Avoid using consecutive numbers, or numbers that are easily associated with you such as your birthday or house number.

- Don’t write down your PIN, especially on your card, or tell anyone else your PIN. This includes police, family members or bank staff. If you do, you may be liable for any loss from misuse of your card.

- Select a different PIN for different cards.

- Use your PIN when prompted by the EFTPOS terminal device.

Tips on Withdrawing Cash from the ATM

- Memorize your PIN and keep it confidential.

- Do not give out any information about your Card to any third party except when reporting any suspected or actual fraudulent transaction to the FAB Contact Center.

- Be aware of your surroundings before, during, and after you use an ATM. If you are apprehensive about your safety, cancel your transaction.

- Remember to remove your Card from the ATM and place withdrawn cash securely before exiting the ATM facility. Don't carry money in the open.

- Stand between the ATM and anyone waiting to use the ATM so others cannot see your PIN or the transaction amount.

- Always take your receipts, so you can check them against your transaction history. If your transaction was not completed, be sure to cancel the transaction prior to leaving the ATM.

title: Student Bill · NYUAD Students
text:
NYU's electronic billing system is the official means of generating bills to enrolled students. The bill will be sent to students electronically (by email) along with instructions for creating a student electronic bill profile.

Parents and other authorized users may also create a user profile related to the student bill and will be notified each time a new tuition bill is available.

- First-time Student Users

- Go to the NYU E-bill website .

- Click the SIGN UP! button and follow steps 1-3. Note: You will need your 8-digit student ID "N" number to set up your user profile.

- How to invite Parents/ Authorized Users to create their own user profile

- When you reach the Bill screen, click the MY PROFILE tab.

- Next, click the INVITE OTHER PAYER button. Enter your Parent's or Authorized User's name and e-mail address.

For a list of FAQs, visit the Bursar's page on our website .

- Value Added Tax (VAT) in the UAE

UAE government has implemented a value added tax (VAT) in the UAE effective 1st January 2018 and therefore the University is required to comply with the VAT laws and is required to charge VAT in accordance with the Federal Decree Law on Value Added Tax and its Executive Regulations issued under Cabinet Decision.

The impact to the cost of attendance is now confirmed and is as follows:

- Tuition, registration and book fees are 0% rated

- Housing fees are exempt from VAT

- The standard VAT rate of 5% will apply toHealth Insurance and Meal Plan fees in Abu Dhabi

A tax invoice will be sent in a format required by the UAE government. Please keep this tax invoice for your records. Please note that tax on this invoice only reflects the actual charges . To view your current Bursar account activity including all charges, financial aid , and payments, please visit the Bursar eSuite in the “Finances” section of Albert or review the steps given below.

- How to Check Your Bursar Account

To heck your balance, can log into your bursar account:

- Visit albert.nyu.edu/students and log in with your NYU NetID and password.

- Click Student Center .

- Select View Bursar Account located under the Finances section.

- Select View Activity .

- Click on the eBills tab to view your most recent billing statement.

You can also print your bill by term if you select Print Official Statement of Account .

- Enrollment and Registration Holds

If you have any fine on your account, you are not eligible to enroll for a payment plan for making payments against tuition.

A bursar registration hold blocks you from registration for classes for current and future terms due to an outstanding on your bursar account. Once you make a payment to clear the outstanding balance, this hold will be automatically removed.

- Apply for a Refund

If you have a credit balance on your bursar account due to over payment, adjustments to your charge or financial aid; you are eligible to request for a refund. In order to do so, please visit our website .

-

Paying Your Tuition Bill

- Payment Methods

- Electronic check (from a US bank account)

- Wire transfer (from a bank outside of the US)

- Personal check (from a US bank)

- Payment plans: The electronic bill will include instructions for setting up a payment plan if needed

More information is available on the Bursar's website .

- How to Pay Your Tuition Bill

- If you have a US Checking account , you can remit payment through the eSuite account. Learn how to log in using eSuite .

- If you have a non US account , you can remit the payment using Flywire which will post to your eSuite account .

- For Making the Payment Online Any Non-US Card

- Visit the International Payments page on the NYU website.

- Select Initiate student account payment for tuition and fees, etc. by Flywire .

- Click on Start Payment @ PAY YOUR STUDENT ACCOUNT BILL.

- USD Check (from US banks only)

- If you are paying with a personal or bank check, please write your student ID number on the check and mail to:

New York University
Office of the Bursar
StudentLink Center
383 Lafayette Street, 1st Floor
New York, NY 10003

Please note:

- Payment by eCheck and personal or bank check is accepted from U.S. financial institutions only.

- Postdated checks will not be accepted.

- If a check is returned, you will be charged a $20 returned check fee and a $25 late payment fee. You will also be prevented from using paper and electronic personal checks for future payment.

- Parents and authorized payers must be invited to create an eSuite account to make a payment.

- Payments made that exceed $10,000 over the account balance due will be applied to a future semester. Please contact our office before you initiate a payment if you have any additional questions about our policies or procedures.

Please note: currently we do not accept cash or Dirham Cheques for payment on tuition.

- Paying Fines on Your Bursar Account

You would like to pay for fines on your bursar account, you have the following options to make a payment

-
Using Debit or Credit card ( FAB or any other card) : Visit the Student Finance Office in A4, 1st Floor - Desk 150E by booking an appointment during the Walk-in hours:
Monday to Friday
10am to 12pm – book an appointment here
2pm to 3pm – book an appointment here

-
Falcon dirhams: Use this link .

- eCheck Payment: Use a US Checking account to remit payment through your eSuite account.

- Non-US Payment: Use a non US account to remit payment through Flywire which will post to your eSuite account, please visit the International Payments page on the NYU website.

Please note: currently we do not accept cash for payment on tuition.

- Deferred Payment Plans

This plan allows you to pay a percentage of the net balance due for the semester by the payment deadline, and defer the remaining amount to be paid later in the term.

For more details, please visit the NYU Deferred Payment Plan page .

Related official links:
https://students.nyuad.nyu.edu/services/financial-services/student-bill/payment-of-bursar-balance-via-falcon-dirhams/

title: Commuting Student Guidelines · NYUAD Students
text:
Commuting Guidelines

The students who do not reside on campus and are commuting have an option to opt out of the meal plan, resulting in no meal plan charge.

Please note any associated financial aid, e.g., housing grant or/and food grant will be cancelled upon commuting status and request for meal plan waiver respectively. The update will be reflected on your Student Center eSuite in five to seven days after the deadline.

If you wish to request a waiver for the meal plan during the semester, you can do so by filling out the Meal Plan Waiver Form . For any details related to your housing assignment for room allocation and allotment, please reach out to Residential Education at nyuad.ResLife@nyu.edu .

The Meal Plan Waiver approval is given on the basis of your Commuter status which means that you are not residing on campus for the entire duration of the related term. If this changes during the course of the term i.e., you enroll for on-campus housing, the FULL meal plan charge would be added to your account.

title: Student Bill and Cost of Attendance · NYUAD Students
text:
NYU Abu Dhabi offers a comprehensive cost of attendance that encompasses various charges to ensure a fulfilling student experience. The following charges are included:

Tuition
Understanding the terminology around student charges is made easier with our handy guide to tuition and fees . You can find detailed information about the tuition charges for NYU Abu Dhabi on our website .

Please note that tuition charges are based on the number of credits enrolled. A standard enrollment entails being enrolled full-time, which typically ranges from 12 to 18 credits per semester. It's important to keep in mind that adding or dropping classes after the billing date may result in corresponding changes to your tuition charges.

Books
To support your academic journey, NYU Abu Dhabi includes a mandatory book fee of USD 865 per semester. This fee is an essential component of your bill and cannot be waived or reduced upon request.

Insurance
As an enrolled student at NYU Abu Dhabi, you will receive both UAE and Global Insurance coverage. The insurance charge per semester is USD 1,208, which includes both local and global coverage.

If you are a UAE National and UAE Resident and choose not to shift to NYUAD Sponsorship and insurance, please inform the Health Center prior to the start of the academic year. We can then adjust your insurance charge to USD 460 per semester, as the global insurance is mandatory and cannot be waived as part of the NYU Abu Dhabi student profile.

Housing
For on-campus housing, NYU Abu Dhabi charges students USD 3,000 per semester. Your housing charge is determined based on the completion of your housing assignment.

NYUAD Meal Plan
To ensure that all enrolled students have access to meals of nutritious value, NYU Abu Dhabi requires a mandatory Abu Dhabi Meal Plan costing USD 2,900 per semester. Please note that you have the option to opt out of the meal plan only if you are commuting. Detailed information regarding this option is available on the Meal Plan Waiver form .

We strive to provide transparent information about the cost of attendance at NYU Abu Dhabi to assist you in planning for your educational journey. Should you have any further questions or require additional assistance, please do not hesitate to reach out on the contact information on this page.

For any inquiries related to financial aid, please refer to their dedicated webpage .

Website: https://nyuad.nyu.edu/en/admissions/undergraduate/financial-support.html

- Where can I view my Financial Aid award letter?

In order to check your Financial Award letter, you can log into your bursar account.

- Visit albert.nyu.edu/students and log in with your NYU NetID and password.

- Click Student Center .

- Select Accept/Decline Awards .

- Click on the academic year you would like to view.

- What is a Deferred Payment Plan?

This plan allows you to pay a percentage of the net balance due for the semester by the payment deadline, and defer the remaining amount to be paid later in the term.

For more details, please visit the NYU Deferred Payment Plan page .

- Why do I have a payment plan enrollment hold on my account?

If you have any fine on your account, you are not eligible to enroll for a payment plan for making payments against tuition.

- Why do I have a bursar registration hold on my account?

You have a bursar registration hold that blocks you from registration for classes for current and future terms due to an outstanding on your bursar account. Once you make a payment to clear the outstanding balance, this hold will be automatically removed.

- How can I receive a refund from the Medical Insurance company?

In order to receive a refund for insurance claim, request the Insurance for:

- US Check — if you have a US account or you are in the US to cash it

- Wire Transfer — if you have a non-US personal account

- If you do not have either of the above, you can request them to transfer the funds to NYUAD with the student ID as reference code. Once we receive it, we will notify you for collection. If you choose this option, please reach out to nyuad.studentfinance@nyu.edu for further assistance.

- How can I setup a personal bank account in UAE?

Please refer to the Banking and Personal Finances page .

title: Study Support · NYUAD Students
text:
Stipend Distribution, 2026-2027

Students eligible to receive personal study support stipends for the semester will receive them as follows:

- Students studying away will have their stipends deposited directly to their NYUAD-issued FAB cards.

- Students enrolled at the Abu Dhabi campus will receive their stipends as Falcon Dirhams, loaded onto their NYUAD ID cards.

Study Support through Falcon Dirhams

What Are Falcon Dirhams?

Falcon Dirhams are a form of campus digital currency that can be used for purchases at select merchants, including on-campus dining outlets, campus pharmacy, and other approved vendors. They are loaded directly onto students’ campus ID cards and are intended to support day-to-day personal study expenses while on campus. — View the list of approved merchants accepting Falcon Dirhams .

Upload Dates for 2026-2027

The upload dates for stipends for the 2026-2027 academic year are as follows:

- Fall 2026: Friday, September 18, 2026

- Spring 2027: Monday, February 8, 2027

Changes in Enrollment Status

In case of Leave of Absence, Term Withdrawal, or Total Withdrawal/Discontinued, the Study Support/Stipend will be prorated based on the date of enrollment status change .

If stipend has already been issued to the student, the student will be billed as follows:

Fall 2026 Billing Timeline

From | To | % Student Keeps | % Student is Billed

September 18 | October 3 | 0% | 100%

October 4 | October 28 | 25% | 75%

October 29 | November 22 | 50% | 50%

Nov 23 | December 17 | 75% | 25%

Dec 18 | Onwards | 100% | 0%

Spring 2027 Billing Timeline

From | To | % Student Keeps | % Student is Billed

February 8 | February 23 | 0% | 100%

February 24 | March 20 | 25% | 75%

March 21 | April 14 | 50% | 50%

April 15 | May 9 | 75% | 25%

May 10 | Onwards | 100% | 0%

Frequently Asked Questions

- I’m a UAE National student, do I receive Falcon Dirhams?

Please review the NYUAD Personal Support/Sheikh Mohamed bin Zayed Personal Support (Falcon Dirhams) Award section under Financial Aid and Renewal .

- Will students on study away receive expense support? What does this mean for study away allowance?

Funding provided aside from study support will not be affected by this directive. Funding for the study away allowance will be issued via FAB card for returning students. Students who have not been on campus to collect their FAB cards will be provided with alternative payment options until they are able to collect their university-issued FAB.

- Has the criteria for receiving expense support changed?

The criteria for the study support will remain the same for international students. UAE Nationals will need to complete an assessment to apply for support. As always, students are granted the study support through the Office of Financial Support based on financial need and must meet the academic credit load requirements. Funds in the form of Falcon Dirhams are distributed by the Office of Student Finance.

- What is the difference between Falcon Dirhams and Dining Dirhams?

Dining Dirhams form a part of the meal plan package and can be spent at food and beverage outlets across campus. Dining Dirhams expire at the end of each semester as defined in the calendar published on the student portal.

Falcon Dirhams can be spent at retailers that currently accept Dining Dirhams, and other campus retailers will be invited to start accepting Falcon Dirhams. Updates on those additional retailers will be provided as they become available.

Unlike Dining Dirhams, Falcon Dirhams will not expire at the end of each semester, rather they will expire at the end of the semester that you graduate. Falcon Dirhams can be tracked on Blackboard.

View the complete list of vendors applicable for both.

- What happens if I plan to enroll in fall, spring, and summer? Will there be separate expense support for each term including summer?

The study support is for the full year, disbursed in two installments in the fall and spring, so students should manage the amount to also cover J-Term and summer as required.

- When will the expense support be disbursed?

Falcon Dirhams will be distributed in two installments, one at the beginning of the fall semester and one early in the spring after the add/drop period.

- Are there any changes to meal plan Dining Dirhams?

Meal plan Dining Dirhams will remain the same. Details on this are available on the Meal Club page . Falcon Dirhams can be spent at retailers that currently accept Dining Dirhams, including the pharmacy and bookstore on campus.

- What happens to the study support if a student takes a Leave of Absence (LOA) or withdraws or does not meet the credit requirement?

Students who take LOA, withdraw, or do not meet the credit requirements to receive the study support will be required to make a refund of the expense support.

If this occurs within the add/drop period, then a full refund will be required, or on a pro-rata basis after add/drop.

The refund amount would be charged to the student account. Due to the changes in the disbursement method, instead of a refund in cash, the refund can be made through use of the next semester's Falcon Dirhams. Affected students can reach out to the Office of Student Finance for more information on the calculation and how this would apply to their situation.

- How will study support work for students who are stuck abroad due to travel restrictions?

All requests will be dealt with on an exceptional basis, and will require initial approval before a student commits funds. Approved support will be advanced to the student via FAB card or equivalent.

Related official links:
https://students.nyuad.nyu.edu/services/financial-services/study-support/falcon-dirhams-available-vendors/
https://students.nyuad.nyu.edu/services/financial-services/financial-aid/

title: Falcon Dirhams for Nirvana Bookings · NYUAD Students
text:
- Nirvana Standard Operating Procedures

Agent Availability:

- Two dedicated agents will be accessible at the Nirvana – NYUAD office during regular working days:
Monday to Friday, 8am to 5:30pm.

- On Saturdays, a single agent will be designated to attend to emergency booking requests, available from 8am to 4pm.

- On Sundays and during public holidays, the Falcon Dirham Travel Desk will be closed.

Booking Request Submission:

- All students should submit their booking requests via email, specifying their flight and hotel preferences.

- Our office will process these requests and provide booking details accordingly.

Processing Time:

- Booking requests will be processed within 5-6 hours during our office hours, 8am to 5pm. Processing time will be calculated based on these hours.

Portal Limitations:

- Please note that booking.com and Airbnb portals can only be used for accommodation bookings, not for other services like activities, etc.

Office Visit Scenarios:

- We encourage students to visit our office for the following scenarios, which will help our agents handle queries more efficiently.

- To make Airbnb accommodation bookings, where we will facilitate the payment process.

- For travel arrangements within 36 hours of travel dates, primarily for emergency purposes. We recommend booking well in advance to avoid price hikes.

- For assistance with complex flight options, students provide specific details for booking.

Nirvana Code of Conduct:

- All students are kindly requested to adhere to the above SOPs.

- We expect all students to follow the office morals, which include not engaging in arguments or questioning other agents when they visit our office after the dedicated office hours specified for Falcon booking requests. These guidelines are in place to ensure a smooth and efficient booking process for everyone. Your cooperation is appreciated.

- How to Send Travel Requests

Please send all your travel queries to a dedicated email: falcondirham@ntravel.ae . You can call a dedicated contact number in emergency situations at +971 2-304-6868 .

Working Hours
Monday to Friday: 9am-6pm
Off on Weekends and Public Holidays

Travel Services Offered

- Air ticket

- Hotel booking

- Airport transfers

- Parks entry tickets (in the UAE)

- Tours (in the UAE)

- Travel Insurance

- UAE Visa

- Car rental (Careem services discontinued)

- Leisure, sports activities, concerts (in the UAE)

Important Considerations

- Ticket date changes: Nirvana will make the date changes on the tickets purchased by the Global Ed team only after the changes are approved by the Global Ed team. (On Campus)

-
Early booking: Plan ahead and book in advance to secure the best fares and rates.

-
Terms and conditions: Read the terms and conditions of the services and clarify if you have any questions.

- Price Matching and Purchasing Mechanism

A: Low cost Airlines and Legacy Airlines to and from the UAE

- Nirvana quotes need to be benchmarked with the Airline website. Nirvana will price-match if there are any discrepancies between both quotes.

- Either Nirvana will buy through the GDS with special approval from the Airlines (in case of fare discrepancies) or through the Airline websites.

- Nirvana will not entertain procuring from a third party website (other than airlines websites) to benchmark their quote (Skyscanner and similar websites).

B: Flights outside of the UAE

- Non-UAE flights will only be booked if they are available in the Global Distribution System (GDS).

- Rate will be offered as per GDS only. Most of the time it will be in line with airline online rates with minor differences due to Rate of exchange or Airline running local country campaigns/promotions.

- Nirvana will not be able to produce any sort of evidence for not facilitating non-GDS booking to students.

Agreed Service Fee:

- Agreed commercial of 1.75% will be in place on top of procured supplier rate.

- Screenshot of original fare purchased will be available to the NYUAD travel team for review.

- Accommodation Booking

- Nirvana will only benchmark with “ booking.com ,” “ expedia.com ” and “ hotels.com ” and not any other online aggregator; however, they will engage with the hotels directly to complete the booking to avoid payment issues caused by intermediaries in the process. Nirvana will only confirm the booking once the facility confirms the booking and payment to Nirvana.

-
Nirvana will book Airbnbs with the following conditions:

-
Nirvana will facilitate by sharing their Virtual card for payment only. The card will be valid for a specified amount and for a single transaction.

-
Nirvana will not book Airbnb on behalf of students, and students must use their own profile and approach Nirvana campus office to obtain the card information to input to complete their booking.

-
Nirvana will not share corporate card information either via email or via phone to students.

- Payment Methods

A combination of maximum five Falcon Dirham cards and other credit cards can be used for payments.

- When do I expect a response to my request?

- An auto acknowledgment will be sent across at receipt of email through the system itself. Post that will respond with complete information addressing all their queries on or before four Business working hours .

- Our working hours are from 9am-6pm, Monday to Friday.

We recommend to pre-plan your trip well in advance to optimize cost to avail lowest possible rates to enjoy the maximum usage of your falcon dirhams

- Walk-in hours during the peak periods

- Fall Break 2022: October 19-23, 2022

- Winter Break: December 21, 2022 - January 3, 2023

- Spring Break: March 15-22, 2023

Dedicated staff are available one month prior to peak periods.

Students are requested to use this facility only for those requests not responded to within four business hours .

- Emergency

Emergency means people stuck at hotel properties or airports and facing some challenges on their existing booking done by Nirvana. If anyone has not received a response for his/her email post after the four business hours , they can approach our counter.

- Complaints and Appreciation

Nirvana Feedback Survey

Mudaliar Murugan
Executive Director of Operations
Email: Mudaliar.Murugan@ntravel.ae

Complete the Confirmation Form

This form should be used once you have made booking arrangements with Nirvana.

This form captures your ID information for Nirvana and also confirms to Nirvana you would like them to use your Falcon Dirhams to make payment for the agreed services.

title: Graduate School Related Expenses · NYUAD Students
text:
Student Finance together with the Career Development Center has created a process to allow juniors and seniors to elect to set aside a portion of their stipend disbursement to be utilized for graduate school related expenses. We recognize that this is a common use of the personal stipend and the following process is intended to ensure students are able to access the stipend for this purpose.

Request for Graduate School Expense Account

Students will be able to elect for funds to be set aside from their stipend, these elected funds would be put in an individual ‘graduate school expense account’ for use by the individual student. Students can elect to set aside funds from their fall and spring semesters stipend as follows:

Fall stipend, as the disbursement has occurred already the amount to be set aside can be equal to the amount of falcon dirhams remaining in the student's Blackboard account. If you did not receive falcon dirhams you would not be able to set aside funds from the fall disbursement.

Spring stipend, you can select to have up to your full spring semester stipend allocated to your graduate school expense account.

If you have selected an amount from your spring stipend and you do not qualify for the stipend in the spring semester it will be taken from your next stipend disbursement when that maybe, or refundable to the University.

For juniors, these allocations can be cumulative, you can begin to set aside funds from this year's disbursement and add to your account from next year's stipend to build up the required funding needed for your graduate school-related expenses.

Please note, the funds that are set aside for graduate school-related expenses are limited to graduate school admissions fees, standardized test preparation materials, standardized testing administration fees, and standardized test preparation courses not funded through the CDC STPA award .

To elect to set aside a portion of your stipend disbursement please complete the application form.

Process for Reimbursement

Once your account has been created and funding applied in early November, you will be able to initiate reimbursement requests for eligible graduate school expenses. In early November the CDC will release a form on the student portal from which you can make the reimbursement request.

The form will require the following details:

- Name/NetID

- Vendor details

- Confirm amount of purchase

- Date of purchase rendered

- Upload receipt

- Verification declaration

The form will be verified by a member of the CDC and you would be notified by email of the acceptance of your reimbursement request. The reimbursement would be issued to your Wirecard.

Students can seek an advance in extenuating circumstances, if you believe this applies to you please reach out to nyuad.career@nyu.edu .

Opting Out

Students may decide they no longer need to hold a graduate school expense account. Or have reached their graduating semester and have completed all their applications. Students would need to make a request through a form (this form will be created and available on the student portal) to close their account or the account will be automatically closed by the 22nd of April of your graduating year.

The remaining funds in the grad school expenses account would be returned to students. This would be returned via the relevant multi-vendor card.

If you have questions regarding the above process please contact nyuad.studentfinance@nyu.edu .

Related official links:
https://students.nyuad.nyu.edu/student-affairs/career-development/grants/test-preparation-award/

title: Legal Services · NYUAD Students
text:
Office of General Counsel (OGC) at NYU Abu Dhabi

Welcome to the Office of General Counsel! We provide legal support and services to NYU Abu Dhabi community. Our team is dedicated to partnering with you to ensure that our campus operates compliantly while fostering excellence and a supportive academic, research, and administrative environment.

Our partnership with NYU’s Office of General Counsel in New York, coupled with specialist experience in the UAE is a key part of our service delivery. This collaboration allows us to deliver seamless, coordinated legal services to better serve the NYU Abu Dhabi community.

If you have any further queries, please direct your questions to the OGC at nyuad.legal@nyu.edu .

OGC Resources

- A Quick Guide to UAE Employment Law

- UAE Criminal Procedure

- Onshore UAE Civil Court System

- UAE Personal Status Law Workshop

Helpful NYUAD Resources and Other Links

- NYU Law Library

- NYU Office of Equal Opportunity

- List of Law Firms

- Undergraduate Academic Policies

Note: While every effort has been made to ensure the accuracy and relevance of the content, the information contained herein does not constitute, and should not be construed as, official or personal legal advice. Users of this resource are encouraged to seek legal counsel for advice regarding their specific legal circumstance.

UAE Law

- Laws Relevant to NYUAD
The NYUAD OGC Legal Register is a detailed compilation summarizing the key provisions of laws, regulations, decisions, and circulars relevant to various areas of NYUAD’s operations. Its purpose is to support compliance efforts and promote operational excellence.

Please note that this register is not a legal document and does not constitute legal advice. For any inquiries, feel free to contact us at nyuad.legal@nyu.edu .

- View the Legal Register

- Other Laws
OGC also provides a description of UAE laws that impact common daily activities or other matters that may be relevant to the NYU Abu Dhabi community here:

- View Inventory of Laws

title: Faculty Awards · NYUAD Students
text:
NYUAD faculty are world-class researchers and scholars, devoted teachers and mentors, dedicated to the mission of the institution and their disciplines.

Awards Ceremony

Recipients of the Faculty Awards will be recognized with an awards ceremony in their honor on Thursday, May 11, 2023, and receive an honorarium of USD 1,000 and a special and durable memento that signifies the appreciation of the institution for the accomplishment of each awardee.

Register your attendance on Thursday, May 11, 2023.

2022-2023 Winners

Transformative Research Award

- Kemal Celik , Assistant Professor of Civil and Urban Engineering, Engineering Division

- Marsha Ginsberg , Associate Arts Professor of Theater, Arts and Humanities Division

- Justin Stearns , Professor of Arab Crossroads, Arts and Humanities Division

Award for Teaching Excellence

- Sohmyung Ha , Assistant Professor of Electrical and Computer Engineering, Engineering Division

- Angelyn Hilgendorf , Senior Lecturer, Academic Enrichment

- Ilya Spitkovsky , Professor of Mathematics, Science Division

Distinguished Service Award

- Olivier Bochet , Associate Professor of Economics, Social Science Division

- Nizar Habash , Professor of Computer Science, Science Division

Categories

The NYUAD Transformative Research Award will be bestowed on up to two (2) standing faculty members at any stage of their research career for transformative and highly impactful research and creative accomplishments that have been published, performed, or otherwise released to the world in the past 3 calendar years (2020-2023). Faculty who are early in their careers will be evaluated based on the promise of research impact, while seasoned faculty will be assessed based on both impact and track record.

The NYUAD Award for Teaching Excellence will recognize outstanding contributions to the educational mission of NYUAD. This award will be bestowed on faculty who will be recognized for excellence in liberal arts education, research mentorship, creativity and innovation in teaching.

NYUAD Distinguished Service Award for standing faculty members who have a history of exemplary service to the University, whether it be through governance or any other service that advances the mission of NYUAD being an innovative, forward looking and inclusive institution. Eligible candidates will have participated in university service for at least one full academic year in the past three years.

Research

Who can be nominated? Eligibility requirements for nominees:

- Currently employed as a full time member of the NYUAD standing faculty

- Completed at least three (3) years of continuous service as an NYUAD standing faculty member in spring 2023

- Previous award recipients and those serving in senior leadership positions (dean, vice provost) are ineligible

- Faculty can be nominated for more than one award

- Any student, alumni, standing, affiliated, visiting and adjunct faculty, administrative, academic and research staff can nominate

- Any faculty member who meets the eligibility requirements can self nominate

- Nominations by students who are enrolled in a course this semester where the faculty member being nominated is responsible for assigning the final grade for the course are not permitted.

title: Service Excellence Awards · NYUAD Students
text:
The NYUAD Service Excellence Awards recognize and celebrate NYUAD administrative, academic, and research staff who demonstrate core institutional values at an exceptional level in the performance of their roles.

To determine the recipients, the selection committee reviews nominations anonymously and will consider many characteristics, but the below criteria will be broadly applied. Each nominee should excel in one or more of the following competencies and values:

Integrity Taking personal accountability to uphold ethical standards; building trusting relationships through honesty, openness, fairness, and candor; and living up to commitments. | Respect Demonstrating a genuine appreciation for others, valuing diversity by treating everyone with high regard and consideration for their individual differences as well as maintaining the highest level of professionalism when working with others through challenging issues. | Customer Focus Providing an excellent level of service to both internal and external customers, identifying and responding to current and future client needs.

Teamwork and Collaboration Collaborate seamlessly across organizational boundaries to achieve shared goals of customer centricity. Working effectively within and across departments; collaborating with others to achieve common goals; and listening and communicating in a way that respects and supports others. | Adaptability and Innovation Adjusting your own behavior to work efficiently and effectively in light of new information, changing situations, and/or different environments. Successfully researching or implementing a new innovative idea to achieve creative accomplishments. | Diversity and Inclusion Demonstrating commitment to values of diversity, equity, and inclusion in performance of responsibilities and in interactions with members of the NYU community.

Additionally, managers who are nominated should also excel in one or more of the following areas:

Mentoring Encouraging employees to be their very best by providing feedback, development opportunities, positive reinforcement, and appreciation for their efforts. | Modeling Setting a positive example by remaining calm in a crisis, encouraging and supporting collaboration and teamwork, demonstrating inclusion, respect and tact, exhibiting humility, helping others achieve success, and being honest and trustworthy. | Motivating Inspiring commitment, providing vision, promoting and ensuring alignment with school/unit and NYU’s goals and/or values and providing coaching and performance management.

Recognition of Winners

Recipients of the Service Excellence Award will be recognized with an awards ceremony in their honor on Thursday, May 11, 2023, and receive an honorarium of USD 1,000 and a special and durable memento that signifies the appreciation of the institution for the accomplishment of each awardee.

Register your attendance on Thursday, May 11, 2023.

title: Earthquake Safety Tips · NYUAD Students
text:
The following safety tips of what to do in case of an earthquake are provided by the US Federal Emergency Management Agency ( http://www.ready.gov/earthquakes ). Please also be aware that there is always a potential for aftershocks after the initial activity, so it is essential that you remain on high alert.

If Indoors

- DROP to the ground; take COVER by getting under a sturdy table or another piece of furniture; and HOLD ON until the shaking stops. If there isn’t a table or desk near you, cover your face and head with your arms and crouch in an inside corner of the building.

- Stay away from glass, windows, outside doors and walls, and anything that could fall, such as lighting fixtures or furniture.

- Stay in bed if you are there when the earthquake strikes. Hold on and protect your head with a pillow, unless you are under a heavy light fixture that could fall. In that case, move to the nearest safe place.

- Do not use a doorway except if you know it is a strongly supported, load-bearing doorway and it is close to you. Many inside doorways are lightly constructed and do not offer protection.

- Stay inside until the shaking stops and it is safe to go outside. Do not exit a building during the shaking. Research has shown that most injuries occur when people inside buildings attempt to move to a different location inside the building or try to leave.

- DO NOT use the elevators.

- Be aware that the electricity may go out or the sprinkler systems or fire alarms may turn on.

And please note, if you are at a campus facility, be guided by the instructions of first responders (ie, NYUAD Department of Public Safety, Civil Defence, Police, Fire, etc.).

If Outdoors

- Stay there.

- Move away from buildings, streetlights, and utility wires.

- Once in the open, stay there until the shaking stops. The greatest danger exists directly outside buildings, at exits and alongside exterior walls. Many of the 120 fatalities from the 1933 Long Beach earthquake occurred when people ran outside of buildings only to be killed by falling debris from collapsing walls. Ground movement during an earthquake is seldom the direct cause of death or injury. Most earthquake-related casualties result from collapsing walls, flying glass, and falling objects.

If in a Moving Vehicle

- Stop as quickly as safety permits and stay in the vehicle. Avoid stopping near or under buildings, trees, overpasses, and utility wires.

- Proceed cautiously once the earthquake has stopped. Avoid roads, bridges, or ramps that might have been damaged by the earthquake.

If Trapped Under Debris

- Do not light a match.

- Do not move about or kick up dust.

- Cover your mouth with a handkerchief or clothing.

- Tap on a pipe or wall so rescuers can locate you. Use a whistle if one is available. Shout only as a last resort. Shouting can cause you to inhale dangerous amounts of dust.

Mass Notification

The safety of all members of the NYUAD community is a top priority.

The ability of authorized university administrators to communicate with members of the NYUAD community in a matter of minutes following an emergency is of critical importance in keeping everyone safe. NYUAD has the capability to send blast text messages to mobile devices in order to provide members of the NYUAD community with direct and timely information. These emergency communications allow recipients to respond safely to emergencies with real-time updates.

NYUAD students are urged to update their cell phone numbers in their student profile .

About the Office of Campus Safety

Led by a team of highly experienced security professionals and staffed by trained security practitioners, NYUAD Campus Safety operates 24 hours a day, seven days a week, and is committed to ensuring the safety of the university's students, faculty, staff, and visitors. The NYUAD Campus Safety team maintains a visible presence with uniformed security guards stationed throughout all campus locations. The department utilizes state-of-the-art technology at all campus locations to assist in achieving its goal of maintaining a safe and secure campus environment at all times. In case of certain emergencies, the department has a mass notification system designed to alert the NYUAD community in a matter of minutes by text, email, and voice messages. To ensure the hands-on involvement of Campus Safety leadership, senior members of the team reside on or near campus, making them immediately available to respond to incidents at all hours. The Campus Safety team also maintains strong and enduring partnerships with Abu Dhabi law enforcement agencies, and with local embassies and consulates.

title: Emergency Preparedness · NYUAD Students
text:
Campus Safety is committed to fostering a more resilient community to ensure our students, faculty, and staff are informed, prepared, and protected while pursuing their endeavors throughout the world.

Emergency Procedures and Resources

- National Emergency Crisis and Disasters Management Authority (NCEMA) Guide for Dealing with Emergencies (PDF)

- Download Personal Preparedness Checklist (PDF)

- Personal Safety Advice for Sheltering (PDF)

Security Incident Notification

Notify the nearest security officer as soon as an incident has occurred or contact the Campus Safety Control Room 0n 02 628 7777.

NYUAD Buildings Evacuation

If the fire alarm is activated, evacuate the premises IMMEDIATELY and assemble at the designated assembly points.

- View the Emergency Assembly Points for Saadiyat (PDF)

- View the Fire Instructions for Saadiyat (PDF)

RAVE Alert

The RAVE Alert system uses the contact information provided in Albert and PeopleSync ( nyuad.peoplelink@nyu.edu ), so please make sure your UAE contact information is up-to-date.

Public Safety is pleased to announce the activation of the Opt-In function for the NYUAD Rave Emergency Notification System. NYUAD community members that are not enrolled in PeopleSync or Albert such as contract staff, NYUAD affiliates, and guests may now Opt-In to receive NYUAD Rave Emergency Notifications during emergencies or incidents that adversely affect our Campus and community.

To enroll, text NYUAD at +6148-884-1667. The following options are available:

- 1-day opt-in: text NYUADALERT1 to +6148-884-1667

- 7-days opt-in: text NYUADALERT7 to +6148-884-1667

- 6-months opt-in : text NYUADCommunity to +6148-884-1667

- 1-year opt-in: text NYUAD to +6148-884-1667

You will receive the following message: "Welcome to NYUAD Alert. This mobile number has been subscribed to NYU Abu Dhabi's alert system."

Upon expiration, you will receive the following message: "Your enrollment in NYUAD Alert has expired. To re-enroll text NYUAD to +61488841667.

When receiving a RAVE alert

In an emergency or an urgent need, the university will send a notification to the contact details we have on file for you. You may receive a notification from RALERT on your mobile phone, or to your NYU and/or personal email address from emergencymanagement@nyu.edu.

Safe NYU App

Safe NYU is New York University’s free mobile campus safety app, developed by the Department of Campus Safety and its Campus Safety Operations division.

The app provides safety and security services, including:

- 999-calling capability for life-threatening situations

- Push Notifications

- Mobile Blue Light: simultaneously send your location and call NYU Campus Safety

- Reporting of incidents or tips via in-app forms, real-time chats or voice calls

Providing safety information for more than 190 countries on six continents, the Safe NYU app goes where you go, offering preparedness tips, transportation information, and emergency numbers at the tap of an icon.

The app also includes links to support resources including victim assistance, the wellness exchange and the bias response line.

To download the app, please click on the links below for your preferred version

- Apple App Store

- Andriod App on Google Play

Personal Preparedness

Do you know what to do in the event of an emergency? Do you know where to get information or how to get in contact with friends and family? It's important to think about these questions before an emergency and have a personal preparedness plan.

Personal preparedness is as easy as one, two, three. The guide and checklist below will help you enhance your personal preparedness in the event of an emergency.

- Step 1 - Get Educated

Learn about safety and preparedness at NYUAD. Find information on the NYUAD Campus Safety section and about the Safe NYU app. Discover information about different threats and hazards and how to prepare for them.

Visit your local embassy's website to register and to read the alerts and warnings.

To request a meeting with Campus Safety to discuss your own personal emergency plan, email

- Step 2 - Get Notified

Download the Safe NYU app and make sure the university has your current cell phone number so that you will receive university emergency alerts. Keep in mind that NYU issues alerts for campus emergencies and weather closures. You may want to be informed about other types of emergencies, such as those affecting other areas of the city, roadways or transportation systems. Consider signing up for alerts issued by Abu Dhabi Ministry of Interior . Media outlets and apps can also provide information regarding emergencies.

A note about social media: When viewing social media for emergency information, make sure to follow authoritative accounts that provide confirmed information. If you are near an emergency, be sure to focus on your safety rather than attempt to post to social media.

- Step 3 - Get Ready

Take action - Turn all of your preparedness research into an actionable plan. Take proactive steps to be ready. Get a flu shot. Practice different evacuation routes from the places you typically go. Collect important information such as critical phone numbers, prescription and insurance information in a paper file stored in a watertight container and make sure it’s backed up electronically in a secure place. Participate in campus trainings and exercises.

Be ready. Tell your classmates and colleagues that you are taking all of these steps to be prepared. Encourage them to be a part of Resilient NYUAD!

Disabilities, Access and Functional Needs
If you require additional assistance in an emergency, be sure to identify your needs ahead of time and communicate them to others. Develop a plan that makes sense for your specific situation. Wear medical alert tags or bracelets and be prepared to tell emergency personnel if you have a disability, use a mobility aide or service animal, whether you have allergies, phobias, or a language barrier. Know the names of all your medications. If you use an augmentative communications device or other assistive technologies, plan how you will evacuate with the devices or how you will replace equipment if lost or destroyed. Include appropriate supplies in your go bag and emergency supply kit. If you use assistive technology devices, such as white canes, CCTV, text-to-speech software, keep information about model numbers and where you purchased the equipment. Plan how you will communicate with others if your equipment is not working.

Communications Plan for Classes, Office, Family and Friends
Write down phone numbers and email addresses for the important people in your life. Having this important information written down will help you reconnect with others in case you don’t have your mobile device or computer with you or if the battery runs down. If you have a household member(s) who is Deaf or hard of hearing, or who has a speech disability and uses traditional or video relay service (VRS), include information on how to connect through relay services on a landline phone, mobile device, or computer. Be sure to identify an out-of-town contact as a central point of contact in case local phone lines are not working.

For your classes or work environments, discuss how you will communicate with each other in an emergency. Develop a plan with different options for contacting each other depending upon available technologies. If voice lines are not working, texting may be an option. Online course environments may allow for virtual class meetings, depending on the situation. If you are a leader, be sure to communicate with the people who rely on your leadership.

Emergency Meeting Places
Decide on safe, familiar places where you can go for protection or to reunite. Make sure these locations are accessible for persons with disabilities or access and functional needs. If you have pets or service animals, think about animal-friendly locations. You should identify meeting places that are local as well as out of the area and communicate these locations to everyone who is part of your plan.

sections.title: Emergency Procedures and Resources · Personal Preparedness
sections.text:
Do you know what to do in the event of an emergency? Do you know where to get information or how to get in contact with friends and family? It's important to think about these questions before an emergency and have a personal preparedness plan.

Personal preparedness is as easy as one, two, three. The guide and checklist below will help you enhance your personal preparedness in the event of an emergency.

- Step 1 - Get Educated

Learn about safety and preparedness at NYUAD. Find information on the NYUAD Campus Safety section and about the Safe NYU app. Discover information about different threats and hazards and how to prepare for them.

Visit your local embassy's website to register and to read the alerts and warnings.

To request a meeting with Campus Safety to discuss your own personal emergency plan, email

- Step 2 - Get Notified

Download the Safe NYU app and make sure the university has your current cell phone number so that you will receive university emergency alerts. Keep in mind that NYU issues alerts for campus emergencies and weather closures. You may want to be informed about other types of emergencies, such as those affecting other areas of the city, roadways or transportation systems. Consider signing up for alerts issued by Abu Dhabi Ministry of Interior . Media outlets and apps can also provide information regarding emergencies.

A note about social media: When viewing social media for emergency information, make sure to follow authoritative accounts that provide confirmed information. If you are near an emergency, be sure to focus on your safety rather than attempt to post to social media.

- Step 3 - Get Ready

Take action - Turn all of your preparedness research into an actionable plan. Take proactive steps to be ready. Get a flu shot. Practice different evacuation routes from the places you typically go. Collect important information such as critical phone numbers, prescription and insurance information in a paper file stored in a watertight container and make sure it’s backed up electronically in a secure place. Participate in campus trainings and exercises.

Be ready. Tell your classmates and colleagues that you are taking all of these steps to be prepared. Encourage them to be a part of Resilient NYUAD!

Disabilities, Access and Functional Needs
If you require additional assistance in an emergency, be sure to identify your needs ahead of time and communicate them to others. Develop a plan that makes sense for your specific situation. Wear medical alert tags or bracelets and be prepared to tell emergency personnel if you have a disability, use a mobility aide or service animal, whether you have allergies, phobias, or a language barrier. Know the names of all your medications. If you use an augmentative communications device or other assistive technologies, plan how you will evacuate with the devices or how you will replace equipment if lost or destroyed. Include appropriate supplies in your go bag and emergency supply kit. If you use assistive technology devices, such as white canes, CCTV, text-to-speech software, keep information about model numbers and where you purchased the equipment. Plan how you will communicate with others if your equipment is not working.

Communications Plan for Classes, Office, Family and Friends
Write down phone numbers and email addresses for the important people in your life. Having this important information written down will help you reconnect with others in case you don’t have your mobile device or computer with you or if the battery runs down. If you have a household member(s) who is Deaf or hard of hearing, or who has a speech disability and uses traditional or video relay service (VRS), include information on how to connect through relay services on a landline phone, mobile device, or computer. Be sure to identify an out-of-town contact as a central point of contact in case local phone lines are not working.

For your classes or work environments, discuss how you will communicate with each other in an emergency. Develop a plan with different options for contacting each other depending upon available technologies. If voice lines are not working, texting may be an option. Online course environments may allow for virtual class meetings, depending on the situation. If you are a leader, be sure to communicate with the people who rely on your leadership.

Emergency Meeting Places
Decide on safe, familiar places where you can go for protection or to reunite. Make sure these locations are accessible for persons with disabilities or access and functional needs. If you have pets or service animals, think about animal-friendly locations. You should identify meeting places that are local as well as out of the area and communicate these locations to everyone who is part of your plan.

title: Lost and Found · NYUAD Students
text:
The NYUAD Campus Safety Department is the central repository for all found property. Any recovered property should be turned over to the Campus Safety main reception desk situated at Saadiyat East Administration Building (A4), Level 1; or, if necessary, a security representative will be dispatched to retrieve the article by calling 02-628-7777 (or 87777 from a campus phone).

Lost and Found operates 24 hours a day, seven days a week. Members of the NYUAD community who wish to inquire about lost items may contact any security guard, call the Campus Safety Department at +971 2-628-7777 (or 87777 from a campus phone).

The Campus Safety Department will store found property in a secure location and make all reasonable attempts to locate the property owner. All unclaimed items, except cash, valuable jewelry, and NYUCards, will be held for 30 days. Unclaimed items will then be disposed of by appropriate means. Cash and valuable jewelry will be immediately forwarded to the local police for vouchering and safekeeping. NYUCards will be destroyed (shredded) immediately. Anyone claiming property at the Lost and Found Department must show a valid NYUCard or other valid identification.
