title: Safety Tips · NYUAD Students
text:
Abu Dhabi is considered one of the safest large cities in the world. Nevertheless, it is a good idea to take certain precautions. While violent crimes and crimes against property are rare, they do occur. Students who are victims of crimes should immediately contact NYUAD Public Safety at +971 2-628 7777 (or 87777 from a campus phone). Campus Safety personnel will help them contact the police and receive support services. (The number for all emergency services in the UAE is 999.)

The following safety tips are recommended to assist members of the NYUAD community in everyday life and while using university facilities in Abu Dhabi and around the world:

- Do not go out alone at night. Buddy up or go in small groups. There is greater safety in numbers, especially when you are getting to know a new location and its diversity of unfamiliar environments.

- When traveling in a group, be sure everyone in the group comes back together. Don't leave anyone behind.

- Always plan your trips with the help of an NYUAD staff member. Make sure you have transport back before you go out so that you never become stranded. Let a staff member know where you are going and when you expect to be back. Research the location of your destination and carry a map. Note street names and nearby landmarks. If you need help planning your trip or are unsure about the safety of the destination, please ask an NYUAD staff member for help.

- Do not dress in a way that marks you as an affluent tourist. Expensive-looking jewelry, for instance, can draw the wrong attention.

- Be aware of your surroundings. Try to minimize the use of headphones and other devices that can jeopardize your recognition of potential dangers.

- Knapsacks and backpacks should always be tightly closed and stored on your lap or where they can be seen at all times while in restaurants or other public venues. NYUAD's Office of Campus Safety will provide free gear guard locks for backpacks and bags with zippers.

- Carry a cell phone at all times and ensure that it is charged.

- In Abu Dhabi, cell phones should be pre-programmed to automatically dial the NYUAD Office of Campus Safety at +971 2-628 7777 (or 87777 from a campus phone).

- Always carry the NYUAD Contact Numbers card, your NYUAD ID card, and a photocopy of the pages of your passport that include your photo and your visa.

- Always carry the UAE ID Card, as this is a legal requirement. Students will be issued UAE ID cards after they have obtained resident student visas.

- Use university transportation whenever possible.

- Travel on streets where there is pedestrian traffic. During evenings, plan a route where streets are well lit. Avoid walking through road tunnels (pedestrian underpasses) on your own at night.

- Use silver taxis rather than yellow or white taxis whenever possible. The name of the taxi driver and the number of the cab is displayed on the monitor in the taxi. We recommend that you always jot it down or text it to an NYUAD friend along with your destination. Make sure someone knows where you are going and when you anticipate being back.

- Females should never ride in the front of a taxi next to the driver, and women traveling alone should not engage drivers in friendly discussion. It is perfectly acceptable to travel in silence after having given the driver your destination.

- If you cannot find a taxi in Abu Dhabi, call 600 53 53 53. That is a taxi dispatch service. Describe as best you can where you are located. Give landmarks and cross streets as part of the description if possible. You will be charged an additional 5 AED on top of your fare for calling for a taxi.

- If you get stranded and cannot reach a taxi dispatch service, call NYUAD Campus Safety at +971 2-628 7777 (24 hours a day, seven days a week).

- If you find yourself in any situation in which you feel uncomfortable or afraid for your safety, immediately call NYUAD Campus Safety at +971 2-628 7777 for advice and assistance.

- If a taxi driver does not know the location of NYUAD Campus, tell the driver "Saadiyat Island, next to Saadiyat Beach"

- Never accept a ride on your own from someone you have just met or do not know well, no matter how helpful or friendly that person may seem. Politely but firmly decline all such invitations.

- Never accept a ride in a vehicle driven by someone who has been drinking alcohol. Politely but firmly decline all such invitations.

- Know that taxi cab drivers have been known to transport intoxicated passengers directly to the police station.

- Lock your apartment at all times.

- Avoid counting money on the street after obtaining funds from an ATM, and don't carry large amounts of cash.

- Do not leave laptop computers or other valuable items unattended in cafes or other public areas.

- Never leave what you are drinking or eating unattended in public places.

- All valuable items should be safely secured at home, including valuable or expensive-looking jewelry, irreplaceable family objects, and all unnecessary credit cards.

- Avoid photographing Muslim women, and do not photograph airports, docks, telecommunications equipment, government buildings, or military and industrial installations. In general, ask permission before photographing people.

- Keep in mind that your behavior here may send messages you do not intent to send. A few reminders to help manage this: If you are wearing a skirt, be sure it falls below the knee. Cover your shoulders. Avoid sleeveless and low cut dresses or tops.

All valuable items should be safely secured at home, including:

- Valuable or expensive-looking jewelry

- Irreplaceable family objects

- All unnecessary credit cards

Students who are victims of crimes should immediately contact NYUAD Campus Safety at +971 2-628-7777 (or 87777 from a campus phone). Campus Safety personnel will help them contact the police and receive support services. The number for all emergency services in the UAE is 999.

title: Victim Services · NYUAD Students
text:
NYUAD cares about its community and is committed to helping those who are the victims of crimes.

If you are a student, staff or faculty member, or otherwise affiliated with NYUAD and have been sexually assaulted, stalked, harassed, or experienced dating violence or domestic violence, the NYU Department of Public Safety (DPS) can help or will put you through the right individuals that can get you the appropriate attention that is required.

The DPS Management Team assists those who are considering reporting their experience to the police as well as those who have already decided to do so.

We assist those requesting assistance through the process of filing a police report and explain UAE law processes.

Upon request, a DPS Management Team Member will accompany victims to the police department, if needed.

Other Services Provided

- Accompaniment to the hospital or other service agency

- Serve as a liaison with law enforcement

- Serve as a liaison with social service agencies

Please feel free to contact DPS Management at any time by calling 02 628 7777.

Victims’ Rights

You have the right:

- To make a report to Public Safety and/or appropriate law enforcement authorities, or choose not to report.

- To file an internal complaint with NYUAD and receive an equitable, respectful process, with an assistance by an advisor of your choice (if desired).

- To be reasonably protected by the University from retaliation for reporting an incident or participating in any investigation or proceeding at NYUAD.

- To receive the University’s assistance in obtaining academic accommodations, medical care, and/or counseling/support services where available and/or appropriate, regardless of whether an investigation is pursued under the applicable disciplinary procedures or with local law enforcement.

text:
Protecting Our Community and the Environment

Environmental Health and Safety (EHS) works to promote a safe, healthy, and environmentally sustainable campus for students, faculty, staff, visitors, and contractors, as well as to provide professional guidance and direction toward compliance with Abu Dhabi Public Health Center and UAE regulations.

OSHE Policy

All employees, students, and contractors must understand and implement the OSHE Policy .

-
Pedestrian and Cyclist Safety at Parking Garage Entrances

With the return to school and cooler weather, more community members are traveling across campus. Please use extra care when using the campus frontage, especially near the east and west parking garage entrances, where vehicles, cyclists, and pedestrians share routes.
If you are driving:

- Slow down when approaching parking garage entrances and exits.
- Stop and give way to pedestrians and cyclists.
- Check carefully for children, who may be less visible and unpredictable. If you are cycling or using a scooter:

- Reduce your speed when approaching vehicle crossings.
- Stay alert and be prepared to stop. Do not assume that motorists can see you.
- Give way where required and be considerate of other road users. NYUAD is reinstating interim traffic-calming measures along the pedestrian routes near the parking garage entrances while working on a longer-term solution.
Please slow down, stay alert, and look out for one another.

title: Occupational Safety, Health and Environment Management System (OSHEMS) · NYUAD Students
text:
Abu Dhabi regulations require NYUAD to have an approved and fully compliant Occupational Safety, Health, and Environment Management System (OSHEMS). NYUAD is committed to creating a safe, healthy, and sustainable learning and working environment for all members of the university community and strives to continually improve its Occupational Safety, Health, and Environment (OSHE) performance.

Please view NYUAD's OSHE Policy and the OSHE Targets and Objectives .

OSHEMS Documents

- Element 1: Roles and Responsibilities

EHS is a shared responsibility and resides at all levels within the University. Whether you are a Dean, Principal Investigator, Manager, or Faculty, you have health and safety responsibilities.

- Roles and Responsibilities Procedure

- Implementation Guide

- Element 2: Risk Management

One of the most essential components of managing EHS hazards and risks is a sound and comprehensive Risk Management Program. Whether you are conducting research, planning an experiment, or working at an Art Studio, a risk assessment is a mandatory requirement.

- Risk Management Procedure

- Risk Register

- Events Risk Assessment Form

- Implementation Guide

- Element 3: Contractor Management

From time to time, you may require the services of an internal or external contractor to help set up for an event or have a unique project. Did you know that if you are hiring a contractor, specific EHS criteria are required before the contractor can start work?

Learn about the process and criteria:

- Contractor Management Procedure

- Contractor Site Safety Online Induction

- NYUAD Contractor EHS Criteria Checklist

- Implementation Guide

- Element 4: Communication and Consultation

The University communicates important health and safety information with the community in various ways through the Communication and Consultation Procedure .

- Implementation Guide

- Element 5: Training, Awareness and Competency

There are several health and safety training courses available to you. Learn about the training and competency procedure:

- Training Awareness and Competency Procedure

- Training Matrix

- Implementation Guide

- Element 6: Emergency Management

- Emergency Action Plan

- Implementation Guide

- NYUAD Fire Wardens List

- Element 7: Monitoring, Investigation and Reporting

EHS targets and objectives are developed for each academic year. This is our roadmap to a mature safety culture. See AY 2026-2027 OSHE Targets and Objectives and OSHE Targets and Objectives Procedure

- OSHE Monitoring Procedure

- Hazard and Incident Reporting and Investigation Procedure

- Implementation Guide

- Element 8: Audit and Inspection

You have implemented the OSHEMS in your department. How successful was the implementation? Are there any gaps? EHS audits occur on a periodic basis by internal and external parties. EHS audits are our EHS scorecard.

Learn about the audit process:

- OSHE Audit Procedure

- Non-Conformance and Corrective Action

- Internal Audit Plan

- Inspections are an excellent method of monitoring your compliance with local regulations and laws. See our OSHE Inspections Procedure , Approved Campus Audits and Inspections Schedule AY 2025-2026 , and Approved Labs Audits and Inspections Schedule AY 2025-2026

- Implementation Guide

- Element 9: Compliance and Management Review

- NYUAD OSHE Policy

- OSHE Legal Compliance Procedure

- OSHE Legal Register/Compliance Matrix

- OSHE Document Control and Record Retention Procedure

- Implementation Guide

Do you want to make a temporary or permanent change to a physical structure/ building or system/process or procedure? Have you managed all of the associated EHS risks? Did you know EHS must approve certain changes? See the EHS Change Request Form and Management of Change Procedure

The EHS Department, Safety Committee(s), and the University leadership periodically review the NYUAD OSH MS to ensure it remains relevant and aligns with the University's strategic plan. See the Management Review Procedure .

title: Operations Safety · NYUAD Students
text:
Operations Safety deals with all non-lab and non-research areas across the campus. This includes academic classrooms, shops, studios, accommodations, and other community spaces such as the dining halls, marketplace, gymnasium, swimming pools, etc.

Programs and Procedures

- Art and Art History Safety

- Art Safety Program

- Driver Fatigue Prevention

- Driver Fatigue Prevention

- Electrical Safety

Most people tend to overlook the hazards associated with electricity. Even brief contact with electricity can lead to death, serious injury, fire, explosion, and massive property damage. Below are a few electrical safety tips:

- Inspect and do not use damaged equipment or frayed electrical cords.

- Don’t overload electrical outlets. Eliminate octopus/daisy-chained connections.

- Use only grounded appliances plugged into three-prong outlets.

- Arrange electrical cords so that they are not a trip hazard.

- Never use extension cords in place of permanent wiring.

- Never suspend extension cords with staples, nails, or wires.

- Is an appliance giving off a strange smell? Unplug it immediately!

- Stay alert for outlets that feel hot. Unplug all cords from hot outlets, and don’t use them again until a qualified electrician has inspected the outlet.

- Know where the electrical panel and circuit breakers are located.

- Always follow the manufacturer’s instructions.

The Health & Safety Performer Recognition Program is a campus-wide initiative that highlights and celebrates the most dedicated health and safety champions across NYUAD.

Beginning this September, the EHS department is consolidating AssessNet, Moodle, and SciShield into a single, integrated software platform: SafetyStratus. This transition modernizes our learning, assessment, and safety management systems into one unified ecosystem.

Key benefits are:

- Single Sign-On (SSO): Access all EHS modules effortlessly using your standard NYU credentials.

- Integrated Experience: Seamlessly navigate between safety compliance, course learning, and assessments without switching systems.

- Streamlined Workflows: Enjoy reduced data duplication and simplified day-to-day administrative tasks.

- Centralized Hub: Utilize a modern, intuitive interface designed for faster access to critical safety information.

title: World Day for Safety and Health at Work · NYUAD Students
text:
The World Day for Safety and Health at Work is a crucial international observance that champions occupational safety and health worldwide. It's a worldwide effort to raise awareness and prevent work-related accidents and diseases. Since its establishment by the International Labour Organization in 2003, this day has highlighted the fundamental need for every workplace to be a safe and healthy environment.

NYUAD's Commitment to Safety

Here at NYUAD, the EHS department joins this global movement annually to celebrate the World Day for Safety and Health at Work. Our goal is to actively cultivate a strong culture of Occupational Safety and Health within our community.

World Day for Safety and Health at Work Celebration!

This year's theme focused on shared responsibility: emphasizing that the safety, health, well-being, and environmental stewardship of our entire community is a collective effort.

The EHS department collaborated with:

- Civil and Urban Engineering

- Office of Ethics and Compliance

- Office of Global Access and Engagement

- Campus Safety

- Wellbeing Working Group

- Sustainability and Stewardship

- Athletics

- Campus Dining Services

- Health and Safety Committee

...to bring to the community a celebration that highlighted how every part of NYUAD contributes to a safer, healthier, and more sustainable learning and working environment.

title: Biological Safety · NYUAD Students
text:
Biological Safety

- Animal Biosafety (IACUC)

NYUAD EHS works in collaboration with the Institutional Animal Care and Use Committee (IACUC) to ensure a safe environment for those who work with animals. All research involving vertebrate animals should be reviewed and approved by the IACUC prior to activity commencement. Additional information on the care and use of laboratory animals can be found in the following documents;

- NRC: Guide for the Care and Use of Laboratory Animals (PDF)

- PHS: Policy on Humane Care and Use of Laboratory Animals (PDF)

- Biohazardous Waste Disposal

Regulated medical waste (RMW) should be placed in red bags and handed over to EHS for pickup by waste management companies authorized by Tadweer.

Other biohazardous waste (not classified as RMW) should be placed in clear autoclavable bags, autoclaved, and disposed of as regular trash. Please contact EHS for proper waste segregation.

See: Use of Autoclave for the Decontamination of Biohazardous Waste (PDF).

- Biological Safety Cabinets

Biological safety cabinets (BSCs) at NYUAD are certified annually through a third-party contractor as per Abu Dhabi OSHAD requirements. Environmental Health and Safety will coordinate and schedule the annual certification for each cabinet on contract. The following methods outline the proper use of a BSC;

- Biological Safety Cabinets Protocol

- Biosafety Manual

NYUAD EHS, through this Program, seeks to minimize the health risks of researchers and the community at large and reduce environmental impacts while meeting regulatory requirements. It is designed to serve as a template for laboratories to personalize for their own needs.

See: NYUAD Biosafety Manual

- Bloodborne Pathogens

The Bloodborne Pathogen Exposure Control Plan applies to all employees, students, and visitors of New York University Abu Dhabi (NYUAD) who could potentially be expected to come into contact with human blood and other potentially infectious materials (OPIM). This plan is designed to minimize or eliminate the risks associated with exposure to bloodborne pathogens for employees as a result of required occupational tasks.

- Embryonic Stem Cell Research (ESCRO)

Researchers looking to conduct experiments using human embryonic stem cells or human pluripotent stem cells must submit a research protocol to the Embryonic Stem Cell Research Oversight (ESCRO) committee.

- Embryonic Stem Cell Research Oversight (ESCRO) Policy

- Embryonic Stem Cell Research Oversight (ESCRO) Review Procedure

- Institutional Biosafety Committee (IBC)

NYUAD has established an Institutional Biosafety Committee (IBC) that is charged with the oversight of biological research involving rDNA/synthetic NA and/or Select Agents and Toxins. All research that falls under these categories must be registered with the IBC and must comply with the NIH Guidelines for Research Involving Recombinant DNA Molecules

To submit your research for IBC review, please log on to the Bioraft website and follow the instructions in the attached guide . PIs can delegate individual lab members to complete registrations (see instructions ); however, only they can "Certify" and officially submit the registration.

title: Health and Safety Committee · NYUAD Students
text:
The goal of the Health and Safety Committee is to ensure NYUAD establishes and maintains appropriate health and safety across the campus and complies with the Abu Dhabi Public Health Center, ADOSH System Framework requirements.

The Committee and its Working Groups are the technical advisors and stakeholder body for all aspects of the University's health and safety program. The Committee has the authority to make recommendations about the conduct of activities within the University, to assure regulatory compliance and reasonable standards for health and safety across campus.

To make safety recommendations related to the Campus and/or the Labs please contact the Health and Safety Committee here.

title: CITIESair - Air Quality Index at NYUAD · NYUAD Students
text:
The Center for Interacting Urban Networks (CITIES) is proud to present CITIESair.

What is CITIESair?

CITIESair is an integrated system of air quality devices and specialized software designed for educational institutions in Abu Dhabi. CITIESair’s mission is to empower data-driven policies to safeguard NYUAD and Abu Dhabi school communities from outdoor air pollution and improve indoor air quality. This project responds to CITIES’ strategic objective of promoting sustainable living, improving the overall well-being of Abu Dhabi citizens, and contributing to the UAE’s efforts to reduce air pollution’s mortality rate from 64.8 in 2017 to 60.2 per 100,000 people by 2030 – UAE National Air Quality Strategy (2021-2031) .

Why is CITIESair important?

Air pollution is among the 4th leading factors for premature death, claiming over 6 million lives worldwide in 2019 [1]. Microscopic particulate matter smaller than 2.5 micrometers (PM2.5) can penetrate and lodge into the lungs and internal organs, causing respiratory and cardiovascular diseases [2, 3]. Several countries worldwide experience prolonged periods of PM2.5 concentrations for different reasons. The UAE, in particular, is susceptible to periods of high PM2.5 concentrations due to its exposed desert geographical topography, anthropogenic emissions, and industrial activities.

Where are the sensors located?

As of November 2024, CITIESair has installed one outdoor sensor and 10 indoor sensors across different buildings, such as the first floors of all A buildings (except for A4), the Campus Center (C2), the second floor of the Faculty buildings (F1 and F2), and the East Dining Hall (D2). For the outdoor air quality station, you are invited to follow it on IQAir to track air quality 24/7 from the convenience of your desktop and smartphone devices.

Impact of CITIESair

We assist institutions in implementing data-driven air quality policies and achieving the highest indoor air quality standards , ultimately enhancing the learning environment for students. People spend most of their time indoors in the UAE; therefore, by maximizing indoor air quality, we can counterbalance the impact of low outdoor air quality on our daily exposure to air pollution. To achieve this, we have equipped every building within the NYUAD campus (and other educational institutions) with indoor air quality sensors, enabling hyperlocal, continuous, and long-term monitoring to assess indoor air quality comprehensively.

First established and piloted at NYUAD, CITIESair has since strategically expanded to 11 other schools across Abu Dhabi emirate and the network is in continuous expansion. CITIESair’s schools network spans not only the core urban center of Abu Dhabi city but also other inland settlements such as in Ghayathi, Ruwais, and Madinat Zayed, with key partnerships with educational institutions from Aldar and ANOC.

Research has shown how better air quality can boost cognitive ability, concentration, sleep quality and ultimately support a better learning environment [4, 5]. From an obscure topic, air quality has become an important consideration for many school residents when incorporating their daily routines, such as exercising or bringing the kids outdoors. Detailed data analytics and visualizations enable real-time outdoor vs. indoor comparison and encourage the expansion of indoor sensor coverage for comprehensive indoor air quality monitoring in schools. This has led to the development of scientifically informed air quality policies and real-time, data-driven decisions in schools such as Theodore Monod and Cranleigh , among others.

Starting from the academic year 2024-2025, CITIESair has launched a year-long pilot air purification study in 2 schools in Abu Dhabi, in partnership with IQAir, to study the efficiency of air purifiers in improving indoor air quality. The result of the pilot study will provide a proof-of-concept for implementation of such systems across CITIESair’s school network to safeguard the respiratory health of every student and community member, especially those with underlying respiratory issues.

Ultimately, CITIESair’s impact extends to academic research. CITIESair’s dataset at NYUAD is publicly available to inform communities, enable research with accurate real-time data, and develop new policies. This data accessibility inspired Capstone students and researchers to experiment with smart air quality notifications, the result of which has been presented at 12th World Environmental Education Congress (WEEC) and 4th Air Sensors International Conference (ASIC). Ultimately, this will inform the university leadership’s on designing data-driven policies on wellness, further cement NYUAD's reputation as an exemplary institution in sustainable living in Abu Dhabi.

References:

[1] Health Effects Institute. 2020. State of Global Air 2020 . Special Report. Boston, MA:Health Effects Institute,

[2] Li, Donghai, et al. “ Fluorescent Reconstitution on Deposition of PM 2.5 in Lung and Extrapulmonary Organs .” Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences, vol. 116, no. 7, 2019, pp. 2488–93.

[3] Xing, Yu-Fei et al. “ The impact of PM2.5 on the human respiratory system .” Journal of Thoracic Disease vol. 8,1 (2016): E69-74.

[4] Wang, Chao, et al. " How indoor environmental quality affects occupants’ cognitive functions: A systematic review ." Building and Environment 193 (2021): 107647.

[5] Sadrizadeh, Sasan, et al. " Indoor air quality and health in schools: A critical review for developing the roadmap for the future school environment ." Journal of Building Engineering 57 (2022): 104908.

title: Space Reservation Request · NYUAD Students
text:
Booking a Space on Campus

Students are able to request the C ampus Center Forums, large Conference Center spaces, specialized Arts Center rooms, lobby, lounges, and outdoor spaces via the EMS Space Reservation System .

You should fill out the form at least seven working days in advance of your event and allow at least two working days to receive a reservation confirmation. Please refer to the Space Guide for more details on location, capacity, and layout of each space.

For any other questions, please reach out to the Space Reservation team at nyuad.spacereservation@nyu.edu

https://students.nyuad.nyu.edu/services/campus-maps-facilities/space-reservation-request/space-guide/

title: Student Travel at NYUAD · NYUAD Students
text:
NYU Abu Dhabi assists with student home travel between their home base city and their approved study location for a given semester. Travel is arranged through an official designated travel agent, currently Nirvana Travel Agency.

All travel funded by NYU Abu Dhabi must be procured through this travel agency but students are free to make personal, independent travel arrangements through any provider. The University also provides assistance to students with securing the necessary visa for studying in the UAE or at other approved study away locations, as well as with all academic related travel, such as January Term, course-related regional trips, and semester-long study abroad programs.

All NYUAD-sponsored travel for students is managed by the Office of Global Education.

Announcements for Global Education

Monday, October 12, 2026

-
Fall Break Travel Reminders

Please note that students who entered the UAE with an entry permit this fall semester, or who are awaiting their UAE student visa renewal should not make travel plans until their UAE student residence visa has been approved and their Emirates ID card has been issued.
Students cannot travel outside of the UAE if their visa is still under process. You will in fact be stopped at the airport by the immigration authorities, and not allowed to leave the country if your UAE visa processing is still ongoing.
Students planning personal travel outside the UAE during the upcoming Fall Break must keep in mind that if their travel is disrupted for any reason, or if they become stranded at their destination, they will be personally responsible for covering any accommodation, meals, flight changes, or other costs associated with their travel and the delay in returning to the UAE.

title: Independent Student Travel · NYUAD Students
text:
NYU Abu Dhabi understands students may wish to travel throughout the region during academic breaks as well as before or after each semester. Students are fully and solely responsible for the financial and logistical arrangements related to their personal independent travel. The University encourages students to carefully review published information about the countries they wish to visit so that they can be fully informed of the relevant health and safety considerations for their destination(s).

NYU Traveler

NYU Traveler is a web-based portal that is linked to NYU's travel safety service. It has been created as a tool to enhance the safety of students, faculty, administrators, and staff. When students register their travel, they will be provided updated information about conditions in their destination that may affect personal safety and well-being. NYU Traveler will also hold students’ travel plans so that NYU can more rapidly and effectively respond to an emergency, remove students from a suddenly risky location while abroad, or contact them to advise them on their safety and appropriate arrangements before their travel to a potentially risky location.

Pre-departure Travel Consultation

Make an appointment for travel advice and recommendations at least two weeks before personal travel. To make an appointment, email nyuad.healthcenter@nyu.edu .

- Have your departure date as well as the list of cities you are visiting ready when making your appointment.

- Students should also review the Wise, Independent Travel Strategies , which provide helpful suggestions for planning and managing safe, affordable, healthy, and purposeful travel.

Related official links:
https://students.nyuad.nyu.edu/services/student-travel/independent-student-travel/wits/

title: Affordable Travel · NYUAD Students
text:
Being able to have an affordable and quality-based travel plan is anyone’s ideal scenario. In order to maximize the boundaries of your Wise Independent Strategies in the area of affordable travel, we have some useful tips to guide your planning process.

For a brief overview of tips to take into consideration when planning for an affordable trip, please refer to these WITS (Wise Independent Strategies) quick tips ! (PDF)

For a more comprehensive set of tips,, you can read more in the options below.

- Finding Discounts and Bargaining

Do your research : Read guides forums, and discussion boards; talk with friends who have been there before:

- 24 Best Travel Sites to Save You Money

Take advantage of student perks :

- Research local options available on site.

- Consider purchasing an STA or ISIC card.

Understand local norms for bargaining :

- Get prices from multiple shops.

- Don’t be afraid to walk away.

- Remember that they have to make a living too.

- Affordable Travel

Affordable Airfare:

- UAE: Fly Dubai and Air Arabia in the

- Europe: EasyJet and W!ZZ Air (wizzair.com)

- Asia: Jetstar and AirAsia (www.airasia.com)

- USA: Delta Airlines and JetBlue (www.jetblue.com)

- Try using other budget airlines when you travel.

- Search lots of airlines with sites like:

- kayak.com

- skyscanner.com

Affordable Accommodations :

- TripAdvisor.com is world’s largest travel review site.

- Airbnb has been a popular site for affordable and legit accommodations.

- You can search for hotels using hostelz.com .

- For last minute hotel deals you can review:

- laterooms.com

- dealbase.com

Affordable Transportation :

- Do some research to get a sense of public transportation option at your destination and how much you should expect to pay.

- Overcharging on transport, private or otherwise, is commonplace in many countries and there is little you can do about it. Be firm — don't get bullied.

- Tip — if there is no meter, agree a fair price before you set off.

title: Healthy Travel · NYUAD Students
text:
Ensuring that you are best prepared in terms of maintaining your health during travel, is extremely important. In order to maximize the boundaries of your Wise Independent Strategies in the area of healthy travel, we have some useful tips to guide your planning process.

For a brief overview of tips to take into consideration when planning for an affordable trip, please refer to these WITS (Wise Independent Strategies) quick tips !

For a more comprehensive set of tips, you can read more in the options below.

- Medicines

Always bring prescriptions with your medications.

Bring over-the-counter meds for common ailments:

- Anti-diarrhea

- Pain reliever

- Antihistamine (allergy blocker)

- Motion sickness

Your preferred brands of medical or personal hygiene products may not be available in every country. Be sure to purchase these at home and bring them with you on your trip.

Bring enough to last you for your whole trip plus a few extra days, just in case.

- Water and Other Drinks

Only drink bottled water unless you know for sure that local tap water is safe.

- Use bottled water when you brush your teeth.

- Keep your mouth closed in the shower.

Avoid ice cubes and ice cream as well as other items that may have been made with or come into contact with contaminated water.

Other beverages should always come in original, factory-sealed containers.

- Food and Food Preparation

If local water is not safe, avoid raw fruits and vegetables. Everything should be cooked thoroughly.

- Only things that can be peeled (bananas, etc.) are safe.

Avoid “street food” and things that have been kept out in the open for long periods of time.

- Be sure you receive clean and dry dishes and silverware

- Water-born contaminants do not survive in the air. If you notice water left on dishes or silverware, dry them off with your napkin and then let them air dry for a few minutes before you are served. This will help eliminate any bacteria present in the water.

- Other Tips

Wash your hands regularly with soap.

- You can wash your hands with water which may not be safe to drink. When you’re finished, simply make sure you thoroughly dry your hands.

Use hand sanitizer, but be discreet.

Stay well hydrated.

- During illness (diarrhea or vomiting), dehydration is a risk that cannot be understated and ORT (oral rehydration therapy) in the form of sachets of salts you add to water is very cheap, widely available even in the remotest of locations, and save thousands of lives every year when serious illnesses (e.g., Cholera) strike in the developing world.

Get plenty of rest while traveling.

- Consider bringing a small pillow, earplugs, and eye mask.

- Be prepared for the lack of AC or ambient noise in your hotel.

Be aware that HIV and other STDs are widespread in both developing and developed countries

title: Prior to Travel · NYUAD Students
text:
Travel planning is so essential to any trip that you take. This will help you prioritize and maximize your experiences. Prioritizing what you would like to experience will plan an important role in how you curate your travel plan and best prepare for it.

For a brief overview of tips to take into consideration prior to travel, please refer to this WITS (Wise Independent Strategies) quick tips ! (PDF)

For a more comprehensive set of tips you can read more in the options below.

- Give Your Trip a Plan and a Purpose

- There are many places to visit! Weigh out your options and clarify why you would like to visit this particular country. Taking into consideration your academic, professional, and personal interests, these would best ground your decisions of traveling. In addition to this, considering the travel advisories and a country’s political atmosphere e.g., unrest, etc., to ensure that you have an uninterrupted trip.

- Find the balance between seeing lots of different places and really getting to know one place in particular. Be sure to strike a balance between exploring the country as much as possible but also taking the time to explore one particular place in depth. You wouldn’t want to miss out on engaging more with the local culture!

- Be prepared but allow for flexibility in all aspects !
You can put in all the hard work and time into planning the perfect trip but these can be disrupted by unexpected events, sudden adverse weather conditions, or events being canceled. You can spend months planning the perfect trip and have all that hard work disrupted by unexpected events or circumstances: museums could be closed for renovation; public transportation could be shut down due to a strike; or events could be canceled due to weather conditions. Always be sure you leave yourself some extra “cushion” in your budget for these types of unexpected issues.

For more ideas about where to go, check out this website: Independent Travel.Info

- Research Your Destination

Check travel and health advisories for the destination:

- US State Department

- UK Foreign Office

- Centers for Disease Control

- Be sure to check for information from your home country as well to be in line with current health guidelines.

Get necessary vaccinations and medications in advance:

- The NYUAD Health Center may be able to provide certain vaccines for you. Other vaccines and medicines should be available in hospitals in Abu Dhabi or your home country.

- It is important to make sure that all of the medications you take regularly are legal in your intended destination.

Research visa requirements and plan ahead:

- Start this process at least a month and a half in advance. Search for a country’s embassy in the UAE and follow visa directions or contact the embassy by phone if necessary. Be prepared to provide passport photos that meet certain specifications, your original passport , and UAE visa as well as copies of the same, applicable visa fees, and any other required documents. Many countries now require you show proof of your financial means. This is normally in the form of a bank statement showing the balance available in your account.

- Check implications that travel to certain countries may have on future travel plans. For example, the US Visa Waiver Program now has additional eligibility restrictions based on travel history to specific countries.

Review maps of the cities you will be visiting:

- Google Maps should be your friend! Once you have arrived in the country, bought a local SIM card, and purchased a local data plans then you now you are free to explore the city areas, etc.

- Identify major landmarks you can use to orient yourself while walking around.

- Figure out how long it will take you to move from place to place and how best to do this.

- Locate your hotel (pin the location) and try to learn something about that particular neighborhood.

- Be sure to have your accommodations or hotels in a safe neighborhood. Have the local Police numbers stored on the phone in the case of an emergency.

Consider buying a local guidebook :

- Be sure to find a guidebook that is up-to-date. Cities change quickly and businesses and attractions may change their hours, change their prices, or even go out of business from one year to the next.

- A useful resource would be reaching out to alumnus and current students who have traveled and have shared useful tips on how to navigate their Independent Student Travel during mid-semester breaks, etc.

- Register with NYU Traveler

NYU Traveler provides several helpful benefits to students while traveling independently. In the event of a major emergency in your destination, the university will be able to quickly locate and attempt to assist your exit from the country.

The system can also provide helpful alerts to smaller disruptions such as transit strikes, inclement weather, or civil unrest which may negatively impact your trip. These alerts are automatically delivered to by SMS or through email.

- Route Logistics and Arrangements

Book accommodations in advance:

- Accommodations should be a priority! You can always figure out meals and activities on the spot, but it’s important to know in advance where you’ll be sleeping each night.

- If you arrive in city without having pre-booked a hotel, you also run the risk of being taken advantage of by taxi drivers or scam artists.

Determine how you’ll move from place to place :

- Do some research in advance about train schedules or other ways you could travel between cities and be certain you can arrive in plenty of time for your airplane flights or other pre-arranged activities.

- One easy way to store all of the important information about your trip is to simply email it to yourself . Attach all of your itineraries, reservations, and confirmation numbers to one email and you’ll always be able to find it in case something gets lost.

- Be sure to have everything confirmed and recorded before you get to your destination, this is to avoid any issues regarding mobility.

Make a budget :

- Be sure to include your airfare, hotel, meals, local transportation, activities, and other personal expenses.

- Be sure to keep extra money available for any unexpected costs or problems that might occur– this is very important.

- Use xe.com for currency conversion.

Have at least two ways to access your money and keep them separate:

- If you’re carrying cash, also carry a credit card. If you’re planning to only use a credit or debit card, be sure to have at least two different cards.

- Keep one source of money with you, but safely store the other one somewhere else. This way if one gets lost or stolen, you still have access to money.

Explore local discount cards for popular attractions:

- Many large cities sell special tourist passes which will admit you to multiple major attractions. These are generally much less expensive than paying for each attraction individually.

- Contact the local tourist information office for more information once you arrive.

For more information, check out Travel Independent website for more information

- What to Pack

Some great suggestions are available on the Travel Independent website. In general, pack lightly and in luggage you can carry easily on your own.

Most importantly, don’t forget:

- Passport and visa (if applicable)

- Geo Blue Insurance Card (covers you outside the UAE)

- Original prescriptions and necessary medications

- Copies of itinerary, reservations, and local contact info

- Copies of important documents (passport, credit cards, IDs)

- These copies may be invaluable to you in the event that anything is lost or stolen. You’ll need to immediately block your credit cards so they can’t be used inappropriately.

- Keep these with you , not in your checked luggage

Make sure your luggage is clearly marked with tags listing your name, address, phone number, and email address.

- Communication and In Case of Emergency

- Think about how you’ll stay in touch and how others can reach you .

- Will you have easy access to the internet while traveling? Can you use email, Skype, or Facebook to keep in touch?

- Will your mobile phone work in another country? Do you have an international calling card you can use from public pay telephone or in your hotel?

- Let family, close friends, and your RA know where you’re going and when you’ll be back.

- Leave an extra set of copies of your important documents (passport, credit cards, IDs) at home.

- Take along an NYUAD Emergency Card

- You can pick these up from the Office of Public Safety. They list the contact information for important resources at NYU Abu Dhabi.

- Your NYU Abu Dhabi provided Geo Blue health insurance will cover you anytime you travel outside the UAE.

- You may also wish to purchase travel insurance .

- Travel insurance may help to reimburse costs associated with missed flights or other trip expenses in the event you become injured or ill as well as travel disruptions due to natural disasters or other unexpected events.

- Some policies may also provide coverage for lost or stolen belongings.

Companies offering travel insurance include:

- worldnomads.com

- insuremytrip.com

Related official links:
https://students.nyuad.nyu.edu/student-affairs/health-center/

title: Purposeful Trip · NYUAD Students
text:
Ensuring that you are best prepared in terms of maintaining your health during travel, is extremely important. In order to maximize the boundaries of your Wise Independent Strategies in the area of crafting a purposeful travel, we have some useful tips to guide your planning process.

For a brief overview of tips to take into consideration when planning for an affordable trip, please refer to these WITS (Wise Independent Strategies) quick tips ! (PDF)

For a more comprehensive set of tips, you can read more in the options below.

Connecting with the Local Population

Find opportunities to talk to and engage with locals:

- Don’t get too caught up being a tourist that you miss out on the people around you. Take time to interact with guides, or people you meet on the street and learn about their lives and their culture. A personal connection you make while traveling could wind up being much more memorable than the pictures of a famous landmark.

- While we encourage engaging closely with the local community, also be extra aware of your surroundings.

- Support local businesses and traditional crafts by purchasing locally produced goods and souvenirs These will likely carry more sentimental value for you and help benefit the local community.

Be considerate:

- Don’t point a camera in someone's face without permission.

- Honor local dress and behavior norms.

Be aware of your ecological and cultural “footprint:”

- Turn off electricity and water sources whenever you aren’t actively using them. In some places, tourist hotels may get priority access to these important resources over the local population.

- Be sensitive to how you are behaving and how you are presenting yourself and your culture. If you leave behind a bad impression, the next person to visit that place may be judged unfairly because of your actions.

title: Safe Travel · NYUAD Students
text:
Have a travel plan that ensures safety is a priority. Having useful tips on how to stay safe during a trip and being responsible for yourself is important in best preparing for unexpected changes/experiences during the trip.

For a brief overview of tips to take into consideration prior to travel, please refer to these WITS (Wise Independent Strategies) quick tips ! (PDF)

For a more comprehensive set of tips, you can read more in the options below.

- What You Can Do to Keep Safe When in Public

While abroad, as in other settings, you can have a major impact on your own health and safety through the decisions you make before and during your travel and by your day-to-day choices and behaviors. You should:

- Consistently apply informed judgment in your day-to-day choices and behaviors.

- Always keep in mind that no matter how immersed you are in a local community, you are still a foreigner and thus your chances of being a victim of criminal activity may be greater than that for the average local person.

- Plan to travel to events, walk around your neighborhood, and explore the city with a partner or in small groups. Be aware of your surroundings as you travel through the city. Let a roommate or friend know where you are going, and when you are planning to return.

- Assume responsibility for all the elements necessary for your personal preparation for your travel.

- Behave in a manner that is respectful of the rights and well-being of others, and encourage others to behave in a similar manner.

- Accept responsibility for your own decisions and actions.

- Fitting In

Understand local laws and customs :

- Check your “vices” and be aware of local regulations about smoking and alcohol. The use of drugs should always be avoided.

Don’t be paranoid, but be cautious in new environments and with strangers :

- Watch out for scams and opportunities that are too good to be true.

- If you are unsure, the sensible approach is to never go somewhere with anybody who approaches you in the street, on the assumption that they are after something.

- Make up an excuse or if you have a companion, simply start up a conversation with that person, completely blocking the stranger out.

- If you’re alone cross the street or try to move away to a public place where they’ll be less likely to continue bothering you.

- In no circumstances should you agree to transport drugs, jewelry, or other items for strangers? You may likely be committing a criminal act and could face stiff penalties at home or while abroad.

Be polite but firm. Don’t give handouts .

- Giving gifts or money to locals may seem like a charitable thing to do, but it can create an unsafe imbalance and atmosphere in the community.

- After you’ve said “No” once, don't make eye contact, and don’t keep repeatedly saying “no” or get angry. If you show any more interest this is when touts are particularly determined and most frustrating. Sometimes beggars or children will make body contact, tugging on your clothing. In this case, remove their hand and look them directly in the eye, making your “no” clear.

- Being Responsible for Yourself

Take situations seriously and don’t try to experience more than you’re prepared for

- Avoid political demonstrations and protests.

- Avoid large gatherings of people in general.

Know that NYU Abu Dhabi cannot as easily help you in the event of legal trouble, medical emergency, or need for evacuation :

- If your passport is lost or stolen while traveling, immediately report it to your nearest embassy and/or the local police department. It may be possible for the embassy to issue you a temporary travel document with which to return home.

Become familiar with the procedures for obtaining emergency health and law enforcement services in the host country.

Research attitudes towards women .

- This is especially important for women traveling alone or in small groups of only women.

Know local emergency contact numbers :

- Inside the UAE, dial 999 if you need to contact emergency responders

- Money Matters

Notify your bank in advance that you’ll be traveling

- If your bank suddenly sees charges in a foreign country, they may assume you’ve become the victim of identity theft and deactivate your card to prevent further fraudulent charges. This can cause a serious problem when you try to pay for meals or check out of hotels and can’t afford to pay the bill.

Exchange some money before you leave, and be aware of fees on cards you use:

- Most credit cards have currency exchange and international transaction fees. Each time you use a debit or credit card while abroad, you could be charged an additional 3-5% (or more) based on the policies of your bank.

Keep money hidden and safe :

- Keep bags closed or locked.

- Wear a breast bag or money belt.

- Don’t carry more than you really need.

title: No Objection Certificate Request Form · NYUAD Students
text:
Embassies and Consulates in the United Arab Emirates often require a document called "No Objection Certificate” as part of a visa application process. If you require such a document due to a visa needed for personal travel, please use the form below to submit a request to our office. You will be notified by email when the certificate is ready for collection — typically within five business days.

Please note that the "No Objection Certificate" can only be issued by the University if your student visa is sponsored by NYUAD. If you are not sponsored by the University, the "No Objection Certificate" should be issued by your visa sponsor.

title: Spring 2026 Student Travel Guidance · NYUAD Students
text:
Support for Voluntary Departure from Campus

Last updated March 4

We are writing to follow up on the next steps outlined in the March 3 Student Webinar for students who are choosing to make a voluntary departure from the UAE in the upcoming days. Our goal is to help you get to where you need to go as safely and smoothly as possible despite the current challenges. Assuming conditions permit later in the semester, we will readily facilitate your return.

To assist you in navigating this process, we have compiled the key resources and contacts below. We encourage you to review these resources as you finalise your travel plans.

IMPORTANT: All students currently on campus in Abu Dhabi must submit one of the travel forms below – see category 1 and 2 – regardless of whether they plan to make a voluntary departure or remain on campus for the time being. Please submit the form that is relevant to you as described in category 1 or 2 below. Please complete the form by 9 pm tonight (Wednesday, March 4) . The form will remain active until 10 am tomorrow (Thursday, March 5), but we appreciate your swift response.

Kindly consider the copy of your form submission as a confirmation that we have received your information. Requests for travel assistance will be reviewed upon submission. We will provide updates as flights become available.

1. NYUAD students who receive home travel support as part of their financial aid packages will work with the NYUAD Student Mobility Team to coordinate their travel arrangements based on when flights become available for their established home base country/city.

-
Please submit the form linked here . The number of flights operating is still limited, and the regional airspace remains mostly closed. You need to be ready to travel on available flights with minimal preparation time for packing and checking out of the residence halls.

-
Students who hold tickets purchased through Nirvana Travel should wait for Nirvana to make these changes. Please do not make independent changes and payments, as you will not be eligible for reimbursement.

2. Students from NYUAD, NYU New York, and NYU Shanghai who have purchased their own flights for the end of the semester should work directly with their airline to change their departure date to the next available flight. NYUAD or Nirvana Travel, its affiliated travel agency, cannot make any changes to that ticket for you since you purchased it yourself.

-
NYUAD students must submit the form linked here .

-
NYU New York and NYU Shanghai students must submit the form linked here .

-
The number of flights operating is still limited, and the regional airspace remains mostly closed. You need to be ready to travel on available flights with minimal preparation time for packing and checking out of the residence halls.

-
If you need financial assistance to cover the cost of rearranging your existing return ticket home or to purchase one, email nyuad.spring26flight@nyu.edu , and we will help you, so please don’t worry about that as you make your decision about whether or not to leave.

Flights Arranged Through One’s Embassy

Students who wish to book flights through their respective embassies are free to do so, but please note that Nirvana Travel cannot assist with these types of flights.

-
Please follow the guidance you receive from your embassy, as these flights must be booked directly by you through the embassy and the affiliated airline.

-
Please be sure to submit the form above that applies to you (category 1 or 2).

-
Please note that NYUAD or Nirvana Travel cannot pay the required fees for such flights on behalf of students. Students must manage this process with the embassy on their own and can submit receipts and proof of flying (i.e., a boarding pass or a flown report) to nyuad.spring26flight@nyu.edu to request reimbursement.

UAE Student Visa Guidance

Students with an active UAE residence visa may exit the UAE using that visa and do not need additional documentation.

If your residence visa has been approved but you have not yet received your physical Emirates ID card , email the NYUAD Immigration team right away and copy nyuad.uaestudentvisa@nyu.edu to request an electronic copy of your Emirates ID.

If your residence visa is still in process , and you plan to depart campus within the next 5-7 days, your current immigration file will be cancelled so you can exit the country. Please email nyuad.uaestudentvisa@nyu.edu for guidance. NYUAD students will need to be issued new immigration documents to return to the UAE in the next semester. We will help you with that.

Your Passport is a Key Document for Travel

Students who do not currently have their passports due to a pending visa application or any other reason must work directly with the relevant embassy and visa service provider to withdraw the application and retrieve their passport as soon as possible.

Many embassies are operating with limited services, so students should continue to follow up persistently. The University cannot intervene in this process, as embassies can assist only the individual traveler.

Residential Life Housing Checkout Instructions

Please review the instructions from the Residential Life and Student Affairs teams regarding the required steps for checking out of campus housing. Before leaving campus, students must:

-
Complete the Housing Check Out Form .

-
Drop your room key in the black box located in your residential building.

-
Your Belongings: For the time being, you may leave your belongings in your rooms.

Key Contacts

-
For questions about travel support for students who purchase their own flights, contact nyuad.spring26flight@nyu.edu .

-
For questions related to travel support for students who receive NYUAD financial aid for home travel, contact nyuad.studentmobility@nyu.edu .

-
Students from NYU New York and NYU Shanghai, contact nyuad.spring26flight@nyu.edu .

-
For questions related to your UAE student visa status, contact nyuad.uaestudentvisa@nyu.edu .

-
For questions related to Nirvana Travel, contact nyuad@ntravel.ae or call 02-628-7250.

-
For information about campus housing and check-out procedures, contact nyuad.ResLife@nyu.edu .

-
For general campus safety questions, please contact Public Safety at Nyuad.publicsafety247@nyu.edu or call 02-628-7777.

Please review the Frequently Asked Questions .

Related official links:
https://students.nyuad.nyu.edu/services/student-travel/spring-2026-student-travel-resources/student-mobility-faqs/

title: Student Mobility FAQs · NYUAD Students
text:
INTERNATIONAL TRAVEL AND UAE RESIDENCE VISA

Frequently Asked Questions

As of March 3, 2026, and subject to change based on current conditions

Student Travel

Q: I have made personal travel plans for Spring Break. Should I continue with these plans?

A: Out of an abundance of caution, we strongly encourage you to reconsider any non-essential international travel plans during spring break. Conditions remain unpredictable, and travel at this time may present unexpected challenges, including flight disruptions, safety risks, increased personal costs, and difficulty returning to campus as scheduled. Choosing to stay local this break can help reduce potential risks – not only for you, but also for our broader campus community. If you have already made plans and are unsure what to do, we encourage you to carefully review the guidance and resources below and fully consider whether postponing or canceling travel may be the safest option.

Q: What travel guidance and resources can I review as I decide what to do for spring break?

A: You should carefully review the guidance and resources below:

-
Independent Student Travel

-
Travel with Your WITS

-
Securing Your Own Visa

-
Request for No Objection Letter

-
Download the Safe NYU app

-
Register your trip with your respective embassy or consulate

-
Register your trip in NYU Traveler and inform your family where you are traveling.

Q: If I travel for Spring Break and get stranded abroad, will the University support me?

A: The University does not provide financial or logistical support for personal travel and cannot take responsibility for the travel choices you make. Please work closely with your family if you are planning any personal travel at this time, and consider the risks with them.

Q: I want to travel home and remain there for the rest of the semester. Will I be able to attend and complete my classes remotely?

A: Yes, you will be able to attend classes remotely.

Q: I am enrolled in the EFSI program during Spring Break. Will this program still take place abroad?

A: This program has been cancelled.

Q: I am enrolled in the Chinese Language seminar going to China during Spring Break. Will this program still take place?

A: This program has been cancelled.

Q: I am funded to travel abroad very soon for research/conference/debate team/athletics. Will my funded travel still take place?

A: All university-funded student travel has been cancelled for the remainder of the semester.

Q: I am enrolled in a June Term class abroad? Will these classes proceed as scheduled?

A: At this time we are planning for all June Term classes to be taught as scheduled. We are closely monitoring the regional situation and the travel and visa conditions for all academic travel destinations. If a different decision has to be made about the June Term classes, we will inform you.

Q: I am approved to study away in Fall 2026. Will preparations for study abroad in the fall continue?

A: At this time we are planning for Fall 2026 study away preparations to continue as scheduled. We are closely monitoring the regional situation and the travel and visa conditions for all academic travel destinations. If a different decision has to be made about any of the Fall 2026 study away programs, we will inform you.

Q: I plan to apply for funding for a summer internship/research project. Will the summer funding process be impacted by the regional situation?

A: At this time we are planning for the summer funding application process to continue as scheduled. We are closely monitoring the regional situation and we will be checking the travel conditions for all summer destinations students will be applying for. As decisions are made, we will inform all impacted students if certain destinations cannot be funded or approved for travel.

Q: Should I expect additional or exacerbated difficulties with the visa(s) I need for my academic travel this summer and/or in the Fall?

A: It is hard to predict what each individual student will need to go through for a visa, and what rules or restrictions each embassy might choose to implement. The Office of Global Education will do our best to guide you but it's very important for students to review all embassy instructions online as well and to follow all official guidelines and timelines.

Q: I am arranging to travel home in the coming days. Will there be transportation provided between campus and the airports in Abu Dhabi and Dubai?

A: Yes, the University will do our best to provide shuttles to the airports in Abu Dhabi and Dubai. More information will be provided on the student portal once a regular shuttle schedule has been established.

UAE Student Residence Visa

Q: If I choose to depart for the rest of the semester, and my UAE visa expires while I’m away, how can I make sure I can get back into the UAE for the next semester?

A: If you hold a valid UAE student residence visa, you can exit and re-enter using your existing visa. If your visa is set to expire in the upcoming months, you will need to work with the Office of Global Education to determine the next steps for your return in the fall based on your specific visa expiration date.

Q: My UAE visa has been issued, but I’m still waiting for my physical Emirates ID card. What do I need to do next?

A: If your residence visa has been approved in the Immigration system, but you have not yet received your physical Emirates ID card, please email the NYUAD Immigration team and copy nyuad.uaestudentvisa@nyu.edu to request a copy of your Emirates ID card.

Q: I haven’t finished the fingerprinting process yet, and was supposed to complete this on March 2. What do I need to do next?

A: Students who still need to complete the fingerprinting process will need to wait for guidance from the NYUAD Immigration team.

title: Printing · NYUAD Students
text:
SafeQ — Our Print Management Solution

NYU Printing (using the SafeQ solution) is a secure and easy-to-use service that provides a full copy, print and scan solution while also conserving resources and helping the environment. You are able to pick up your print jobs from any multi-functional printer on the Saadiyat Campus using your NYU Card or NetID and password.

Additional Information

- Service Details

- Students, Faculty and Staff are eligible for this service

- This service is available 24/7/365

- The service is provisioned automatically when you join NYU

- How to use the NYU print service

All NYU Abu Dhabi multi-functional devices help secure your printing tasks. You will need to use your NYU Card as a means of authentication in order to print.

Once you have sent your printing job to the NYUAD Saadiyat print queue, you should do the following:

- Identify yourself by placing your NYU Card over the small card reader on the right of the printer

- Select the file (s) that you wish to print by using the touch screen

- Press Print to print the selected jobs or Print All to print all jobs in your queue. You may also Delete files that you no longer wish to print from this screen.

- Once you have printed, log out by clicking the Logout button on the top right of the screen.

- Printer locations

Printers have been strategically located throughout campus so you should never be too far from a printer.

- Default print settings

The default printing settings are to print on A4 paper, in black and white and double-sided. This is more environmentally friendly and cost-effective.

- Queued print jobs

Print jobs are stored for 72 hours before being deleted.

- Print charges

There are no charges for printing costs.

- Direct printing

Direct printing is not allowed. The printing service has been set up to only allow printing via NYU cards.

- How do I print using my personal computer?

All NYUAD-issued computers come pre-installed with the printing drivers installed and ready to use. If you are using your own computer or laptop, please refer to the correct installation instructions for your system:

- Mac OS X

- Windows

- Linux

title: Email · NYUAD Students
text:
NYU Email is an integral part of the NYU Google Apps set of online communications and collaboration applications.

E-mail can be accessed via a web browser at http://email.nyu.edu

Setting a Google Apps Password

If you prefer to use an email program on a mobile device, or through a email client (rather than the recommended NYU Email and NYU Calendar web interfaces), you will need to set a separate Google Apps password.

You can set or change your Google Apps password any time by following these instructions. Google Apps passwords do not expire.

- Go to start.nyu.edu using any web browser.

- On the first screen, enter your NYU NetID (appears on the back of your NYUCard), then click Start !

- Verify that your NYU NetID appears in the "Your NetID" field, then type your existing NYU NetID password (i.e., the one you use to log into NYUHome) into the "Your Password" field. Click Continue .

- Click the Set an NYU Google Apps for Education password link.

- Read and follow the on-screen directions to set or change your NYU Google Apps password. The password requirements (at least eight characters, etc.) are the same as those for your NetID password. ITS recommends that you use different passwords for your NetID password and your NYU Google Apps password.

Accessing NYU Email on Mobile Devices

- Android

- iOS

Additional Information

- Accessing NYU Email on Desktop Clients

NYU Abu Dhabi Information Technology does not recommend using desktop clients such as Outlook or Apple Mail for Google Apps. If you access your Google Mail/Calendar using either Microsoft Outlook or Apple Mail then you will encounter problems. Users have reported on many occasions email messages not being fully synchronized and calendar entries going missing.

Google provide very little support for their Sync tool -

“Our SLA applies specifically to our services. Client software, which runs on desktops, is a fundamentally different support problem because of the widely divergent desktop environments”

Google classes any problems with desktop mail clients as the lowest priority for them to investigate faults and advises not to use them - this means that it is far more effective and efficient to use the Google Apps web interface. This way you can be certain that all of your emails are present and that your calendar entries are accurately recorded.

- Sending an Email on Behalf of an Alias

NYU Email allows you to set up a "send from" email address as long as you are a member of that NYU email alias, or owner of that alternate email address.

- Click the gear icon in the upper right corner of your Mail window

- Select Settings, then click the Accounts tab.

- Click Add another email address you own.

After you follow the prompts, an email will be sent to the alias with your verification code. After you enter the verification code you can "send from" that email alias when composing a message.

Note: During the verification step, everyone on that email alias will receive the confirmation message. You may wish to warn people ahead of time to disregard this message. If there are a large number of people on the alias, you may wish to use a different solution for sending from a different address such as Email Direct .

If the confirmation message is going to an NYU Group, make sure that the posting permissions for the Group are set to Public, to ensure the verification message is received.

Note: To view messages you send or copy to yourself, you must use an address that is in your "From" drop-down menu or "Send As" list.

- Out of Office or Vacation Messages

You can create and manage automated out-of-office and vacation messages via the NYU Email web interface ( email.nyu.edu ):

-
Click the gear icon in the upper right corner, then select Settings .

-
In the General tab, scroll down and find the "Vacation responder" section.

-
Use the radio button to turn the Vacation responder on or off.

-
You can specify a range of dates during which the vacation message will be active by entering dates in First Day and Ends fields. If you set an end date, the vacation message will end automatically on that date.

-
In the Subject field, enter the subject line of your vacation message.

-
In the Message field, enter the body of your vacation message.

When you are finished, click the Save Changes button near the bottom of the screen.

- Google Application Storage

NYU Google Apps have unified storage between NYU Email and NYU Drive. Each user will receive 30GB of storage to be used across both services.

If you find that you require more space for either NYU Email or NYU Drive, more storage can be purchased on your account by going to https://www.google.com/settings/storage / . Once logged in with your NYU Google Apps account, you can select the amount of additional storage desired. A credit card is required to purchase additional storage . The card will be charged on a monthly basis.

- Service Details

Who is Eligible?

All NYUAD Faculty, Staff and Students are eligible for this service.

How to Request the Service

There is no need to request an email account, this will be set up prior to your arrival at NYU Abu Dhabi. If you need help or support please log a case with the IT Service Desk.

Hours of Availability

- This service is available 24/7.

- Support for this service is during standard NYUAD business hours.

Further questions

Please feel free to contact the IT Service Management Team should you have any feedback or improvement suggestions for the NYU email service.

title: Configuring Email on iOS · NYUAD Students
text:
Before you begin

- Ensure that you have set your Google Apps password .

- Make sure that you have the latest operating system. Google Sync is only supported on iOS versions 3.0 and above. To check which OS version you are currently running on your iOS device, go to Settings > General > About > Version. To upgrade, follow the Apple support website instructions .

- Perform a sync with iTunes to ensure that Contacts and Calendars from your device are backed up to your computer.

Setting up NYU Email and NYU Calendar on iOS devices (iPhone, iPod, iPad)

- Adding your NYU Google Apps account in iOS 7

- Open the Settings application on your device's home screen.

- Open Mail, Contacts, Calendars.

- Select Add Account...

- Select Exchange.

- Enter your NYU Email address (yourNetID@nyu.edu) in the "Email" section.

- Enter your Google Apps password in the "Password" section.

- Change the "Description" to NYU.

- Select Next at the top right of the screen.

- In the "Server" field, enter m.google.com .

- Leave the "Domain" field blank.

- Enter your NYU Email address (yourNetID@nyu.edu) in the "Username" section.

- Leave the "Description" section as is.

- Select Next at the top right of the screen.

- Select the options that you would like to sync on your device.

- Select Save.

- When prompted, select the appropriate action for existing contacts on your device:

- Unless you want to delete all the existing contacts and calendars on your phone, select Keep on my iPhone (or iPad/iPod) when prompted. This will also allow you to keep syncing with your computer via iTunes.

- If you want to sync only the "My Contacts" group, you must choose Delete Existing Contacts. If you choose to keep existing contacts, it will sync the contents of the "All Contacts" group instead. If there are no contacts on your phone, the contents of your "All Contacts" group will be synced.

- Adding your NYU Google Apps Account in iOS 6 and Below

- Open the Settings application on your device's home screen.

- Open Mail, Contacts, Calendars.

- Select Add Account...

- Select Microsoft Exchange.

- Enter your NYU Email address (yourNetID@nyu.edu) in the "Email" section.

- Leave the "Domain" field blank.

- Enter your NYU Email address (yourNetID@nyu.edu) in the "Username" section.

- Enter your Google Apps password in the "Password" section.

- Enter NYU in the "Description" section.

- When the "Server" field appears, enter m.google.com. Select Next.

- Select the options that you would like to sync on your device.

- Select Save.

- When prompted, select the appropriate action for existing contacts on your device:

- Unless you want to delete all the existing contacts and calendars on your phone, select Keep on my iPhone (or iPad/iPod) when prompted. This will also allow you to keep syncing with your computer via iTunes.

- If you want to sync only the "My Contacts" group, you must choose Delete Existing Contacts. If you choose to keep existing contacts, it will sync the contents of the "All Contacts" group instead. If there are no contacts on your phone, the contents of your "All Contacts" group will be synced.

- Set up "Send Mail As" feature and secondary calendars

To enable this feature, do the following:

- On your iOS device, go to email.nyu.edu .

- Log in with your NYU account. If you are logged in with a personal gmail account you will need to log out of that account first.

- Once your inbox has loaded, go to m.google.com/sync/settings/ .

- Select your device and click Enable "Send Mail As" for this device.

- Select the calendars you would like to sync with the device.

- Scroll down and click Save.

If you have set a personal alias (e.g., firstname.lastname@nyu.edu) as your default email address, it will now appear on your iOS device. For additional information, see NYU Email: How to send mail from an alias, NYU Groups address, or another email address you own .

- New Invitations

To enable New Invitations for your NYU Calendar on your iOS device:

- Sign into your NYU Calendar using the web browser on your device.

- Go to Calendar Settings > Calendars > Select on the Notifications for the calendar you want to sync.

- Under "Email," check New Invitations (and any of the other Invitation settings you want enabled), then click Save.
