title: Proofpoint Security Feature · NYUAD Students
text:
How does URL Defense protect NYU Email?

URL Defense is a tool that automatically rewrites links in incoming, external email messages sent to @nyu.edu email accounts to protect you when you click on the link. At the time it is clicked, the links are compared against known malicious websites. If a link is deemed safe, you will be directed to the requested web page. If a link is deemed unsafe, you will receive a notification (example below) that the website has been blocked. Links in email attachments are not rewritten, but if one contains a link that is deemed malicious at the time the email is received, then it is blocked by NYU's anti-malware filters.

What do rewritten URL Defense links look like?

Links in incoming NYU Email from external sources will initially look the same as usual, but if you hover over a link in HTML view within NYU Email, you will see a preview of the address at the lower left of the screen (example below) that begins with "urldefense.proofpoint.com" followed by the remainder of the link and a string of letters and numbers, as shown below. If you're viewing your email in plain text mode, you'll see the full, rewritten link in the body of your email. The rewritten link will first direct you to link Defense to compare it against known malicious websites, as described above.

What should I do if I receive a blocked message notification?

If the email was sent from someone you know, please advise them of the problem. The site will continue to be blocked until the security issues are resolved. Please note that intentionally visiting a website deemed malicious may lead to the compromise of your device and the data stored thereon and may also impact data on connected systems.

Will I see any difference when I click on a link?

When you click on a link, you will see a brief display of the rewritten link before being redirected to your destination (or to the blocked message above).

How does URL Defense differ from the NYU Email spam filter?

NYU has long employed tools to protect incoming, external email to @nyu.edu email addresses from malicious content. The new URL Defense feature enhances those efforts by rewriting links that were not blocked by the spam filter so that they can be checked against known malicious sites whenever they're clicked, even if it's long after delivery. You may continue to use the "Report spam" or "Report phishing" in your NYU email to train it to recognize and block phishing messages from arriving in your Inbox.

Why aren't links in email sent to Stern (@stern.nyu.edu), Law (@law.nyu.edu) or Courant (@courant.nyu.edu) accounts being rewritten?

At this time, URL Defense only rewrites links in incoming, external email sent to @nyu.edu email addresses. Other NYU domains will be addressed in the future.

What if I want to access a blocked link?

If you want to access a blocked link, please note that there is a potential risk to your device and the data stored thereon, as well as a risk to data on all connected systems, if you visit a malicious site. Instead of visiting a blocked link, use a search engine to look up the name of the individual/entity represented in the link as a way to potentially get more information on the blocked link. You can optionally visit some of the retrieved web pages, but please keep in mind, you may run a risk if you do so, since a simple online search will not indicate whether retrieved site links are safe for clicking.

Why is my entire attachment blocked instead of just the embedded link(s) that may be causing problems?

URL Defense scans links in files that are attached to email messages, but it does not rewrite links in those attachments like it does in the body of an email. Therefore, an attachment is blocked in its entirety if one or more links in it is deemed malicious. This feature was already in place before the launch of URL Defense.

What if I need to access a blocked attachment?

You can contact the sender and request that s/he remove embedded linkS from the attachment and resend it.

What if I was able to access a link I believe was malicious?

If you believe that you may have disclosed and therefore compromised sensitive information on a malicious site, such as an account username and password, it is recommended that you:

- Change your username and password on all affected sites as soon as possible.

- Run an antivirus scan on your computer.

Additionally, if you believe that a link on incoming external email was malicious and was not blocked by URL Defense, please report it to the Service Desk via nyuad.it@nyu.edu

Why is NYU implementing this security feature?

NYU IT is committed to protecting the sensitive information of the NYU community, as well as the University's networks and data. As detailed in the Policy on Responsible Use of NYU Computers and Data and the Appropriate Use of Email at New York University , this responsibility is also shared by all members of the NYU community. The implementation of URL Defense helps support data security by blocking access to many malicious websites. Websites that are linked to within email messages and attachments can be safe when they're first sent (and thus not detectable by spam filters) but then become malicious after the email is received. URL Defense helps protect you against these exploits by rewriting links in email to first direct you to a website that checks whether the requested web page is safe at the time you click it before sending you there. See the FAQs above for further details.

Who can I contact with questions?

If you have a general IT support question, or if you believe an attachment or an embedded link in an email message was blocked in error (false positive) or that a fraudulent site was not properly blocked (false negative), contact the Service Desk via nyuad.it@nyu.edu .

title: IT Security · NYUAD Students
text:
Privacy, Safety and Trust

NYU Abu Dhabi’s Cybersecurity program has three pillars at its core: privacy, safety and trust.

- Privacy of any data that is handled by NYUAD IT in order to achieve the academic mission and be compliant with legal and regulatory frameworks.

- Safety of data and systems that are managed by NYUAD IT from misuse to ensure that the community feels safe to use IT resources.

- Trust in NYUAD to safeguard the privacy and safety of data handled and NYUAD systems to operate reliably in supporting the academic mission of the institution as well as operational excellence and community engagement goals.

If you have any further queries or concerns, we invite you to contact the IT Leadership team at nyuad.it.leadership@nyu.edu and we will be happy to assist you.

title: Multi Factor Authentication (Duo) · NYUAD Students
text:
For full MFA setup guides, instructions, and FAQs, visit the NYU MFA global page .

What is MFA?

Multi-Factor Authentication (MFA) requires you to prove your identity in two or more ways when logging in — not just your password.

Think of it like a lock that requires both a key and a fingerprint.

NYUAD uses Duo Security for MFA, protecting all campus systems, and is switching to MFA Level 4.

Why MFA Level 4?

- Standard push notifications can be tricked by phishing attacks.

- MFA Level 4 requires you to actively type a matching code, making it impossible for attackers to approve a login on your behalf — even if they have your password.

- This stops adversary-in-the-middle (AiTM) phishing attacks cold.

What's Different: MFA Level 4

Before: Standard Duo Push

- Your phone buzzes. Open Duo Mobile and tap Approve

After: Verified Duo Push

- The only change — A three-digit code appears on your screen. Open Duo Mobile, type the code, then tap Approve.

How to Login Using MFA 4

- Enter NetID and password — same as always.

- Verify your identity — Duo prompt appears.

- Open Duo Mobile App — notification arrives on your phone.

- Enter 3-digit code — type the code from your screen into Duo app.

- You're in — login complete.

Supported Authentication Methods

- Verified Duo Push

- Touch ID / Face ID

- Windows Hello

- Security Key (USB/NFC)

Methods No Longer Supported

- SMS/Text code

- Hardwards token

- Landline / flip phone

- Duo Mobile Passcode

For full MFA setup guides, instructions, and FAQs, visit the NYU MFA global page .

title: MFA Cyber attacks · NYUAD Students
text:
Protect your MFA so it can protect you.

Multi-factor authentication (MFA) is so effective at securing accounts and personal information that it has caused cyber attackers to adjust their tactics. Increasingly, they're attempting to circumvent MFA by fooling people into giving out your confidential MFA code or responding to a fake MFA authentication request. Targeting the human, rather than the technology, to undermine security is called social engineering, and it's how most cyber attacks succeed.

What's the threat?

Cyberattackers who compromise MFA via this type of phishing attack can gain access to everything you have access to —including NYU Email, NYU cloud storage, Workday, internal systems, and anything else you use your NYU login to access.

One compromised account could open the door for an attack on other critical systems and services. They can even disrupt or reroute your paycheck and add their own device to your MFA profile.

How are cyber attackers attempting to fool us?

- The primary method attackers use is to send fake MFA authentication notices, often a lot of them, in an attempt to fool you or annoy you into clicking APPROVE (you might hear this called MFA bombing ) or giving someone your passcode.

- They can come via SMS text message, email, phone call, or even what looks like a notification from Duo. By phone, the attacker will usually claim to be a co-worker or IT support staff.

- The goal is to get you to:

- Approve a fraudulent Duo notification.

- Give them your passcode if you authenticate by passcode or SMS text message.

- Click something on a convincing fake authentication site that collects your data.

Examples of phishing emails and fake logins

How can you protect yourself (and others)?

While attacks on MFA constitute a significant security threat, they are easily blocked using one simple method:

- If you didn't initiate MFA authentication immediately before getting the notification, DO NOT RESPOND. If it's someone on the phone, hang up. That's usually all it takes to beat this sort of scam.

- Don't react to any sense of urgency or panic they attempt to create.

- If they claim to be from NYU, they're lying. No one at NYU will EVER contact you and ask for information about your MFA credentials , just as no one at NYU will contact you asking for your password.

- Multiple authentication requests can be annoying, especially in the middle of the night. Attackers are relying on your frustration to succeed.

- If you receive an authentication request you did not initiate, select DENY on the Duo screen. You will then be asked: “Was this a suspicious login?” Select Yes , and Duo administrators will be alerted.

- Report the attempt immediately to security@nyu.edu so NYU's Global Office of Information Security (GOIS) can investigate the attack and help protect you and everyone else at the University.

- You can see what devices have been added to your MFA profile via the instructions below.

Think you might have been compromised?

- First, don't panic—but do take action quickly. The faster you report the incident, the less damage the attacker can do. Scammers are good at what they do, so there's no need to feel bad if they got you.

- Change your NYU password .

- Email security@nyu.edu to report the incident. Please include as much information as you can. If you're unable to send email, contact the NYU IT Service Desk by phone.

- Review the list of devices associated with your MFA enrollment and remove any you didn't add yourself (see the Manage your MFA devices" instructions above).

What is NYUAD doing to help protect the community?

NYU is constantly evolving its cybersecurity infrastructure to counter attacks. This includes increasing rapid response to incidents, studying reports and trends to be on high alert when a known attack is impacting multiple community members, and continuing to expand the database of attacks used to screen phishing and social engineering attempts.

Additional information

- MFA Related Phishing Attempts

- Tricks Used By Scammers to Bypass MFA

title: MFA Tips · NYUAD Students
text:
Multi-Factor Authentication (MFA) adds a second layer of security to help prevent anyone other than you from accessing your sensitive information online. The service NYU uses for MFA is called Duo.

Below are two tips that will help you authenticate faster with Duo for a better experience.

Tip 1: Authenticate less often
Did you know that you only need to authenticate with MFA once a day? The next time you authenticate, tick the ‘remember me for one day’ option and you will not be prompted for authentication for 24 hours. Please ensure that you are using the “push” option and not the (slower and more expensive) “call me” option!

Tip 2: Get a push notification automatically
Did you know that you can receive a push notification automatically without having to choose it? Follow the below steps:

- Go to start.nyu.edu and click Log In , and enter your NYU NetID and password.

- On the MFA Authentication screen, select My Settings & Devices . You will be prompted to confirm your identity by authenticating with MFA on your current device.

- In the When I log in dropdown menu (if you have several devices, you may need to scroll down to see this menu), select Automatically send this device a Duo push.

- Click Save.

Tip 3: Authenticate with multiple devices
Do you have a secondary device to authenticate with in the event that you lose your mobile phone? Set up your home and office numbers to receive a telephone call to authenticate. Instructions are located in the ‘Useful Information’ section on the Intranet under ‘Adding another device or phone number(s) to MFA’.

Tip 4: Use TouchID on your MacBook
Do you have a MacBook Pro with the Touch ID option? If so, you can now use the Touch ID option to authenticate. This can be done by enrolling another device. Instructions are located in the ‘Useful Information’ section on the Intranet under ‘How to use the MacBook Touch ID for authorization’.

title: Wireless (Wi-Fi) · NYUAD Students
text:
Wireless networking (NYU Roam) is available for users to connect their devices in a secure and convenient method anywhere on campus.

Getting Started

In order to connect your device to the wireless network (SSID NYU), please click on one of the following set-up guides:

- Mac

- Windows 10

Additional Information

- Gaming Consoles, Wireless Printers, Apple TV's, etc.

WPA devices, by default, are unable to connect to the Wireless (NYU Roam) network due to additional encryption protocols. If you'd like to connect one of these devices, please submit this form .

Examples of these type of devices include:

- Gaming consoles

- Personal wireless printers

- Kindle e-book readers

- Apple TV consoles

If you are in a residence at the Saadiyat Campus then you can connect these to the NYU Abu Dhabi Residential Wi-Fi Service via the Netgear routers located in apartments and lounges.

Note: NYU Abu Dhabi Information Technology provides support for the network connection only and not for your personal hardware devices connecting to the Netgear routers (gaming consoles, etc.).

- Usage Policy

Access to NYU Abu Dhabi's network must be exercised in conformity with all applicable NYUAD's policies and procedures . In particular, be sure to familiarize yourself with policies regulating the use of peer-to-peer applications . Failure to abide by these policies can result in the suspension of network privileges and referral of the matter to the appropriate disciplinary process.

- Service Details

Who is Eligible?

NYURoam Wireless service is available to community members with an active NYU NetID and password. This includes most administrators, faculty, staff, students and selected partners.

Those without a NetID and password are not eligible to connect to the Wireless (NYU Roam) service.

How to Request the Service

Students, Staff and Faculty with a NetID and Password will automatically have access to this service.

Hours of Availability

- This service is available 24/7.

- Support for this service is during standard NYUAD business hours.

Further Questions

Please feel free to contact the IT Service Management Team should you have any feedback or improvement suggestions for the NYU email service.

- Having an issue with the NYU Wireless Network?

If you are having issues connecting to the NYU wireless network, please use the form here to report the issue. A member of IT will be in contact.

https://students.nyuad.nyu.edu/services/technology-and-support/nyuroam-wireless-network/connecting-with-windows-10/

title: Residential Wi-Fi · NYUAD Students
text:
Service Description

Residential Wi-Fi allows users to connect their personal devices (e.g., computers, smartphones, gaming consoles, personal printers, ebook readers, and Apple TVs) to the Internet or communicate with one another wirelessly within the student lounges on campus.

Who Is Eligible for This Service?

Students living on Saadiyat Campus.

How to Request

Each student lounge has a router that can connects to the Internet. User devices can connect to the router wirelessly or through a wired connection. The network ID and password are printed on the signage in the lounge.

Hours of Availability

24/7/365

Additional Information

- Student Lounge Wi-Fi Information Pack

Students can connect their personal and gaming devices to the Internet by typing in the Wireless Network (SSID) and password as printed on the signage in the room.

- How is Res Wi-Fi different to Wireless?

Res Wi-Fi allows you to connect your personal devices (printers, gaming devices, Apple TVs, etc.) to the Internet, which cannot connect to the NYU network. Please refer to Connecting to the Internet at NYU Abu Dhabi .

title: Wireless Speed Test · NYUAD Students
text:
Test Your Connection

Click "GO" below to conduct a speed test for your Wi-Fi connection on campus . The test will display your current wireless speed. Typical high-definition video streams use 5 Mbps. A result of 10 Mbps or more is considered adequate for general use. For more information on what is being measured, please see definitions below.

What does ping mean?

A ‘ping’ is a method of checking if the computer is connected to a network. It also determines the latency or delay between two computers. It is used to ensure that a host computer which your computer tries to access is operating. A long ping (above 100ms) means a slower connection. You want a low ping time as possible.

What is Jitter?

Jitter, or network jitter, is the variance in time delay in milliseconds (ms) between data packets over a network. It is a disruption in the normal sequence of sending data packets. For example, If you have “computer A” communicating with “computer B”, the two will transfer data packets. Over a network, the packets travel in equal intervals. This will allow the receiving computer to process the data. When there is high jitter, these intervals become disrupted. Ideally, jitter should be below 30ms.

What is Download?

Download speed is the speed that information on the Internet (e.g., text and graphics) is transferred to your computer; that is, how long it takes your computer to load websites and download files to display on your screen. Download speeds of 15Mbps and above is a good download rate.

What is Upload?

Upload speed is the speed that your computer can transfer or send information to the Internet. For example, if you want to send photos to a website to be printed by your local vendor, you “upload” the photos to the site. Upload speeds of 10Mbps and above is a good upload rate.

Please note that you will only see the test below if you are connecting from the NYUAD campus .

title: Remote Connectivity VPN · NYUAD Students
text:
Remote connectivity to the NYU network is via a Virtual Private Network (VPN). A VPN is a secure communications protocol that tunnels through another network and enables you to access NYU resources when you are off-campus.

The VPN will assist you with accessing the file share, services and other administrative systems whilst being off-campus.

How to connect

- Locate Cisco AnyConnect Secure Mobility Client

- For Windows, you can find this via the Start Menu -> All Programs -> Cisco -> Cisco AnyConnect Secure Mobility Client

- For Macs, you can find this via Finder -> Applications -> Cisco -> Cisco AnyConnect Secure Mobility Client

- In the window that opens, type this server address vpn.abudhabi.nyu.edu. In the login window that opens, enter your NYU NetID and password in the "Username" and "Password" fields. In the "Second Password" field enter one of the options below:
> " push " - to receive a push notification via MFA Duo App (recommended)

> " SMS " - to receive a text message to your primary registered phone number

- You will be asked to authenticate on the MFA Duo app on your mobile phone

- A banner message with NYU support information will appear; click OK .

- Once connected, you will see the below Cisco icon (or similar) appear with a lock in the taskbar at the bottom of your screen. This confirms connectivity to NYU AnyConnect VPN services.

Additional Information

- Service Details

- Students, Faculty and Staff are eligible for this service

- This service is available 24/7/365

- The VPN software is pre-installed on NYU Abu Dhabi-issued laptops and computers

- Can I use the VPN on my mobile device?

Yes, VPN Mobile is supported on both Android and iOS. Follow the steps in the section Configuring VPN on Android devices and Configuring VPN on iOS devices respectively.

- Configuring VPN on Android devices

To install the Cisco AnyConnect Secure Mobility Client for Android and iOS from the Google Play Store:

- Open the Play Store on your Phone.

- Select Search.

- In the Search Box, enter "anyconnect" and tap cisco anyconnect in the Suggestions list. tap Free, then INSTALL APP

- When the installation is complete, OPEN the Cisco AnyConnect Secure Mobility Client App.

- A confirmation window will open asking if you want to enable this software. Tap OK to accept.

- Tap Add VPN Connection in the AnyConnect home screen.

- Tap Description to enter a unique name for the connection entry (e.g., "NYU AnyConnect VPN").

- Tap Server Address and type vpn.abudhabi.nyu.edu into the text box

- Tap Save

- Tap OFF next to "AnyConnect VPN" to toggle it to "ON."

- Enter your NYU NetID and password in the "Username" and "Password" fields, then tap Connect.

- A banner message with NYU support information will appear; tap Accept.

- If the connection is successful, the "Status" section will display the word "Connected" and a "VPN" icon will appear in the Status Bar.

- Ending a VPN connection on an Android

- When you are ready to terminate your VPN connection, follow these steps:

- Tap the Cisco AnyConnect Secure Mobility Client icon.

- Tap ON next to "AnyConnect VPN" to toggle it to "OFF".

- When the connection is successfully terminated, the "Status" section will display the word "Disconnected" and the "VPN" icon will no longer appear in the Status Bar

- Configuring VPN on iOS devices

To install the Cisco AnyConnect Secure Mobility client for Apple iOS from the Apple App Store:

- Open the App Store on your iPhone.

- Select Search.

- In the Search Box, enter "anyconnect" and tap cisco anyconnect in the Suggestions list. tap Free, then INSTALL APP

- When the installation is complete, OPEN the Cisco AnyConnect Secure Mobility Client App.

- A confirmation window will open asking if you want to enable this software. Tap OK to accept.

- Tap Add VPN Connection in the AnyConnect home screen.

- Tap Description to enter a unique name for the connection entry (e.g., "NYU AnyConnect VPN").

- Tap Server Address and type vpn.abudhabi.nyu.edu into the text box

- Tap Save

- Tap OFF next to "AnyConnect VPN" to toggle it to "ON."

- Enter your NYU NetID and password in the "Username" and "Password" fields, then tap Connect.

- A banner message with NYU support information will appear; tap Accept.

- If the connection is successful, the "Status" section will display the word "Connected" and a "VPN" icon will appear in the Status Bar.

- Ending a VPN connection on an iPhone

- When you are ready to terminate your VPN connection, follow these steps:

- Tap the Cisco AnyConnect Secure Mobility Client icon.

- Tap ON next to "AnyConnect VPN" to toggle it to "OFF".

- When the connection is successfully terminated, the "Status" section will display the word "Disconnected" and the "VPN" icon will no longer appear in the Status Bar.

- I'm having issues connecting to/setting up the VPN - what should I do?

If you cannot connect to the Abu Dhabi VPN (vpn. abudhabi. nyu.edu ), you may want to try connecting to the NY VPN ( vpn.nyu.edu ) or vice versa. However, from Abu Dhabi, you will find that the Abu Dhabi VPN is much faster.

- How do I download the VPN for my computer or laptop?

You can download and install the VPN by following these instructions.

title: Wired (Cabled Network) · NYUAD Students
text:
The NYUAD cabled network provides fast, reliable and secure access to NYU-NET throughout the campus.

Connecting personal computers to the wired network

Personal computers require some additional configuration to connect to the NYUAD wired network. Please review the instructions available in the knowledge base articles below on how to connect your personal computer to the wired network:

- Windows 7/8/8.1/10

- Windows 11

- MacOS 10.8+

- Linux Red Hat

- Linux Ubuntu

Connecting personal devices to the wired network

To connect devices (gaming consoles, printers, etc.) that do not support network authentication (802.1.x), you will need to connect to the Device Registration Portal using a separate computer already connected to the network (via cable or wireless) and manually register those devices.

The device registration portal allows you to add up to 5 devices and perform other operations, such as edit and delete your already registered devices. The registration is only required once, however, it will expire if the device is not connected to the network after a period of 6 months.

To register your device, follow these steps:

- From a computer that is already connected to the NYUAD-NET, browse to the Device Registration Portal and login using your netID and password (Shibboleth).

- Click on the Add button and enter the following information:

- Device Name: the name of your device, e.g., Research-Printer-01.

- Device ID: the MAC address of your device. Please visit the What's a MAC Address and how to find it? page for more information.

sections.title: Connecting personal devices to the wired network
sections.text:
To connect devices (gaming consoles, printers, etc.) that do not support network authentication (802.1.x), you will need to connect to the Device Registration Portal using a separate computer already connected to the network (via cable or wireless) and manually register those devices.

The device registration portal allows you to add up to 5 devices and perform other operations, such as edit and delete your already registered devices. The registration is only required once, however, it will expire if the device is not connected to the network after a period of 6 months.

To register your device, follow these steps:

- From a computer that is already connected to the NYUAD-NET, browse to the Device Registration Portal and login using your netID and password (Shibboleth).

- Click on the Add button and enter the following information:

- Device Name: the name of your device, e.g., Research-Printer-01.

- Device ID: the MAC address of your device. Please visit the What's a MAC Address and how to find it? page for more information.

- Description: a description of your device so it can be identified easily on the network, e.g., John's Research instrument for computer science.

- Click on the Submit button.

- Your device is registered and will be listed in the Managed Devices section.

- Once the devices are registered, they will display a status of Pending. Once you connect your registered device to the network, the status will change to Active.

title: Bikes on Campus · NYUAD Students
text:
The campus has no dedicated bike lanes. As all pathways on campus are designed for pedestrians, when riding on campus, be cautious, considerate, and yield to pedestrian traffic.

Bicycles may not be ridden indoors.

Bike Racks

Bicycles must be secured to bike racks on campus, and not chained to light posts, trees, handrails, etc. Bike racks are only available on the high line, and can be reached from the main road via the ramps behind West Apartments (B1) and East Apartments (B2) on the north side of the campus. Abandoned bicycles or bicycles chained to unapproved elements will be confiscated.

title: Campus Parking · NYUAD Students
text:
The Department of Campus Safety manages the NYUAD Campus Parking facility, ensuring safe, accessible, and well-regulated parking for all community members. Below, you will find essential information on how to register for parking, where to park, and updates on upcoming system enhancements.

Apply for a Parking Permit

All NYUAD community members are required to hold a valid parking permit to access the campus parking garage.

- Complete the Parking Permit Application form on the Self-Service Portal.

- Upload a copy of your current vehicle registration as part of the application.

- Once submitted, you will receive an email acknowledging receipt of your application.

- After processing, a confirmation email will notify you when your permit is ready for collection.

- Collect your RFID parking permit from the Campus Safety Desk, located at the Service Center, C2 Building, Level 0.

- Affix the RFID permit to the rearview mirror of your vehicle to activate access at parking entrances.

Note: All parking-related queries and permit requests must now be submitted via the Self-Service Portal.

Where to Park — Parking Zone Access by User Type

1. Campus Residents

- Designated Parking : Basement 2 — Zones 1 and 4

- Requirement : Residents must park in their B2 assigned zones (1 and 4) to ensure optimal space availability for commuters in B1.

- Access : 24/7 access permitted with a valid parking decal.

2. Daily Commuters (Faculty, Staff, Students, and Contractors)

- Permitted Parking :

- Basement 1 (B1): First-come, first-served (excluding reserved VIP and retail parking)

- Basement 2 (B2): Zones 2 and 3 only

- Timing : Commuter parking is allowed between 7am and 11pm unless otherwise authorized.

3. Visitor Parking

- Designated Parking : Only allowed in B1, in available, unmarked spaces.

- Permits : Visitors do not require a permit.

- Visitor details are logged at the parking entrance by Campus Safety Officers.

- Visitors may not park in resident-reserved or restricted areas.

Parking Violations and Fines

To ensure compliance and safety, Campus Safety actively monitors for parking violations. Penalties include:

- First Violation — Warning letter

- Second Violation — AED 500 fine

- Third Violation — AED 500 fine and possible access restrictions

- Parking without credentials in any People of Determination (POD) space will incur a fine of AED 1,000 for each violation.

- One-year reset timeline applies.

Paying Fines

Fines can be paid in person at the Campus Safety Desk (C2 Level 0), using a debit or credit card.

Unpaid Fines:

- Students may face holds on university services

- Employees may have fines deducted via payroll.

- Repeat visitor violations may result in denied access.

title: Transportation Request · NYUAD Students
text:
Book Transport for University Events and Activities

Book your transportation through the Transportation Request Form .

NYUAD Transportation Booking Guidelines

- The use of NYUAD transportation for personal or non-NYUAD-related purposes is not permitted.

- NYUAD transportation is strictly for university-related business and academic purposes. Personal or non-NYUAD-related travel is not permitted.

- Advance Request Requirement: All trips require a completed Transport Service Request Form submitted at least 72 hours in advance of the proposed travel time.

- Request forms must be submitted online. Phone requests will not be processed, except in emergencies.

- Transportation booking requests must include a clear business or academic justification, which will be reviewed and approved by the requesting department's budget approver.

- All transportation charges will be billed directly to the requesting department.

- Services and bookings are subject to vehicle availability with the service provider.

title: BikeShare · NYUAD Students
text:
The NYUAD BikeShare program is reopening on 22nd of September 2026.

The program allows you to borrow bikes and explore Saadiyat in a fun, eco-friendly way!

Please watch the Announcements Page on Tuesdays to sign up for a bike.

BikeShare Program Guidelines

- Bikes are available to be loaned out over a five-day period.

- Use the Bike Request Form to request a bike. The link to request a bike will be posted on the Student Portal on Tuesdays.

- Students can't sign up for a bike two weeks in a row.

- Bikes will be picked up Thursday and scheduled to return the following Tuesday (five days total)

- Collection and return location will be NYUAD Bike Room, B2. (Take the public elevator in front of A5, Go to Basement 2, and turn right. It's a couple of doors down, clearly labeled)

- If immediately required outside the opening hours, students may email NYUAD.bikeshare@nyu.edu and loan out bikes if available. Students will be required to pay deposits to the mechanics upon collection.

Damages

Students shall maintain bikes in excellent condition and hose the bike if necessary. If bikes are returned damaged or dirty, student will be required to pay for damages or in extreme cases may lose their BikeShare privilege.

AED 50 — Key replacement

AED 30 — Dirty bike

AED 50 — Lock replacement

AED 100 - Major damage to bike

Rules

A helmet is provided and must be worn at all times while riding an NYUAD bicycle. No exceptions. Failure to do so will result in a ban from the BikeShare program.

Bikes must be locked securely when not in use, and the school helmet must not be left on the bike.

The bikes are not to be taken off Saadiyat Island unless on a school sponsored function.

Long-term bike requests are reviewed on a case by case basis. A training schedule along with competition registration information must be submitted This is only for athletes participating in competitions.

Students requesting bikes for rental are responsible for the maintenance of their bikes . If there are any issues, reach out to the bike mechanics at nyuad.bikeshare@nyu.edu .

Bike Types

A student may check out one of the following bikes for the load period:

- Mountain Bike - Small, Medium, Large

- Road Bike - Small, Medium, Large

- Hybrid Bike- Small, Medium, Large

For any program related matters and queries — including group rides and late rentals — please contact NYUAD.bikeshare@nyu.edu .

title: Community Events · NYUAD Students
text:
Community Events

NYU Abu Dhabi Athletics hosts a number of sporting events for the community each year as a way to engage with the community beyond our campus. Community events are free to participate in and provide the Falcon Feeling experience to all our guests! Community events happen either annually as one-off events or occur as regular programs throughout the year.

Katching Relay

Think you can get a team together to collectively beat the world’s top marathon runner? Katching Relay does just that! Teams of 10 to 14 runners take to the track in 200 or 400 meter bursts to beat the men's marathon world record time. The event is free to participate in and is open to the entire community. Please watch Intranet Announcements for more information.

Falcon Ride

Started in 2018, the annual Falcon Ride is an annual community group cycle ride at Al Hudayriat Island. Shirts, medals, and refreshments are provided for all participants as a way to join together in fitness and in celebration. The community ride is open to everyone from all levels.

title: Community Sports · NYUAD Students
text:
NYU Abu Dhabi's Community Sports Program is designed to provide an opportunity for students, faculty, staff, family members, alumni, and all other NYUAD community members to participate with each other in organized recreational athletic activities. This format promotes a supportive atmosphere that provides leadership opportunities, community interaction, and recreation for all individuals, regardless of their skill or ability.

Each semester we have an Open Play and Community Sports League season.

Open Play starts off the semester scheduling a weekly time, date, and location for the community regardless of skill level to join, enjoy, or try a new sport. Moreover, Open Play also allows for natural teams to form and practice for the Community Sports Leagues later in the semester.

2026-2027 Fall Open Play Schedule

Volleyball

Every Tuesday, 6pm – 8pm

Location: C2 – Performance Gym

Futsal

Every Friday, 6pm – 8pm

Location: C2 – Performance Gym

Additional Information

Other sports may be added if there is sufficient interest. To request an additional sport, please email Campus Recreation Specialist Khalifa Al Suwaidi .

To sign up and to find the most up-to-date schedule, please refer to FABS .

Open Play is typically only offered during the academic year (Fall and Spring semesters).

title: Climbing Wall · NYUAD Students
text:
Climbing Wall (*Currently Closed)

Location: West side of the Performance Gymnasium in the Campus Center (C2)

Class times will be posted on the FABS Class Registration Module each week. Community members can register for a class up to 3 days in advance. Class size is limited.

All climbers will be required to attend an auto-belay course (ABC) prior to attending an open climb session. The sessions can be found on Class Registration. The auto-belay course will be a 2 hour session with the first hour being an introduction to the wall and the auto-belay system. The second hour of the session will consist of a climbing assessment and practice on the wall. Once a community member has completed this course they are then free to register for Open Climb courses. The ABC course is listed under Class Registration.

Participants must be registered on FABS and have a valid NYUAD ID to participate. Guests are not permitted to use the Climbing Wall.

Community members under 18 must have a parent/guardian sign a liability waiver at the wall in order to participate. The wall is not open for guests.

Women only classes will be offered. The Climbing Wall is an open space.

For more information, please contact nyuad.athletics.reception@nyu.edu

- Rules of Use

Open Climb (14 years +) Community members (students, staff, and faculty) can enjoy a supervised session during the week to climb! Afternoon and evening sessions are available. Please check the schedule on FABS to book your spot. Check in is directly at the Climbing Wall.

Top Roping Sessions

Top rope climbing is a form of climbing that requires a climbing partner as a belayer, a rope that runs through an anchor system at the top of the route, makes use of personal protective equipments and essential friction devices that helps control the rope during climbing and belaying.

After the course, you will be able to tie-in, safely belay your climbing partner with manual and mechanical friction devices and understand safety rules between climbing and belaying. This course is a 3 day course, where you must complete day 1 to advance to day 2. The third day of the course is an assessment day. You must have completed the ABC course and 3 Open Climb sessions to participate in the Top Rope sessions. For questions on the Top Rope sessions, please reach out to Coach Ella .

Equipment: Please note that participants must use the following NYUAD equipment (ropes and carabiners) provided by NYUAD. Harnesses and shoes are also available to use. If you have your own harness, this must be signed off by a wall supervisor, be less than 10 years old and in good condition.

-
Guest Policy: No guests are allowed on the Climbing Wall.

title: Competition Pool · NYUAD Students
text:
Regular Operating Hours and General Guidelines

No preregistration is needed but you must be a FABS member to use the pool. A valid NYU Abu Dhabi ID must be presented at reception in order to use the Locker Room facility.

Regular Pool Hours

Monday to Thursday: 6am-2pm and 3pm-10pm

Fridays: 6am-10pm

Saturday to Sunday: 8am-8pm

During PHE class hours there may be limited lanes for community swimming

Women's Only swim hours: (pool will be closed to male community members)

Thursdays & Saturdays: 12 pm - 2 pm

Mondays & Wednesdays : 4:00 pm - 6:15 pm

Requirements

Keep personal belongings to a minimum and store them in the designated areas.

Only flip-flops are allowed on the pool deck. Trainers or outdoor shoes are not permitted.

Follow the entry and exit directional signage.

Attendees must bring their own water — water dispensers will not be available.

The pool does not lend out goggles or swim caps unless you are participating in the University Swim Team or a PHE course in the pool. All equipment must be returned at the end of the semester.

Usage Guidelines

Max. 6 swimmers per lane

- Pool will be set to 50 m lanes in the mornings and on Friday- Sunday.

- Pool will be set to 25 m lanes on weekday afternoons Monday- Thursday.

Users should store personal belongings in the designated area for their lane.

All participants may bring a small bag with their own swimming aids (kick-boards, pull buoy, etc.), goggles and towel.

Location

The NYUAD Aquatics Center features a 50-meter competitive pool located on Level B1 in the Campus Center (C2) building.

- Regular Programming (Descriptions)

During the Academic Year, the Pool offers a wide variety of programming for all ability levels. Timings vary and will be posted here at the start of each term. Programming may include:

Physical Education

Beginner's Swimming courses are regularly offered every semester. Classes are available to register through Albert. All undergraduate students are eligible to sign up.

Student Intercollegiate Swim Practice

The swim club is for those who are at least intermediate level swimmers and have confidence in swimming in more than one stroke. The programs designed for practice will have individualized goals, stroke correction, and training guidelines to help prepare for competitions.

Ladies-Only

During this time, only female swimmers and female lifeguards are permitted in the pool area.

- Rules of Use

A valid NYU Abu Dhabi ID must be presented at reception in order to access the locker facility. There will be no access without a proper ID.

Individuals are not allowed in the pool area unless there is a lifeguard on duty and the facility is open.

Do not distract on-duty lifeguards and other aquatics staff.

All individuals must shower before entering in the pool.

Individuals with skin diseases, open cuts, sores, bandages, colds, coughs, or infected eyes are not permitted in the pool.

All individuals must wear appropriate swimwear in order to enter the pool area. Clothing deemed suitable for swimming includes material made of Spandex, Lycra, or nylon. Swimming in street clothes and shoes, underwear, see-through swimwear, and/or other inappropriate clothing is strictly prohibited.

Food and drinks — including gum — are not permitted. Glass containers are prohibited. Water in an appropriate container (sports bottle, etc.) is permitted.

No diving in water less than 1.5m and swimming under the bulkhead is prohibited.

Access for Minors is as follows:

-
Resident children aged 13 and under can access the pool accompanied by an Adult (18+) with a reservation

-
Resident children 14 and over can access the pool unaccompanied

Any form of boisterous play (running, dunking, wrestling), which may endanger the safety of patrons in the pool area is prohibited. The use of toys, balls, etc. are at the discretion of the lifeguard.

No water wings, rings, back floats (including those built into bathing suits) or other flotation devices are permitted. Only Coast Guard-approved and labeled life-jackets designed to provide vertical support may be worn in the pool.

No unauthorized private lessons of any kind are permitted in the pool.

FAQs

- Why is the pool so cold?

The pool temperature ranges from 26-28 degrees, which is the optimal range for a pool that serves as both a competition and recreational pool.

- What is Women's Only Swim?

During this time, only female swimmers and female lifeguards are permitted in the pool area. Please see Women's Only schedule above.

- Is a 50m swim available?

Pool will be set to 50 m lanes in the mornings Monday- Thursdays and all day Friday-Sunday.

Pool will be set to 25 m lanes on weekday afternoons.

- Why aren’t flotation devices, i.e. water rings, allowed?

To adhere to standard safety guidelines, Coast Guard-approved life jackets are the only flotation devices allowed.

Contact the Pool

Campus Center (C2), Level B1

Pool Reception
+971 2 628 7207

nyuad.athletics.reception@ nyu.edu

title: Equipment · NYUAD Students
text:
Recreational equipment is available to the campus community while they use the athletic facilities. Campus community members who are using an athletic space can request equipment from the Equipment Issue Room by emailing nyuad.athletics.reception@nyu.edu before their session. All borrowed equipment must be returned at the end of the session.

A valid NYUAD ID Card is required to check out items. For more information, please contact nyuad.athletics.reception@nyu.edu .

Opening Hours

Location: Campus Center (C2), first floor.
Regular Operating Hours: Monday to Friday 7am-10pm, Saturday to Sunday 8am-8pm

Team Uniforms Issuing Policy

For students on University Sports Teams: Your coach will assign you your uniform number at the start of the semester. Uniforms are handed out in pairs (same size top and bottom), and uniforms cannot be traded. Uniforms must be picked up by 4pm on the day of competition . There will be no issuing of uniforms after 4pm, so please plan ahead. Friends and teammates cannot check out your uniform for you. All uniforms need to be returned to the Equipment Issue Room by 9 pm on the day following the game so they can be laundered and stored. Late return of uniforms will prevent an athlete from practicing until the uniform is returned.

Female Athletes

For female athletes requesting more coverage, the Equipment Room can provide the following black items for checkout:

- Long-sleeve shirts

- Tights or black joggers

- Hijabs

- Student athletes should not compete in their own attire. All uniforms for competitions should come from the Equipment Room.

Equipment

Equipment Borrowing Policy
Recreational equipment

Recreational equipment (badminton, tennis, basketball, soccer equipment, etc.) can be collected at the Equipment Issue Room when checking in for a booked session (subject to availability). Equipment must be returned to the EIR at the end of the session. All equipment must be returned in good working order.

Failure to return equipment on time may result in the loss of future borrowing privileges.

Return of Borrowed Items

All items borrowed from the Department of Athletics must be returned during the Equipment Issue Room open hours . Items are not to be left unattended on the reception counter whilst the Equipment Issue Room is closed. Any items that go missing due to not following the return procedure will result in a replacement charge, payable by the last assignee for that item.

Guests

Guests may not sign out equipment. Items must be signed out by a sponsoring community member and must have paid for a guest pass and signed a waiver. See the Guest Policy for more information.

The following recreational items are available to be checked out from the Athletics Equipment Issue Room during the open hours:

- Balls — basketballs, volleyballs, tennis balls, soccer balls, shuttlecocks, squash balls, net balls

- Rackets — tennis, badminton, squash

- Frisbees

- Sleeping Bags — a limited number are available to check out for up to three days.

- Camping Tents for 2-3 people — a limited number are available to check out for up to three days.

- Camping Lanterns

- Bikes — all student bikes are checked out through the NYUAD Bike Share program . The Bike Share program is closed May- August. For more information, please contact: nyuad.bikeshare@nyu.edu

*All items are subject to availability.

Lost & Found
All lost and found items are held in the pool reception of the equipment room until the end of the day after being handed in. After this, all items will be sent to Public Safety in A4 building.

Lockers
Lockers are available for a semester at a time and are open to NYUAD Community at no charge and are available to book on a first come and first served bases. All lockers must be reserved using the Fitness and Athletics Booking System (FABS) .

Locker Borrowing Policy
View the Locker Borrowing Policy

Forgotten your access code? Visit the Athletics Equipment Issue Room, and a member of the on-duty staff will be able to assist you.

If you wish to change the location of a booked locker, you must log on to FABS and cancel your current locker by clicking the locker number, click the action button (upper right-hand corner), and cancel the reservation. Now you can book a new locker.

Lockers will be sanitized yearly from July 15-31. All lockers must be cleared out during this time. You will be able to select a new locker from August 1.

Please note, you will have activate your FABS membership first before you can book a locker.

sections.text:
Recreational equipment is available to the campus community while they use the athletic facilities. Campus community members who are using an athletic space can request equipment from the Equipment Issue Room by emailing nyuad.athletics.reception@nyu.edu before their session. All borrowed equipment must be returned at the end of the session.

A valid NYUAD ID Card is required to check out items. For more information, please contact nyuad.athletics.reception@nyu.edu .

sections.title: Opening Hours
sections.text:
Location: Campus Center (C2), first floor.
Regular Operating Hours: Monday to Friday 7am-10pm, Saturday to Sunday 8am-8pm

sections.title: Team Uniforms Issuing Policy
sections.text:
For students on University Sports Teams: Your coach will assign you your uniform number at the start of the semester. Uniforms are handed out in pairs (same size top and bottom), and uniforms cannot be traded. Uniforms must be picked up by 4pm on the day of competition . There will be no issuing of uniforms after 4pm, so please plan ahead. Friends and teammates cannot check out your uniform for you. All uniforms need to be returned to the Equipment Issue Room by 9 pm on the day following the game so they can be laundered and stored. Late return of uniforms will prevent an athlete from practicing until the uniform is returned.

Female Athletes

For female athletes requesting more coverage, the Equipment Room can provide the following black items for checkout:

- Long-sleeve shirts

- Tights or black joggers

- Hijabs

- Student athletes should not compete in their own attire. All uniforms for competitions should come from the Equipment Room.

sections.title: Equipment
sections.text:
Equipment Borrowing Policy
Recreational equipment

Recreational equipment (badminton, tennis, basketball, soccer equipment, etc.) can be collected at the Equipment Issue Room when checking in for a booked session (subject to availability). Equipment must be returned to the EIR at the end of the session. All equipment must be returned in good working order.

Failure to return equipment on time may result in the loss of future borrowing privileges.

Return of Borrowed Items

All items borrowed from the Department of Athletics must be returned during the Equipment Issue Room open hours . Items are not to be left unattended on the reception counter whilst the Equipment Issue Room is closed. Any items that go missing due to not following the return procedure will result in a replacement charge, payable by the last assignee for that item.

Guests

Guests may not sign out equipment. Items must be signed out by a sponsoring community member and must have paid for a guest pass and signed a waiver. See the Guest Policy for more information.

The following recreational items are available to be checked out from the Athletics Equipment Issue Room during the open hours:

- Balls — basketballs, volleyballs, tennis balls, soccer balls, shuttlecocks, squash balls, net balls

- Rackets — tennis, badminton, squash

- Frisbees

- Sleeping Bags — a limited number are available to check out for up to three days.

- Camping Tents for 2-3 people — a limited number are available to check out for up to three days.

- Camping Lanterns

- Bikes — all student bikes are checked out through the NYUAD Bike Share program . The Bike Share program is closed May- August. For more information, please contact: nyuad.bikeshare@nyu.edu

*All items are subject to availability.

Lost & Found
All lost and found items are held in the pool reception of the equipment room until the end of the day after being handed in. After this, all items will be sent to Public Safety in A4 building.

Lockers
Lockers are available for a semester at a time and are open to NYUAD Community at no charge and are available to book on a first come and first served bases. All lockers must be reserved using the Fitness and Athletics Booking System (FABS) .

Locker Borrowing Policy
View the Locker Borrowing Policy

Forgotten your access code? Visit the Athletics Equipment Issue Room, and a member of the on-duty staff will be able to assist you.

If you wish to change the location of a booked locker, you must log on to FABS and cancel your current locker by clicking the locker number, click the action button (upper right-hand corner), and cancel the reservation. Now you can book a new locker.

Lockers will be sanitized yearly from July 15-31. All lockers must be cleared out during this time. You will be able to select a new locker from August 1.

Please note, you will have activate your FABS membership first before you can book a locker.

title: Fitness and Athletics Booking System (FABS) · NYUAD Students
text:
Fitness and Athletics Booking System (FABS)

Fitness and Athletics Booking System (FABS) is a digital platform that eases the process of booking sports facilities, lockers and group fitness classes.

To use the system, you will need to create a membership account. Membership is free and valid from the date of joining and ends July 31 of every year. Membership can be renewed as of August 1 of every year.

- How to Activate your Membership

- Log on here

- First choose your ”Affiliation” and then “Sign up”. Please use your net ID email when registering.

- Log in with University SSO if you have an active NYUAD ID username and password, if not, click on local account and ‘create’ account. A confirmation email would be sent to your email address and then follow steps below. Fill out all required fields with your personal details. Please note that “Password” shouldn’t be less than 8 characters.

-
If you registered through “Local Account” a confirmation email will be sent to your email including the activation code.

-
After entering the code and clicking "activate” the next page will prompt users to "sign up" (if the system prompts you with “This plan requires a membership - please click the drop down menu next to your name on the upper right side of the page. Click my account and fill the required information) . Click on that to add their Emergency contact and then sign the waiver by ticking the box on the lower left hand and click next.

Please note: Local Accounts won’t be activated automatically.

To sign the waiver , tick the box, and click Save.

Upon successful registration, an email should be sent to your inbox.

- How to Register to use a Facility

1. Please go to the Facility Scheduling Module and log in to FABs using your Multi-Factor Authentication to use the following spaces:

- Performance Gym Courts (Badminton & Basketball)

- Blue Studio (Yoga & Dance)

- Squash Courts

- Tennis Courts

2. Click on the space and timeframe that you would like to book. You will be asked to confirm the booking.

3. Users will need to check in at the Athletics Reception Desk prior to using the booked space. Walk-ins will still be admitted if the space is available. Group bookings should be arranged through the Athletic Reception Desk.

Reservations are not needed in the following spaces. Check in is at the Athletic Reception Desk unless noted below:

- Fitness Center

- Women’s Fitness Center (check in at Women's Gym)

- 200 M Track

- 400 M Track

- Indoor Pool (check in at Pool Reception)

- Faculty Pool (check in at Pool Entrance)

- Locker Registration

How to Book a Locker

Locker registration for AY 23/34 will begin on August 1, 2023.

- Please go to the locker registration page .

- Click on Facilities and select “Lockers”.

- On the upper right of the page, click the drop down menu and choose your preferred locker location (according to your gender).

- Choose your preferred locker number (select from the unhighlighted ones). Top lockers are noted with a blue line.

- Click “Reserve”.

- You will be prompted to confirm your reservation. Click "Close"

- You will receive a email with directions on resetting your locker combination.

How to Cancel Your Locker

For assistance on canceling your locker, please reach out to nyuad.athletics.reception@nyu.edu, or visit them at the Equipment Room Desk C2/L1.

- Group Class Registration

How to Book a Group Fitness Class

- Log on to here using your Multi-Factor Authentication.

- Select your class from the Group Fitness Class Options. You will receive an email confirming your class registration

After you have registered for your class:

- Note down the date and time of the class on your own personal calendar.

- Please show up at least 10 minutes before the start of the class so the instructor can check you in before the class starts.

- To view all the classes you have registered for, select “My Classes” on the top left corner of the Class Registration Page

How to Un-Register for a Class

- Log on to https://nyuad.dserec.com/online/membership using your Multi-Factor Authentication.

- Select the class you would like to un-register for and select “Unregister” on the bottom right corner. You can also unregister for your class from the “My Classes” page by selecting “View”.

- An email notification will be sent to your inbox indicating you have successfully unregistered.

title: Fitness Center and Womens' Only Gym · NYUAD Students
text:
Facility Rules

Clothing and Footwear
Athletics wear including sneakers should be worn at all times. Clothing should appropriately cover the body including the midriff and should not have any profane language or logos. For practical, comfort and safety reasons no denim of any sort, dresses, skirts, dress shirts or trousers, sandals, boots or open shoes should be worn by anyone participating in any training.

Injury exceptions: For any requests for exceptions to the attire rules due to an injury these must be emailed to Athletics at nyuad.athletics.reception@nyu.edu . This request must include a doctors/specialists note detailing what exceptions are needed and the duration they will be required for.

Access and Entry
The Fitness Centers are accessible to all NYUAD Community Members age 16 and older. Users must have a valid NYUAD ID. Domestic staff and member's guests are not allowed to use the Fitness Centers. There will be no access without a proper ID. Please be prepared to produce your ID if asked by a member of our on-duty staff.

Equipment Use
Learn how to use and become familiar with equipment before use, asked a member of on-duty staff for assistance if needed.

Use the equipment as instructed and do not drop or bang the weights.

Athletic shoes must be worn when lifting machines, free weights and/or using cardio machines.

When lifting try to have a spotter.

For hygiene purposes please wipe the equipment after use.

All equipment must be returned to their stations, please keep the Fitness Center tidy.

Fitness Center and Women's Only Gym equipment is not available to lease.

No food or Beverage
No food or beverages should be consumed in the fitness center or studios. Only water or a sports drink in a spill proof plastic water bottle.

Accident Reporting
Report any accident or incident to the on-duty staff.

Equipment Use During Peak Hours
Please restrict use of cardiovascular machines to 30 minutes during peak hours.

Use of Mobile Device
Keep the use of mobile devices to a minimum.

Absolutely no photos or filming are allowed in the gym. Violators will be asked to leave the gym immediately.

Respectful Behavior
Please be courteous, considerate, and respectful to other community members working out.

Athletics staff aim to provide a nurturing and supportive environment for all our community. In return, we ask our community to comply with staff directives and Departmental rules and regulations. The Athletics staff will approach any individual who puts themselves or others at danger, or behaves inappropriately through words or actions and ask them to leave. Additionally, any violation of rules and regulations within the Fitness Center and Women's Only Gym, including verbal abuse of employees and or disorderly conduct will not be tolerated. The Athletics staff will use the following procedure to address a violation of Department's rules and regulations.

- The Athletics Department including its contracted staff from EFS has the right to enlist the assistance of Public Safety to remove individuals from the facility if the situation warrants assistance

- Workout privileges and usage of any Athletics services revoked for the remainder of the semester or till the situation is addressed and resolved.

- If individuals committing the offense wish to resolve and continue using our services, they need to meet with the Director of Athletics.

Access for Minors
Only children 16 and older are permitted in the Fitness Center and Women's Only Gym. No exceptions.

No Private Instruction
No unauthorized private instruction of any kind by non-NYUAD staff is permitted in the facilities.

Athletics management reserves the right to change the policies and guidelines as deemed necessary, for the safe and functional operation of the facilities.

Failure to adhere to the above Rules and Regulations will result in your FABS membership being suspended.

text:
Regular Operating Hours

Equipment Issue Desk

Performance Gym and Indoor Track

- Weekdays 6am- 10pm

Fitness Center

Indoor Competition Pool

- Monday-Thursday: 6am- 2pm / 3pm- 10pm

- Fridays: 6am- 10pm

- Weekends 8am- 8pm

Please check for women's only hours and PHE hours on the Competition Pool page

Women's Only Gym

- Weekdays 6am- 10pm

- Weekends 8am- 8pm

The Performance Gym (3 multi-purpose courts and 200 Meter indoor track)

- Weekdays 6am- 10pm

- Weekends 8am- 8pm

Climbing Wall (located in the Performance Gym)

Please check FABS for available climbing hours.

Squash Courts (3 available)

- Weekdays 6am- 10pm

- Weekends 8am- 8pm

Location

The Performance Gym, (Courts, Climbing Wall, and Indoor Track), are located on Level 1 of the Campus Center (C2) building.

The Women's Only Gym is located on Level 1, C2 on the West side of the building (next to the Convenience Store).

Squash Courts are on the East side of Level 1, C2 next to the Athletics Office.

The Indoor Pool is located on level B1 of the Campus Center building (C2).

Facility Rules of Use

Please ensure that all rules and regulations are followed.

- Indoor facilities are open to all NYU Abu Dhabi students, staff, and faculty members. Users must have a valid NYU Abu Dhabi ID and must be registered on FABS. There will be no access without the proper registration mentioned above.

- Any abusive or profane language will result in immediate dismissal. Please treat staff members with respect.

- No food or drink (with the exception of water in a non-breakable container) is allowed in the indoor athletic spaces

- Roller blades, skateboards, bicycles, tricycles, and scooters are not allowed.

- Appropriate sportswear required. Shirts covering the midriff must be worn at all times.

- Only non-marking athletic shoes allowed on the courts and indoor track. No street shoes, track spikes or bare feet allowed.

- Unauthorized private lessons are prohibited in any indoor or outdoor athletic space.

- All scheduled practices, PE classes, and NYUAD programming takes precedence over other use.

- Equipment is available to borrow through the Equipment Room for your registered session by emailing nyuad.athletics.reception@nyu.edu .

- Access for minors: Resident children aged 13 and under can access the performance gym, pool, squash courts, tennis courts and 400m track when accompanied by an Adult (18+)

- Resident children 14 and over can access the performance gym, pool, squash courts, tennis courts, and 400m track unaccompanied

- The Fitness Center and Women’s Only Gym can be used from age 16. No exceptions.

To access the Outdoor Facilities, exit the external doors near the entrance to the Fitness Center on Level 1 (East Side), down the steps, and take the path towards the outdoor track.

Track is to be used for running and walking only.

All users should run or walk counterclockwise (keep the grass on your left).

Be considerate to other track users.

Users must have a valid NYU Abu Dhabi ID and FABS account to use the Outdoor Track.

Pets are prohibited.

Smoking is prohibited.

Any abusive or profane language will result in immediate dismissal. Please treat staff members with respect.

Glassware/glass containers are prohibited.

Strollers, roller blades, skateboards, bicycles, tricycles, and scooters are not allowed.

Appropriate sportswear required. Shirts covering the midriff must be worn at all times.

Athletic shoes must be worn at all times on the outdoor track & fields. Track spikes are allowed.

Slower runners and walkers use the outside three lanes of the track.

Unauthorized private lessons are prohibited in any indoor or outdoor athletic space.

All scheduled practices, PE classes, and NYUAD programming takes precedence over other use.

Tennis Courts

- Location

To access the Tennis Courts, exit the external doors near the entrance to the Fitness Center on Level 1 (East Side), down the steps, and take the path towards the outdoor track. Courts are to the right.

- Tennis Court Rules of Use

General Tennis Court Rules

Doubles play is allowed

Equipment can be borrowed from the Equipment Issue Room for your session.

Users must have a valid NYU Abu Dhabi ID and FABS account to use the Tennis Courts. All users should check in at the Athletics Reception Desk.

Players are expected to observe rules of tennis courtesy as well as rules of good conduct at all times in and around the Tennis Courts.

Entry onto the Courts should be made with due consideration to the current match taking place. Do not enter whilst the ball is still in play.

Players must enter through the center gate and then move to the appropriate court to avoid hindering play.

Only tennis equipment and balls may be used on the courts.

Players must wear appropriate tennis attire and non-marking court shoes. A shirt covering your midriff must be worn at all times.

The tennis courts are designated for tennis only; no other activities are allowed on the courts (unless authorized by Department of Athletics).

Glassware or glass containers may not be brought in to the court areas at any time.

No food or chewing gum shall be consumed on the courts at any time.

Players are responsible for removing all trash (including empty water bottles and empty ball containers) from their court area before they leave.

No roller blades, skateboards, bicycles, tricycles, ribsticks, and/or children’s buggies are permitted on the courts at any time.

Equipment may not be moved, altered, or removed without authorization from Department of Athletics.

-

- No unauthorized private tennis lessons of any kind are permitted on the courts.

title: Sports Performance Center · NYUAD Students
text:
Prepare with Purpose. Return with Power.

The Sports Performance Centre is the driving force behind every University Sports Team athlete.

It provides the world-class Strength & Conditioning (S&C) infrastructure necessary to maintain your competitive edge, maximize physical capabilities, and fast-track your return to play.

How We Build Elite Athletes

No guesswork. Evidence-led. We track your performance throughout the academic year to identify your critical work-ons. By matching your individual data with the specific demands of your sport, we build a program tailored exactly to what you need to succeed.

Whether you are fully fit or working your way back from an injury, our program delivers three core pillars:

-
Testing & Data-Driven S&C: We use regular testing data to establish individual baselines. This objective data allows us to provide personalized strength & conditioning programs built specifically for the demands of your sport.

-
Active Return-to-Play Rehab: If you are injured, we act as the bridge between your medical clearance and the competitive field.

-
Performance Habits & Recovery: We teach you the daily routines and habits required to perform at your best. You will also have direct access to our contrast bathing pools to speed up muscle recovery between games.

Please Note: We work in collaboration with the Health Centre for injury assessment and clinical diagnosis, allowing us to seamlessly assist in your post-injury Return-to-Play (RTP) pathway. The Sports Performance Centre focuses strictly on performance S&C and active rehabilitation under medical advice.

————————————————————————————————————————

Sports Physicals

Medical clearance is mandatory to compete. Testing takes place at the start of every academic year.

-
New Athletes: First-time physicals are prioritized to ensure immediate clearance.

-
Returning Athletes: If you have previously completed your medical, you must notify your coaches immediately of any health changes.

————————————————————————————————————————

Hours & Access

The Sports Performance Centre operates throughout the Fall and Spring terms.

-
Primary Access: Open to all University Sports Team (UST) athletes.

-
Advance Registration: To secure your space, book in advance here.

-

Questions? Contact Coach Joe: js16432 @nyu.edu

title: Traditions · NYUAD Students
text:
NYUAD Athletics seeks to cultivate belonging, catalyze development, and foster engagement by promoting a supportive and inclusive community across campus and the UAE. Our traditions have played an essential role in community building with three hallmark traditions; the Falcon feast, Defend the Nest and The Interclassico.

Defend the Nest

Each November, the NYUAD Basketball Teams take center court in an evening of rivalry matches. The Men and Women’s Basketball Teams play back to back games in front of packed stands supported by the NYUAD and greater Abu Dhabi communities. The evening highlights our sense of belonging with festivities, performances, fun competitions, and the birthday of Faiza the Falcon.

Interclassico

The Interclassico is a long-held tradition at NYU Abu Dhabi that on the outside, appears to be a football match held in April; but in reality, it is much deeper than that. The event brings together the Underclass (First-years, Sophomores, and Juniors) against the Seniors and Alumni of previous years for a game of co-ed soccer, with each side hoping to claim the victory. By the end, however, it’s less about the score, but about the relationships that have been formed over the years. It’s a way to say goodbye to the beloved Seniors — but not forever — as the bonds will continue long past graduation day.

The Falcon Feast

The intercollegiate sports year ends with the annual Falcon Feast. Student-athletes, the coaching staff, and NYUAD leadership gather to recognize and acknowledge the best of the best from our student athletes and share a meal to celebrate the year in sports.
