title: Professional Health Programs · NYUAD Students
text:
Overview

Start off your journey to Schools of the Health Professions here. Explore the valuable information provided on this page and its tabs, and join the NYUAD Health and Medicine Career Community on Handshake to receive other relevant updates and programming invitations.

Who?

Pre-health students are those who seek admission to health related professional school after completion of their degree. NYUAD does not have an official pre-health track or major, however, some specific requirements need to be fulfilled for certain graduate and professional programs.

What?

The health professions provide a wide range of career opportunities that involve keeping populations in good health. These include clinical careers in medicine, dentistry, nursing, physical therapy amongst others, as well as non-clinical careers such as health education and research. Explore a wide range of degree types on The Professions page and learn more about career prospects on O*NET .

Where?

The health professions are practiced throughout the world. To that end, health professional schools are also available throughout the world. Students are highly encouraged to utilize the Association of American Medical College (AAMC ), World Directory of Medical Schools , and NYUAD Graduate School Map for exploring and considering schools they may not have thought of before.

When?

In most countries, health professionals almost always require a specialized degree and a license to practice or conduct research. Some students enroll directly in a health professional program after completing their bachelor’s degree while others prefer to gain professional experience, do volunteer work or travel before committing to their studies.

Why?

The health professions can be extremely satisfying, sometimes lucrative, but the most successful practitioners are unequivocally driven, passionate and compassionate. Without this dedication, it is hard to put in the long hard hours, both in education and in practice.

How?

Explore the valuable information provided on this page and its tabs, schedule a Handshake appointment with your Pre-health Advisor , and join the NYUAD Health and Medicine Career Community on Handshake to make first your steps towards becoming a health professionals.

https://students.nyuad.nyu.edu/student-affairs/career-development/graduate-study/professional-health-programs/the-professions/

sections.text: The health professions provide a wide range of career opportunities that involve keeping populations in good health. These include clinical careers in medicine, dentistry, nursing, physical therapy amongst others, as well as non-clinical careers such as health education and research. Explore a wide range of degree types on The Professions page and learn more about career prospects on O*NET .

sections.title: Overview · Where?
sections.text: The health professions are practiced throughout the world. To that end, health professional schools are also available throughout the world. Students are highly encouraged to utilize the Association of American Medical College (AAMC ), World Directory of Medical Schools , and NYUAD Graduate School Map for exploring and considering schools they may not have thought of before.

sections.title: Overview · When?
sections.text: In most countries, health professionals almost always require a specialized degree and a license to practice or conduct research. Some students enroll directly in a health professional program after completing their bachelor’s degree while others prefer to gain professional experience, do volunteer work or travel before committing to their studies.

sections.title: Overview · Why?
sections.text: The health professions can be extremely satisfying, sometimes lucrative, but the most successful practitioners are unequivocally driven, passionate and compassionate. Without this dedication, it is hard to put in the long hard hours, both in education and in practice.

sections.title: Overview · How?
sections.text: Explore the valuable information provided on this page and its tabs, schedule a Handshake appointment with your Pre-health Advisor , and join the NYUAD Health and Medicine Career Community on Handshake to make first your steps towards becoming a health professionals.

title: The Process · NYUAD Students
text:
Preparing and Applying for the Schools of the Health Professions

The decision to go to health professional school is not made overnight. If you are considering a career in the health professions, you should start your planning from your first year of study at NYUAD. Below is a sample four-year plan for a student considering going straight into health-professional school after graduating from NYUAD. You should meet with a pre-health advisor to help develop your own, personalized 4-year plan.

The decision to go to Schools of the Health Professions is not made overnight. To gain a comprehensive understanding of the preparation and application process, students are encouraged to watch the video provided below. The video also outlines a well-structured timeline for applications to the US Schools of the Health Professions.

Requirements for Admissions

It is important to excel academically if interested in health professional school. However, it is also important to be involved in activities outside of the required classes. Dedication, leadership, and advancement are key traits that many health professional schools look for in a candidate. Padding resumes with as many opportunities as possible is not advised, as health professional schools want students to show maturity, reliability, passion, and commitment to a few activities rather than limited engagement with many activities: think quality over quantity. The specific prerequisites vary from school to school.

- Academics

Academics play an important role in applying to health professional school. A science major is not required as long as you fulfill the academic requirements of school(s) to which you will apply for. Additionally, most health professional schools like to see a balance between the sciences and the humanities.

There is usually no minimum GPA for US health professional schools. To help determine your competitiveness for US medical schools, the Association of American Medical Colleges provides up to date statistics on medical school applicants, enrollments, matriculants, international student admissions, etc. on a yearly basis.

It is best to check with programs directly for academic requirements via their website. If you are applying to the US Schools of the Health Professions, please review the list of links to direct program information , which was carefully assembled by the Association of American Medical Colleges application system, AMCAS . Additionally, please review the Medical School Admissions Requirements, MSAR, database for more information about academic requirements at the US Schools of the Health Professions.

- Clinical

In order to have a full understanding of the profession you seek to enter, clinical experience is key. This also helps convince admissions committees that you know, understand, and are excited by a career in healthcare. Clinical experience should start early in your undergraduate career, with your time-commitment and responsibilities increasing as you get closer to application.

These experiences can be secured independently or through the CDC’s employer network.

We encourage you to reflect on the following as you assess your involvement in clinical arenas:

- Have you had more than one sustained experience volunteering in hospitals, clinics, or private offices?

- Did you interact with patients?

- Have you shadowed, or observed, healthcare professionals?

- What did you learn about health care and the profession through this experience?

- Research

Conducting research as an undergraduate can aid your application to health professional schools. This experience demonstrates your intellectual curiosity and scholarly development. It does not matter what form this research takes (bench, clinical, field), as long as you demonstrate your commitment to furthering the body of shared knowledge. We encourage you to consider the following as you assess your involvement in research:

- What have you accomplished and learned through your research experience?

- Why are you conducting research? What drives your passion in research?

- How do the skills you have gained through research apply to your career aspirations?

- Community Service

A career in the health professions is a dedication to help others. Civic engagement builds cultural awareness, caring and demonstrates your commitment to others. Your community service does not have to be in healthcare. You can work in after-school programs, take on environmental initiatives or help communities in any way you find beneficial, whether it is your local community or one further away from home.

- Have you worked extensively and over a sustained period of time with a single organization or for a particular cause?

- How has this work influenced your awareness and understanding of the world?

- Are you committed to a particular organization or cause? Why?

- Leadership Experience

Engaging in both on-campus and off-campus activities allows you to cultivate your leadership capabilities and demonstrate your proactive approach. Leverage the diverse array of SIGs, Student Government, and other on-campus and off-campus opportunities to immerse yourself in experiences that align with your passions and aspirations.

- What have you learned about yourself or others through participation in university groups?

- How has this experience been beneficial to you?

- If you change your involvement with university groups, what would it be and why?

Standardized Tests

Almost every professional school requires some sort of standardized test. These tests are used to gauge the applicant's aptitude in various subject areas and likelihood of succeeding in health professional school. The Career Development Center offers books and competitive awards to help students prepare for standardized tests, such as MCAT, DAT, OAT, and GRE, required by their respective graduate program. Visit the Grants page to learn more about these resources.

- MCAT

All applicants to US medical schools must complete the Medical College Admission Test . It is also required for many medical schools throughout the world. It is designed to be difficult and test a broad range of knowledge.

Importantly, the MCAT is not offered in the UAE. More information regarding test registration, dates and locations can be found on the AMCAS website .

- DAT

The required standardized test for acceptance into American dental school is the Dental Admissions Test (DAT) . It is a computerized multiple choice test that can be taken at almost any point in the year.

Schools generally do not have a minimum requirement for the DAT, but the higher DAT score, the more competitive a candidate you are.

- OAT

The Optometry Admission Test (OAT) is the required standardized test to be accepted into US optometry schools.

There is no minimum OAT score requirement to be accepted into optometry school.

- GRE

GRE : The Graduate Record Exams (GRE) is the most universally recognized standardized test for nursing, public health and veterinary schools.

The GRE can be taken in almost any country, including in the UAE. Testing is offered in various locations throughout Abu Dhabi almost every weekday. Please see the ETS website for registration and other details about the GRE.

NYUAD Committee Package

The Prehealth Committee Package is an internal application that is prepared by the Committee on Recommendations to Schools of the Health Professions and sent to the Association of American Medical Colleges application system, AMCAS , the centralized application system for the majority of US medical schools.

The Committee Package consists of:

- Cover Letter: describes the programs at NYUAD providing detailed information about our curriculum and programs to help admissions committees understand the strength of our institution and our applicants to Schools of the Health Profession.

- Committee Letter: an in-depth explanation of the applicant's personal, academic and professional history. This individual letter is based on the information provided by students in the Committee Package Application, Committee Package Interviews and the applicant’s recommendation letters.

- Recommendation Letters: an evaluation of academic and professional qualifications, skills, achievements, interests or character. For more insights on who to select for recommendation letter writers and how to obtain the letters, please visit the Essential Information page .

The Committee Package application opens in December each year and must be submitted by February. Monitor the NYUAD Health and Medicine Career Community Newsletter, Student Portal Announcements, pre-HAB and neSMAH SIGs for the exact opening and closing dates.

All students and graduates who plan on applying to the School of the Health Profession must meet all Committee Package deadlines and fulfill all admission requirements, in order for the CDC to produce and submit the Committee Package on their behalf

Application Process

The application for health professional schools is generally completed over the summer between junior and senior year. Some students decide to take a gap year or two before applying. If you wish to do that, make sure you discuss it with your pre-health advisor.

- Centralized Application Services/Primary Application

Many schools participate in a centralized application service which allows you to fill out one application for multiple schools. However, not all schools do this, so be sure you know the application procedure for each school to which you apply.

AMCAS : The American Medical College Application Service is for medical schools in the United States. The AMCAS is a very detailed application process that asks for a significant amount of information.

ADEA AADSAS : American Dental Education Association, Associated American Dental Schools Application Service is for dental schools in the United States. It is a very detailed application process that asks for a significant amount of information. Reach out to us at nyuad.preprof@nyu.edu if you have any specific questions.

Nursing CAS: The common application system for nursing school in the US.

VCAS : The Veterinary Common Application System, a centralized application system for veterinary school in the US.

OptomCAS : The centralized application service for optometry schools in the US.

SOPHAS : The centralized application service for public health schools in the US.

- Secondary Application

Many schools have a secondary application that you must complete after submitting your primary or centralized application. You will receive the secondary application only if your primary or centralized application is strong and the school thinks you are a potential good candidate for their program. Check each school to which you apply for information on their secondary application, if any. It is recommended that the turnaround time for secondary applications be 10-14 days upon receipt of the application.

Interview

Interviews are required for admission to most health professional schools. For US medical schools, the interview is always on campus. It is the applicant’s responsibility to make it to the interviews. Some schools will not require interviews or will provide the option to complete them via Skype. The following are the types of interviews that students applying to medical school should be aware of:

- Informed Interview

The informed interview is when the interviewer has read an interviewees file and asked questions based on the file. Harvard Medical School conducts these types of interviews.

- Informal Interview

The person interviewing you will make you feel relaxed. This type of interview is a more of casual conversation with the interviewer wanting to learn about the student.

- Pressure Interview

This type of interview is designed to see how the candidate acts under pressure. The interviewer typically asks difficult questions, which one is expected to answer quickly.

- Group Interview

In a group interview, the candidate is interviewed with other candidates sometimes having to discuss an issue or article revolving around the medical field.

- Blind Interview

The interviewer does not know anything about the candidate and tries to obtain an objective opinion of him/her. Some medical schools have both a blind and informed interview

- Multiple Mini Interviews (MMI)

In an MMI, students are interviewed for 5-10 minutes by several different people. The interviewee is often presented with a situation outside of each interviewing room, given a few minutes to consider the situation, then must go in and present their ideas to the interviewer.

- Skype Interview

These interviews take place virtually via Skype or other video call. They can be challenging as body language can be hard to read and connection is not always smooth. Many back-up plans are needed to ensure a good connection and uninterrupted interview.

- Phone Interview

Phone interviews force you to rely on clear and articulated speech. Because there is no way to read the interviewer's body language, you must always remain on point and professional.

Re-Applicants

The NYUAD Pre-Professional Advising Office will support NYUAD students and graduates who wish to re-apply to health professional schools. We strongly recommend that you meet with a Pre-Health advisor to discuss ways to strengthen your application.

Re-applicants who have already interviewed with our office in the past do not need to have a second committee interview or fill out a new Pre-Health Committee application.

Re-applicants who would like an updated Committee Letter must get in contact with the Pre-Health advisor to determine next steps.

Related official links:
https://students.nyuad.nyu.edu/student-affairs/career-development/grants/
https://students.nyuad.nyu.edu/student-affairs/career-development/graduate-study/grad-school-essential-information/

title: The Professions · NYUAD Students
text:
Explore a wide range of degree types through this drop-down list, and visit O*NET to learn more about career prospects.

- Medicine

For those passionate about helping others, medicine is a critically important and a highly respected profession. While a medical degree is primarily to prepare practicing doctors, medical degrees are also useful in other areas of the healthcare industry such as health management and maintenance organizations, pharmaceuticals, medical equipment manufacturing, health insurance companies, and other institutions.

There are a wide range of specialties within the medical profession including family and internal medicine, general surgery, emergency medicine, oncology, anesthesiology, dermatology, pediatrics, plastic surgery, obstetrics and gynecology, and allergy and immunology medicine amongst others.

Students should be prepared for a long, intensive, and expensive educational commitment beyond the undergraduate level. Most medical school programs are four years — often consisting of two years of basic sciences curriculum followed by two years of clinical rotations — in addition, three to eight years of internship and residency depending upon specialization. These years of internship, residency and fellowship require many hours of work per week (upwards of 80+ hours), and long shifts. These years are not glamorous and often very grueling, but very rewarding if you are passionate about medicine. It is difficult to complete a medical degree and residency without true passion for practicing medicine.

Types of Degrees:

The Doctor of Medicine (MD), Bachelor of Medicine, Bachelor of Surgery (MBBS), and Doctor of Osteopathic Medicine (DO) are common medical degrees offered worldwide. These degrees are virtually identical and all prepare graduates to practice medicine as physicians anywhere in the world. The MD and DO are the most prevalent in the United States while the MBBS is more commonly found in the rest of the world.

- The Doctor of Medicine (MD) is the universal degree awarded to students who successfully complete medical school in the US and Canada. It is also offered at some schools throughout the rest of the world. This is a four-year program where the first two years involve intense science courses followed by two years of clinical rotations in hospitals.

- The Doctor of Osteopathic Medicine (DO) is also a US-based degree. Osteopathic medicine has historically a greater emphasis on primary care and holistic health. Those holding a DO have all the same rights, privileges and responsibilities as those with an MD The curriculum is also four years, with a similar structure as an MD. The main difference is about 400 hours of clinical work with hands-on manual medicine and the body's musculoskeletal system, called osteopathic manipulative medicine.

- The Bachelor's of Medicine, Bachelor's of Surgery (MBBS) is the most common degree required for practicing medicine outside of the US. The degree is often six years in length and it allows students to start medical school directly after secondary school. Nevertheless, many of these programs have a graduate entry program that is only four years long, allowing those who hold a bachelor's degree to join their medical program without repeating many of the science courses they have already taken.

- Dentistry

Dentistry is the practice of oral health care. This includes specific treatments such as restorative care, orthodontics, prosthetics, endodontic therapy, general examinations, x-rays and cleanings. Generally, three or more years of undergraduate education plus four years of dental school is required to graduate and become a general dentist. Additional post-graduate training is required to become a dental specialist, such as an orthodontist, periodontist or oral and maxillofacial surgeon.

Types of Degrees The Doctor of Dental Surgery (DDS) and the Doctor of Dental Medicine (DMD) are the two main degrees offered in the US for those wishing to become practicing dentists. The two degrees are completely equivalent according to the American Dental Association Commission on Dental Accreditation. State licensing boards accept either degree as equivalent, and both degrees allow licensed individuals to practice the same scope of general dentistry. Other dental degrees offered throughout the world that can lead to practical applications include the Bachelor of Dentistry (BDent) or the Bachelor of Dental Surgery (BDS).

- Veterinary

Veterinary medicine is the branch of medicine that deals with the prevention, diagnosis and treatment of disease, disorder, and injury in animals — domesticated and wild. The scope of veterinary medicine is wide, covering all animal species with a wide range of conditions.

Types of Degrees: In North America, veterinary school graduates receive the Doctorate of Veterinary Medicine (DVM) while in the UK and elsewhere the Bachelor of Veterinary Surgery (BVS) is more common. Becoming a practicing veterinarian requires achieving the relevant degree and passing the licensing exam for the desired location of practice.

- Physical Therapy

Physical therapists (PTs) are healthcare professionals who diagnose and treat individuals of all ages who have medical problems or other health-related conditions that limit their abilities to move and perform functional activities in their daily lives. They help these individuals with plans to promote motility and restoration of their normal functions. Physical therapists work in a variety of settings from private practices, hospitals, sports and fitness facilities, work settings, nursing homes, schools, and home health agencies. Worldwide, physical therapy training ranges from basic worksite education in hospitals and outpatient clinics to professional doctoral degree programs.

Types of Degrees :

- The Master of Physical Therapy (MPT) is a direct entry to a two-year program where the first year is focused on teaching important concepts in physical therapy and the second year consists of field work with students practicing physical therapy in a clinical setting. There is a transitional MPT degree which is conferred only to students who have already completed a physical therapy education bachelor and who wish to advance their career further.

- The Doctor of Physical Therapy (DPT) is a professional three-year degree that requires clinical rotations during the summers. After graduating from an accredited program and becoming licensed, a Doctor of Physical Therapy (DPT) may continue his or her education by entering a residency and then fellowship program. Residencies and fellowships are not required but are becoming more common in physical therapy education.

- A PhD in Physical Therapy is usually open to licensed physical therapists holding a master's degree in physical therapy. This is a research-based degree which aims at preparing critical thinkers and independent researchers to further expand the knowledge base of the physical therapy profession.

- Nursing

A nurse is a healthcare professional who is focused on caring for individuals, families, and communities. They are a crucial part of the health care team. Nurses are capable of assessing, planning, implementing, and evaluating care independently of physicians, and they provide support from basic triage to emergency surgery. They deal with the majority of personal interaction within medical practice. Wherever you find doctors, you will find nurses as well.

Types of Degrees : Nursing has many levels of practice from associate degrees (two-year programs) to doctorate-level education. Depending on the field of nursing and degree of education and specificity of practice, nurses can take on a variety of roles. To become a nurse requires admittance to specific nursing programs. To become a registered nurse (RN) requires completing either an associate's or bachelor's degree in nursing. A nurse practitioner (NP) has a master's degree or higher. Below are the most common professional degrees in nursing.

- The Bachelor’s of Science in Nursing (BSN) can be obtained through an accelerated program in 12-15 months but can also take up to 24 months. The curriculum generally is setup to study one field within nursing while doing clinical rotations in that area.

- A Master's of Nursing (MSN) can be obtained either simultaneously with the BSN, or as a separate degree program. It takes about four years to complete a BSN/MSN dual degree program, and students become Nurse Practitioners (NPs) upon completion. This degree is also considered an entry-level degree for nurse educators as well as managers. Additionally, it prepares a nurse to pursue a career as a health policy expert, a nurse administrator, or a clinical nurse leader. Finally, it can help as a requirement for applying to a doctorate of nursing.

- A Doctor of Nursing Practice (DNP) is a more research-based degree that nurses are obtaining more often now after a few years of work as a NP. The degree focuses more on the clinical aspects of a disease process such as advanced practice, diagnoses, and treatment of diseases. It prepares the nurse to act as a primary care provider. Some programs offer a MSN/DNP dual degree.

- Optometry

Optometry is the health care profession that deals specifically with the health of eyes, visual pathways, and visual perception in humans. Optometrists examine, diagnose, treat, and manage diseases, injuries, and disorders of the visual system, the eye, and associated structures, as well as identify related systemic conditions affecting the eye.

Types of Degrees : An optometrist has completed pre-professional undergraduate education in a college or university and four years of professional education at a college of optometry, leading to the doctor of optometry (OD) degree, the main degree for practicing optometrists. Some optometrists complete an optional residency in a specific area of practice.

- Public Health

The field of public health aims at protecting, promoting, and improving the health and well-being of populations. Public health focuses on the prevention of disease throughout the world — from small rural towns to large cities, and across countries — with a strong focus on the most vulnerable societies. The field can be practiced in private companies, medical centers, or governmental health departments. The five core areas that degrees in public health expose students to are:

- Biostatistics

- Epidemiology

- Environmental Health

- Health Policy/Administration

- Social and Behavioral Sciences

Types of Degrees : There are various postgraduate degrees within the realm of public health including: Master of Public Health (MPH), Master of Science in Public Health (MSPH), Doctor of Public Health (DrPH) and Doctor of Philosophy (PhD). The MSPH and PhD are considered academic degrees geared for theoretical thinking within the field of public health, while the MPH and DrPH are more professional degrees for the practice of public health. Many people who work in this field also hold an MD.

The Advancement Opportunity Grant (AOG) has started accepting applications from the first day of classes. If you are unsure about the opportunity you are applying to, please email nyuad.cdcgrants@nyu.edu to schedule an appointment.

Applications Open
August 31 - December 4, 2026
January 4 - May 3, 2027, 3pm GST
Any application submitted after the deadline will not be reviewed.

Please note that you must remain in the country until your visa and health card have been issued.

Important Note

- To be considered for funding, you will have to apply for an AO grant 21 business days before the event.

- The AO Committee has 15 business days from the date the application is submitted to respond (excluding weekends) with a funding decision. Applications will not be reviewed during university or public holidays.

Pursue Your Dream

AOG provides opportunities for you to participate in competitions, conferences, workshops, activities, and events that will benefit your academic, professional, and personal goals.

Apply for Advancement Opportunity Grant

Read through the grants guidelines before you begin filling out the application form.

Other Funding Opportunities at NYUAD

There are several sources of funding for students at NYUAD. Before you complete an application, please ensure that you are completing the appropriate application. If you are not sure who best to send your application to, please review the contact information on Career Development's Funding page.

Testimonials from Students

MENA Climate Week, Abu Dhabi, UAE

My overall experience at MENA Climate Week was incredibly enriching and inspiring. The event brought together a diverse group of experts, policymakers, and activists, allowing for a vibrant exchange of ideas and best practices. I had the opportunity to attend a variety of sessions covering topics from renewable energy innovations to climate adaptation strategies specific to the MENA region. Engaging in these discussions not only deepened my understanding of the complex climate challenges we face but also highlighted the importance of regional collaboration and innovative thinking in driving sustainable solutions. Additionally, networking with like-minded individuals and organizations provided valuable insights and potential partnerships for future projects. Overall, MENA Climate Week was a pivotal experience that reinforced my commitment to addressing climate change and equipped me with new tools and perspectives to bring back to the NYUAD community.
-- Hoor Ali, Class of 2026

Reclaiming The Narrative, An Arts, Culture and Ideas Symposium (NYU Accra), Accra, Ghana

The symposium was filled with lively panel discussions, inspiring keynote speeches, and beautiful art exhibitions. Presenting my novel "Don't You Forget" allowed me to connect with other writers and readers, leading to meaningful conversations about the power of storytelling. Listening to literary greats like Wole Soyinka, Aminatta Forna, Jennifer Makumbi, and Chris Abani was especially inspiring, which reminded me of the deep impact that words can have. The creative and intellectual energy of the symposium was invigorating and it renewed my passion for literature and deepening my understanding of its importance in society. Overall, the symposium was not just a chance to share my work, but also an opportunity to learn, grow, and be inspired by a community of people who are passionate about the arts and culture.
-- Confidence Ezemba, Class of 2025

title: FAQs · NYUAD Students
text:
FAQs for Students Applying for Advancement Opportunities (AO)

- Can first year students apply for AO funding?

First Year students will NOT be considered for AO funding in the fall. First year students may only apply for AO funding spring semester.

- Can a senior apply for AO funding?

Yes, there will be a limited budget for seniors and offered on a first come, first serve basis in the fall semester only. The opportunity must be completed by January 31 of the following year. There will be no exceptions to this offering. Once the funding has been fully utilized, an announcement will be made on the student portal.

- When should I apply for AO funding?

You may submit your AO application for funding starting from the first day of classes until one week before the end of the semester. The AO Committee has 15 business days to reply with a decision on your application from the date of submission.

- Does AO funding assist students with the visa process?

No, visas are the full administrative and financial responsibility of the student. You must liaise with Global Education for guidance and research the visa requirements of the country in which you tend to visit.

- Am I provided a Support Letter which verifies I am a full-time student at NYUAD to assist with my request for a visa?

Yes, the Career Development Center provides a Support Letter upon request from the student to be presented to the embassy of the country traveling to for a visa. It is also called a no-contest certificate, as this letter is issued by the University confirming you are a full time student, the name of the AO, and clarifies we support your visa request and we state the amount of the award.

- If I am not granted a visa, what do I do with the AO award?

As per the AO Guidelines, you will return the funds to the Career Development Center within one week of being denied a visa.

- Do AO fund opportunities cover the summer?

Yes, providing the application has been reviewed, approved before the application end date in the spring semester and depending upon whether funds are still available.

- If a group of eight students wanted to compete in a competition, how many students can be funded for the same opportunity?

If you are in a competition, AO funding would fund one team (maximum of two students) if the students meet the AO funding guidelines. This will allow AO funds to stretch and give other students a chance of securing funding for their opportunity.

- If a group of four students wanted to attend the same conference, how many students would possibly be granted funding?

It is strongly encouraged if a number of students wish to attend the same conference, AO funding would like to see students present at the conference. The maximum number of students who would be considered for the same conference is two. This will allow AO funds to stretch and give other students a chance of securing funding for their opportunity.

- If I have questions about AO funding, who should I reach out to?

You may email the AO Committee: nyuad.cdcgrants@nyu.edu with your questions. Someone from the AO Committee will respond to you within 2-business days.

- Does AO funding fund non-credit bearing courses or certifications online or in-person?

No, AO funding does not support funding non-credit bearing courses and/or certifications online or in-person .

- Can I use AO awarded funds towards a different opportunity?

No. AO awarded funds are allowed to be used only for the opportunity applied to. If you are no longer participating in the opportunity you were awarded for, you will be required to return the funds.

title: Funding Guidelines · NYUAD Students
text:
Guidelines for Students Applying for Advancement Opportunities (AO)

This fall, Advancement Opportunity (AO) funding is available to eligible NYUAD students through a competitive application process. AO funding can provide partial or full funding to help students to cover the cost of attending a competition, conference, webinars, or workshop that provides high-level, quality leadership development and that shows a clear connection to the student’s major or career.

AO funding is limited, competitive, and only students meeting the qualification requirements will be considered. Not everyone who applies will receive funding.

Every AO should demonstrate the high-value advancement and development benefits of participation for the student and should be aligned with the students’ academic, extracurricular and professional goals as well as the mission of NYUAD. Simply attending a conference is not considered an AO. Students must prove they will be active participants — for example, as a speaker, presenter, or facilitator. The AO offers a dynamic, meaningful experience that aims to enrich a student’s leadership capabilities and academic development, as well as give students a chance to represent NYUAD on a national or global level.

The AO Committee consists of stakeholders across campus, including a student, staff, and faculty. The role of the student will be of a ‘Student Reviewer’ on the Committee, the student will explicitly research the opportunity proposed by the applicant and act purely as an adviser to the Committee. The Student Reviewer is not a decision-maker role on the Committee. The approval request of an AO funding application falls solely upon the AO Committee.

- Eligibility Requirements

To be eligible for AO funding, the student must satisfy the following criteria.

- The student must be a full-time matriculated student at NYUAD.

- Study Away Restriction: Students on a Study Away semester are ineligible to apply.

- At the time of the opportunity. the student must be actively residing at the Abu Dhabi campus and be enrolled full-time.

- The student must be in good academic standing with a minimum cumulative GPA of 3.0 (including first year grades).

- The student must not have already received AO funding more than two times during their enrollment at NYUAD.

- The student must be in good disciplinary standing * (to be verified by the judicial officer).

- The student must have completed all requirements (survey, testimonial) for any previously awarded AO funding.

- The student must apply for an AO grant 21 business days before the event.

* Good disciplinary standing indicates that a student has been duly enrolled in the University and is eligible to participate in all activities of the University. A student is presumed to be in good standing unless the student forfeits that status by established misconduct.

In order for your application to be eligible, the following criteria must also be met:

- The company/organization must not have any economic and trade sanctions listed against them as stated by the Office Of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC).

- The country in which the opportunity is located in must not have a travel alert or warning listed against them by the US Department of State. Please note that countries with a level 3 or 4 warning will generally not be eligible for funding.

- Post-Advancement Opportunity

- Post AO trip, students are required to fulfill the reporting requirements outlined in the AO award letter within one week.

- Complete a survey about the AO experience.

- Write a brief summary (200 words) about how they will apply what they have learnt to something that benefits the larger NYUAD student body.

- Must provide 1-2 pictures, if possible, with captions from the program along with a testimony (screen shot of welcome page, selfie of you with welcome page, etc).

- Ensure to list in the survey universities and organizations that attended the opportunity.

- Selection Criteria

Applications must meet all stated criteria and eligibility requirements. They are further scored on the completeness of the application, quality of response, and the applicant's ability to convey how the opportunity will benefit their major or career.

Given NYU Abu Dhabi’s own institutional priorities, preference will be given to AOs that provide:

- Opportunities to partner with UAE organizations, educational institutions and peers.

- Networking with both industry leaders and other university students.

- NYU Abu Dhabi with representation and exposure in areas or fields of relevance to the institution.

- An opportunity for meaningful intercultural exposure and competency building.

- Advancement of academic goals and personal development for the participating student.

- Clear learning objectives that will have an impact/bring benefit to the wider NYUAD student body and campus.

- Terms And Conditions

AO funding is granted to eligible students through a competitive application process. Receiving this funding confers the responsibility of upholding the program requirements. Failure to adhere to the stated criteria will result in the consequences outlined below. If the funding recipient (1) does not complete the opportunity for which they receive funding, and/or (2) is found to have provided inaccurate data or information in support of their application, the student will:

- Meet with the Associate Dean of Students.

- Be required to return the full amount of funding.

- Receive a Dean's Academic Hold if the required funds are not returned by the specified date. A Dean’s Academic Hold withholds your final transcript and diploma.

- Students who are funded by the university for another activity are not able to be funded for an advancement opportunity that occurs during the same time. AO funding can only be considered if the two opportunities do not overlap.

- Application Process

- Submit a complete application in the Student Portal. Incomplete applications will not be reviewed.

- AO applications are accepted on a rolling basis from September to May. In the event funds are depleted prior to May, an announcement will be posted on the Student Portal. No applications will be accepted or reviewed from between the end of May and to the beginning of September. Applications will not be reviewed over weekends or during university or public holidays.

- The AO Committee will not issue a letter excusing a student from class. Fulfilling academic requirements is the students’ priority. It is the student’s responsibility to clear any absences with their professors in advance. If there are objections to the student missing class, the AO Committee recommends the student not attend the AO.

- The AO Committee has 10 business days from the date the application is submitted to respond (excluding weekends) with a funding decision. Applications will not be reviewed during university or public holidays.

- If awarded, you will receive an email requiring you to sign and return your award letter.

- Once the AO committee receives your signed award letter, your award will be processed. Processing time is 10 business days for the funds to be uploaded to your student Wirecard.

- All AO funding must be approved prior to the start of the AO event. Under no circumstances will AO funding be retroactive.

Funding from NYUAD is not guaranteed in any case. The university is not responsible for funding a non-NYUAD opportunity solely because a student has received an invitation or because it was advertised through NYUAD.

All decisions made regarding each application are final. There will be no appeal process.

Selection Criteria

The AO Committee will look at applications based on their individual merit. When considering a student’s request for funding, priority will be given to students who have met the eligibility requirements stated previously and have demonstrated the following:

- Thorough and detailed completion of the application, including the attachment of required supporting documents

- Development of leadership through active involvement in such things as:

- Holding a leadership role or being an active member of Student Government, a Student Interest Group, or NYU Abu Dhabi team for at least one semester

- A demonstrated, meaningful one to two semester commitment to community service with the same organization

- Developing a thorough entrepreneurial idea and initiative while a student at NYU Abu Dhabi. The student will submit the opportunity assessment, business plan and/or proposal, with financials, as part of their AO application

- Involvement with the planning and implementation of an initiative that has successfully brought together students at NYUAD and/or from at least two global network campuses

- A member of a core or executive team of students creating, organizing and implementing a student-led conference or summit at NYU Abu Dhabi.

- Travel Logistics

In order for your application to be eligible, the following criteria must also be met:

- The company/organization must not have any economic and trade sanctions listed against them as stated by the Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC).

- The country in which the opportunity is located in must not have a travel alert or warning listed against them by the US Department of State. Please note that countries with a level 3 or 4 warning will generally not be eligible for funding.

- Which type of airline ticket should I book?

You are advised to book a refundable ticket.

All decisions made regarding each application are final. There will be no appeal process.

title: GMAT Registration Fee Waiver · NYUAD Students
text:
The GMAT Registration Fee Waiver is NOW CLOSED. If you have any questions please email nyuad.career@nyu.edu .

The Graduate Management Accreditation Council (GMAC) typically grants the Career Development Center (CDC) annual Graduate Management Admission Test (GMAT) registration fee waivers for those NYUAD students that demonstrate financial need and who will take the exam online before the expiration of the waiver. The GMAT is an exam typically required for application to graduate programs worldwide in business, finance, economics and more. To learn more about this exam please visit GMAC.com . This application process is only offered once, in the fall semester of an academic year.

Note: This waiver is only available for current NYUAD students. Visiting students are required to inquire about waivers at their home campus.

Available Waivers

The waivers can only be used for taking the GMAT online and cannot be used for in-person tests. The waivers will expire on February 6, 2027 , so you must register and take the exam prior to this date.

Important Requirements and Information

- Eligibility Requirements

Eligibility requirements to apply for this waiver, as defined by GMAC, include:

- be a current junior or senior student graduating in December 2026 at the time of application,

- cannot have received a waiver in a previous year,

- register and take the exam by the expiration date,

- take the exam in the format allowed by the waiver,

- and demonstrate financial need as determined through CDC consultation with the NYU Office of Financial Support.

- Selection Criteria

Selection is based on:

- level of financial need, as determined by CDC consultation with the NYU Office of Financial Support,

- timeliness of application.

- Terms and Conditions

Given the limited number of waivers available, the requirements set by GMAC to receive these waivers, as well as the uncertainty of receiving waivers from year to year, terms and conditions do apply.

- Students who receive the GMAT waiver are required to submit a copy of their test score reports to nyuad.career@nyu.edu before graduating. Failure to do so will result in a transcript/diploma hold.

- Should the amount of eligible applicants exceed the amount of waivers, priority will be given to applicants with higher financial need.

- Timeliness of an application is determined by the submission of a complete application.

- Applicants who have been granted a GMAT waiver in previous years will not be eligible to apply and will not be considered in future cycles.

- All decisions made regarding each application are final. There will be no appeal process.

- All issues related to registration, taking the exam in person, or any complications, should be addressed directly to GMAC at customercare@gmac.com .

text:

Summer Internship Grant

The Career Development Center (CDC) offers summer internship grants to eligible NYUAD undergraduate and graduate students enrolled in the MSc or MFA programs through a competitive application process. This supplemental grant helps students pursue internships in the UAE and across the globe each summer.

Internships for the purposes of this grant are work-experience opportunities that are off-campus and not supervised by a university faculty mentor or researcher. The student is interning in-person and on-site (in an office environment, government agency, or other CDC-approved location) in an effort to explore a possible career path.

Please note that research opportunities, summer courses, and PPTP are not eligible for this grant. There are other grants for summer research , summer courses , and summer research as a recent alumni through the Postgraduate Practical Training Program . Students cannot begin an internship while simultaneously participating in June J-term, Summer Research Assistantship Program, Summer Courses, Real AD, Summer Academy Chaperone program or any other NYU Abu Dhabi funded summer program.

Why Do an Internship?

A summer internship is a great opportunity for you to gain practical and professional experience. Many students choose to take on an internship during the summer given the flexibility to take on opportunities full time to have a more meaningful and immersive experience outside of the classroom.

In addition, the real-world experience you gain through internships give you a competitive edge when making full-time job applications. In fact many students end up being offered a full-time position with the company they interned at. Here is an article outlining 10 reasons why an internship is important to all students .

Finding Your Internship

Applying for the Summer Internship Grant requires you to have secured an internship in the first place. Here are a few tips to help you kickstart your internship search.

Start Early: Companies and certain industries have variable hiring timelines. In the UAE for example, there aren’t set times for recruitment for internships, so if you would like to pursue an internship opportunity, you should be proactive and plan ahead when it comes to networking and searching for these opportunities.

Did you know that a majority of students don’t wait for an opportunity to get posted but are proactively reaching out to employers and organizations they are interested in? Don’t underestimate the value of networking and cold-emailing!

Explore Where Students Worked Before: Use the student work experience map and the post-graduation employment map to explore work experiences that NYUAD students and alumni have had across a range of industries and organizations. All data is self-reported by NYUAD students and alumni, and a helpful starting point in your search. This information can be valuable as you can look up some of these organizations and the work they do in the region, as well as visit their respective websites to see what opportunities they may have available.

Seek Advice and Feedback: Getting an internship is a learning journey. You are not expected to be an expert from day one. Our experienced career advisors are here to discuss your career goals, your internship search strategies, review your CV and other application materials, and more! Simply book an appointment via Handshake or visit the CDC during walk-in hours from Monday to Thursday between 2:00 pm and 4:00 pm .

title: About the Summer Internship Grant · NYUAD Students
text:
Summer Internship Grant

The Career Development Center (CDC) offers summer internship grants to eligible NYUAD undergraduate and graduate students enrolled in the MSc or MFA programs through a competitive application process. This supplemental grant helps students pursue internships in the UAE and across the globe each summer.

Internships for the purposes of this grant are work-experience opportunities that are off-campus and not supervised by a university faculty mentor or researcher. The student is interning in-person and on-site (in an office environment, government agency, or other CDC approved location) in an effort to explore a possible career path.

Please note that research opportunities, summer courses, and PPTP are not eligible for this grant. There are other grants for summer research , summer courses , and summer research as a recent alumni through the Postgraduate Practical Training Program . Students cannot begin an internship while simultaneously participating in June J-term, Summer Research Assistantship Program, Summer Courses, or Real AD.

At a Glance

What the grant covers

The grant is a supplemental contribution to help make internships possible for students who face unsurmountable financial barriers. It is not intended to fully fund students' internship but rather provide a level of financial support which, when combined with students' internship compensation and what can be reasonably expected of students to independently source and adjust to, provide sufficient coverage for students to participate in internships.

As such, grant amounts are calculated based on the expected cost of living in the city of the internship. The cost of living calculation includes accommodation, food and ground commute but does not include flight costs to and from the internship location. The internship grant amount is also capped at a maximum of USD 4,000 irrespective of the internship location and duration.

title: Summer Internship Grant Application Deadlines · NYUAD Students
text:
Important Update!

The Career Development Center is implementing more rigorous internship verification steps as from the AY 2025/26.

Students are highly encouraged to apply as early as possible and not wait till the deadline to submit their applications. Applying close to the deadline do not affect your chances of being awarded the grant BUT your grant confirmation and funds disbursement can be delayed for an additional two weeks pending verification of your internship details.

Our Application Cycles

We have three application cycles with deadlines on 23rd March, 29th April and 13th May . Students who require university sponsored US visas (I-20 extension) or UAE student visa renewal 1 must apply in Cycle 1 .

Students who do not need any visa support from the university may apply in either Cycle 1 or Cycle 2. This would include students who intend to intern in their home country or any other country where they are already eligible to work 2 . Cycle 3 is only for students who receive internship offer letters after April 29th or students whose applications have been rejected in Cycle 1 or Cycle 2.

Cycle Deadlines

Application Cycle 1: US F1 Visa Extension (NYC and D C) / UAE Visa Renewal / Home Country / Passport Country / Work Eligible Country (no visa needed)

Application Opens | February 16, 2026

Application Deadline | March 23, 2026 at 08:59 AM GST (Abu Dhabi time) *** You have to follow this deadline if you require ANY visa support including an I-20 extension. ***Graduate students can only apply for funding for internships in the UAE or for internships in their home country or in a work-eligible country.

Notification Date | March 27, 2026

Application Cycle 2: Home country / Passport Country / Work Eligible Country (no work visa needed)

Application Opens | March 23, 2026 at 09:00

Application Deadline | April 29, 2026 at 08:59 AM GST (Abu Dhabi time) *** Please note that this cycle only considers students who have internships in their home country or other work eligible country. ***If your internship is in the US and you require a visa extension OR your internship is in the UAE and you require a student visa renewal, you have to meet the first deadline (March 23rd). Exceptions cannot be made due to visa processing timelines.

Notification Date | May 4, 2026

Application Cycle 3: Home country / Passport Country / Work Eligible Country (no work visa needed)

Application Opens | April 29, 2026 at 09:00

Application Deadline | May 13, 2026 at 08:59 AM GST (Abu Dhabi time) *** Please note that this cycle only considers students who have internships in their home country or other work eligible country. ***If your internship is in the US and you require a visa extension OR your internship is in the UAE and you require a student visa renewal, you have to meet the first deadline (March 23rd). Exceptions cannot be made due to visa processing timelines.

Notification Date | May 15, 2026

1 Students who have been outside of the UAE for more than 180 consecutive days will have their visa automatically nullified. If they intend to return to the UAE to intern in the summer, they will need a new entry permit and their student visa renewed. To allow enough time for this process, students must apply in Cycle 1.

2 It is the student’s responsibility to ensure that they have researched and fully comply with the legal requirements of interning in their chosen country.

title: Eligibility & Grant Conditions · NYUAD Students
text:
Eligibility Requirements

To qualify for a Summer Internship Grant, the student, host organization and internship opportunity must meet the following eligibility criteria.

Student Eligibility

- Matriculation Status: The applicant should be a full-time matriculated and enrolled student at NYUAD. They should have completed at least two semesters before the start of their internships and have at least one full semester to complete before graduation by the end of their proposed internship, or be a graduate student enrolled in the MSc or MFA program. Students on leave of absence are not eligible.

- Academic Standing: Students should be in good academic standing. They should have a minimum cumulative GPA of 3.0 (including first year grades). If their GPA is below 3.0, students should meet an academic advisor to discuss their summer internship plans and receive formal approval from the Academic Resource Center before applying for the Summer Internship Grant.

- Disciplinary Standing: Students should be in good disciplinary standing and should not have engaged in any prohibited conduct as defined by the NYUAD student conduct policy and associated NYU global policies.

- CDC Orientation: Students should have completed the CDC orientation. Use this guide to verify completion status. Students who have not attended the orientation should complete the online orientation available on Brightspace .
Please note: completion of the course does not result in an automatic Handshake label being added. The team will assess your full completion of the content and the quizzes of the course and add the label.

- Previous Awards: Students should not have already been granted two summer internship grants while being a student at NYUAD. The $200 stipend for virtual opportunities does not count towards this total.

- Past Grants Compliance: Students must have never failed the Summer Directed Study Course in previous summers in which they received funding, if they were required to complete such course.

- Concurrent Opportunities: Students may not receive more than one type of award from the Summer Opportunities Program in the same summer. For example, they cannot be awarded a Summer Internship Grant along with a Summer Research Grant, a Summer Research Assistantship, REAL AD funding, Summer Academy Chaperone position or any other similar NYUAD funded summer opportunity.

Host Organization Eligibility

- No Sanctions: The company/organization must not have any economic and trade sanctions listed against them as stated by the Office Of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) .

- Travel Warnings: The country in which the internship is located must not have any economic and trade sanctions or a travel warning listed against them by the US Department of State . Please note that countries with a level 3 or 4 warning will generally not be eligible for funding unless it is the student's home country.

- Physical Presence: The company must have a physical location with suitable amenities (eg office of suitable size) to support the type of work proposed in the internship. Otherwise the internship will be considered a remote opportunity.

- No Conflict: The company must not be owned or be directed by a current New York University Student from any campus.

-

Internship Opportunity Eligibility

- Full-Time: The internship opportunity must be full-time (usually a minimum of 35 hours per week or as mandated by local law).

- Internship Duration: The internship should be a minimum of six weeks. Exceptions can be made for legal and medical shadowing and arts residency opportunities.

- Start Date: The internship must start after the end of the semester. If the students is participating in J-term or Summer Courses then their internship start date must be after the end of J-term or their Summer Courses.

- End Date: The internship must end before the first week of classes of the fall semester.

- Off-Campus Only: On-campus opportunities are not eligible for summer internship grants at any NYU site, or any other university campus.

- Offer Letter: An offer letter for the internship must be issued and submitted. The offer letter should include the expected internship dates, work-hours, mode of work and any compensation or benefits, as outlined in this template .

- Fee-Based Opportunities: Grants will not be issued to support internship opportunities that require a fee.

- Modality: Students must spend a minimum of 3 days per week in-person at the employer's premises. Otherwise the internship will be considered remote and will only be supported by a USD 200 fixed stipend. The modality must be explicitly stated in the internship offer letter or contract.

- No Conflict: The student's internship supervisor cannot be a current New York University student from any campus.

Conditions of Award

The Summer Internship Grant is awarded to eligible students through a competitive application process. Receiving this grant confers upon the recipient the responsibility to uphold all the program requirements outlined below.

Summer Directed Study Course
All students supported by NYUAD for an internship through funding, housing or visa support are required to enroll in a 1-credit Directed Study Course. The course is designed to help you evidence and document your experience and will appear on your transcript. This allows you to legitimize your experience to potential employers and will also act as a way to reflect on what you have learned and how you have grown as a result. If you are awarded funding for an internship or research opportunity, you will be enrolled in the course by the end of May.

Students interning in the US with visa support from the university will be required to attend at least four in-person classes at the course site (New York) as part of the Directed Study Course.

General Terms and Conditions
The general terms and conditions of receiving the Summer Internship Grant are outlined in this document . Students are responsible to make sure they have read and understood these terms and conditions acknowledge that by submitting an application for the summer internship grant, they are agreeing to the said terms and conditions.

Consequences of Breach of Conditions

If a funding recipient does not complete the internship for which they receive funding and fails to inform the CDC OR is found to have provided inaccurate information in support of their application, the student will:

- Be required to return up to the full amount of funding, including costs incurred by the university such as housing costs and directed study course costs.

- Receive a Dean's Academic Hold if the required funds are not returned by a specified date. A Dean's Academic Hold withholds your final transcript and diploma.

- Be investigated by the student conduct team and face additional disciplinary consequences if found to have misrepresented information.

- Be disqualified from receiving any CDC grants in the future.

- Be required to meet with the Associate Dean of Students/Director of the Career Development Center

For example, they cannot be awarded a Summer Internship Grant along with a Summer Research Grant, a Summer Research Assistantship, REAL AD funding, Summer Academy Chaperone position or any other similar NYUAD funded summer opportunity.

Host Organization Eligibility

- No Sanctions: The company/organization must not have any economic and trade sanctions listed against them as stated by the Office Of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) .

- Travel Warnings: The country in which the internship is located must not have any economic and trade sanctions or a travel warning listed against them by the US Department of State . Please note that countries with a level 3 or 4 warning will generally not be eligible for funding unless it is the student's home country.

- Physical Presence: The company must have a physical location with suitable amenities (eg office of suitable size) to support the type of work proposed in the internship. Otherwise the internship will be considered a remote opportunity.

- No Conflict: The company must not be owned or be directed by a current New York University Student from any campus.

-

Internship Opportunity Eligibility

- Full-Time: The internship opportunity must be full-time (usually a minimum of 35 hours per week or as mandated by local law).

- Internship Duration: The internship should be a minimum of six weeks. Exceptions can be made for legal and medical shadowing and arts residency opportunities.

- Start Date: The internship must start after the end of the semester. If the students is participating in J-term or Summer Courses then their internship start date must be after the end of J-term or their Summer Courses.

- End Date: The internship must end before the first week of classes of the fall semester.

- Off-Campus Only: On-campus opportunities are not eligible for summer internship grants at any NYU site, or any other university campus.

- Offer Letter: An offer letter for the internship must be issued and submitted. The offer letter should include the expected internship dates, work-hours, mode of work and any compensation or benefits, as outlined in this template .

- Fee-Based Opportunities: Grants will not be issued to support internship opportunities that require a fee.

- Modality: Students must spend a minimum of 3 days per week in-person at the employer's premises. Otherwise the internship will be considered remote and will only be supported by a USD 200 fixed stipend. The modality must be explicitly stated in the internship offer letter or contract.

- No Conflict: The student's internship supervisor cannot be a current New York University student from any campus.

sections.title: Conditions of Award
sections.text:
The Summer Internship Grant is awarded to eligible students through a competitive application process. Receiving this grant confers upon the recipient the responsibility to uphold all the program requirements outlined below.

Summer Directed Study Course
All students supported by NYUAD for an internship through funding, housing or visa support are required to enroll in a 1-credit Directed Study Course. The course is designed to help you evidence and document your experience and will appear on your transcript. This allows you to legitimize your experience to potential employers and will also act as a way to reflect on what you have learned and how you have grown as a result. If you are awarded funding for an internship or research opportunity, you will be enrolled in the course by the end of May.

Students interning in the US with visa support from the university will be required to attend at least four in-person classes at the course site (New York) as part of the Directed Study Course.

General Terms and Conditions
The general terms and conditions of receiving the Summer Internship Grant are outlined in this document . Students are responsible to make sure they have read and understood these terms and conditions acknowledge that by submitting an application for the summer internship grant, they are agreeing to the said terms and conditions.

sections.title: Consequences of Breach of Conditions
sections.text:
If a funding recipient does not complete the internship for which they receive funding and fails to inform the CDC OR is found to have provided inaccurate information in support of their application, the student will:

- Be required to return up to the full amount of funding, including costs incurred by the university such as housing costs and directed study course costs.

- Receive a Dean's Academic Hold if the required funds are not returned by a specified date. A Dean's Academic Hold withholds your final transcript and diploma.

- Be investigated by the student conduct team and face additional disciplinary consequences if found to have misrepresented information.

- Be disqualified from receiving any CDC grants in the future.

- Be required to meet with the Associate Dean of Students/Director of the Career Development Center

title: Housing, Visa & Legal Requirements · NYUAD Students
text:
Internship Housing, Visa, & Legal Requirements

Please note that the university is unable to support visa applications for work experiences outside of applicants' work-eligible countries, except for I-20 extensions for US F-1 visa holders but under the strict and limited conditions outlined below. Students wishing to intern overseas need to make their own visa arrangements and take full responsibility to inform themselves of any applicable visa or other legal requirements.

United States

The university will not be able to process new visa applications, including issuing new I-20s for existing F-1 visa holders for summer 2026. Only I-20 extensions will be possible. As a result, only the following students will be eligible for University sponsored US visas:

- Students who are spending the Spring 2026 Semester at any US-based NYU Campus except NYU Tulsa*

- CPT eligible students : Students who will have spent the past year (Fall 2025 & Spring 2026) in the US.

*Guidance is currently pending for students spending the Spring 2026 Semester at NYU Tulsa. This page will be updated as soon as more information is available.

Internship Conditions

For students who have spent only the Spring 2026 semester in the US ( not CPT eligible ), the following internship conditions apply:

- Location: Students may only intern within the New York metro area as the justification for students' I-20 is that they are undertaking in-person academic study at the New York campus.

- Compensation: Students may only participate in unpaid work experiences .

- Arrival Dates and Work Hours : Students should liaise with their employer to ensure that their internship dates and expected arrival in the US are aligned with the Directed Study Course. Students should make the necessary arrangements to attend all in-person sessions of the Directed Study Course. As it stands, students must arrive in the US by June 1st.

For CPT eligible students, the following internship conditions apply:

- Location: CPT-eligible students may be located further from the NY area but must make all necessary arrangements to attend all in-person sessions of the directed study course. IMPORTANT: Students must maintain and preserve documentation of attending classes which includes but is not limited to flight itineraries, boarding passes, train tickets or any other transportation documents and confirmation of participating in the classes.

- Compensation: Students may participate in paid or unpaid internships.

- Arrival Dates and Work Hours : Students should liaise with their employer to ensure that their internship dates and expected arrival in the US are aligned with the Directed Study Course. Students should discuss work hours with their employers so that they are able to attend all in-person sessions of the Directed Study Course. As it stands, students must arrive in the US by June 1st. We will update this page once course dates are confirmed.

Again, please note that this restriction is to remain compliant with U.S Government regulations and NYU has no control over it. If you have already secured and intend to pursue an internship outside of the NY metro area please contact the CDC at nyuad.cdcgrants@nyu.edu for guidance.

Directed Study Course

This course is legally required for all students receiving summer funding OR any form of support from NYUAD to participate in a summer program.

In order to remain fully compliant with the conditions and stipulations of an F-1 visa, which is issued for an individual to undertake in-person academic study , the Directed Study Course has been updated since AY 24/25. Students will be required to attend weekly in-person sessions at the New York site. The exact session dates are being finalized and will be published here as soon as they are available. Students need to make necessary arrangements to attend all the sessions in order to maintain their visa status.

The course will appear on students' NYUAD transcript and be graded on a Pass/Fail basis. To pass the course, students must meet attendance requirements and complete all assignments.

Please note that this requirement derives from U.S. government regulations and NYU has no control over it. The law mandates international students to be physically present in the summer course. Failing to meet the requirement will result in immediate cancellation of the visa and will jeopardize your ability to obtain a US visa in the future.

Housing in the US

Given consistently low demand for NYU housing over the previous years, past arrangements to offer on-campus housing at the NYU and DC sites have been discontinued. Students are therefore responsible find their own off-campus housing.

If you have any questions or queries regarding US visa support please email us at nyuad.cdcgrants@nyu.edu.

UAE

Visa and Legal Requirements

Students wishing to conduct an internship in the UAE in summer 2026 must have an active UAE student visa, or other valid work status (eg, UAE passport, Golden Visa, parent-sponsored visa, etc).

***Please note that students who have been outside of the UAE for more than 180 consecutive days will have their visa automatically nullified. If they intend to return to the UAE to intern in the summer, they will need a new entry permit and their student visa renewed. To allow enough time for this process, students must apply for the Summer Internship Grant in Cycle 1.

***Please check your UAE visa expiry date. If your visa is expiring in the summer, reach out to the Office of Global Education at NYUAD as soon as possible to renew.

NYUAD Housing

Please note the following important regulations about NYUAD summer housing.

- NYUAD housing is only available to students who have secured in-person internships in Abu Dhabi. For other UAE locations, students will have to arrange their own housing.

- Your endorsed NYUAD summer housing will start on the closest available check-in date to your internship start date. Should you need housing for more days before the start of your internship, you will have to make your own arrangements.

- No on campus housing will be available after July 24th, 2026

- Your on-campus check-in and check-out dates will be shared with you by the Student Life Housing & Operations Team, you CANNOT stay on campus any day before, or after these dates. Please plan accordingly.

Please find on-campus housing timelines below:

May 7th, 2026 | Instructions will be sent by the Res Life team only to eligible students on how to apply for summer housing in Abu Dhabi.

May 7th, 2026 | Summer housing application opens

May 11th, 2026 | Deadline to apply for summer housing. Any applications received after 09:00 am GST (Abu Dhabi Time) on this day will be subject to a USD $100 late application fee . This fee will not be covered by NYUAD summer funding and will be your personal responsibility.

May 16th, 23:59 GST | Cancellation Deadline. You MUST apply for housing before the deadline even if you haven’t received an internship offer yet. If, for any reason, your internship plans do not work out, you MUST cancel your housing application before May 16th, 23:59 GST . Cancellation fee will be charged for cancellations made after this deadline.

July 25th, 2026 | Last possible stay date. No rooms will be available after this date. Therefore, please plan to arrange housing off campus from July 24th until the end of your internship.

Europe

Visa Requirements

The Office of Global Education is unable to support visa applications in Europe. This is because all European NYU sites are closed during the summer. In general, your options are the following:

- Your employer is willing to sponsor your visa

- Sponsor your own visa if possible: Please research visa requirements and application duration ahead of time).

- Enroll in NYU's Summer European Internship Program . Please note that this course is run by NYU New York and is not eligibl e for NYUAD financial aid. You should research the cost of this course ahead of time.

Other Legal Requirements

If your internship is in Spain, Italy or France , you will be legally required to provide a signed copy of an internship agreement form, often called Convention de Stage , or Convenio de Prácticas*. This form may only be obtained if students enroll in the NYU's Summer European Internship Program and is provided by NYU New York Staff. The requirement applies for both international students and EU citizens.

In some cases, this requirement may apply to other European countries. Please be aware that if your employer requests a signed copy of this form, you will be required to enroll in the NYU's Summer European Internship Program .

*Please note that the CDC is legally unable to sign these forms and only enrolling in the NYU's Summer European Internship Program will provide NYU New York staff the ability to sign this document.

Housing

Students interning in Europe are responsible for making their own housing arrangements.

Other Locations

Students choosing to intern in their home country or any location other than the UAE, Europe, and the US, are required to confirm any legal requirements and to arrange their own visa and housing. Students are strongly advised to research the requirements and visa durations in advance.

< Back to Main Page

Related official links:
https://students.nyuad.nyu.edu/student-affairs/career-development/grants/internships/
