title: Interview Travel Grant · NYUAD Students
text:
Deadline : May 8, 2026 4pm GST

The CDC is pleased to announce that the Interview Travel Grant now also covers inter-city travel within the UAE . Read below to find out more.

About the Interview Travel Grant

The Career Development Center (CDC) offers interview travel grants to eligible NYUAD students through a competitive application process. This funding can help students cover the cost of attending a final round interview related to their post-graduation plans. The interview must take place in person rather than virtually or by phone. These grants are not designed to cover all costs and should be considered supplemental. As such, students should consider additional sources to fund their opportunities throughout the academic year.

Available Grants

There are two main types of grant available: international travel or local travel within the UAE.

International Travel

There are three possible grant amounts available depending on the length of a one-way direct flight from your study site at the time of your application to the interview site. If there is no direct flight, the grant will be determined on a case-by-case basis by the funding committee by consulting NYUAD’s travel agent and using nearby cities which do have direct flights. Please remember that these grants are supplemental and are not meant to always cover all costs.

- 0 to 5 hour flight time: USD 300 (AED 1,100)

- 5:01 to 8 hour flight time: USD 500 (AED 1840)

- 8:01 hour flight time and over: USD 1000 (AED 3670)

Local travel within the UAE

Students may receive up to a total USD 165 (AED 600) for land-based inter-city travel within the UAE. This total is for the whole round trip and not per leg of the trip. Since the Interview Travel Grant operates on a reimbursement basis, students are advised to ensure they receive a payment receipt for their trip to submit to the CDC. Please note that this grant does not cover travel within Abu Dhabi .

Important Requirements and Information

All decisions made regarding each application are final. There will be no appeal process.

- Eligibility Requirements — Undergraduate Students

An application for an Interview Travel Grant will only be considered if the following eligibility criteria are met. The student must:

- be a full-time matriculated student at NYUAD

- be in good academic standing with a minimum cumulative GPA of 3.0 (including first year grades). If not students should have approval from their academic mentor as indicated in the Mentor Approval form.

- not have already received an interview travel grant in the same academic year AND not have already received an Interview Travel Grant twice during their time at NYUAD.

- be in good disciplinary standing * (to be verified by the judicial officer)

- have attended a CDC Orientation (formerly called Internship Orientation). Follow this guide to check if you have completed the CDC Orientation.

- have completed the Mentor Approval form

* Good disciplinary standing indicates that a student has been duly enrolled in the University and is eligible to participate in all activities of the University. A student is presumed to be in good standing unless the student forfeits that status by established misconduct.

In order for your application to be eligible, the following criteria must also be met.

- The company/organization must not have any economic and trade sanctions listed against them as stated by the Office Of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) .

- The country in which the interview is located in must not have a travel alert or warning listed against them by the US Department of State .

Please note that for international travel, applications must be submitted at least five business days before the date of the interview in order to be considered and for local travel, applications must be submitted at least two business days before the date of the interview.

- Eligibility Requirements — Graduate Students

An application for an Interview Travel Grant will only be considered if the following eligibility criteria are met. The student must:

- be a full-time matriculated student at NYUAD as an MSc/MFA student. PhD students are not eligible for this grant.

- be in good academic standing

- have not already received an interview travel grant before

- be in good disciplinary standing * (to be verified by the GPPO)

- have received approval from the program head (MS/MFA) for overseas travel if relevant

* Good disciplinary standing indicates that a graduate student has been duly enrolled in the University and is eligible to participate in all activities of the University. A student is presumed to be in good standing unless the student forfeits that status by established misconduct.

In order for your application to be eligible, the following criteria must also be met.

- The company/organization must not have any economic and trade sanctions listed against them as stated by the Office Of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) .

- The country in which the interview is located in must not have a travel alert or warning listed against them by the US Department of State .

Please note that for international travel, applications must be submitted at least five business days before the date of the interview in order to be considered and for local travel, applications must be submitted at least two business days before the date of the interview.

- Travel Logistics

All flight arrangements are the responsibility of the student (undergraduate and graduate students). The CDC is not responsible for obtaining any required visas. The office will provide any supporting documentation necessary upon request.

All housing arrangements are the responsibility of the student (undergraduate and graduate students). Students who have secured interviews should look into options provided by the interview site, staying with family or friends, or budget accommodations.

- Selection Criteria

Applications must meet all stated criteria and eligibility requirements. They are further scored on the completeness of the application, quality of response, and the applicant's ability to convey how the opportunity will benefit their career.

- Terms and Conditions

Interview travel funding is granted to eligible undergraduate and graduate students through a competitive application process. Receiving this funding confers the responsibility of upholding the program requirements. Failure to adhere to the stated criteria will result in the consequences outlined below..

If the funding recipient (1) does not complete the interview for which they receive funding, (2) is found to have provided inaccurate data or information in support of their application, and/or (3) has not completed the NYUAD Funded Individual Student Travel Form , the student will:

- Meet with the Associate Dean of Student Affairs and Director, Career Development Center,

- Be required to return the full amount of funding, and

- Receive a Dean's Academic Hold if the required funds are not returned by the specified date. A Dean’s Academic Hold withholds your final transcript and diploma.

- Application Process — Undergraduate Students

- Applications will be accepted on a rolling basis up to one week before the end of the fall and spring semesters . No applications will be accepted during the summer. Applications will not be reviewed over weekends or during university/public holidays.

- To ensure a thorough application review, we require that students submit their application at least 5 business days (excluding weekends) before their interview for international travel and at least 2 business days before their interview for travel within the UAE.

- If awarded, you will receive an email requiring you to: (1) complete the Funded Individual Student Travel form, and (2) sign and return your award letter.

- Once the CDC confirms you have completed the travel form and receives your signed award letter, your grant will be processed. Processing time is five business days for the funds to transfer to your account.

- After completion of the interview, you will be required to complete a brief survey on your interview experience.

Get Support for Your Big Idea

Do you have an idea that will inspire people to help make a significant impact on our local community?

Students are welcome to submit a student-led conference-funding proposal through the Application Form .

Important Dates

- Applications open on the first day of classes and remain open for a month.

- Applications for the academic year will be reviewed by the end of September.

- Funding decisions on applications will be made the second week of October 2025.

- All conference/events must be completed by the first week of May.

Applications are not on a rolling basis throughout the year; students are strongly encouraged to plan to meet with the Career Development Center to discuss their proposal before submitting it.

Get a Staff/Faculty Advisor

Student-led conferences are required to secure a staff or faculty advisor who can provide assistance with developing the content and curriculum for your event. title: Standardized Test Preparation Grant · NYUAD Students
text:
Important Update as of September 1, 2026:

This page is currently being updated with application dates and deadlines for the upcoming grant cycle. Please check back soon for updated application information.

Program guidelines remain unchanged. The Test Preparation Grant is intended to support eligible test preparation courses for standardized exams not currently covered by NYU New York Kaplan All Access.

Please note that meeting the eligibility requirements and submitting an application does not guarantee funding. All eligible applications are subject to review, and grant awards are made based on program guidelines and available funding.

Given the launch of the NYU New York Kaplan All Access initiative, which offers NYU students free access to Kaplan’s industry-leading test preparation courses, the standardized test preparation grant program beginning with the 2024-25 Academic Year is only eligible for test preparation courses for exams that are not covered by Kaplan.

We are actively monitoring the initiative and the Standardized Test Preparation Grant Committee will meet annually to update our policies. Any future changes to the grant will be promptly communicated to all NYU Abu Dhabi students through official Career Development Center channels, including newsletters, the student portal, Handshake, and more.

The Grant

The Career Development Center (CDC) offers a Standardized Test Preparation Grant (STPG) to eligible NYUAD undergraduate students through a competitive application process. The grant can be used to take one preparation course for one standardized test required for acceptance into graduate and professional programs worldwide. The preparation course must be for an exam that is not already being administered through the NYU New York Kaplan All Access program .

Best Practices for Utilizing the Kaplan All Access / FAQ

As part of our commitment to your academic and professional success, students have access to Kaplan’s All Access test preparation courses for standardized tests such as the DAT, GMAT, GRE, LSAT, MCAT, OAT, and FE. Here are some tips on how to make the most out of this resource:

- Plan Ahead

All Kaplan test prep courses available to NYU students have a 12 month access period which begins the date you enroll. You should take this into account when planning the best time to register. For example, if you're hoping to take the GRE exam the summer before your senior year, it might be best for you to enroll in a Kaplan course 12 months prior to ensure you can access the content and complete the course.

Additionally, there are people at NYUAD who can help you plan for your next steps. You can schedule an appointment with our Graduate School and Career Advisors on Handshake or visit us during our walk-in hours at the CDC for quick questions.

- Schedule Regular Study Times

Consistency is key in preparation. Schedule regular study sessions and stick to them. Kaplan’s online resources are accessible 24/7, making it easier to fit test prep into your busy schedule.

- Take Practice Tests

Utilize Kaplan’s full-length practice tests to assess your progress. These tests provide a realistic experience and help you identify areas where you need further study.

- Engage with Interactive Resources

Take advantage of interactive study tools like video lessons, flashcards, and quizzes. These resources can help reinforce learning and make complex concepts more manageable.

- Seek Help When Needed

If you find certain topics challenging, use Kaplan’s live support or tutoring options. Asking questions and understanding answers thoroughly can boost your confidence and preparation level. You can call Kaplan customer care at 1-800-KAP-TEST or reach out to the team online .

- Utilize On-Demand Video Lessons

For topics you find particularly challenging, Kaplan’s on-demand video lessons allow you to learn and review at your own pace, ensuring you fully understand before moving on.

- Regularly Review Course Updates

Stay updated with any changes or additions to the Kaplan courses, as these might include vital information or improved strategies for test-taking.

FAQ

Q: How do I access the Kaplan All Access courses ?

A: You can access the Kaplan All Access courses by logging into the Kaplan portal with your NYU credentials to get started. If you have any questions about navigating the Kaplan site, you can view or download the user guide for NYU students .

Q: What if I encounter issues accessing the courses ?

A: Please contact the Kaplan team . You can also email us at nyuad.career@nyu.edu . We’re here to ensure you have everything you need for your test preparation.

Q: Are there any limits on how many courses I can take ?

A: No, there are no limits. You have full access to all the courses in the fields supported by Kaplan All Access. It is best for you to prioritize the test preparation course for the exam that you know for sure you need to take because you only get 12 months access to a course at a time.

Grant Guidelines

Current NYU students are now able to take the following Kaplan test preparation courses for free:

- Dental Admissions Test (DAT®)

- Graduate Management Admission Test (GMAT®)

- Graduate Record Examination (GRE®)

- Law School Admissions Test (LSAT®)

- Medical College Admission Test (MCAT®)

- Optometry Admissions Test (OAT®)

- Fundamentals of Engineering Exam (FE)

If there is a standardized exam required for admission to a graduate school and Kaplan All Access does not currently provide a preparation course for that exam, you can email nyuad.career@nyu.edu to inquire about the exam. Please include the following information in your email:

- The link(s) to the graduate program(s) you’re applying to with information in regard to the standardized exam requirements

The grant can cover up to the cost of the preparation course up to 2000 USD. The course can be online or in-person. Priority will be given to students of financial need.

The following is not covered by the Standardized Test Preparation Grant. However, students who receive Falcon Dirhams can elect for funds to be set aside for graduate school and professional expenses by establishing an individual graduate school expense account . This is a great option for students who would like to set aside some funds to cover expenses for exams or fees that fall outside of the grant:

- English proficiency exam preparation or registration

- CFA exams or other professional qualifying exams

- The purchase of test preparation materials

- The cost of registration for a standardized exam

- For students pursuing the London Track or have an interest in taking the Solicitor's Qualifying Examination (SQE): At this time, the SQE exam is not eligible for the Standardized Test Preparation Grant because it does not meet the grant requirements set by the committee given it is not an entrance exam for graduate studies.

The STPG program does not cover test preparation course reimbursements. The grant committee will only fund eligible and awarded students for payments to be made for a test preparation course going forward from the date a student would be awarded. Any program/costs incurred before the grant announcement are not eligible.

Before Applying

Applicants are highly encouraged to:

- research the various test preparation options to consider which one is most beneficial for them,

- take a diagnostic test to gauge their preparation needs,

- connect with their academic mentor to discuss preparation and graduate school plans,

- and meet with a CDC advisor to discuss graduate school plans and review the completed application before submission.

Important Requirements and Information

Eligibility Requirements

To be eligible for a standardized test preparation grant, students must meet the following eligibility requirements:

- Be a full-time sophomore, junior, or senior enrolled at NYUAD (first years are not eligible) at the time of application. Students on Leave of Absence are not eligible to apply.

- Be in good disciplinary standing* as per a conduct check.

- Be in good academic standing with a minimum cumulative GPA of 3.0

- Have not received a standardized test preparation award previously during their tenure at NYUAD.

- Complete a CDC Orientation prior to submitting an application. You can view if you are credited with taking the CDC Orientation in the lower left hand corner of your Profile in Handshake under Labels. If you haven't participated in or completed a CDC Orientation yet, kindly proceed to this page to complete a brief online orientation and once completed. Once finished, please send an email to nyuad.career@nyu.career to notify us of your completion.

Selection Criteria

The grant committee, made up of CDC staff, reads and scores all applications. Applications are evaluated on how well applicants have articulated their understanding of themselves, preparation for the exam, and planning for graduate school.

For more insight into the elements of a strong application please see the following scoring rubric which is used by the committee when reviewing applications.

Application Questions | Answered Effectively | Answered Somewhat Effectively | Not Answered Effectively

How will you benefit from a test prep course and the course format you are considering? | The applicant clearly articulates why this particular test prep program works for their learning style, schedule and /or needs. The applicant is specific and addresses their individual needs. The applicant describes the specific structure or components of the program and why it works for them. | The applicant articulates why this particular test prep program works for their learning style, schedule and /or needs but does not provide specific details. The applicant provides a limited description of the program structure or components and why it works for them. | The applicant does not clearly articulate why this particular test prep program works for their learning style, schedule and /or needs. The applicant is not specific and does not address their individual needs. The applicant does not provide details about the structure or components of the prep program and why it works for them.

Provide details of how you have prepared and will prepare for the exam and your plans for providing your exam score to the CDC before you graduate from NYUAD. | The applicant has prepared for the exam by reviewing, researching and/ or taking practice tests. They describe how and when they will study for the exam. They also articulate specifically when they will provide the test scores to the CDC. | The applicant has not prepared for the exam by reviewing and/or taking practice tests. They don’t describe how and when they will study for the exam. Or they do not articulate specifically when they will provide the test scores to the CDC. | The applicant does not describe effectively how they prepared for the exam and does not describe how and and when they will study for the exam. They do not articulate specifically when they will provide the test scores to the CDC.

Explain your rationale for applying for graduate school and how it fits into your future career trajectory. What specific skills and knowledge do you stand to gain by continued education? | The applicant describes what they plan on studying, the specific skills and knowledge they will acquire through graduate education and how it will help them in their career, or to figure out their career goals. | The applicant describes what they plan on studying, the skills and knowledge they will acquire and how it will help them in their career with limited detail and scope. And/or the applicant does not describe their career goals effectively. | The applicant does not describe the skills and knowledge they will acquire and how graduate school will benefit their career. The applicant does not articulate their career goals.

Provide an example of a school(s) you may apply to and note your rationale for selecting this program. Include a summary of their academic profile and then assess your feasibility of being accepted. | The applicant identifies one or more graduate/professional school(s) they plan on applying to. They describe the requirements of the program and explain how they meet, or plan to meet, the requirements of the program. The choice of school and plan is convincingly feasible and well reasoned for acceptance. | The applicant identifies one or more graduate/professional school(s) they plan on applying to and describes the requirements of the program with limited detail and scope. The applicant does not explain how they meet or plan to meet the requirements of the program. The plan for being accepted may not seem feasible and/or the reasoning is lacking. | The applicant does not identify one or more graduate/professional schools they plan on applying to and does not identify the requirements of the program. The applicant also does not explain how they meet or plan to meet the requirements of the program. Acceptance to their choice of school does not seem feasible.

Overall quality of application (thoroughness/clarity of answers, etc.) | The applicant is thorough, clear and detailed in their answers. | The applicant is somewhat clear and detailed in their answers. | The applicant is unclear in their answers.

Please note, once an application is submitted any changes to the application information (i.e. grant type, course type, etc.) may impact your eligibility to receive the funding.

It is strongly advised that students review their application with a CDC advisor, for feedback, before submitting it.

Terms and Conditions

The Standardized Test Preparation Grant is granted to eligible students through a competitive application process. Receiving this grant confers the responsibility of upholding the program requirements. Failure to adhere to the stated criteria will result in the consequences outlined below.

Recipients of the grant must adhere to the following:

- provide a receipt of purchase for the test preparation program and amount detailed in their application

- take the course and standardized test for which they received the preparation funding before they graduate

- provide the CDC with the official resulting test score for the standardized test they received preparation funding for before they graduate

Note:

- The review process is blind and there is no appeal process. Grant decisions are based on the strength of applications and all decisions made regarding each application are final.

- Students who cancel a score of a standardized exam will be required to return the full amount of funding they received.

- Students who take the LSAT exam and choose to use the Score Preview option but decide not to keep their score will be required to return the full amount of funding they received.

If the funding recipient (1) changes the course or does not complete the course for which they receive funding, (2) is found to have provided inaccurate information in support of their application, and/or (3) does not report their score to the CDC before graduation, the student will:

- meet with the Assistant Dean of Students/Director of the Career Development Center,

- be required to return up to the full amount of funding, and

- receive a Dean's Academic Hold if the required funds are not returned by the specified date. A Dean’s Academic Hold withholds your final transcript and diploma.

Application Dates and Deadlines

**Applications received after the deadline will be reviewed in the next application cycle.

Any future changes to the grant will be promptly communicated to all NYU Abu Dhabi students through official Career Development Center channels, including newsletters, the student portal, Handshake, and more.

sections.title: The Grant
sections.text: The Career Development Center (CDC) offers a Standardized Test Preparation Grant (STPG) to eligible NYUAD undergraduate students through a competitive application process. The grant can be used to take one preparation course for one standardized test required for acceptance into graduate and professional programs worldwide. The preparation course must be for an exam that is not already being administered through the NYU New York Kaplan All Access program .

sections.title: Best Practices for Utilizing the Kaplan All Access / FAQ
sections.text:
As part of our commitment to your academic and professional success, students have access to Kaplan’s All Access test preparation courses for standardized tests such as the DAT, GMAT, GRE, LSAT, MCAT, OAT, and FE. Here are some tips on how to make the most out of this resource:

- Plan Ahead

All Kaplan test prep courses available to NYU students have a 12 month access period which begins the date you enroll. You should take this into account when planning the best time to register. For example, if you're hoping to take the GRE exam the summer before your senior year, it might be best for you to enroll in a Kaplan course 12 months prior to ensure you can access the content and complete the course.

Additionally, there are people at NYUAD who can help you plan for your next steps. You can schedule an appointment with our Graduate School and Career Advisors on Handshake or visit us during our walk-in hours at the CDC for quick questions.

- Schedule Regular Study Times

Consistency is key in preparation. Schedule regular study sessions and stick to them. Kaplan’s online resources are accessible 24/7, making it easier to fit test prep into your busy schedule.

- Take Practice Tests

Utilize Kaplan’s full-length practice tests to assess your progress. These tests provide a realistic experience and help you identify areas where you need further study.

- Engage with Interactive Resources

Take advantage of interactive study tools like video lessons, flashcards, and quizzes. These resources can help reinforce learning and make complex concepts more manageable.

- Seek Help When Needed

If you find certain topics challenging, use Kaplan’s live support or tutoring options. Asking questions and understanding answers thoroughly can boost your confidence and preparation level. You can call Kaplan customer care at 1-800-KAP-TEST or reach out to the team online .

- Utilize On-Demand Video Lessons

For topics you find particularly challenging, Kaplan’s on-demand video lessons allow you to learn and review at your own pace, ensuring you fully understand before moving on.

- Regularly Review Course Updates

Stay updated with any changes or additions to the Kaplan courses, as these might include vital information or improved strategies for test-taking.

FAQ

Q: How do I access the Kaplan All Access courses ?

A: You can access the Kaplan All Access courses by logging into the Kaplan portal with your NYU credentials to get started. If you have any questions about navigating the Kaplan site, you can view or download the user guide for NYU students .

Q: What if I encounter issues accessing the courses ?

A: Please contact the Kaplan team . You can also email us at nyuad.career@nyu.edu . We’re here to ensure you have everything you need for your test preparation.

Q: Are there any limits on how many courses I can take ?

A: No, there are no limits. You have full access to all the courses in the fields supported by Kaplan All Access. It is best for you to prioritize the test preparation course for the exam that you know for sure you need to take because you only get 12 months access to a course at a time.

sections.title: Grant Guidelines
sections.text:
Current NYU students are now able to take the following Kaplan test preparation courses for free:

- Dental Admissions Test (DAT®)

- Graduate Management Admission Test (GMAT®)

- Graduate Record Examination (GRE®)

- Law School Admissions Test (LSAT®)

- Medical College Admission Test (MCAT®)

- Optometry Admissions Test (OAT®)

- Fundamentals of Engineering Exam (FE)

If there is a standardized exam required for admission to a graduate school and Kaplan All Access does not currently provide a preparation course for that exam, you can email nyuad.career@nyu.edu to inquire about the exam. Please include the following information in your email:

- The link(s) to the graduate program(s) you’re applying to with information in regard to the standardized exam requirements

The grant can cover up to the cost of the preparation course up to 2000 USD. The course can be online or in-person. Priority will be given to students of financial need.

The following is not covered by the Standardized Test Preparation Grant. However, students who receive Falcon Dirhams can elect for funds to be set aside for graduate school and professional expenses by establishing an individual graduate school expense account . This is a great option for students who would like to set aside some funds to cover expenses for exams or fees that fall outside of the grant:

- English proficiency exam preparation or registration

- CFA exams or other professional qualifying exams

- The purchase of test preparation materials

- The cost of registration for a standardized exam

- For students pursuing the London Track or have an interest in taking the Solicitor's Qualifying Examination (SQE): At this time, the SQE exam is not eligible for the Standardized Test Preparation Grant because it does not meet the grant requirements set by the committee given it is not an entrance exam for graduate studies.

The STPG program does not cover test preparation course reimbursements. The grant committee will only fund eligible and awarded students for payments to be made for a test preparation course going forward from the date a student would be awarded. Any program/costs incurred before the grant announcement are not eligible.

sections.title: Before Applying
sections.text:
Applicants are highly encouraged to:

- research the various test preparation options to consider which one is most beneficial for them,

- take a diagnostic test to gauge their preparation needs,

- connect with their academic mentor to discuss preparation and graduate school plans,

- and meet with a CDC advisor to discuss graduate school plans and review the completed application before submission.

sections.title: Important Requirements and Information · Eligibility Requirements
sections.text:
To be eligible for a standardized test preparation grant, students must meet the following eligibility requirements:

- Be a full-time sophomore, junior, or senior enrolled at NYUAD (first years are not eligible) at the time of application. Students on Leave of Absence are not eligible to apply.

- Be in good disciplinary standing* as per a conduct check.

- Be in good academic standing with a minimum cumulative GPA of 3.0

- Have not received a standardized test preparation award previously during their tenure at NYUAD.

- Complete a CDC Orientation prior to submitting an application. You can view if you are credited with taking the CDC Orientation in the lower left hand corner of your Profile in Handshake under Labels. If you haven't participated in or completed a CDC Orientation yet, kindly proceed to this page to complete a brief online orientation and once completed. Once finished, please send an email to nyuad.career@nyu.career to notify us of your completion.

sections.title: Important Requirements and Information · Selection Criteria
sections.text:
The grant committee, made up of CDC staff, reads and scores all applications. Applications are evaluated on how well applicants have articulated their understanding of themselves, preparation for the exam, and planning for graduate school.

For more insight into the elements of a strong application please see the following scoring rubric which is used by the committee when reviewing applications.

Application Questions | Answered Effectively | Answered Somewhat Effectively | Not Answered Effectively

How will you benefit from a test prep course and the course format you are considering? | The applicant clearly articulates why this particular test prep program works for their learning style, schedule and /or needs. The applicant is specific and addresses their individual needs. The applicant describes the specific structure or components of the program and why it works for them. | The applicant articulates why this particular test prep program works for their learning style, schedule and /or needs but does not provide specific details. The applicant provides a limited description of the program structure or components and why it works for them. | The applicant does not clearly articulate why this particular test prep program works for their learning style, schedule and /or needs. The applicant is not specific and does not address their individual needs. The applicant does not provide details about the structure or components of the prep program and why it works for them.

Provide details of how you have prepared and will prepare for the exam and your plans for providing your exam score to the CDC before you graduate from NYUAD. | The applicant has prepared for the exam by reviewing, researching and/ or taking practice tests. They describe how and when they will study for the exam. They also articulate specifically when they will provide the test scores to the CDC. | The applicant has not prepared for the exam by reviewing and/or taking practice tests. They don’t describe how and when they will study for the exam. Or they do not articulate specifically when they will provide the test scores to the CDC. | The applicant does not describe effectively how they prepared for the exam and does not describe how and and when they will study for the exam. They do not articulate specifically when they will provide the test scores to the CDC.

Explain your rationale for applying for graduate school and how it fits into your future career trajectory. What specific skills and knowledge do you stand to gain by continued education? | The applicant describes what they plan on studying, the specific skills and knowledge they will acquire through graduate education and how it will help them in their career, or to figure out their career goals. | The applicant describes what they plan on studying, the skills and knowledge they will acquire and how it will help them in their career with limited detail and scope. And/or the applicant does not describe their career goals effectively. | The applicant does not describe the skills and knowledge they will acquire and how graduate school will benefit their career. The applicant does not articulate their career goals.

Provide an example of a school(s) you may apply to and note your rationale for selecting this program. Include a summary of their academic profile and then assess your feasibility of being accepted. | The applicant identifies one or more graduate/professional school(s) they plan on applying to. They describe the requirements of the program and explain how they meet, or plan to meet, the requirements of the program. The choice of school and plan is convincingly feasible and well reasoned for acceptance. | The applicant identifies one or more graduate/professional school(s) they plan on applying to and describes the requirements of the program with limited detail and scope. The applicant does not explain how they meet or plan to meet the requirements of the program. The plan for being accepted may not seem feasible and/or the reasoning is lacking. | The applicant does not identify one or more graduate/professional schools they plan on applying to and does not identify the requirements of the program. The applicant also does not explain how they meet or plan to meet the requirements of the program. Acceptance to their choice of school does not seem feasible.

Overall quality of application (thoroughness/clarity of answers, etc.) | The applicant is thorough, clear and detailed in their answers. | The applicant is somewhat clear and detailed in their answers. | The applicant is unclear in their answers.

Please note, once an application is submitted any changes to the application information (i.e. grant type, course type, etc.) may impact your eligibility to receive the funding.

It is strongly advised that students review their application with a CDC advisor, for feedback, before submitting it.

sections.title: Terms and Conditions
sections.text:
The Standardized Test Preparation Grant is granted to eligible students through a competitive application process. Receiving this grant confers the responsibility of upholding the program requirements. Failure to adhere to the stated criteria will result in the consequences outlined below.

Recipients of the grant must adhere to the following:

- provide a receipt of purchase for the test preparation program and amount detailed in their application

- take the course and standardized test for which they received the preparation funding before they graduate

- provide the CDC with the official resulting test score for the standardized test they received preparation funding for before they graduate

Note:

- The review process is blind and there is no appeal process. Grant decisions are based on the strength of applications and all decisions made regarding each application are final.

- Students who cancel a score of a standardized exam will be required to return the full amount of funding they received.

- Students who take the LSAT exam and choose to use the Score Preview option but decide not to keep their score will be required to return the full amount of funding they received.

If the funding recipient (1) changes the course or does not complete the course for which they receive funding, (2) is found to have provided inaccurate information in support of their application, and/or (3) does not report their score to the CDC before graduation, the student will:

- meet with the Assistant Dean of Students/Director of the Career Development Center,

- be required to return up to the full amount of funding, and

- receive a Dean's Academic Hold if the required funds are not returned by the specified date. A Dean’s Academic Hold withholds your final transcript and diploma.

title: Jobs, Internships, and Experiences · NYUAD Students
text:
Interning as an NYUAD Student

The below process should be followed for all internships undertaken as an NYUAD student, even if you pursue internships while studying away. Information on completing internships during study away can be found below.

- 1. Confirm if you have completed a CDC Orientation

The CDC Orientation is a one-hour workshop to orient you to the process to intern and gain experience, navigate the UAE labor market, and leverage CDC resources and services. This will be held in-person for freshman students during the first semester Weyak program.

The CDC Orientation is also available as a self-paced video . Once you've completed the course (in either format) we will update your Handshake profile to indicate that you've completed the CDC Orientation. You can view this on your Handshake profile under "public labels". Please note that it may take up to two weeks for your Handshake profile.

You must complete a CDC Orientation:

- Once in your four years (or again as a refresher if you want),

- For all work experiences (on and off campus) while an NYUAD student, and

- To be eligible for CDC Grants: Summer Internship Grant, Standardized Test Prep Grant, Interview Travel Grant, Advancement Opportunities Grant, Student Led Conferences Grant

- 2. Confirm your academic eligibility

A cademic a pproval to intern is reviewed once a year for the current academic year and summer following. You are academically eligible to intern for fall, spring, and summer internships if:

- You have a cumulative GPA of 3.0 or above

- If you have a cumulative GPA below 3.0:

- You must see an academic advisor in the Academic Resource Center to discuss your academic progress

- You must provide a written rationale, including a list of activities they are involved in, explaining why you should be approved for internship and how you will balance academic coursework and internship responsibilities

- May be referred to Student Success and Well-Being for coaching

- May need approval from the Office of the Vice Provost for undergraduate education

- 3. Secure your internship

Offer letters may be via email, and must include:

- A start and end date,

- Supervisor details, and

- The job description

See the Gaining Experience page to help you find and secure your opportunity.

- 4. [Optional] Apply for a Summer Internship Grant (if pursuing an internship over the summer)

Applying for a Summer Internship Grant is optional, competitive, supplemental, and does not cover all costs of your summer experience. Summer internship grants are NOT guaranteed.

- 5. Report your internship through the Report Your Experience form

Completing the Report Your Experience form allows us to:

- Process your No Objection Letter (NOL) and Letters of Support. NOL’s are a legal requirement set by the UAE Ministry of Labor for all students completing internships off campus in the UAE. Letters of Support are sometimes required by companies in the application process, in which case you will need to complete the Report Your Experience form before securing the position.

- Maintain this interactive internship map so you can explore the global experiences of your peers.

-

- 6. Provide feedback and reflect on your experience

Completing the Internship Reflection Survey helps you to contextualize your experience, synthesize the skills you learned, and consider how you can apply your growth to future opportunities.

The Internship Reflection Survey:

- Allows you to evaluate your supervisor and internship experience

- Helps us understand how we can better support students through internships and develop stronger internship programs with our employer partners

The Internship Reflection Survey will automatically be sent to you at the end of each semester and allow you to evaluate your experience and supervisor.

-

Internship Letters

There are a few common letters asked or required by employers for internships.

- No Objection Letter (UAE Ministry of Labor Letter)

This is legally required by the UAE Ministry of Labor for all off-campus internships in the UAE. It is requested by completing the Report Your Experience form , and selecting off-campus and the UAE as the location. You will be asked for internship start and end-date, your internship offer letter, and supervisor details.

- Support Letter (no-contest certificate)

Also called a no-contest certificate, is a letter issued by the University demonstrating that we support you in pursuing your internship. These letters can be required by the employer during the recruitment process. It is requested by completing the Report Your Experience form , and selecting "Support Letter" under the Internship Letters section of the survey. Employers sometimes have different requirements for this letter, so be sure to briefly describe it in the Report Your Experience form .

- If you require multiple letters

In the Report Your Experience form , you can select that you require both a No-Objection Letter and a Letter of Support.

If you require a Support Letter during the recruitment process for an off-campus internship in the UAE , and you do not know the details for your No Objection Letter (start and end-date, supervisor details, offer letter), you will have to complete this survey twice. Once to get the Support Letter in order to complete the recruitment process, and a second time after receiving the internship offer to provide us with your supervisor details so we can issue the No Objection Letter.

What have other students done?

Check out this interactive map of past student internships.

How to use the internship map :

- Click on various elements to filter and click again to undo the filter.

- Use the reset button on the bottom left to go back to the original view.

- Hover over the teal squares on the far right to see exact position titles with various companies.

- Use the company or organization filters on the left to target specific opportunities.

Internships During Study Away

You can complete internships during your study away experience. For most sites you need to complete an application form well in advance of your study away semester. Details on what opportunities you can pursue and the process for each site can be found on NYU's Study Away Internships page .

Types of Experience

There are many types of professional experience you can gain while an NYUAD student. — Learn all about them

Academic Credit for Internships

NYUAD does not generally award academic credit for internship experiences.

At present, these strict requirements are met only in the 4-credit internship course offered at many of the NYU Global Sites. It is not generally available at the Abu Dhabi, New York, or Shanghai portal campuses.

During the summer NYUAD does give recognition on a student’s transcript upon successful completion of all requirements associated with a non-credit Internship course. The coursework typically includes in person course meetings when the internship is in New York or Washington, DC. The work is done online for internships pursued elsewhere.

title: On-Campus Jobs · NYUAD Students
text:
Assistantship Program

The Student Assistantship Program provides students at NYUAD with on-campus work experience opportunities within academic and administrative departments throughout the school year. The program, as part of a broader Student Employment Portfolio, is an integral part of students' professional preparation for off-campus and future opportunities. Through on-campus student employment, students earn money, develop transferable skill sets, and build capacity for institutional programs, projects, and research.

The program is open to undergraduate, master's, and visiting students. In all cases, students are only eligible when they are physically present and enrolled in classes at NYUAD.

Students can apply to available assistantship positions through Handshake .

Student Eligibility Requirements

- Physical Presence: Students are required to be physically present and based at NYUAD, enrolled in classes, and in good disciplinary standing to be eligible. Remote work is not supported; therefore, students cannot continue an assistantship when they are abroad, studying away, or on a leave of absence.

- Minimum Age 18: Students must be at least 18 years old. If the student is under 18 years of age, they must download the Under 18 On-Campus Work Authorization Form , meet an advisor at the CDC to approve their assistantship and sign the form, and send a copy of the form to the Student Employment Team .

- Contracts Required: A hiring form MUST be submitted by the supervisor, and a contract issued to the student, before work begins. Failure to do so may result in legal implications.

- Timesheet Submission Required: Timesheets are to be submitted by the student and approved by the supervisor promptly within three payment cycles . Further delay will require submitting an off-cycle payment approval form, and a series of DOA approvals. Please contact the assistantship team for more information.

- Pre-Approval Required for Grad Student Research Hires: Faculty intending to hire graduate degree students for research projects must be able to justify that the research work cannot be completed by an undergraduate student. The Office of Student Research will review requests before confirming appointments.

Student Work Schedule

- Student Employment Position Maximum: Students can work a maximum of TWO on-campus student employment positions at a time.

- Academic Year Maximum Hours: During the academic year, students are allowed to work for a maximum of 15 hours-per-week across positions.

- J-Term / Summer Course Maximum Hours: Students enrolled in J-Term in Abu Dhabi or the 4-week summer course can work for 10 hours per week for the duration of their course across positions.

- Maximum Hours Per Day: Student assistantship work hours should not exceed 7 hours a day. Hours worked beyond the maximum approved hours will not be compensated.

- Weekly Work Schedule Variable: Weekly work schedule will be determined by the student assistant and their supervisor based on the position’s requirements and the student’s availability.

Onboarding and Offboarding

- Reposting Positions on Handshake Each Year: Student Assistantship positions need to be posted on Handshake prior to hiring each academic year.

- New Hiring Forms Each Year: New hiring forms need to be submitted to hire students each AY; positions are not carried over from the previous year.

- Contract Validity: Assistantship contracts are valid for one academic year, and expire with the end of classes in the summer. Students enrolled in J-Term in Abu Dhabi or the 4-week summer course can carry on their assistantship for 10 hours per week during this period.

- Early Termination: In cases of students or supervisors looking to end an assistantship early, a two-week written notification is required prior to a mutually discussed last day of work.

- Poor Performance: Students underperforming in their assistantships should be sent a written warning notice addressing their deficiencies by the supervisor; failure to correct these after mutual discussion and a two-week notification can result in termination of the assistantship. The student employment team is to be immediately informed of these cases.

- Cause(s) for Immediate Termination: Student assistantship positions may be terminated immediately and without notice of a remedial period if the student commits a major offense including but not limited to theft and misconduct. Any incident involving documented misconduct may affect future hiring of the student through the program.

- Summer Research Hiring Cycle: To work in research positions during summer outside of classes, faculty need to hire students with fresh hiring forms through the Summer Research Assistant Program .

Payment Information

- Student Assistantships Paid Via Fixed Rate: All undergraduate students are paid a fixed rate of AED 38.5 / USD 10.48 an hour; Masters’ students are paid a set rate of AED 59 / USD 16.06 an hour.

- No Payment for Capstone Related Research: Student assistants should not be paid for research related to their Capstone projects.

- No Honorariums: Students cannot be paid by an honorarium.

- US Citizen Requirements: US citizens hired for assistantships will be contacted by the student employment team to fill out a W4 form on the Humanic platform. US citizenship holders (including dual citizenship with another country) are required to declare their US citizenship status at the time of hire. Failure to declare may lead to incorrect tax reporting and potential compliance issues for both the student and NYUAD

- Visiting Student Payments: Visiting students hired for assistantships will be issued FAB cards by the Student Finance Team on which they will receive their payments.

- Late Payments: Timesheets are to be submitted by the student and approved by the supervisor promptly within three payment cycles. Further delay will require submitting an off-cycle payment approval form, and a series of DOA approvals. Please contact the assistantship team for more information.

-

Payment Cycle

Student payments are processed bi-monthly as follows:

For hours worked from the 1st-12th of the month:

- Students complete their timesheets between the 12th-14th of the month.

- Supervisors must review and approve their timesheets by the 17th of the month.

- Students are expected to receive payment at the end of the month.

For hours worked from the 13th - end of the month:

- Students complete their timesheets between the 1st-3rd of the following month.

- Supervisors must review and approve their timesheets by the 6th of the month.

- Students are expected to receive payment in the middle of the month.

Please refer to the Payroll Cycle Cut-off Dates .

Delays in timely submission and approval of timesheets will result in delayed student payments.

sections.title: Assistantship Program
sections.text:
The Student Assistantship Program provides students at NYUAD with on-campus work experience opportunities within academic and administrative departments throughout the school year. The program, as part of a broader Student Employment Portfolio, is an integral part of students' professional preparation for off-campus and future opportunities. Through on-campus student employment, students earn money, develop transferable skill sets, and build capacity for institutional programs, projects, and research.

The program is open to undergraduate, master's, and visiting students. In all cases, students are only eligible when they are physically present and enrolled in classes at NYUAD.

Students can apply to available assistantship positions through Handshake .

sections.title: Student Eligibility Requirements
sections.text:
- Physical Presence: Students are required to be physically present and based at NYUAD, enrolled in classes, and in good disciplinary standing to be eligible. Remote work is not supported; therefore, students cannot continue an assistantship when they are abroad, studying away, or on a leave of absence.

- Minimum Age 18: Students must be at least 18 years old. If the student is under 18 years of age, they must download the Under 18 On-Campus Work Authorization Form , meet an advisor at the CDC to approve their assistantship and sign the form, and send a copy of the form to the Student Employment Team .

- Contracts Required: A hiring form MUST be submitted by the supervisor, and a contract issued to the student, before work begins. Failure to do so may result in legal implications.

- Timesheet Submission Required: Timesheets are to be submitted by the student and approved by the supervisor promptly within three payment cycles . Further delay will require submitting an off-cycle payment approval form, and a series of DOA approvals. Please contact the assistantship team for more information.

- Pre-Approval Required for Grad Student Research Hires: Faculty intending to hire graduate degree students for research projects must be able to justify that the research work cannot be completed by an undergraduate student. The Office of Student Research will review requests before confirming appointments.

sections.title: Student Work Schedule
sections.text:
- Student Employment Position Maximum: Students can work a maximum of TWO on-campus student employment positions at a time.

- Academic Year Maximum Hours: During the academic year, students are allowed to work for a maximum of 15 hours-per-week across positions.

- J-Term / Summer Course Maximum Hours: Students enrolled in J-Term in Abu Dhabi or the 4-week summer course can work for 10 hours per week for the duration of their course across positions.

- Maximum Hours Per Day: Student assistantship work hours should not exceed 7 hours a day. Hours worked beyond the maximum approved hours will not be compensated.

- Weekly Work Schedule Variable: Weekly work schedule will be determined by the student assistant and their supervisor based on the position’s requirements and the student’s availability.

sections.title: Onboarding and Offboarding
sections.text:
- Reposting Positions on Handshake Each Year: Student Assistantship positions need to be posted on Handshake prior to hiring each academic year.

- New Hiring Forms Each Year: New hiring forms need to be submitted to hire students each AY; positions are not carried over from the previous year.

- Contract Validity: Assistantship contracts are valid for one academic year, and expire with the end of classes in the summer. Students enrolled in J-Term in Abu Dhabi or the 4-week summer course can carry on their assistantship for 10 hours per week during this period.

- Early Termination: In cases of students or supervisors looking to end an assistantship early, a two-week written notification is required prior to a mutually discussed last day of work.

- Poor Performance: Students underperforming in their assistantships should be sent a written warning notice addressing their deficiencies by the supervisor; failure to correct these after mutual discussion and a two-week notification can result in termination of the assistantship. The student employment team is to be immediately informed of these cases.

- Cause(s) for Immediate Termination: Student assistantship positions may be terminated immediately and without notice of a remedial period if the student commits a major offense including but not limited to theft and misconduct. Any incident involving documented misconduct may affect future hiring of the student through the program.

- Summer Research Hiring Cycle: To work in research positions during summer outside of classes, faculty need to hire students with fresh hiring forms through the Summer Research Assistant Program .

sections.title: Payment Information
sections.text:
- Student Assistantships Paid Via Fixed Rate: All undergraduate students are paid a fixed rate of AED 38.5 / USD 10.48 an hour; Masters’ students are paid a set rate of AED 59 / USD 16.06 an hour.

- No Payment for Capstone Related Research: Student assistants should not be paid for research related to their Capstone projects.

- No Honorariums: Students cannot be paid by an honorarium.

- US Citizen Requirements: US citizens hired for assistantships will be contacted by the student employment team to fill out a W4 form on the Humanic platform. title: Degree Attestation · NYUAD Students
text:
Degree Attestation

Many countries, including the UAE, require your educational degrees to be attested, or verified, prior to you being able to work there. This can include high school, bachelor's, and other degrees. Depending on where your high school degree is from and where you want to work, the requirements and process to get your degrees attested will vary. This can take time and often requires original copies of your educational degrees. Parts of the process may require you to go to offices in the country where your high school degree was issued.

We strongly suggest you start thinking about this early and research the requirements for attestation of your high school and NYUAD degrees based on where you are from and what country(ies) you are considering employment in. We also suggest you get multiple original copies of your high school diploma in case you need that degree attested in multiple countries.

For the UAE you must apply for certificate equivalency through the Ministry of Education's website . The ministry has a live chat as well as a call number for any inquiries.

A Guide

As the degree attestation process varies greatly depending on high school curricula, country, and bureaucratic requirements, we are unable to provide a one-size-fits-all approach for NYUAD degree attestation. We have attempted, however, to organize the steps in a way that is representative of our Alumni experiences. The below steps are presented as a guide. We encourage you to use these resources to inform your preparation for degree attestation and for communicating with relevant stakeholders for your individual process. We also strongly recommend that you save all of the receipts involved in the process.

- Step 1: In Your High School Country

-
Collect Your High School Certificates (final 4 years are recommended).

-
Get these stamped by the Ministry of Education as proof that they are real. You could also ask the MoE for a letter stating that your school is real.

-
Take these stamped Certificates to the Ministry of Foreign Affairs to get them stamped again. This provides proof that the MoE stamps are real.

-
Take these stamped Certificates to the UAE Embassy in Your High School Country for them to attest them.

-
The next step after UAE Embassy Attestation of Your High School Certificates takes place within the UAE.

- Step 2: In Abu Dhabi

-
Collate Your stamped High School Certifications.

-
Take them to the UAE Ministry of Foreign Affairs and International Cooperation in Abu Dhabi. Here they will attest that the UAE Embassy in Your High School country is real.

-
Upon graduating, take your High School Certifications AND your original NYUAD Diploma, Official Transcripts, and Graduation Letter from Registrar, to the UAE Ministry of Education. You will also need to make an online application on their system: moe.gov.ae/En/EServices/ ServiceCard/Equ/Pages/ RequiredDocs.aspx

-
Once they have processed, return to the MoE with NYUAD diploma for stamp.

-
Take Your NYUAD Diploma to the Ministry of Foreign Affairs for final stamp.

Useful Links

As we continue to explore the process and experiences of degree attestation in the UAE, we want to bring to focus the material that has already been created and utilized by our community:
Gazelle Article
NYUAD Facebook Forum (Facebook page)
Student Portal
IB Attestation Questions (email)

- Attestation Service Provider: BVS Global

BVS Global is a service provider that has recently been used to attest the NYUAD Diploma in the UAE Embassy in Washington D.C., U.S.A. They may be able to attest the NYUAD Diploma without the need for High School Certificate Attestation, and so could be another way to attest your NYUAD Diploma without going through the traditional process. We cannot guarantee that this is the case, but we encourage you to investigate further using the information below:

-
BVS Global

-
www.bvsglobal.com

-
NYUAD Contact:
Email: nyuad@bvsglobal.com
Mobile number: +971 50 124 3388

Related official links:
https://students.nyuad.nyu.edu/campus-life/career-development/job-search/degree-attestation/

title: FAQs · NYUAD Students
text:
- How many hours can I intern?

During the academic year, first year students can work 10 hours per week, second year students can work 15 hours per week, and juniors and seniors can work up to 20 hours per week.

- When can I do an internship? Do they have to be during the summer?

NYUAD students have the option of completing internships in the UAE during any time of the year, including the academic year. During the summers, students can intern anywhere they receive a legitimate offer. You can also pursue internships during study abroad. For all internships, on- or off-campus, students are REQUIRED to fill out a Mentor Approval form and attend a CDC Orientation.

- Can I be paid?

Employers can remunerate interns at their discretion. Notably, the majority of employers who host internships do not offer a salary, but students are encouraged to request reimbursement or a stipend to cover travel expenses.

- Where have other students interned?

Students intern all around the world. Explore what they have done through this interactive internship map .

- Handshake doesn't have jobs or internships I like, what should I do?

Email the Career Development Center team ! We want to help you find the experience you want and need in order to make your post-graduate dreams a reality.

- What is a CV book?

CV books are one avenue for external employers to engage with NYUAD students. Student participation is entirely optional and students are required to have their CVs approved by a counselor prior to submission. Employers often request CV books as a way of reviewing a lot of candidates with a common interest very quickly. For some employers, this streamlines the process, as they are able to recruit for multinational sites without posting a job for each individual location. CV book deadlines are announced in advance and late submissions are not accepted.

- What is a Ministry of Labor Letter or a No Objection Letter? Why do I need one?

NYUAD students are sponsored by the university while they are in the UAE. Subsequently, students engaged in any off site internship must fill out the Opportunities Survey so that the CDC can issue a No-Objection Letter. This letter informs the Ministry of Labor of NYUAD's consent to the intern's placement off campus.

- How do I get a letter of support or a no-objection letter for my internship?

There are a few common letters asked or required by employers for internships.

No Objection Letter: This is legally required by the UAE Ministry of Labor for all off-campus internships in the UAE. It is requested by completing the Opportunities Survey, and selecting off-campus and the UAE as the location. You will be asked for internship start and end-date, your internship offer letter, and supervisor details.

Support Letter: Also called a no-contest certificate, is a letter issued by the University demonstrating that we support you in pursuing your internship. These letters can be required by the employer during the recruitment process. It is requested by completing the Opportunities Survey, and selecting "Support Letter" under the Internship Letters section of the survey. Employers sometimes have different requirements for this letter, so be sure to briefly describe it in the Opportunities Survey.

If you require a Support Letter during the recruitment process for an off-campus internship in the UAE, and you do not know the details for your No Objection Letter (start and end-date, supervisor details, offer letter), you will have to complete this survey twice. Once to get the Support Letter in order to complete the recruitment process, and a second time after receiving the internship offer to provide us with your supervisor details so we can issue the No Objection Letter.

- Do I have to intern?

Internships are not a requirement at any point, just strongly encouraged. For the student considering working full time, 71 percent of employers indicated that they wanted to hire students with previous relevant experience in internships. For the students considering graduate or professional school, internships provide a unique chance to get exposure to the intended profession, which can provide valuable feedback and inform future decision-making.

- Does the CDC fund travel to and from internships?

Unfortunately the CDC does not have the budget to fund student travel to and from internship sites. Students are encouraged to use their stipend and share taxis, take local buses, and be creative about ways to travel at low costs. Additionally, students can ask employers to help cover some of their travel expenses.

title: Internships · NYUAD Students
text:
Work-related experiences like jobs and internships bridge the gap between what you learn in class and the world of work. They help:

- Clarify your interests and options

- Improve your employability

- Build a network of professional relationships

- Understand workplace culture and expectations

- Learn field-specific skills

- Shape the applications of classroom knowledge

The Internship Process at NYUAD

When looking to gain work experience, be sure to follow the NYUAD internship process . This is important for you to get the most of your experiences, for university accreditation and reputation, as well as to comply with legal requirements. The full process is detailed on our Job Search page .

Steps to a Successful Search

- Define What You Want

Start out by asking yourself some questions about your interests, skills, and values. What you like, what you’re capable of, and what you care about will shape the possibilities and provide context for your search.

- Questions to ask yourself (see section below)

- Consult with a career advisor

- Know the Basics

Get acquainted with the options for work experience and NYUAD guidelines so you can pursue what works best for you and have the best experience possible.

- Get a sense of expectations and ethics at the (required) CDC orientation.

- Understand the difference between full-time jobs, part-time jobs, internships, and on-campus employment .

- Investigate the timeline for hiring in your area of interest and the industry layout. Use our industry maps to help get started here. They are available in our office or in the callout on the right.

- Upgrade your Tools and Skills

Focus some energy on your messaging — how you tell your story (out loud or on paper), how you make a first impression, and how you leverage the internet.

- Update your CV and cover letter .

- Brush up on professional etiquette.

- Establish a strategic social networking presence, with appropriate privacy settings.

- Consider how you will market your degree and your global experiences.

- Connect with a career advisor for feedback.

- Plan Your Search and Stay Productive

Diversify your search activities so you have balance between the energizing and draining aspects of the search. Plans help you pace yourself and involving people keeps you accountable to your goals.

- Establish a timeline and system to keep track of your activities.

- Create your 30 second introduction or self-marketing pitch.

- Develop a network of contacts in your field of interest, connect with NYUAD Alumni.

- Consider the breadth of your applications. How many opportunities should you be applying to? Probably more than you think.

- Strive to craft personalized CVs and cover letters for different opportunities to communicate depth of intention and interest.

- Locate Opportunities

You only need one yes, but getting there takes creativity, intentionality, and commitment. Depending on your industry of interest and the hiring timeline, you can expect to use very different resources. However, you can be sure that your search will have some blend of relationship-building (actual people you are meeting in the field) and online postings.

- Handshake : Apply to positions posted by employers targeting NYUAD talent.

- External Search Engines: Try the following search engines if you don't find jobs or internships that suit you on Handshake . Or reach out to our office and we can help you cold contact the employer, or develop a relationship with them to encourage them to post positions with us. Visit aggregate search websites for publicly posted opportunities.

- Our suggested search engines to start with:

- LinkedIn Job Search

- Indeed.com

- Idealist.org

- Catholic Volunteer Network (open to all, not just for Christians)

- Bayt.com

- Milkround.com

- Gulftalent.com

- Extended list of job and internship search resources

- Connect with professionals in the field of interest to explore hidden opportunities (around 80% of jobs are filled through relational connections).

- Follow relevant thought leaders and organizations on social media.

- Follow up in a couple weeks after applying to ask about the status of your application and if you can provide any additional materials or information.

- Practice Interviewing

Revisit your messaging in the interview context. While you can’t anticipate exact questions, practicing can help you develop flow, confidence, and agility.

- Conduct a mock interview with a career advisor or via Big Interview .

- Understand interview basics and etiquette.

- Report and Reflect on Your Experience

Successfully securing an opportunity is a huge accomplishment, so take time to celebrate. Report your experience to us so future students can benefit. When your experience concludes, make sure to review what you learned and integrate your experience into your next steps.

- Report your opportunity via the Opportunities Survey .

- Reflect on what you have learned and review next steps with a career advisor .

- Update your CV with the most meaningful aspects of your new role.

Questions to Ask Yourself

- Exploring Opportunities

- What do I like and dislike?

- What am I good at?

- Do my likes and dislikes align with the opportunity I am seeking?

- What is motivating me to pursue this?

- What are the job prospects?

- What kind of life can I have with this career?

- Where do I find these opportunities?

- How well do I know the organizations that hire for these roles?

- How do I best prepare?

- What have my peers done ?

- Engaging in Work Experience

- What do I hope to accomplish in this work experience?

- What are my expectations of this experience?

- Who have I communicated my goals and expectations to?

- Do you feel like you fit at the organization? Why or why not?

- How has your perception of the work environment or job changed since you started?

- What steps have you taken to address the challenges and disappointments that you have observed?

- What is surprising?

- What have you contributed?

- What have you done that has made your supervisor’s life easier?

- In what ways do you feel like you can improve your performance?

- Post-Experience

- What have you done that you didn’t ever think you’d be able to do?

- How did you change as a result of this experience?

- What was your biggest success?

- Were your expectations for this experience realistic? Why or why not?

- How would you describe what you learned about your work style?

- What did you learn from the challenges you experienced?

- How do you want your supervisor to remember you?

- Have you identified any skills or areas that you would like to further develop?

- What transferrable skills did you develop?

- How has this experience impacted your goals?
