- Establish a strategic social networking presence, with appropriate privacy settings.

- Consider how you will market your degree and your global experiences.

- Connect with a career advisor for feedback.

- Plan Your Search and Stay Productive

Diversify your search activities so you have balance between the energizing and draining aspects of the search. Plans help you pace yourself and involving people keeps you accountable to your goals.

- Establish a timeline and system to keep track of your activities.

- Create your 30 second introduction or self-marketing pitch.

- Develop a network of contacts in your field of interest, connect with NYUAD Alumni.

- Consider the breadth of your applications. How many opportunities should you be applying to? Probably more than you think.

- Strive to craft personalized CVs and cover letters for different opportunities to communicate depth of intention and interest.

- Locate Opportunities

You only need one yes, but getting there takes creativity, intentionality, and commitment. Depending on your industry of interest and the hiring timeline, you can expect to use very different resources. However, you can be sure that your search will have some blend of relationship-building (actual people you are meeting in the field) and online postings.

- Handshake : Apply to positions posted by employers targeting NYUAD talent.

- External Search Engines: Try the following search engines if you don't find jobs or internships that suit you on Handshake . Or reach out to our office and we can help you cold contact the employer, or develop a relationship with them to encourage them to post positions with us. Visit aggregate search websites for publicly posted opportunities.

- Our suggested search engines to start with:

- LinkedIn Job Search

- Indeed.com

- Idealist.org

- Catholic Volunteer Network (open to all, not just for Christians)

- Bayt.com

- Milkround.com

- Gulftalent.com

- Extended list of job and internship search resources

- Connect with professionals in the field of interest to explore hidden opportunities (around 80% of jobs are filled through relational connections).

- Follow relevant thought leaders and organizations on social media.

- Follow up in a couple weeks after applying to ask about the status of your application and if you can provide any additional materials or information.

- Practice Interviewing

Revisit your messaging in the interview context. While you can’t anticipate exact questions, practicing can help you develop flow, confidence, and agility.

- Conduct a mock interview with a career advisor or via Big Interview .

- Understand interview basics and etiquette.

- Report and Reflect on Your Experience

Successfully securing an opportunity is a huge accomplishment, so take time to celebrate. Report your experience to us so future students can benefit. When your experience concludes, make sure to review what you learned and integrate your experience into your next steps.

- Report your opportunity via the Opportunities Survey .

- Reflect on what you have learned and review next steps with a career advisor .

- Update your CV with the most meaningful aspects of your new role.

sections.title: Questions to Ask Yourself
sections.text:
- Exploring Opportunities

- What do I like and dislike?

- What am I good at?

- Do my likes and dislikes align with the opportunity I am seeking?

- What is motivating me to pursue this?

- What are the job prospects?

- What kind of life can I have with this career?

- Where do I find these opportunities?

- How well do I know the organizations that hire for these roles?

- How do I best prepare?

- What have my peers done ?

- Engaging in Work Experience

- What do I hope to accomplish in this work experience?

- What are my expectations of this experience?

- Who have I communicated my goals and expectations to?

- Do you feel like you fit at the organization? Why or why not?

- How has your perception of the work environment or job changed since you started?

- What steps have you taken to address the challenges and disappointments that you have observed?

- What is surprising?

- What have you contributed?

- What have you done that has made your supervisor’s life easier?

- In what ways do you feel like you can improve your performance?

- Post-Experience

- What have you done that you didn’t ever think you’d be able to do?

- How did you change as a result of this experience?

- What was your biggest success?

- Were your expectations for this experience realistic? Why or why not?

- How would you describe what you learned about your work style?

- What did you learn from the challenges you experienced?

- How do you want your supervisor to remember you?

- Have you identified any skills or areas that you would like to further develop?

- What transferrable skills did you develop?

- How has this experience impacted your goals?

title: Work Experiences · NYUAD Students
text:
There are many ways to gain professional experience while a student. Below outlines the primary categories. These can all be completed on or off campus. Help us celebrate your achievements and maintain our internship map by completing the Opportunities Survey for every opportunity you complete.

Internships

Internships are temporary positions that provide a learning experience within a professional setting.

Internships are a great way to gain experience, learn about a company or industry, build your network, and explore potential career paths. Many organizations prefer to hire full-time positions from their interns, so it may fast-track you to a job. Through an internship you will:

- Develop the ability to receive and respond to feedback in a professional setting

- Build a network of professional relationships related to a field of interest

- Gain understanding of workplace culture and expectations

- Receive training and support from your supervisor regarding specific tasks

- Discern whether or not the field of the internship is a viable career option

Be sure to follow the internship process when pursuing these opportunities!

- On-campus Internships

NYUAD departments regularly take on interns and assistants (see details on assistantships below). On-campus internships provide an avenue for students to gain meaningful professional experiences in a relatively familiar environment. For a list of current on-campus internships, please view the current internship postings in NYUAD CareerNet.

- Off-campus Internships

Off-campus internships can help students build their network, and organizations are more likely to offer full time positions to former interns. Over 70% of employers prefer to hire candidates with relevant work/internship experiences. While more than 200 off-campus internships were posted on NYUAD CareerNet in the past year across a variety of industries, the majority of internships that exist are found through networking.

For internships when studying away , check out these NYU pages to help get your search started. Please note that your point of contact for questions or a further discussion should still be the CDC, Global Education, and your faculty mentor.

Internship Guidelines

- Payment

The CDC does NOT provide funding for internships other than through the Summer Internship Grant , which is a competitive, supplemental grant to pursue internships during the summer months only. Employers will sometimes provide a stipend to cover travel/commuting expenses or meals, but it is not guaranteed.

- Internship Hours

- First Years: up to 10 hours per week

- Sophomores: up to 15 hours per week

- Juniors: up to 20 hours per week

- Seniors: up to 20 hours per week

- Internship Criteria

Internships must have:

- Learning objectives/goals related to your academic coursework, professional, and/or personal goals

- Supervision by a professional with routine feedback

- A defined beginning and end

- A length of about 3-12 weeks

- Internship Location

Internships can be pursued anywhere in the world given that you are able to make it happen. Some internships can also be completed remotely. Internships can also be pursued during your study away semester(s). Learn more about the process for study away internships on NYU's Study Away Internships page .

Part-Time Jobs

- On-Campus Student Assistantships

Many offices offer paid on-campus positions called student assistantships. The Student Assistantship Program provides you the opportunity to earn money through part-time, hourly jobs in campus administration or operations. You must be a currently matriculated student, on the Abu Dhabi campus. Assistantships can last for up to 10 months at a time.

Student assistantships are NOT designed to replace on-campus internships or undergraduate research assistantships . Assistantship roles do not involve the same developmental or training aspects of internships, and there is a stipend attached of 30 AED/hour.

Student assistantships provide you with hands-on, practical work experience. However, the work does not need to be in a field related to your major and/or aligned to your career interests.

- Off-Campus Part Time Jobs

Students will sometimes pursue jobs, often during the summer, to earn money. Part time jobs provide professional experience and are generally not tied to learning objectives or career goals.

Any job experience while an NYUAD student should be reported through the Opportunities Survey .

Research

Research is generally conducted under the supervision of a faculty member. See the Undergraduate Research Program page to learn how you can get involved. Be sure to still report your research experience through the Opportunities Survey !

Volunteerism

Volunteering and service-based learning are great ways to get involved in the community. See the Community Outreach pages to learn how you can get involved.

Entrepreneurial Venture

Entrepreneurship is the process of designing, launching, and running a new business. StartAD can help connect you with other students, faculty, researchers and the wider community to catalyze innovative and technology centered ventures. Be sure to still report your entrepreneurial experience through the Opportunities Survey !

Creative Production or Performance

Creative productions and performances is the creation of, or participation in, an artistic work. The Theater Program puts on annual student shows, and students completing artistic capstones often ask for help from their peers. Be sure to still report your artistic experience through the Opportunities Survey !

title: Conflict Transformation · NYUAD Students
text:
Our Mission

The Center for Student Belonging's Conflict Transformation pillar work seeks the expansion of proactive conflict transformation strategies to promote conflict competence within the greater NYUAD campus community. Rather than merely addressing conflicts as they arise we are proactively delivering ongoing training to empower students to skill-fully navigate conflicts in complex intercultural contexts.

Our Programs and Workshops

- Intercultural Conflict Styles (ICS) Workshop

The Intercultural Conflict Style Inventory® (ICS®) is the leading, cross-culturally valid assessment tool for identifying core approaches to improving communication, resolving conflicts and solving problems across cultural differences. We host workshops on the ICS which are designed to facilitate awareness around one's on conflict style and increase individual's competence at bridging differences across different conflict styles.

- Restorative Practices

Restorative Practices deal with conflicts by emphasizing student's accountability for their actions, understanding the broader impacts to the campus community and actively developing their conflict competency. Often contrasted with more punitive approaches to addressing breaks in community harmony through their behaviour, Restorative Practice's primary goal is to restore healthy community interaction and mindful ethics and behaviour.

Our programs use restorative practices proactively to build a restorative community culture on campus. This proactive effort includes a shared commitment to fostering positive relationships based on respect, empathy, accountability, and belonging. It also includes the intentional implementation of specific restorative tools, namely the restorative circle process.

- Student Leader Trainings

These trainings focus on developing student knowledge, skills and abilities in the areas of conflict transformation. Some of the group that have received this training include; Resident Assistants, WEYAK, REACH, Student Government, Identity SIGs etc. If you are interested in receiving a training for your student group, please email @nyuad.conflicttransformation@nyu.edu to inquire about specialised trainings.

- Conflict Transformation Consultation

title: Restorative Practice Ambassador (RPA) · NYUAD Students
text:
Restorative Practice Ambassadors (RPA), a leadership development program that focuses on building students’ conflict competence, a core leadership and life skill for NYUAD and beyond. The RPAs will be ambassadors of cultivating a campus culture of proactive conflict transformation.

The RPA role is designed to equip students with the leadership skills and confidence to effectively manage conflicts that arise in everyday life and as part of being in a uniquely diverse global campus community. They are student leaders who have been trained to create a safe space for talking through difficult issues, to assist peers to better understand each other, and find their own solutions. They will help students clarify what is important, understand how they are being impacted by a difficult situation, and discuss options for creating peaceful solutions. Examples of common conflicts RPAs will address include; roommate conflicts, communication challenges between peers, conflicts among SIG leaders and members, student to student conflicts, etc.

The RPAs will be trained to provide one to one individual conflict coaching to their peers, facilitate peer to peer mediations and interpersonal dialogue, and educate other students in conflict transformation practices. This role generally works within a conflict transformation framework; an alternative approach to resolving disputes that views conflict as an opportunity for growth, leadership development and community building.

Contact: nyuad.conflicttransformation@nyu.edu

title: Intercultural Education · NYUAD Students
text:
Our Programs and Workshops

- Sustained Dialogue

Sustained Dialogue is an initiative designed to create a 'brave space' where students can connect, practice empathy and vulnerability, and lean into differences on a range of sensitive topics in a cohort of their peers. Sustained Dialogue seeks to transform perspectives through meaningful dialogue by creating opportunities for students to convey and exchange not just their opinions about thought provoking matters, but also share their personal stories and life experiences in a judgment free zone. Sustained Dialogue Ambassadors (DA) are students who are trained facilitators that co-lead semester long dialogue cohorts.

- Student Leader Trainings

These trainings focus on developing student knowledge, skills and abilities in the areas of intercultural awareness and cultural understanding. Some of the group that have received this training include; Resident Assistants, WEYAK leaders, REACH, Student Government, Culture Student Clubs etc. If you are interested in receiving a training for your student group, please email @nyuad.interculturaled@nyu.edu to inquire about specialised trainings.

title: Meaning Making and Purpose · NYUAD Students
text:
Meaning Making and Purpose

In Meaning Making and Purpose, we encourage students to explore pathways toward meaning making, their values and aim to create conditions for greater self-awareness and understanding of collective truths.

Our Programs and Workshops

- Mindfulness Mondays

It is a program crafted to create a space to breath, meditate and connect to community and well-being. It is held on the first and the third Monday of every month in the Serenity Room.

- Journeying Within

Interested in learning how to cultivate your own spirituality? Looking to becoming more spiritually aware and in tune with your sense of identity?

Join the Department of Spiritual Life, InterCultural Education and Conflict Transformation (SLICECT) in a 4-part series on spirituality, meaning making, spiritual practices, connection, and values.

This training will focus on experiential learning as well as introducing various frameworks and concepts in spirituality and spiritual practice

- Ramadan

SLICECT helps to organize Ramadan programs in collaboration with other departments such as the Office of Inclusion and Equity, and Community Outreach.

- Religious Sites Visit

Students are given opportunities to visit various religious sites and explore their spiritual traditions. In the past, students have visited the Abrahamic Family House, Sheikh Zayed Grand Mosque, Dubai Temples, etc.

- Crisis Support in Difficult Times

Coaching and support for impacted students on matters pertaining to personal/collective values and spirituality when navigating global crises and difficult times; facilitating one-on-one coaching and group-based work in dean's outreach program; facilitating grief spaces for students as needed on an ongoing basis. To book a session a session, email nyuad.spirituallife@nyu.edu .

- Jubail Mangrove Mindfulness Walk

This walk will entail mindfulness within ourselves, those around us, and our environment. You will have a moment to connect and explore the pleasant landscape, to feel the subtle beauty of nature around us, and to feel reconnected with the environment without any distractions.

- NYU Global Spiritual Advisors

Because students at NYUAD are often far from their home faith communities, NYU New York Chaplains are available to speak with students via phone or video conference. Our Student Life advisors and local affiliates are also available for pastoral care and support. This may include comfort in times of sorrow, prayer in times of need, and conversation regarding spiritual reflection and vocational discernment.

Spaces of Worship

Coexistence Board Student Clubs

Belonging and Purpose Ambassadors (BPA)

- Muslim Prayer Rooms

We have six prayer rooms (three rooms for male worshipers, and three rooms for femal e worshipers). They are located in the Campus Center (C2), Conference Center (A6), and A1. They are open at all times.

title: Civic Engagement and Service · NYUAD Students
text:
Building Bridges, Community, and Impact

Civic Engagement and Service (formerly Community Outreach) builds bridges between NYUAD and the UAE through cultural, outreach, and volunteer engagements. We offer a wide range of programs that connect you with your community, support civic engagement, and promote ethical, inclusive leadership grounded in the UAE’s rich diversity.

Our goal is to help you grow, give back, and lead with purpose.

"SNAP was the class I always looked forward to the most every week, it was a moment where I could focus on others more than myself, work with a team, and learn from everybody on the court, from the coach to the parents and from my friends and mainly the kids. This experience made me realize that sometimes the smallest actions are the ones that count the most, and that fulfill you the most at the end of the day."
-- lian Contreras Ruvalcaba, Class of 2026

“As an Emirati, I learned so much from this trip about the nuances between the cultures of different tribes in the UAE. Being able to first-hand witness the musical practices, homes, dances, food and lives of the Shehhi tribe helped me truly reflect on the diversity that exists in our UAE community.”
-- Sarah Alkaabi, NYUAD Class of 2020, Reflecting on Kashtah trip to Dibbah

“Volunteering through the help of community outreach has never been more supportive and successful. Forming lifelong memories and impacts, especially with children with special needs is not just a great opportunity but a privilege. I hope that we, as students at NYUAD, see the amazing potential and opportunities we have to use volunteering as a conduit of change.”
-- Munib Mesinovic, Class of 2020, Rhodes Scholar, Reflecting on volunteering at the Future Centre

title: Get Involved · NYUAD Students
text:
Whether you have an hour or a semester, we’ll help you find opportunities that match your interests, values, and availability. From one-time events to long-term projects, there’s space for everyone to contribute, learn, and grow.

Step by Step: How to Volunteer as an NYUAD Student

- Explore Opportunities

Check out our current volunteering opportunities on Linktree . From one-time events to ongoing programs, there’s always something happening, and we’re constantly adding new ways to get involved.

- Attend Orientation

While not required, we strongly encourage students to attend the Volunteer and Impact Orientation hosted by Civic Engagement and Service at the start of each semester. It’s a great way to get grounded in our guiding principles, explore current programs, and learn what meaningful service at NYUAD looks like.

- Training and Preparation

Volunteering works best when you’re prepared. Many of our service programs include built-in training to help you understand the community context, build relevant skills, and engage respectfully and effectively. We also offer standalone workshops throughout the year based on the needs of different projects and partners.

- People of Determination (POD) Support with Fatma Al Jassim

- Tutoring Best Practices with Nancy Gleason

- Working with Learners with Different Needs with Special Olympics & Applied Behavioral Training Institute (ABTI)

- Teaching English as a Second Language (TESOL) with Eton Institute

- Storytelling for Impact with Carole Chapelier

- Volunteer Guidelines and Responsibilities

Volunteering through Civic Engagement and Service comes with a shared commitment to the causes, people, and communities you are working with. When you join a program, you are expected to fully participate, from training and reflection to giving feedback at the end.

We expect volunteers to follow through on their commitments. If you’re unable to continue, communicate early. Disengaging without notice erodes trust and may affect future participation. If a program isn’t completed, the experience should not be listed on your resume or CV. Full participation is required for the experience to be formally recognized.

This values-based agreement outlines what we ask of every NYUAD volunteer.

- Time: Show up on time, avoid scheduling conflicts, and be realistic about what you can commit to. It’s better to do less with care than to overextend yourself.

- Mindset: Stay curious, engaged, and open to new experiences, even when things don’t feel familiar or go as expected.

- Accountability: Honor your commitments. Your presence matters to the people and communities you are working with.

- Communication: Let us know as soon as you can if an emergency, challenge, or change in your commitment arises, so we can support you and keep everyone informed.

- Collaboration: Keep in touch with your peers! Sometimes that means a quick Zoom or five-minute check-in to keep everyone on the same track.

- Respect: Protect the privacy of community members. Always get permission before taking photos or posting publicly on social media.

- Flexibility: Even the best-laid plans can shift on the ground. Be prepared to adapt to unpredictable or unplanned situations.

- Commitment: Follow your chosen program through from orientation and training to service, reflection, and feedback. Your full participation respects the people and effort that make it possible.

- Storytelling for Change

Your act of volunteering with a community may end, but your power to continue being an advocate and champion for change does not. We encourage you to actively find ways to be a lifelong ambassador for the causes that are most important to you.

Volunteers can share their stories to educate, inform, and inspire: tag @nyuadoutreach on Instagram, contribute a testimonial for our email newsletters , or collaborate with us on a short blog or video reflection of your experience.

- Resources

Below you will find a list of online resources related to philanthropy, volunteerism, and humanitarian issues. We encourage you to browse through to broaden and deepen your understanding of local and global contexts and explore the intersections of social good and global development. By no means an exhaustive list, but a starting point to explore issues that resonate most with you individually.

UAE Resources

- Volunteers.ae — UAE Volunteering Platform

- Ma’an Abu Dhabi — Authority of Social Contribution

- Emirates Red Crescent

- Dubai Cares

- Dubai Humanitarian

Global Resources on Philanthropy, Service, and Social Impact

- Guardian Global Development

- Stanford Social Innovation Review

- Huffington Post Impact

- NonProfit Quarterly

- CNN Global Heroes

- Chronicle of Philanthropy

- Forbes Philanthropy

- Wall Street Journal Philanthropy

- UC Berkeley’s Greater Good Science Center

Careers in Global Development

- Devex

- Net Impact

- Idealist.org

NYUAD Resources

- Virtual Do Good Guide : Compiled in response to COVID-19, this interactive hub from Civic Engagement & Service gathers resources for remote learning and social-impact action.

- If you are interested in internships, part time, or full time employment opportunities within social impact, be sure to make a career counseling appointment with the Career Development Center . You can also browse their industry resources .

"Surprisingly, university can at times make your vision tunneled. You get consumed into the workload and managing classes that the true meaning of acquiring an education becomes lost. When I volunteered, I gained perspective on what it is that I am trying to do with my degree. I first thought that I was volunteering because people needed me, but I then came to the realization that it was me who was in need of this experience."
-- Shamsa Al Najjar, Class of 2020

“Through the training, Fatma revolutionized my thinking by teaching me new modes of conceptualizing and understanding the experiences of people of determination. This opened my eyes to the many ways in which our environment is implicitly and explicitly ableist, broadening my perspective and allowing me to critically reflect on the nature of the world around me.”
-- Athena Thomas, Class of 2020, People of Determination Support Training

Volunteering works best when you’re prepared. Many of our service programs include built-in training to help you understand the community context, build relevant skills, and engage respectfully and effectively. We also offer standalone workshops throughout the year based on the needs of different projects and partners.

- People of Determination (POD) Support with Fatma Al Jassim

- Tutoring Best Practices with Nancy Gleason

- Working with Learners with Different Needs with Special Olympics & Applied Behavioral Training Institute (ABTI)

- Teaching English as a Second Language (TESOL) with Eton Institute

- Storytelling for Impact with Carole Chapelier

- Volunteer Guidelines and Responsibilities

Volunteering through Civic Engagement and Service comes with a shared commitment to the causes, people, and communities you are working with. When you join a program, you are expected to fully participate, from training and reflection to giving feedback at the end.

We expect volunteers to follow through on their commitments. If you’re unable to continue, communicate early. Disengaging without notice erodes trust and may affect future participation. If a program isn’t completed, the experience should not be listed on your resume or CV. Full participation is required for the experience to be formally recognized.

This values-based agreement outlines what we ask of every NYUAD volunteer.

- Time: Show up on time, avoid scheduling conflicts, and be realistic about what you can commit to. It’s better to do less with care than to overextend yourself.

- Mindset: Stay curious, engaged, and open to new experiences, even when things don’t feel familiar or go as expected.

- Accountability: Honor your commitments. Your presence matters to the people and communities you are working with.

- Communication: Let us know as soon as you can if an emergency, challenge, or change in your commitment arises, so we can support you and keep everyone informed.

- Collaboration: Keep in touch with your peers! Sometimes that means a quick Zoom or five-minute check-in to keep everyone on the same track.

- Respect: Protect the privacy of community members. Always get permission before taking photos or posting publicly on social media.

- Flexibility: Even the best-laid plans can shift on the ground. Be prepared to adapt to unpredictable or unplanned situations.

- Commitment: Follow your chosen program through from orientation and training to service, reflection, and feedback. Your full participation respects the people and effort that make it possible.

- Storytelling for Change

Your act of volunteering with a community may end, but your power to continue being an advocate and champion for change does not. We encourage you to actively find ways to be a lifelong ambassador for the causes that are most important to you.

Volunteers can share their stories to educate, inform, and inspire: tag @nyuadoutreach on Instagram, contribute a testimonial for our email newsletters , or collaborate with us on a short blog or video reflection of your experience.

- Resources

Below you will find a list of online resources related to philanthropy, volunteerism, and humanitarian issues. We encourage you to browse through to broaden and deepen your understanding of local and global contexts and explore the intersections of social good and global development. By no means an exhaustive list, but a starting point to explore issues that resonate most with you individually.

UAE Resources

- Volunteers.ae — UAE Volunteering Platform

- Ma’an Abu Dhabi — Authority of Social Contribution

- Emirates Red Crescent

- Dubai Cares

- Dubai Humanitarian

Global Resources on Philanthropy, Service, and Social Impact

- Guardian Global Development

- Stanford Social Innovation Review

- Huffington Post Impact

- NonProfit Quarterly

- CNN Global Heroes

- Chronicle of Philanthropy

- Forbes Philanthropy

- Wall Street Journal Philanthropy

- UC Berkeley’s Greater Good Science Center

Careers in Global Development

- Devex

- Net Impact

- Idealist.org

NYUAD Resources

- Virtual Do Good Guide : Compiled in response to COVID-19, this interactive hub from Civic Engagement & Service gathers resources for remote learning and social-impact action.

- If you are interested in internships, part time, or full time employment opportunities within social impact, be sure to make a career counseling appointment with the Career Development Center . You can also browse their industry resources .

"Surprisingly, university can at times make your vision tunneled. You get consumed into the workload and managing classes that the true meaning of acquiring an education becomes lost. When I volunteered, I gained perspective on what it is that I am trying to do with my degree. I first thought that I was volunteering because people needed me, but I then came to the realization that it was me who was in need of this experience."
-- Shamsa Al Najjar, Class of 2020

“Through the training, Fatma revolutionized my thinking by teaching me new modes of conceptualizing and understanding the experiences of people of determination. This opened my eyes to the many ways in which our environment is implicitly and explicitly ableist, broadening my perspective and allowing me to critically reflect on the nature of the world around me.”
-- Athena Thomas, Class of 2020, People of Determination Support Training

title: Intern with Us · NYUAD Students
text:
Civic Engagement and Service offers competitive paid student assistantships. Our ‘impact internship’ cohort program is a rewarding and immersive opportunity that engages students as builders, collaborators and drivers of key outreach programs. We encourage you to get involved as much as possible with volunteer programs to enhance your application.

Applications usually open in advance to the start of each academic term, and job listings can be found on Handshake (login required).

Civic Engagement and Service interns

“As an intern with Community Outreach, I loved finding new ways to connect NYUAD with the Abu Dhabi community. The freedom and responsibility of the position allowed me to combine my work with my passions. It was a privilege to play a role in the important work Community Outreach does within NYUAD and the city.”
-- Annalisa Galgano, Class of 2017

“I feel better prepared for what I hope to do in the future. Community Outreach cemented my passion for service and helped me realize the importance of connecting people within and across communities. My internship taught me more about Abu Dhabi — my home — and for that I am forever grateful.”
-- Sofia Gomez Doyle, Class of 2018

Reach Out to Us for Advice or with New Ideas

In addition to interning with us, we also serve as a resource for student leaders interested in connecting with community-based organizations in meaningful ways. Interested in discussing a new community project proposal? Want to expand your SIG into the UAE community? Seeking connections for your Capstone related to social impact? Know you want to make a positive and lasting impact but are not sure how? We are here to help.

Contact nyuad.civic.engagement@nyu.edu . We look forward to hearing from you.

title: Service and Impact · NYUAD Students
text:
We believe volunteering is a powerful starting point for becoming an advocate and agent of change. You’ll join local initiatives, meet people from different backgrounds, connect with communities across the UAE and beyond, and take part in hands-on experiences that let you learn by doing.

When supported by reflection and mutual learning, volunteering becomes service: an experience where you grow with the communities you serve and deepen your understanding of the world around you.

There are many ways you can get involved, and we’re here to help guide you on your journey.

Video: Students return to Liwa season after season — planting, harvesting, and giving back — while learning from local communities and exploring the UAE’s cultural heritage.

Andrew Riad, Class of 2022, shares what inspired him to become active in the lives of children of determination and what he gained from the experience.

Why Get Involved?

- Connect classroom learning to purposeful action.

- Expand your community networks outside of NYUAD.

- Develop a stronger sense of belonging with Abu Dhabi and your new home.

- Cultivate a deeper understanding of global citizenship and social impact work.

- Enhanced well-being: working to help others boosts motivation and performance and can counteract the effects of stress, isolation and anxiety

- A safe and accessible way to learn about diverse and lesser visible communities

- Gain important CV building experience.

- Build important skills that will help you thrive in your future such as: complex problem solving, creativity, critical thinking, coordinating with others and emotional intelligence.

- Make a positive impact on your community and the world.

title: Signature Programs · NYUAD Students
text:
At Civic Engagement and Service, we design mutually beneficial partnerships to foster a deep commitment to service and engagement with the UAE. Through volunteering, sustained service, and capacity-building, we promote meaningful community involvement, embrace the rich diversity of the UAE, and cultivate ethical and inclusive leadership.

We cultivate a diverse range of unique student-centered and community-driven opportunities for you to engage with and contribute to Abu Dhabi and the UAE’s community development.

Our programs are all anchored in the concept of local action for global issues, using the sustainable development goals (SDGs) framework .

- Inclusion

A programming pillar of focus is the inclusion of “ people of determination ,” or individuals with intellectual or physical disabilities. NYUAD volunteers can get involved through initiatives such as SNAP , Unified Champion Schools Summit, Adaptive Sports & Fitness with Coach AK , and the Inclusion Conference.

Video: Andrew Riad, Class of 2022, shares what inspired him to become active in the lives of children of determination and what he gained from the experience.

- Youth Leadership Network

We support UAE cultural preservation efforts by serving as a bridge between NYUAD and Abu Dhabi. Students interact and learn about Emirati culture, and give back to their community at the same time. We work with key partners in the cultural landscape of Abu Dhabi such as Qasr Al Hosn, Department of Culture and Tourism, Abu Dhabi Media, and more.

The Youth Leadership Network (previously known as the Boys' Education Network and the Girls' Education Network, respectively) is a leadership development program for high school students in Abu Dhabi. Through weekly workshops, NYU Abu Dhabi facilitators work to help young girls and boys engage, grow, and lead — with special attention placed on a different key impact area each year, as well as technical and soft skill-building for leadership. The program:

- Helps participants build strong individual leadership skills, engage in team-based activities, and learn to collaborate effectively in multicultural environments.

- Encourages participants to think creatively about issues faced by their communities and how to take tangible steps towards solutions.

- Supports participants in learning about the importance of civic engagement within their environment.

- Connects participants with NYUAD student mentors who serve as role models to support them throughout their academic journeys.

The program explores a different key local issue each year. In one project focusing on cultural preservation in the UAE, the Youth Leadership Network cohort spent five weeks developing a Capstone aimed at enhancing museum engagement at Qasr Al Hosn.

Video: Highlight reel of Youth Leadership Network - Class of 2022

- Environmental Sustainability

Driven by NYUAD’s Commitment to a Livable Planet, we work hand-in-hand with university and local partners to turn student energy into real-world impact through conservation projects, field research, and awareness campaigns that strengthen climate resilience and protect UAE biodiversity.

- Restore local ecosystems through mangrove and Ghaf tree planting and annual beach-cleaning “Nurdle Hunts.”

- Protect wildlife on Turtle Patrol surveys and other citizen-science outings.

- Spark climate action by running Yalla Return recycling drives and working with Student Interest Groups and the Student Gov Sustainability Committee.

Volunteer Testimonial

"The moment I arrived at the site I knew that this experience would be a unique one that will teach me a lot. The coordinators from the university and the organization were very welcoming and taught us a lot about the impact of the work we were doing, which was really motivating."
-- Lujain Elmallah, Class of 2026

- Migrant Communities

We work closely with the ADvocacy SIG and community partners to support the inclusion and development of migrant worker communities in the UAE as well as around the world. Student volunteers tutor refugee students in English and other subjects through Al Muntaha Tutoring. During the holy month of Ramadan, students distribute daily Iftar meals to those in need.

- Community Outreach Events

There are a wide range of one-off community service events and opportunities that allow you to volunteer and give back within a shorter term commitment. These events are usually organized by our community partners and request NYUAD volunteers for support in event planning, fundraising or cause awareness. Popular annual events include the Abu Dhabi Art Festival, Formula 1, and Pink Run for breast cancer.

- Social Impact Leaders

Jane Goodhall, Roots & Shoots program

Social Impact Leaders is our speaker series that hosts thought leaders in sustainable development to ignite thoughtful dialogue and inspired action. Past speakers included:

- Dr. Jane Goodall: acclaimed conservationist and pioneering primatologist

- Sir Robert Swan: polar explorer and founder of 2041 Foundation

- Sana Amanat: co-creator of Marvel’s first Muslim female superhero

- Dr. Unni Karunakara: former international president of MSF/Doctors without Borders

Do you have a social impact thought leader you wish to propose as a speaker? Contact nyuad.civic.engagement@nyu.edu .

title: Sufara’a Student Ambassadors · NYUAD Students
text:
Sufara'a Ambassadors

Who Are Sufara'a?

Sufara'a [سفراء] is an Arabic word for ambassadors.

Each year, students with strong leadership skills and a demonstrated commitment to community engagement will be selected by Civic Engagement and Service to serve as Ambassadors within the NYUAD Sufara'a Program.

NYU Abu Dhabi Sufara’a are the university's specialized service ambassadors. They lead and facilitate signature programming designed by Civic Engagement and Service, represent the NYUAD within the community, and act as guides for visiting high school students on-campus. Sufara’a are dedicated volunteers who are highly passionate about one or more of the key impact areas within the scope of Civic Engagement and Service.

Selection as a Sufara’a is widely regarded as one of NYUAD’s highest service honors. Less than 15 students earn the title each year, following a rigorous interview and vetting process that weighs leadership record, cultural fluency, and community impact. Sufara’a alumni join a growing alumni network of changemakers and frequently step into leadership roles on campus and in local service initiatives.

What distinguishes Sufara'a programs from other Civic Engagement and Service programs?

Sufara’a is one of the most selective and impactful Civic Engagement and Service programs at NYU Abu Dhabi. Each year, a small group of students is chosen to serve as ambassadors for the university. Selected students are distinguished by their level of training, trust, and responsibility they receive.

Sufara’a take part in ongoing skill-building and mentorship, preparing them to lead meaningful peer-to-peer programs and support student learning across campus. They are also given the unique opportunity to represent NYUAD through programming with visiting high school students, helping shape the first impressions of future university students.

What Is Expected of Me Part of Sufara'a?

NYU Abu Dhabi Sufara'a will collaborate with Civic Engagement and Services and other departments to:

- Serve as an ambassador to NYU Abu Dhabi, facilitating connections between the university and the broader community.

- Engage in comprehensive training sessions related to key impact areas: environment, inclusion, culture, health, and migrant communities.

- Assume a leadership role in key community events.

- Commit to consistent in-person engagement for two concurrent semesters, contributing approximately 10 service hours per month.

Past Sufara'a Led Programs

- Culture: Youth Leadership Network

The Youth Leadership Network (previously known as the Boy's Education Network and the Girl's Education Network respectively) is a leadership development program for high school students in Abu Dhabi. Through weekly workshops, NYU Abu Dhabi facilitators work to help young girls and boys engage, grow, and lead — with special attention placed on a different key impact area each year, as well as technical and soft skills building for leadership.

In preparation, Sufara’a undergo extensive training to ensure they are well-equipped to effectively facilitate the program's sessions. The training covers the program's goals and objectives, the curriculum for each session, strategies for effective facilitation, and best practices for engaging with high school students. The training also includes opportunities for the facilitators to practice their facilitation skills through role play and receive feedback from the trainers as well as their peers.

- Environment: Green Sufara'a with Yalla Return

As part of NYUAD’s commitment to a liveable planet, and the “Road to COP28,” we are partnering with startAD company Nadeera to increase recycling rates in Abu Dhabi. Nadeera’s “Yalla Return” encourages recycling in a fun and easy way. Users drop off recyclables at centers or their residences' dedicated containers and receive credits in exchange for cash, vouchers, or donations. Users also receive personalized feedback on their recycling.

The Green Sufara’a are students who are passionate about sustainability and the environment. In preparation, Sufara’a undergo a training from Yalla Return on their app, and the recycling process.

Sufara’a engage in a door-to-door approach to recycling, where they greet residents, provide them with a recycling kit, explain the recycling process, and address any questions that may arise. Sufara’a and Yalla Return will have a booth at COP28 UAE, in the Youth Hub/Green Zone, and will educate attendees about recycling and their community work during the semester.

- Inclusion: Unified Schools Summit

In partnership with Special Olympics UAE’s Unified Champion Schools (UCS), Community Outreach is launching a new leadership program for high-school level unified teams* who are interested in implementing a creative project idea that promotes inclusion in their school or community.

The 10 best project ideas will be selected to participate in a one-day Summit designed and facilitated by Sufara’a to support unified team members in developing leadership, entrepreneurial, and project management skills.

By the end of the Summit, each team will have the chance to pitch their idea and will be awarded a grant to implement their project idea in the next academic year (fall 2023) under the mentorship and guidance of NYUAD students.

*Unified teams have 25-50% of their members with an intellectual or developmental disability.

- Health: World NTD Day

In collaboration with the Reach Campaign, Sufara’a will train in raising awareness of neglected tropical diseases (NTDs), and deliver workshops to Abu Dhabi middle and high school students who will be invited to the NYUAD campus on World NTD Day.

Nearly one in six people worldwide are affected by NTDs - a group of bacterial, viral, and parasitic diseases which disproportionately affect the poorest and most vulnerable people in the world. By engaging schools, Sufara’a raises awareness of the low cost of treatment for diseases such as river blindness. As little as 2 AED provides the medicine and treatment to protect one person from this and several other co-endemic diseases, for an entire year.

- Migrant Communities: Iftar Sa’em

In collaboration with Grace Conservation, for the duration of the holy month of Ramadan, NYUAD volunteers will distribute meals at Grace Conservation’s Mussafah warehouse. Sufara’a will lead the daily efforts and coordinate directly with staff on the ground based on daily distribution needs.

Why Be a Sufara'a?

The program is designed to equip students with the tools, training, and experience to serve as effective ambassadors both within the local and global contexts. As a Sufara’a, you can expect:

- Access to University Leadership : Engage directly with university decision-makers and senior administrators.

- Priority Access to Events : Receive preferred access to key Civic Engagement and Service events and programs.

- Key Networking Opportunities : Build connections with community leaders and external partners to expand your professional network.

- Community Impact : Make a meaningful contribution during the academic year through ongoing service.

- Personal Growth : Strengthen your leadership, public speaking, and time management skills through hands-on experiences.

While Sufara’a is a great opportunity to work on your personal and collective organizational and time management skills, it also has the unique quality of being community focused. Moreover, the selected Sufara’a cohort has the singular opportunity to partake in leadership workshops and networking events with high-profile individuals and field experts.

Sufara'a Requirement

- Eligibility

- Current student at NYUAD rising second or third or fourth year

- Good academic standing with a minimum GPA of 3.0

- Ability to commit for one academic year (two continuous semesters)

- Desirable Qualities

- Good interpersonal and communication skills, with leadership potential to become effective leaders in the community

- Enthusiasm to improve upon one’s knowledge and understanding in one or more key impact areas: environment, inclusion, culture, health, and migrant communities.

- A desire to develop an awareness of cultural diversity.

- Sufara'a Scope of Work

- Attend assigned meetings, training modules, events, and activities both on and off-campus

- Represent Sufara’a during meetings, events, and activities and participate in various events internally & externally

- Commit to 10 volunteering hours per month.

- Welcome and host official delegations, community organizations, and high school students who visit the NYUAD campus.

- How to apply to become a Sufara’a

- Submit the application form .

- Submit a Curriculum Vitae (CV)reflecting your recent contribution within NYUAD or in the community of UAE.

The training covers the program's goals and objectives, the curriculum for each session, strategies for effective facilitation, and best practices for engaging with high school students. The training also includes opportunities for the facilitators to practice their facilitation skills through role play and receive feedback from the trainers as well as their peers.

- Environment: Green Sufara'a with Yalla Return

As part of NYUAD’s commitment to a liveable planet, and the “Road to COP28,” we are partnering with startAD company Nadeera to increase recycling rates in Abu Dhabi. Nadeera’s “Yalla Return” encourages recycling in a fun and easy way. Users drop off recyclables at centers or their residences' dedicated containers and receive credits in exchange for cash, vouchers, or donations. Users also receive personalized feedback on their recycling.

The Green Sufara’a are students who are passionate about sustainability and the environment. In preparation, Sufara’a undergo a training from Yalla Return on their app, and the recycling process.

Sufara’a engage in a door-to-door approach to recycling, where they greet residents, provide them with a recycling kit, explain the recycling process, and address any questions that may arise. Sufara’a and Yalla Return will have a booth at COP28 UAE, in the Youth Hub/Green Zone, and will educate attendees about recycling and their community work during the semester.

- Inclusion: Unified Schools Summit

In partnership with Special Olympics UAE’s Unified Champion Schools (UCS), Community Outreach is launching a new leadership program for high-school level unified teams* who are interested in implementing a creative project idea that promotes inclusion in their school or community.

The 10 best project ideas will be selected to participate in a one-day Summit designed and facilitated by Sufara’a to support unified team members in developing leadership, entrepreneurial, and project management skills.

By the end of the Summit, each team will have the chance to pitch their idea and will be awarded a grant to implement their project idea in the next academic year (fall 2023) under the mentorship and guidance of NYUAD students.

*Unified teams have 25-50% of their members with an intellectual or developmental disability.

- Health: World NTD Day

In collaboration with the Reach Campaign, Sufara’a will train in raising awareness of neglected tropical diseases (NTDs), and deliver workshops to Abu Dhabi middle and high school students who will be invited to the NYUAD campus on World NTD Day.

Nearly one in six people worldwide are affected by NTDs - a group of bacterial, viral, and parasitic diseases which disproportionately affect the poorest and most vulnerable people in the world. By engaging schools, Sufara’a raises awareness of the low cost of treatment for diseases such as river blindness. As little as 2 AED provides the medicine and treatment to protect one person from this and several other co-endemic diseases, for an entire year.

- Migrant Communities: Iftar Sa’em

In collaboration with Grace Conservation, for the duration of the holy month of Ramadan, NYUAD volunteers will distribute meals at Grace Conservation’s Mussafah warehouse. Sufara’a will lead the daily efforts and coordinate directly with staff on the ground based on daily distribution needs.

sections.title: Why Be a Sufara'a?
sections.text:
The program is designed to equip students with the tools, training, and experience to serve as effective ambassadors both within the local and global contexts. As a Sufara’a, you can expect:

- Access to University Leadership : Engage directly with university decision-makers and senior administrators.

- Priority Access to Events : Receive preferred access to key Civic Engagement and Service events and programs.

- Key Networking Opportunities : Build connections with community leaders and external partners to expand your professional network.

- Community Impact : Make a meaningful contribution during the academic year through ongoing service.

- Personal Growth : Strengthen your leadership, public speaking, and time management skills through hands-on experiences.

While Sufara’a is a great opportunity to work on your personal and collective organizational and time management skills, it also has the unique quality of being community focused. Moreover, the selected Sufara’a cohort has the singular opportunity to partake in leadership workshops and networking events with high-profile individuals and field experts.

sections.title: Sufara'a Requirement
sections.text:
- Eligibility

- Current student at NYUAD rising second or third or fourth year

- Good academic standing with a minimum GPA of 3.0

- Ability to commit for one academic year (two continuous semesters)

- Desirable Qualities

- Good interpersonal and communication skills, with leadership potential to become effective leaders in the community

- Enthusiasm to improve upon one’s knowledge and understanding in one or more key impact areas: environment, inclusion, culture, health, and migrant communities.

- A desire to develop an awareness of cultural diversity.

- Sufara'a Scope of Work

- Attend assigned meetings, training modules, events, and activities both on and off-campus

- Represent Sufara’a during meetings, events, and activities and participate in various events internally & externally

- Commit to 10 volunteering hours per month.

- Welcome and host official delegations, community organizations, and high school students who visit the NYUAD campus.

- How to apply to become a Sufara’a

- Submit the application form .

- Submit a Curriculum Vitae (CV)reflecting your recent contribution within NYUAD or in the community of UAE.

title: Scheduling Appointments · NYUAD Students
text:
Walk-ins

The Health Center welcomes walk-ins during its open hours (please see right panel), and we try to accommodate students as soon as possible. However, for some services we require appointments and these can be done by phone, email, or online. All appointments are during the Health Center’s open hours.

Online Appointment Tutorial

This video will guide you on how to make an online appointment on the Online Student Health Center Portal (https://shcportal.nyu.edu/).

Appointments Procedures

- Medical and Immunization Appointments

Medical appointments are strongly recommended ; however, the Student Health Center can accommodate urgent and emergent walk-ins as well.

To make an appointment for a medical check-up or immunization visits, you can:

- Walk-in to the Health Center to make an appointment in person.

- Book an appointment online via the Online Student Health Center Portal (https://shcportal.nyu.edu/).

Please refer to the Medical Services tab for emergency situations and for after-hours medical guidance.

- Sports Appointments

Medical appointments are required for Pre-participation Sports Physicals.

To make an appointment for a sports check-up, you can:

- Visit the Health Center to make an appointment in person.

- Book an appointment online via the Online Student Health Center Portal (https://shcportal.nyu.edu/).

Please refer to the Medical Services tab for emergency situations and for after hours medical guidance.

- Travel Appointments

Travel appointments are available for any travel.

The earlier you prepare for your trip abroad, the better. Please email nyuad.healthcenter.nyu.edu with your itinerary as soon as you know where you are traveling for us to determine your travel health requirements.

We advise you to schedule appointments at least 2-3 weeks in advance of your trip if possible.

To make an appointment for a travel, you can:

- Visit the Health Center to make an appointment in person

- Book an appointment online via the Online Student Health Center Portal (https://shcportal.nyu.edu/).

Please refer to the Travel tab for more information on travel support services by the Health Center

- Counseling Appointments

Counseling is by appointment only, with exceptions made only for emergencies.

To make a counseling appointment, you can:

- Visit the Health Center to make an appointment in person.

- Contact the Health Center at +971 2-628-8100 .

- Email the Health Center via nyuad.healthcenter@nyu.edu .

There is currently no system to book counseling appointments online.

Please refer to the Counseling Services tab for counseling support after hours and on weekends.

- Dietitian Appointments

Dietitian services are by appointment only.

To make an appointment with the campus dietitian, you can:

- Visit the Health Center to make an appointment in person;

- Contact the Health Center on +971 2-628-8100 (or 88100 from campus landline);

- Email the Health Center via nyuad.healthcenter@nyu.edu ;

There is currently no system to book dietitian appointments online.

title: Campus Dietitian · NYUAD Students
text:
How Can the Campus Dietitian Help?

Our dietitian will view your life holistically, becoming an active partner in understanding your nutrition goals and creating plans to achieve them. We provide both one to one and group education sessions to the NYUAD community.

Services include:

- How to achieve a healthy diet while living on campus

- Weight management for weight maintenance, losing weight and gaining weight

- Supporting your sports or athletic goals with the correct diet

- Managing existing diet-related diseases such as diabetes, celiac disease, digestive diseases (e.g., irritable bowel syndrome (IBS)), and food allergies

- Reviewing your relationship with food to see if your food and weight have too much of an influence on your daily life

- Vegetarian or vegan diets to achieve nutritional balance while excluding certain food groups

Make an Appointment

Schedule an appointment by contacting the Health Center at +971 2-628-8100 or dropping by the Center.

>Appointments are available for Sundays to Thursdays, from 9am-5pm.

What to Expect in your First Personal Session

You will be asked to complete a 3-day food and activity diary before your first session. This will help you to focus on your current habits and also allow more time for discussion in your first appointment.

We will then:

- Work together to identify your nutrition goals for the future and look back to understand how you have previously managed your nutrition. We will work out what worked well, and what was less successful.

- Create a realistic and individualized plan that will support your goals.

- Agree on frequency of visits, to monitor progress, set new goals, and determine how best to attain them.

Group Education Sessions

Details of group nutrition education sessions will be advertised via announcements.

title: Counseling Services · NYUAD Students
text:
On-campus Confidential Counseling Services

Counseling — or psychotherapy — is a confidential professional relationship that empowers students to address their personal problems in a non-judgemental, supportive space

The counseling relationship differs from friendships and patient-doctor contacts. Counselors are able to be objective because they are not involved in your daily lives.They don't give specific advice or tell you what to do. Instead, counselors serve as skilled listeners who help you clarify issues, uncover your feelings and help you develop strategies to manage problems more effectively.

NYUAD counselors follow a short-term counseling model with unlimited number of sessions at students' disposal. The number and frequency of sessions are solely based on each student's clinical needs and will be decided by the student and their counselor.

Commitment to Inclusiveness

The Health Center is committed to providing quality care to all members of the NYUAD community who rely on our service. We recognize that race, ethnicity, gender, sexual orientation, religion, culture and socio-economic status may affect the health of an individual and/or influence an individual's healthcare choices. With that in mind, we strive to be sensitive to the diverse needs of our student body. Our commitment is to treat all patients with respect, compassion, and sensitivity.

Our Team

View counselor profiles .

Other Options for Psychotherapy Outside of NYUAD

Students' local and international health insurance can be used for psychotherapy in the community outside of NYUAD for those students who prefer to do so.

We have ongoing partnerships with different mental health providers in the community. Your NYUAD counselors can help you identify most appropriate options for your specific needs.

What kind of problem is appropriate to discuss with a counselor?

Anything that troubles you.

Here is a partial list of common student concerns:

- Depression

- Homesickness

- Stress

- Anxiety

- ADHD

- Alcohol or drugs

- Eating concerns

- Academic anxieties

- Roommate and friendship problems

- Family problems

- Suicidal thoughts

- Sexual concerns

- Identity concerns

Initial Session

Typically, counseling involves an initial session where you meet with your counselor to discuss your primary concerns. From that point onwards, therapy can differ in frequency and content, but will always be confidential, collaborative, time-limited and using evidence based skills. Our counselors share a dedication to providing state-of -the-art services based on current research and thinking in psychology.

What is Cognitive Behavioral Therapy?

- Additional information about Cognitive Behavioral Therapy (CBT) approach.

- Common Myths and Misconceptions about CBT

Schedule an Appointment

Monday-Thursday , 9am-5pm
Friday , 9am-12pm, 2:30-5pm

Stop by our front desk at the Health Center or call us at +971-2-628-8100 to schedule an appointment to see a counselor. We are available Monday to Thursday between 9am-5pm and Friday 9am-12pm and 2:30-5pm. Alternatively, email us at nyuad.healthcenter@nyu.edu .

After-hours (after 5pm, Weekends)

The Wellness Exchange (Available 24/7)

To speak to a certified counselor for immediate support, the Wellness Exchange is available 24/7 at +971 2 628 5555 (85555 from campus) or via NYU Wellness Exchange App, available for Android & iPhone . The App functions 24 hours a day and in six languages.

The Wellness Exchange is your key to accessing NYU's exclusive health and mental health resources. This private, 24/7 hotline puts you in touch with professionals who can help address your day-to-day challenges, as well as other health-related concerns.

Wellness Exchange support includes support for:

- Academic stress

- Depression

- Sexual assault

- Anxiety

- Alcohol and other drugs dependence

- Eating disorders

- Relationship issues

- Adjustment difficulties

- Homesickness

- Just need someone to talk to

- To call about a friend etc.

No concern is too big or too small. The Wellness Exchange is here for you, whatever the reason.

title: FAQs · NYUAD Students
text:
Physical Health

- What do I do if I have a medical concern in the evening or on the weekend?

Call 999 and then Public Safety (02 628 7777) for any life- or limb-threatening medical emergencies.

For less serious concerns, when the Health Center is closed, students can call the Nurse Advice Line (02 628 8100) and speak to a registered nurse who will help answer their medical concerns and/or direct them to care as appropriate.

Public Safety and ambulance numbers can always be found at the back of your NYU ID card. Public Safety is trained to provide first aid services that will support a student before the ambulance arrives.

It is advisable that you maintain a small first aid kit for yourself to cater for minor emergencies. For tips about what to put in your first aid kit, visit this website .

- How far is the nearest pharmacy?

The Al Manara Pharmacy, NYUAD branch is open on campus. It operates Sunday-Thursday 11am to 6 pm during the academic year. The Al Manara, Saadiyat branch is open Sunday-Thursday 9am to 11pm and Friday 3pm to 11pm. Free, regularly scheduled shuttles are available into the city and to Yas Island where other pharmacies are located. The pharmacy at the St. Regis does not accept the student health insurance.

- How far is the nearest hospital?

Cleveland Clinic Abu Dhabi (CCAD) is the nearest hospital, and it is a 10-minute ride from campus. In addition to emergency room visits, students are referred to community hospitals and providers for x-rays, blood work or referral to a specialist. Free, regularly scheduled shuttles drop students off near many of the referral locations and are often used by students for their routine appointments. All students have local health insurance and can access care at any local participating providers.

- What services are available from the Health Center and what services do I need referrals to outside institutions?

The Health Center serves as the first point of contact for student medical needs at NYUAD. We can:

- Identify and treat common medical conditions such as those seen by a general practitioner. This can include colds and flu, fever, injuries, counseling, travel medicine, preventive medicine, and sports injuries;

- Assess the urgency of your medical problems and direct you to the best place for care;

- Provide preventative and health education;

- Make referrals to medical specialists when necessary. For example, this may include:

- Dental Care

- Reproductive Health Care

- Orthopedic Treatments

- Specialist Procedures

- Where can I get recommendations for specialist services?

Given the personal nature of medical care, it is highly recommended that students seeking recommendations for specialists come to the Health Center to see a physician. The physician can look at the individual’s history and will also have the most updated list of places that the Health Center is comfortable referring students to. The facilities that the Health Center refers students to can change with regards to services and staff, so they are under constant review.

- Where can I go for orthopedic injuries since these services are not offered at Cleveland Clinic?

Usually, the Health Center refers cases with orthopedic injuries to Burjeel Hospital, but they recommend that students get evaluated by one of the doctors first at the Health Center. The doctor can then decide where to send the student according to the nature and severity of injury.

- Where can I go for gynecology or reproductive health services, which are also not offered at Cleveland Clinic?

The Health Center does not have a specific hospital or clinic to refer to for gynecology issues. We recommend that you first see one of the doctors at the Health Center so that further management and referrals can be made accordingly.

- Can I get reimbursed for hospital-related travel?

Students cannot currently get reimbursed for hospital-related travel with the exception of ambulance transportation, which is covered under Sukoon Insurance. However, students in an extenuating circumstance can approach the Dean of Students' office to communicate their concern.

- How does my health insurance work?

Please see the Health Insurance page for more information.

Mental Health

- Is there a mental health counselor on campus? Are there a limited number of sessions?

NYUAD takes mental health very seriously, and we have on-campus clinical psychologists as well as a full-time psychiatrist. They are available by appointment for one-on-one counseling sessions throughout the academic year, as well as for walk-ins for urgent concerns. There is no limit to the number of sessions a student can attend. Students can arrange an appointment in person, by email: nyuad.healthcenter@nyu.edu , or by calling +971-2-628-8100 .

- What if I have a mental health concern in the evening or on the weekend?

The Wellness Exchange (02 628 5555) is a 24/7 mental health hotline for the entire NYU Global Network and connects students to a mental health specialist.

Medications

- What is the process of bringing in personal medications into the UAE?

In October 2018, the UAE Ministry of Health implemented a requirement that all travelers coming into the UAE must complete an electronic form to obtain online approval to carry medications into the country. Individuals must register on the Ministry of Health website and fill out the form. The approval is processed and emailed within five working days. This approval must be presented at immigration. This form typically requires:

- Details of the medication, including the batch number, trade name, and active ingredients

- Copy of the prescription

- A letter from your doctor stating you require the medication

Previously, travelers may have been asked to produce prescriptions upon arrival to the UAE. It is still advised that students traveling with personal medications look at the list of banned or restricted drugs published by the Ministry of Health before filling out the online form. The Health Center can support students to understand what the limitations are in regards to bringing in medications.

- Am I allowed to bring in drugs that are not sold in the UAE?

It depends on the specific drug. Sometimes the generic version of a drug is available in UAE but the brand name might be different. It is important to ensure that the drug is legal in the UAE first, and also that it is not a drug which needs an accompanying prescription to have the relevant stamps on it for immigration purposes.

- Are antidepressants available?

Yes, Prozac, Zoloft, and Celexa, and several other medications are available at pharmacies. As antidepressants are controlled substances in the UAE, not all medications are available, and students may have to renew their prescriptions monthly. Students can consider bringing prescription medicine from home, but it is mandatory to have the original prescription bottle and a physician-signed prescription. Otherwise, make an appointment with a doctor at the Health Center, and they can prescribe a suitable alternative.

- Are ADD/ADHD drugs available?

Yes, most ADD/ADHD medications are available in the UAE. As these prescriptions are controlled substances, students may have to renew their prescriptions monthly by a UAE clinical psychiatrist. This can be facilitated by one of our Health Center providers. Students can consider bringing prescription medicine from home, but it is mandatory to have the original prescription bottle and a physician-signed, stamped prescription.

- Can I bring in my own antidepressants or ADD/ADHD meds into the country?

In general, yes. These medications should be in their original prescription bottle and accompanied by a signed and stamped doctor’s note. Medication should be carried in carry-on luggage, not checked in baggage. Please review the regulations that apply to bringing medication into the UAE to ensure that you are in line with the immigration policies of the UAE.

We urge you to please review our document for Students Traveling With Medication to the UAE for more comprehensive guidance.

- Can I ship medications into the country?

Shipping medication into the country is not recommended, as there may be issues with customs. However, in special circumstances, it is allowed. Contact the Health Center for more information.

- Can I continue my allergy shots on campus?

The Health Center can administer allergy shots. Students can be referred to community allergists, but this is not covered by the health insurance, and specific serums may not be available. Routinely, UAE allergists will conduct their own testing and prescribe based on their findings.

- If I bring my medications, will the nurses administer them?

For medications prescribed by an outside doctor, please make an appointment with a Health Center Physician. Once an evaluation is done and the medication deemed appropriate, the Health Center physician can provide orders for onsite administration of medications by a nurse.

- Can the Health Center store my medications?

The Health Center does not store individual student medications. The medical staff will assist students in arranging for proper storage in their residences.

- Are my diabetic supplies available?

Yes, the majority of diabetic medications and supplies are available in the UAE. Make an appointment with a HC physician if you need refills.

- Are travel vaccines available?

Vaccines and prescriptions for anti-malarial medications are provided by appointment at the Health Center for school-related travel. The yellow fever vaccine is only available at certain UAE government health facilities.

-

General

- What is the legal drinking age?

It is illegal to drink alcohol on a student visa, regardless of age. Public intoxication can have serious legal consequences and visa implications.

- Where can I get access to contraception on campus?

It is strongly suggested that students wondering about contraception come to the Health Center and see a nurse or doctor to discuss this in greater detail. Alternatively, if they prefer, they can see a physician regarding their contraception options in their home country.

Condoms are available over the counter at any pharmacy and grocery store, including the pharmacy on campus.

- Is emergency contraception available in the UAE?

Yes, emergency contraception is available in the UAE. Please visit the Health Center for further information.

- What do I do if I have a medical concern in the evening or on the weekend?

Call 999 and then Public Safety (02 628 7777) for any life- or limb-threatening medical emergencies.

For less serious concerns, when the Health Center is closed, students can call the Nurse Advice Line (02 628 8100) and speak to a registered nurse who will help answer their medical concerns and/or direct them to care as appropriate.

Public Safety and ambulance numbers can always be found at the back of your NYU ID card. Public Safety is trained to provide first aid services that will support a student before the ambulance arrives.

It is advisable that you maintain a small first aid kit for yourself to cater for minor emergencies. For tips about what to put in your first aid kit, visit this website .

- How far is the nearest pharmacy?

The Al Manara Pharmacy, NYUAD branch is open on campus. It operates Sunday-Thursday 11am to 6 pm during the academic year. The Al Manara, Saadiyat branch is open Sunday-Thursday 9am to 11pm and Friday 3pm to 11pm. Free, regularly scheduled shuttles are available into the city and to Yas Island where other pharmacies are located. The pharmacy at the St. Regis does not accept the student health insurance.

- How far is the nearest hospital?

Cleveland Clinic Abu Dhabi (CCAD) is the nearest hospital, and it is a 10-minute ride from campus. In addition to emergency room visits, students are referred to community hospitals and providers for x-rays, blood work or referral to a specialist. Free, regularly scheduled shuttles drop students off near many of the referral locations and are often used by students for their routine appointments. All students have local health insurance and can access care at any local participating providers.

- What services are available from the Health Center and what services do I need referrals to outside institutions?

The Health Center serves as the first point of contact for student medical needs at NYUAD. We can:

- Identify and treat common medical conditions such as those seen by a general practitioner. This can include colds and flu, fever, injuries, counseling, travel medicine, preventive medicine, and sports injuries;

- Assess the urgency of your medical problems and direct you to the best place for care;

- Provide preventative and health education;

- Make referrals to medical specialists when necessary. For example, this may include:

- Dental Care

- Reproductive Health Care

- Orthopedic Treatments

- Specialist Procedures

- Where can I get recommendations for specialist services?

Given the personal nature of medical care, it is highly recommended that students seeking recommendations for specialists come to the Health Center to see a physician. The physician can look at the individual’s history and will also have the most updated list of places that the Health Center is comfortable referring students to. The facilities that the Health Center refers students to can change with regards to services and staff, so they are under constant review.

Please see the Health Insurance page for more information.
