title: Health Insurance · NYUAD Students
text:
NYU Abu Dhabi provides a dual health insurance system to ensure students receive seamless, comprehensive medical coverage both inside the UAE and internationally. This system combines Sukoon/Bupa for UAE-based care and Blue Cross Blue Shield Global Solutions (formerly GeoBlue) for international coverage.

This dual system ensures that NYUAD students have uninterrupted coverage worldwide

UAE Insurance (Sukoon / Bupa)
This is an enhanced plan that complies with the Health Insurance Law for the Emirate of Abu Dhabi (No. 23 of 2005) and fully meets UAE visa requirements for the Emirate.

Sukoon, administered by Bupa Global, provides comprehensive health insurance coverage within the United Arab Emirates and the GCC Area. Sukoon hand-picked network of worldclass providers are specifically curated to meet the diverse needs of NYUAD students.

- Read a summary of your Sukoon/Bupa coverage in the Sukoon Brochure/Table of Benefits (PDF)

Enrolment Timeline

In compliance with local regulations, students must be physically present in the UAE before enrolment can be initiated.

How to Access Your Insurance Card

- No physical card — digital only

- Access it through the Bupa Global MembersWorld app

Locating Healthcare Providers

Please search the Sukoon medical network providers at medicalnetwork.tameen.ae .

When You Need Care

- Visit a hospital or clinic in the UAE.

- Show your digital insurance card.

- Most services are covered with no co-pay.

Submitting a Claim

If a claim is needed:

- Fill out the Bupa Global claim form

- Submit the completed claim form with receipts to info@bupa-intl.com or via the app.

Important Notes

- Covers a wide network of providers in the UAE and GCC.

- Coverage renews each year automatically.

- First-year students receive access after arriving in the UAE.

Sukoon Contact Information

Email: BupaConnect@bupa-intl.com
Phone: 800-823-2872 (toll-free inside the UAE)
44(0) 1273-323-563 (outside the UAE)
Sukoon website

Global Insurance Blue Cross Blue Shield Global Solutions (Formerly GeoBlue)
All matriculated NYUAD students are eligible for the mandatory global health insurance plan through BCBS. New enrolment begins at the start of the academic year, prior to students departure from their home country.

BCBS (Geo Blue) plan provides easy and unique access to global medical expertise with a responsive, multi-channel service.

Read a Summary of Benefits

- BCBS Guide /Table of Benefits (NYADB)

- BCBS Guide /Table of Benefits (NYADE)

BCBS offers a mobile app that can be used to browse medical providers around the world and to review your schedule of benefits. The app is available for Android and iOS Devices .

Activate Your Account

- Activate your account from the welcome email .

- Download and keep your BCBS ID card .

In an Emergency

- Go to the nearest hospital immediately.

- Contact BCBS team to request a direct pay.

Locating Healthcare Providers

- Use the BCBS app or website to find covered providers.

- Try to request direct pay 48 hours in advance .

Submitting a Claim

- Complete the GeoBlue Medical Expense Claim Form .

- Email it to claims@geo-blue.com with receipts or submit online via the app.

Important Notes

- Coverage for newly enrolled students begins prior to their departure.

- Coverage renews each year automatically.

- Global Network providers in over 190 countries worldwide.

- Multilingual global health team available 24/7.

Outside of the UAE, if you have issues with your Global Insurance card, you will need to contact BCBS directly.

BCBS (GeoBlue) Customer Service:

- Email BCBS (GeoBlue) at customerservice@geo-blue.com

- +1-844-268-2686 (toll-free inside the US)

- +1-610-268-2686 (outside the US)

- Visit www.bcbsglobalsolutions.com

title: Global Insurance FAQs · NYUAD Students
text:
Global Health Insurance

Where do I collect my Global Health insurance card?
Blue Cross Blue Shield (BCBS), NYUAD’s global health insurance provider, will send students a welcome email before the start of the academic year containing their membership details. Students are strongly encouraged to register and activate their online membership immediately upon receiving this email.

Download and Print

Please use the link provided in the welcome email to access the Membership Hub , where you can download and print your BCBS ID card .

If you encounter any issues during registration or activation, please contact BCBS Customer Service at: customerservice@geo-blue.com .

Mobile App

BCBS Blue Cross Blue Shield (BCBS) offers mobile applications — primarily BCBS Global Core and BCBS Global Solutions — designed to give students and members seamless access to their health coverage while traveling or studying abroad.

The BCBS App is available for both Android and iOS devices, and students are encouraged to download it for convenient access to their global coverage.

When do I need to carry my BCBS Card?
Students should always maintain access to their Membership Hub , as it is the primary platform for viewing their digital BCBS ID card and accessing all services provided through BCBS Global Health Insurance.

How do I submit a claim for my Global Health insurance?
Manual Reimbursement: If a student encounters a non-direct billing facility, they must download and complete the BCBS Global Claim Form, BCBS Medical Expense Claim . The completed form, accompanied by scanned copies of all itemized invoices and payment receipts, must be emailed directly to claims@geo-blue.com .

Online Submission: Log in to your BCBS membership Hub and fill the claim digitally. You can track the online progress of reimbursement directly through your online account.

What is the difference between UAE Health insurance and Global Health insurance?
NYUAD operates a complementary, dual-plan health insurance ecosystem to provide seamless care locally and internationally:

Local Coverage (Within the UAE) : Managed by Sukoon (administered by Bupa Global) for all medical and mental health services. UAE insurance is linked to students' UAE residency visa requirements.

Global Coverage (Outside the UAE) : Managed by Blue Cross Blue Shield for medical and mental health services during university seminars, study away, or personal travel.

Do I have an insurance co-pay for BCBS Global insurance?
Deductible and copays are USD 0, but BCBS insurance have a cost-sharing structure on some services

Coinsurance 100% : Inpatient hospital, prescriptions, primary care office visits, all mental health and substance abuse outpatient and inpatient, emergency services, preventative care.

Coinsurance 90% : All other services including specialist visits, diagnostic testing, outpatient surgery, and physical therapy, chiropractic, acupuncture services, etc.

How does my BCBS Global health insurance get renewed?
All returning students' BCBS health insurance policies will automatically renew on August 1 , following the expiration of current coverage on July 31.

If I have my own country’s health insurance, do I need to switch?
All enrolled students automatically receive Blue Cross Blue Shield (BCBS) health insurance, regardless of any coverage they hold from their home country.

Who do I contact if I get to the hospital and have a problem using my insurance card?
Students who experience policy issues or trouble accessing healthcare providers while abroad should contact the 24/7 BCBS support team directly.

BCBS (GeoBlue) Customer Service
Email BCBS (GeoBlue) at customerservice@geo-blue.com
+1-844-268-2686 (toll free inside the US)
+1-610-268-2686 (outside the US)
Visit www.bcbsglobalsolutions.com

Where can I access the details of my BCBS Global health insurance?
Blue Cross Blue Shield (BCBS) offers mobile apps — primarily BCBS Global Core and BCBS Global Solutions — designed to give students and members seamless access to their health coverage while traveling or studying abroad.

The BCBS App is available for both Android and iOS devices, and students are encouraged to download it for convenient access to their global coverage.

Which doctors are covered by the BCBS global health insurance policy?
BCBS Global has an extensive network of providers offering direct-pay access with no copays or deductibles. To make sure you don't have to pay out-of-pocket for your visit, please complete these steps:

- Download the BCBS Global mobile app .

- Go to Find a Provider, select Hospital & Medical Center, and search for Facilities in Your Area .

- Request a Guarantee of Payment (GOP) if the service outside US.

- Important : Before your appointment, request a GOP through the app. This is a crucial step that authorizes BCBS to pay the facility directly. Be sure to request coverage for both the consultation and any required diagnostic tests.

Global Dental Coverage

What dental coverage do I have with BCBS global health insurance while abroad?
BCBS Global plan does not include routine dental coverage.

Dental services are covered only in cases of accidental dental injury or trauma.

Global Optical Coverage

Vision testing, prescription glasses, and contact lenses
Vision testing and prescription glasses or contact lenses are not covered by BCBS health insurance.

Global Physical Therapy Coverage

Is physical therapy covered by BCBS Global health insurance?
Physical Therapy is covered by BCBS Global health insurance, but students need to access their BCBS Membership hub to identify and book an appointment with a provider from the BCBS network and request a direct pay at least 48hrs prior to the appointment .

- Download the BCBS Global mobile app .

- Go to Find a Provider, select Hospital & Medical Center, and search for Facilities in Your Area .

- Request a Guarantee of Payment (GOP) if the service outside US.

- Important : Before your appointment, request a GOP through the app. This is a crucial step that authorizes BCBS to pay the facility directly. Be sure to request coverage for both the consultation and any required diagnostic tests.

title: UAE Insurance FAQs · NYUAD Students
text:
UAE Health Insurance

Where do I collect my UAE (Sukoon/Bupa) health insurance card?
There are no physical Sukoon insurance cards. To access your digital card:

- Download the Bupa Global Members app.

- Log in or register, using the unique policy number, which was sent to you by Bupa Global in your welcome email.

How do I submit a claim for my UAE insurance?

- Manual Submission: Download and complete the Bupa Global Claim Form . Return the completed form with scanned copies of any invoices and receipts of your treatment to info@bupa-intl.com .

- Online Submission: Log in to your Bupa Global members portal and fill the claim digitally. You can track the online progress of reimbursement directly through your online account.

What is the difference between UAE health and Global health insurance?
Sukoon/Bupa health insurance provides access to medical and mental health services strictly within the UAE. UAE health insurance is also linked to students’ UAE residency visas and is a requirement.

BCBS health insurance provides access to medical and mental health services globally.

Do I have an insurance co-pay in the UAE?
Sukoon/Bupa health insurance provides full coverage with no co-pay required for the UAE and GCC.

How does my UAE insurance get renewed?

- Returning students: health insurance cards get renewed before the start of the academic year.

- First-year students: health insurance cards are processed after their arrival to the UAE.

Who do I contact if I get to the hospital and have problems with using my UAE insurance card?
If you have issues relating to insurance, please contact nyuad.caremanagement@nyu.ed.

Where can I access the details of my UAE insurance policy?
You can access and manage your coverage using the Bupa Global Members World app available on the App Store or Google Play Store. Register using the policy number and membership details provided in your official welcome email from Bupa Global.

The app allows you to access your digital Sukoon insurance card, submit claims, track reimbursements, and view coverage details.

If you have any additional questions, please contact BupaConnect@bupa-intl.com .

Which doctors are covered by the insurance policy?
You can access medical providers covered by Sukoon health insurance through medicalnetwork.tameen.ae

What dental coverage do I have with my UAE health insurance?
Students holding Sukoon health insurance have access to routine dental care with a limit of one thousand US dollars (USD 1,000) per academic year.

Can you recommend a list of dentists that I should visit?
The Health Center recommends the providers below:

- NMC Royal Medical Center – Electra Street branch

- Burjeel Medical Center

- Boston Dental Clinic

We advise that you visit the Health Center to determine the best course of action related to dental care concerns.

Eyesight testing for prescription glasses is not covered by Sukoon health insurance, but we can help arrange for medical eyesight testing if the service is required.

UAE Hospital Coverage

Does my insurance cover all hospitals in the UAE?
Sukoon provides comprehensive health insurance coverage within the UAE and GCC with a network of world-class medical providers specifically curated to meet the diverse needs of the NYUAD community.

Please visit medicalnetwork.tameen.ae to explore medical providers covered by Sukoon insurance.

We encourage you to visit the Student Health Center for a list of preferred health providers in the UAE.

Is physical therapy covered by my insurance?
Physical therapy is covered by insurance if a referral from a local provider and pre-authorization of treatment approval are obtained by the medical facility.

title: Medical Services · NYUAD Students
text:
Service Lines and Scope of Care

The Student Health Center welcomes scheduled appointments during normal business hours. Our clinical team also assesses students with urgent and emergent medical and mental health needs on a walk-in basis. Our scope of service is as follows:

- Primary Care

Let NYUAD serve as your medical home while you’re away from home! From management of chronic medical conditions to routine health check-ups, our student health clinic is broadly equipped to handle most medical needs for our students. Our primary care services include: acute illness management, sports physicals, well-woman exams, reproductive health, routine check-ups, travel medicine, managing chronic medical conditions, allergies, specialty referrals, and more.

- Mental Health Services

College life can be stressful, but you’re not alone! Our counselors and physicians are here to help. We commonly treat a wide range of mental health concerns, including depression, anxiety, grief reaction, and ADHD. In addition, we have a 24-hour Wellness Exchange Hotline for immediate mental health crises. Please talk to us! — See our Counseling Services

- Urgent Care

For college life’s unexpected events and minor emergencies. We offer same-day appointments. We commonly treat rashes, strains and sprains, respiratory infections, flu, urinary tract infections, minor laceration repairs, asthma flairs, diarrhea, and dehydration.

- Ancillary Services

To best serve our students, we offer routine bedside testing to give us immediate results. These tests include: strep testing, flu testing, urinalysis, and blood sugar testing. We also provide lab draws, vaccines, and medication injections (limited).

- Outreach Services

We collaborate with other departments within Campus Life to enhance health awareness for our students. Examples include weekly “Healthy Life Workshops,” “Dine with the Dietician” sessions, and mental health group sessions.

Life-Threatening Medical Emergencies

First call 999 for an ambulance, and then get in touch with Public Safety at +971 2-628-7777 (or 87777 from campus) so public safety can assist the medical team to your location quickly.

After-hours Non-life-threatening Urgent Medical Needs

For urgent medical concerns that do not require an ambulance, proceed to the nearest emergency room:

Cleveland Clinic Abu Dhabi
Al Falah Street, Al Maryah Island
Tel: +971 2-659-0200

Open 24/7

After-hours Medical Nurse Advice Line

When the Health Center is closed and you need non-emergent medical information and guidance on all types of health questions, tips for handling an illness/injury, or medical usage and interaction, please call the after-hours nurse advice line on +971 2-628-8100 and get connected to our Abu Dhabi Department of Health-licensed, registered nurses. Provide your name, phone number, and N number, and the nurses will help you make informed decisions about your health situation based upon physician-approved guidelines. Your call is completely confidential.

Related official links:
https://students.nyuad.nyu.edu/student-affairs/health-center/counseling-services/

title: Mandatory Requirements · NYUAD Students
text:
Immunizations Before Arriving

First-Year students will receive a detailed email from the Health Center regarding mandatory health and immunization requirements. Below are some important deadlines.

Please note that the mandatory vaccines must be received prior to your arrival in Abu Dhabi. Non-compliance may affect your living expenses stipend (if applicable) and class registration. Please review the NYU Abu Dhabi Students page for more immunization information and to complete important forms. If you are unable to meet minimum vaccination requirements, please email nyuad.immunization@nyu.edu . You can read more about immunization FAQs on the NYUAD Student Immunization FAQs page.

- First-Year Immunization Forms

Please visit the NYU Student Health Center (different from the NYUAD student portal) to upload your documents. You must complete your Immunization History Form and Health History Form and Wellbeing Questionnaire. This can be completed online — please follow the instructions on the NYU Abu Dhabi Students page. First-Year students need to submit these forms by July 1 before their first year at NYUAD .

You can find more information on important deadlines on the NYU Health Requirements page for NYUAD students . You may need to contact your healthcare provider or school to collect your immunization records, so please be proactive in collecting your records.

- Mandatory Immunization Requirements

- Evidence of vaccination with at least two doses of combined measles, mumps, rubella (MMR) vaccine (if not immune by documented history of having these illnesses or by blood titer). Please note that the first MMR must have been received after your first birthday.

- Evidence of vaccination with one dose of the ACWY meningococcal meningitis vaccine within the past five years (and after age 16).

- Travelling With Medication to the UAE

NYUAD and the government of Abu Dhabi fully recognize that some students require prescription medications from their home country for legitimate health reasons. Immigration authorities are receptive and hospitable to travelers who require legitimate prescription medication. Authorities are also aware of the rise in global narcotic abuse and are charged with preventing the importation of illicit substances into the UAE. For those reasons, the Abu Dhabi Ministry of Health has provided a simple registration process for travelers.

We urge your to please review our document for Students Traveling With Medication to the UAE for more comprehensive guidance.

Abu Dhabi Visa Health Requirements

After students arrive, NYUAD will organize a group trip to the immigration office for those students who are not UAE residents to obtain a UAE residence visa, as required by UAE law. A medical check at a government hospital or medical clinic is a required part of the immigration and visa process.

The medical check consists of a physical exam, including a skin exam for leprosy, blood tests for HIV (AIDS), Hepatitis B, Hepatitis C, and Syphilis, and a chest x-ray to screen for Tuberculosis (TB). If results and/or findings are positive for any of these conditions, the student may be required to receive immediate treatment and may be required to travel back home.

We strongly urge you to be screened for these conditions prior to your departure for Abu Dhabi. You should also discuss pre-departure screening with your health-care professionals or with the Health Center ( nyuad.healthcenter@nyu.edu ).

Regardless of what tests are done in your home country, all tests must be performed in the UAE after arrival in order to obtain a residence visa. The results of testing or physical examinations completed in home countries are not accepted for the fulfillment of the visa requirements.

Recommended Immunizations

These are vaccines that are available at the Health Center to consider during your time at NYUAD and before any travel:

- Hepatitis A

- Hepatitis B

- Influenza (Flu)

- Polio (completion of original series and an adult booster if you are 18 or over)

- Varicella

- Typhoid

- Tetanus

To review vaccine information statements from the CDC, please review our Recommended Immunizations .

Please visit our Appointments page to learn how you can receive vaccinations.

You are also able to review your immunization records on the Online Student Health Center Portal .

Questions?

If you have any questions, please review the FAQs on the NYU Health Requirements for NYUAD Students page and the Immunization FAQ page on the Student Portal. If your question is still unanswered, please contact the Health Center NYUAD at nyuad.healthcenter@nyu.edu .

title: Immunizations FAQs · NYUAD Students
text:
Immunization FAQs

- What immunizations are available at the NYUAD Health Center?

The NYUAD Health Center provides most recommended immunizations free of charge. Please follow this link to review comprehensive list.

- Do I need to make an appointment to receive immunizations?

Making an appointment link will guarantee a time slot for receiving an immunization. However, the Health Center allows walk in appointments for this service.

- Is the HPV vaccine available in the UAE?

The HPV vaccine is available in the UAE and can be received at local healthcare facilities. The cost for consultation and HPV are not covered by insurance and therefore will be an out of pocket expense.

- Are immunizations available at the NYU Student Health Center?

Yes, immunizations are available at the NYU Student Health Center, however you will be charged for these vaccinations in New York.

- Can I receive the yellow fever vaccine at the Health Center?

In the UAE, yellow fever vaccination is provided at the government SEHA Clinics.

- Why do you need the information requested on the Student Immunization History form?

These vaccinations are required to proactively address emerging health threats to a student residential population in a higher education campus setting, and to protect the overall health, safety, and welfare of the NYUAD campus and community.

- What happens if I do not provide the immunization information?

We take the health and safety of our community seriously. To ensure that your health is at minimum risk from an outbreak, we must enforce the NYUAD immunization requirements.

Students who fail to comply may have their living expenses stipend (if applicable) suspended and a Registrar hold placed on their accounts. As a result, they may not be able to register for any classes or access their living expenses stipend (if applicable) until they are compliant.

- Are all the vaccines required?

The required vaccinations are 2 MMR vaccines and an ACWY meningococcal vaccine. The first MMR must have been received after your first birthday; the meningococcal vaccine must be within the past 5 years (and after age 16).

Given the high likelihood that you will be traveling during your years at NYUAD, we strongly advise that you receive as many of the listed vaccinations as possible, but they are not required.

- How do I get my vaccination record?

There are several sources, including but not limited to the following: your childhood immunization record may be with your parents; your doctor or clinic should have records; the health authority in your country may keep records; schools often have records. If you cannot locate any records, you can either repeat the vaccines or have your doctor check for immunity (through laboratory confirmation). There is no immunity test for the meningitis vaccine. You will need to receive another dose if you do not have documentation of a dose within the past 5 years.

- What if I only have my immunization information in an Immunization Record Card or baby book from my pediatrician?

We will accept official information as long as it is signed and stamped by a clinician or the office that issued the record. If the documentation is not stamped and signed you can take the Student Immunization History form and take the vaccination records to a medical provider and have the form filled out, signed and stamped by a medical provider.

- If I have my own copy of health and immunization records, is it still necessary to complete the Student Immunization History form?

Yes. You must fill out the computer appropriate form and upload the form to the Student Portal.

- If my records are in a foreign language do I need to get certification of vaccination in English?

Yes. We ask that you provide a translation of your immunization records if they are not in English. You may want to contact your local ministry of health to see if they can issue you an international vaccination certificate in English.

- What if I cannot receive my required vaccinations by the specified deadline? Or if I receive additional vaccinations after I have already uploaded my form?

Please make every effort to complete your vaccinations and upload the vaccination form by the required deadline. If you think that you will have difficulty complying with the mandatory immunization requirements, please email nyuad.immunization@nyu.edu.

- What is meant by 2 MMRs?

MMR is an immunization vaccine against measles, mumps, and rubella (German measles). It is generally administered in childhood after the first birthday, with a second dose before starting school (i.e. age 4/5). The second dose of MMR can be given as early as 4 weeks (28 days) after the first dose and is considered a valid dose if both doses were given after the child's first birthday. The second dose is not a booster, but rather is intended to produce immunity in the small number of people who fail to respond to the first dose.

You can satisfy this requirement with 2 MMR vaccines; 2 individual vaccines of each measles, mumps, and rubella; or 1 MMR and 1 each of measles, mumps, and rubella vaccines. Alternatively, your healthcare provider can order laboratory confirmation of immunity for each- measles, mumps and rubella.

- In the event that my measles, mumps, and rubella (MMR) records are not available and cannot be located, what do I need to do?

Two options are available. You may take the vaccinations again (at least 28 days apart) or you may take a blood test (MMR titers). The blood test will indicate whether you have positive immunity or not. If you do not have positive immunity, then vaccinations will be necessary. Please note that titers are generally not covered by insurance and vary in expense.

- Is it safe to get another MMR vaccine if I have already received 2 vaccines but don’t have documentation?

In general, although it is not ideal, receiving extra doses of the MMR vaccine poses no medical problem. Alternatively, your healthcare provider can order laboratory confirmation of immunity for each- measles, mumps and rubella. If you lack immunity to any of the 3 illnesses, you should receive the combination MMR vaccine.

- Which Meningitis vaccine should I receive?

Incoming college and university students are required to receive the MCV4 vaccine prior to attending school to combat bacterial meningitis (meningococcal disease). You should receive the quadrivalent (MCV4) vaccine, which protects against serogroups A, C, W, and Y. Acceptable vaccines include Menactra (USA), Menveo (USA), Mencevax (worldwide) and Nimenrix (EU). Meningitis vaccines other than the quadrivalent ACWY vaccine will not satisfy the mandatory vaccine requirement.

- What should I do if the meningitis vaccine is not available in my country?

It is important to start this process as early as possible. We strongly urge you to receive the required vaccinations prior to arrival at NYUAD. Failure to do so may affect class registration. We do recognize that there are a few countries where these vaccinations are not available. Please contact nyuad.immunization@nyu.edu if you have difficulty obtaining the mandatory vaccines.

- What if I cannot receive my required vaccinations by the specified deadline? Or if I receive additional vaccinations after I have already uploaded my form?

Please make every effort to complete your vaccinations and upload the vaccination form by the required deadline. If you think that you will have difficulty complying with the mandatory immunization requirements, please email nyuad.immunization@nyu.edu.

- What is meant by 2 MMRs?

MMR is an immunization vaccine against measles, mumps, and rubella (German measles). It is generally administered in childhood after the first birthday, with a second dose before starting school (i.e. age 4/5). The second dose of MMR can be given as early as 4 weeks (28 days) after the first dose and is considered a valid dose if both doses were given after the child's first birthday. The second dose is not a booster, but rather is intended to produce immunity in the small number of people who fail to respond to the first dose.

You can satisfy this requirement with 2 MMR vaccines; 2 individual vaccines of each measles, mumps, and rubella; or 1 MMR and 1 each of measles, mumps, and rubella vaccines. Alternatively, your healthcare provider can order laboratory confirmation of immunity for each- measles, mumps and rubella.

- In the event that my measles, mumps, and rubella (MMR) records are not available and cannot be located, what do I need to do?

Two options are available. You may take the vaccinations again (at least 28 days apart) or you may take a blood test (MMR titers). The blood test will indicate whether you have positive immunity or not. If you do not have positive immunity, then vaccinations will be necessary. Please note that titers are generally not covered by insurance and vary in expense.

- Is it safe to get another MMR vaccine if I have already received 2 vaccines but don’t have documentation?

In general, although it is not ideal, receiving extra doses of the MMR vaccine poses no medical problem. Alternatively, your healthcare provider can order laboratory confirmation of immunity for each- measles, mumps and rubella. If you lack immunity to any of the 3 illnesses, you should receive the combination MMR vaccine.

- Which Meningitis vaccine should I receive?

Incoming college and university students are required to receive the MCV4 vaccine prior to attending school to combat bacterial meningitis (meningococcal disease). You should receive the quadrivalent (MCV4) vaccine, which protects against serogroups A, C, W, and Y. Acceptable vaccines include Menactra (USA), Menveo (USA), Mencevax (worldwide) and Nimenrix (EU). Meningitis vaccines other than the quadrivalent ACWY vaccine will not satisfy the mandatory vaccine requirement.

- What should I do if the meningitis vaccine is not available in my country?

It is important to start this process as early as possible. We strongly urge you to receive the required vaccinations prior to arrival at NYUAD. Failure to do so may affect class registration. We do recognize that there are a few countries where these vaccinations are not available. Please contact nyuad.immunization@nyu.edu if you have difficulty obtaining the mandatory vaccines.

title: Travel Health Services · NYUAD Students
text:
Travel Consultations

Travel consultations are available by appointment to NYUAD students. The consult includes the latest information about the country of your designated travel. Also provided are the recommended vaccines.

We're prepared to provide you with the latest health information and immunization services for your trip.

The earlier you prepare for your trip abroad, the better. Please email nyuad.healthcenter@nyu.edu with your itinerary as soon as you know that you are traveling to determine your travel health requirements.

We advise you to schedule appointments at least 2- 3 weeks in advance of your trip if possible.

Please bring records of prior immunizations with you to your appointment if possible. This will avoid duplication of vaccines that you may have already received.

During your travel consultation, you will receive comprehensive information regarding recommended vaccinations and how to stay healthy and safe while you're traveling.

Your consultation session will also cover:

- Travel Tips

- Travel Safety

- Diseases (i.e. Hepatitis, Malaria, Yellow Fever)

- Safe Food and Water

- Illness and Injury Abroad

- Depending upon your destination, you may receive prescriptions for Malaria prevention.

title: Health Insurance · NYUAD Students
text:
NYU Abu Dhabi provides a dual health insurance system to ensure students receive seamless, comprehensive medical coverage both inside the UAE and internationally. This system combines Sukoon/Bupa for UAE-based care and Blue Cross Blue Shield Global Solutions (formerly GeoBlue) for international coverage.

This dual system ensures that NYUAD students have uninterrupted coverage worldwide

UAE Insurance (Sukoon / Bupa)
This is an enhanced plan that complies with the Health Insurance Law for the Emirate of Abu Dhabi (No. 23 of 2005) and fully meets UAE visa requirements for the Emirate.

Sukoon, administered by Bupa Global, provides comprehensive health insurance coverage within the United Arab Emirates and the GCC Area. Sukoon hand-picked network of worldclass providers are specifically curated to meet the diverse needs of NYUAD students.

- Read a summary of your Sukoon/Bupa coverage in the Sukoon Brochure/Table of Benefits (PDF)

Enrolment Timeline

In compliance with local regulations, students must be physically present in the UAE before enrolment can be initiated.

How to Access Your Insurance Card

- No physical card — digital only

- Access it through the Bupa Global MembersWorld app

Locating Healthcare Providers

Please search the Sukoon medical network providers at medicalnetwork.tameen.ae .

When You Need Care

- Visit a hospital or clinic in the UAE.

- Show your digital insurance card.

- Most services are covered with no co-pay.

Submitting a Claim

If a claim is needed:

- Fill out the Bupa Global claim form

- Submit the completed claim form with receipts to info@bupa-intl.com or via the app.

Important Notes

- Covers a wide network of providers in the UAE and GCC.

- Coverage renews each year automatically.

- First-year students receive access after arriving in the UAE.

Sukoon Contact Information

Email: BupaConnect@bupa-intl.com
Phone: 800-823-2872 (toll-free inside the UAE)
44(0) 1273-323-563 (outside the UAE)
Sukoon website

Global Insurance Blue Cross Blue Shield Global Solutions (Formerly GeoBlue)
All matriculated NYUAD students are eligible for the mandatory global health insurance plan through BCBS. New enrolment begins at the start of the academic year, prior to students departure from their home country.

BCBS (Geo Blue) plan provides easy and unique access to global medical expertise with a responsive, multi-channel service.

Read a Summary of Benefits

- BCBS Guide /Table of Benefits (NYADB)

- BCBS Guide /Table of Benefits (NYADE)

BCBS offers a mobile app that can be used to browse medical providers around the world and to review your schedule of benefits. The app is available for Android and iOS Devices .

Activate Your Account

- Activate your account from the welcome email .

- Download and keep your BCBS ID card .

In an Emergency

- Go to the nearest hospital immediately.

- Contact BCBS team to request a direct pay.

Locating Healthcare Providers

- Use the BCBS app or website to find covered providers.

- Try to request direct pay 48 hours in advance .

Submitting a Claim

- Complete the GeoBlue Medical Expense Claim Form .

- Email it to claims@geo-blue.com with receipts or submit online via the app.

Important Notes

- Coverage for newly enrolled students begins prior to their departure.

- Coverage renews each year automatically.

- Global Network providers in over 190 countries worldwide.

- Multilingual global health team available 24/7.

Outside of the UAE, if you have issues with your Global Insurance card, you will need to contact BCBS directly.

BCBS (GeoBlue) Customer Service:

- Email BCBS (GeoBlue) at customerservice@geo-blue.com

- +1-844-268-2686 (toll-free inside the US)

- +1-610-268-2686 (outside the US)

- Visit www.bcbsglobalsolutions.com

title: Join the RA Squad: Be a Campus Leader · NYUAD Students
text:
Ever wondered who the Resident Assistants (RAs) are? They’re your go-to campus leaders, living on each floor of our residential colleges. RAs create a vibrant community by organizing fun events, offering peer support, and helping with academic queries. Plus, they ensure everything runs smoothly and safely in the dorms — making them essential to your experience at NYUAD. Whether it’s hosting late-night study sessions or leading mental health check-ins, RAs are always ready to lend a hand.

But first, who's Residential Life ? Residential Life fosters a supportive and vibrant on-campus community for all students. Our team is dedicated to creating a safe, inclusive, and engaging living experience, offering resources, programs, and guidance to help students thrive personally and academically.

Residential Life includes a team of nine professional staff members. Resident Assistants report to Residential College Directors and indirectly work, as needed, with the Housing Operations and Central Staff team.

Ready to take on the challenge and become a student leader? Here's what you need to know about the RA selection process and compensation structure for 2027-2028.

Life of a NYUAD Resident Assistant

A Resident Assistant offers daily peer support, plans fun events to build community, handles duty and crisis response, attends meetings and office hours, and helps with facilities and operations - it's all about leadership and making the dorms feel like home!

During your tenure as a Resident Assistant, you will have the opportunity to build on your leadership, problem-solving, and administrative skills, all while also creating a sense of community and lifelong friends for yourself. As an RA, you will also serve on the emergency response team.

Info Sessions

We highly recommend that you attend the Info Session TBD in the Career Cafe, Student Affairs Suite, Campus Center (C2) to know more about the role and responsibilities.

Role Requirements

- Full-time NYUAD student status

- Good University standing

- 3.0 cumulative GPA throughout service

- Full academic year commitment (Fall & Spring in Abu Dhabi mandatory)

- No participation on the Student Government Executive Board during the RA term.

- No involvement as a REACH member while serving as an RA for the first time.

- Participation in RealAD, the Marhaba Committee, and Weyak Facilitator roles is not permitted.

Time Management

Your role as a Resident Assistant will encompass distributing your time between tasks, including but not limited to the list below:

- RA Training

- Conflict Mediation

- Check Ins/Outs

- Emergency On-Call Shifts

- Office Hours

- Monthly, Weekly, and 1:1 Meetings

- Programming

How to Apply

Applying is simple! Applications will be available on Handshake soon. Don't forget to follow all the steps mentioned. You must:

- Submit the Handshake application

- Fill the application form included on the Handshake application

- Attach your resume as part of the Handshake application

Note: There are two separate applications for new (first-time) and returning candidates. Ensure you submit the right one!

- Application Opens : TBD

- Deadline : Early January

Individual Interviews

Whether you're on campus or studying abroad, this interview allows you to showcase your unique skills and leadership potential. It'll take place virtually for those candidates studying away and in-person for those candidates on campus at NYUAD for Spring 2027.

Shortlisted candidates will receive invites for individual interviews in February, where you can dive deeper into why you’d make a great RA.

Status Notifications

Final decisions will be made after a thorough evaluation of each candidate’s application, interview, and fit within the team. All candidates will be notified of their final status (i.e., offer, alternate, no offer) via email in April 2026.

Frequently Asked Questions

- Can I be an RA for only part of the year if I’m studying away?

The RA role is a full academic-year commitment, so it requires your presence for both fall and spring semesters. If you’re unsure about studying away, apply anyway - you can always withdraw if your plans change. Just make sure to notify us at nyuad.reslife@nyu.edu if that happens.

- Do I have to reapply if I’ve been an RA before?

Yes! All returning RAs need to go through the application process again.

- Can I apply to be a Summer RA if I’m in Abu Dhabi?

Starting Summer 2027, the Summer RA role will be open to everyone! The Summer RA selection process will be separate from the academic-year RA process, so anyone interested in a summer position will need to apply through the dedicated Summer RA application process. Stay tuned for more details!

- Can I choose which Residential College I’ll live in as an RA?

You’ll get a chance to tell us your preferences for Residential Colleges during the recruitment process. While we’ll do our best to match you with your preferred residential building, it’s not guaranteed. Placement depends on:

- The number of residents in each residential building

- How many RAs are needed in each community

- Male/female floor ratios

- Class year mix of RA teams

- Number of returning RAs, etc.

If you're offered an RA spot, your letter will mention your assigned community (like A5 Non-Visitation, A2 Visitation, etc.), but your building and room details will come in the summer.

- How long do I have to accept or decline the RA position if I’m offered a spot?

Your offer letter will tell you the deadline to accept or decline, which is typically about a week from the offer date, but it could be less! If you don’t respond by the deadline, it’ll automatically be considered a decline..

- Can I defer my RA offer to next year?

Nope! Your offer is for the specific academic year. If you want to apply for a different year, you’ll need to go through the process again.

- What if I’m an alternate but don’t want to be considered anymore?

You can definitely decline your alternate status if you change your mind. Just know that once you opt out, you can’t ask to be reconsidered as an alternate later.

- I heard RAs move in early — how early is that?

Exact dates aren’t out yet, but expect to return to campus in early August 2026.

- What’s the time commitment like as an RA?

Being an RA takes about 11 hours per week, spread across staff meetings, one-on-ones, collaboration with Residential Life, duty shifts, programs/events, and more. Some weeks might require more time, others less, but the general rule is: academics come first, RA duties come second, before other extracurriculars.

Need More Info? We're Here to Help!

Got any questions or need more details? Don’t hesitate to reach out to us at nyuad.ResLife@nyu.edu . We’re here to support you on your journey to becoming an RA at NYU Abu Dhabi - every step of the way!

title: Life in Our Residential Colleges · NYUAD Students
text:
Welcome to Your Campus Home!

Our Residential Life team is all about helping you make the most of your university experience. From community events to personal support, we’re here to ensure you feel connected, empowered, and supported every step of the way.

In each community, you'll find Resident Assistants (RAs) and Residential Community Directors (RCDs) who work closely with you to build a fun, supportive, and engaging environment. Whether through one-on-one chats, group events, or just hanging out, your RA team is here to make your residential life unforgettable!

Our Residential Buildings

A1 Residential Community: The Only A That Matters!

A vibrant community for first-year students led by RCD Gladys Tarisayi Mwedzi, an NYUAD alumna. With 14 RAs, this community is all about creating a warm, welcoming environment for first-year students. You’ll often find Gladys trying out TikTok dances or sharing meals with friends.

- For more info, contact: nyuad.a1team@nyu.edu or visit the RA Help Desk in the A1C 2nd Floor Lobby

A2 Residential Community: A2 Home 2 You!

Curious and community-driven, Alya AlSuwaidi brings her background in philosophy, sociology, and student affairs to her work in Residential Life. A graduate of Sorbonne Abu Dhabi, she holds a double Bachelor’s in Philosophy and Sociology, studied in French, as well as a French language diploma.

During her four years at Sorbonne, she led the university’s Humanitarian Initiative, spearheading projects focused on mental health awareness and community support. She’s passionate about building inclusive spaces, advocating for well-being, and supporting student growth.

A creative at heart, she enjoys writing, café hunting, and exploring new cultures through language and travel. Fluent in Arabic, English, French, and Tagalog.

- For more info, contact: nyuad.a2team@nyu.edu or visit the RA Help Desk in the A2C 2nd Floor Lobby

A5 Residential Community: A5 Out of 5!

A space for upper-class students led by RCD Ishmal Khalid, an NYUAD alumnus who loves to travel and experiment with new cuisines and desserts. With 16 RAs, this community is designed to give you the space to thrive academically and socially.

- For more info, contact: nyuad.a5team@nyu.edu or visit the RA Help Desk in the A5C 2nd Floor Lobby

A6 Residential Community: A-Sixy and I Know It!

Mansour Abdoulaye is an NYUAD alumnus with a Bachelor’s degree in Economics. Before returning to NYUAD as the A6 Residential College Director, he worked in student finance in his hometown of Niamey, Niger. He has a deep commitment to student support and inclusive leadership, and is passionate about creating spaces where students can thrive both personally and academically.

- For more info, contact: nyuad.a6team@nyu.edu or visit the RA Help Desk in the A6C 2nd Floor Lobby

Building Community and Having Fun

Our Residential Communities host tons of programs each semester, ranging from floor-specific events to campus-wide and off-campus adventures, to bring students together and help you connect with campus life. Whether it’s a movie night, a cultural tour of Abu Dhabi, or supporting events in Student Affairs, there’s something for everyone!

Head over to Engage and sign up for activities within your Residential Community. And don’t forget to check in with your RA — they’re here to help you get the most out of your time at NYUAD.

Student Residents' Rights and Responsibilities

As a resident, you have the right to:

- Peace and Quiet
You deserve a space where you can sleep and study without disruption. Be considerate of others during and outside of quiet hours — it's about creating a space where everyone can focus and relax.

- Security of Your Stuff
Your belongings should feel safe and respected. In return, it's your responsibility to respect the property of others and the community spaces we all share.

- Safety
You have the right to feel safe from any kind of verbal, physical, or emotional intimidation. And it's your job to help keep the environment safe by acting responsibly.

- Cleanliness
Everyone enjoys a clean space, so while you have the right to live in a clean environment, you also have the responsibility to keep common areas tidy and your own space in good condition.

- Respect
Mutual respect is key to community living. You're entitled to voice concerns when someone’s behavior affects your space or comfort. Just be sure to show the same respect to others and their needs.

- Communication
Speak up! Whether it's an issue with a roommate or a community concern, you're encouraged to communicate clearly and respectfully with your Resident Assistant, Residential College Director, or fellow residents.

- Support
Staff are here to help. Whether it’s resolving conflicts or answering questions, reach out for guidance whenever needed.

- Fairness
You have the right to expect fairness in how policies are applied. It’s also your responsibility to follow these policies and procedures.

The best way to ensure these rights? Keep the communication going. Your Residential College Director is here to support you because building a respectful community is what makes it all work. See information on student conduct and policies .

Residential Furnishings and Room Amenities

The University provides each resident with:

-
A bed with a twin XL mattress

-
Desk and desk chair

-
Drawer space

-
Closet or wardrobe space

Recommended Items

Depending on the residence hall assignment and personal preference, residents may wish to bring:

Essentials

-
Bedding ( extra-long twin sheets), linens, and towels

-
Minimal personal belongings, including clothing, toiletries, medications, and study materials

-
Personal technology, including laptops, televisions, gaming consoles, and approved smart devices

Permitted Room Amenities

Residents may bring:

-
Non-halogen desk or floor lamps

-
Area rugs

-
Oil diffusers

-
Irons and steamers may only be used in the designated laundry room. However, both irons and steamers may be stored in residential rooms when not in use.

-
Posters and decorations

-
Clothes hangers

-
Microfridge for suite-style rooms. Individual fridges needs to be approved by the Moses Center for Accessibility and Inclusive Culture

Decorations must be secured using painter’s tape only. Residents may be charged for wall damage caused by adhesives, command hooks, or double-sided tape.

Televisions and speakers should be compact and used responsibly to avoid disturbing roommates or neighboring residents.

Furniture and Accessibility Accommodations

Personal furniture may not be added to residential rooms.

Students requesting specialized furniture or housing accommodations related to a disability must submit documentation and requests through the Moses Center for Accessibility and Inclusive Culture in accordance with University accommodation procedures.

Cooking and Kitchen Appliances

Some residence halls provide microfridge units (combined microwave and refrigerator units).

For fire safety reasons:

-
Hot plates, toaster ovens, grills, air fryers, and similar appliances are prohibited.

-
One toaster is permitted only within apartment-style suite kitchens and must remain stored and used in the kitchen area.

-
Personal fridge. Students approved by the Moses Center for Accessibility and Inclusive Culture for a mini-fridge are required to purchase a model from the approved mini-fridge list provided by Residential Education. The approved list includes multiple options at different price points to ensure compliance with EHS and Facilities Management requirements. All mini-fridges must successfully complete a PAT test before being used in the residence halls.

Related official links:
https://students.nyuad.nyu.edu/student-affairs/student-conduct/nyuad-student-conduct-policy/policies/

title: Undergraduate Housing Information · NYUAD Students
text:
NYUAD guarantees undergraduate housing for students throughout their academic careers, provided the following conditions are met:

- New and Returning Students : Students must meet all housing application deadlines and maintain full-time matriculated status. Returning students must also be enrolled for the selected semester and submit their housing application by the deadline.

- Summer Housing : Available to students attending classes or participating in NYUAD-affiliated internships or research opportunities. Students must meet all application deadlines and be enrolled in an approved summer program. Upon completion, students must check out of their room on the date specified by Residential Life.

- Visiting Students (NYU New York or NYU Shanghai Students studying at NYUAD): Visiting students are guaranteed housing as long as they meet all housing application deadlines and maintain full-time matriculated status during their stay.

To apply for housing at NYU Abu Dhabi, visit the Abu Dhabi Housing Portal .

Following University guidelines, all housing-related communications from NYUAD are sent directly to students, not parents or guardians. This includes important information like deadlines and application instructions, which are sent via email.

Your NYU NetID is your official NYU email address, and all notifications will be sent there. It's your responsibility to regularly check your University email to stay up-to-date.

All housing communications, deadlines, and notices will be sent to your official NYUAD email — so check it regularly!

title: Housing Assignment Process · NYUAD Students
text:
We do our best to match you with your preferred room but keep in mind that due to availability, we can’t guarantee every request will be met. For first-year students, geographic diversity plays a big role in how we assign rooms. This helps foster connections across different regions, so you can broaden your network and make the most of NYU’s global community.

You won’t be able to request specific roommates during your first year at NYU. Why? Because we believe it’s important to meet new people, explore different perspectives, and step outside your comfort zone! We want you to celebrate what you have in common with others while embracing the differences that make NYU Abu Dhabi such a unique place.

For continuing students, the Room Selection process works by assigning you a system-generated time slot, based on your class year as recorded by the Registrar, to pick your room. Keep an eye on your inbox for your exact time slot! If you miss the housing application deadline, you won’t get a time slot and won’t be able to participate in room selection.

Here’s what we consider when assigning rooms for everyone:

- Gender

- Reasonable Accommodations approved by the Moses Center (pending availability)

- Visitation preference

- Geographic diversity (first-year students only)

- Roommate preference

- Your answers to the housing lifestyle questionnaire (though this is a lower priority)

While we try our best, room preferences aren’t always guaranteed — but we’ll do what we can to get you settled comfortably!

Non-visitation Housing

Non-visitation communities within our residential colleges are designated areas where individuals of the opposite sex are not permitted entry. If you're interested in this living experience, you can indicate your preference on your housing application.

Email us at nyuad.ResLife@nyu.edu for more information.

Residential Life Team

Curious about who's behind the scenes? Meet the team that’s here to make your on-campus experience awesome!

title: Housing Options · NYUAD Students
text:
NYU Abu Dhabi offers four main housing communities: A1, A2, A5, and A6, with each floor divided by gender. Every community is supported by Resident Assistants (RAs) who are there to help with education, health, safety, and building a strong community.

First Year Housing | A1 is home to our first-year students, helping them settle into university life

Continuing Student Housing | Returning and visiting students reside in A2, A5, and A6.

Non-Visitation Housing | These are specific buildings and areas where residents of the opposite gender aren’t allowed to visit. If you're interested in this option, just let us know in your housing application.

Accommodation Details

- What is My Room Like?

Rooms range from four-person suites with single rooms, four-person suites with double rooms, to double rooms with shared bathrooms.

Most suites have a shared living room, kitchenette, and two bathrooms. Whether you're in a single or sharing a double, each resident has their own desk and bed. The suite usually comes with seating furniture, a table, and chairs.

- Reasonable Housing Accommodations

In line with federal, state, and city disability laws, New York University offers reasonable accommodations to students who need them.

To learn more, visit the NYU Accessibility Housing (https://www.nyu.edu/students/communities-and-groups/student-accessibility/housing.html) page.

- Why Would A Room Not Be Available?

Sometimes, rooms are reserved for various reasons, like:

- Accessibility needs through the Moses Center for Student Accessibility (https://www.nyu.edu/students/communities-and-groups/student-accessibility.html)

- Facility upgrades

- Temporary or emergency housing

- Reserved staff spaces (like RA Rooms)

- Residential Campus Facilities You Can Count On

- 24/7 front desk with Campus Safety

- Community kitchens and laundry rooms

- Computer rooms with printers, copiers, and scanners

- A lounge area in each building for you to chill and connect.

For more information, speak with your Resident Assistant or email nyuad.ResLife@nyu.edu .

title: Rates and Deadlines · NYUAD Students
text:
Residential Life primarily focuses on assigning housing in accordance with established policies during the housing application process. We do not handle financial aid allocation or housing payment procedures and we do not have access to students' financial aid information or status. It's essential for students to take personal responsibility for managing these details. For support or inquiries about financial aid and or our housing payments, please reach out to nyuad.studentfinance@nyu.edu or visit the Service Center during business hours.

Housing Costs

- Fall and spring semesters : USD 3,000 per semester

- January Term : USD 373* (ensure you are covered by aid or academic course)

- Summer : USD 188 per week (meal swipes are dependent on opportunity funding)

* Rates subject to change

Housing Cancellations

Changed your mind about staying in NYUAD housing? No problem — just make sure to let the Residential Life team know! You have until the day before the term starts to cancel. If you miss the deadline, you’ll face a cancellation fee of USD 100-150, which will be added to your student account.

To cancel, email your request to nyuad.ResLife@nyu.edu . Make sure to review the Housing License for important details, key housing dates, and deadlines

Residential Fine Guidance

We aim to utilize the established fine policies and directives in housing contracts to deter negative behavior and potentially utilize funds collected in a restorative manner for the benefit of the larger housing community.

Please visit our linktree for the current list of fines.

title: Student Conduct · NYUAD Students
text:
Student Conduct at NYUAD supports the maintenance of a safe, accountable, and inclusive community. NYUAD is committed to providing education on the rights and responsibilities of communal membership and the development of individual students.

NYUAD resolves student conduct matters in which a student's behavioral choices may be negatively impacting themselves or others by utilizing a range of responses including: informal guidance, restorative practice, and formal adjudication. NYUAD Student Conduct Officers determine the best approach while also ensuring fundamental fairness in all circumstances. In doing so, Student Conduct Officers work collaboratively with students, faculty, administration, and other community partners to promote student success. — See the Student Reporting Guide (PDF) for where to report concerns

title: Cultural Expectations · NYUAD Students
text:
As an international community of scholars here in the United Arab Emirates, it is important to be conscious of local laws and cultural norms. The UAE is built on generations of Islamic traditions that are rooted firmly in its culture and tribal heritage, forming the very cornerstone of everyday life for an Emirati family. Not all of the specific behavior below is covered by the NYUAD student conduct policy, but NYUAD students are expected to be aware of and respect UAE cultural norms and local laws, as they would respect the cultures and norms of any country they are visiting. Violations of law that substantially disrupt regular operations at NYUAD or threaten the safety and security of the community may result in disciplinary action. Please be mindful of the following while in the UAE:

- Alcohol

According to the student conduct policy, NYUAD undergraduate students are not permitted to purchase, possess, consume, sell, distribute or be in the presence of alcohol on campus.

Being drunk and disorderly is a serious offense in the UAE and is punishable by law.

By law, there is zero tolerance for any person driving under the influence of alcohol. Penalties range from confinement to a fine, deportation and confiscation of the vehicle.

- Attire

While NYU Abu Dhabi does not have a policy on attire or its own dress code, the UAE is a Muslim country and its dress code is based on respect for the religion and culture, morals and values of the UAE. In practice, there are varying degrees of tolerance for clothing styles and how to dress in the UAE. Only male and female gender roles are recognized under UAE law and clothing in most public spaces and government offices must adhere to traditional UAE norms for male and female clothing.

Individuals may feel more comfortable when dressed modestly, which is a requirement in public areas, such as shopping centers, many university campuses, and businesses, and during periods of religious significance such as Ramadan.

Access to official and business buildings may be denied if your dress code is considered inappropriate. Clothing should not expose certain parts of the body, be transparent, display offensive pictures or slogans, display obscene language that might cause religious or cultural offense, or display language that might be interpreted as a symbol of political protest .

- Communal Eating

When taking food from communal dishes, it is the cultural norm for people to use only the right hand.

- Criticism of the Government and Islamic Religion
Criticism of the UAE Government, UAE leaders, or the Islamic faith is illegal and could lead to criminal charges if it has the potential to incite social or political unrest, or is interpreted as taking the form of insult, defamation, slander, or libel. Abuse of the symbols of the UAE’s rulers, including the flag and national emblem is considered a crime.

- Cyclist Regulations

Cyclists must stay on dedicated cycling paths and road lanes. Deviating from the paths or violating traffic law is subject to a fine.

- Disturbing Public Order and Defamation

Spreading false news or rumors and propaganda that defame individuals, disturb public security and harm public interest are crimes punishable by law.

- Drug Possession

Illicit drugs are not tolerated. Drug possession and trafficking are extremely serious offenses, with offenders receiving penalties for prohibited substances, regardless of the amount.

Students must make sure that medicines and medications that may otherwise be prescribed in home countries are not restricted before traveling to the UAE. The UAE Ministry of Health's Drug Control Department in Abu Dhabi publishes a list of controlled medicines and medications. These items are essentially only available in hospitals and in large community pharmacies, under the prescription of doctors, and cannot be imported by individuals. However, the UAE Ministry of Health's Drug Department does have regulations for the personal import of such items.

- Formal Greetings

There are many ways of greeting a person in the UAE. Some men and women choose not to shake hands upon meeting, which should not be considered an insult or offensive. It is generally polite to begin with a verbal greeting, and then allow the person you are greeting to indicate whether shaking hands is welcome.

Typically, men stand when a woman enters the room, and everyone stands when new guests arrive at a social gathering or business meeting, and when an elderly or high-ranking person arrives or leaves.

- Music and Dancing in Public Areas

Loud music and dancing are forbidden in public parks, beaches or common residential areas and allowed only in licensed venues. If a venue does not have a dancing license, you may be asked to stop dancing.

- Public Displays of Affection

Physical displays of affection, regardless of gender, sexuality, or marital status, are considered private matters that should be kept out of public spaces . If a complaint is made, the outcome may lead to criminal charges.

- Public Expression

Any act or verbal or written speech, including on social media, that either violates or is deemed to violate "rules of decency" or "public morals," including public appeals, broadcasts of a song, shouts, cursing, or statements that are immoral or publicly prompt debauchery is punishable by law.

- Public vs. Private

Conduct that occurs in public, including on social media, is regulated by UAE law and custom. The NYUAD campus is open to visitors and most common areas are considered public spaces. Campus residential spaces are private.

- Recorded Conversation

Recording conversations without the consent of all parties to the conversation, including content from private chats, is illegal.

- Sexual Relations

Sexual contact outside of marriage is illegal, as is any public exhibition of sexuality or sexual activity.

- Sitting

Sitting in a manner that allows the sole of a shoe to face another person is considered an insult in the UAE.

- Smoking

Smoking is forbidden in government facilities, offices, malls and shops. Smoking outside designated areas is punishable with a fine. Smoking is not allowed on campus and this includes vaping.

- Taking Photos

There are restrictions on photography in the UAE. This includes military, government and airport buildings and facilities, where photography is strictly prohibited. Such buildings and facilities are often marked with signs stating "no photography."

It is against UAE law to record or take photos or videos of people without their express consent. Taking or sharing photos or videos of people without their consent, including content from private chats, is prohibited. This law also applies to all areas of the NYUAD campus.

- Using Profanity

Swearing and vulgar language are illegal. Rude gestures are considered a serious public offense and may lead to criminal charges.

- Work Visas

It is illegal to work in the UAE without the correct working visa. 'Visa runs' are illegal.

title: Who Will Know? · NYUAD Students
text:
If you come forward with a complaint, who will find out? The answer depends on whether you tell a confidential resource or a private resource. In either case, no information will be shared with anyone outside of the process without your explicit permission. In other words, your story would never be shared with department chairs, faculty, classmate, media, etc. (and, your parents would only be told in an emergency situation).

Confidential

The people listed as confidential resources have the legal privilege of keeping your information private by not sharing it with anyone else without your permission. There are only a few times this would not hold true, including if there was an immediate concern for the health and safety of people in the NYU community — including you. At those times only the necessary information would be shared, not your entire story.

Private

Information that you share with anyone other than the confidential resources listed above will be shared with NYU's Title IX Coordinator and may also be shared with a limited circle of individuals who "need to know" in order to assist in the investigation and resolution. Sharing will happen only as absolutely necessary to aid in the investigation and resolution — and never with anyone outside the process.
