title: FAQs · NYUAD Students
text:
General Questions

- I was assaulted, harassed, or stalked. What now?

If you have experienced any sexual misconduct, relationship violence or stalking, we are here to support you. You don’t have to handle this alone. Confidential counseling and medical support are available to assist you, 24 hours a day.

Visit or call the Student Health and Wellness Center at +971 2-628-8100 . Alternately, you can call a Crisis Response Counselor at the Wellness Exchange who can provide confidential guidance about your options — call +971 2-628-5555 for support.

Learn more about what to do after an incident .

- I was accused of sexual misconduct. What now?

NYU Abu Dhabi is committed to providing support for all members involved in a sexual misconduct case. If you are a student respondent — an individual accused of violating NYU’s Sexual Misconduct, Relationship Violence, and Stalking Policy , we urge you to seek support from your on campus resources. Speaking with a counselor — either at the Student Health and Wellness Center or through the Wellness Exchange — can provide you with a safe, confidential and compassionate listening space.

NYU Abu Dhabi also offers Student Support Facilitators to help complainants or respondents understand their rights and responsibilities as they relate to the investigation, fact-finding, report review, any appeal and resolution. While the Student Support Facilitator honors the privacy considerations of the individual, the Student Support Facilitator is not a confidential resource. The Student Support Facilitator serves to support students by answering questions, providing resources and appropriate referrals, and offering assistance throughout the process. The Student Support Facilitator at NYU Abu Dhabi may assist a complainant or respondent in identifying alternate sources for advocacy, legal representation, confidentiality or support; in managing academic, housing, access to dining facilities, and other immediate and on-going separation needs, as necessary.

- Will my conversations with NYU Abu Dhabi remain confidential?

While your story will never be shared with anyone outside of the process without your explicit permission, there are distinct differences between confidential and private conversations — which may impact your decision on who you wish to confide. Learn more .

- I have information that I think should be listed on this website. What can I do?

Student involvement and feedback are welcome! If there are topics or information missing from this website, or issues we need to further clarify, please contact nyuad.healthpromotion@nyu.edu or Remy Shanker to share your thoughts.

Definitions

- What is consent?

NYU's Sexual Misconduct, Relationship Violence, and Stalking Policy defines consent as "the affirmative agreement to engage in a specific sexual activity with another person. Consent requires an outward demonstration, through mutually understandable words or actions, indicating that an individual has freely chosen to engage in a sexual activity." Consent cannot be obtained through: (1) the use of force of coercion; or (2) by taking advantage of the incapacitation of another individual. Learn more .

- What is sexual misconduct?

Prohibited conduct in NYU's Sexual Misconduct, Relationship Violence, and Stalking Policy includes sexual or gender-based harassment, sexual assault, and sexual exploitation. Also prohibited are relationship violence, stalking, and retaliation:

- Sexual assault is having or attempting to have sexual contact with another individual by force or threat of force, without consent, or where that individual is incapacitated.

- Sexual harassment is any unwelcome sexual advance, request for sexual favors, or other unwanted conduct of a sexual nature, whether verbal, non-verbal, graphic, physical or otherwise.

- Gender-based harassment includes harassment based on gender, sexual orientation, gender identity, or gender expression, which may include acts of aggression, intimidation or hostility, whether verbal or non-verbal, graphic, physical or otherwise, even if the acts do not involve conduct of a sexual nature.

For the full definitions of these prohibited behaviors — as well as the definitions of sexual exploitation, relationship violence, stalking, and retaliation — see NYU's Sexual Misconduct, Relationship Violence, and Stalking Policy , which we encourage the NYU Abu Dhabi community to read.

- What is Title IX?

Title IX of the Education Amendments of 1972 is a comprehensive United States law that prohibits discrimination on the basis of sex in any federally funded education program or activity. Under Title IX, discrimination on the basis of sex can include sexual harassment or sexual violence, such as rape, sexual assault, sexual battery and sexual coercion. Therefore, every university has a responsibility to respond promptly and effectively to reports of sexual misconduct. If a school knows or reasonably should know about sexual harassment or sexual violence that creates a hostile environment, the school must take immediate action to eliminate the sexual harassment or sexual violence, prevent its recurrence and address its effects. Even if a student (or his or her parent) does not want to file a complaint or does not request that the school take any action on the student's behalf, if a school knows or reasonably should know about possible sexual harassment or sexual violence, it must promptly investigate to determine what occurred and then take appropriate steps to resolve the situation. A criminal investigation into allegations of sexual harassment or sexual violence does not relieve the school of its duty under Title IX to resolve complaints promptly and equitably. Learn more .

Resources

- How can I receive immediate support in a crisis?

NYU Abu Dhabi provides immediate comprehensive support for all survivors of sexual assault. A nurse and a counselor are available and on call 24-hours a day to provide support and connect students to resources. Additionally, the Wellness Exchange has Crisis Response Counselors (CRC) that are available by phone 24-hours a day, every day of the year to provide support for students.

The Student Health and Wellness Center and the Wellness Exchange will act as your personal liaison throughout the process of accessing care and services following a sexual assault. They will walk you through the medical, counseling, legal, academic and housing assistance options available.

Not only will they respond in an immediate emergency, but they also can help you plan and schedule any follow up services and support you might need. Call the Student Health and Wellness Center at +971 2-628-8100. When calling the Wellness Exchange hotline at +971 2-628-5555, just ask for the CRC. If you are abroad at an NYU global site, we have established local Wellness Exchange phone numbers you can call for help.

- What other resources does NYU Abu Dhabi offer?

Medical Assistance

In the immediate aftermath of a sexual misconduct incident it is critical that you receive any medical support you may need. Immediately call the Student Health and Wellness Center to speak with a doctor or nurse who can provide you with medical care: +971 2- 628-8100.

Counseling and Emotional Assistance

A survivor of sexual assault can experience emotional as well as physical consequences. Sexual assault is a traumatic experience that can have both immediate and long-term effects.

Initial reactions vary and may include shock, denial, anxiety, guilt, anger, and self-blame. A survivor may experience nightmares, changes in their eating patterns, and depression. Therefore, individuals who have been sexually assaulted are strongly encouraged to obtain help from a professional counselor as soon as they are ready after the incident occurs.

Students can contact the Student Health and Wellness Center at +971 2- 628-8100, Sunday to Thursday, 9am-5pm to set up an appointment with a counselor. Students can also call the Wellness Exchange at +971 2-628-5555 anytime to speak with a counselor over the telephone.

Understanding the Process

Complainants and respondents may have specific questions about the reporting, investigation and resolution process following a sexual misconduct complaint. Tina Wadhwa and Remy Shanker in Student Persistence and Well-being are non-confidential resources who can answer any questions you may have, and provide you with detailed information about what to expect if you are involved in a Sexual Misconduct, Dating Violence or Stalking situation. Further, they act as a liaison should you need support in filing a complaint or contacting the Title IX coordinator.

Residential Help

In some cases of sexual assault, you may have residential or housing needs. Ensuring your safety in your living environment is important, so we stand ready to assist in connecting you to the appropriate resources.

NYU's Office of Equal Opportunity (Title IX office) is available to discuss your housing needs and assist you in obtaining appropriate and available housing accommodations through our Residential Life and Housing Office. If you would prefer for your counselor to speak to the Title IX coordinator on your behalf, you can ask for their support by speaking with your NYU Abu Dhabi counselor or by calling the Wellness Exchange Hotline at +971-2-628-5555.

Academic Help

In the case of a sexual assault or any kind of sexual violence and misconduct, survivors may have a variety of responses and feelings that may impact functioning. We realize there may be academic needs, and we are available to help assist you in receiving support from your school. The Office of Equal Opportunity can assist you in this process and is able to keep information private, only sharing key information to those who need to know. You can contact title9@nyu.edu directly or ask your counselor for their confidential support.

Understanding Your Experience

- I was sexually assaulted in the past. What can I do?

Sexual assault, no matter when it happens, can change your life. It can change your view of yourself and others. You may experience changes in your sleeping and eating patterns. You may have nightmares or flashbacks about the assault. You may be afraid of being alone, or fear being in crowds. Support and help are available for you.

Students can contact the Student Health and Wellness Center at+971 2-628-8100 (Sunday to Thursday, 9am-5pm) to set up an appointment with a counselor . Students can also call the Wellness Exchange at 02-628-5555 anytime to speak with a counselor over the telephone.

- I don't know what to call my experience, but I don't feel comfortable with a sexual encounter I had. What can I do?

If you've had a sexual encounter that left you feeling uncomfortable or violated, but you are not quite sure what to call it, there are people available to listen and support you. Call the Wellness Exchange 24-hour Support Line at +971 2-628-5555 to speak with a counselor — you don't have to give your name. Alternately, you can visit or call the Student Health and Wellness Center at +971 2-628-8100. Either option can connect you with NYU Abu Dhabi resources.

- I'm feeling so many different emotions about this experience. Is this normal?

Reactions to a traumatic experience such as sexual assault vary from person to person. The following are examples of both physical and emotional reactions that a survivor might experience.

Physical Reactions:

- Aches and pains: headaches, back aches, stomachaches

- Sudden sweating, heart palpitations

- Changes in sleep patterns, appetite, interest in sex

- Constipation or diarrhea

- Easily startled by noises or unexpected touch

- More susceptible to colds and illness

Emotional Reactions:

- Shock

- Disbelief

- Embarrassment

- Shame

- Guilt

- Depression

- Disorientation

- Denial

- Fear

- Anxiety

- Anger

- Social withdrawal

- Self-blame

- Concern for the perpetrator

- Lack of concentration resulting in academic difficulties

Helping a Friend

- What can I do to help a friend?

Surviving a sexual assault can be a traumatic experience, and reactions can be varied, in time and in kind. You may be supporting a friend or family member who has survived a sexual assault, and many questions may arise in how to best support them, how to ask the right questions, and offer the best help.

It can be difficult to know how to handle such situations. We can help guide you in understanding your experience as a helper, and the ways to understand and support your loved one. These skills can be utilized regardless of the relationship, whether you're a friend, faculty, staff or parent.

To talk more about how to help a friend or family member you can call the Student Health Center .Alternately, you can call the Wellness Exchange anytime to speak with a counselor confidentially at +971 2-628-5555. We have also established local phone numbers to reach the Wellness Exchange if you are at a different NYU global site.

- What do I do if the assault has recently occurred?

In certain instances, a person may not know what actually happened. They may have woken up and are unsure whether they were assaulted. Again, empower them to make their own decisions. If they want to speak with a counselor, encourage them to contact the Student Health and Wellness Center at+971 2-628-8100 to set up an appointment with a confidential counselor. Students can also call the Wellness Exchange anytime to speak with a counselor over the telephone; it's confidential and available 24-hours a day, every day at +971 2-628-5555.

title: What Is Consent? · NYUAD Students
text:
NYU's Sexual Misconduct, Relationship Violence, and Stalking Policy defines consent as "the affirmative agreement to engage in a specific sexual activity with another person. Consent requires an outward demonstration, through mutually understandable words or actions, indicating that an individual has freely chosen to engage in a sexual activity." Consent cannot be obtained through: (1) the use of force of coercion; or (2) by taking advantage of the incapacitation of another individual.

We encourage you to familiarize yourself with the following details about consent:

- Pressuring someone repeatedly to engage in sexual activity is called coercion. Coercion is NOT consent.

Coercion is repeatedly reassuring your partner that the sexual activity is okay, that your partner will enjoy him/herself, and continuing with sexual activity. Coercion can include:

- Physically maneuvering your partner’s body when she or he keeps pulling away

- Asking repeatedly to engage in sexual activity until your partner says "yes"

- Stating that you will suffer some sort of physical consequence if your partner does not complete a sexual act with you

- An individual who is incapacitated lacks the ability to make informed, rational judgments and cannot consent to sexual activity.

You cannot obtain consent from someone who is:

- Drunk or high

- Passed out

- Asleep

- Physically incapacitated

- Mentally incapacitated

- Being engaged in a long-term partnership, including marriage, does not create automatic consent.

Long-term partners and married couples still need to get consent every time.

- Consent is valid only for that precise moment.

There is no such thing as blanket consent. Consenting to something at 9pm does not necessarily mean it's consensual at 9:15pm.

- Just because you've had consent before, doesn't mean you still do.

Engaging in consensual sexual activity earlier in the day/evening/week/month/year does not grant consent for future sexual activity.

- Consent can be withdrawn at any time.

Including in the middle of engaging in sexual activity.

title: What to Do After an Incident · NYUAD Students
text:
Coping with sexual misconduct, especially sexual violence, can present many challenges and emotions — but you don't have to handle it alone. It doesn't matter what time it is or how long ago something happened. Talk to the Wellness Exchange , the Student Health and Wellness Center , Health Promotions Student Persistence and Well-being , or someone you trust (a friend, loved one or family member) for support as you decide how you want to respond.

What to Do After an Incident?

- Once you're safe, contact the Student Health & Wellness Center for medical support

In the immediate aftermath of a sexual misconduct incident, it is critical that you receive any medical support you may need. Immediately call the Student Health and Wellness Center and speak with a doctor or nurse who can provide you with medical care at +971 2-628-8100.

- If you do not require medical support, call a counselor

Our Counseling Center (+971 2-628-8100 during business hours) or Wellness Exchange (+971 2-628-5555) have counselors on hand to offer confidential support over the phone, meet with you in person during emergencies and discuss your medical, mental health, and legal options. Counselors are available 24 hours a day, every day of the year.

- Read about confidentiality

Privacy and confidentiality have distinct meanings. Medical and mental health professionals are able to keep conversations confidential (subject to certain exceptions explained here ). Other NYU administrators, however, are only able to keep details private. Learn more .

- Be kind to yourself

Remember that an assault is never the survivor's fault. Counseling Services at the Student Health and Wellness Center offer you short-term counseling, self-improvement classes, referrals, and psychiatric medication services — most of which are free. Sexual assault is a traumatic experience that can have both immediate and long-term effects. Survivors of sexual assault are encouraged to obtain help from a professional counselor as soon as they are ready after the incident occurs. You don't have to go through this alone.

- It may also be useful to speak with the Office of Sexual Misconduct Support Services

Tina Wadhwa and Remy Shanker are non-confidential support that can provide you with detailed information about the policy and procedures related to the assessment, investigation and adjudication of a sexual misconduct violation. She can also connect complainants and respondents to campus resources.

- Consider making a formal report to NYU

Contact NYU's Office of Equal Opportunity at title9@nyu.edu , to submit a formal complaint, or report an incident online . Once you file a report with NYU, you may request that the matter remain private or that no investigation be conducted. However, NYU will balance that request against its commitment to a safe learning, living, and working environment for all community members. For more detailed information, please consult the policy .

- Consider academic or residential support

NYU will provide temporary or permanent protective accommodations and measures, which may include separation orders, residence modifications, academic accommodations or work schedule modifications, where appropriate and reasonably available under the circumstances. sections.title: What to Do After an Incident · NYUAD Students
sections.text: Coping with sexual misconduct, especially sexual violence, can present many challenges and emotions — but you don't have to handle it alone. It doesn't matter what time it is or how long ago something happened. Talk to the Wellness Exchange , the Student Health and Wellness Center , Health Promotions Student Persistence and Well-being , or someone you trust (a friend, loved one or family member) for support as you decide how you want to respond.

sections.title: What to Do After an Incident?
sections.text:
- Once you're safe, contact the Student Health & Wellness Center for medical support

In the immediate aftermath of a sexual misconduct incident, it is critical that you receive any medical support you may need. Immediately call the Student Health and Wellness Center and speak with a doctor or nurse who can provide you with medical care at +971 2-628-8100.

- If you do not require medical support, call a counselor

Our Counseling Center (+971 2-628-8100 during business hours) or Wellness Exchange (+971 2-628-5555) have counselors on hand to offer confidential support over the phone, meet with you in person during emergencies and discuss your medical, mental health, and legal options. Counselors are available 24 hours a day, every day of the year.

- Read about confidentiality

Privacy and confidentiality have distinct meanings. Medical and mental health professionals are able to keep conversations confidential (subject to certain exceptions explained here ). Other NYU administrators, however, are only able to keep details private. Learn more .

- Be kind to yourself

Remember that an assault is never the survivor's fault. Counseling Services at the Student Health and Wellness Center offer you short-term counseling, self-improvement classes, referrals, and psychiatric medication services — most of which are free. Sexual assault is a traumatic experience that can have both immediate and long-term effects. Survivors of sexual assault are encouraged to obtain help from a professional counselor as soon as they are ready after the incident occurs. You don't have to go through this alone.

- It may also be useful to speak with the Office of Sexual Misconduct Support Services

Tina Wadhwa and Remy Shanker are non-confidential support that can provide you with detailed information about the policy and procedures related to the assessment, investigation and adjudication of a sexual misconduct violation. She can also connect complainants and respondents to campus resources.

- Consider making a formal report to NYU

Contact NYU's Office of Equal Opportunity at title9@nyu.edu , to submit a formal complaint, or report an incident online . Once you file a report with NYU, you may request that the matter remain private or that no investigation be conducted. However, NYU will balance that request against its commitment to a safe learning, living, and working environment for all community members. For more detailed information, please consult the policy .

- Consider academic or residential support

NYU will provide temporary or permanent protective accommodations and measures, which may include separation orders, residence modifications, academic accommodations or work schedule modifications, where appropriate and reasonably available under the circumstances. We will work with you to coordinate this assistance upon request, regardless of whether an investigation is pursued. Contact NYU's Office of Equal Opportunity at title9@nyu.edu for assistance.

title: Student Conduct Flow Chart · NYUAD Students
text:
Download Student Conduct Flow Chart (PDF)

The Community Values standards apply to all of the NYUAD campus, which is a public space, so violations can be reported in numerous ways.

They are reported to Community Values Team (CVT) via:

- Student Life On-Call Staff

- Campus Safety Reports

- Student/Staff/Faculty individual reports

- Community-Based Reports

- RAs (Residential Assistants)

- RCDs (Residential College Directors)

Community Values violations are often directed to individual Community Values Team (CVT) members, based upon their specific sphere of responsibilities. More complex incidents are brought to the entire CVT by the individual members.

The responsible CVT member then initiates contact with the student(s) involved via email . This email explains the specific Community Values violation and where it is written in the Student Conduct Portal pages. An exploratory interview appointment is completed.

At that time, the CVT member will determine the next step.

More complex incidents are brought to the entire CVT where they evaluate the most restorative and educational approach in addressing the violation. (This may include anything from a verbal or written warning, a restorative practice option, or at times an actual student conduct sanction).

Appropriate options are presented to the student in violation of the NYUAD community values . (Assessment of student responsibility is determined by the “preponderance of evidence,” meaning a reasonable person looking at the available information would be at least 51% sure that the student was responsible for the incident).

NEXT STEPS:

Student carries the restorative practice agreed upon (by both Community Values Team member and the student),

or if a sanction is issued, this information is listed on their records .

A time-limited appeal process can be initiated by the student by notifying in writing either the Head of Community Values and Conflict Transformation, Frank Hunt Blaney (or, the Senior Dean of Students, Aisha Al Naqbi ).

title: NYUAD Student Government · NYUAD Students
text:
Mission

The New York University Abu Dhabi Student Government, elected by the student body, represents, advocates, and serves the student body. Student Government aims to center integrity, transparency, and mutual trust in all its work. In recognition of the global context it operates in, and the diverse stakeholders it works with, Student Government aims to build strong bonds of inclusion and extensively collaborate with university administrators, staff, and faculty to advance long-term student and institutional interests. The NYUAD Student Government abides by the tenets set forth in its Constitution .

Vision

Student Government aims to build a shared experience in which every student — despite their background, opinions, and/or goals — is a valued stakeholder in the NYUAD community. Our efforts are targeted toward creating a space and culture in which students take ownership of all matters pertaining to their undergraduate experience at NYUAD. Through student-centered advocacy, and decentralizing agency and information, Student Government strives to drive transformational institutional change. Student Government hopes to construct a community culture that is marked by mutual trust and respect, and in which every student feels empowered to not only succeed in their personal journey, but also to build a collective student legacy at our rapidly growing, though still young, university.

title: Elections · NYUAD Students
text:
When Are Elections Held?

NYUAD Student Government elections are held three times per year, in April, September, and November .

Who is Elected and When?

- April

The Executive Board, Management, Class Representatives, and Academic Representatives are all elected in April during the General Elections. The only exception is the First Year Class Representative election, which takes place in September.

The application for Committee Chairs for the following semester is also open at the same time. However, note that the Committee Chairs are appointed by the newly elected Executive board through a selection process instead. After Committee Chairs are appointed, they select committee members who form a team dedicated to meet students’ specific interests.

- September

The First Year Class Representative will be elected by the 2nd week of September. The application will open during the first GA and will be communicated to all first-year students via official means of communication and miscellaneous online platforms. All first-year students who are passionate about improving the first-year student experience are strongly encouraged to apply.

- November

In November, a midterm election occurs for the Sophomore and Junior Class Representatives as well as the NYUAD Senator, who only serve one-semester terms. New Committee Chairs are also appointed in November for the upcoming semester.

Elections Commissioner

The Election Commissioner is responsible for overseeing and conducting fair Student Government elections. The Elections Commissioner is a one-year long elected position.

The Commissioner typically organizes online profiles and platforms for the candidates, a Candidates Forum where students can ask questions, and voting processes. The elected Commissioner will select a committee of commissioners at their discretion which while serving on a semester-by-semester basis with the option of reapplying.

If you have any questions regarding elections, you are welcome to contact the Election Commission at nyuad.elections@nyu.edu .

The General Assembly (GA) hears the concerns of the student body and is the best forum for all students to discuss and vote on student-body-wide concerns. It is also rumored that special treats (read: Magnolia’s Banana Pudding) are served as a reward for GA attendance.

title: Student Government Structure · NYUAD Students
text:
In order to comprehensively represent the entire student body, the Student Government is composed of five separate bodies, with the Executive Board acting as the executive head of the structure. Consult the chart below to better understand the body’s structure and working.

Executive Board

In order to comprehensively represent the entire student body, the Student Government is composed of five separate bodies, with the Executive Board acting as the executive head of the structure. Consult the chart below to better understand the body’s structure.

Position | Description

President | The President liaises with other NYU campuses and schools, represents the interests of the student body to university leadership, and chairs all meetings of the Executive Board, Student Council, and General Assembly. The President sets the agenda for Executive Board and Council meetings along with the Vice President. Additionally, the President oversees all academic-related advocacy, chairing the Academics Board composed of all four Academic Representatives.

Vice President | The Vice President oversees all student experience related advocacy led by the Class Representatives and Committee Chairs. They also represent student interest in regular meetings with university administration.

Chief of Staff | The Chief of Staff manages internal council workflows, record-keeping, and represents student interests in regular meetings with university leadership. They also officially communicate on behalf of the Student Government and chair the Public Relations Committee. Additionally, the Chief of Staff oversees Management.

Senator | The Senator represents the interests of the NYUAD student body in the Student Senators’ Council, Student Government Assembly, and the University Senate. They report back to the council on a regular basis and ensure connectivity of the Abu Dhabi campus with other portal campuses.

Management

Management consists of the Chair of Events, Chair of Budgets and SIGs, and the Chair of Diversity. Management works on various student-body wide issues relating to programming, funding and SIG management, and advancing diversity, equity, and inclusion goals. Oftentimes, it will also act as an advisory body for the Executive Board and may assist it in advancing student body-wide interests.

Position | Description

Chair of Budgets and SIGs | The Chair of Budgets and SIGs oversees the Student Government budget and leads the Funding Board, which is responsible for allocating funding to all Student Interest Groups (SIGs) on campus.

Chair of Events | The Chair of Events plans and executes all large-scale programming for the entire student body, with the support of a dedicated committee — the Events Board.

Chair of Diversity | The Chair of Diversity works closely with Spiritual Life, Intercultural Education and Conflict Transformation (SLICECT) and the Office of Inclusion and Equity (OIE) to advance institutional diversity, equity, inclusion, and belonging goals. The Chair of Diversity also serves as a member and represents student interests on the Inclusion, Equity and Action Committee (IEAC).

Chair of the Domestic Students Advisory Board | The Chair of the Domestic Students Advisory Board (DSAB) leads the DSAB, an autonomous body within the Student Government that operates to address the unique needs, interests, and concerns of domestic students in all aspects of their differentiated experience.

Class Representatives

The four Class Representatives serve to represent the specific interests of their classes in meetings with the Executive Board, the Student Council and the university administration. Their work revolves around class-centered programming, advocacy, and ensuring effective communication on class-specific issues. In addition to this, they serve as members of the Funding Board, which makes all funding decisions relating to SIGs on campus. Lastly, they act as the chair of their class committees, actively setting the agendas, priorities, and the mandate of the committees.

Academic Representatives

The four Academic Representatives represent students from each academic division: Engineering, Arts and Humanities, Sciences, and the Social Sciences. They are responsible for liaising with their respective deans and advocate for the interests of their division on the Council and in meetings with the university’s academic leadership. They also serve on various committees such as, but not limited to, the Faculty Council, Academic Affairs Advisory Committee, Undergraduate Curriculum Committee, Core Curriculum Committee, Capstone Task Force, etc. Lastly, they also act as the chair of their respective student academic committees.

Committee Chairs

There are eight Committee Chairs in the NYUAD Student Government; each Committee Chair works to advance student interests within the mandate defined by their committee charters. These committees are defined as such: Athletics, Campus Spaces, Dining, Financial Affairs, Global Affairs, Health and Wellness, Library and IT, and Sustainability. As chairs of the aforementioned committees, they are the leading agenda-setters on institutional work and student priorities in these areas. They liaise with a variety of administrators across the board in order to effectively advocate for student interests relating to their jurisdiction. Committee Chairs are appointed by the Executive Board and are non-voting members of the council.

title: Art Gallery · NYUAD Students
text:
The NYUAD Art Gallery presents museum-quality exhibitions of art and culture across historical and contemporary topics, with a special emphasis on subjects of regional concern and international significance. The scholarly mandate of the NYUAD Art Gallery will complement nearby museums and commercial galleries. We will regularly host faculty- and guest-curated exhibitions and artist research residencies in collaboration with the academic divisions.

Mission and Themes

The gallery’s mission is to catalyze cross-disciplinary intellectual and creative activity within the university, to link NYUAD to the Abu Dhabi public, and to serve as a regional arts hub for local and international communities.

During its first five years, the gallery will investigate three thematic areas:

- The Environment: Built and Natural

- Arabic and Islamic Art and Culture

- Art in Global Dialogue

Each area is of particular relevance to NYUAD and its role. We also hope to mount one annual experimental exhibition, the product of a curatorial practicum and cross-disciplinary opportunity for student-faculty working groups to experiment with exhibition strategies.

The Team

The gallery’s team of museum-trained professionals support arts throughout the campus — student and faculty arts initiatives, such as the Christo and Jeanne-Claude Award, student exhibitions, and capstone presentations. We will also manage a gallery for student and faculty projects in the Arts Center, and care for the campus art collection. The team works closely with academic departments as well as our public-facing peers in the Institute and the Arts Center.

What To Expect in Future Exhibitions

The coming years will see exhibitions ranging from historic Islamic medical manuscripts, mid-century-Modern art, historic Arabic photography, and a variety of faculty- and guest-curated projects, in addition to contemporary and modern exhibitions curated by the gallery’s director. Those interested in developing exhibitions are encouraged to contact Maya Allison at maya.allison@nyu.edu .

Visit the NYUAD Art Gallery website.

title: Campus Art · NYUAD Students
text:
The Arts at NYU Abu Dhabi

NYU Abu Dhabi has a multi-faceted program dedicated to the arts, which includes arts programs that simultaneously serve the public and the academic arts curriculum. The arts as a core program launched when NYUAD welcomed its first class in 2010. NYUAD’s strong tradition of creative activity emerges alongside similar world-class cultural organizations on Saadiyat Island.

The arts at NYUAD serve as an engine for education, dialogue, and cultural exchange. As part of this mission, the University has developed a Campus Art Collection. These works include new site-specific art commissions, and key acquisitions presented in campus areas where both the internal and public communities mingle. The works are specifically chosen for their range and ability to support a curriculum that exposes students to challenging ideas, bodies of knowledge, cultural traditions, and transformative achievements.

Alongside the Campus Art Collection, the campus serves as a site for cultural dialogue on multiple fronts, inside the classroom and with the public, encompassing several arts venues. The Arts Center presents distinguished professional artists from around the world alongside student, faculty, and community productions. The NYUAD Art Gallery department includes a teaching museum-gallery that presents curated landmark exhibitions led by museum-trained staff, and a Project Space for emerging artists, faculty, and students in the Arts Center, as well as substantial book publication activity.

Through the Collection, the Arts Center, and the Art Gallery, the University demonstrates its recognition that bringing important artworks to the student, faculty, and UAE community is critical to the success of this unique academic institution. Support of artists through building a collection is a key responsibility for a leading educational institution.

About the Campus Collection

In 2012, an Art Committee was formed at NYUAD to develop an overarching vision for the Campus Art for NYUAD’s campus on Saadiyat Island. The committee comprises NYUAD representatives from the faculty, arts, and administration, as well as members of the University’s government partner.

To date, there are two site-specific commissions, and a number of substantial works, in the collection. A key work greets visitors to the Welcome Center: the 2017 accession of the monumental installation by the late Hassan Sharif (UAE, 1951-2016), entitled Copper (2015)

Copper by Hassan Sharif

Among the first accessions for the Campus Art Collection is a monumental installation by the late Hassan Sharif (UAE, 1951-2016), entitled Copper (2015), now permanently installed in the Welcome Center.

- Learn more about Copper

Hassan Sharif made a vital contribution to conceptual art and experimental practice in the Middle East through 40 years of performances, installations, drawing, painting, and assemblage. As an artist, he pursued a pointedly contemporary vocabulary, drawing on the intermedia of Fluxus and the potential in British Constructionism's systemic processes of making. Hassan Sharif ’s early career included co-founding the Emirates Fine Arts Society. In the 1980s, after Sharif returned from studying art in London, he co-founded an avant-garde group, complete with a manifesto and exhibitions. His early exhibitions generated both excitement and heated public debates. He is now the most eminent contemporary artist from the UAE, and is represented in major museum collections internationally. He is best-known for his laborious textile sculptures, a reference that is here beautifully rendered in copper.

On Cosmic Clouds by Tomás Saraceno

The first major site-specific commission was unveiled in 2017, titled On Cosmic Clouds , by renowned Argentinian artist Tomás Saraceno. It is on permanent view in the Library of NYU Abu Dhabi. Saraceno conceived this project specifically for the library, suspending three sculptural constellations under the architectural oculi that span the arching ceiling.

- Learn more about On Cosmic Clouds
On Cosmic Clouds scatters sun from the oculi above in a myriad of reflections across the space. These constellations are clusters of modular units, partially covered with mirrored panels, interconnected by strings that form a delicate net composition. The sculptural elements hang in positions devised to program ever-shifting, space-activating illuminations that respond to the room’s colors, textures, and the direction of the sunlight.

-
Berlin-based Saraceno’s research delves into the worlds of art, architecture, natural sciences, astrophysics and engineering. His floating sculptures, community projects, and interactive installations propose and explore new, sustainable ways of inhabiting and sensing the environment. On Cosmic Clouds posits interdisciplinary research as a symbiosis of art, science and knowledge, towards a better way of living, in tune with the planet, Sun and natural forces.

-
On Cosmic Clouds is ultimately a reinterpretation of an astronomical apparatus: a sundial that creates and maintains linkages with the outside world and skies above the Library, recording Earth’s sidereal, or astronomical, day. The astronomical metaphor is also inspired by the early forms of navigation based on stellar movements, a science originally developed in the Arab world.

Whirlabout (Dynamo) by Alice Aycock

In April 2019, a sculpture by American artist Alice Aycock was installed in the West Plaza of the NYUAD campus. Entitled Whirlabout (Dynamo) , the artist conceived the piece specifically for the University. Responding to its site outside the Experimental Research Building, she visualizes the energy of thought and ideas as a series of spiral vortexes gathering momentum – each vortex emerging from the one below as whirlpools of thought firing like exuberant neural patterns of energy.

- Learn more about Whirlabout (Dynamo)
Aycock intended for the work to have a somewhat random, haphazard quality – piling up on itself, spinning off into the air and forming a dynamic three-dimensional massing of forms. The sculptural assemblage is a metaphor for the way ideas connect in dynamic and unpredictable ways in pursuit of knowledge. The sculpture operates as an exclamation point vis-à-vis the architecture of the surrounding buildings. It also references wind and weather patterns (e.g. dust storms and sandstorms and cyclones).

-
Aycock has lived in New York City since 1968. Her works can be found in numerous collections including the Museum of Modern Art, the Whitney Museum, the Brooklyn Museum, the Louis Vuitton Foundation, the LA County Museum, the National Gallery of Art, the Sheldon Museum of Art, Storm King Art Center, and the Sprengel Museum in Hanover, Germany. She exhibited at the Venice Biennale, Documenta VI and VIII and the Whitney Biennial. Aycock’s public sculptures can be found in many major cities in the U.S.

The University’s Chief Curator, Maya Allison, chairs the Campus Art Committee and spearheads the ongoing initiative. Her department’s museum team oversees the care of the campus collection, including regular cleaning and conservation activity.

title: Institute Events · NYUAD Students
text:
The NYU Abu Dhabi (NYUAD) Institute serves as the primary venue in Abu Dhabi for sophisticated research, creative production, and academic excellence. By hosting a diverse array of symposia, seminars, presentations, cinematic screenings, galleries, and stage productions, it promotes the university's scholarly goals while building bridges between international and local academic circles. Our initiatives span the spectrum of technology, sciences, and liberal arts, emphasizing key investigative fields such as artificial intelligence, medical advancements, biological sciences, aerospace, and sustainable energy, alongside the rich cultural heritage of the Emirates. These high-caliber programs elevate the academic work conducted at NYU Abu Dhabi, establishing a vital connection with the university's prestigious global research and graduate divisions. By gathering world-class specialists and visionaries for engagements in both New York and Abu Dhabi, the Institute reinforces the Global Network and encourages partnership with leading institutions across the world. It stands as a focal point for the intellectual community in the UAE and the Gulf, inviting broad participation beyond the university and driving meaningful global dialogue.

All Institute public events are free, and transportation is provided to the venue of the event. Students can find out about Institute events and research by going to the Institute’s website . In addition, the Institute publishes monthly brochures and posters that can be found around campus.

title: First Year Experience · NYUAD Students
text:
First Year Experience

Incoming students' first-year experience kicks off as early as the summer before joining NYUAD on campus. This entails a steady flow of email communications from the Class Year Experience team on topics ranging from immigration, class registration, information sessions, online modules, and more.

On arrival to campus during the First Year check-in window, students are welcomed in person and are invited to mandatory orientation sessions throughout Marhaba week.

Students are connected with their Weyak Facilitators during Marhaba and will stay connected with them across the Fall semester as they complete the Weyak Program. This programming focuses on four key areas:

- Space — Navigating the NYUAD campus and establishing a sense of belonging in its spaces, while exploring Saadiyat Island, Abu Dhabi, and the broader UAE.

- Self — Building confidence and fostering a deeper sense of personal identity throughout the NYUAD experience.

- Community — Forming connections with the first-year class and the wider campus community, while learning about community expectations, cultural norms, and campus policies.

- Purpose — Setting goals for personal growth and finding meaningful ways to contribute to NYUAD, the UAE, and the wider communities to which students belong.

Students’ First Year Experience also involves interconnected collaborations across departments and stakeholders, including the First Year Class Representative. Class Year Experience works closely with these partners to create and facilitate focused programs and activities for first-year students across the academic year.

If you would like to work with the Class Year Experience team to support first-year students, check out our Marhaba Student Committee Member and/ or Weyak Facilitator opportunities!

He will always say yes to a conversation so if you ever see him on campus, say hi.

title: Marhaba · NYUAD Students
text:
What is Marhaba?

Marhaba , meaning “welcome” in Arabic, is a vibrant and essential orientation program designed for all first-year students. Kicking off with move-in, Marhaba sets the stage for an exciting transition into university life. The program features engaging sessions led by Student Affairs staff, faculty, campus administrators, and student leaders — all aimed at helping new students feel at home away from home.

Marhaba offers invaluable support for first-year students as they:

- Reflect on their experience of being new to campus and gain a deeper understanding of Saadiyat Island, Abu Dhabi, and the UAE.

- Receive a comprehensive orientation to campus life, resources, and community expectations.

- Strengthen connections within their class and with the broader NYUAD community.

- Navigate cultural understandings.

- Are introduced to academic programs.

- Are introduced to spaces and opportunities that foster holistic growth, e.g., sports, Student Interest Groups (SIGs), volunteering opportunities, etc.

- Prepare for an enriching journey at NYUAD

Intercultural Development Inventory

The Intercultural Development Inventory (IDI) is an assessment tool that helps measure awareness and sensitivity to cultural differences. It is used globally to foster intercultural dialogue and build skills for engaging with cultural complexity. NYUAD has chosen the IDI to support its goal of creating a more inclusive community. By enhancing intercultural intelligence, the IDI aligns with the results from the Our NYUAD, Journey to Belonging survey, helping promote a stronger sense of belonging through a shared framework for understanding cultural and identity differences.

All first-year students are required to complete the IDI assessment prior to Marhaba. During Marhaba, they will attend a session that provides a debrief of their class results, including their collective orientation. After Marhaba, students will participate in two additional IDI-related sessions as part of the Weyak Program, where they will review their Individual Development Plan (IDP) and continue to deepen their understanding of intercultural competencies.

Intercultural Conflict Style Workshop

All first-year students are required to attend the Intercultural Conflict Style (ICS) workshop to learn more about how they engage with conflict. Students can also get support from Restorative Practice Ambassadors (RPAs), who are trained student leaders who focus on conflict coaching and mediation.

Schedule

Marhaba programming will run August 20 to August 24, 2025 . Download the Corq App to access the full schedule.

title: The 2026 Presidential Welcome RealAD Show · NYUAD Students
text:
Paired with a welcome by NYU President Linda G. Mills, NYUAD Vice Chancellor Fabio Piano, and NYUAD Associate Vice Chancellor of Student Affairs Baishakhi Taylor, The RealAD Show is an annual production for first-year students that uses theater – written and performed by upper-year NYUAD students – to present some of the experiences students may encounter as they transition to university life. Through dance, music, comedy, and drama, the cast portrays life at NYUAD and across the global network, covering topics such as well-being, mental health, diversity, and being in and of the UAE, while highlighting available campus resources.

As part of our commitment to creating more space for presence and connection IRL (In Real Life) , this will be a device-free experience. Inspired by the power of the arts to bring people together, we invite attendees to set aside their devices and fully immerse themselves in the experience. Attendees will receive a phone pouch to secure devices for the duration of the performance. The pouch is a keepsake for other moments to make space for greater connection and engagement.

About The RealAD Show

Every summer, a new group of students comes together from across NYU's global campus to make their show from scratch.

There are no scripts when the process begins.

Over the course of the summer, the cast write songs, scenes, monologues, comedy, and whatever else the year demands. They talk about what they are experiencing, what they wish someone had told them, what they are afraid to say out loud, and what they think the students arriving behind them need to hear.

Hundreds of pieces are written. Most never make it into the show.

What remains becomes a kind of time capsule: this group of students, at this particular moment, expressing what it's like to be here.

The result is performed for thousands of incoming students across NYU New York, Abu Dhabi, and Shanghai.

Your Well-being, Health, and Safety Resources

As an NYU Abu Dhabi student, while academics might be your primary focus, taking intentional steps to nurture your physical, mental, social, emotional, and spiritual well-being is crucial to meeting your goals. This holistic approach can help you navigate challenges and enrich both your personal and academic experiences. We are dedicated to supporting your involvement in opportunities that enable you to excel at university and beyond. The resources highlighted below are designed to empower and support your ongoing well-being journey.

NYUAD Student Health Center
The Student Health Center offers free of cost, appointment-based, and urgent care support for all NYUAD students. If you're experiencing stress, anxiety, having trouble sleeping, focusing, struggling with your relationship with food, body image, or have lost interest in things that have brought you joy- the Student Health Center can help. Please reach out to nyuad.caremanagement@nyu.edu to learn more about using your health insurance within and outside of the UAE.

Wellness Exchange
The Wellness Exchange is a mental health resource at NYUAD. Call the 24-hour hotline at (+971) 2 628-5555 or chat via the Wellness Exchange app 24/7 ( iPhone | Android ) with a certified counselor about any day-to-day challenges or health concerns, including medical issues, stress, depression, anxiety, and eating disorders. No concern is too big or too small.

NYUAD Student Persistence and Well-being
Student Persistence and Well-being empowers students to cultivate holistic well-being to thrive academically and personally. Book a session with a Student Support Coach, who can help you build skills and strategize to meet your goals. Health Promotions and Student Well-being provides both mandatory and opt-in initiatives that promote mental health, foster resilience, and support emotional regulation through integrated campus opportunities. Student Persistence and Accessibility connects students of determination with the Moses Center for Student Accessibility (CSA) at NYU for appropriate accommodations and resources across NYU’s global network.

REACH - NYUAD’s Peer Support Group
REACH (Raising Empowered Advocates for Community Health) is a well-being peer support group at NYUAD that fosters brave spaces on campus through workshops, dialogue sessions, community-building activities, and by highlighting university resources and support.‘ The Nook ’, a peer support space, is open to all students to chat with a trained peer about whatever is on your mind.

Here4U Online Digital Well-being Hub
Here4U is NYUAD's digital well-being hub, designed to bring together resources in a creative, engaging, and self-reflective format that offers quick, evidence-based tools and practical strategies to support students across a wide range of well-being needs - from managing stress and staying motivated to finding balance, building connections, navigating uncertainty, and developing healthy habits. Designed with accessibility, flexibility, and ease of use in mind, Here4U allows students to access support on their own terms, at their own pace. The website is fully available in both English and Arabic, making well-being resources more accessible to our diverse student community.

The NEST العُشّ
NYU IRL (In Real Life) is a campus-wide commitment to being more present. Take a look at our upcoming IRL programs at NYUAD to make space for shared moments of deeper connection and engagement. At the center of this movement is The NEST العُشّ (Al-‘Ush), located in A5A-204. The NEST العُشّ is NYU Abu Dhabi's permanent device-free space designed to help our community step away from screens and into the moment. Programming includes open drop-in hours, game nights, vision-boarding sessions, and workshops that invite you to pause - play - connect. This is your invitation to look up, lean in, and make the most of our time together.

NYUAD Residential Life
Residential Life manages student housing and enriches the undergraduate experience by building community, organizing programs, and fostering a strong sense of belonging within the residences. Resident Assistants (often referred to as RAs), are student leaders who work to promote an inclusive community, and can support and guide you in the residences, help resolve conflicts (often with Restorative Practice Ambassadors), and connect you with resources.

NYUAD Athletics (Go Falcons!)
From Physical and Health Education courses and intercollegiate competitions to cherished NYUAD traditions, the Athletics team offers opportunities for students to enhance their physical well-being and fosters a strong sense of community and belonging. Whether on the fields, mats, courts, or engaging in activities, like biking, kayaking, swimming, or climbing, there’s something for everyone. Use the online booking system, FABS , to register for facility access, group classes, and to rent lockers and equipment.

NYUAD Student Life and Weyak Program
Student Life supports intentional student learning, leadership, and community engagement that enhance the academic program and enrich students with a broader understanding of themselves and of the UAE. The Weyak program supports first-year students through trained upper-class students who can serve as your informal mentor and advocate in helping you transition into university.

NYUAD Center for Student Belonging
The Center for Student Belonging offers a variety of programs that enable students to develop and refine their cultural humility by engaging with differences and commonalities, exploring values, and reflecting on their personal growth. Restorative Practice Ambassadors (RPA) are student leaders who are skilled in proactive conflict transformation and collaborate with RAs and other groups to cultivate a culture of conflict competence at NYUAD. Connect with an RPA at nyuad.conflicttransformation@nyu.edu and learn more about their programs and initiatives.

NYUAD Career Development Center
The Career Development Center (CDC) plays an integral role in your undergraduate experience by providing guidance, advising, programs, and resources . From choosing a major, CV support, finding jobs and internships, and all the next steps in students' unique career paths, the CDC empowers students throughout their time at NYUAD and beyond.

NYUAD Civic Engagement and Service
Civic Engagement and Service (CES) builds bridges between NYUAD and the UAE through cultural, outreach, and volunteer engagements. Connecting with the culture of the UAE is an important part of creating a well-rounded experience during your time at NYUAD. Service programs are a great way to proactively immerse yourself in the UAE, give back, and seed social impact.

NYUAD Campus Safety
Campus Safety is committed to providing safety and security for our community and property, enabling the pursuit of academic and professional goals. For quick references, please note that the Campus Safety information is available at the back of your campus ID, and you can contact them 24 hours a day, 7 days a week at 02-628-7777 or nyuad.campussafetylink@nyu.edu .

UAE Cultural Expectations, NYUAD Community Values, and Relationship Respect
NYUAD students are expected to be aware and respectful of UAE cultural norms and local laws , which are deeply rooted in Islamic traditions and Emirati cultural heritage. Fostering a campus culture of mutual care and respect is central to our community, and we are committed to a community centered on Non-Discrimination and Anti-Harassment , free of bias, prejudice, discrimination, retaliation, and harassment regardless of any demographic factors - no matter the location of NYU. Please also familiarize yourself with NYU’s global sexual misconduct, relationship violence, and stalking policy , which highlights prohibited behavior, pathways for reporting, and resources available.

Maybe Next Year It's You!

If something in the show resonated with you, or if you found yourself thinking about what you would have said, you might want to make The RealAD Show with us.

Auditions for The 2027 RealAD Show will take place in Spring.

We are looking for students who are curious, funny, thoughtful, musical, strange, honest, theatrical, not theatrical at all, or simply have something they want to explore.

You do not need to see yourself as a writer or performer.

Want to hear when auditions open? Sign up for updates or follow us on Instagram at @nyurealityshow .

The Process

The RealAD Show is made through conversation, experimentation, writing, music, movement, rehearsal, and a lot of trial and error.

You do not have to arrive knowing how to write a monologue or compose a song.

You do not have to have your NYUAD experience figured out.

The cast spends the summer asking questions together:

- What is happening to us?

- What are we learning?

- What are we struggling with?

- What are we not talking about?

- And what might be useful to say to the people coming next?

The Center for Student Belonging offers a variety of programs that enable students to develop and refine their cultural humility by engaging with differences and commonalities, exploring values, and reflecting on their personal growth. Restorative Practice Ambassadors (RPA) are student leaders who are skilled in proactive conflict transformation and collaborate with RAs and other groups to cultivate a culture of conflict competence at NYUAD. Connect with an RPA at nyuad.conflicttransformation@nyu.edu and learn more about their programs and initiatives.

NYUAD Career Development Center
The Career Development Center (CDC) plays an integral role in your undergraduate experience by providing guidance, advising, programs, and resources . From choosing a major, CV support, finding jobs and internships, and all the next steps in students' unique career paths, the CDC empowers students throughout their time at NYUAD and beyond.

NYUAD Civic Engagement and Service
Civic Engagement and Service (CES) builds bridges between NYUAD and the UAE through cultural, outreach, and volunteer engagements. Connecting with the culture of the UAE is an important part of creating a well-rounded experience during your time at NYUAD. Service programs are a great way to proactively immerse yourself in the UAE, give back, and seed social impact.

NYUAD Campus Safety
Campus Safety is committed to providing safety and security for our community and property, enabling the pursuit of academic and professional goals. For quick references, please note that the Campus Safety information is available at the back of your campus ID, and you can contact them 24 hours a day, 7 days a week at 02-628-7777 or nyuad.campussafetylink@nyu.edu .

UAE Cultural Expectations, NYUAD Community Values, and Relationship Respect
NYUAD students are expected to be aware and respectful of UAE cultural norms and local laws , which are deeply rooted in Islamic traditions and Emirati cultural heritage. Fostering a campus culture of mutual care and respect is central to our community, and we are committed to a community centered on Non-Discrimination and Anti-Harassment , free of bias, prejudice, discrimination, retaliation, and harassment regardless of any demographic factors - no matter the location of NYU. Please also familiarize yourself with NYU’s global sexual misconduct, relationship violence, and stalking policy , which highlights prohibited behavior, pathways for reporting, and resources available.

sections.title: Maybe Next Year It's You!
sections.text:
If something in the show resonated with you, or if you found yourself thinking about what you would have said, you might want to make The RealAD Show with us.

Auditions for The 2027 RealAD Show will take place in Spring.

We are looking for students who are curious, funny, thoughtful, musical, strange, honest, theatrical, not theatrical at all, or simply have something they want to explore.

You do not need to see yourself as a writer or performer.

Want to hear when auditions open? Sign up for updates or follow us on Instagram at @nyurealityshow .

sections.title: The Process
sections.text:
The RealAD Show is made through conversation, experimentation, writing, music, movement, rehearsal, and a lot of trial and error.

You do not have to arrive knowing how to write a monologue or compose a song.

You do not have to have your NYUAD experience figured out.

The cast spends the summer asking questions together:

- What is happening to us?

- What are we learning?

- What are we struggling with?

- What are we not talking about?

- And what might be useful to say to the people coming next?

title: Weyak Program · NYUAD Students
text:
What Is the Weyak Program?

In Arabic, "Weyak'' translates to "with you," encapsulating the essence of the Weyak Program at NYU Abu Dhabi. Designed to empower first-year students, the Weyak program aims to cultivate familiarity with campus resources, nurture essential skills for college success, and foster growth within a supportive living and learning community.

Weyak Facilitators serve as first-year students’ primary point of contact for peer mentoring support across Marhaba and the fall semester. They play an instrumental role in delivering a semester of curated sessions in line with Class Year Experience’s Weyak Curriculum, which is focused on helping students navigate their new experiences at NYU Abu Dhabi. They will also lead fun and meaningful community programming that helps first-year students further understand the culture of NYUAD, Abu Dhabi, and the UAE.

Vision

To be an inclusive, supportive living and learning community for first-year students throughout their college transition.

Mission

To provide holistic support to first-year students by building a living and learning community of care, fostering a strong sense of belonging on campus, and developing key skills for their college success.

Principles of Curriculum Design

The Weyak curriculum is designed and anchored in the following core principles:

- Community Building – this sits at the heart of all content and activity design. To allow for open, honest, authentic, and at times, difficult conversations, a restorative practice approach will be taken, and training and facilitation skills provided.

- Identity Exploring — this will be central to first-year students’ journey where developmentally, they will either naturally ask or be led to explore questions such as “who am I?” (= self), “where do I fit in?” (= belonging), and “who are there together with me” (= community).

- Intercultural Awareness and Sensitivity — students will first learn about where they are on the intercultural development continuum and, through time, learn about how to shift from a monocultural to an intercultural mindset.

- Experiential Learning — students will be given abundant information and support resources through which they get to explore and possibly design the college journey that best meets their goals and expectations through some degree of trial and error.

Related official links:
https://students.nyuad.nyu.edu/student-affairs/center-for-student-belonging/intercultural-education/

title: Senior Year Experience · NYUAD Students
text:
You are getting ready to graduate from NYU Abu Dhabi. Now what?

The completion of your senior year is a series of significant milestones and the beginning of a new adventure. You may experience some nostalgia as well as excitement and apprehension. You’ve worked hard, and you will fulfill your goal of graduating from NYU Abu Dhabi.

Class Year Experience works hand-in-hand with multiple collaborators, stakeholders, and student groups to support your Senior Year Experience. This includes programming across the academic year and includes activities such as 200 Days, 100 Days, and 50 Days to Commencement Milestones, and co-facilitated Senior Year Class Representative events. Moreover, opportunities such as commencement-related roles and opportunities are also embedded throughout the senior year curriculum.

Ma’a Salama Programming

“Ma’a Salama” means “Goodbye” in Arabic, and it is the term used to describe Ma’a Salama Week — the last days of your senior year between the final day of spring semester exams and commencement. Ma’a Salama traditionally includes campus-based events, facilitated off-campus activities, and passive programming for students and their families to attend as per their own schedule leading up to the commencement ceremony. These programs are an opportunity to cement the relationships you have forged, help you transition to your next journey, and dedicate time to say goodbye to friends, staff members, and faculty from across NYU Abu Dhabi.

Senior Year Class Representative

Lujain Elmallah
Email: le2205@nyu.edu

Lujain is a senior from Egypt studying Computer Science and Interactive Media. She is excited to join the student government and work on creating a memorable experience for this year's graduating class with a focus on post-graduate support and creating a strong sense of community that leaves a lasting connection. Beyond Student Government, she is passionate about film, photography, and travel, and enjoys exploring creative ways to bring people together through shared experiences.

Career Development Center
Your final year of undergraduate studies is a time of both celebration and transition, and the NYUAD Career Development Center is here to help you wherever you're headed — be it a job, graduate program, fellowship, a gap year, or any other new journey. Check out the steps that can help you in your transition from college to professional life.

Getting Started

- Review CDC Ultimate Career Guide (Handshake – Career Center – Resources).

- You can have your CV, cover letter, and LinkedIn profile reviewed by an advisor by booking an appointment or visiting us during our walk-in hours Monday to Thursday 2-4pm.

- Need to refine your CV? Utilize our CV/Resume Template (Just make a copy and type away!).

- Review our Back to Basics Series: CV, Cover Letter, Networking, and Interviewing.

Finding Opportunities

- Set up job alerts on Handshake, LinkedIn and other job search websites .

- Review slides shared at the Senior Career Prep Bootcamp.

- Utilize the NYUAD jobs label to review the latest opportunities posted on Handshake.

- Explore Vault Guides and GoinGlobal to find and learn more about different industries.

- Prepare for your interview and practice using Case Coach, Big Interview , and Yoodli .

- Learn about work visa options through our recorded sessions with Immigration Law Firm Fragomen US (J-1) and UK (HPI) Session, US (H1B) , Canada, NZ and Aus Session , UAE, Bahrain, and Saudi Arabia Session .

- Check out where NYUAD students have gained work experience: Use the student work experience map and the post-graduation employment map to explore work experiences that NYU Abu Dhabi alumni have had. All data is self-reported by NYUAD alumni.

- If you’re considering research opportunities, review post-graduate opportunities at NYUAD .

Exploring Graduate School

- Interested in Graduate School?

- Review our Essential Information and Preparation for Graduate Studies pages on the student portal.

- Check out where NYUAD students have gone to graduate school: Use the graduate school map to explore graduate and other professional programs NYU Abu Dhabi alumni have attended. All data is self-reported by NYUAD alumni.

- Utilize Kaplan All Access (access will expire after 12 months so if you’re planning on taking a standardized exam after you graduate, add your preparation course now !)

- Set a graduate school advising appointment on Handshake to talk about your timeline and next steps.

Next Steps

- Let us know where you landed after graduation by filling out the First Destination Survey (stay on the lookout for this within 6 months after graduation).

- Join the New York University Abu Dhabi NYUAD Alumni Network LinkedIn Group to stay connected!

Civic Engagement and Service
The Civic Engagement and Service (CES) department offers a wide range of programs to help students learn about and give back to their communities. We are here to help students embrace the UAE's rich diversity, foster a deep commitment to civic engagement and service, and cultivate ethical and inclusive leadership.

In Abu Dhabi, at this global crossroads, we focus on building key meta-competencies for NYUAD students, including service, cultural empathy, and an appreciation for the UAE’s unique cultural context.

Service-Learning Cultural Experiences

Through initiatives like the Kashtah program, students engage with the community, connect with the people of the UAE and learn from their stories, all while contributing to meaningful causes and deepening their understanding of the local culture and environment.

Kashtah in Emirati Arabic refers to a day trip taken in pleasant weather. These Kashtah excursions immerse students in authentic intangible heritage, provide opportunities to engage with the local culture and connect with Abu Dhabi Emirate nature in a unique setting. It is not only a unique cultural experience but also a holistic service-learning experience with many opportunities to give back.

Mentorship on Service-Learning and Social Impact Opportunities

We design volunteering and service-learning opportunities for students that promote meaningful community involvement, strengthen local, regional and global communities through advising, supporting and empowering students that are driven by social purpose.

We provide NYUAD students with professional training and work experience using inclusive, thoughtful, and innovative out-of-the-classroom experiences, which encourage the development of global leadership skills, providing resources, talent, and mentorship opportunities to organizations and community members seeking to engage NYUAD students, designing avenues for NYUAD students to give back to the UAE community through civic engagement, public service, and research highlighting the mutual benefits of philanthropy and civic engagement to both students and organizations to maximize the effectiveness and breadth of the community service experience.

Recommendation Letters

We can write recommendation letters for students who volunteer frequently with our department, as well as for those who demonstrate exemplary leadership and good conduct.

Commencement
NYU Abu Dhabi's Commencement Ceremony for the Class of 2026 will take place on May 19, 2026.

Communications from the Class Year Experience team will be shared throughout the academic year with key updates, commencement expectations, announcements, and application forms. These will be in collaboration with multiple university stakeholders, including the Career Development Center, Civic Engagement and Service, External Relations and Communications, and many more partners.

Emails will include action items such as: applying for student Commencement roles; Registering for Commencement and Name-calling; Portraits and video interviews; submitting Yearbook memories; etc.

Academic attire will be distributed to graduating students in late spring, and further information about this process will be communicated closer to the time.

If you have any questions, please email nyuad.cye@nyu.edu .

Spiritual Life, Intercultural Education, and Conflict Transformation

Intercultural Education

We support students in developing the cultural awareness and adaptability needed to thrive in diverse global settings. For seniors, this means reflecting on their intercultural journeys and preparing to apply their learning beyond NYUAD. This is achieved through the following:

- Intercultural Development Inventory (IDI) Class Debrief & Reflection Session : Seniors explore how their experiences have shaped their cultural perspectives and develop strategies for navigating new environments with intentionality and cultural humility.

- 1:1 IDI Debrief : Students receive a personalized deep dive into their assessment results, helping them gain deeper insights into their intercultural growth.

These conversations equip students with the tools to translate their intercultural learning into actionable skills for the workplace, graduate school, and life beyond graduation.

Conflict Transformation

Students can take the Intercultural Conflict Style (ICS) assessment to learn more about how they engage with conflict. Students can also get support from Restorative Practice Ambassadors (RPAs), who are trained student leaders who focus on conflict coaching and mediation.

Commencement Photos and Videos
A separate, commencement-specific media release has been introduced to address the unique circumstances related to graduation events and to ensure clarity, transparency, and student choice. Your response to the Commencement Media Release Form affects the use and sharing of photos, video, and audio recorded during Commencement-related activities.

To understand what choosing yes or no means, please visit the Commencement Media Use – What your Choice Means page.

Important: The student media release form you have signed previously remains relevant for all usage that is not related to Commencement.

Questions?

If you have questions about the Commencement Media Release, please email nyuad.photography@nyu.edu

Related official links:
https://students.nyuad.nyu.edu/academics/research/post-graduation-opportunities/
https://students.nyuad.nyu.edu/student-affairs/career-development/graduate-study/grad-school-essential-information/
https://students.nyuad.nyu.edu/student-affairs/career-development/graduate-study/
https://students.nyuad.nyu.edu/services/external-relations/commencement-photos-and-videos/

title: Student Activities · NYUAD Students
text:
Student Activities

What you learn in the classroom is only a small part of your college experience. For many students, serving on Student Government, leading a student club, and participating in programming on and off campus will be the defining moments of your time here. If you are planning to host an event, we can also help with your event planning.

Student Clubs

A primary goal for the Office of Student Life and Student Government is to ensure that students have the opportunity to pursue their passions, alongside exploring new interests and activities.
