title: Organizing Events · NYUAD Students
text:
Any events funded through the Office of Student Life should follow the event protocols listed below. This will typically include student clubs, Student Government, Debate, and any other ad-hoc events that have gained prior approval from the Office of Student Life .

- Step 1: Event Ideation

Events should be organized to facilitate the execution of the mission and vision of your organization. Funding will be provided based on how the event serves a need of the community. It will help to identify key goals and objectives of the event, which will also guide the event logistics. Here are additional considerations to keep in mind:

1. What are the goals behind the event?
2. What will define a successful event?
3. Has this event been done in the past? What worked and what didn't?
4. What other events are happening around the time you want to do this event? View upcoming events .
5. Are there any student affairs departments or student clubs you can collaborate with?

You may visit the Office of Student Life team in E-201 and E-202.

- Step 2: Book Event Location

Booking the right space for your event will depend on different factors including expected attendance, AV requirements, setup requirements, and availability.

Here is a guide on how you can book various locations.

Location | Lead Time | Capacity | AV | How to Book

Baraha Rooms | 2 + days | Up to 35 | Pre-installed | EMS

East/West Forum | 1-2 weeks in advance | East: 128 West: 200 | Pre-installed Projector, Speakers, and Mic | EMS

Outdoor Spaces (East/West Plaza, D1 Highline, Sexton Square) | More than 2 weeks | Variable | Additional AV Required Request 3 + weeks in advance | EMS

Classrooms/Academic Spaces | 5 days | Variable | Most classrooms have Pre-installed Projector, Speakers, and Mic | Fill out this form .

Gain approval of space booking before proceeding with further event organization. Please note that adding facilities and AV details in the EMS form will not provide those services. Follow the instructions below.

- Step 3: Request Setup (Tables, Chairs, Special Arrangements, Transport)

Please note that adding facilities and AV details in the EMS form will not provide those services. Please follow the instructions below. Tables and chairs may be requested by emailing the facilities team . Use this sample template .

Any special arrangements can also be requested in this email. This request needs to be made at least a week in advance.

If you have approved funding for transportation as listed in your budget, you will need to reach out to the Office of Student Life to coordinate the next steps.

- Step 4: AV

If your event requires AV (Audio Visual) support, specify your requirements in the AV section of the EMS Space Reservation Form . Select that AV support is required and provide a detailed list of the equipment and services needed. You must also identify a Student Club leader as the primary point of contact.

The EMS Space Reservation Form , including all AV requirements, must be submitted at least three weeks before the event . The AV Team will review the request and contact the designated primary contact. If you have not received a response, follow up with the AV Team at nyuad.av@nyu.edu .

For any large-scale event, we highly recommend that you submit your A/V request at the beginning of the semester and more than 3 weeks prior to your event date.

- Step 5: Submit an Event Request

If you are a registered student organization on Engage, please submit an event request to access funding and to advertise your event.

Come to office hours to get the event request approved. Here is a guide on how to submit an event request .

Connect with a Peer Leader during office hours via Engage to complete the event approval process.

- Step 6: Finances

To make a payment, you may follow one of the following options in order of preference:

1. P-card: Visit the Student Life during between 4 and 5 pm everyday to make a purchase using the p-card.
2. Reimbursement via Petty Cash: Visit the Student Life during between 4 and 5 pm and get reimbursed with petty cash. Bring your printed receipt. We try our best to provide the exact amount for your reimbursement; please be aware that if the exact change is not available, there may be a slight delay in your petty cash reimbursement. Fill out a purchase request. Please note that any amounts above 500 AED will require prior approval.
3. Reimbursement via upload to FAB Card: Reimbursements can be provided via an upload to your FAB cards if the amount is too high or payment via petty cash/p-card is not possible. This will take 3 weeks.

https://students.nyuad.nyu.edu/student-affairs/

title: Resources for Club Leaders · NYUAD Students
text:
Here are some resources that will assist you in your journey as a club leader.

- Club Funding Guidelines

Clubs are required to submit their budgets for the upcoming academic year around the end of the spring semester. This allows the Student Government Funding Board and the Office of Student Life to review budgets and ensure that clubs can plan their semester activities with their approved allocation in place.

Please submit your budget on Engage .

When evaluating a club’s budget request, the Student Funding Board will take into consideration the following criteria:

- Club Mission and Goals Does the request directly relate to the club’s stated objectives

- NYUAD Policies Does the request adhere to all relevant NYUAD policies and procedures?

- Cultural Sensitivity Does the request align with the NYUAD and UAE Values

- Benefit and Impact How large an impact will the funding request have on the club, its members, and/or the campus community?

- Scope : Club funding is not intended to support students studying abroad or fund international travel or accommodations. The primary audience for club funding should be students.

- Past Performance : Club's adherence to deadlines, success of past events, and performance factor into the amount of funding assigned.

- Accuracy of Budget Request : Using accurate estimations of attendees and numbers quoted in the funding guidelines will demonstrate effort put into submitting the budget.

The funding guidelines can be found below. These include the amount you can request across different categories like food, prizes, decorations, transport and more.

Number of Events: Clubs will only get funding for a maximum of 4 events per semester.

-
Food: Limited to AED 20 per person based on the estimated attendance for any club event. Allocation will be based on justification and previous event attendance.

-
Hallmark Funding: Provided for a maximum of one hallmark event per culture or community-based club per semester. Hallmark events are distinguished by their scale and intercultural learning objectives.

-
Expert Instruction : Funding will not be provided for paid lessons or coaching for individuals or groups affiliated with a club.

-
Prizes : Limited to a maximum value of AED 100 per event. Cash prizes and gift cards of any kind are not permitted.

-
Decorations: A maximum of AED 500 per event for decor for large-scale or club Hallmark events serving 100+ students. A maximum of AED 300 can be allocated for small to medium events serving 25-100 student attendees.

-
Conferences: Club funding cannot be used for payment toward conferences.

-
Subscriptions: Not allowed.

-
Local Transportation: May be provided where campus shuttles are not feasible. Please consult the Office of Student Life for transportation options.

- Reallocation Policy

In the event that clubs need to reallocate a portion of their approved budget request to a different event or purchase, the following guidelines apply.

- Reallocations may only happen from one category to another, for example, for food for one event to food for another event

- There should be a case made for the change including but not limited to the change in the needs of the community, additional events, and identified collaborations.

>Please note that after November 15 in the fall semester and April 15 in the spring semester, reallocations will not be considered.

- Engage Instructional Videos

1. Submitting an Event Request
2. Submitting a Purchase Request
3. How to Track Event Participation
4. Engage Basics
5. Club Alias Guide

- Club Leadership Transition

All clubs are expected to select leaders for the upcoming semester before the current one ends. This facilitates a smoother transition period and ensures that all clubs have leaders in place and can start the semester successfully. Each semester, Student Life will announce the timeline for elections in support of clubs completing this important process. Engage Elections allows you to set up voting within your club members, or E-board members exclusively.

There are two ways you can elect your new members:

1. Elections via Engage: Set up voting within your club members, or E-board members exclusively. This allows you to vote anonymously and view results anonymously, which is key! If you want to vote internally within your E-Board, you can set up an internal voting process using the Election feature and limit voters to your E-board by setting up an Eligibility list. Please see below step-by-step guidance, you can also refer to this short video .

2. Forms via Engage: If you want to review applications amongst the E-Board, you can set up your application under Forms and add reviewers to comment and vote on each application.

For a more detailed guide on using Engage for elections, read this guide .

- Non-NYUAD Guest Speakers and Performers

Before inviting an external speaker, performer, media representative, or notable guest, clubs must contact the Office of Student Life at nyuad.studentlife@nyu.edu . Student Life will coordinate with other relevant university offices as needed. Some events may require approval from the Department of Culture and Tourism (DCT Abu Dhabi). As the review process can take 10–15 working days, all required information should be submitted, whenever possible, at least 30 days before the event.

Do not confirm or publicly announce an external guest until all required approvals have been received.

- Guest Access

Prior to their arrival on campus, all external guests should be logged with Campus Safety no less than ten business days prior to their arrival on campus. Please email a list of all expected visitors to nyuad.campussafetylink@nyu.edu and copy nyuad.studentlife@nyu.edu . Guests will be directed to designated parking spaces on the B1 level when they arrive on campus. Visitors may collect a Visitor’s Pass from the Welcome Center if they will be on campus for an extended time during the day, or will need to access multiple buildings. Clubs are encouraged to meet visiting guests outside or in the lobby of the building where your event is taking place. By escorting your guest(s) through the campus, you ensure that they will not get lost or be stopped unnecessarily. It is also helpful to notify the security guards on duty in the area of your event so that they can further help direct guests to the correct location.

- Posters

The Campus Signage Procedure explains the areas that are permitted for faculty, staff and students to post relevant public messages such as flyers and posters around campus. This procedure is campus-wide and applies to all members of the NYUAD community including (but not limited to) faculty, staff, students, residents and guests.

Please note that exhibiting or affixing any unauthorized sign, advertisement, notice or other lettering, flags or banners, or hanging any projections that are inscribed, painted or affixed to any part of the outside of a building or the inside of the building which may be viewed outside of one's room is a violation of policy.

Procedure

Signage Spaces: Bulletin boards are located throughout the campus. They are designated for the posting of notices, flyers, posters and other communications for the community. No other areas, including but not limited to; internal and external walls, sidewalks around campus, glass doors and windows, outside of all elevators, building columns, and trees are designated for signage posting.

All signage should be posted using the appropriate method. For bulletin boards the only method is push pins. If you require push pins, these can be obtained from the facilities helpdesk: nyuad.facilities@nyu.edu or ext. 88888, option 3.

Some bulletin boards are designated to specific departments, groups, clubs, or specific locations. These boards are clearly labeled. These organizations have final say as to what can be posted on their boards and when the postings are to be removed.

All posted signage is subject to the following guidelines and any individual may bring forth a complaint. Posters in violation of the aforementioned and following criteria may be subject to removal.

Criteria

- If you wish to post on a bulletin board you may do so, but you are to remove your posting once the event has passed — within 24 hours.

- Event advertising cannot be posted more than 10 working days prior to the event/activity.

- Your signage must include your email address or other contact information, as well as clearly indicating sponsoring group’s or department’s contact information.

- If a poster or flyer is posted without the sponsor’s name and contact information, these fliers are subject to removal.

- Posters may not be posted over other active posters.

- Posters must not exceed 3 feet in length or width.

- Anything above this size constitutes a banner and is not permitted.

- Posters should be computer generated, but can include artistic hand drawings.

- Posters and flyers are permissible as long as they do not violate cultural norms of the UAE.

- One poster per activity/message is allowed on each approved bulletin board.

- Posters are not allowed in emergency staircases.

- Graffiti is not permissible (Definition — any defacement of property).

- Chalking is not permissible.

- Posters or flyers are not to be placed on cars.

Special Signage

Large outdoor signage or advertising (including geopolitical symbols or flags) is not allowed in public areas without prior approval. Requests for approval of large outdoor signs or advertising should be made through the facilities helpdesk nyuad.facilities@nyu.edu . Requests will be reviewed by a committee and sponsors will be notified of approval.

The NYUAD Operations department reserves the right to remove any and all signage that has not been posted in accordance with the above criteria. NYUAD is not responsible for missing, stolen or damaged materials. By posting on campus, the individual or organization agrees to hold the University harmless for any assessed damages or liabilities incurred.

Related official links:
https://students.nyuad.nyu.edu/student-affairs/student-conduct/nyuad-student-conduct-policy/policies/campus-signage-procedure/

title: Student Activity Spaces · NYUAD Students
text:
There are a number of great spaces on campus that are available for students. Whether you’re planning a club event, welcoming an off-campus speaker, or just looking to relax and enjoy one another’s company, there’s a space for you! Some spaces are very specialized and require a reservation, while others are more flexible and informal - show up at anytime! Below you can find a list of available spaces, as well as suggested usage and information about booking, AV, and more.

Baraha

In the local Emirati dialect, baraha means "open space." That’s exactly what you’ll find on the second floor of the Campus Center (East side). This focal point for students offers a wide range of activities and gathering places to relax, study, and have fun. The space is neatly divided into several zones depending on what you’re looking for.

- Lounge

At one end of the Baraha, you’ll find a quieter set of small couches where you can sit with friends or curl up with a good book. On the other side, you’ll find a large set of circular couches and a big screen television. This is the perfect location to watch a big sporting event or follow world events on the news.

- Work Space

These two massive wooden tables are a great place to spread out and work on a group project or study for an upcoming exam. You could also use them for arts and crafts, board games, a small party, or to reach out to classmates about an important event or issue.

- Activity Space

After a long day in class, everyone needs to find time to relax and unwind. What better way to do this than to play your game of choice with classmates.

- Two professional pool tables

- Two professional ping pong tables

- Foosball

Student Life Lounges

sections.title: Student Activity Spaces · NYUAD Students
sections.text: There are a number of great spaces on campus that are available for students. Whether you’re planning a club event, welcoming an off-campus speaker, or just looking to relax and enjoy one another’s company, there’s a space for you! Some spaces are very specialized and require a reservation, while others are more flexible and informal - show up at anytime! Below you can find a list of available spaces, as well as suggested usage and information about booking, AV, and more.

sections.title: Baraha
sections.text:
In the local Emirati dialect, baraha means "open space." That’s exactly what you’ll find on the second floor of the Campus Center (East side). This focal point for students offers a wide range of activities and gathering places to relax, study, and have fun. The space is neatly divided into several zones depending on what you’re looking for.

- Lounge

At one end of the Baraha, you’ll find a quieter set of small couches where you can sit with friends or curl up with a good book. On the other side, you’ll find a large set of circular couches and a big screen television. This is the perfect location to watch a big sporting event or follow world events on the news.

- Work Space

These two massive wooden tables are a great place to spread out and work on a group project or study for an upcoming exam. You could also use them for arts and crafts, board games, a small party, or to reach out to classmates about an important event or issue.

- Activity Space

After a long day in class, everyone needs to find time to relax and unwind. What better way to do this than to play your game of choice with classmates.

- Two professional pool tables

- Two professional ping pong tables

- Foosball

title: Student Clubs · NYUAD Students
text:
Find Others Who Share Your Passions

NYUAD Engage is the primary platform for Student Activities at NYUAD. It maintains a directory of clubs officially sponsored by the University and allows students to connect directly with club leaders online, and helps club leaders manage membership and budgets. All NYU students have access to Engage — simply use your NetID to log in.

- What Clubs Are Available?

Log into Engage to learn more about all the clubs currently active on campus.

- How Do I Join a Club?

You can join a club by requesting to be a member on the club’s Engage page.

Another way to do so is attending the Student Life Fest that takes place at the beginning of each semester. Co-organized by Student Government and the Student Life Team, they provide a wonderful opportunity to explore the diverse pantheon of clubs on campus and meet the students who lead them. As you walk around, you’ll have the chance to join as many groups as you like, learn about upcoming events, and watch demonstrations and performances.

Finally, you can also get in touch with the leadership of the club (via emails provided on the club’s Engage page) to acquire more information and join it. Remember, most clubss hold events that even non-members are welcome to attend!

- What Is Engage?

Engage is a platform all three campuses use that houses Student Life events from student clubs, Student Government, and Residential events. Engage allows students to connect directly with club leaders online, and helps club leaders manage membership and budgets. All NYU students have access to Engage — simply use your NetID to log in.

- How Do I Create a New Club?

- Can't find a club that already fits your interests? If there's a topic you love and you think that other students share your passion for it, you can start your own Student Club. For a detailed overview of the process, please review the Club Handbook on Engage .

- Choose a name

- Identify a Club Advisor

- Draft a Mission Statement

- Write a Governing Document

- Select a President and a Treasurer

- Find at least 10 other interested students

- Complete the Club Registration Form on Engage

- Once the club has been recognized by the Student Government with Student Life’s review, the group is eligible to request a budget in order to acquire funding for events.

You may also find it very helpful to schedule a meeting with a member of the Office of Student Life before you begin registering your club. We can help you think through the challenges your group may face and connect you with resources that will make you more successful.

title: Student Leadership Training · NYUAD Students
text:
Student Leadership Training

Student Leadership training provides foresight and prepares students to adapt to a complex, shifting, and uncertain world. This entails grounding ourselves in ‘proven’ evidence-based techniques and leadership frameworks, but also going beyond that to adopt a forward-thinking approach that is aligned with the latest developments in the field.

Leadership training is given to Student life leadership roles such as RAs, Weyak leaders, club leaders, and student assistants.

Leadership Competencies

Training focuses on creating awareness, practicing, and mastering leadership competencies that reflect their role. Some competencies are:

- conflict management - team building - integrity and honesty - external awareness - flexibility and resilience | - change management - leverage diversity - partnerships and collaboration - coaching and mentoring - communication and interpersonal skills | - accountability - strategic thinking and problem solving - innovation and entrepreneurship - the growth mindset

title: Marhaba Student Committee · NYUAD Students
text:
The Marhaba Student Committee (MSC) is a group of upperclass students dedicated to creating a welcoming and engaging environment for first-year students as they transition to life at NYUAD. Their goal is to foster a strong sense of belonging and catalyze the development of first-year students as they transition to life on campus at NYUAD.

In this role, student leaders take the lead in Marhaba, guiding new students as they join the NYUAD community. The position involves project-based work over the summer and includes in-person training sessions before Marhaba week. Their contributions are essential in creating a memorable and impactful orientation experience for incoming students.

Working on the Marhaba Student Committee will allow current students to actively build skills in areas such as leadership development, team management, peer mentorship, and event planning.

Apply Now!

If you're ready to embark on this exciting journey and contribute to the success of Marhaba Week, submit your application by March 30, 2025 11:59pm GST . We're looking forward to welcoming dynamic and passionate individuals to join our Marhaba Student Committee!

For inquiries, please email nyuad.cye@nyu.edu , and to submit your application, please visit Handshake .

title: Weyak Facilitator · NYUAD Students
text:
Become a Weyak Facilitator and Shape the NYUAD First-Year Experience!

Are you enthusiastic about fostering a supportive community, empowering your peers, and making a lasting impact on the NYUAD experience? Seize the opportunity to be a part of the upcoming Weyak Program as a dedicated Weyak Facilitator!

About Weyak

Experience the magic of "Weyak," meaning "with you" in Arabic, as you become an integral part of the Weyak Program at NYUAD. This transformative initiative is crafted to empower first-year students, guiding them through the exciting journey of university life while building a community of care and support.

Why Become a Weyak Facilitator?

As a Weyak Facilitator, you'll play a pivotal role in shaping the experiences of incoming students and contribute to the vibrant community at NYUAD. Here's a glimpse of what awaits you:

Training and Administrative Responsibilities

Engage in comprehensive training remotely from the second week of August to prepare for Marhaba Week and in-person training. This training begins a few days before the launch of Marhaba.

Dedicate bi-weekly late afternoons/early evenings for staff meetings, training, or Weyak Sessions.

Marhaba Week Magic

Participate in Marhaba by supporting the Marhaba Student Committee in sharing essential information and guidance with first-year students, planning events, and supporting first-years as they arrive on campus. You will connect with your Weyak groups remotely before Marhaba to have the chance to get to know them and be ready to welcome them as they arrive in Abu Dhabi. You will then support them throughout Marhaba!

Weyak Curriculum Delivery

Take the lead in delivering the Weyak curriculum throughout the fall semester, covering topics such as self-discovery, community values, self-care, intercultural competency, and more.

As a Weyak Facilitator, you'll have the opportunity to develop key skills in areas such as time management, conflict resolution, confidence, responsibility, public speaking, organization, peer mentorship, intercultural awareness, teamwork, and communication.

Apply Now!

If you're ready to embark on this exciting journey and contribute to the success of the Weyak Program, submit your application by March 30, 2025 11:59pm GST . We're looking forward to welcoming dynamic and passionate individuals to join our Weyak family!

For inquiries, please email nyuad.cye@nyu.edu , and to submit your application, please visit Handshake .

FAQs

- Is this position for the whole year or only one semester?

This position is for one semester only.

- Can I apply if I am studying away in the Spring?

Yes, you only have to be at the NYU Abu Dhabi Campus for fall 2024 to be eligible for this position.

- Will Weyak Facilitators live in A1?

No, Weyak facilitators can live in their chosen housing in the upperclassmen communities.

- What is the time commitment for the Weyak Facilitator position?

The employment period for the Weyak Facilitator position is July (remote), August (remote and in-person) and the entirety of the fall semester to Winter Break (in-person).

The Weyak Facilitator position requires an average of up to 3 hours per week of work time. This is an average of the time commitment required for team meetings, session preparation and facilitation, trainings, communications, etc..

title: Student Persistence and Well-being · NYUAD Students
text:
Student Persistence and Well-being empowers students to cultivate their holistic well-being, enabling them to thrive both academically and personally. The department provides one-on-one coaching to help students identify challenges and achieve their goals. It also provides mandatory and opt-in initiatives aimed at promoting mental health, mitigating risks, and fostering resilience by embedding well-being opportunities within existing spaces to strengthen emotional regulation. Additionally, the department collaborates with staff, faculty, and students to support students of determination while serving as a liaison to the Moses Center for Accessibility and Inclusive Culture at NYU.

title: NYU IRL (In Real Life) and The Nest | العُشّ · NYUAD Students
text:
We all know the feeling: wanting to put your phone down but not knowing if anyone else will join you.

NYU IRL is a first-of-its-kind university-wide commitment to being more in the moment. We’re creating phone-free spaces, events, and resources to make it easier to be present across Abu Dhabi, New York, Shanghai.

Why IRL, Why Now?

- Recognizes the growing impact of technology and social media on attention, relationships, and well-being

- Responds to increasing experiences of loneliness, isolation, and disconnection among students

- Creates more opportunities for face-to-face connection

- Encourages us to look up, be present, and engage with those around us

- Not anti-technology - it’s about balance and making space for real-world experiences

What IRL Makes possible

- Foster a culture of presence, connection, and belonging

- Create opportunities for authentic, in-person connection

- Strengthen community across NYUAD

- Support well-being and flourishing through meaningful real-life connection

This is your invitation to look up, lean in, and make the most of our time together.

Upcoming IRL Events at NYUAD: Fall 2026

-
The 2026 Presidential Welcome RealAD Show
September 14-15, 2026
For the first time, this signature NYUAD tradition will be device-free, bringing the student experience to life through comedy, music, dance, and drama while inviting us to be fully present and immersed in the experience.

-
Around the Longest Table joins the Hiwar Series
First week of November 2026
Formerly known as Dinner with Strangers, this IRL gathering is a collaboration between Student Persistence and Well-being, the Center for Student Belonging, and the Office of Global Access and Engagement. It brings our community together over a shared meal to put our phones down, be present, and meaningfully connect.

-
Daily Programming at the NEST العُشّ
All Fall
Join Student Persistence and Well-Being at The NEST العُشّ for daily themed programming throughout the semester, with opportunities to drop in, connect, play, and take a break.

-
Global Salon on Tech & Society
Fall 2026-Date TBD
Hosted by Student Affairs, the Global Salon on Tech & Society will bring together students, faculty, staff, and instructors from across the university for a device-free, interdisciplinary conversation about the role of technology in society.

- IRL Activation Grant: Supplemental Event Funding

AY 26-27

Have an event that would be better if everyone were fully present? The IRL Activation Grant provides student clubs and student leader groups with additional funding to bring NYU IRL to life by adding a meaningful device-free element to an existing event. Funding may support analog activities, facilitation, secure device storage supplies, or other costs directly connected to the device-free experience. Events may take place anywhere on campus, including the NEST | العُشّ (Al-‘Ush) . Applications must be submitted at least three weeks before the event. Apply here .

-
Doggy Destress
December 10, 2026
Hosted by NYUAD’s Peer Support Group, REACH, Doggy Destress is a chance to step away from the end-of-semester rush and recharge. Spend some time with our four-legged friends, or enjoy snacks, art activities, and games if that’s more your vibe.

The NEST | العُشّ (Al-‘Ush) at NYU Abu Dhabi

At the center of the NYU IRL movement is the NEST | العُشّ (Al-‘Ush)- NYUAD’s device-free space at A5A 204 — designed to help our community step away from screens and into the moment. Take a look at our daily themed programming that includes open drop-in hours, game nights, vision-boarding sessions, and workshops that invite you to pause - play - connect.

title: Student Support Coaching · NYUAD Students
text:
Student Affairs Office Relocations

Service/Team | Former Location | New Location (Effective Soon) | Note

Student Support Coaching (Student Persistence & Well being) | Student Affairs Suite | C2-E232, C2-E233, C2-E234 (Baraha side - former study rooms) | Email nyuad.supportcoaching@nyu.edu for appointments.

Academic and personal coaching to help students thrive

Student Support Coaching supports students with academic and personal coaching to help students thrive at NYUAD. We utilize evidence-based practices and a strength-based approach to address the specific challenges a student is experiencing. Our Student Support Coaches meet with students individually to provide one-to-one coaching where they share strategies , build specific skills, and create action plans to help students meet their personal and academic goals. We extend these strategies for success to groups via group coaching and presentations. — Meet the Student Support Coaching Team

We understand that the transition to and through university is unique for each student. We also understand that most students will experience academic or and/or personal challenges along the way. To us, success is more than just doing well. When all students can reach their full potential it significantly improves their well-being, creates a more meaningful academic journey — and most importantly — fosters a greater sense of belonging for them.

What we can help with:

- Identifying what it means to be a successful college student - Goal-setting - Building capacity around college-level study techniques and exam preparation - Resiliency - Cultivating or improving time management skills - Combatting imposter syndrome - Combating imposter syndrome | - Managing stress - Navigating classroom dynamics - Managing communication with faculty - Cultivating healthy relationships - Supporting first-generation and low-income students with accessing university resources - Schedule a session with the Student Support Coach team

Resources for Academic and Personal Success

Creating capacity to healthily navigate your academic and personal responsibilities while in university starts with understanding the expectations of the environment. The resources below are great ways to build your academic aptitude, and identify areas that may require the support of a Student Support Coach.

- Action Planning

Identifying specific, measurable, and achievable immediate, short-term, and long-term goals is key to building your academic aptitude. Use this action planning document (PDF) as a tool to keep you on track with mapping out and assessing the progress you have made toward your goals.

- Homework vs. Studying

Understanding the importance of designating time for homework and studying as separate objectives can really strengthen your academic outcomes. If you would like to explore the difference between homework and studying, in addition to calculating how much time you may need to devote to studying, check out our homework vs. studying guide (PDF).

- Note-Taking

The student note-taking guide (PDF) delves into how mastering your note-taking skills directly contributes to learning. We also offer note-taking method templates so you can jump right in!

- Charting Method (PDF)

- Cornell Notes Method (PDF)

- Mind Mapping Method (PDF)

- NYUAD Jargon

On top of navigating your academic and co-curricular responsibilities, it can feel like there is a whole new world of lingo that your peers or NYUAD community members are utilizing that you may be unsure about. Here's a NYUAD jargon list of tools, terms, and locations that you may hear referred to while on campus.

- Academic and Personal Well-being

Your academic and personal well-being is important (to you and us)! Check out our student well-being guide * for helpful sleep, time management, study help, and focus apps and tools.

*This is not an exhaustive list so please continue to explore if you don’t see an app that addresses your current needs.

- Other Helpful Tips and Resources

- ADD / ADHD Steps for Success (PDF)

- English

- Arabic

- Moses Center Accessibility Guide (PDF)

- English

- Arabic

- Text to Speech (tts) Voice Reading Apps

-
NaturalReader converts text, PDF, and 20+ formats into spoken audio so you can listen to your documents, ebooks, and school materials anytime, anywhere.

-
Speechify is a text to speech screen reader that can read any text, PDF, document, book, email, file, or article online out loud on your phone.

-
PDF : Your PDF documents can also be utilized in tts mode. Follow the instructions in the link to activate.

Student Testimonies

“During my first year at NYUAD, I struggled with participating in class. Gaining confidence to speak out and reach out to professors was very intimidating. On top of that, I wish that terms like “critical thinking” and “intercultural learning” that are often used in classrooms were unpacked so I can better engage with such methods.
-- Anushka Malla Upadhyay, Class of 2021, Theater and Social Research and Public Policy

“I look forward to using the Office of Student Success as a resource as I enter my second year of college. Especially as our class transitions from a year of remote learning to in-person classes, I believe that the office will be able to help the students navigate the changes in academic and social experiences.”
-- Colin Campbell, Class of 2024, Biology

“One of my biggest concerns as an incoming first year is the difficulty of the classes. I don’t feel as prepared as I should have been to take on college level courses due to the past year of remote learning. Feeling unprepared makes me feel less confident in myself and makes it a lot harder for me to speak out and participate in class. It’s reassuring to know that there is an entire office dedicated to targeting those concerns.’
-- Ina Negoiu, Class of 2025, Biochemistry

"Navigating academic and social settings with students from vastly different backgrounds can be challenging. Developing the soft skills that will prepare students to communicate these differences with an open mind is crucial in making sure that students have a successful NYUAD experience."
-- Sameera Singh, Class of 2022, Political Science and Theater

“Completing Capstone required intentional time management because it often requires students to take charge of their own timeline. Having resources available for time management and goal setting would have been helpful in making my Capstone journey smoother.”
-- Hatim Benhsain, Class of 2021, Interactive Media

title: Assistive Technology · NYUAD Students
text:
Types of Assistance Available

Hardware

Desktop Computer with Pearl Reader and Headphones

- Functions as an audiobook system for blind and visually impaired users.

- Capable of reading one page at a time.

- Allows two pages to be placed side by side for scanning.

- Integrated with JAWS screen reader software for accessibility.

- Designed for users who are blind or visually impaired.

- Scans and reads printed text one page at a time using OCR.

- Allows manual scanning of facing pages (one after the other).

Keystrokes Reference Guide

- Provides essential keyboard shortcuts for visually impaired students.

Software

JAWS Software Subscription

- Embedded within the Pearl Reader setup.

- Enables screen reading and navigation of scanned text.

OCR (Optical Character Recognition) — Conversion of printed texts to a readable format

- OCR technology can be used in situations where a book is not digitally available.

- Books can be scanned into OCR format and read aloud using text-to-speech applications.

Human Support

A staff member in the Center for Academic Technology (CAT) is available to assist students who struggle with using the hardware.

title: Reasonable Academic Accommodations · NYUAD Students
text:
Video tutorial: How to register for academic accommodations.

Reasonable Accommodations are adjustments to policy, practice, and programs that “level the playing field” for students with disabilities and provide equal access to NYU‘s programs and activities. Each student who registers with the Moses Center for Student Accessibility works with a Disability Specialist to develop a reasonable accommodation plan.

Academic Accommodation Includes (but not limited to):

- Testing accommodations

- Extended time for class assignments

- Use of a computer for exams

- Materials in an alternate format

- Provision of sign language interpreters

Reasonable academic accommodations do not negate requirements for successful completion of a program, course, or service or adherence to acceptable standards of behavior. It is important to note that some accommodations are not appropriate in all courses.

How to Register

- Complete the Online Application Form

If you have not registered with the Moses Center for Student Accessibility before, you should complete the Online Application Form .

It is advised not to submit multiple identical applications as this only duplicates effort on both ends. The committee meets on a bi-monthly basis.

It is, however, advisable that any additional documents obtained after an application has been submitted be sent to the Moses Center at mosescenter@nyu.edu .

Please also note that you may be required to register for reasonable accommodations on a yearly or semi-annual basis based on the expiration dates of any approved accommodations.

If you are submitting documentation in support of your application, you will also be required to complete the Authorization for Release of Information Form (PDF), which can be uploaded at the time of your registration.

- Any Third-Party Documentation (If Available)

If available, any third-party documentation which supports your request for accommodations should also be uploaded in the Application for Services form, if you have any trouble uploading documents, you may email them directly to the Moses Center for Student Accessibility at mosescenter@nyu.edu .

It will be helpful if these third-party documents:
(a) include a specific diagnosis,
(b) identify and provide a current picture of the substantial limitations in one or more major life activities,
(c) offer recommendations for specific related accommodations and explain how those recommendations relate to the substantial limitations, and
(d) include the title and signature of the evaluator

Examples of documentation include a current neuropsychological evaluation of psycho-education evaluation (generally for LD or ADHD), a Supporting Documentation for Consideration of Accommodations form (PDF) completed by a qualified health professional/clinician, or a detailed letter from a qualified evaluator or treatment provider.

- Submit Your Application

Once you have completed the new student registration and have submitted all of your appropriate documents, you will be contacted by a Moses Center Disability Specialist.

It may be helpful, in order to streamline the process, to have any pertinent documentation available during the first conversations with the Moses Center Disability specialist, but it is not necessary.

Please do not hesitate to register if you do not have any available or current documentation or if you need assistance in understanding what documentation might be appropriate to clarify and support your application for appropriate accommodations.

Separate Process For Reasonable Housing Accommodation

Please note that applying for Reasonable Housing Accommodations is an additional/separate process. If you require both Reasonable Housing and Reasonable Academic Accommodations , you must complete both applications.

Related official links:
https://students.nyuad.nyu.edu/student-affairs/student-persistence-well-being/student-persistence/reasonable-housing-accommodations/

title: Accessible Housing · NYUAD Students
text:
Video tutorial: How to request housing accommodations.

Requirements for Reasonable Housing Accommodations

The Moses Center for Accessibility and Inclusive Culture will review your request for reasonable accommodations if you:

- Have a documented disability. Please see the full definition of disability in the Informational Packet for Requesting Reasonable Housing Accommodations (PDF).

- Are eligible to reside in University housing .

- Complete the Authorization of Release of Information Form (PDF).

- Complete the Supporting Documentation for Consideration of Accommodation (PDF). Your healthcare provider should complete this form, or provide other supporting documentation.

After students complete steps 1-4, students can submit the Request for Reasonable Housing Accommodations . Requests are reviewed each Wednesday (excluding holidays or University closures). Decisions will typically be emailed to the student's NYU email address within two business days after the committee meeting

A housing accommodation approval does not guarantee a housing assignment; all approved accommodations are subject to the availability of the requested housing at the location of study, and must be in alignment with local laws and regulations. All students are subject to the NYU deadlines to request housing.

Studying at NYU Sites out of Abu Dhabi?

All students studying at any NYU site are required to email these completed forms and any supporting documentation to the Reasonable Housing Accommodations team in New York at mosescenter@nyu.edu for consideration. Information provided to the Moses Center is kept confidential and will only be shared in the Student Health and Wellness Center in New York as necessary to evaluate the request.

The student needs to carefully review the Financial Aid Award letter before applying for special housing accommodation through the Moses Center portal. The student may be responsible for the costs beyond those covered by the NYU Abu Dhabi financial aid. For more information about financial aid packages, please refer to the Office of Financial Support at nyuad.financial.support@nyu.edu.

Review of Your Documents

Your request and supporting documentation will be reviewed by a committee consisting of representatives from the Moses Center and the Student Health Center, including medical and counseling professionals. The committee meets bi-monthly in New York.

Once the committee has made their decision, they will inform the NYUAD Residential Education Operations Team about which accommodations are approved.

Due to the varied impact a disability may have on different major life activities, the Moses Center for Student Accessibility reserves the right to request separate, specific documentation for each housing or academic accommodation application.

Types of Housing Accommodations*

Single Rooms

Elevator Access to Classroom Spaces

Americans with Disabilities Act (ADA) Compliant Rooms

Specialized Suite Furniture and/or Fittings

*Approved housing accommodations are only provided if available.

Deadlines

The Moses Center decides what reasonable housing accommodations students are eligible for. As such, NYUAD students who qualify for reasonable housing accommodations are required to apply before the deadlines established by the Moses Center, specified on the Moses Center for Accessibility and Inclusive Culture Portal .

Your reasonable housing accommodation request may not be able to be fulfilled if you have missed the specified deadlines. Please contact the Reasonable Housing Accommodations team at mosescenter@nyu.edu if you have concerns or questions.

Separate Process For Reasonable Academic Accommodation

Please note that applying for Reasonable Academic Accommodations is an additional/separate process . If you require both Reasonable Housing and Reasonable Academic Accommodations, you must complete both applications.

Related official links:
https://students.nyuad.nyu.edu/campus-life/residential-education/housing/apply/new-student-housing/
https://students.nyuad.nyu.edu/student-affairs/student-persistence-well-being/student-persistence/reasonable-academic-accommodations/

title: Services for Students with Disabilities · NYUAD Students
text:
Supporting Students

We encourage students to participate fully in all aspects of life at NYUAD. Student Persistence and Accessibility works in close partnership with the Moses Center for Student Accessibility in New York to provide reasonable and appropriate accommodations for students with documented disabilities.

Both teams in Abu Dhabi and New York are available to advise students on NYUAD's policy, procedures, resources, and assist with approved accommodations. Any information provided by a student is voluntary and will be kept confidential.

All NYU students requesting accommodations are required to apply for academic accommodations through the Moses Center in New York. Once these accommodations have been decided upon, support will be provided to initiate the given accommodations through the Student Persistence and Accessibility team.

To Qualify

Students qualify as persons with disabilities if their diagnosed physical, learning, or psychological impairments limit them in one or more major life activities.

To register for services with the Moses Center, a student must provide current medical documentation of a disability. Medical documentation should include a specific diagnosis and be completed by a qualified licensed professional. If you feel you have a disability, but do not have any current documentation, please visit the Health Center on campus to meet with a medical doctor and/or therapist. For mental health-related accommodations, you must meet with the therapist at least four times.

The Student Persistence and Accessibility team does not make the final decision on accommodations. All accommodation requests are reviewed by the Moses Center team in New York. Please ensure that you only share your medical records on the secure Moses Center portal . Please do not share your medical records with anyone, as medical information is protected by HIPAA policies .

The Moses Center does not provide evaluation services for learning disabilities or ADHD.

Accommodation Letters

Students who require accommodation letters for their faculty should use the Moses Center's Student Online Portal to request them. Once you have requested an accommodation letter for a professor, the latter will receive an automated email alerting them that their student has an accommodation letter ready to be viewed through the Moses CSD Faculty Online Portal. — Learn how to request accommodation letters .

Temporary Disabilities

Students with temporary disabilities must follow the same registration procedures as all other registered students. When appropriate, accommodations are approved temporarily.

Obtaining Disability Documentation from the Moses Center

Students who need to have a copy of their disability documentation forwarded to another party must complete a signed release. The release form is available from nyuad.spa@nyu.edu .

Request Accommodation for NYU Study Abroad Program

Students who plan to attend an NYU Study Away program can seek academic and/or housing accommodations. — Learn about study-away accommodation

What Are Reasonable Accommodations?

Reasonable accommodations are adjustments to policies, practices, or procedures that facilitate equal access for students with disabilities to NYUAD's programs, activities, and services.

Accommodation plans and other related services are individualized based on each student’s disability-related needs, disability documentation and NYU program requirements and are therefore determined on a case-by-case basis.

Related official links:
https://students.nyuad.nyu.edu/student-affairs/student-persistence-well-being/student-persistence/studying-away/

title: Studying Away · NYUAD Students
text:
Studying Away in NYU's Global Network

With many studying away at locations throughout the University's global network, it is a concern of NYU that all our students are able to get the reasonable accommodations they need as they pursue Study Away Opportunities . We therefore strongly encourage all students with documented disabilities who are considering global opportunities at NYU to contact the Moses Center for Students Accessibility at mosescenter@nyu.edu prior to selecting a program . A Moses Center Specialist will discuss reasonable accommodations at your locations of interest.

Request Accommodation for NYU Study Abroad Program

Students who plan to attend an NYU Study Away program and seek academic or housing accommodations at a particular site should contact the Moses Center to request accommodations.

Students must be registered with the Moses Center to be eligible for accommodations whether they are NYU students or students from another institution.

The Moses Center will work with the student and the Study Away Program to arrange approved accommodations. Students with disabilities planning to study away are strongly urged to obtain information in advance regarding the specific site’s programs and facilities and to arrange a meeting with a CSD representative to discuss potential barriers.

Already Registered in a Global Program?

If you have already registered with the Moses Center, have been enrolled in a global program, and are requesting Reasonable Academic Accommodations while at your study away location, you must notify the Moses Center.

To notify the Moses Center, students should contact their Disability Specialist or mosescenter@nyu.edu .

Students are encouraged to let the Moses Center know they are studying away as soon as possible, preferably at least four to six weeks before departure . The Moses Center will then send a verification letter to the student’s global site and the student will be instructed to discuss the implementation of their academic accommodations with their study away site's Moses Center liaison.

All students accepted to study away programs who are requesting reasonable academic accommodations MUST be registered with the Moses Center.

Students who wish to request Reasonable Housing Accommodations at NYU’s global sites must complete the Request for Reasonable Housing Accommodations Application .

Related official links:
https://students.nyuad.nyu.edu/academics/global-education/study-away/

title: Testing Accommodations · NYUAD Students
text:
Request Testing Accommodations

Students with testing accommodations need to complete the Testing Accommodation Form at least seven business days prior to their exam, excluding the exam date . However, students are encouraged to submit the form for all their exams at the beginning of the semester to avoid late, last-minute requests. This is to ensure that the Student Persistence and Well-being team can communicate with faculty and facilitate exam proctoring. Please note that business days are from Monday to Friday.

Note: Any weekend, public holiday, or exam day requests are not calculated in the seven-day period .

Examination Process

Before the Exam

- After receiving an accommodation letter from the Moses Center, it is the responsibility of the student to request that the letter be sent to the professors whose courses they want accommodations for. To request accommodations for a specific exam, the student must fill out the Testing Accommodation Form after informing the respective professor(s) and agreeing on a date, time, location, and information on the delivery of the exam. The form should be filled out seven days before the exam.

- Once the accommodation letter has been sent to the professors, the student should email their professors inquiring if they can arrange their accommodations. Only if the professor is unable to arrange the accommodation should the student contact the Student Persistence and Accessibility team, in which case, support will be provided based on proctor availability.

- "Smaller proctored testing environment" is an exam environment that has 15 or fewer test-takers (it is not a single or private room). The Dean of Students Office can provide help with proctoring if the professor can not provide the approved accommodations.

- No books, notes, electronics, or personal belongings are allowed inside the exam room. Exceptions are made by the professors and need to be highlighted on the Testing Accommodation Form (e.g., calculator, etc.)

Day of the Exam

- Students need to arrive at least 10 minutes before the exam to ensure everything is in place. If a student is late, their exam time will be cut short and the ending time of the test will not change.

- The professor will be notified if a student is late or did not show up for the exam.

- Students taking an exam at the Dean of Students Office or the Testing Center must leave their belongings outside the room unless the professor has instructed the exam proctor to bring items in the room, e.g., pen or scratch paper, etc.

- Mobile phone(s) or any other electronic devices need to be completely switched off and out of the room, along with the student’s other belongings, except when the device is officially approved.

- Talking is not allowed during exam time, and the professor will be notified of any behavior that violates the NYUAD Academic Integrity Policy .

During the Exam

- Any cheating or other form of academic dishonesty will be reported to the appropriate University officials and may result in disciplinary action.

- Please be mindful of other students who are taking the exam in the same room and avoid unnecessary noises.

- Students should alert the proctor if they have any questions about the exam, and the professor will be contacted.
If you finished your exam early, you need to alert the proctor and leave the room quietly.

After the Exam

- Ensure all information is accurate and your name and date in on the exam paper. Hand all exam papers to the proctor and leave the room quietly.

- Your professor will indicate how the exam will be returned to them in the form. After you hand in your exam to the Moses Exam Center, make sure to check how the exam will be returned to the professor. You may need to deliver the exam to the professor.

title: Student Well-being · NYUAD Students
text:
Student Well-being at NYUAD promotes a holistic approach to well-being, grounded in the understanding that true flourishing arises from more than any single aspect of life. Guided by the eight dimensions of well-being , we invite students to explore how each dimension contributes to their overall health, fulfillment, and capacity to flourish. We recognize that these dimensions are deeply interconnected and that change or imbalance in one area can ripple into others. Our goal is to help students develop early awareness of this interdependence and to engage intentionally with their whole well-being during their university journey.

Through interactive workshops, credit-bearing courses, and peer-led initiatives, Student Well-being supports students in strengthening key Violet Ready Metacompencies, including self-awareness, resilience, and resource mindfulness. By cultivating these capacities, students become better prepared to meet academic demands, navigate personal transitions, and thrive both during and beyond their time at NYUAD

Mandatory Training Programs

-
Life Skills Part II Workshop

Flagship Programs and Opt-in Initiatives

- Everyday Resilience Workshops

- Mindful Self-Compassion Workshops

- Emotional Regulation & Resilience (PHE Course)

- Holistic Well-being (PHE Course)

- Here4U (Digital Well-being Hub)

Student Testimonies

“I really liked how engaging the training was, and how I felt like it was not just an information session.”
Participant of Mindful Self-Compassion Workshop

“I liked how the training made me feel present in the moment, and I remember feeling very calm after the first training we had.”
Participant of ACT Training

“I liked the activities, it made us bond with our classmates and that helped in improving the quality of the class. That is because the classroom became a safe space.”
Participant of Emotional Regulation and Resilience Course

“I learned a lot of techniques about how to recognize destructive patterns and how to address them and how to deal with them. I’ll carry the breathing techniques and the 'name to identify' techniques with me.”
Participant of Emotional Regulation and Resilience Course

https://students.nyuad.nyu.edu/student-affairs/student-persistence-well-being/student-well-being/well-being-dimensions/

title: Well-being Dimensions · NYUAD Students
text:
Well-being at NYUAD

At NYU Abu Dhabi, we understand that well-being is a continuous, active process of becoming aware of and making intentional choices towards a healthier and more fulfilling life. Everything we do and feel, connects us to our well-being. By engaging with each of the eight dimensions of well-being, we can cultivate balance, strengthen resilience, and create meaningful growth across all areas of life. Student Affairs offers resources, workshops, and peer-led initiatives that help you explore and strengthen each of these eight dimensions throughout your university journey. By taking intentional steps toward balance, whether through reflection, community, or physical activity, you invest not only in your own well-being but in the well-being of the NYUAD community as a whole.

Individual and Community Benefits

-
Greater self-awareness and emotional balance

-
Healthier lifestyle choices and physical vitality

-
Enhanced mindfulness and improved emotional well-being

-
Stronger connections within a supportive campus community

-
Increased sense of purpose and personal fulfillment

Your Well-being at NYUAD

Well-being is an active process of becoming aware of and making healthy and positive choices towards a healthier and fulfilling life. Well-being refers to a more holistic, whole of life experience, whereas wellness refers just to the physical aspects of health.

Our vision is to cultivate and promote enhanced health, greater attitude towards well-being, heightened individual performance and educating the NYUAD community on their current and future well-being endeavors.

The Well-being Wheel

Our model of well-being includes eight interconnected dimensions: Emotional, Physical, Environmental, Financial, Intellectual, Occupational, Spiritual, and Social.

Each dimension contributes uniquely to your overall well-being, yet none exist in isolation. Growth or neglect in one area can influence the others. When balanced and nurtured, the eight dimensions work together to create a foundation for lifelong health, meaning, and resilience.

The Library will resume in-person services starting Monday, April 27, 2026 from 9am to 5pm (Monday–Sunday) for NYU Abu Dhabi students, faculty, and staff.

At this time, we are unable to accommodate external visitors, including affiliated program members (e.g., community access users and university fellows).

All eligible loans (excluding ILL and EZ Borrow items- borrowed from NYU's partner institutions) have been extended through the start of the Fall 2026 semester for faculty, staff, and students. This extension ensures continued access to library materials while many members of the NYUAD community are away.

Virtual support remains available via email ( nyuad.library@nyu.edu ) or chat using the widget at the bottom of our webpages.

Please refer to the NYUAD Library webpage for any updates to our services and hours.
